### 8.178 An intrinsic symbol carries its declaring module; `verify-freestanding` green; `cross-check`, the other OS's half on this host - 2026-09-13

§8.177's item 0, closed at its cause, and the gate that would have caught
it the day it landed.

#### The cause, read rather than instrumented

The handoff proposed instrumenting `callee_family` for the bare
`frame_address(0)` in the Linux `backtrace` tier: is `ident.res` `Def` or
`Pending`, and what does `intrinsic_owner_of` answer.  Reading the writer
answered it without a probe, and the probe would have read a false zero
on the wrong function.  `Symbol::intrinsic` set `source_module` to the
placeholder string `"<intrinsic>"` - `Symbol::constant`, two constructors
below, takes the declaring module as `mod_str` - so `bare_name_res`
stamped the call `Def("<intrinsic>::frame_address")`, a canonical name
nothing is registered under: the index holds the intrinsic's signature
under `CryoRt::Backtrace::frame_address` (`qualify_symbol_sym_home` of
the leaf and the declaring file, `type_resolution.cryo`'s intrinsic arm)
and under the bare leaf.  `callee_family` reads the `Answered` stamp, so
the `Pending` arm - the one door to `intrinsic_owner_of` - was never
taken; the family had no overloads; E0202.  Before §8.173 the bare
binder's HOME step re-derived the key from the leaf and the cursor and
rescued it; that step was deleted with the rest of the ladder, and the
placeholder was exposed.  It dates from the resolver's first commit (2026-02-28).

The fix is the declaring module in the symbol, and nothing in sema: a
same-module intrinsic is an ordinary `Def` whose key is the index's, and
the pin it produces is the intrinsic's own symbol (`frame_address`, C
linkage), which `callee_is_intrinsic` reads as the intrinsic and lowers
inline - the object shows `fp = %rbp`, no undefined `frame_address`.
Routing it through `Pending` → `intrinsic_owner_of` instead would have
widened §8.93's hold, the wrong side of that fence.

Population: one.  `runtime/backtrace/src/lib.cryo:45` is the only
`intrinsic function` declared outside `stdlib/core/intrinsics.cryo`, and
`intrinsics.cryo` calls none of its own bare (its mentions are comments).
Predicted 0 objects moved on both populations; measured examples **0 of
1,126**, tests **0 of 2,182**, suite green (2,116 unit, 179 negative, 45
projects), LSP builds directly, b1 unmoved (B1 0, 56 rows), lane golden
unmoved.  `cd runtime && cryo build --target=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`: E0202
at `lib.cryo:62` before, `Project compilation succeeded` after, all five
freestanding tiers.

#### The gate: `make cross-check`

Every "zero disagreements over the corpus" since §8.152 was measured on a
Windows host, over a tree with the Linux half pruned by config gating
before name resolution saw it: **326 `![target(linux)]` /
`![target(unix)]` attributes across 32 stdlib files, 23 across 6 runtime
files, 11 across 7 compiler files, 6 across 4 LSP files**, and no gate on
this host name-resolved any of them.  CI covers Linux and fires on `main`
alone, which is how the tier stayed red.

`cryo build --target=<triple>` selects the other OS's gates and compiles
every module through name resolution, sema and codegen to object files;
the link is skipped, so no cross toolchain and no WSL.
`scripts/cross-check.py` runs it over `runtime/`, `stdlib/`, `compiler/`
and `tools/CryoLSP`, cold (build directories removed and re-created
first - the driver creates the build directory but not its parent, and a
missing parent reads as `codegen failed for module ...: no such file`),
reads exit codes, and refuses a build that reported no population or a
total under 350 modules.  The default triple is the OS the host is not:
`x86_64-pc-linux-gnu` here, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` on Linux (the `pc`
vendor is what `cryo version --triple` reports on both, and the
per-triple directories the tree carries spell it so).  Built with the
compiler under test, for `lsp-check`'s reason.  About 80 seconds on this
host: runtime 10 modules in 5 tiers, stdlib 154, compiler 245, LSP 266.

The pair, on the tree this entry fixes:

* **HEAD's compiler** (`a7c842df`, copied out of the build tree) under
  the gate: `cross-check: FAIL -- runtime: build exited 1`, `E0202:
  cannot find function frame_address`, `backtrace/src/lib.cryo:62:19`.
  Every host gate over the same tree was green.
* **This tree's compiler**: `cross-check: OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu: ...;
  0 errors`.

And the control on the instrument's reach into the stdlib, since the
runtime alone would not show that: `libc::setenv` renamed to
`libc::setenv_nope` inside the `![target(unix)]` `set_var` in
`stdlib/env/_module.cryo`.  The host stdlib build over the mutation:
`Project compilation succeeded`, exit 0 - the function is pruned before
the name is looked up.  `make cross-check` over the same tree: `FAIL --
stdlib: build exited 1`, `E0233: cannot find libc::setenv_nope`,
`./env/_module.cryo:134:21`.  Restored.  The Linux-host arm was
exercised once through WSL with the Linux pin: runtime and stdlib
compile for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, 164 modules.

What it cannot see: nothing links and nothing runs, so a symbol the other
OS's libc lacks, or a wrong object, is still `verify-freestanding`'s and
CI's to find.  `tests/` and `examples/` are host-native projects and are
not built; their gated surface is the stdlib's, which is built whole.

#### Owed by §8.177: the predicate's latent case

`callee_is_intrinsic` treats a pin equal to the bare leaf as the
intrinsic.  An `extern "C"` function is pinned to its C symbol, which IS
its leaf, so an extern declared under a pure-magic intrinsic name - one
`IntrinsicKind::is_name` knows and no `intrinsic function` declares,
`bswap32`, the casts - would inline as the intrinsic instead of being
called.  Measured empty: 51 pure-magic names (105 in the table, 58
declared in `intrinsics.cryo` plus `frame_address`) against 986 distinct
extern-block function names over 92 blocks, intersection ∅; the same
scan lists `malloc` / `free` / `realloc` when widened to declared names,
so it sees a hit.  Latent, not live.  Recorded so nobody rediscovers it
by declaring `bswap32` in an extern block; the fix when it is live is a
pin that carries the declaration's identity rather than a symbol a leaf
can equal.

**Tally unchanged: 33 shadowed, 33 old paths deleted, 32 at zero and one
at §8.93's allocator residue; 30 artifacts gone.**  This entry deletes no
lane; it removes a placeholder and adds a gate.

#### What this leaves

The handoff's items 1-4 stand as §8.177 wrote them: the impl head's
HOME → BARE lookup in `type_resolution.cryo` (3 sites, §0.2's row), then
`qualify_symbol_sym_home` (48 sites), `Resolver::lookup_prelude`'s
two-export tie, `codegen_target_name`'s rewritten spelling.  Parked for
Jake, unchanged: D5, the keyword ruling (§8.165), the extern-visibility
default (§8.167, normative in `docs/cryo.md` §18.1 and never confirmed).

### 8.179 Consumer 34: the impl head's HOME → BARE lookup in `type_resolution.cryo`, deleted; three sites read the stamp - 2026-09-13

§8.174 deleted the impl head's spelling carrier from sema and left the
same shape standing three times in `type_resolution.cryo`:
`lookup_type(qualify_symbol_sym_home(node.target_type, file))`, then
`lookup_type(node.target_type)` - the writer's module prefixed to the
spelling, then the bare spelling - at the two FuncSig-phase sites that
resolve an impl block's method signatures and at `run_struct_field_sync`'s
site that places the block's methods on the owner type.  Name resolution
runs first and stamps `ImplBlockNode.res`; each site now reads it as
sema's `impl_target_type` does: `Def(q)` → the index under `q`,
`PrimTy(n)` → the index under `n`, an unanswered slot → the
monomorphizer's `spec_owner`.  The owner's canonical name, which the
FuncSig sites hand `resolve_method_signatures` for the self-growing
check, comes off the same stamp (`impl_owner_qname`) instead of a second
`qualify_symbol_sym_home`.

#### Measured

Shadow at the three sites, the old pair kept, the stamp's answer computed
beside it, one line per disagreement in type OR name.  **91,910 over the
six halves, 0 failing halves**:

* **74,977 primitive heads** (`implement i32`, `implement trait Clone for
  u8`, ...): the TYPE agrees; only the name differs, because
  `qualify_symbol_sym_home` prefixes the writer's module to a primitive
  too (`std::core::clone::i8`), a key nothing is registered under - so
  the self-growing check has been comparing every primitive impl against

  instantiations to grow) and now `i8`.
* **16,930 `Def` heads where the old pair answered INVALID and the stamp
  answers the type** - every one a trait implemented for ANOTHER module's

  the LSP's `semantic_tokens.cryo`.  The HOME key names the writer's

agreeing lines printed (182 + 182 + 317), none of that build's 480

#### Why the objects did not move, and that it was predicted wrong

Predicted before the run: a small nonzero mover set, in objects whose
bodies call a cross-module-implemented method with a literal argument -
the newly listed methods feed `lookup_method_param_types`'s
expected-type propagation.  Measured: examples **0 of 1,126**, tests **0
of 2,182**, suite green (2,116 unit, 179 negative, 45 projects).  The
zero is explained by the consumers, not banked: `lookup_method_param_types`
is reached only when `lookup_callee_function_type` has not already bound
the method, and a trait-implemented method binds through the trait
registry first; the receiver back-fill the FuncSig sites now perform was
already performed by sema's `impl_target_type` for the same heads; the
self-growing check gains no candidate (a `fmt(&this, &Formatter)` grows
nothing); `scope_member_binds_type` is asked only after the static-call
pin has had its turn.  Two probe programs confirm it: a trait implemented
in one module for another module's struct, called as `p.weigh(2)` and
`Parcel::weigh(&p, 0)`, and a namespace-less single file with an

### 8.181 D16, RULED: an impl head writes its target's parameters, or names an instantiation; the bare form is refused - 2026-09-13

§8.180 found a bare impl head on a template whose parameters all default
carrying two meanings in the tree - the default instantiation
`String<GlobalAlloc>` when written in another module, the template when
written in its own - and asked which.  **Jake's ruling: neither.  The
spelling is refused.**  The writer says which is meant, as in Rust:
`implement<A> trait Display for String<A>` for the template, or
`implement trait Display for String<GlobalAlloc>` for the instantiation;
`implement trait Display for String` is a compile error because the
parameters are missing, and no default meaning is assigned.  Source-
breaking for every head that elides them; taken knowingly.

**Decided, not built.**  What building it needs, so the next agent starts
from a decision:

* **The population** - `scripts/impl-head-elided-params.py`, committed
  with this entry.  BARE heads (no arguments on a generic template):
  **4**, all `String` - `stdlib/collections/string.cryo:456` and `:464`
  (same-module, the symbolic walk today), `stdlib/fmt/display.cryo:502`
  and `stdlib/fmt/write.cryo:91` (cross-module, the concrete path today).
  Every other defaulted template (`PathBuf<A>`, `Mutex<T, A>`,
  `Rc`/`Arc`/`Weak`, `Box`, `RawBuffer`, `RwLock`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`,
  `Array`) already writes its parameters on every head.  PARTIAL heads
  (some arguments written, the trailing defaulted ones elided -
  `implement<T> trait Display for Array<T>` with `Array<T, A =
  GlobalAlloc>`): **7**, in `box`, `array`, `hashmap`, `hashset`.  Rust
  fills the default there (`impl<T> Trait for Vec<T>` is `Vec<T,
  Global>`); the ruling names the BARE form and does not decide the
  partial one - ask before touching it.  **Asked and ruled in, §8.187:
  every parameter is written, the partial form is refused by the same
  rule, and the population is 11.**  The script matches by leaf with
  locality (own file, then own directory, then own tree) and lists
  cross-tree collisions as UNMATCHED (0), so `tests/`' many independent
  `Counter`s do not count.
* **The code**: `E0302_GENERIC_PARAM_MISMATCH` is declared in
  `diag/_module.cryo` with no emitter (as are E0300 and E0301); the shape
  - 0 of N parameters written where N are declared - is a parameter-count
  mismatch, so reuse it rather than mint.  If a reviewer reads the name
  as something else, mint; survey first either way.
* **The diagnostic says what to write**, not only what is wrong: for
  `implement trait Display for String` it names both accepted spellings,
  the template form with the head's own `<A>` and the instantiation with
  the default filled in, since the writer of the bare form may not know
  the parameter exists.  A `suggest` with two alternatives, or a note
  carrying both, as `E0154`'s "write the path out" does.
* **Where**: after name resolution stamps the head (`Def` of a template
  entry with parameters) and before TemplateRegistration attaches it -
  the stamp says the target is a template, the head says it wrote no
  arguments.  `ast_validation`'s `validate_impl_block` (E0062, the
  target-less head) is the same kind of check one pass too early to know
  the target is generic.
* **Then** `visit(ImplBlockNode)` in `sema.cryo` reads `target_key()`
  like every other site (§8.180 left it on `qualify_symbol_sym_home`
  because the two meanings disagreed there): once the bare form is
  refused there is nothing ambiguous left to resolve, the symbolic
  branch is for a head that wrote the template's parameters and the
  concrete path for one that wrote an instantiation, and the last
  impl-head `qualify_symbol_sym_home` goes.
* **Interacts with the keyword ruling** (§8.165): `implement int` stamps
  `Pending` because `int` is an alias keyword, not a template, so it is
  not this ruling's population - but the same site sees both, and the
  keyword ruling is what makes `int` resolve as `i32` for a head.  Build
  D16 without depending on it; expect the two checks to sit side by side.

**Tally unchanged: 35 shadowed, 35 old paths deleted, 34 at zero and one
at §8.93's allocator residue; 33 artifacts gone.**

### 8.186 Consumer 40: a constant in pattern position binds from its stamp; codegen's leaf-keyed `resolve_global` for it deleted - 2026-09-14

The identifier-value lane's twin (§8.167), one node kind over.  An

is recognised by the name layer, which records the resolution in its own
table, moves the name into `value` and stamps NOTHING on the node - the
base `PatternNode` carried no slot (only `EnumPatternNode` did).  Codegen's

so two modules declaring one leaf (`libc::FIONBIO` and `syscall::FIONBIO`
are the §8.166 example) compare the subject against whichever registered
first.

name layer with `bare_name_res` - the same answer an identifier naming the
constant gets: a module-level constant by its canonical name, a local one
as `Local`.  Codegen reads it: `Local` → the local slot, `Def(q)` →
`resolve_global_in_namespace(leaf, namespace of q)`, the same split
`codegen_identifier` performs; the cloner copies the slot.

#### Found, not built: a specific import naming nothing is silent

The stale `registry` import compiled without a diagnostic, and so does
`import M::{ nonexistent };` in a scratch project (exit 3, the program's
own answer).  `process_import`'s Specific branch tries the module's
offering, then its export closure, then the private-declaration gate, then
"a sub-module `M::name`" - and an absent sub-module has no exports, so the
entry binds nothing and says nothing.  `import M;` of an unknown path is
silent by the same design ("the use site reports it"), which holds only
while there IS a use site.  Rust refuses both (E0432).  E0502_INVALID_IMPORT
is declared with no emitter.  A diagnostic decision, so it is Jake's; not
built.

#### Two rulings, 2026-09-14 (Jake)

* **The extern-visibility default is RATIFIED**: an `extern "C"` function
  is public unless marked `private`.  The change §8.167 recorded as
  worker-authored and unconfirmed stands, and `docs/cryo.md` §18.1's text
  is normative rather than provisional.  §0.1 carries it as D17 so it
  cannot be lost the way D2 was; it comes off the parked list.
* **D16 covers EVERY elided parameter, not only the all-defaulted head.**
  "Rust would refuse them too - it wants every parameter written, and
  that's how I want it."  So `implement trait Foo for hashmap::HashMap`
  (trailing parameters elided) is refused exactly as `implement trait
  Display for String` is: the writer names every parameter, as parameters
  (`implement<K, V, H> trait Foo for HashMap<K, V, H>`) or as a concrete
  instantiation.  One rule, one diagnostic (E0302, naming both spellings,
  leading with the one a writer should prefer - for a container's long
  instantiation that is the parameter form).  The population is **11**:
  §8.181's 4 bare `String` heads plus the 7 partials in `box`, `array`,
  `hashmap`, `hashset`; `impl-head-elided-params.py --count` reads
  `bare=0,partial=0` when built, and §8.181's deferral of the partials is
  withdrawn by this.

### 8.188 Consumer 42: an impl head's key is its stamp, its specialization, or (for an alias keyword) its spelling; `qualified_target_name` and codegen's re-derivation deleted - 2026-09-14

`ImplBlockNode::target_key` answered in four arms: the stamp (`Def` → the
canonical name, `PrimTy` → the spelling), then `qualified_target_name`,
then `target_type`.  `qualified_target_name` was a SECOND carrier of the
same fact: type resolution wrote it from the stamp or the spelling on
every written head, the async lowering wrote it beside the `Def` stamp it
also set, the cloner withheld it - so it was the stamp's name where the
stamp answered and the spelling where it did not, and it had its own
family of readers (mono's two pin targets, three "is this block for the
receiver" comparisons, `register_spec_method_in_di`, the generic
registry's `impl_target_rank`, sema's async declare pass - whose `else`
was one of the two `qualify_symbol_sym` cursor sites left in sema).
`codegen_target_name` wrapped `target_key` with three counters on the
unstamped case.  And `impl_owner_qname` in type resolution was the
destination rule written a second time: the stamp, else `spec_owner`'s
arena name.

`target_key(arena)` is that rule now, on the node, and every reader takes
it: `Def` → the name; `PrimTy` → the spelling; else the specialization the
monomorphizer placed the clone under, by arena id; else, for a head on an
ALIAS KEYWORD only, the spelling; else nothing.  `qualified_target_name`,
`codegen_target_name`, its three counters and `impl_owner_qname` are gone.

#### Two things the shadow found

* **A clone is walked before it is placed.**  `Monomorphizer` clones a
  template's impl blocks, then walks their bodies - registering each
  spec method in the index, pinning the calls inside - BEFORE
  `passes/specialization.cryo` places the clone and records `spec_owner`.
  During that walk the head carried only what `mono/specializer.cryo` had
  spelled into `target_type`: the BARE spec identifier
  (`6String$LN$…$G`), which the old arm 4 answered and the index keyed
  spec methods under, unqualified, until placement re-registered them
  under the arena's name.  The monomorphizer records `spec_owner` on each
  kept clone at the point it decides the concrete type, so the walk reads
  the same owner placement will.  51 shadow lines over the six halves, all
  this shape (`String<GlobalAlloc>` 48, `Array<i32, GlobalAlloc>` 3), old
  the bare identifier and new the arena name; `register_spec_method_in_di`
  now keys the qualified name with the bare identifier as its alias, a
  superset of what it registered before.
* **An impl head on an alias keyword is stamped by nothing.**
  `implement trait Show for int`: `int` is not a primitive spelling (a
  module may own it - `std::fmt::float` does), so the name layer answers
  `Pending`, no clone owns it, and the spelling is its only carrier - the
  hold the `new int[100]` row already records, under the keyword ruling
  (§8.165).  Without the arm, `E0308_primitive_alias_duplicate` failed: the
  head keyed under nothing, and the coherence check saw one impl where
  there are two.  `ResBase::is_alias_keyword` names that population
  beside `is_primitive_spelling` (its complement among the lexer's type
  keywords), and `target_key` holds a spelling arm for exactly it.  One
  head in the tree, that test's.

#### Measured

Seven shadows (the key's old arms against the new; both pin targets; the
three identity comparisons; the DI registration key; the async owner).
Control, every comparison inverted for one build: on the LSP alone
39,002,301 key agreements, 58,583,022 rank agreements, 6,776,526 identity

`ir_generator`'s `visit(SizeofExprNode)` answered in two rungs: re-resolve

#### Found by the mutation: an unknown type in expression position is refused by nothing

The corpus had no `sizeof` whose annotation fails, so the population the
rung could serve was built by hand: `sizeof(Nope)` with no `Nope` anywhere,
and `sizeof(Foo::Nope)` with `Foo` a struct.  Under HEAD and under the pin

to the constant 0.  `1 as Nope` compiles the same way.  The name layer
declines the annotation silently (`stamp_decline`); type resolution's
undefined-type check (`emit_undefined_type`, E0203/E0240/E0155 with a
did-you-mean) is called from its declaration walk and a hand-rolled body
walker that visits var declarations, cast STATEMENTS and lambda parameters
and nothing else; sema, which resolves cast targets and now `sizeof`
operands, has no diagnostic for a failed resolution; the resolver's own
failed exit says "caller should create error".  So every expression-position
annotation naming no type is silent, and `sizeof` was silently 0.

Codegen refuses it now (E0900, at the operand's span), which is the wrong
code for a user's typo and the right state for "nothing upstream decides
this": `tests/tests/projects/sizeof_undeclared_type` pins the REFUSAL as a
`compile_fail` project (the negative suite runs `cryo check`, which stops
before codegen), builds and exits 0 under the pin, and moves its expected
code when a diagnostic for the expression position is decided - which pass
owns it (the resolver's failed exit, or sema alongside its cast target) is a
diagnostics decision and is Jake's.  Roster 49 → 50 projects.

`sema/diagnostics.cryo`'s `collect_bare_type_names`, a mirror of type
resolution's did-you-mean pool with no caller, went too.

### 8.190 D16 built: an impl head names every parameter of its template (E0302); sema's last writer-module lookup deleted; an inherent head's `<...>` is its `target_args` - 2026-09-14

D16 as ruled (§8.181, widened in §8.187): a head on a template writes every
parameter, as parameters of its own or as a concrete instantiation, and an
elided one is refused - whether every parameter defaults (`implement trait
Clone for String` over `String<A = GlobalAlloc>`) or only the trailing ones
(`implement<T> trait Clone for Array<T>` over `Array<T, A = GlobalAlloc>`).

**Where.**  `refuse_elided_template_params`, in type resolution's
`register_decl_in_index`, immediately before the head is attached to its
template: every template is registered by then (TemplateRegistration runs
over all modules first), where stage 3's own attach sees no template for a
head whose target's module comes later in pass order.  A WRITTEN head is one
whose stamp answers `Def`; a clone carries no stamp and is not asked.  The
template's `param_count` against the head's `target_args.length`; a
mismatch is E0302 at the target's span, naming the template, its count and
the head's, then both spellings with the parameter form first - `write the
parameters: implement<T, A> trait Clone for Array<T, A>` and `or a concrete
instantiation: implement<T> trait Clone for Array<T, GlobalAlloc>`, the
defaults spelled from the template's own declaration and `..` where a
parameter has none.  An inherent block is offered its one spelling.
`spell_annotation` renders the head's own text for the suggestion.

**An inherent head's `<...>`.**  `implement enum Option<T>` has no leading
`implement<...>`, so its trailing list DECLARES `T`, and the parser recorded
it as `generic_params` alone - `target_args` empty, "empty for inherent
impls" by the field's comment - while `docs/grammar.md` reads the same list
as the target's `GenericArgs`.  The one head in the tree written both ways,
`implement<T> struct MyVec<T>` (`tests/lang/impl_trait_iter.cryo`), declared
`T` twice.  The parser now records the trailing list as `target_args` on
every head and declares only the names a leading list did not, so
`target_args` means "what the head writes after the target" for every kind
of head, and the check counts one thing.  0 objects moved for it (below).

**Sema's last writer-module lookup.**  `visit(ImplBlockNode)` asked
`greg.get_template(qualify_symbol_sym_home(target_type))` to learn whether a
non-generic head's target is a template, and walked the methods symbolically
over the template's parameters if so.  Shadowed against the stamp
(`greg.template_of(res)`) over six halves: 82k heads, **386 DIFFER**, every
one the two concrete `String<GlobalAlloc>` heads written OUTSIDE `string.cryo`
(`fmt/display.cryo`, `fmt/write.cryo`): the cursor key
`std::fmt::display::String` names no template, so those two took the
concrete path - `this` the TEMPLATE type - while the same heads in
`string.cryo` took the symbolic walk.  Two meanings by writer module, the
§8.180 shape, on the heads D16 makes the writer spell.  The branch reads the
stamp now; `qualify_symbol_sym_home` 34 → 33, none left in `sema.cryo`.

### 8.191 A braced import entry that names nothing the module offers is E0502 at the import - 2026-09-14

Jake's ruling (§8.187's "found, not built"): `import M::{ nonexistent };`
is an error where it is written, not at a use site that may never exist.
The braced form only; the plain `import Unknown;` is silent by the same
design and is a separate question, taken back to him.

`process_import`'s Specific branch asked three rungs - the module's own
offering, its `export` closure, the private-declaration gate - and then
"a sub-module `M::name`", which for an absent sub-module has no exports
and bound nothing.  The sub-module rung now asks the graph whether
`M::name` IS a module and refuses when it is not: E0502 at the import,
"`M` does not offer `name`", the closest spelling as the fix
(`find_best_candidate` over the offered set) and a note listing what `M`
offers - its public exports, its re-export closure's, its sub-modules -
capped at twelve.  An `export` naming a private declaration is not a name
the module fails to offer; it stays E0241's and the rung steps over it.

#### Measured before refusing

The rung instrumented over six halves: **1,168 sub-module entries, 5
unbound.**  Four are dead imports in `compiler/src`, reached through the
LSP half, which is the only half that compiles the compiler: `registry` in
`type_resolution.cryo` and `types/Resolver.cryo` (the module §8.185
deleted, still imported by name in two files), `ResSlot` from
`compiler::resolver` in `call_specializer.cryo` (offered by
`compiler::resolver::res`, which the file also imports), `BaseASTVisitor`
from `compiler::ast` in `name_resolution.cryo` (offered by
`compiler::ast::visitor`, which the same brace list names as a sub-module
- the entry bound nothing and the name resolved anyway).  The fifth is
`reexport_private`'s `export ReexportPrivate::Store::{ Shown, Hidden }`, an
export naming a private: E0241's, and the reason the rung steps over that
case.  All four dead entries removed.

Then `cross-check`, which compiles the OTHER OS's gated half: two more,
`command.cryo`'s ungated `import std::ffi::libc::{ _get_osfhandle,
_open_osfhandle }` naming externs declared under `![target(windows)]` -
offered on this host, not on Linux, and every use inside a
`![target(windows)]` function.  No import in the tree is target-gated, so
the uses take the qualified spelling (`libc::_open_osfhandle`) and the
entries go.  The refusal found nothing else on either surface.

Objects **0 of 1,126, 0 of 2,241**: an entry that bound nothing binds
nothing still.  Suite green (2,122 unit, 183 negative -
`E0502_import_names_nothing_offered`, `import std::fmt::{ printn }` -

### 8.192 Consumer 44: a written type declaration is found under its own key; type resolution's qualified-miss→bare retry, the enum-variant three-rung ladder and its second name store deleted - 2026-09-14

`type_resolution.cryo` asked the arena's name index at 17 sites, and at
seven of them asked twice: a key derived from the ambient cursor
(`qualify_binding_sym`, which is `qualify_symbol_sym` for a file-namespaced
declaration), then on a miss the bare leaf - the four type arms of
`register_decl_in_index` (struct, union, class, enum), the inline-method
signature repair, and the enum-variant populate as the tail of a three-rung
ladder (`decl_index.lookup_type` → arena qualified → arena bare).  The bare
retry's comment said it served "monomorphized types (e.g. `Pair_i32`)"; the
Phase 4 minting in `pass_registry.cryo` derived the same key from the same
cursor, so registration and lookup agreed by walking in the same order
rather than by asking the declaration.

The declaration's own key (`decl_type_key`: a C import's alias-qualified
name, else the registered name when minted qualified, else the WRITING
file's module prefixed to the leaf - §8.185's rule) is now what Phase 4
mints under and what every reader in this file asks by: the E0207
duplicate check, Phase 4 registration, Phase 2's inline-method repair
(handed the key by its caller, not a name to re-derive), Phase 3's trait
populate, Phase 1's alias target, Phase 5's struct/union/enum arms.  Each
asks the DeclarationIndex once - the store `impl_owner`, the resolver's
2c step and the Phase 5 class arm already ask - and the arena's name index
is asked by nothing in type resolution: `arena.lookup_by_name(` 17 → 0 in
the file, 2 in the compiler (the resolver's second store behind the index
in 2c, TemplateRegistration's base type).  The bare retry is deleted at
every site; the class base is read from the stamp in the index.

#### Measured

One shadow over the six halves, every outcome printed, at every site: the
old answer (its rung named), the arena under `decl_type_key`, and the index
under the same key.  **100,893 lines, all `agree`**: 19,278 struct + 6
union + 132 class + 7,493 enum + 8,640 trait + 3 alias registrations, 19,416
inline-method repairs, 9,194 trait populates, 3 alias targets, 111 class
bases, 7,493 enum populates, and 29,124 Phase 4 mints (struct 20,935, enum
8,180, union 6, alias 3) whose cursor key equalled `decl_type_key`.  The
bare rung answered **0**; the enum ladder's index rung answered all 7,493
and its two arena rungs 0; the index and the arena held the same id at
every one of the 71,769 lookups.  Mint counts exceed registration counts
only in halves where `cryo check` stops before Phase 4 (the negatives,
`compile_fail` projects); the LSP and the examples, which build to
completion, match exactly.

**Control** (the LSP built directly and the 14 examples, one build): the
struct arm's qualified rung looked up under a key nothing holds - 2,247
lines read `none` / `new-only`, and the bare rung rescued **0 of 2,247**.
The arena holds no bare key for a declared type: its only bare keys are a
specialization's reserved names (`reserve_spec_names`, `add_name_alias`),
and a specialization never reaches these arms - `SpecInjector::register`
takes every type clone with a valid concrete (`create_concrete_type` never
returns invalid for a type node; `get_qualified_name` of a valid aggregate
is valid), and the injector's two fallbacks into `register_decl_in_index`,

by construction, not by corpus luck; there is no front-end mutation that
produces it short of registering a written type under its leaf, which is
§1's defect and not a shape the model admits.

Predicted 0 objects.  Measured examples **0 of 1,126**, tests **0 of
2,241**; suite green (2,122 unit, 183 negative, 47 projects on this host).
`lsp-check`, `cross-check` green before the object run.  `b1-check`
unmoved.

the same way; `callee_is_intrinsic` compares the pin's name.

### 8.196 Consumers 50-52: the function-declaration key written once (`decl_fn_key`), the spec clone's `source_module` stamp deleted; `family_symbol`'s slot and minting rungs deleted; a global's second key deleted - 2026-09-15

`qualify_symbol_sym_home` had 25 call sites and a §0 row calling it "a
surface, not a lane".  Read one by one, every site derives a DECLARATION's
own registration key - the node's name under the module of the file that
wrote it - and none takes a written reference and guesses where it was
declared.  That is the declaration-key rule, and §8.192 already named it
for types (`decl_type_key`).  For functions it was written four times,
each copy carrying a "must stay in lockstep" comment naming the others:
`register_decl_in_index`, codegen's `fn_qualified_name` and
`type_decl_qualified_name`, and `find_top_level_function_by_key`.  Each
copy had a second arm: a monomorphized FUNCTION spec is placed in whichever
module owns its type argument and its identifier is bare, so the
monomorphizer stamped the template's namespace onto the clone
(`tag_decl_source_module` → `DeclarationNode.source_module`) and the key
was `<that>::<identifier>` when the stamp was set, the home arm otherwise.
The same field carries a FILE PATH on impl blocks (type resolution's
`ImplementationBlock` arm), one field with two meanings.

Two rules now.  `decl_fn_key(name, span_file)` beside `decl_type_key`,
both delegating to `qualify_symbol_sym_home`, which has no other caller;

### 8.199 Consumers 59-61: the annotation-leaf trait checks read the head's stamp; the where-arg binder compares identities; `FilterIter` gets its `min`/`max` back - 2026-09-15

Three readers compared a WRITTEN annotation's leaf with a registry keyed
by identities.  Sema's `projection_bound_fails` and type resolution's
synthesis-time twin `default_method_applies_to_impl` decide whether a
projection-bounded trait default (`min where This::Item: Ord`) applies to
an impl by taking the impl's positional trait argument (`Iterator<Rank>`'s
`Rank`), peeling it to its head LEAF, and asking `traits_implemented_by`
under that leaf.  `TypeResolver::bind_where_arg_params_from` destructures a
where-bound's argument (`Future<Result<T1, E>>`) against the type a
projection yields by comparing the written base's leaf with the type's
template leaf (`proj_bare_name`), and `resolve_concrete_member` gated on
the same leaf.

The head's stamp is the key now: `ann_head_key` (sema) and
`head_type_key` (type resolution) read the `Named` head's slot - a
declared type's canonical name, a primitive's spelling, and nothing for a
parameter, a projection or an unstamped head, which name no registered
type and are kept as undecidable.  The binder compares the base's stamp
with `template_key_of`, moved from `TraitChecker` to the arena so it has
one home; `proj_bare_name`, `symbol_bare_leaf`, `ann_head_leaf`,
`impl_declares_param` and `impl_declares_generic_param` are gone.

Sema's check, over the six halves: **one** concrete Item reached it, the
negative test `E0358IterMinNonOrd`, where both the leaf and the key say

### 8.202 RULED: seven decisions from Jake, 2026-09-15 - the counter is removed, the bare allocator leaf is an error, `import Unknown;` is an error, unknown types in expression position are an error and a defaulted parameter resolves where declared, the trailing-list trait heads fall under D16, the `Res` contract is authoritative and staged, and the trait registry's re-key is measured before it is ruled

Recorded here, in the ledger, so they cannot evaporate the way D2 did:
each is a §0 row (D11 amended; D18-D24 new), and §7.2 mechanism 3 is
amended in place.  None of the seven is built by this entry.

1. **§7.2 mechanism 3 is AMENDED.**  Jake: "Yes, I want this
   instrumentation to be removed completely."  The paragraph that called
   the `CRYO_RESOLVE_COUNTER` instrumentation "not scaffolding to be
   removed after Phase 4" and "the mechanism that keeps the property true,
   permanently" was written when B1 was 753 and is wrong now that B1 is 0
   on every pinned arm of both hosts: what keeps the property is the
   absence of the lanes, the `lane-check` ratchet over the source, and the
   negative tests and mutation projects.  The counter, its audit streams,
   `scripts/b1-gate.py` and `tests/b1-baseline.txt` go - roughly 1,600
   compiler lines and 4,000 script lines.  D11 becomes a deletion.
   Ordering: `lane-check` and the projects must be in place before the
   gate goes (they are); the `b1-check` Makefile target, the CI step and
   the `[host:*]` re-pin recipe go with it.

2. **§8.93 - a bare `malloc`/`free`/`realloc` with no declaration in the
   writing module is an ERROR** (D19).  D6's rule: a bare name means a
   declaration in scope, or nothing.  The diagnostic says to write
   `libc::free` or `heap::free`.  No freestanding carve-out: under `no_std`
   the name IS declared - extern or intrinsic - so the rule is satisfied
   there too and stays uniform.  Today's behaviour is a live hazard: bare
   `free` reaches `alloc::heap::free`, which aborts on a libc pointer.
   This closes the one bare path `callee_family` kept (`intrinsic_owner_of`
   for a `Pending` leaf, §8.173) and the 60 plural-family symbol pins
   §8.195 counted.

3. **`import Unknown;` is an ERROR** (D20).  Jake: "If a module doesn't
   exist, it should be erroring that it doesn't exist."  The same
   treatment the braced form got in §8.191 (E0502 at the import, naming
   what is offered).  Measure the population over six halves first, as
   §8.191 did - a plain import of a module the graph does not hold may be
   a config-gated module on the other OS; `cross-check` is the control.

4. **An unknown type in EXPRESSION or TYPE-ARGUMENT position is an
   ERROR** (`sizeof(Nope)`, `1 as Nope`, `String<Nope>`), **and a
   defaulted type parameter resolves in the module where the type was
   DECLARED** (D21).  `String<A = GlobalAlloc>` written as `String` fills
   in `GlobalAlloc` resolved in `string`'s own scope; the user never
   imports it.  A user who writes `String<GlobalAlloc>` needs `GlobalAlloc`
   in scope, because they wrote it.  This is Rust's general rule - a name
   resolves in the scope where it is written - and is also why a function
   body, a type alias's right-hand side and an impl body resolve where
   they are written.  The second part is what makes the first safe:
   without it, refusing unknown types would force an import for a default
   nobody wrote.  §8.193's two `String<GlobalAlloc>` heads that imported
   `GlobalAlloc` are the written-argument case and stay as they are.

5. **The six trailing-list trait heads are COVERED by D16** (D22).
   `implement trait Atomic<T>` with `T` declared nowhere becomes
   `implement<T> trait Atomic<T>` - same error code, same diagnostic,
   likely the same commit as the remaining D16 work (the concrete
   spelling not yet honoured by impl selection, §8.190).

6. **The `Res` contract is AUTHORITATIVE, landed gradually** (D23).  An
   unstamped node is an error; D1 is right and the tree is wrong.  Do NOT
   flip all the silent `_ =>` arms at once: convert each to a hard door
   (`require_scope_res` is the shape) as its population is measured to
   zero, and track the count in §0 - 22 silent arms at the ruling, against
   12 hard doors (`grep -rho 'require_scope_res(' compiler/src
   --include=*.cryo | wc -l` → 13, the definition included).  The rule is
   ruled; the enforcement is staged.

7. **The trait registry's re-key is NOT ruled; it is MEASURED first**
   (D24).  Jake accepted the recommendation to decline a blind ruling:
   shadow the TRAIT half - the bare table keyed by `extract_trait_leaf`,
   the precise index by leaf, `resolve_trait_impl_for_type`, `type_has_
   drop_impl`, `origin_trait`'s leaf fallback, the trait's methods under
   its bare name, the operator table's trait leaves, `trait_bound_names`
   / `trait_ref_matching` - against the head's `qualified_trait_name`

### 8.205 Consumer 64: a method call binds the stamped trait's method, else an inherent one, else the sole trait's - never the impl block written first; the L120 check reads the file that holds the arm - 2026-09-16

#### What audit 9 found, and what it was

`find_spec_impl_method`'s `first_m` arm: with no `preferred_trait`, the
first impl block placed under the receiver's specialization that carried
a generic method of the call's name answered.  Measured in the previous
session at 75,503 calls, `first` reached 80 times, every one with exactly
ONE candidate - safe by the corpus's population, not by the code.  The
§0 row that claimed the mechanism `DELETED` had its check reading
`sema/call_resolver.cryo` alone; the arm was in `mono/call_specializer.cryo`.

The same arm was not one place.  Eight probes - a plain or generic type,
a plain or generic method `go`, the trait block written first or second,
every receiver with an inherent `go` returning 1 and a `Beta::go`
returning 2 - under HEAD's compiler (`6e32022e`) printed:

| shape | trait first | inherent first |
|---|---|---|
| plain type, plain method | **2** | 1 |
| generic type, plain method | **2** | 1 |
| generic type, generic method | **2** | 1 |
| plain type, generic method | 1 | 1 |

(The pin, `bin/cryo.exe`, printed 2 for the generic-type / plain-method
shape in BOTH orders.)  Three selectors, each walking its own store in
registration order and binding the first hit:

* sema's `select_method`, over the receiver's own method list.  Type
  resolution's `StructFieldTypeSync` and mono's `MonoTypePopulator` fold
  every impl block's methods into `StructType.methods` beside the inline
  ones, in declaration order, trait impls included, and the binder's
  first set was that list.  This is the plain-method rows: a generic
  type's spec is bound by the post-mono re-check over the list the
  populator filled from the placed clones.
* sema's `find_generic_method_for_call` (the stash / return-type finder),
  over the template's own methods, then `tmpl.impl_blocks` as one list,
  then the trait registry, then the inherent owner, then the
  inherent-impl registry.  The trait registry ahead of the inherent
  owner is why the plain-type / generic-method shape differed in BOTH
  orders here (mono's ladder happened to ask its inherent store first
  and masked it).
* mono's `find_spec_impl_method` (the audited arm) and
  `find_generic_trait_method_under`, first hit each.

`docs/cryo.md` §13 said nothing about which of an inherent and a trait
method a call names.  Rust's rule - inherent candidates before trait
candidates, two traits providing the name an error - is what the tree
already half-implemented (E0154 for two traits), so it is written down
as §13.4 and applied at every selector, one precedence:

1. a call STAMPED with a trait (through a bound, or a same-name recursion
   inside that trait's impl - `MonoDispatchAnnotator`'s two rules) names
   that trait's method; the trait stores are asked for it first.  At the
   generic definition the receiver is `T`, which has no inherent methods,
   and the concrete type it is instantiated with does not change what
   the source named;
2. else an INHERENT method, from whichever store holds it;
3. else the sole trait impl providing the name;
4. else nothing.  Several unstamped trait candidates are the E0154 sema
   raises; mono makes no binding for a program that is refused.

A first draft asked the inherent stores before the stamped trait and
ran the inherent body for `via_bound<T>(x: &T) where T: Beta` - the
parked reproducer's `trait=2` half read `trait=1`.  The stamp is a
RESTRICTION for a bound-directed call, not a tie-break.

#### The instrument

Each selector computed both answers and printed one `SHADOW` line per
selection, its two kinds (`inherent`, `trait:<identity>`, `none`) and
`agree` / `DIFFER` by node identity; the stash finder's line carried
whether the call was stamped.  Control by the probes above: every
trait-first shape printed `DIFFER` at the selector that decided it, and
the plain-type / generic-method shape printed `DIFFER` at the stash
finder in both orders and `agree` at mono's ladder.

Over the six halves (`scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh m2`, 647,698 lines, 0
failing halves):

| selector | selections | differ |
|---|---|---|
| `select_method` (own set) | 518,079 | **0** |
| mono's ladder | 80,903 | **0** |
| `check_method_call_arg_types` (E0154) | 12,867 | **0** |
| `find_generic_method_for_call` | 35,849 | **14,478** |

The 14,478: **10,775** stamped `Debug` calls (`fmt<W>` recursions inside
`Debug` impls, rule 2) the old walk answered with `Display`'s `fmt<W>` -
the first trait impl in `tmpl.impl_blocks`, an identical signature, which
is why nothing ever showed; **3,467** stamped calls answered under the
same trait from the registry's clone placed under the specialization
instead of the template's node; **236** unstamped, one trait, the
clone's node again (`Iterator` 187, `AsyncWrite` 22, a test's `GmsrSink`
17, `Write` 8, `TdgWrapper` 2).  The finder answers a SIGNATURE - the
call's bindings and return type - and the clone's is the template's
substituted; the object comparison below is the check that this moved
nothing.  Zero receivers in the corpus hold both an inherent and a trait
method of one name, so the corpus could not have caught any of the three
selectors: the population was built as a project.

#### Deleted, in the same commit

`find_spec_impl_method` (replaced by `find_spec_impl_inherent_method`
and `find_spec_impl_trait_method`, the second taking the trait the call
is stamped with or answering the sole candidate), the `first_m` arms of
it and of `find_generic_trait_method_under`, the primitive branch of
mono's ladder that asked the trait registry before the inherent-impl
registry (the two branches were one ladder once ordered, the user-kind
branch's `is_synth_default || is_generic()` filter being always true for
a method the finder requires to be generic), the mixed set in
`select_method` (`pick_own_method` walks one set, inherent or trait, at
every tier), the trait registry's place ahead of the inherent stores in
`find_generic_method_for_call`, and the ambiguity check's one-list walk
(an inherent method beside two traits' is bound, not refused).  The
`find_inherent_method` comment claiming a leaf "is not a key" now states
the invariant the index enforces (one key per type since §8.193; the
previous session's leaf-rung shadow measured 0 hits in 75,394, absent by
construction).

Pinned: `inherent_method_over_trait` (`run`, the eight shapes, an
inherent `go` between `Beta::go` and `Gamma::go`, and two bound-directed
calls; the pin prints `nn_tf=2 gn_tf=2 gn_if=2 gg_tf=2` for the eight and
refuses the ninth as E0154; this tree prints nine `=1` and two `=2`).
`E0154_ambiguous_trait_method` keeps the two-traits-no-inherent refusal.

L120's row check is paired: 0 over `sema/call_resolver.cryo` +
`mono/call_specializer.cryo`, 18 treewide with the survivors named.

#### The §0 checker could not read an alternation

The new row's check, `grep -rho 'a\|b' … | wc -l` → 5, reported `tree
says 0` from `ns-status-check` while the same line printed 5 in a shell.
`ns_ledger.rows` turns every `\|` in a cell back into `|`, because a
table cell escapes its column separator that way and the checker cannot
tell that escape from a basic-regex alternation - so the pattern ran as a
LITERAL pipe and matched nothing.  Six rows already in §0 were written
that way, every one expecting **0**: D11's two, the home-module row's,
`family_symbol`'s, `qualify_symbol_sym_home`'s, the import-alias row's.

### 8.206 D5 TAKEN: modules and types share one namespace, the collision is E0205 where the pair is completed, and the module-vs-type adjudication is deleted with the cursor lane it fed - 2026-09-16

#### The ruling, read against the resolver's own scoping

§8.130 records the ruling as Rust's model - `mod x` beside `struct x` is
E0428 - and §8.170 paraphrased it as "refused at `type struct Buffer`" for
`namespace Gpu::Buffer;` declaring that struct.  In Rust those are two
different programs: `mod buffer { struct buffer }` is legal, because a
module's name is not in scope inside itself.  In this resolver it is.
`CompilationContext::modules_written_as` counts a module as spelled by any
whole-segment suffix of its namespace when the module is the writer's own
(`cand_ns.id == use_ns.id`), imported, the whole name, or the prelude's -
so inside `Gpu::Buffer`'s file the one segment `Buffer` already names the
module, and a `type Buffer` declared there is a second owner of one name
in one scope.  That is the E0428 shape under Cryo's scoping, and it is
what §8.130's instrument counted ("namespace leaf spelled like a type
declared in the same file"): three survivors, all in `tests/`.  The
importer's side is the same pair completed from the other end: `import
Gpu::Vertex;` makes `Vertex` spell the module in the importing scope, and
a `type Vertex` declared or imported there is the second owner.  Both are
"a module and a type carrying the same name", both are refused as the
ordinary redeclaration error, E0205, at the entry that completed the pair.
Written down as `docs/cryo.md` §14.6 and §4 rule 5 here.

#### The mechanism

`NameResolver::refuse_module_type_collisions`, once per module scope at
the end of its walk - after the imports are bound, since either side can
complete the pair.  For each entry of the scope that names a type
(`symbol_names_type`: declared as one, or an import whose target is one,
resolved through the owning module's export set as every qualified path
is), `modules_written_as(name, ns)` says whether the name spells a
reachable module; failing that, `<ns>::<name>` is asked of the module
graph directly - `namespace A;` declaring `type N` beside a module
`A::N` shares its canonical name whether or not `A` imports it.  Probed
before the corpus with one project per shape under the built compiler:
the own-leaf declaration (`src/widget.cryo:2:1`), a declaration under an
imported module's leaf (`main.cryo:3:1`), an import of a type under an
imported module's leaf (`main.cryo:4:1`), the sibling (`main.cryo:3:1`),
every one E0205 naming the module; a legal control - module `Buffer`
declaring `Handle`, `Buffer::make` its function, `Buffer::USAGE` its
constant - exits 7.

Name resolution is fatal per module, so a program with two collisions in
two files reports the first module's; the two pinned shapes are two
projects for that reason.

#### The population, measured with the refusal live and the tests untouched

`corpus2.sh m4` over the six halves: **1** failing half,
`module_type_name_collision`'s test half (`src/gpu/buffer.cryo:9:1`), and
the unit suite refusing to compile at `tests/lang/static_method_value.cryo:30`
(`make test exit=2`).  A third is invisible to that run and was found by
building it directly: `namespace_gate_methods`, a `compile_fail` project
expecting E0240, now failed at `src/handler.cryo:9:1` with E0205 instead -
the half reports a wanted non-zero exit and nothing else.  Those three
are exactly §8.130's three; `compiler/src`, `stdlib`, `tools/CryoLSP` and
`examples/` hold none, which the compiler's own build, `lsp-check` and
`cross-check` say as well as the structural argument does.

* `namespace_gate_methods`: the module renamed `Handling`; its trait
  `Handler` and its E0240 are the test, and the collision was incidental.
* `static_method_value.cryo`: the type renamed `Emitter`.  Its three tests
  - a static taken as a value from inside the type's body and from
  outside, a module function taken the same way - are the coverage worth
  keeping; the collision was the file's premise and is refused now.
* `module_type_name_collision`: `collect` → `compile_fail`, E0205 at
  `src/gpu/buffer.cryo:9:1`, its `tests/` half deleted (it exercised the
  adjudication).  `module_type_import_collision` is new, E0205 at
  `src/main.cryo:8:1` for the declaration-under-imported-leaf shape;
  `E0205_type_named_as_its_module` is the single-file negative.

#### Deleted, in the same commit

* `check_module_type_collision` (114 lines): the E0154 for a member BOTH
  the module and its same-leaf type declared.  It adjudicated a pair the
  name layer now refuses at its declaration.
* `stamp_module_scope`'s module-owns-member probe: a segment bound in
  scope as a type answered type-relative UNLESS a same-spelled module
  owned the next segment.  A segment bound as a type is type-relative.
  Its import-target lookup and the new check's are one helper,
  `symbol_names_type`.
* `scope_owner_key`'s cursor lane (`resolve_scoped_at` between
  `spec_owner` and the stamp; §8.170 measured 1,974,585 answers serving
  the one refused shape) and, with their last reader gone,
  `CompilationContext::resolve_scoped` and `resolve_scoped_at`.
* `resolve_scope_call`'s cross-kind trying.  The ladder asked the static
  method, variant, module function and C-import stores in turn for every
  segment; §8.195 measured the stamp deciding every answer but two, the
  refused shape's `Buffer::make`.  A `Def` segment now asks the module
  store alone; any other segment - a type, a primitive, a type parameter,
  a C-import alias, which the name layer stamps type-relative because the
  alias is a namespace symbol rather than a graph module (§9 Q2) - asks
  the three type-owned stores.  One more `require_scope_res` door (D23,
  13 → 14 mentions).

`bare_alts` and `DeclarationIndex::resolve_qualified_scoped` are NOT
deleted: with the cursor lane gone the compiler has no reader of either,
but `tools/CryoLSP`'s completion handler resolves a typed leaf through
`resolve_qualified_scoped` and the LSP is Jake's, deferred until the
compiler's migration is complete.  The 13 `register_name_mapping` writers
stay to feed that one reader; the row says so.

Outside the ledger: `compiler/src` 3 files, +122 / -232; the spec, four
test files, the roster (`--update`: the `collect` project's five tests are
deliberately gone, two projects and a negative added, no other host's
entry touched).

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK (`lane-check` unmoved); `test-census` OK (2,122 unit, 184
compile-fail, **54** of 57 projects on this host); `lsp-check` OK (264
modules, 0 errors); `cross-check` OK (243 compiler modules).  Objects
(`.objcmp/m5-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,334** shared

### 8.207 D19 TAKEN: a bare allocator leaf is E0202 naming its declarers; the intrinsic's bare key, its four durability guards and codegen's leaf-spelled allocation are deleted - 2026-09-16

#### The one bare path, and what held it

`callee_family` answered a `Pending` callee - a bare name the name layer
bound to nothing - through `intrinsic_owner_of(leaf)`, the record of
which `intrinsic function` declared that leaf.  That record was written
by `register_intrinsic_function_type`, which also registered the
intrinsic under its bare leaf in every function table (return, signature,
mangled slot, overload entry, `bare_alts`) and dropped an `extern "C"`
twin's entry from the leaf's overload index so the leaf "dispatcher" saw
the intrinsic alone; four guards in `register_function`,
`register_function_type_owned`, the overload restamp and
`register_mangled_name` then refused any later same-leaf write, so that
`alloc::heap::free` could not rebind a bare `free` program-wide.  All of
it existed so that `free(p)` written in a module declaring no `free`
would bind SOMETHING, and which something depended on the link: the
intrinsic where the guards held, `heap::free` - which reads a segment
header and aborts on a libc pointer - where they did not
(`bare_intrinsic_priority.cryo`'s premise).  D19 says the spelling names
nothing, as every other undeclared bare name does.

#### Built

* `callee_family`'s unanswered arm returns no family.  The call then
  falls to `resolve_direct_call`'s E0202, which now carries a note when
  the leaf is a free function of some module:
  `collect_module_declarers_of_leaf` walks the overload keys for
  `<module>::<leaf>` where `<module>` is in the graph (a type's static
  shares the key shape and is excluded), and the note names each and its
  suffix spelling - for `free`: `std::core::intrinsics`, `std::ffi::libc`,
  `std::alloc::heap`; write `intrinsics::free`, `libc::free` or
  `heap::free`, or import it.  Data-driven, so `malloc` names two and
  `realloc` three, and a leaf nothing declares keeps the did-you-mean.
* `note_intrinsic(leaf, owner)` replaces `register_intrinsic_function_type`:
  the leaf → declaration record alone, read by codegen's
  `callee_is_intrinsic` to tell a pin to the intrinsic from a pin to a
  function sharing its leaf.  Type resolution's intrinsic arm registers
  the declaration under its qualified name only; the bare
  `register_function`, `register_name_mapping`, `register_mangled_name`
  and `register_overload_mangled_owned` writes and the four durability
  guards are deleted (`decl_index.cryo` -87 lines net).
* Codegen's synthesized allocation (`expr_ops.cryo`, three `malloc`
  sites and the `delete` rung behind the `std::alloc::allocator::free`
  shim) names `std::core::intrinsics::malloc` / `::free` - the family
  the intrinsic registers as - instead of the leaf the deleted bare
  registration supplied.  `core/intrinsics.cryo`'s header no longer
  claims the three declarations exist to hold the bare leaf: they are
  the allocator a program without `std::alloc::allocator` names.

#### Population

`grep -rn -E '(^|[^:A-Za-z_.])(free|malloc|realloc)\(' --include=*.cryo
stdlib compiler/src tools examples tests runtime`, minus definitions,
comments and `.method(` forms: **13** bare calls.  Legal under D19, the
writing module declaring the leaf: `stdlib/ffi/libc.cryo` 3 (extern
block), `stdlib/alloc/heap.cryo` 1 (`public function free`), and the two
E0453 negatives' 4 - each declares `malloc`/`free` in its own `extern
"C"` block, which the previous handoff had counted as bare-with-no-
declaration; they are not.  Refused: `tests/lang/bare_intrinsic_priority.cryo`'s
5, one file, which asserted the bare bind ("must keep binding the
intrinsic").  It is `E0202_bare_allocator_leaf.cryo` now, three
annotated calls, the note checked by hand.  `compiler/src` holds none
and `stdlib` none but the four declared ones, which is what the
compiler's own build says.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` OK (2,120 unit, 185 compile-fail, 54 of
57 projects on this host); `lsp-check` OK (264 modules, 0 errors);
`cross-check` OK (243 compiler modules, the freestanding runtime tiers
compiling `new` through the renamed rung); objects
(`.objcmp/m6-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,333**.
`ns-status-check` 201 rows.

**Tally: 66 shadowed, 66 old paths deleted, 66 at zero - §8.93's
allocator residue is closed; 96 artifacts gone** (+

### 8.208 D20 TAKEN: an import path the graph holds no module under is E0502 at the import, measured at zero first - 2026-09-16

#### What the shape is

A path naming no FILE was already refused at discovery (E0500, `cannot
find module`), plain or braced.  What survived was the path the loader
resolves to a file whose namespace is spelled otherwise: `import
core::option;` reaches `stdlib/core/option.cryo`, the graph registers
`std::core::option`, and `process_import`'s `find_module_index` misses -
so the import bound nothing, and as a plain `import M;` (D7: it binds no
names by design) said nothing.  The braced form of the same path reached
`refuse_unoffered_import` per entry with a message about a module that
does not exist.  A module gated off this OS (`![config(linux)]` on
Windows) is NOT this shape: the graph holds it, empty, and the import
names it.

#### Measured first

The refusal was landed as a `SHADOW\tIMPORT-UNKNOWN` line first and
run over the six halves (`corpus2.sh m7`: **0** lines, 0 failing halves)
and, since `cross-check.py` keeps only error lines, over the four
Linux-target builds by hand (`runtime`, `stdlib`, `compiler`,
`tools/CryoLSP` with `--target=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`: **0** lines, every
build exit 0).  Control: a scratch project writing `import core::option;`
printed the line and compiled; one importing a `![config(linux)]` module
on this host printed nothing and compiled.  So the population is zero
and the instrument can report non-zero.

#### Built

`refuse_unknown_module_import`, ahead of every style in `process_import`:
E0502 `` `core::option` is not a module's name ``, labelled at the import,
with a help naming every module the path is a whole-segment suffix of
(`Resolver::ns_written_as` over the graph) - the mistake the shape comes
from is writing where an import wants the whole name the abbreviation a
qualifier is allowed.  The braced form no longer reaches its entries
against a missing offering.  Pinned by `E0502_import_names_no_module`.

### 8.209 D21 TAKEN: an unknown type in a body annotation is E0203 where it is written, the reporter walks the whole annotation by stamp, and `1 as Nope` no longer compiles - 2026-09-16

#### Four answers to one question

Under `8ad52d6a`, a type declared nowhere was reported four ways by
position: a declaration's annotation `const x: Nope` was E0203 from type
resolution's gate; `sizeof(Nope)` was E0900 at codegen (the pinned
refusal of an operand nothing decided); `Array<Nope>` in a local's
annotation was E0636 at codegen against `Array::new`, the instantiation
having failed silently; and **`1 as Nope` compiled and ran** - the cast
target unresolved, the cast emitted as nothing, exit 1.  `docs/cryo.md`
§12.2 already said "a name that exists nowhere is an error in every
position, expression and type-argument positions included: `sizeof(Nope)`,
`1 as Nope` and `Array<Nope>` are refused".  The spec was normative and
the tree was the defect.

Two gaps, one mechanism each:

* Sema resolves three annotations in bodies itself - a local's, the
  `sizeof`/`alignof` operand's (`resolve_layout_operand`), the cast
  target's (`resolve_cast`) - and on failure left the slot unset with no
  diagnostic.  Type resolution's own body walk covers locals in
  non-generic bodies only.
* The reporter's `extract_unresolved_named` PEELED to the head: for
  `Tagged<bool>` it reached `Tagged`, which resolves, so
  `annotation_failure_is_certain` was written to fire on a bare `Named`
  alone and to leave every wrapped form unreported ("those wrapped forms
  are left to their existing handling" - which was nothing).

#### Measured first

The three sema sites printed a `SHADOW` line per failed resolution with
the first name in the annotation the name layer had NOT stamped, or
`<stamped>` when every name was placed, and the walk's mode.  Over the
six halves (`corpus2.sh m9`, 6,655 lines): unstamped names **2**, both
`sizeof_undeclared_type`'s `Nope` (once per sema walk, pre- and
post-mono); stamped-but-unresolvable **6,653**, every one a LOCAL's
annotation (3,937 in the symbolic walk, 2,401 in the post-mono re-check,
308 concrete pre-mono, 7 symbolic post-mono), none a `sizeof` or a cast.
Control: the three probe programs printed `sizeof Nope`, `cast Nope`,
`local Nope` respectively.

The 6,653 are a FINDING, not this entry's: a local whose annotation the
type layer cannot resolve while every name in it is placed - a
projection, a form reduced later, an annotation the substituter did not
rewrite - and sema proceeds on the initializer's type.  Unrowed; nothing
here changes what they do.

#### Built

* `extract_unresolved_named` is a walk over the WHOLE annotation by
  stamp - pointers, references, arrays, tuples, function shapes, generic
  base and arguments - returning the first `Named` leaf with no answer
  and no pre-resolved type.  A placed name is not the failure;
  `Tagged<bool>` names `bool`.  `annotation_failure_is_certain` asks it
  (`top_level_named` is deleted); the deferred forms it must not fire on
  (`typeof`, `implement Trait`, a projection) hold no unplaced name.
* Every branch of `emit_undefined_type` that reports a leaf marks it
  `Res::Err` afterwards, so the leaf is placed for the next asker: type
  resolution's body walk and sema's pre- and post-mono walks ask the same
  annotation, and one unknown name is one diagnostic.
* Sema's three sites call `refuse_unresolved_body_annotation` on
  failure: the runner's certainty predicate, then its reporter -
  E0203 at the leaf's span with the did-you-mean, or E0240 with the
  import to add, exactly as a declaration gets.

The default-parameter half of D21 was already the name layer's:
`declare_generics` stamps a parameter's default annotation in the
declaring file (§8.193), and §8.204 found the use-site re-homing that
stood beside it read by nothing.

Pinned: `sizeof_undeclared_type` moves from E0900 to E0203 at
`src/main.cryo:9:27` (codegen's E0900 stays as the door behind sema's);
`E0203_cast_to_undeclared_type` and `E0203_type_argument_undeclared` are
new.  Outside the ledger: `compiler/src` 2 files, +78 / -42.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` OK (2,120 unit, 188 compile-fail, 54 of
57 projects on this host); `lsp-check` OK (264 modules, 0 errors);
`cross-check` OK (243 compiler modules); objects
(`.objcmp/m10-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,332**
shared; the one object that differs is HEAD-only, `sizeof_undeclared_type`'s
`Main.o`, which HEAD's codegen wrote before its own E0900 and this tree
never reaches.  `ns-status-check` every row.

**Tally: 66 shadowed, 66 old paths deleted, 66 at zero; 97 artifacts

when that report is owed.  They become doors when that report moves to
the name layer (stamp `Err`, report there), which is the next step and
not this one.  `head_type_key`'s 442 include green programs and are
uncharacterised.

Each `_ =>` arm is replaced by `slot.require(site)`: `Err` on a missing
answer, which `def_id()` turns into an invalid id and every consumer

reports if the build otherwise succeeds - the same door
`require_scope_res` is.  The sixth deletes a leaf path: the trait-impl
head's `origin_trait` was `ot_trait_leaf` (`extract_trait_leaf` over the
written annotation) overwritten by the stamp when it answered, the §0
row "falling to the head's LEAF", unmeasured until now; with 0 unstamped
heads the leaf was a fallback for nothing, and `origin_trait` and
`qualified_trait_name` are the stamp alone.  `extract_trait_leaf` keeps
its other caller, the trait registry's bare key (D24's).

### 8.212 D24 MEASURED: the trait registry's leaf key loses an impl in one shape, one program holds it, and the re-key is Jake's call - 2026-09-16

#### What was measured, and where

D24 asks for the trait half shadowed whole before it is ruled on.
§8.194 measured one reader (193,199 answers, 9 disagreeing).  This
entry instruments the two places a leaf key can differ from an identity
key at all:

* **Registration.**  `register_trait_impl` and `register_trait_impl_typed`
  overwrite an existing `(leaf, target)` entry ("latest impl wins").  An
  overwrite by a block whose `TypeAnnotation::trait_identity` differs
  from the entry's is an impl the table LOSES; an overwrite by the same
  identity is the same node registered under a second key (stage 3
  under the written target, type resolution under the canonical one, a
  placed clone under its specialization).
* **Readers holding an identity.**  `type_implements_trait` and
  `type_satisfies_opaque_bound` receive the bound's identity
  (`TraitRef::identity()`, a stamped annotation) and hand
  `dispatch_leaf(...)` to `resolve_trait_impl_for_type`; the block the
  leaf finds carries its own identity, compared to the one meant.  The
  Drop/Copy queries and the operator desugars (`Add`, `Index`, `Deref`)
  pass a LEAF by design - an operator names "the `Add` implemented for
  this type", whatever module declares it - and are a different
  question (coherence, not identity); they were logged with the
  well-known identity where one exists and every one agreed.

Over the six halves (`corpus2.sh m15`, 1,047,373 lines, 0 failing
halves, `.objcmp/d24-measurement-lines.txt`):

| site | answers | differ |
|---|---:|---:|
| overwrite, bare table, same identity | 4,034 | - |
| overwrite, typed table, same identity | 206 | - |
| overwrite, typed table, **different identity** | **1** | `trait_leaf_dispatch`: `(Render, Shape)`, `Alpha::Render`'s block replaced by `Omega::Render`'s |
| bound check (`type_implements_trait`) | 84,514 | **3**, all `trait_leaf_dispatch`: a `T: TraitLeafDispatch::Alpha::Render` bound answered by `Omega::Render`'s block |
| opaque-bound check | 6 | 0 |
| Drop typed / bare, `wellknown("Drop")` meant | 795,165 | 0 |
| other readers, identity meant | 5,378 | 0 |
| other readers, leaf meant (operator traits) | 158,066 | not a disagreement |

#### What the one shape is

Two traits sharing a leaf, both implemented for one type - `Alpha::Render`
and `Omega::Render` for `Shape` - collapse to one table entry under
`(leaf, target)`, so `traits_implemented_by(Shape)` offers `Render`
once and `lookup_trait_impl(Render, Shape)` hands back whichever impl
registered last.  A bound `T: Alpha::Render` checked against `Shape` is
then answered by `Omega`'s block: satisfied here because neither impl
carries a where-clause, and a type implementing ONLY `Omega::Render`
would satisfy an `Alpha::Render` bound the same way.  The project passes
today because sema's concrete-receiver binder reads the type's folded
method list (both impls' methods, each with its own `origin_trait`) and
never the registry.  §8.194's 9 were this project's 6 and 3 `LeafDispatchA::Pulse`
heads that the typed table, keyed by the target's canonical name since
§8.199, no longer collapses.

Nothing in `compiler/src`, `stdlib`, `tools/CryoLSP`, `examples/` or the
unit suite holds the shape.

#### What is not decided here

Re-keying the trait half by identity would make both impls visible to
every registry reader and answer a bound by the trait it names.  It is
one program in the tree and it is Jake's call, by the ruling; the
previous re-key was backed out for being decided rather than measured,
and this is the measurement.  The instrument is not in the tree: it was
reverted after the run, and this entry rides with the next code commit
rather than alone.

### 8.213 D2 and D9 TAKEN: `Namespace::Function` folds into `Value`, and a type declaration takes a `where` clause - 2026-09-16

#### D2: two namespaces, as Rust has

`Namespace` is `Type` and `Value`.  `Value` accepts every value-bearing
symbol kind - variable, parameter, constant, enum variant, function,
method, intrinsic - and `Function` is deleted.  A function is a value
reached by the same walk as a constant; a third namespace would let one
spelling bind a function and a constant at once, which no rule of the
language allows.

Nothing ever asked in `Function`, and nothing asked in `Value`: both
callers of `resolve_path` pass `Namespace::Type`
(`git grep -n 'Namespace::' -- compiler/src | grep -v namespace_kind`
→ 3 lines: `resolver.cryo:608`, `name_resolution.cryo:627`, and the
word inside W0011's help text), so the fold changes no answer and no
object.  The row's check moves 3 → 2.

#### D9: `where` on `type struct` / `union` / `class` / `enum`

The parser reads `parse_trait_bounds` between the head and the body
`{`; the four declaration nodes carry `where_bounds: TraitBound[]` with
`add_where_bound`; the cloner copies them; the name layer stamps them
with `stamp_trait_bounds(&node.where_bounds)` right after
`declare_generics`, so a bound's trait resolves in the declaring scope
like a method's does.  `TraitChecker::unsatisfied_trait_ref` walks a
bound list under a substitution and hands back the first bound whose
concrete argument does not implement its trait, or null; a bound whose
argument is still abstract is deferred to the concrete instantiation.

Two doors read it, because an instantiation reaches the compiler by two
routes:

* **A written annotation** - `TypeResolver::resolve_generic`, E0306
  `at(span)` of the annotation, `also_at(bound.span)`.  This is the one
  with a span, and it is why `cryo check` refuses `Holder<Plain>`.
* **An instantiation only inference writes** - a struct literal, a
  static call, a clone's concretized argument - reaches the
  monomorphizer's `refuse_unsatisfied_type_bounds` with the template and
  its arguments in hand; E0306 at the bound, naming the instantiation.
  It does not bump `error_count` itself: doing so produced a spurious
  E0900 on top of the real report.

`docs/cryo.md` §11.3 carries the rule and an example; `docs/grammar.md`
adds `("where" WhereClause)?` to the four aggregate productions.

Tests: `tests/tests/lang/type_where_bound.cryo` (2, a struct and an
enum instantiated under a satisfied bound); negatives
`E0306_type_where_bound` and `E0306_enum_where_bound` (the annotation
door, under `cryo check`); project `type_where_bound_inferred`
(`compile_fail`, the mono door: `Holder::wrap(Plain{..})` with no
annotation naming `Holder<Plain>` → E0306 at `src/main.cryo:7:32`; its
inversion, `implement trait Tagged for struct Plain` added, compiles and
returns 7).  Name resolution is fatal per module, so the two doors need
two programs, and `cryo check` stops before mono, so the mono door needs
a PROJECT rather than a negative file.

Outside the ledger: 10 files, +242 / -17, plus 6 new test files (+155).

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
191 passed; projects: 55 passed)`, roster 2,122 / 191 / 58
(`.objcmp/m18-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules
(`.objcmp/m16-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/m16-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/m17-objcmp.out`, with `type_where_bound.cryo` moved
out because HEAD's parser refuses `where` on a struct and cannot build
that half): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,332** - a pure fold and
a new syntax nothing in the corpus uses yet.  The batch sat in
`git stash@{0}` (and `.objcmp/d2-d9-batch.patch`) across a session
boundary; before this commit the popped tree was diffed against the
patch copy and matched it exactly, and the gates were re-run from a
clean `compiler/build` (`.objcmp/u1-*.log`).  `ns-status-check` every
row: D2 and D9 rows rewritten, `make test` 2,122 / 58 / 191, the 0.3
roster lines, D15's `::{` 583 → 584 (the new project's `src/main.cryo`).

**Tally: 67 shadowed, 67 old paths deleted, 67 at zero; 99 artifacts
gone** (+ `Namespace::Function`).

### 8.214 D23, seventh door: `head_type_key`'s 442 were a keyword primitive with no slot, not an unstamped head - and a primitive `Item` was misread as symbolic - 2026-09-16

#### The characterisation

§8.211 left `head_type_key` (type resolution's synthesis-time filter
for a projection-bounded trait default, `default_method_applies_to_impl`)
entered 442 times on green programs, the arm uncharacterised.  Its
instrument printed only "entered"; this one printed the slot's state,
the annotation's variant, its spelling, the impl head and the default's
name (`corpus2.sh h1`, 7,862 lines, 0 failing halves,
`.objcmp/h1-lines.txt`), over every empty answer the function gave:

| slot | annotation | entries | what |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `Pending` | `Primitive` | **448** | `Chars`'s `Iterator<u32>` 436 (stdlib, 2 per compilation), five test and example iterators with `Item = i32` 12 - `min`/`max` every time |
| `Pending` | `Named` | **0** | no unstamped nominal head anywhere |
| `Answered(GenericParam)` | `Named` / `Pointer` | 6,978 | `Iterator<T>`, `Iterator<T*>` - a parameter, no key by design |
| `Answered(TypeRelative)` | `Named` | 436 | `FilterIter`'s `Iterator<I::Item>`, a projection written as a path - no key by design |

The outer arm was never an unstamped head.  A primitive written by its
keyword parses as `TypeAnnotation::Primitive`, which carries no `res`
slot at all - the keyword-ness D18 rules away - and `head_named_slot`
turned that into `Pending`.  The 442 → 448 is the corpus growing by
§8.213's tests.

#### The defect underneath

An empty key meant "symbolic, keep the default".  So an impl with
`Item = u32` kept every projection-bounded default whatever `u32`
implements, and a default bounded on a trait `u32` lacks was synthesized
and type-checked against it.  Control, under HEAD: a trait `Source` with
`total(&this) where This::Item: Zap { this.get().zap() }`, implemented
`Source<u32> for Nums` with no `Zap` for `u32`, and `main` calling only
`get()` - **refused**, E0358 `no method named zap found on type u32`
inside the trait's own default body; the same program with a declared
`Item` (`Num`) lacking `Zap` compiles and prints 3.  Sema's call-side
twin `ann_head_key` had the same arm, so `n.total()` was not refused at
the call either (`cryo check` exit 0) and would have failed in codegen.

#### The change

`head_type_key` matches the annotation the way its twin does: a `Named`
head goes through `n.res.require("type_resolution:annotation head")`
(the door), a `Primitive` answers its own name - the key it is
registered under, and the answer a `PrimTy` stamp gives, so D18 changes
nothing here - `Generic`/`Reference`/`Pointer` peel, and everything else
(array, tuple, function, projection) is empty by design.  `ann_head_key`
gains the same `Primitive` arm.  `head_named_slot` keeps its one other
caller, the trait-impl head's door.

Tests: `tests/tests/lang/trait_default_primitive_item.cryo` (2: the
control above compiles and `get()` answers 3; a declared `Item` with the
bound reaches the default); negative `E0358_primitive_item_default`
(`n.total()` refused at the call).  Mutation, for the twin: with
`ann_head_key`'s `Primitive` arm reverted and the type-resolution fix in
place, `cryo check` on the negative exits **0** - the arm is what
refuses the call; restored, E0358 at `31:7`.  The standing control for
the other direction is `min_max_non_monotonic` (`FixedI32`,
`Iterator<i32>`, `.min()` answers 1): `i32` implements `Ord`, so the
default is still synthesized for a primitive that satisfies the bound.

Outside the ledger: 2 compiler files, +26 / -12; 2 new test files,
roster +2 unit +1 negative.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
192 passed; projects: 55 passed)`, roster 2,124 / 192 / 58
(`.objcmp/u2-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules
(`.objcmp/u2-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/u2-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/u2-objcmp.out`, the new unit test moved out because
HEAD's compiler refuses it - which is the defect): **examples 0 of
