### 8.215 The extern block's bare C name was the last first-claimant-wins registration, and a call pinned by symbol alone bound whichever declaration registered first: a live miscompile, fixed by pinning the declaration - 2026-09-16

#### The defect (audit round 10)

`type_resolution.cryo`'s extern arm registered a declaration under its
bare C name only when `lookup_func_type(fn_node.name)` was invalid -
first claimant wins - and warned W0011 on a later block whose signature
differed, with text saying "the unqualified name resolves to the first
declaration".  Sema, on the stamp, bound the declaration the call
named; but the identifier call's pin was `CalleePin::Symbol("llabs")`,
and codegen answered a symbol through `symbol_signature` - the FIRST
overload entry carrying it, with the comment "they share the signature,
so the first answers", the very premise W0011 exists to say is
violated.  So sema checked the arguments against one declaration and
codegen emitted the call at another's.

Reproducer, three files: `first.cryo` declares `llabs(i32) -> i32`,
`second.cryo` declares `llabs(i64) -> i64`, `main.cryo` imports
`Second::{ llabs }` and calls `llabs(-4294967301)`.  At HEAD
(`631fedba`): builds, `declare i32 @llabs(i32)`, the argument
truncated, **exit 3 where 7 is correct**.  Under the pin `db5af63c` the
same program is REFUSED (E0214: the old model bound the first claimant
in sema too, so the i64 argument mismatched) - a program the pin
refused had become a silent miscompile.  The second shape, both
declarations called from one module through their qualified paths with
the narrow one first, the pin **compiles and exits 4** for 7: that one
was a miscompile under the old model as well.

Corpus population: `grep -c W0011` over a stdlib build → 0; the one
test, `W0011_duplicate_extern_symbol.cryo`, never calls the symbol.
Empty by luck.

#### The fix: the pin carries the declaration

* **Sema.**  `try_pin_overload_mangled_callee` pins a family of ONE
  signature by the family (`CalleePin::Family(family)`, the
  declaration's key) and a set by the selected signature's own symbol,
  which a Cryo mangling makes unique - the qualified `Module::f()` call
  and the value form already pinned the family ("a free function's
  registry key is its qualified name"); the identifier call now agrees.
  The pin reader on re-resolution reads a family's one signature through
  `lookup_func_type(fam)` so `![implicit]` converters are inserted for
  it as for a symbol: found by the unit suite, not by reasoning -
  `ImplicitArgConversion::string_literal_converts_to_owned_string`
  crashed (0xC0000374) on the first cut, because the `Family` arm
  returned the registered return early and skipped the converter.
* **Codegen.**  A free or extern call is emitted at the PINNED
  signature's function type (`pinned_signature` → `build_function_ltype`),
  not at `LLVMGlobalGetValueType` of the symbol - which is declared once
  per LLVM module, at whichever declaration reached it first.  With
  opaque pointers `call i64 @llabs(i64 %x)` against
  `declare i32 @llabs(i32)` is well-formed IR, and it is what Rust
  emits for the same program (`clashing_extern_declarations` is a
  warn-by-default lint there, and each call uses its own item's
  signature).  A method's symbol is its own mangling, so a method call
  keeps the declared type.
* **Type resolution.**  The extern declaration is registered under its
  own key (`decl_fn_key`) and nothing else; the bare-name claim, the
  `ext_bare_taken` guard, `extern_bare_owner` and its two accessors are
  deleted - with the comment that a bare `malloc` "has to bind to the
  compiler-backed intrinsic", a rule D19 made an error.  W0011 is keyed
  by the SYMBOL (`extern_symbol_first`: the first extern block's key and
  function type under each C name; an intrinsic reaching the same C
  name is not an extern block and stays silent, as before - the first
  cut compared every entry under the symbol and warned on
  `libc::malloc`/`realloc`/`free` against `intrinsics::` in every build)
  and its text says what is true now: a call binds the declaration it
  names, and at most one of the two matches the C definition.
* **Codegen's `strcmp`.**  The one reader of the bare extern key over
  the six halves was string equality's `resolve_function("strcmp")`
  (`expr_ops.cryo`), which already declared its own fallback when the
  index had none.  It declares its runtime dependency once per LLVM
  module and asks the index nothing.

#### Measurement before the deletion

Every name-keyed index reader probed against the extern-claimed keys
(`extern_bare_owner_of(name) != 0`), `corpus2.sh x1`,
`.objcmp/x1-lines.txt`, six halves:

| reader | hits | what |
|---|---:|---|
| `lookup_func_type_overloads` + `lookup_overload_mangled` | 1,007 + 1,007 | ONE key per half (`strcmp`: 993 pairs in the LSP, 14 in the unit suite, whose `string_as_cstr.cryo` also declares it) - `resolve_function("strcmp")` |
| `lookup_func_type` | 12 | the registration's own `ext_bare_taken` / `prev_type` reads, on a second declaration of one name |
| `lookup_func_return`, `lookup_mangled_name`, `get_function_module` | 0 | |

#### Mutation proof, both directions

`tests/tests/projects/extern_duplicate_symbol_binds_declaration` (run,
exit 7) and `extern_duplicate_symbol_both_called` (run, exit 7) are the
population.  Old path: HEAD's compiler exits 3 on the first; the pin
exits 4 on the second (objcmp's HEAD half also builds both, and reports
them failing there).  New path: 7 and 7, IR `call i64 @llabs(i64 %load)`
beside `declare i32 @llabs(i32)`.  The narrow declaration's own call in
the second project answers -5, as C does for a caller that passes 32
bits where the callee reads 64: the program wrote the wrong signature,
and the test asserts only the declaration the wide call named.

Outside the ledger: 5 compiler files, 2 new projects (6 files), the
lane golden.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
192 passed; projects: 57 passed)`, roster 2,124 / 192 / 60
(`.objcmp/u3-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules, 0 W0011
(`.objcmp/u3-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/u3-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/u3-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 4 of
2,446 - the two new projects' `Main.o`, once per side**, HEAD's half
reporting them `[FAIL] (exit 3, expected 7)` and `(exit 4, expected 7)`.
`lane-check` LOOKUP 44 → 43, re-pinned: `type_resolution.cryo` 23 → 21
(the guard's two `lookup_func_type(fn_node.name)` reads),
`call_resolver.cryo` 1 → 2 (the pin reader's `lookup_func_type(fam)`,
keyed by the pinned family and not by a spelling, beside the

**Tally: 68 shadowed, 68 old paths deleted, 68 at zero; 103 artifacts

### 8.216 The callee pin carries a declaration: the index's function registry gets one entry per definition (a symbol is part of its identity), registration returns the entry and stamps the node, and every consumer that mangled a symbol to name a declaration reads the entry instead - 2026-09-16

#### What the pin was

`CalleePin::Symbol(s)` carried the linker symbol as a string, and every
reader of it asked the index by that string: codegen's `resolve_symbol`
through `mangled_to_overload_pos`, `pinned_signature` through
`symbol_signature`, sema's re-resolution reader through
`lookup_func_type_by_mangled` - each taking the FIRST entry under the
symbol.  Every writer of it computed the string: sema's
`pin_method_callee_from_qname` and codegen's `declare_method`,
`codegen_method_prologue` and the vtable slot each ran
`MangledName::for_method_or_trait_impl` + `with_method_spec_args` "in
lockstep" with `register_methods_with_module`; `lambda_synth` and
`free_function_symbol` ran `for_free_function`; mono's
`mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` ran the method mangling once more.
Seven copies of one computation, each a place the symbol could come
apart from the registration's.  The symbol readers were 16 sites over
four index accessors (`lookup_mangled_name` 9, `lookup_overload_mangled`
5, `symbol_signature` 1, `lookup_func_type_by_mangled` 1); the writers
15 `set_resolved_callee(CalleePin::Symbol(...))` and the vtable slot's
`resolve_pinned(CalleePin::Symbol(computed))`.

#### Measurement before the change (`corpus2.sh p1`, `.objcmp/p1-lines.txt`, 2,660,779 lines, 0 failing halves)

| what | population |
|---|---:|
| symbol reads (`lookup_func_type_by_mangled`, `symbol_signature`) naming exactly ONE entry | 1,239,625 + 54,348 |
| symbol reads naming several entries | **0** |
| symbol reads naming no entry (a mint the index never registered) | 500 + 24 |
| codegen `resolve_symbol`: held by the module / declared extern from its one entry / held with no entry | 459,296 / 29,493 / 12 |
| sema pin writes whose `(key, signature)` had exactly one entry | 130,894 of 130,894 |
| `family_overload_symbol`'s `lookup_mangled_name` fallback rung entered | **0** of 42,577 |
| `family_answer` plural | 0 |
| an entry RESTAMPED with a second symbol (`register_overload_mangled` on an entry already carrying a different one) | **11,493**, over 229 keys |
| codegen method definitions whose mint had an entry | 147,434 of 147,434 |
| vtable slots with a node and an entry | 665 of 665 |

The restamps are the finding.  The registry's entry was `(key,
signature, owner)`, and three shapes put two DEFINITIONS in one entry:
an inherent method and a trait impl's of the same name and signature on
one type (`GnIf::go` inherent then `Beta::go`), two traits' same-named
methods on one type (`Display::fmt` and `Debug::fmt` on `P`), and two
specializations of one generic method whose signature does not mention
its parameter (`GroupTag::group<T>`, 12).  Each later registration
overwrote the entry's symbol, and `mangled_to_overload_pos` mapped both
symbols to the one position - so a symbol still answered its own
signature (the two share it), but `lookup_overload_mangled(key, ft)`
answered whichever registered LAST.  Every static pin
(`pin_scope_callee_combined`, `try_pin_static_method_overload`,
`pin_scope_value_static_method`) asked exactly that: over the corpus
none reached a collapsed key (0 of 88,317 `(key, ft)` reads had two
entries, because the entry WAS collapsed - the instrument could not
see it; the restamp count is the one that could).  So the symbol was
the finest identity the index held, finer than its own entry; a pin
carrying `(DefId, signature)` would have been COARSER than the string
it replaced, and collapsed `Display::fmt` onto `Debug::fmt`.

The 524 no-entry reads and the 12 held-with-no-entry: closure
specializations (`lambda_synth` minted the symbol and registered
nothing; codegen's `free_function_symbol` minted it again and
registered it itself, `DE-FREE-SLOT` 24) and four sema method pins on
iterator-adapter combinators (`take`/`filter` on a user struct) whose
template node the index never registers; mono re-pins those at
materialization.  `MONO-REG no-entry` 456 were the EMPTY symbol
(`mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` with no receiver key: no pin, and no
registration).

#### The change

* **Registry identity is `(key, signature, owner, symbol)`.**
  `register_signature` finds that entry or appends one; a registration
  carrying a symbol the entry does not already hold is a different
  definition and gets its own.  An entry also records the TRAIT its
  declaration implements (`overload_func_trait`, empty for an inherent
  method or a free function; `entry_trait` reads it) - the one property
  that tells an inherent method from a trait's under one key and one
  signature without reading the `$tr$` off the symbol.  `register_function_type`,
  `register_function_type_owned`, `register_overload_mangled`,

### 8.217 The scope-call argument check keys a module segment by its stamp; the module-suffix scan behind the spelling is deleted - at a tied suffix it checked nothing, and a mismatched argument compiled into a binary that died of heap corruption - 2026-09-16

#### What the scan was

`check_scope_call_arg_types` (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`) type-checks the
arguments of a `Scope::member(args)` call against the one signature
registered under the callee's key, and is the ONLY place a module-qualified
call's arguments are checked (measured below).  It keyed the call by
`<spelling>::<member>`, where the spelling came from `scope_owner_key`,
which answers `scope.scope_name` for a `Res::Def` segment - a module
qualifier is not a type-owner claim, so that function leaves it as written.
`fmt::println` is not the key `std::fmt::println` is registered under, so
every abbreviated module call missed the exact key and fell into a second
lane: walk every module in the graph, match the written scope as a
whole-segment suffix of each namespace, and take the one candidate whose
`<namespace>::<member>` has exactly one overload.  Its comment still
explained itself by mirroring `resolve_module_qualified_function`'s
suffix match - a lane M5 deleted (§0 L122); the stamp has named the module
since.

#### Shadow (`corpus2.sh u2`, `.objcmp/u2-lines.txt`, 162,460 lines, 0 failing halves, `make test` OVERALL PASS 58 projects)

At the scan, the stamp's answer was computed beside it -
`resolve_module_qualified_symbol(scope_name, member_name, scope)`, the one
path that resolves a module call's RETURN - and the two compared:

| shape | lines |
|---|---:|
| module segment, scan named one function, the stamp the same one | 126,642 |
| type segment: no exact overloads, the scan walked every module, found nothing | 35,804 |
| **module segment, the scan named nothing, the stamp answers** | **14** |

The 14 (`.objcmp/u1-keep/u2-disagree.txt`), every one a `Def` segment:
12 where two modules share the written suffix - `resolution_module_suffix`
`Code::val` (2) and `Text::tag` (2), `resolution_trait_default` `Text::tag`
under `Alpha` (4) and `Beta` (4) - so the scan found two candidates, tied,
and CHECKED NOTHING; 2 a re-export, `reexport_basic` writing
`Aggregate::make_widget` for what the stamp names
`ReexportBasic::Inner::make_widget`, which no namespace's suffix reaches.
The scan was never right where the stamp was wrong.

#### The check it skipped is the only one

Every `check_args_against_params` caller was tagged with the call's
position and a probe built under HEAD `1451d792` and the tree
(`.objcmp/u1-keep/u2mut/`: `Alpha::Text::tag() -> i32` and
`Beta::Text::tag(s: String) -> i32`, both in the graph through a registry
module, `main` importing `Beta::Text`):

| `Text::tag(...)` | HEAD `1451d792` | tree |
|---|---|---|
| `("hello")` | builds; the binary exits `0xC0000374` STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION | builds; exits **5** |
| `(5)` against `String` | **builds**, no diagnostic; `0xC0000374` | **E0214** `expected String, found i32` |
| `("a", "b")` | E0900 `LLVM module verification failed: Incorrect number of arguments` | **E0215** `takes 1 argument(s) but 2 were supplied` |

Under HEAD no `check_args_against_params` caller reached the call at all
(0 tagged lines at its position, `head-*.log`): at a tied suffix the
module call's arguments were checked by NOTHING, the raw literal or the
`i32` was passed where a by-value `String` was expected, and the callee's
drop freed garbage.  Under the tree the module arm reaches it (`tree-*.log`,
`scope-arm` 2-3 lines at `7:24`) and nothing else does - so the arm is
not a second copy of a check the family reader also performs (the
identifier call's converter path is for identifier calls, and the earlier
probe that suggested otherwise was measuring a graph with ONE `::Text`
module: `alpha_text.cryo` was imported by nothing and never compiled).

#### The change

`check_scope_call_arg_types` dispatches on the segment's stamp as
`resolve_scope_call` does: a `Def` segment's key is
`resolve_module_qualified_symbol`'s answer (the stamp's qualified name +
member, gated on a registered return), a type segment's the owner key as
before.  The suffix scan, its M5 comment, and the dead
`import compiler::module_graph::{ ModuleInfo }` are deleted; a module
segment with no such key, or several overloads, returns instead of
falling into the inherent static-method gather (a module owns no static
methods; the name layer refuses a module and a type sharing one name).
`require_scope_res` 14 → 15, `names_module` 3 → 7.

Two run projects hold the pair: `module_suffix_tie_checks_arguments`
(the conversion, exit 5; HEAD's binary crashes) and
`module_suffix_tie_rejects_mismatch` (`compile_fail`, E0214 with `found i32` in its label; HEAD compiles it).

### 8.218 The index's per-module ownership tables are deleted: written on every registration, read by nothing - 2026-09-16

#### What they were

`DeclarationIndex` kept, beside every function and type registration, the
module that registered it: `module_funcs: Pair<name, module>[]`,
`module_types: Pair<name, module>[]`, and two O(1) indices over the first
- `module_func_first` (name → first module, "first-wins ownership") and
`module_func_pairs` (a packed `(name, module)` membership set) - written
by `note_module_func` on every push.  Four accessors read them:
`get_functions_in_module`, `is_function_in_module`,
`get_function_module`, `get_type_module`; the header comment said codegen
used them to enumerate a module's exports for the define-vs-extern
decision.  Three registrars took a `module` argument to feed them -
`register_methods_with_module` (12 callers), `register_function_type_with_module`
(5), `register_type_with_module` (9) - and `owner_mod` was plumbed from
`SpecInjector::register` through `register_injected_decl` into
`register_decl_in_index` so that an injected specialization's ownership
would name its template's module rather than the demanding one.

#### Measurement (the current tree at `ccb310aa`, `grep -rl <name> compiler/src tools --include=*.cryo`)

| symbol | files outside `decl_index.cryo` |
|---|---|
| `module_func_first`, `module_func_pairs`, `note_module_func` | 0 |
| `module_types` | 1 - a comment, `type_resolution.cryo:453` |
| `get_type_module` | 1 - `arena.cryo`, the arena's own method of that name |
| `get_function_module`, `is_function_in_module`, `get_functions_in_module` | 0 |
| `module_funcs` | 1 - `sema/diagnostics.cryo` `collect_bare_callable_names`, reading `.first` |

Inside the file the four accessors were the only readers of the four
tables (`module_func_pairs` also gated the `module_funcs` push against a
second overload of one method).  `module_funcs.second` was read by
`get_functions_in_module` alone.  So every table was write-only through
its accessors, and the one outside reader wanted the function NAMES.
ABSENT, not starved: nothing asked; a clean deletion, no shadow to run.

Control on the instrument: the grep that reports 0 for the accessors
finds the arena's `get_type_module` and the comment mentioning
`module_types`, so it is not a grep that finds nothing.

#### The change

* The four tables, `note_module_func` and the four accessors are
  deleted.  `module_funcs` becomes `callable_names: u32[]` - every
  function key ever registered, once, in registration order, deduplicated
  at the push by `callable_names_seen` - and `collect_bare_callable_names`
  reads it; its own string dedup goes, since interned symbols make id
  identity string identity, and its order is the old first-occurrence
  order.
* The `module` parameter comes off the registrars, which are renamed
  for what they now do: `register_methods` (the combined `Type::method`
  keys), `register_function_signature` (a free function's key, symbol
  and entry); `register_type_with_module` was `register_type` plus a
  `module_types` push and its 9 callers call `register_type`.
* `owner_mod` is stripped from `SpecInjector::register`,
  `register_injected_decl` and `register_decl_in_index`, with the
  `module_sym` locals that carried it: `type_resolution.cryo`'s
  `register_decl_in_index` head, the extern arm's `ext_mod_sym`, the
  intrinsic arm's `i_mod_sym`, `specialization.cryo`'s `register`, and
  `AsyncDecl.module_sym` in `async_lower.cryo`, a field whose only reader
  was the argument to the deleted parameter (found by the LSP gate's
  warning count moving 490 → 491, W0001 unused variable; 490 again).
  `owner_module_sym` in `specialization.cryo` stays: it also sets
  `entry.owner_source`.

#### Gates

lsp-check OK (264 modules, 0 errors, 490 warnings); cross-check OK
(`.objcmp/u3-cross2.log`); `make test-census` OK, 2,124 / 192 / 63;
lane-check unchanged (`LOOKUP_OTHER` 28: none of the deleted names was a
`lookup_*`); ns-status-check OK.  **Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved**
(`hash-tree.sh E` against `D`, HEAD `ccb310aa`'s half, `.objcmp/u3-hashE.out`;
`t-E.txt.log` OVERALL PASS 2,124 / 192 / 60, 0 allocation failures).

#### Findings, not chased

* `collect_bare_callable_names` keeps only keys with no `::`, and

* The globals' analogue - `register_global_with_module`,

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `sema/diagnostics.cryo`,
`sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`,
`mono/call_specializer.cryo`, `passes/specialization.cryo`,
`passes/type_resolution.cryo`.

### 8.219 A stamped declaration answers its type through the index by its id: `type_of_def` / `func_type_of_def`, and six readers that unwrapped a `DefId` to key a lookup hand the id over instead - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

A `Res::Def(q)` is the name layer's answer, and `q` is a `DefId`.  Six
readers held one and turned it back into a string to ask the index the
type it names - `q.qualified_name()` then `lookup_type` (the index
directly, 2) or `lookup_type_exact` / `lookup_func_type_exact` (through
`TypeUtils`, 4).  Each is a `DEFID_UNWRAP` whose only consumer is a
name-keyed lookup, which is the case the lane baseline's own header calls
out: "a re-keyed lookup here has re-derived what it was handed, and
should take the DefId instead".  The index already answered a `Res`
without a caller-side unwrap (`type_of_res`, `func_type_of_res`, each
unwrapping once inside the index); a `DefId` in hand had no such door.

#### The change

* `DeclarationIndex::type_of_def(DefId)` and `func_type_of_def(DefId)`:
  the definition's canonical name is the map's key, so the id is
  unwrapped there and nowhere a reader stands.  `type_of_res` and
  `func_type_of_res` ride on them (the index's `DEFID_UNWRAP` stays 2).
* Six sites hand the id over: `TypeResolutionPasses::impl_owner`'s `Def`
  arm; the class base (`require_base_res` → `type_of_res`, its local
  `base_q` gone); `pattern_resolver`'s enum pattern type; the struct
  literal's base in `sema`; `TypeUtils::def_type`, the DefId-keyed door
  that records an unregistered definition, which unwrapped internally;
  and the function VALUE's type in `sema` (`func_type_of_res`).  At the
  last, the canonical name is still derived once, for the `Family` pin
  and the visibility gate - both keyed by name by design - so that
  unwrap stays and the entry says why.
* Not taken, each unwrap being for TEXT or for a name-keyed consumer of
  another kind: the base-constructor symbol (`decl_visit_emitter`), the
  `Family` pins, `callee_family`, `resolve_module_qualified_symbol`'s key
  build, the const table's qualified-name reads, the generic registry's
  `get_template(def.qualified_name())`, the annotation-head keys.  Those
  are the next slices: each wants its consumer re-keyed, not just the
  lookup.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 43 → 41 (`type_resolution` 21 → 19, the two
`lookup_type` calls), `DEFID_UNWRAP` 38 → 33 (`type_resolution` 5 → 3,
`pattern_resolver` 1 → 0, `sema` 2 → 1, `type_utils` 4 → 3), re-pinned;
predicted −2 and −6 before the edit, the sixth unwrap kept for the pin as
above.  lsp-check OK (490 warnings); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u4-cross.log`);
`make test-census` OK, 2,124 / 192 / 63; ns-status-check OK (a new row).
**Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh F` against `E`, HEAD
`41208b28`'s half, `.objcmp/u4-hashF.out`; `t-F.txt.log` OVERALL PASS
2,124 / 192 / 60, 0 allocation failures) - the same map under the same
key, asked with the id instead of the id's name.

### 8.220 A `Type::method` path two traits provide at one signature is reported in sema as E0154, naming both traits; codegen's E0636 / E0900 refusal of the unpinned path was the wrong layer with the wrong text - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

§8.216's `choose_entry` selects the entry a `Type::method` path names
from the fits its signature (value form) or its arguments (call form)
leave: one fit is it, an inherent method beside trait methods is it, and
several trait methods with no inherent one is a tie that pins nothing.
Unpinned, the path reached codegen, which has no spelling fallback for a
scope call since the `mangled_names` map went, and refused it there: the
call form as E0636 `codegen: cannot resolve 'P::go'` / `no such
associated function` (the method exists twice, not never), the value
form - `pin_scope_value_static_method` falls to `CalleePin::Family` - as
E0900 "names several functions and the call was not pinned to one of
them" (true, and unexplained).  Rust reports both forms of this tie as
one error, E0034 "multiple applicable items in scope", with a note per
candidate ("candidate #1 is defined in an impl of the trait `Beta` for
the type `P`").  Cryo's method-call form of the same tie, `p.go()`, is
already E0154 (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`, "call to `go` is ambiguous: it
is provided by multiple traits implemented for this type"; §13.4 of
`docs/cryo.md` names the code).  The static-path form is the same
ambiguity spelled as a path, so it is reported under the same code, as
Rust does; a distinct code for the path spelling is Jake's to mint if he
wants one, and is a one-line change.

#### The change

`choose_entry` takes the path node and, at a tie of two or more trait
entries with no inherent one, reports it (`report_static_path_tie`):
E0154 "`P::go` is ambiguous: `go` is provided by more than one trait
implemented for `P`", the label naming both traits, a note per candidate
in Rust's words, and nothing during a symbolic generic-body walk (the
concrete instantiation reports, as the method form's guard does).  Both
callers hand the node over: `try_pin_static_method_overload` (the call
form, from `pin_scope_callee_combined`) and `entry_of_signature` (the
value form).  No pinning decision moved: every non-tie answer is the one
`choose_entry` gave before.

Probes (scratch, each under the tree's compiler before and after):
| probe | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tie`: `Beta::go(&this)` + `Gamma::go(&this)` for `P`, `P::go(&p)` | E0636 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `stat_call`: `static make()` in both traits, `P::make()` | E0636 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `stat_value`: `const f: () -> i32 = P::make;` | E0900 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `disamb`: `Beta::go(&p) * 10 + Gamma::go(&p)` | E0636 at codegen | E0636 at codegen |

The last row is a **finding**: the explicit trait-path call
`Trait::method(receiver, args)`, which the method-form E0154's own note
proposes as the disambiguation ("disambiguate by calling the trait method
explicitly, e.g. `Trait::method(receiver, args)`") and §13.4 describes
("resolved by calling the trait method explicitly"), compiles under no
compiler in reach - not the tree, not HEAD `1451d792`'s
(`.objcmp/cryo-head.exe`), not the pin (`bin/cryo.exe`, 2026-09-11):
sema types it silently and codegen refuses `Beta::go` as unknown.  The
corpus holds no use of the form (`grep -rn -E
'[A-Z][A-Za-z]+::[a-z_]+\(&[a-z_]+[,)]' tests/tests examples` finds only
`Type::method(&recv)` static calls on inherent methods).  So the
diagnostic for the tie names no way out today: the language has no
working trait-qualified call.  That form is a language question
(`Trait::method(recv)` as the note promises, Rust's `<P as Beta>::go(&p)`,
or both), Jake's, and this entry does not add a help line that promises
either.  The method form's note that promises the broken form is left as
written; its wording is Jake's too.

Negative `E0154_static_path_two_traits` (2 annotations: the call form
`CfP::go(&p)` and the value form `CfP::make`).  **Mutation pair**: the
same file through `cryo check` under the pin and under `1451d792`'s
compiler exits 0 - sema alone accepts the ambiguous program, the refusal
lived only in codegen - and under the tree exits with the two E0154s.
`static_path_prefers_inherent_method` (the inherent-wins rule, exit 33)
passes unchanged.

#### Gates

`make test` (in `hash-tree.sh G`'s log, `.objcmp/t-G.txt.log`) OVERALL
PASS: unit ok, compile-fail 192 → **193**, projects 60; roster merged
(`roster-check --merge`, 1 added).  lsp-check OK (490 warnings);

### 8.221 `register_decl_in_index` asked the index for a written type under its own key and registered the answer back under the same key, six arms; deleted - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

Every one of the six type-declaration arms of `register_decl_in_index`
(struct, union, class, enum, trait, alias) opened with the pair

    const qualified_sym = ctx.decl_type_key(node.name, ..., node.span.file);
    const ty = ctx.decl_index.lookup_type(qualified_sym);
    if (ty.is_valid()) { ctx.decl_index.register_type(qualified_sym, ty); }

- a name-keyed lookup whose only consumer was a registration of what it
found under the key it was found by.  `register_type(k, ty)` writes
`type_map[k] = ty` and `type_reverse[ty] = k`, so the pair is a no-op
unless the reverse map named some OTHER key for that type at the time -
a repair of `lookup_type_name`'s answer that nothing said it was, and
that nothing would have noticed disappearing.  The six were 6 of the 19
`LOOKUP` sites in `type_resolution.cryo`, audit 10's bucket B (a key
derived from a declaration in hand); the type-declaration stage
(`pass_registry.cryo`) had already registered every one of these types
under exactly this key.

#### The measurement

A shadow before each re-registration (`shadow_rdi`): `agree` when the
map held the key and `lookup_type_name(ty)` was already the key,
`DISAGREE` with both names otherwise, and `INVALID` when the key was
not registered at all; tagged `src`/`clone` by `is_source_decl`.  Six
halves (`corpus2.sh u2`, `.objcmp/u2-lines.txt`): **37,976 lines, all
`agree`** - struct 20,520, trait 9,295, enum 8,020, class 132, union 6,
alias 3; **0 `clone`** (the spec injector registers a clone's type itself
under the arena name, and its fallback into these arms was never taken);
0 `DISAGREE`, 0 `INVALID`; 0 failing halves; `make test` in the run
OVERALL PASS 193 / 60.  Control by inversion: the comparison flipped
(`prev.id != key.id`), the same scratch project printed 166 `DISAGREE`
and 0 `agree` where it had printed 166 `agree` - the instrument reports a
disagreement when there is one.  ABSENT, not starved: the repair had
nothing to repair.

#### The change

The six pairs are deleted; the arms keep what the type-declaration stage
does not own - `register_name_mapping`, `set_decl_visibility`,
`register_methods` - each still keyed by `decl_type_key`, which is the
slice that wants the node to carry its registration's id (next).  The
doc comment says the arm asks the index nothing about the type.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 41 → **35** (`type_resolution` 19 → 13), re-pinned;
predicted −6.  **Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh H`
against `G`, HEAD `a577364f`'s half, `.objcmp/hash-H.out`; `t-H.txt.log`
OVERALL PASS unit ok / 193 / 60); predicted 0.  lsp-check OK (490
warnings).  §0: the `LOOKUP` cell 41 → 35 on §8.219's row; a new
machinery row.

Outside the ledger: `passes/type_resolution.cryo`, the lane golden.

### 8.222 `is_candidate_public`'s permissive default answered "public" for every extern-block function - a `private` extern was callable by qualified path from any module; every registration records its verdict now, and a candidate with none is a recorded defect - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

`DeclarationIndex::is_candidate_public(q)` read `decl_visibility` and
answered `true` for a key with no entry.  Three doors ask it:
`enforce_callee_visibility` (sema, the E0353 gate for a qualified call
and for a function taken as a value), and the two E0203 explainers in
type resolution, `unreachable_declarer` and `suggest_reaching_import`.
The default sat outside `lane-check` by construction - no `lookup_*`
name - while D12 names `lane-check` as the enforcement for exactly this
class.  Audit 9 flagged it; nothing had measured whether the default was
ever the answer.

#### The measurement

A shadow at the three doors (`visibility_recorded`, a temporary index
query; door, `recorded`|`DEFAULT`, the key on `DEFAULT` only).  Six halves
(`corpus2.sh u3`, `.objcmp/u3-lines.txt`): **102,408 asks, 29,828
answered by the default.**

| door | recorded | DEFAULT |
|---|---|---|
| `callee` (`enforce_callee_visibility`) | 72,573 | **29,825** |
| `unreach` (`unreachable_declarer`) | 5 | 2 |
| `suggest` (`suggest_reaching_import`) | 2 | 1 |

The 29,825 are 237 distinct keys, every one a function declared in an
`extern` block: `std::ffi::libc` (75 keys; `strlen` 4,511, `memcpy`
4,320, `printf` 2,412 ...), `std::sys::syscall` (83), `std::ffi::openssl`
(23), `compiler::bindgen::clang` (54), and the `ExtDup` project's two
`llabs`.  The extern-block arm of type resolution registers the signature
and the link symbol and never wrote a verdict; the free-function arm
writes `func.is_public` beside its registration.  The 3 type asks are one
key, `NamespaceGate::Depot::Crate`, a generic struct asked by the E0203
explainers while resolving `Orphan` - a module that does not import
`Depot` and so is resolved before `Depot`'s Phase 4 (where
`register_decl_in_index` wrote a type's verdict) has run; the verdict
existed later, not yet.

STARVED of a writer, not absent - and load-bearing in the wrong
direction.  The parser gives an extern-block function its written
visibility (`private function llabs(v: i64) -> i64;` is `is_public =
false`; the parser's own comment says a private one binds nothing at an
`import ... { llabs }`), and the qualified path around that: probe
`.objcmp/u1-keep/privext` - `PrivExt::Ffi` declares the private extern,
`PrivExt::Main` calls `Ffi::llabs(-9)` - **compiled and ran under HEAD
(`767e956f`), exit 9**; the shadow shows the one `DEFAULT` line for it.

#### The change

* **Every type registration records its verdict with its key.**
  `register_type(key, ty)` → `register_type(key, ty, is_public)`,
  writing `decl_visibility` in the same call, so no type is ever in the
  map without one and no reader can be earlier than the write.  28
  callers: the type-declaration stage's six (`node.is_public`; a trait
  and an alias carry no modifier and are public), its 19 primitives, the
  spec injector (`SpecInjector::node_is_public`, the template's verdict
  the cloner copied onto the node), the async wrapper struct and the
  closure struct (synthesized, public).  `register_decl_in_index`'s five
  type-arm writes go: they were a second, later writer of the same
  verdict, and the gap above was the window between the two.
* **The extern-block arm records each imported function's verdict** under
  its key and, for a C import, under the `alias::name` key too -
  `fn_node.is_public`, the same rule the free-function arm applies.
* **The `None` arm is a door**: `record_unregistered_def(...)` - the
  build ends in E0900 "canonical name(s) named no registered declaration"
  when nothing else failed it - and it answers `true` meanwhile, the
  top-level default, so a public item whose registration lost its verdict
  is reported as the registration defect it is rather than as "private".
  The comment on `decl_visibility` no longer says "permissive".

Project `extern_private_function_is_private` (compile_fail, E0353 with
the message asserted): HEAD's compiler builds and runs it (exit 9), the
tree refuses it at the call.  **Mutation pair for the door**: with the
extern arm's write commented out, the same probe fails under the tree
with `E0900: 194 canonical name(s) named no registered declaration; first
consumed at decl_index: visibility of a candidate no registration recorded
a verdict for` (the stdlib's own extern calls), where HEAD's compiler over
the same program reported nothing and ran it.  Restored, the probe is
E0353.

Not taken: `register_type_forward_only` (the four alias keywords) records
no verdict - D18's arm, and no door asked one of its keys over the
corpus; a `Type::method` static call's visibility is
`enforce_static_method_visibility`'s, a different map.

#### Gates

PASS: unit ok, compile-fail 193, projects 60 → **61**; roster merged.
lsp-check OK (490 warnings); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u3-cross.log`).
**Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh I` against `H`,

### 8.223 An impl head's concrete target argument is not honoured by impl selection: `implement<T> trait Show for Wrap<T, Alpha>` is selected for `Wrap<i32, Beta>`, and two heads differing only in that argument collapse to one - a miscompile with no diagnostic, pinned RED, scoped, not built - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

§8.190 parked this: D16's ruling offers the concrete spelling
(`implement<T> trait Clone for Array<T, GlobalAlloc>`), type resolution
accepts it, and the five sites that bind a head's `target_args`
(`trait_specializer.cryo`, `method_binding.cryo` ×2,
`call_specializer.cryo`, `types/resolver.cryo`) bind EVERY `Named`
argument as a parameter name, so `GlobalAlloc` is bound to whatever the
subject carries.  The binding is the smaller half.  The larger is
SELECTION: the trait-impl registry keys an impl by `(trait, target key)`
where the target key is the TEMPLATE's canonical name
(`template_key_of`; `register_trait_impl_typed`, `register_trait_impl`,
both "latest impl wins"; `impl_target_rank` compares keys and never an
argument), so a head with a concrete argument is an impl for every
instantiation of the template, and two heads for one template that differ
in a concrete argument are one slot.

Two probes (`.objcmp/u1-keep/concrete`, `concrete2`; a two-parameter
`Wrap<T, A>`, two marker structs `Alpha` and `Beta`, a trait `Show`):

| program | Rust | pin `bin/cryo.exe` (2026-09-11) | `1451d792` | tree `1292de9f` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one head `for Wrap<T, Alpha>`; `wb: Wrap<i32, Beta>`; `wa.show() * 10 + wb.show()` | refused: `Wrap<i32, Beta>` has no `show` | builds, **11** | 11 | 11 |
| heads `for Wrap<T, Beta>` (2) then `for Wrap<T, Alpha>` (1); the same expression | **12** | builds, **22** | 22 | 22 |

The second is the fifth miscompile of the migration's class: both
subjects run one body, no diagnostic, every gate green.  Pre-existing -
the pin agrees - not a regression of the migration; the migration is what
made the head's argument a stamped `Res` the selector could read.

The population where the two readings differ is EMPTY BY LUCK: 11 heads
in the tree carry a concrete argument (`grep -rn -E 'implement.* for
(struct )?[A-Za-z_:]+<[^>]*\bGlobalAlloc\b' stdlib ...` → 11: `Box`,
`Array` ×2, `HashMap` ×2, `HashSet` ×2, `String` ×4, every one
`GlobalAlloc`), and nothing instantiates a collection with a second
allocator (`grep -rn -E '(Array|Box|HashMap|HashSet|String)<[^>]*[A-Z][a-z]+Alloc\b'
... | grep -v GlobalAlloc` → 3, all `Box<Arena>` with the allocator
defaulted).  The first program that does gets `GlobalAlloc`'s `clone`
body over an arena-allocated array.

#### Pinned, red

Two run projects hold the shape and FAIL at this commit, honestly:
`impl_concrete_arg_filters_impl` (compile_fail E0358 - `wb.show()` names
no method, as a struct with no impl at all is refused today with E0358 -
where the tree builds it and exits 11: `[FAIL] (expected build to fail)`)
and `impl_concrete_arg_selects_impl` (run, exit 12, where the tree exits
22: `[FAIL] (exit 22, expected 12)`).  `make test` is OVERALL FAIL with
those two named until the change below lands; every objcmp / corpus
half over `tests/` reads them the same way, and `corpus2.sh` reports
`failing halves: 1` for the compile_fail one (it builds).  A red project
over a known miscompile is the record; a green suite over it was the
mask.

#### The change this wants (scoped, not built - a registry reshape, D24's)

Rust selects an impl by UNIFYING the impl's self type against the subject:
the impl's own generic parameters are variables that bind, everything
else must be equal, and coherence guarantees at most one impl matches.
For Cryo:

1. The registry holds a LIST of heads per `(trait identity, template
   key)` - the key D24 rules (the trait's identity, not its leaf) with
   the template as the second component; "latest wins" goes.
2. One selector, `select_impl(trait, subject) -> ImplBlockNode*`: for
   each head under the key, walk `target_args[i]` against
   `inst_type_arg_at(subject, i)`: an argument stamped `Res::GenericParam`
   (a parameter of the head) BINDS; one stamped as a type (`Res::Def`, a
   primitive, a nested `Generic` whose base is a type) FILTERS - the
   subject's argument must be that type, recursively.  No head matching
   is no impl (E0358 at the call, as today for a type with none); two
   heads matching one subject is an overlap, reported once at
   registration, not at every use.  The stamps are already there
   (§8.193 stamped every head's `target_args`).
3. Every reader goes through the selector: `resolve_trait_impl_for_type`
   (10 callers), `lookup_trait_impl` (6), `impl_target_rank` (3),
   `traits_implemented_by` (9: a bound check `Wrap<i32, Beta>: Show`
   answers yes today), and the five binding sites bind only a
   `GenericParam`-stamped name.  `has_trait_impl_typed` and
   `lookup_trait_impl_typed` (1 each) fold into it.
4. Measure over the six halves before deleting the key-only readers:
   every selection today answers with one head per key, so the selector
   must agree at every one of them (§8.194's 193,199 answers are the
   control population) and differ at exactly the two projects.

This is the same registry D24 re-keys and the same readers; building the
two as one reshape is one measurement instead of two over the same 28
sites.  The sequencing is Jake's.  The interim alternative - refusing at
registration a second head for a key already held, or a head with a
concrete argument at all - would be a new diagnostic for a compiler
limitation and is not taken here.

#### Gates

No compiler change: nothing to hash.  roster merged (+2 projects);
`make test` over the two: `projects: 0 passed, 2 failed` (the record).
§0: the project count 64 → 66; D16's row says the parked half is pinned
red here.

Outside the ledger: the two projects, the roster.

**Tally: 72 shadowed, 72 old paths deleted, 72 at zero; 115 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: a finding pinned, nothing deleted).

### 8.224 The two-trait tie is E0156 in both spellings, naming each candidate where it is declared and the trait-qualified call that chooses; `Trait::method(recv, ...)` resolves to the receiver's implementation; and the Rust trait-in-scope rule is MEASURED, not built: 277 sites break under it and it settles 0 of the tree's 28 ties - 2026-09-17

Jake ruled (2026-09-17) that the two-trait tie is an ERROR - never a
pick by declaration or import order - and asked for a diagnostic that can
be acted on, with a proposed code; he leans toward, and has NOT ruled,
Rust's rule that a trait's methods are callable only where the trait is in
scope, and asked for its blast radius before ruling.  Three measurements
below; the diagnostic and the qualified call stand whichever way he goes.

#### The diagnostic: E0156

`E0156_AMBIGUOUS_TRAIT_METHOD`, one code for the tie in every spelling,
as Rust's E0034 is (§8.220 had put the path form under E0154, the
method form's code; E0154 stays for two FUNCTIONS or two MODULES a name
reaches).  One emitter, `report_trait_method_tie`, reached from the
method form (`p.go()`, the detector that was E0154's), the call form
(`P::go(&p)`, `choose_entry` through `report_static_path_tie`) and the
value form (`P::make`):

    error[E0156]: `go` is provided by more than one trait implemented for `P`
     --> src/main.cryo:25:20
     25 |     const b: i32 = P::go(&p);
        |                    ^~~~~ which `go` is meant here is ambiguous
     note: candidate #1: `Beta::go`, from `implement trait PluralStatic::Main::Beta for P`
     --> src/main.cryo:16:5
     16 |     go(&this) -> i32 { return this.v * 2; }
        |     ^~
     note: candidate #2: `Gamma::go`, from `implement trait PluralStatic::Main::Gamma for P`
     --> src/main.cryo:20:5
     help: name the trait the call is meant through: `Beta::go(&p)` or `Gamma::go(&p)`

Each candidate is placed at its declaration: the index's function
registry entry now carries its declaration's span
(`register_signature(..., span)`, `entry_span(id)`; every registrar
hands the node's name span over), so the path form reads it off the
entry and the method form off the `MethodNode` the detector walked.  The
help quotes the program's own receiver spelling (`source_text` over the
receiver's span through the renderer's source cache; `&` added when the
method form auto-referenced a value), lists every candidate's qualified
call, and spells the trait by its full path when two candidates share a
leaf (`Alpha::Render` / `Omega::Render`).  A tie of STATIC methods
(`P::make()`, `P::make` as a value) has no receiver to select by; the
help says so rather than proposing a form that does not exist - Rust's
`<P as Beta>::make()` has no Cryo spelling, and that is a language
question left open here.

#### The trait-qualified call resolves

§8.220 found `Beta::go(&p)` - the form §13.4 and the old E0154 note
proposed - compiled under no compiler (E0636 at codegen).  It resolves
now: `pin_trait_qualified_call`, entered from `pin_scope_callee_combined`
when the scope's stamp is a trait, takes the first argument's type behind
its references and pointers as the receiver's, asks the receiver's family
(`<Owner>::go`) for the entries THAT trait delivers, selects by the
arguments with the two passes every static pin uses, pins the entry and
types the call from the implementation's signature.  Project
`trait_qualified_call_disambiguates`: `Beta::go(&p) * 10 + Gamma::go(&p)`
→ **25** (HEAD `80f51c3c`: E0636).  §13.4 of `docs/cryo.md` now names
E0156 and this form.

Not resolved: a trait-qualified call to a GENERIC method
(`Display::fmt(&p, &sink)` with `fmt<W>`) - the type path `P::fmt(&p,
&sink)` specializes through `try_resolve_static_method_template` off the
generic registry, which holds ONE template per `P::fmt` key, so two
traits' `fmt<W>` on one type collapse there exactly as §8.223's impls do
(the registry-shape defect, D24's).  The help for a generic-method tie
therefore names a form the compiler does not yet instantiate; the
tree's one such tie is the negative `E0156_ambiguous_trait_method`.
Also not resolved: a trait-qualified call on a receiver the index holds
no family for (a primitive's impl) - left to codegen's refusal as
before.

#### Measurement 1 - does Cryo require the trait in scope today?  No.

Probe `.objcmp/u1-keep/scope`: `Scope::Traits` declares `Beta`,
`Scope::Shape` implements it for `P` (`import Scope::Traits::{ Beta }`),
`Scope::Main` writes `import Scope::Shape::{ P };` and nothing else.
Both `p.go()` and `P::go(&p)` **compile and run (exit 6)** under
`80f51c3c` with `Beta` imported nowhere in `Main` and `Scope::Traits`
not even transitively imported by it.  (Aside: a plain `import M;` does
not bring `M`'s names into scope bare - `P` needs the brace form or
`Shape::P` - so "trait in scope" in Cryo would mean the brace or
wildcard import of the trait ITEM, exactly Rust's `use m::Beta;`.)

#### Measurement 2 - what breaks if it starts?  277 call sites, 61 files.

Instrument: at every binding of a call to a trait's method (both method
binders, the static path pins, the value pin), the writing module
(`call_use_site_ns(span)`) is asked whether the trait's leaf resolves in
its module scope to a symbol from the trait's module (`same` module,
`import` - brace or wildcard, re-exports included -, `prelude`, `OUT`;
`other` when a different symbol of that leaf is in scope), tagged
`bnd` when the call was bound-directed (`member.resolved_trait`, which
Rust admits without an import: the bound names the trait).  Six halves
(`corpus2.sh m1`, `.objcmp/m1-lines.txt`, 392,011 lines; tabulated by
DISTINCT source site with the per-half relative paths normalized,
`.objcmp/u1-keep/tsc_tab.py`):

| verdict | sites | of which bound-directed |
|---|---|---|
| prelude (`Drop` 182k lines, `Ord`, `Eq`, `Iterator`, `Clone`, `Add`...) | 5,773 | 37 |
| import | 1,434 | 140 |
| same module | 227 | 51 |
| **OUT** | **458** | 181 (177 of them `Future`, `.poll()` through a bound) |
| other | 0 | |

**277 sites are OUT and unbound** - the sites the strict rule breaks:
stdlib 135 (`net` 71, `future` 26, `thread` 13, `sync` 13, `process` 4,
`io` 4, `collections` 2, `test` 2), `tests/` 118 (116 unit-suite files,
2 negatives), `tools/CryoLSP` 19, `examples/` 5, **`compiler/src` 0** of
its 51,240 lines.  By trait: `Allocator` 85, `AsyncWrite` 55, `AsyncRead`
47, `JsonExtract` 27, `TryFrom` 22, `Hasher` 12, `Read` 10, `Seek` 8,
`Default` 6, `Pulse` 2, `Future` 2, `RandomSource` 1.  61 files; the
list is `.objcmp/u1-keep/m1-out-sites.txt`.  Hand control:
`stdlib/thread/_module.cryo:213` calls `alloc.deallocate(...)` with
`import std::alloc::allocator;` and `::{ GlobalAlloc }` written and
`Allocator` in neither - OUT, as the instrument said.

The LOOSE reading - the trait's MODULE imported in any form, which is
not Rust's rule but is the one the tree was evidently written to -
breaks **6 sites in 5 files** (`u1-keep/loose.py`): 3 `TryFrom`
(`u32::try_from(...)` in three examples), 2 `Future` (one negative),
1 `RandomSource` (`hashmap.cryo:83`).  271 of the 277 strict-OUT sites
import the module and omit the trait's name from the brace list.

#### Measurement 3 - does the scope rule settle ties in practice?  0 of 28.

The same instrument at the E0154/E0156 detector, one line per candidate
trait at every call whose receiver has two traits providing the method
(bound-settled or not), and at every static-path tie (`corpus2.sh m2`,
`.objcmp/m2-lines.txt`, paired by site in `u1-keep/tie_tab.py`):

| shape | sites | both traits in scope | one | neither |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| method call, bound-directed (`where T: Display` / `Debug`; `Alpha::Render` / `Omega::Render`) | 25 | 23 | **0** | 2 |
| method call, unbound (the E0156 negative) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| static path, unbound (the E0156 negative, 2 sites) | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

**28 tie sites; at none of them would the scope rule alone choose.**
The one real collision in the tree is `Display::fmt` / `Debug::fmt` (24
of 28), and every module that formats imports both; the bound settles
it, as it would under any rule.  The remaining ties are the projects
built to hold them.  So on this tree the rule buys nothing against the
tie population and costs 277 sites (strict) or 6 (loose); its value, if
any, is prospective - and E0156 fires just as often either way.

#### Gates

`make test` (`hash-tree.sh J`'s log, `.objcmp/t-J.txt.log`) OVERALL
FAIL with exactly §8.223's two projects; compile-fail 193 (the two
negatives renamed `E0156_*`, annotations re-pinned to the new text),

**Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh J` against `I`:

### 8.225 A type declaration carries the id its registration minted: `register_type` returns a `DefId`, the six declaration nodes hold it, and 21 readers that asked the index for the node's own type by a key re-derived from the node ask `type_of_def(node.def)`; the re-derivation was WRONG for 117 declarations per half - the futures of a trait default's `async` methods - which sema and codegen silently skipped - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

A type declaration (`StructDeclNode`, `UnionDeclNode`, `ClassDeclNode`,
`EnumDeclNode`, `TraitDeclNode`, `TypeAliasDeclNode`) is registered once,
by the type-declaration stage, under `decl_type_key(name,
binding_namespace, span.file)` - a C import's alias, else a name already
qualified, else the module of the file that WROTE it, else the cursor.
Every later reader that wanted the declaration's own type derived the
key AGAIN from the node with the same call and asked `lookup_type` -
audit 10's bucket B, "a canonical name derived from a declaration in
hand".  Twenty-one such readers: codegen's four forward declarations
and the class-methods walk (`declaration_emitter`), the directive
pass's four layout propagations, type resolution's three method-signature
owners, the trait populate, the alias target and the four field
populates, and sema's struct / union / class visits (six
`lookup_type_exact` calls).

A re-derived key is a GUESS about what the registration used, and the
two disagree wherever the node's provenance is not the registration's:
a specialization is registered by its injector under the arena's name
(the TEMPLATE's module prefixed to the spec identifier) while its clone
carries the template node's span, and for the future of an `async`
trait DEFAULT method the two modules differ - the future is minted in
the impl's module (`std::io::buf`, where `implement<S> trait AsyncRead
for BufStream<S>` is written) and its declaration's span is the
default body's file (`std::io::traits`).

#### The change

* `DeclarationIndex::register_type(key, ty, is_public)` returns
  `DefId::of_definition(key)`: the registration is the one place that
  knows the referent by construction, so the mint lives there
  (`DEFID_MINT` 22 → 23, the one mint added by this migration's own
  direction) and every writer stamps it - the six arms of the
  type-declaration stage, `SpecInjector::register` (a new `stamp_def`,
  since the cloner leaves the field invalid: a clone's registration is
  its own, never its template's), the async future struct, the closure
  struct.  The primitives register no node.
* Each of the six nodes carries `def: DefId`, invalid until stamped.
* The 21 readers ask `type_of_def(node.def)`; the key derivation at each
  is deleted.  The comment in sema's struct visit that explained how the
  key would be right for a clone ("the TEMPLATE's file, so the key is
  the arena's `template module :: spec`") described the case that was
  wrong.

#### The measurement

A shadow at every converted reader (`shadow_tdef`: the stamp's answer
beside the re-derived key's - `AGREE` one valid type, `NOSTAMP` no stamp
but the key answers, `KEYINV` the stamp answers and the key does not,
`BOTHINV`, `DISAGREE`).  Six halves (`corpus2.sh t1`,
`.objcmp/t1-lines.txt`, scripts in `.objcmp/u1-keep/s12/`): **104,578
asks: 104,344 `AGREE`, 234 `KEYINV`, 0 `NOSTAMP`, 0 `DISAGREE`, 0
`BOTHINV`**; tests 84,648, examples 14,575, LSP 5,355; failing halves 1
(the §8.223 compile_fail project that builds, as at every half since
`80f51c3c`); `make test` in the run OVERALL FAIL projects 62 / 2, the
two §8.223 reds and nothing else.  Twenty of the 21 sites answered
(`dp_class` 0: no class in the corpus carries a `![repr]`).

The 234 are 117 declarations per half at two readers each, sema's
struct visit and codegen's struct forward declaration - **33 distinct
(key, stamp) pairs, one shape**: the specializations of the future
structs of `AsyncRead`'s six default `async` methods (`ensure`,
`read_exact`, `read_some`, `read_until`, `read_line`, `skip`; stdlib
`io/traits.cryo`, `AsyncRead` at 442) for `BufStream<S>` at five `S`, registered
`std::io::buf::NNBufStream$m$Future_k$LN$…$G$G` and re-derived
`std::io::traits::…`, plus the unit suite's `MockSink$send$Future_8` at
three (`CryoTests::Tests::Stdlib::IoAsyncTraits::…` against
`std::io::traits::…`).  At HEAD both readers get an invalid type for
them: sema visits the future's inline methods with no owner - it has
none, `poll` lives in the impl block, so nothing is typed wrongly - and
codegen returns before `map_type`, so the LLVM struct is declared at
first use instead of at its declaration.  Neither reaches an object
(below); both are the shape of the four miscompiles this migration has
found, a reader guessing a registration's key and the guess being
wrong for a provenance the guesser did not know about.  Control by
inversion: the instrument's non-`AGREE` arm fired 234 times through the
same print the `NOSTAMP` verdict uses; the first probe (`examples/
01-hello`, 1,007 asks) showed 12 `KEYINV` before the corpus ran.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 35 → **17** (`declaration_emitter` 8 → 3,
`directive_processing` 4 → 0, `type_resolution` 13 → 4), `DEFID_MINT`
22 → 23, re-pinned; predicted −18 and +1.  Predicted `LOOKUP_ROUTED`
20 → 14 and it stayed 20: the gate's five-name rule counts
`types.lookup_type(` and not `types.lookup_type_exact(`, so the six
sema calls were in no bucket - **a gate blind spot, a finding**: the
`TypeUtils` wrappers `lookup_type_exact` (15 → 9 treewide),
`lookup_func_type_exact` (4) and `lookup_type_sym` (7) are counted
nowhere, 26 → 20 sites, while `LOOKUP_ROUTED`'s header says "answered by
a TypeUtils wrapper".  lsp-check OK (490 warnings, `.objcmp/t2-lsp-check.log`);
cross-check OK (`.objcmp/t2-cross.log`).  **Objects: 0 of 1,126 + 2,719
moved** (`hash-tree.sh K` against `J`, HEAD `1a14f114`'s half,
`.objcmp/t2-hashK.out`; `t-K.txt.log` OVERALL FAIL 62 / 2, the §8.223
pair, 0 allocation failures); predicted 0, with the one candidate for
movement being the 117 futures now forward-declared at their
declaration - a named LLVM type's creation order is not in the object.
§0: `LOOKUP` 35 → 17 on §8.219's row, `decl_type_key` 24 → 15 in
`type_resolution` and 8 → 3 in `sema` on their rows, `lookup_type(qualified_sym)`
4 → 0 on §8.221's row.

Not taken, each a bucket-B site whose consumer wants the NAME (a
registration key, a mangling, `current_impl_target`): the 38
`decl_type_key` callers left - the type-declaration stage's own 12
(six the E0207 pre-pass, six the registrations), type resolution's 13
(six `register_name_mapping`, three `resolve_method_signatures` keys,
three `resolve_inline_method_signatures`, the trait registry's
`register_trait_decl`), sema's 3 (`declare_async_methods`), codegen's 6
(`declare_method`'s owner ×3, `current_impl_target` ×3),
specialization's 3, the async mint.  For the 117 futures above those guess the same wrong module
today and reach nothing only because a future struct has no inline
methods; the slice that ends the guessing is those consumers taking the
`DefId` (the owner of a method registration, the impl target) and
unwrapping it for text where text is what they emit.  And the
`!type_ref.is_valid()` arm at each converted reader is reachable now
only by an UNSTAMPED node (0 over six halves): the D23 step is a door
there, but at the reader, since `type_of_def` also answers `type_of_res`
for a `Res` that is legitimately not a definition.

Outside the ledger: `AST/declaration.cryo`, `decl_index.cryo`,
`passes/pass_registry.cryo`, `passes/specialization.cryo`,
`passes/type_resolution.cryo`, `passes/directive_processing.cryo`,
`sema/sema.cryo`, `sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`,
`codegen/ops/declaration_emitter.cryo`, the lane golden.

**Tally: 73 shadowed, 73 old paths deleted, 73 at zero; 115 artifacts
gone** (+1 lane, the re-derived key at a declaration's own readers,
shadowed and deleted here; the artifact count is unchanged - `decl_type_key`
stays for the registrations and the name-keyed consumers).

### 8.226 Codegen's method owner is a TYPE, not a name: `declare_method`, `codegen_method_prologue` and `current_impl_target` take a `TypeRef`, the three `lookup_type(target_type)` and both `()`-suffix hacks are deleted, and the impl head's owner is read by ONE `DeclarationIndex::impl_owner` where type resolution and sema each carried a copy - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

Codegen carried the type a method is on as a NAME.  `declare_method(node,
target_type)` and `codegen_method_prologue(node, target_type)` each asked
`lookup_type(target_type)` for the receiver's type (three asks between
them - `declare_method` twice, for `this` and for a by-value receiver's
ABI class), each followed by a hack for the unit type: when the name
missed and ended in `()`, `arena.get_unit()`.  `VisitorState::current_impl_target`
held the same name across a body walk.  The name came from five sources:
an impl block's `target_key` (the stamp spelled out: a `Def`'s canonical
name, a `PrimTy`'s spelling, a clone's `spec_owner` turned back into its
arena name - a `TypeRef` unwrapped to a name so a reader could look the
`TypeRef` up again) at the declare and the body walk, and
`decl_type_key(node…)` at the struct, union and class walks - the guess
§8.225 measured wrong for a trait default's future.

Type resolution and sema each already read an impl head's owner as a
`TypeRef` off the stamp (`TypeResolutionRunner::impl_owner`,
`SemanticAnalyzer::impl_target_type`) - the same three-arm function
twice, one recording an unregistered `Def` through `def_type` and one
not.  A third copy in codegen was the mirror this tree forbids.

#### The change

* `DeclarationIndex::impl_owner(node, site)`: the one reader of an impl
  head's owner.  `Def` → `type_of_def`, an invalid answer recorded as an
  unregistered definition against `site` (the door sema's copy had and
  type resolution's lacked); `PrimTy` → the spelling's registration;
  unanswered → `spec_owner`.  The two copies are deleted and their six
  callers (type resolution's two signature walks and the field sync,
  sema's generic, template-instance and concrete impl arms) ask the index.
* `current_impl_target: TypeRef`; `declare_method(node, owner: TypeRef)`;
  `codegen_method_prologue(node, owner: TypeRef)`.  The impl walks pass
  `impl_owner(node)` (the template-target skip still asks the generic
  registry by `target_key`, a name-keyed table by design); the struct,
  union and class walks pass `type_of_def(node.def)` (the class declare
  already held it for the vtable).  The three lookups and both hacks are
  gone; the receiver is `owner`.  Diagnostic text is the arena's display
  name of the owner (`resolve_display_name`), which is what the rest of
  codegen prints for a type; the E0900 "target type not found" wording
  becomes "the owner has no type", since there is no longer a name that
  could be looked up and missed.
* `declare_method`'s `di`, `arena` and `ctx_ptr` locals fed only the
  deleted lookups and go with them (the LSP gate's warning count would
  have said so: 490 → 490).

#### The measurement

A shadow at the five owner sources (`shadow_owner`: the name path's
answer with the `()` hack replayed, beside the owner `TypeRef`; `AGREE`
one valid type, else `NAMEINV` / `OWNERINV` / `BOTHINV` / `DISAGREE`, both
ids on every line).  Six halves (`corpus2.sh t3`, `.objcmp/t3-lines.txt`,
script `.objcmp/u1-keep/s12/owner_tref.py`): **95,622 asks, all `AGREE`** -
impl blocks 41,405 at each of the declare and the body walk, structs
6,276 ×2, classes 128 / 126, unions 3 ×2; 0 `AGREE` lines with unequal
ids (the instrument's own control, `awk '$5=="AGREE" && $6!=$7'`);
failing halves 1 (§8.223's, as at every half since `80f51c3c`); `make
test` in the run OVERALL FAIL 62 / 2, the same two.  The unit hack's
whole population, `implement trait Drop for ()` (`core/drop.cryo:52`), is
66 asks per site whose name is the bare `()` - registered under that
spelling by the type-declaration stage, so `lookup_type` answered before
the suffix test ever ran: the hack was dead, and its deletion is
measured rather than argued.  The struct walk's population here excludes
§8.225's 117 futures (a walk with no methods returns before the owner is
set), which is why they were reachable at §8.225's readers and not at
these.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 17 → **13** (`declaration_emitter` 3 → 0,
`type_resolution` 4 → 3, the deleted copy's `PrimTy` arm; the index's
own is not the surface), re-pinned; predicted −4.  lsp-check OK (490
warnings, `.objcmp/t4-lsp-check.log`); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/t4-cross.log`).
**Objects: 0 of 1,126 + 2,719 moved** (`hash-tree.sh L` against `K`,
§8.225's half, `.objcmp/t4-hashL.out`; `t-L.txt.log` OVERALL FAIL 62 / 2,
the §8.223 pair, 0 allocation failures); predicted 0.  §0: `LOOKUP` 17 →
13 on §8.219's row; §8.174's row's checks re-pointed at the one reader
(`node.spec_owner` in `decl_index.cryo` 1, `.impl_owner(` treewide 8);
§8.222's `record_unregistered_def` in `decl_index.cryo` 1 → 2 (the
`Def` door).  `decl_type_key` callers 38 → 32.

Left as they are: `resolve_method_signatures`' `owner_qname` (the
resolver compares a return or parameter type's instantiation against
the owner by ARENA NAME in `is_self_growing_instantiation`, because an
impl block's owner `TypeRef` "is often invalid at this pass" - a
`TypeRef` identity there is D1's question, not this entry's); the
generic registry's `get_template(target_key)` template skip at both impl
walks (name-keyed by design, D24's registry); sema's
`declare_async_methods(…, qname)` (its impl caller passes a key, and it
looks the owner up by it - the same shape as this entry, next).

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo`,
`sema/sema.cryo`, `codegen/state/visitor_state.cryo`,
`codegen/visit/decl_visit_emitter.cryo`,
`codegen/ops/declaration_emitter.cryo`, the lane golden.

**Tally: 74 shadowed, 74 old paths deleted, 74 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (+1 lane, the owner by name at codegen's method declare and
prologue; +3 artifacts: `TypeResolutionRunner::impl_owner`,
`SemanticAnalyzer::impl_target_type`, the `()`-suffix hack - counted once
for its two copies).

### 8.227 `lane-check`'s `LOOKUP_ROUTED` counts every `lookup_*` on the `TypeUtils` receiver, not the five names: 19 wrapper calls (`lookup_type_exact` 8, `lookup_func_type_exact` 4, `lookup_type_sym` 7) were in no bucket, and the old gate printed `OK` over a tree with a new one - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

§8.225 predicted `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 20 → 14 for six `this.types.lookup_type_exact`
calls it removed, and the row did not move.  The gate places a call by
its receiver (`lookup_bucket`) but only for the five names mechanism 5
gives; every OTHER `lookup_*` name is counted only when the receiver is
the index (`LOOKUP_OTHER`).  A `TypeUtils` wrapper under a sixth name
(`lookup_type_exact` beside `lookup_type`) was therefore in no row at
all, though the row's own header reads "answered by a TypeUtils
wrapper" - so a call could move between `types.lookup_type(` and
`types.lookup_type_exact(` and leave the surface without a number
moving, the hole `LOOKUP_OTHER` was built to close on the index side.

#### The change

`scan()`'s any-name loop places a `LOOKUP_ROUTED` receiver too; the
row's header (golden and docstring) says "under ANY `lookup_*` name".
Nothing else in the gate changes; `LOOKUP_LOCAL` keeps the five-name
rule, since a `this.` receiver's other `lookup_*` methods are unrelated
symbol-map methods and not a funnel.

#### The pair

Mutation: one line in `sema.cryo`, `const zz_probe: SymbolStr =
this.types.lookup_type_sym(TypeRef::invalid());`.

* OLD gate over the mutated tree: `lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 13 (6
  files), LOOKUP_OTHER = 30 (6 files), LOOKUP_ROUTED = 20 (3 files), …`.
* NEW gate over the same tree: `lane-gate: DRIFT … LOOKUP_ROUTED TOTAL
  39 -> 40 (INCREASE -- a lane regrew) … compiler/sema/sema.cryo 5 -> 6`.
* Restored: `OK -- … LOOKUP_ROUTED = 39 (5 files)`.

Re-pinned 20 → **39** (`call_resolver` 11 → 20, `method_binding` 7 →
11, `sema` 2 → 5, `member_resolver` 0 → 2, `diagnostics` 0 → 1).
Predicted 40 from a count taken before §8.226, which deleted sema's
`impl_target_type` and its `lookup_type_exact`; recounted, the tree
holds 19 wrapper calls, and the gate's 39 is right (`gate_diff.py` in
`.objcmp/u1-keep/s12/`: no line where the gate's scan and a direct
regex disagree).

Outside the ledger: `scripts/lane-gate.py`, the lane golden.

**Tally: 74 shadowed, 74 old paths deleted, 74 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: a gate widened, nothing deleted).

### 8.228 Sema's async declare pass takes the owner's type and registration key from the caller - a declaration's stamp, an impl head's `impl_owner` - instead of re-deriving a key and looking the owner up by it; the same 117 futures per half were being re-derived under the wrong module there too - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

`declare_async_methods(methods, params, qname, impl)` took one thing, a
NAME, and did two with it: `lookup_type_exact(qname)` for the owner's
type, and `AsyncOwner.qname` for the key the lowering re-registers each
method's signature under (`reset_method_overloads`, `register_methods`)
and mints the future's name from.  Its three declaration callers derived
the name with `decl_type_key(node…)` - §8.225's guess - and its impl
caller with the head's `target_key`.  The pass runs before and after
monomorphization, so the clones §8.225 found reach it.

#### The change

`declare_async_methods(methods, params, owner_ty, qname, impl)`: the
caller hands over what it holds.  A declaration: `type_of_def(node.def)`
and `node.def.qualified_name()` - the registration's own key, which is
what a name-keyed registrar wants and what the guess was standing in
for.  An impl block: `impl_owner(ib)` (§8.226's one reader) and
`target_key`.  The pass looks nothing up; an invalid owner or key is
still `reject_undeclarable_async`.

#### The measurement

A shadow at the three declaration callers (`shadow_async_owner`: the
guessed key beside the stamp's, and each one's type).  Six halves
(`corpus2.sh t5`, `.objcmp/t5-lines.txt`, script
`.objcmp/u1-keep/s12/async_owner.py`): **29,965 asks: 29,848 `AGREE`,
117 `KEYINV`, 0 `NOSTAMP`, 0 `DISAGREE`** (struct 29,572 + 117, class
262, union 14); failing halves 1 (§8.223's); `make test` in the run
OVERALL FAIL 62 / 2, the same two.  The 117 are §8.225's 33
declarations (the `AsyncRead` default futures for `BufStream<S>`, the
unit suite's `MockSink$send`), guessed under `std::io::traits` where
the registration is `std::io::buf`: at HEAD the guess found no type and
the pass returned through `reject_undeclarable_async` over a method list
that is empty for a future struct - so no diagnostic and no work either
way, and the same accident that made §8.225's readers harmless.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 39 → **38** (`sema` 5 → 4, the
`lookup_type_exact`), `DEFID_UNWRAP` 33 → **36** (`sema` 1 → 4: the
three registration keys read from the stamp - an unwrap that feeds a
name-keyed registrar, in place of a re-derivation that was wrong),
re-pinned; predicted −1 and +3.  lsp-check OK (490 warnings,
`.objcmp/t6-lsp-check.log`); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/t6-cross.log`).
**Objects: 0 of 1,126 + 2,719 moved** (`hash-tree.sh M` against `L`, §8.226's half,
`.objcmp/t6-hashM.out`; `t-M.txt.log` OVERALL FAIL 62 / 2, the §8.223 pair,
0 allocation failures); predicted 0.  §0: `decl_type_key` in
`sema.cryo` 3 → 0 on §8.185's row; the lane cells.  `decl_type_key`
callers 32 → 29: what is left derives a key for a REGISTRATION (the
type-declaration stage's 12, type resolution's 13 name-keyed
registrations, specialization's 3, the async mint) - every reader of a
declaration's own type or key now reads the stamp.

Outside the ledger: `sema/sema.cryo`, the lane golden.

**Tally: 75 shadowed, 75 old paths deleted, 75 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (+1 lane, the async owner by re-derived key; no artifact).

### 8.229 RULED: three decisions from Jake, 2026-09-17 - `(Beta for P)::make()` is the impl-qualified call form, the two-trait tie is an error, and the Rust trait-in-scope rule is REJECTED on its measurement

Three rulings that existed only in prose (§8.224's head blockquote, the
handoff) get their §0 rows. None is reopened here; each is recorded with
the basis Jake ruled on so it is not proposed again.

#### D25 - `(Beta for P)::make()` is Cryo's impl-qualified call form (RULED - UNBUILT)

The motivating case is §8.224's open item (b): a tie of STATIC trait
methods - `P::make()` where `Beta::make` and `Gamma::make` are both
implemented for `P` - has no receiver to disambiguate it, so E0156 fires
with no suggestable spelling; the receiver form `Tr::m(&recv, ...)` only
covers a method with a receiver.

Jake ruled the form `(Beta for P)::make()`. It reuses `for` exactly as
`implement trait Beta for P` does, so it adds no lexical territory and
avoids the `<P as Beta>` parsing problem (a `<` at expression start is
already a comparison). It MUST cover the receiver case too -
`(Beta for P)::go(&p)` - so E0156 has ONE rule to suggest rather than a
short form that works sometimes; and it must compose inside a generic:
`(Beta for T)::make()` with `T` a type parameter bound by `Beta`. Not
built: the parser, the resolution of the parenthesized head (a trait and
a type, both stamped), the selection of THAT trait's impl for the type,
and E0156's help naming the form.

#### D26 - the two-trait tie is an ERROR (TAKEN, §8.224)

Ruled 2026-09-17, built the same day as `E0156_AMBIGUOUS_TRAIT_METHOD`:
a receiver with no inherent `m` whose trait impls provide `m` twice is
refused in both spellings (`recv.m(...)`, `T::m(recv, ...)`), never a
pick by declaration or import order; the error names each candidate at
its declaration. It had no §0 row - the built diagnostic was on §8.224's
head and nowhere in the current-state table.

#### D27 - the Rust trait-in-scope rule is REJECTED (RULED)

Jake leaned to Rust's rule ("a trait's methods are only callable when
the trait is in scope"; `import` does the disambiguating) and asked for
the blast radius first (§8.224, measurements 1-3). Ruled AGAINST on that
measurement, 2026-09-17. The measurement is on the row so the proposal
does not come back without new numbers:

* **Cryo does not require the trait in scope today**, in either call
  form: `p.go()` and `P::go(&p)` both compile and run with `Beta`
  imported nowhere in the calling module and its module not transitively
  imported (probe `scope`, §8.224 measurement 1).
* **Requiring it breaks 277 call sites across 61 files**: stdlib 135,
  `tests/` 118, LSP 19, examples 5, `compiler/src` 0 (measurement 2;
  `scripts/ns-migration/8.224/shadow_tsc.py` + `tsc_tab.py` re-derive it
  from a corpus run).
* **It resolves 0 of the 28 tie sites** in the corpus: at no site is
  exactly one candidate in scope - 23 `Display`/`Debug` `fmt` ties have
  BOTH imported, 2 `Alpha::Render`/`Omega::Render` have NEITHER, 3 are the
  negatives with both by design (measurement 3; `shadow_tie.py` +
  `tie_tab.py`).

E0156 fires just as often under either rule; D25 is what gives a tie a
spelling, not scope.

Outside the ledger: nothing - three rows and the legend's `REJECTED`
status. Rides with §8.230's commit.

**Tally: 75 shadowed, 75 old paths deleted, 75 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: rulings recorded, nothing built).
