### 8.230 `lane-check` counts name-keyed calls by the receiver's TYPE, not by a name pattern: a name-crossing method is any the `DeclarationIndex` or `TypeUtils` declares with `SymbolStr` in its signature, read from the definition file on every run; 24 readers were outside the gate by construction, and the old gate printed `OK` over a tree with a new `owner_of(name)` - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

The gate pinned readers by a NAME PATTERN: the five names mechanism 5
gives (`LOOKUP`), and `lookup_*` for the rest (`LOOKUP_OTHER`,
`LOOKUP_ROUTED`). Any name-keyed reader called anything else was outside
the gate *by construction* - which is why eleven audit rounds each found
more. §8.227 widened the name list to cover the `TypeUtils` wrappers;
that closed 16 sites but did not change the rule. At `d4453224` the
tree held **24 sites blind by name**: `is_candidate_public` 3,
`namespace_of` 3, `is_prelude_ns`/`ns_imports` 4, `find_global_*` 3,
`get_global_*` 2, `global_extern_symbol` 2, `is_global_thread_local` 2,
`intrinsic_owner_of` 1, `extern_symbol_conflict` 1 (the index), and
`resolve_method_owner` 2, `alias_global` 1 (`TypeUtils`).

#### The rule

A name-keyed method is one whose **signature mentions `SymbolStr`** -
as a parameter (a name in, an answer out) or as the return type (an
answer in, a name out: the same boundary crossed the other way -
`entry_symbol`, `lookup_type_name`, `lookup_type_sym`; without the return
half, `lookup_type_sym`'s 7 calls would have LEFT the gate). The set is
parsed from `type struct DeclarationIndex { … }` in `decl_index.cryo` and
`type struct TypeUtils { … }` in `type_utils.cryo` on every run
(`name_crossing_methods`; `--names` prints both sets). A reader added
tomorrow as `owner_of(name)` is inside the rule the moment it is
declared, because the signature is the one thing a name-keyed reader
cannot be written without. The five names are the only list the gate
still holds, and the list decides which ROW a call lands in, never
whether it is counted.

Rows, by receiver (`receiver_kind`: `di`/`*.decl_index` the index,
`types`/`*.types` the funnel, `this` the owner's own or a same-named
local; `DeclarationIndex::`/`TypeUtils::` a static; anything else
refused):

* `LOOKUP` - the five, on the index. Unchanged: **13**.
* `LOOKUP_OTHER` - every other name-crossing READ (`&this`, or a
  static) on the index. 30 → **62**: −5 type-keyed `lookup_*` that are
  not a name crossing (`lookup_implicit_converter(u64, u64)` 4,
  `lookup_array_type(TypeRef)` 1 - `grep -rn 'decl_index\.lookup_\(implicit_converter\|array_type\)(' compiler/src`),
  +37 non-`lookup_` readers: the 21 index sites above, `entry_symbol` 10,
  `entry_trait` 3, `entry_key` 1, `prelude_namespaces` 1, and the static
  `DeclarationIndex::split_global_key` 1 (`symbol_resolver.cryo`).
* `REGISTER` - NEW: a name-keyed WRITE (`mut &this`) on the index, a
  registrar handed a key the CALLER derived from a declaration it holds.
  **84** (`pass_registry` 34, `type_resolution` 27, `specialization` 7,
  `async_lower` 7, `lambda_synth` 3, `instance` 2, `call_specializer` 2,
  `directive_processing` 2). This is the row the registrars-take-the-`DefId`
  slice moves; it was in no row at all.
* `LOOKUP_ROUTED` - every name-crossing method on `TypeUtils`. 38 →
  **41** (+`resolve_method_owner` 1, `find_template_module` 1,
  `alias_global` 1; `sema` 4 → 6, `call_resolver` 20 → 21).
* `LOOKUP_LOCAL` - a set name on `this` outside the defining file (a
  same-named local method). Unchanged: **9**.

The owner exclusion is per set: `decl_index.cryo`'s own calls to index
methods and `type_utils.cryo`'s own calls to funnel methods are not the
surface; the funnel's calls INTO the index are (`type_utils.cryo`
`LOOKUP` 5, `LOOKUP_OTHER` 7). Two controls on the instrument: the
parser refuses a definition file it finds no `type struct` or no
name-crossing method in, and refuses an index set missing any of the
five (the `LOOKUP` row would be void); every count above was predicted
from an independent per-receiver survey before the gate ran and landed
exactly (`LOOKUP_OTHER` 62, `REGISTER` 84, `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 41).

#### The pairs

Read side - `owner_of(&this, name: SymbolStr) -> TypeRef` declared on
the index, one call `this.ctx.decl_index.owner_of(name)` in `sema.cryo`:

* OLD gate (§8.227's, its golden) over the mutated tree: `lane-gate: OK
  -- LOOKUP = 13 (6 files), LOOKUP_OTHER = 30 (6 files), LOOKUP_ROUTED =
  38 (5 files), …`.
* NEW gate over the same tree: `lane-gate: DRIFT … LOOKUP_OTHER TOTAL 62
  -> 63 (INCREASE -- a lane regrew) … compiler/sema/sema.cryo 0 -> 1`.

Write side - `bind_owner(mut &this, name: SymbolStr, ty: TypeRef)`
declared on the index, one call from `pass_registry.cryo`:

* OLD gate: `lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 13 … LOOKUP_OTHER = 30 …`.
* NEW gate: `lane-gate: DRIFT … REGISTER TOTAL 84 -> 85 (INCREASE -- a
  lane regrew) … compiler/passes/pass_registry.cryo 34 -> 35`.

Restored: `lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 13 (6 files), LOOKUP_OTHER = 62 (9
files), REGISTER = 84 (8 files), LOOKUP_ROUTED = 41 (5 files),
LOOKUP_LOCAL = 9 (2 files), LOOKUP_ARENA = 2, REENTRY = 6, HOME_WRITE =
0, DEFID_MINT = 23, DEFID_UNWRAP = 36`. Ten rows; §0's
`grep -c '^\[' tests/lane-baseline.txt` moves 9 → 10.

#### Also in this commit: the generators of §8.221-§8.228's landed edits

`scripts/ns-migration/<entry>/` now holds the edit scripts and shadow
instruments that produced §8.221, §8.222, §8.224, §8.225, §8.226 and
§8.228 (README there), which had lived only in the gitignored
`.objcmp/u1-keep/`. The rule is that a generator lands with what it
generated; these did not, and the audit could not re-run §8.225's shadow
or re-derive §8.224's 277 from outside. The one edit made in the copy:
the `s12/` scripts' absolute checkout path is derived from the script's
own location. §8.227's `gate_diff.py` is NOT carried: it was a control on
the previous gate's `ANY_LOOKUP_RE`, which this entry removes.

Outside the ledger: `scripts/lane-gate.py`, the lane golden,
`scripts/ns-migration/`.

**Tally: 75 shadowed, 75 old paths deleted, 75 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: a gate's rule replaced, nothing deleted).

### 8.231 The 29 readers of a type declaration's own type are D23 doors: `type_of_decl(node.def, site)` records an unstamped node and reports it on BOTH exits of the build - the old readers skipped in silence and the program was refused with errors that blamed it (`E0201 cannot find value this`, `E0204 no field x on Point`); 0 over examples, tests, the LSP and the cross-target build - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

Every reader §8.225, §8.226 and §8.228 moved onto the stamp asks
`type_of_def(node.def)` and then either tests the answer and skips (`if
(!type_ref.is_valid()) { continue; }` - the four codegen forward
declarations, the four layout-propagation arms, the four field-sync
arms, the trait populate, the alias target) or hands it on unchecked
(codegen's three method-declaration walks and three method-body walks,
sema's three owner visits and three async declares, type resolution's
three signature owners). The invalid arm is reachable now only by an
UNSTAMPED node - `type_of_def` answers every stamp its registration
minted - and an unstamped type-declaration node is an internal defect
by construction: the type-declaration stage registers every arm with no
error exit before the registration (`pass_registry.cryo`, the walk over
`root.statements`), and the three synthesizers (`SpecInjector::stamp_def`,
the async future, the closure struct) stamp what they mint. D23's rule:
a silent arm becomes a door once its population is measured to zero.

#### The door

`DeclarationIndex::type_of_decl(d, site)`, beside `type_of_def` (which
stays: it also serves `type_of_res` for a `Res` that is legitimately not
a definition, and a door there would fire on those). An invalid `d`
records `record_unstamped_decl(site)` - a THIRD tally in `res.cryo`,
beside the `Pending` and unregistered ones, because it is a different
fact: not a path nobody resolved, not a canonical name the index cannot
serve, but a declaration node no registration reached. A valid `d` the
index does not answer goes to the unregistered tally. Both hand back an
invalid type, so every caller stops exactly as before; the 14 checked
arms keep their `continue`/`return` as the stop, now recorded, and the
15 unchecked ones hand on an invalid type that is now recorded too.

**The report is unconditional and on both exits.** The two existing
tallies are reported only when the build has no other error and only at
the end of the success path, on the argument that a build with a user
error may legitimately have skipped a pass. Neither holds here. No user
error can leave a declaration unstamped (above), and the consumers of an
unstamped one refuse the program with errors that blame it, so a report
gated on a clean build would be hidden by its own cascade - and a report
placed only on the success path is never reached at all, because the
staged front-end returns through `project_failure` at the first failing
stage. This was found by the mutation below: the first cut of the door
recorded 138 and printed nothing. `CompilerInstance::report_unstamped_decls(ctx)`
is called from `project_failure` and from the success path (exclusive:
the failure exit is only ever a stage's early return).

#### The pair

Mutation (`scripts/ns-migration/8.231/mutate_nostamp.py`): the struct arm
of the type-declaration stage registers the type and throws the `DefId`
away, so every struct reaches its readers unstamped. Probes
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.231/probes/`): `nostamp`, a struct with a
method `sum(&this)` (exit 7); `nostamp2`, a struct read by field (exit
7). Both run under `d4453224` (`.objcmp/cryo-N0.exe`).

* OLD readers + mutation (`.objcmp/cryo-N1-nostamp.exe`): `nostamp` →
  `error[E0201]: cannot find value \`this\` in this scope` ×2,
  `Project compilation failed (2 errors, 0 warnings)`; `nostamp2` →
  `error[E0204]: no field or method \`x\` on type \`Nostamp2::Main::Point\``
  and the same for `y`, `(2 errors)`. A correct program refused, the
  user blamed, the cause named nowhere.
* DOORS + mutation (`.objcmp/cryo-N2-doors-nostamp.exe`): the same two
  errors AND `error[E0900]: 138 type declaration(s) reached a consumer
  with no registration stamped; first consumed at type_resolution/struct
  methods`, `(3 errors)` - 138 being every struct the probe's modules
  declare, counted at each reader reached before the stage refused.
* DOORS, clean (`.objcmp/cryo-N3-doors.exe`): both probes `Compiled`,
  exit 7.

#### The measurement

The door is its own instrument: with the report unconditional, any
build in which a reader met an unstamped node prints E0900. Over the
clean tree: `make lsp-check` → `lsp-gate: OK -- compiled 264 module(s)
… 0 errors`; `make cross-check` → `cross-check: OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu:
runtime 10 module(s) in 5 tier(s), stdlib 154 module(s), compiler 243
module(s), tools/CryoLSP 264 module(s); 0 errors`; `hash-tree.sh N` →
examples `# objects: 1126  fails: 0`, tests `OVERALL FAIL (unit: ok;
compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 62 passed, 2 failed)` - the two
§8.223 names and nothing else; `grep -c E0900` over all three logs → 0.
That is §8.225's 0 `NOSTAMP` / 0 `BOTHINV` over 104,578 asks and
§8.228's 0 `NOSTAMP` over 29,965, re-measured by the door itself, with
the inversion above as the control that the door can report.

Objects: **0 of 1,126 + 2,719 moved** (`comm -3` of halves `M` and `N`,
examples and tests). `lane-check` unchanged (the door calls
`type_of_def(d)` inside the index; no new unwrap): `OK -- LOOKUP = 13,
LOOKUP_OTHER = 62, REGISTER = 84, LOOKUP_ROUTED = 41, … DEFID_UNWRAP =
36`. D23's `.require("` count stays 14; the 29 doors are counted by
`grep -rho 'type_of_decl(' compiler/src --include=*.cryo | wc -l` → 30
(29 readers + the definition).

`scripts/ns-migration/8.231/doors_tdecl.py` produces the tree
(re-applied over a checkout and diffed against the built tree:
identical).

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `resolver/res.cryo`,
`instance.cryo`, the eight reader files, `scripts/ns-migration/8.231/`.

**Tally: 75 shadowed, 75 old paths deleted, 75 at zero; 118 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: 29 silent arms are doors; nothing deleted).

### 8.232 `register_methods` takes the owner TYPE and the index derives the key from its own reverse map: 9 of 13 callers hand over the `TypeRef` they hold (130,001 asks, 129,711 `AGREE`); the 4 whose owner the index cannot name stay on a key door named for what it is - an `async` owner's instance, a spec registered before its type, the D18 head; and `register_decl_in_index`'s six bare-name mappings, every one of 38,974 a duplicate of the stage's, are deleted - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

`decl_type_key` had 29 callers, all registration-side (§8.228). Five
were `register_decl_in_index`'s arms deriving a declaration's key a
second time - the type-declaration stage had derived it, registered
under it and stamped the node - to feed two registrars: `register_methods(key,
…)` and `register_name_mapping(bare, key)`. The registrar that takes a
key is what makes the caller derive one; a registrar that takes what
the caller HOLDS makes the derivation unnecessary. What every caller
holds is a type: the declaration arms hold `node.def` (the stamp, so
`type_of_decl`), the synthesizers hold the `TypeRef` they registered a
line earlier, the injector holds `spec_type`, the spec impl walk holds
`entry.specialized_type`. The index holds the reverse map
(`lookup_type_name`), so the key a type is registered under is the
index's to answer and nobody else's to guess.

#### The measurement

`rm_tref.py --shadow`: at all 13 `register_methods` callers, the old key
beside `lookup_type_name(<the TypeRef in hand>)` (`RM`: `AGREE`,
`KEYINV`, `OWNERINV`, `NONAME`, `DISAGREE`); at the six
`register_name_mapping` arms, whether the pair is already held (`NM`:
`DUP`/`NEW`). Six halves (`corpus2.sh s4`, `.objcmp/s4-lines.txt`,
168,975 lines; failing halves 1, the §8.223 compile_fail project that
builds, as at every half since `80f51c3c`):

* **`NM`: 38,974, every one `DUP`** (`nm_struct` 21,037, `nm_trait`
  9,565, `nm_enum` 8,235, `nm_class` 132, `nm_union` 5; the alias arm
  0 - no alias reaches `register_decl_in_index` under its condition).
  The stage writes the same pair for the same node under the same
  condition (`pass_registry.cryo`'s six arms), and the index dedupes.
  Six calls that registered nothing: deleted, with the five keys that
  fed only them (the enum and alias arms are gone whole; the trait arm
  keeps its key for `register_method`'s bare-name twin, D24's).
* **`RM`: 130,001 - 129,711 `AGREE`, 289 `NONAME`, 1 `OWNERINV`, 0
  `DISAGREE`, 0 `KEYINV`.** Nine sites agree at every ask (`tr_struct`
  21,043, `tr_union` 6, `tr_class` 132, the injector's 5,916, the spec
  impl walk's 31,945, the future's `poll` 746, the closure's 44, and
  the impl-block site's 68,581 of 68,582). Three shapes do not, and
  they are findings rather than conversions:
  - **`async/repoint method`: 206 `NONAME` of 392.** `owner.ty` is the
    owner INSTANCE (`BufStream<S>` with its parameters, 167;
    `Http2Connection` 11, `WebSocket` 7, seven test owners), built by
    `async_owner_instance` and never registered; `owner.qname` is the
    template's key. The index cannot name the instance, so the
    registration must go by the key until `AsyncOwner` carries the
    registered type beside the instance (it is handed both).
  - **`mono/spec method on inherent owner` 65 and `on impl` 18
    `NONAME`.** `call_specializer` registers a spec method under the
    ARENA's name for the receiver (`arena.get_qualified_name(recv_type)`:
    `NonNull<h>` 49, `String<GlobalAlloc>` 32, `Array<i_N, GlobalAlloc>`
    1, a test's `GgTf<i>` 1) for a specialization the index holds no
    type for at that moment - registered before, or without, the
    injector's `register_type`. The method key exists where the type
    key does not; a reader asking `Type::method` finds it, a reader
    asking the type does not. The second store answering where the
    first cannot is the shape D1 exists to close; not this entry's.
  - **`type_resolution/register impl methods`: 1 `OWNERINV`**, key `int`
    - the D18 alias-keyword head, in `E0308_primitive_alias_duplicate`,
    a negative. `impl_owner` answers nothing for a head the name layer
    leaves `Pending`; the key is its spelling. D18's, ruled, unbuilt.

#### The change

* `DeclarationIndex::register_methods(owner: TypeRef, methods, intern,
  arena, site)`: `lookup_type_name(owner)` is the key; a type the index
  cannot name records `record_unregistered_def(site)` and registers
  nothing - a key guessed there would be a second registration under a
  name no reader asks. It delegates to `register_methods_by_key(key,
  …)`, the previous body under a name that says what it is, kept for
  the four callers above and counted by `REGISTER`.
* The nine callers pass the type: `register_decl_in_index`'s three arms
  `type_of_decl(node.def, site)` (the §8.231 door, so an unstamped
  clone reaching this walk is reported), `SpecInjector` `spec_type` ×3,
  the spec impl walk `entry.specialized_type`, `async_lower`'s future
  `struct_ref`, `lambda_synth`'s `struct_ref`.
* The six `register_name_mapping` calls and five `decl_type_key`
  derivations in `register_decl_in_index` are deleted. `decl_type_key`
  callers 29 → **24**: the stage's 12 (6 the collision pre-walk, 6 the
  registrations), type resolution's 8 (the trait arm's key for
  `register_method`, `resolve_method_signatures`' three owner keys,
  `register_trait_decl`'s, the three inline-signature owner keys),
  specialization's 3, the async mint.

#### Gates

`make lsp-check` → `lsp-gate: OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors`;
`make cross-check` → `cross-check: OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu: … 0 errors`;
`hash-tree.sh O` → examples `# objects: 1126  fails: 0`, tests `OVERALL
FAIL (unit: ok; compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 62 passed, 2
failed)` - the two §8.223 names; **0 of 1,126 + 2,719 objects moved**
(`comm -3` of halves `N` and `O`); 0 E0900 in any log. `lane-check`:
`REGISTER` 84 → **69** (`type_resolution` 27 → 18, `specialization` 7 →
3, `async_lower` 7 → 6, `lambda_synth` 3 → 2: −9 registrations by type,
−6 mappings), every other row unmoved; re-pinned. §0: `type_of_decl(`
30 → 33, `register_name_mapping(` 13 → 7, `decl_type_key` in
`type_resolution.cryo` 15 → 10, `record_unregistered_def` in the index
3 → 4.

`scripts/ns-migration/8.232/rm_tref.py` produces the tree; `--shadow`
the instrumented one.

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo`,
`passes/specialization.cryo`, `mono/call_specializer.cryo`,
`sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`, the lane golden,
`scripts/ns-migration/8.232/`.

**Tally: 76 shadowed, 76 old paths deleted, 76 at zero; 124 artifacts
gone** (+1 lane, the re-derived registration key at nine method
registrations; +6 artifacts, the duplicate name mappings).

### 8.233 D24 TAKEN and §8.223 built as one reshape: the trait-impl registry is ONE table of heads keyed by the trait's identity and the target's key, a LIST per key, and ONE selector unifies a head's written target arguments with the subject's; `impl_concrete_arg_selects_impl` exits 12 where the pin exits 22 and `impl_concrete_arg_filters_impl` is E0358 where the pin builds - `make test` is no longer red by design - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

Two tables and a set: the bare `trait_impls` keyed by `(trait leaf or
written root, target name)` and written under the head's written target
AND its key by stage 3, under the canonical target by type resolution,
under the specialization's name by the spec walk and under the future
struct's by the async lowering, "latest impl wins"; the typed
`trait_impls_typed` keyed by `(trait leaf, template qualified-name id)`
behind `precise_trait_leaf`, with a bare fallback; and, over them, five
readers each asking in its own way - `resolve_trait_impl_for_type` (10
callers, a leaf in hand), `lookup_trait_impl` (6), `impl_target_rank` (3
scans of the whole table), `traits_implemented_by` (9), the two mono scans
by `impl_targets`.  One slot per `(leaf, template)` is what §8.223
measured as a miscompile (two heads differing in a concrete argument
collapse; a head for `Wrap<T, Alpha>` answers for `Wrap<i32, Beta>`),
what §8.212 measured as D24's collapse (two same-leaf traits for one
type), and - found here - what folded `From<i8>` and `From<u8>` for one
`u64` to whichever registered last.

#### What is there now

* **One table.**  `GenericRegistry::trait_heads`, `TraitImplHead {
  trait_id, target_key, block }`, indexed by `(trait identity, target
  key)` to a LIST in registration order; `register_trait_impl(trait_id,
  target_key, block)` keeps a block once per key.  Four writers, all by
  identity: TemplateRegistration (`TypeAnnotation::trait_identity` of the
  head, `node.target_key`), type resolution's arm (the same head, for a
  clone routed there after stage 3), the spec walk (under the
  specialization's name), the async lowering (the future's `Future`).
* **One selector, in two halves as Rust has them.**  Candidate assembly
  in the registry: `heads_for(trait_id, subject)` is the clones the
  monomorphizer placed under the subject when it is a specialization
  with a name of its own, else the written heads under its template key
  whose target arguments UNIFY with the subject's (`head_matches` /
  `annotation_unifies`: a `Res::GenericParam` argument binds, a `Def` or
  `PrimTy` one must be that type by the arena's template key, a nested
  `Generic` recursively, a `Pointer`/`Reference` through the arena's; a
  subject argument that is still abstract cannot refute a concrete one,
  as a where-bound over an abstract argument is deferred).
  `trait_impls_of(subject)` is every such head of every trait;
  `template_head_for` / `template_trait_impls_of` are the written heads
  only, for the three projection readers that substitute a head's written
  trait arguments and must not see a clone.  Confirmation in the checker:
  `TraitChecker::select_impl(trait_id, subject, depth)` is the first
  candidate whose where-clause holds (`impl_bounds_hold`, the tail of the
  old `type_implements_trait`), `impls_of(subject)` every one; a placed
  clone applies outright (`impl_applies`), because mono confirmed its
  bounds when it placed it and substituted them away on the clone - the
  shadow's first cut checked a clone's bounds and refused `CopiedIter`'s
  `Iterator` clone whose `where I: Iterator<T*>` the checker cannot bind.
* **The operator traits are identities.**  `is_wellknown_trait_path`
  claims `std::core::ops::{Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Rem, Neg, Not, BitNot,
  BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor, Shl, Shr, Deref, Index}` and `std::core::cmp::{Eq,
  Ord}` beside the markers, `Drop` and `Future`; the desugars in
  `sema.cryo` and `member_resolver.cryo` ask `wellknown(leaf)` and select
  by it, as Rust's `+` is `core::ops::Add` and a user trait spelled `Add`
  overloads nothing.  Every operator-trait leaf in the tree is declared
  exactly once, in the stdlib (`grep -rn 'trait (Add|Sub|...|Index)\b'
  stdlib tests examples tools compiler/src --include=*.cryo`), so no
  program's binding moves.  The claim moves to the type-declaration
  stage (`pass_registry.cryo`), where the identity is minted, so an
  ownership query of a module resolved before `std::core::drop`'s asks
  by an identity that exists; the shadow's 5,660,398 `Drop` asks never
  met the hole, but the old leaf lookup did not depend on the claim and
  the new one does.
* **Every reader through the selector.**  `type_implements_trait` (the
  Drop-inherent arm kept for a type with no `Drop` head at all),
  `type_satisfies_opaque_bound` (`heads_for` non-empty as the lenient
  fallback), `diagnose_method_bounds_failure` (returns the identity; the
  E0358 renders its leaf as the tie report does), `type_has_drop_impl`
  (`heads_for(wellknown("Drop"))`); sema's `check_method_call_arg_types`
  and `select_method` over `impls_of(base_ref)` - the receiver's `TypeRef`
  threaded through `select_method` - `find_method_in_trait_impls`,
  `find_generic_method_in_trait_impls`, `lookup_method_through_trait_impls`
  (by subject now; 97 of 1,275 asks answer, every one the same by
  identity as by leaf), `find_generic_trait_default`,
  `projection_default_unavailable`, the projection reducer,
  `proj_concrete_trait_args_for`; mono's
  `find_trait_impl_method_for_target` and `find_self_returning_default`
  (the two-pass scans and `impl_targets` deleted), `concrete_trait_args_for`;
  `TypeResolver`'s assoc-projection reader.  The two Item bound checks
  (sema's `projection_bound_fails`, type resolution's
  `default_method_applies_to_impl`) ask the selector with the Item's TYPE
  read off its stamp (`item_type_of`: `type_of_def(d)` for a declaration,
  `resolve_primitive` for a primitive) and the bound's `TraitRef::identity()`;
  `name_implements`, `name_implements_trait`, `head_type_key` and sema's
  `ann_head_key` are deleted.
* **The fix's two mechanisms.**  Mono's `filter_bounds_violating_impls`
  takes the instantiation's arguments and drops a head whose written
  arguments do not unify (`head_matches_args`), beside the where-clause
  filter - so `Wrap<i32, Beta>` gets only `Wrap<T, Beta>`'s clone and
  exits 12.  Sema's `resolve_method_call` gates the declaration index's
  answer on `MethodBinder::trait_method_unavailable(recv, name)`: a method
  that only trait impl heads of the template declare, none of which
  `impls_of` selects for this instantiation, is no method - the index
  holds every head's methods under the template's key and only the
  selection can tell them apart - so `wb.show()` is E0358 at the call.
* **A synthesized node born stamped.**  The selector's `require` on a
  head argument found the async lowering's `generic_param_anns` minting
  `Fut<T, …>`'s parameter annotations `Pending`: 71 per example, 991 over
  the unit suite (`error[E0900]: 71 path-bearing node(s) ... first
  required at generic_registry:impl head argument`, `.objcmp/w1-fail.log`).
  The name layer stamps a written parameter `Res::GenericParam`; the
  synthesizer stamps its own the same way now, and the second run reads
  0.

### 8.234 `scope_owner_key` answers a registered owner or nothing: the spelling arms - a module's `Def`, an `Err`, a `Pending` and a `TypeRelative(GenericParam)` base all answered `scope.scope_name` - are deleted; 229,475 answers over six halves, 0 bound anything a build keeps - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

The static-call owner key (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`) is asked by five
readers - the callee hint for expected-type propagation
(`lookup_callee_function_type`), `resolve_scope_call`'s type lane, the
template-return fallback, `find_static_method_template` and the scope-call
argument check.  It answered the substituter's `spec_owner` by arena id,
then the stamp's base name for a `TypeRelative(Def | PrimTy)`, and **the
written spelling for everything else**: `Res::Def` (a module), `Err`, a
slot never answered, and the `GenericParam` base of a `TypeRelative`.
§8.217 deleted the module-suffix scan that consumed a module's spelling
and left this producer, and audit 11 named it the "drained lane,
uncounted replacement" shape: nothing measured which stamps reached the
arm or whether the spelling it answered ever bound anything.  The
function's own comment said a module qualifier "is not a type-owner claim,
and this does not manufacture one" while the code manufactured one.

#### What is there now

`scope_owner_key` returns `SymbolStr::empty()` for every stamp that names
no type owner.  A type parameter's spelling is never a registration key:
the substituter that replaces `T` with the instantiation's argument records
that argument on `spec_owner` (`ASTTypeSubstituter::visit(ScopeResolutionNode)`,
from `subst.replacements[i]`, one per parameter by construction) and the
first arm answers it by arena id.  A module qualifier has no owner key;
its member is the module lane's, from the stamp.  A segment nothing in
the program owns has no key, because a lookup by its spelling can only
find a registration itself keyed by a bare spelling.  The callee hint
refuses a module segment outright (`Res::Def` → no hint; the lane that
owns it, `lookup_module_qualified_param_types`, is asked next by
`resolve_call` and reads the same `lookup_func_type_exact` table under the
module's canonical name), so no spelling is probed for a module there.
Every consumer of the key tolerates the empty symbol - `get_template`,
`lookup_type`, `lookup_method_return`, `resolve_method_owner` are map
misses on id 0, and `InternTable::resolve` gives `""`.

#### Measured

The shadow tree (`scripts/ns-migration/8.234/shadow.patch` over
`fd3756af`: `shadow_sok` prints the stamp kind, the key and whether the
caller's lookup under that key hit, at all five readers) over the six
halves, `corpus2.sh x1`, **2,509,947 lines**, `failing halves: 0`
(`cut -f4,5,6,10 .objcmp/x1-lines.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`,
`.objcmp/x1-tab.txt`):

| stamp reaching the spelling arms | answers | bound by that spelling |
|---|---:|---|
| `Def`, spelling a SUFFIX of the module's name | 227,941 (hint 130,115, static-method template 97,826) | **0** |
| `Def`, spelling the module's canonical name | 466 (hint 236 + 230) | 236 `HIT` at the hint - the key IS the canonical name, and the hint's next probe (`bare_sym`, the C-import door) is the same string; the module lane gives the same signature |
| `TypeRelative(GenericParam)`, spelling the parameter (`T::try_from`, `T::__pluck`, `T::default` in the template's own body) | 1,068 (534 + 267 + 267) | **0** - `symbolic_name_is_generic_param` stands the call down after the probes |
| `TypeRelative(GenericParam)`, spelling substituted | **0 through the arm** - 105 substituted segments, every one answered by `spec_owner` (`SPEC`; `u64::try_from`, `std::collections::str::Str::try_from`, `i32::default`) | - |
| `Err` / `Pending` | **0** | - |

The `TypeRelative(Def)` and `PrimTy` arms, which stay, answer the rest:
2,280,367 lines, of which the C-import alias is the `TRDef-other …
miss-bareHIT` shape (968 - the alias is stamped `TypeRelative(Def(alias))`
and its qualified name misses; the bare spelling hits; §9 Q2's).

Controls, `.objcmp/sok-ctl/` under the shadow compiler (`cryo check
<file> --stdlib=stdlib` from `tests/`):

* `Nope::thing(1)` prints `Pending` at the hint, the call and the
  template lookup, hits nothing, and is E0233 - the instrument reports
  the kind the corpus never produced.
* `implement int { static seven() }` + `int::seven()` prints `Pending …
  HIT` at the hint, `static` at the call, `HIT1` at the argument check:
  the ONE spelling that binds, because the D18 head registers its methods
  under the bare key `int` and `int` is an alias keyword the name layer
  leaves unanswered.  The build is refused by E0900 (27 unanswered slots)
  either way, so the arm never bound a program that built.  Under the
  clean tree the same call is still bound - by
  `try_resolve_cimport_function`'s `lookup_func_return("int::seven")`, the
  spelling-keyed C-import door, which is Q2's lane and not this one; E0900
  still refuses it.
* `make<T>() where T: Default { T::default() }` instantiated at
  `Wrap<Wrap<i32>>` and `i32` (the case a `spec_owner` the index cannot
  name would reach the spelling arm): every substituted segment answers
  `SPEC` - `CryoTests::SokSpec::4Wrap$LN$L9CryoTests.7SokSpec.4Wrap$Li$G$G$G`
  named by the index - and 0 reach the arm.

#### Objects and gates

`hash-tree.sh Q` against half `P` (`fd3756af`): examples **0 of 1,126**
(`comm -3 .objcmp/ex-P.s .objcmp/ex-Q.s`), tests **0 of 2,665**

PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 64 passed)`, roster

compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490 warning(s)` (`.objcmp/x2-lsp.log`).
`make cross-check`: `OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu … 0 errors`
(`.objcmp/x2-cross.log`).  `lane-check` unmoved.  `ns-status-check`: the
`require_scope_res(` row 15 → 16 (the hint's module refusal), the

Left for Q2: the callee hint's `bare_sym` probe and

Outside the ledger: `compiler/src/compiler/sema/call_resolver.cryo`;

### 8.235 `AsyncOwner` carries the owner's REGISTERED type and the async repoint registers by it (392 of 392 named, where the instance named 186); the trait-impl arm registers by `impl_owner` with the alias-keyword head alone on the key door; the two mono spec-method sites are an ORDERING defect - 83 keys the index cannot name at registration, every one registered later by the injection pass - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.232 left `register_methods_by_key` four callers because the index could
not name their owner.  Two were findings and one was D18's:

* `async_lower`'s `repoint_method` registered under `owner.qname`, a key
  sema's declare pass derived (`target_key(arena)` for an impl,
  `def.qualified_name()` for a declaration) and carried on `AsyncOwner`
  beside `ty` - which is the owner INSTANCE `async_owner_instance` builds
  for a generic owner (`BufStream<S>` over its own parameters), a type the
  index never registered.  206 of 392 asks `NONAME` by the instance.
* `call_specializer`'s two spec-method registrations key by the arena's
  name for the receiver (`impl_node.target_key`, `arena.get_qualified_name
  (recv_type)`); 83 asks named a type the index did not hold.  §8.232 asked
  WHY before anyone touched it: order, or never injected.
* `type_resolution`'s trait-impl arm registered under `canonical_target`
  (`node.target_key`), whose one disagreement with `impl_owner` is the D18
  head (`implement trait Show for int`): stamped by nothing, its spelling
  its only key, ruled and unbuilt.

#### Measured

The shadow (`scripts/ns-migration/8.235/shadow.patch` over `7e2541a2`)
over the six halves, `corpus2.sh x3`, **2,139 lines**, `failing halves: 0`
(`.objcmp/x3-lines.txt`; `awk -F'\t' '$3=="RPT"' | cut -f4,7,8`, `'$3=="SPO"'
| cut -f4,5,8,9,11,12`, `'$3=="SPOEND"' | cut -f5`):

| instrument | asks | result |
|---|---:|---|
| `RPT` - the repoint: `lookup_type_name(owner.decl)` beside `owner.qname` | 392 | **392 `AGREE`**, 0 `NONAME`: 186 where `ty` is the declaration itself, 206 where `ty` is the instance the index cannot name (`inst-noname`) and `decl` is named |
| `SPO` - the mono sites: the index's name for `recv_type` beside the key, the type's kind, and whether the index holds ANY type under the key (`fwd-*`) | 1,663 | 1,099 `AGREE` (`fwd-same`); **83 `NONAME` with a key, every one `fwd-none`** (`NonNull<u8>` 49, `String<GlobalAlloc>` 32, `Array<i64, GlobalAlloc>` 1, a test's `GgTf<i32>` 1) - a concrete `Struct` the index holds no type for at that moment; 480 `NONAME` with an EMPTY key (an unmaterialized `InstantiatedType`, `get_qualified_name` invalid: the site returns before registering, the `pin_spec_entry` "not keyed" shape already documented); 1 `fwd-OTHERREF` (`TakeIter`, an unmaterialized instantiation whose key the index holds for the struct) |
| `SPOEND` - at the build's end, whether each `NONAME` key holds a type | 84 | **84 `registered-later`, 0 `NEVER`** |

So the mono sites are **order**: `call_specializer` registers a spec's
methods in the mono round that materializes them, and the spec TYPE is
registered by `SpecializationPasses` (`SpecInjector::register` →
`register_type(arena_qname, spec_type)`) when the pass walks the entries
afterwards - under the same key, so the methods land where the type will
be, but at a moment the index cannot yet name the owner.  Converting the
two sites to `register_methods(TypeRef)` needs the type registered when
the entry is PLACED, not when the pass walks it; that is a pipeline
reorder and its own unit, recorded here and not built.

The trait-impl arm needs no new measurement: §8.232's 68,582 asks are
68,581 `AGREE` and the one `OWNERINV` is the `int` head.

#### What is there now

* `AsyncOwner { method, ty, decl, written, params, impl_node }`: `decl` is
  the owner's registered type, exactly what the declare pass was handed
  (`type_of_decl(node.def)` for a declaration, `impl_owner(ib)` for an
  impl); `written` is the owner as the source spelled it (a declaration's
  `name`, an impl's `target_type`), text for the future's minted name and
  the refusal of an undeclarable method, never a key.  `qname` is deleted
  with the three `def.qualified_name()` and one `target_key(arena)`
  derivations that fed it.  The future's minted name is
  `leaf(written)$method`, which is the leaf the canonical key gave (a
  written path ends in the type's leaf).
* `repoint_method` asks the index by the type: `reset_method_overloads
  (owner.decl, name, intern)` - new on `DeclarationIndex`, the type-keyed
  twin of `reset_function_overloads`, deriving the combined key from its
  own reverse map - then `register_methods(owner.decl, …,
  "async_lower/repoint method")`.  `AsyncLower::reset_method_overloads`
  is deleted.
* The trait-impl arm dispatches on what the head is: an alias-keyword head
  (`ResBase::is_alias_keyword(target_type)`) registers by its spelling
  through `register_methods_by_key` - D18's door, held for exactly that
  population and nothing wider - and every other head by
  `register_methods(impl_owner(node, …), …)`.  `E0308_primitive_alias_
  duplicate` still reports E0308 (the coherence check precedes the
  registration); a control `implement int { static seven() }` still
  answers `i32::seven()` with E0233, as before.
* `register_methods_by_key` has three callers: the two mono sites (order,
  above) and D18's door.

The refusal `cannot resolve the owner type `%s` of `async` method …`
names the written owner now where it named the derived key; the path is
reached only for a head `impl_owner` cannot type (a `Pending` head, D18's;
an unregistered declaration, which the door reports), and for the `int`
head the two spellings are one.

**New public API names, for Jake**: `DeclarationIndex::reset_method_overloads
(owner: TypeRef, method: SymbolStr, intern)`; `AsyncOwner::{decl, written}`
(fields).

#### Objects and gates

`hash-tree.sh S` against half `Q` (`7e2541a2`): examples **0 of 1,126**,
tests **0 of 2,665** (`comm -3 .objcmp/ex-Q.s .objcmp/ex-S.s`; `comm -3
.objcmp/t-Q.s .objcmp/t-S.s`).  `make test-census`: `OVERALL PASS (unit:
ok; compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 64 passed)` (`.objcmp/x4-census.log`).
`make lsp-check`: `OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490 warning(s)`
(`.objcmp/x4-lsp.log`).  `make cross-check`: `OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu …
0 errors` (`.objcmp/x4-cross.log`).  `lane-check`: `REGISTER` 69 → **68**
(`async_lower` 6 → 5), `DEFID_UNWRAP` 35 → **32** (`sema.cryo` 4 → 1),
re-pinned; a first cut read `LOOKUP_OTHER` 62 → 64 for two
`lookup_type_name(owner.decl)` reads in `async_lower` and the gate refused
it - the mint takes the written leaf and the reset moved into the index,
where the key is derived once.  `ns-status-check`: the `DEFID_UNWRAP` row
35 → 32.

Outside the ledger: `sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/sema.cryo`,
`decl_index.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo`, `tests/lane-baseline.txt`,
`scripts/ns-migration/8.235/` (`shadow.patch`, README row).

### 8.236 The closure-arg specialization's identifier goes through the one mangler: `mint_closure_spec_name` spelled arena ids (`apply__cl_2985`), so three objects moved on every session that created a type earlier; it is `specialized_identifier(orig, closure types)` now, and a mutation that shifts every arena id moves the old symbol and not the new - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

`LambdaSynth::mint_closure_spec_name` named a closure-arg specialization
`<orig>__cl_<id>_<id>…` with the ARENA ID of each closure type - a number
that depends on how many types the compiler created before it, so a
change anywhere that allocates one more type renames the symbol.  That is
why `Lambdas.o`, `MoveLambda.o` and `examples/13-closures/Main.o` moved
in §8.216 and §8.233 ("every `__cl_NNNN` id +1") and why every object
comparison since has had to fold the ids to read 0.  Audit 11 lists it as
one of mono's two symbol mints outside registration.
`MangledName::specialized_identifier` says no call site outside its module
may invent a specialization-name format; this one had.  Nothing reads the
`__cl` form: 0 in `compiler/src`, `tools`, `tests` (`grep -rn '__cl'`).

#### What is there now

The identifier is `MangledName::specialized_identifier(orig, &closure_tys)`,
the encoding every specialization carries: `apply` over `Main::__Closure_0`
is `5apply$LN$L4Main.11__Closure_0$G$G`, and the symbol
`C$4Main.345apply$LN$L4Main.11__Closure_0$G$G$FN$L4Main.11__Closure_0$G_i$Ri`
- the same shape a generic function's spec has today
(`C$3std.11collections.5array.3513sort_range_by$LN$L4Main.4Todo$G$G$F…`).  A
closure type's name is its module and a per-build counter
(`mint_closure_name`), a function of the source.

#### Measured

The pair, on `examples/13-closures/…/Main.o` (`sha256sum`), with an arena
mutation that allocates one unrelated extra type on every pointer-type
miss (`get_pointer_to_q`, so every later id shifts):

| mint | unshifted | shifted |
|---|---|---|
| OLD (`fd3756af`'s) | `1e8990c7958d7696` (half `S`) | **`a6d4a32e5508e878`** - moved; `apply__cl_3086` where `S` held another id |
| NEW | `7aa7ddf1a4c2e049` | `7aa7ddf1a4c2e049` - unmoved |

`hash-tree.sh T` against half `S` (`e326c7ed`): examples **1 of 1,126**,
tests **2 of 2,665** - exactly `13-closures/Main.o`, `Lambdas.o`,
`MoveLambda.o`, the three closure-spec objects, renamed once
(`comm -3 .objcmp/ex-S.s .objcmp/ex-T.s`; `comm -3 .objcmp/t-S.s
.objcmp/t-T.s`).  `make test-census`: `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok;
compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 64 passed)` (`.objcmp/x5-census.log`).
`make lsp-check`: `OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490 warning(s)`
(`.objcmp/x5-lsp.log`).  `make cross-check`: `OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu … 0
errors` (`.objcmp/x5-cross.log`).  `lane-check` unmoved.

Also here: the stale comment on `collect_bare_type_names`
(`type_resolution.cryo`) that named the index's `module_types` table, deleted
in §8.218, says what the pool is and why without the table.

Not this entry's: `mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` (the other mint audit 11
names) computes the symbol a spec method WILL be emitted under as the key
`mark_method_spec` records it by - a derivation, not an invention, but it
is still a mangle outside registration; and the spec's `$O`-indexed
`C$cl$` form for a closure (`cryo-mangling-spec.md` §11) is not what the
tree emits for a closure type or its specializations, which is a spec-vs-
code question for Jake.

### 8.237 `TraitRef::identity()` is a door: the unstamped arm that answered the written leaf entered 0 times over six halves and records a missing answer now; and `BoundedParamType`'s leaf-matched operator arm is NOT a lane - the kind is uninhabited and its consumers are kept by ruling - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.233 left two things open here.  `TraitRef::identity()` answered
`resolved_name` when the name layer had stamped the bound and **the
written leaf otherwise** - "a door with no tally": 22 readers, none able
to tell a stamped identity from a spelling.  And `bounded_param_trait` /
`trait_ref_matching` (`sema.cryo`) matched a bounded parameter's bound to
the operator's trait by LEAF, where §8.233 had made the concrete-type arm
ask by the claimed identity.

#### Measured

* **`identity()`'s fallback: 0 entries over the six halves** (a print at the
  arm, `scripts/ns-migration/8.237/shadow.patch` over `b3b36ca6`,
  `corpus2.sh x7`: `SHADOW lines … : 0`, `failing halves: 0`).  The
  instrument fires: `function f<T>(a: T) -> T where T: Nope` prints 2
  `TRID leaf` lines (`.objcmp/sok-ctl/nobound.cryo`).  Every written bound
  is stamped by `stamp_trait_ref_identity`, every synthesized one by its
  synthesizer (§8.233's `generic_param_anns` fix was the last hole), and
  no negative in the suite writes a bound naming nothing.
* **The bounded-parameter arm is dead by construction, and kept by
  ruling.**  `TypeArena::create_bounded_param` has no caller and `new
  BoundedParamType` no other site (`grep -rn 'create_bounded_param('
  compiler/src` → the definition alone), since `f3082103` deleted the
  inline `<T: Bound>` form, the kind's only producer.  A shadow at the
  operator desugar's bounded arm printed 0 lines on hello-world before the
  grep said why.  That commit's own entry rules the ~45 consumer sites
  (mangling, codegen, mono, `call_resolver`, `member_resolver`,
  `method_binding`, the LSP's hover) **kept**: "a zero needs a control
  proving it is not starvation, and no such control can exist once the
  only inhabiting syntax is gone", pending the ruling that extends `where`
  to type declarations, which may feed the kind rather than retire it.
  So the leaf match §8.233 named is a consumer of an uninhabited kind -
  neither a lane to shadow nor a deletion for a worker.  Recorded, not
  touched.

#### What is there now

`identity()` answers `resolved_name` or nothing; the unstamped arm records
`record_pending_bug("trait bound identity")` and returns the empty symbol,
so a consumer stops as it would for a bound nothing satisfies, and a
build that reported nothing else is refused at its end by the existing
E0900 flush.  The control's diagnostics are unchanged under the door
(`E0306: the trait bound `i32: Nope` is not satisfied`, then E0200 - E0306
renders the bound from its written path), and the E0900 stays quiet
behind them as every pending tally does.

#### Objects and gates

`hash-tree.sh U` against half `T` (`b3b36ca6`): examples **0 of 1,126**,
tests **0 of 2,665** (`comm -3 .objcmp/ex-T.s .objcmp/ex-U.s`; `comm -3
.objcmp/t-T.s .objcmp/t-U.s`).  `make test-census`: `OVERALL PASS (unit:
ok; compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 64 passed)` (`.objcmp/x7-census.log`).
`make lsp-check`: `OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490 warning(s)`
(`.objcmp/x7-lsp.log`).  `make cross-check`: `OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu …
0 errors` (`.objcmp/x7-cross.log`).  `lane-check` unmoved.

Outside the ledger: `AST/_module.cryo`; `scripts/ns-migration/8.237/`
(`shadow.patch`, README row).

### 8.238 A specialized type is registered when its entry is placed, by the monomorphizer, so the two spec-method sites register by the receiver's TYPE: 1,662 of 1,663 named at registration (§8.235's 83 `NONAME` keys and its 480 empty keys were the same ordering seen from two sides), the one unnamed receiver is an instantiation the worklist has not drained and is deferred by kind, and `register_methods_by_key` has one caller - D18's door - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.235 measured the two `call_specializer` registrations
(`register_spec_method_in_di`, `_inherent`) as an ORDERING defect: a
generic method materialized on a specialized receiver was registered
under the receiver's KEY (`impl_node.target_key`, `arena.get_qualified_
name(recv_type)`) because the receiver's type was not in the index yet -
`SpecInjector::register` wrote it when `run_generic_expression_resolution`
walked the entries after the module's monomorphization.  83 keys named no
type at that moment, every one registered later; 480 more registrations
had an EMPTY key and were skipped at the site altogether.

#### Measured

The conversion with a print at both sites (`scripts/ns-migration/8.238/
shadow.patch` over `2e3e7f42`, `corpus2.sh y1`, `.objcmp/y1-lines.txt`,
**1,663** `SPO` lines - §8.235's count exactly - `failing halves: 0`,
`OVERALL PASS … projects: 64 passed`; `cut -f4,5,7,8,9,10 | sort | uniq -c`):

| verdict | rows | what they are |
|---|---:|---|
| `AGREE` - the index names the receiver, the same string the old key was | **1,182** | every row that had a key: the 1,099 §8.235 named AND its 83 `NONAME` (`NonNull<u8>`, `String<GlobalAlloc>`, `Array<i64, GlobalAlloc>`, a test's `GgTf<i32>` - 574 rows under those four keys, all named now) |
| `NAMED-nokey` - the index names the receiver, the old site had no key | **480** | all `inherent`, all `String<GlobalAlloc>`, kind `InstantiatedType`, `materialized`, `arena-noname`: the receiver is the wrapper id **between the entry's placement and the populate-time flip** - `String`'s own bodies calling `this.push<T>` / `try_push<T>` during the nested-call walk.  §8.235 read these as "an unmaterialized `InstantiatedType`"; the instantiation WAS materialized (its entry placed, `has_materialized_spec` true), only the arena slot not yet flipped, which is why `get_qualified_name` answered nothing and the site returned.  The same 480 and the 83 were one ordering seen from two sides |
| `DISAGREE` | **0** | |
| `NONAME`, `DEFERRED` | **1** | `tests/unit`, the `impl` site, `std::core::iter::TakeIter`'s template block: a generic method walked on `TakeIter<Range<i32>>` before the worklist drained it - the corpus's only receiver that is an instantiation with NO entry placed.  The old site keyed it under the template's `std::core::iter::TakeIter`, "a definition nothing emits" (`pin_spec_entry`); nothing is registered there now and 0 objects moved |

**The door fires.**  With the type registration moved back to the pass
(`SpecInjector::register` registering the type, the monomorphizer not -
HEAD's ordering under the new sites), `examples/01-hello` is refused:
`error[E0900]: 7 canonical name(s) named no registered declaration; first
consumed at mono/spec inherent method` (`.objcmp/y3-mut-hello.log`; 7 =
hello's 2 old-`NONAME` + 5 in-window rows).  Under the by-key sites the
same ordering built hello green with the 2 keyed silently (§8.235's
`x3-lines.txt`).

#### What is there now

* The monomorphizer registers the specialized TYPE at the seam where its
  identity is decided - after `resolve_specialized_ast`, before the entry
  is pushed and the nested-call walk runs:
  `decl_index.register_type(qualified_spec_sym, concrete_type, …)`, the id
  stamped on the clone (`Monomorphizer::stamp_def`, `node_is_public` moved
  in from `SpecInjector`).  The name is the one this function minted, not
  asked of the arena: the slot is still an unflipped wrapper there and
  `get_qualified_name` answers nothing (the first cut asked the arena and
  registered no type at all - every example refused, `.objcmp/y1-ex10.log`
  500 errors).  `SpecInjector::register` registers what the clone CARRIES
  (its methods, the bare-name mapping) under the type the index already
  holds; it registers no type and stamps nothing.
* `register_spec_method_in_di` / `_inherent` call
  `register_methods(recv_type, …)` (sites `mono/spec impl method`,
  `mono/spec inherent method`) behind `receiver_unmaterialized`: an
  `InstantiatedType` with no entry placed (`!state.has_materialized_spec`)
  is deferred, as the method sits on the template's block and binds
  through the node once the owner exists; every other receiver is a type
  the index holds, and one it cannot name is recorded.  The 480 in-window
  registrations happen at the walk now (the pass's later registration of
  the same clone method is the same entry: `register_signature` dedupes on
  key, function type, owner and symbol); their pins are still withheld,
  because `mangled_symbol_for_spec_method`'s target is the ARENA's name
  for the receiver, empty in the window - a follow-up, recorded not built.
* `register_methods_by_key` has ONE caller: D18's alias-keyword door in
  `type_resolution.cryo`.

#### Objects and gates

### 8.239 What enters name resolution, and by which route: `resolve_path` answers 2 sites and `Resolver::lookup` - the unfiltered rib walk - answers 9, measured at 3,059,355 asks; the namespace filter binds the same symbol at every site but 417, of which 11 are a class constructor called by its name (§9 Q13); `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` - `resolve_path`'s `Def` projected to a string and re-wrapped - is deleted - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§5.2 names `resolve_path(segments, ns, scope) -> Res` as THE way into name
resolution.  Audit 11 counted its callers at 2, both one-segment, both
`Namespace::Type`, and asked what the other ways in were.  Nobody had
measured them.

The routes, enumerated (`grep -rn 'this\.resolver\.[a-z_]*(' name_resolution.cryo`;
the `Resolver`'s reading API - `lookup`, `lookup_in_module`, `lookup_prelude`,
`lookup_overloads`, `resolve_path` - has no caller outside that file):

| route | sites | what it answers |
|---|---:|---|
| `resolve_path` | 2 | the base-class name (`visit(ClassDeclNode)`); `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` in `resolver.cryo`, itself called twice by `type_spelling_res` - the annotation lane's bare leaf from the writer's module scope, and the C-import alias spelling - and projecting the `Res` to a qualified-name STRING its callers re-wrapped as `Res::Def` |
| `Resolver::lookup(name, current_scope)` - the rib walk with NO namespace filter, prelude last | 9 | the identifier (`bare_name_res`, a second `Res` builder beside `res_for_head`), the scope head (`record_resolution` + `stamp_module_scope`), the annotation's generic-parameter probe and its path head (kind checks), `new`, the struct literal, the enum pattern and the impl target (`record_resolution` for the LSP; the stamp comes from `type_spelling_res`), the constant pattern (kind check) |
| `lookup_in_module` | 7 | the rooted remainder: an import's target, a re-export's, the module lane's `walk_module_rooted_type`, an ambiguity check - the segment-after-head work §5.1 says is "resolved within what the previous segment named", which `resolve_path` hands to the type layer as `TypeRelative` and the module lane finishes here |
| `lookup_overloads` | 1 | the overload SET at a call (`record_overloads`) - a different question |

#### Measured

The nine `lookup` sites with a print (`scripts/ns-migration/8.239/shadow.patch`
over `7d6705ac`, `corpus2.sh z1`, `.objcmp/z1-lines.txt`, **3,059,355** `RP`
lines, `failing halves: 0`; the suite's two output-exclusion projects read
FAIL under a shadow that prints names, the known trap): the symbol the
unfiltered walk bound beside the one the namespace-filtered walk
`resolve_path` makes would bind (`cut -f4,5,7 | sort | uniq -c`):

| verdict | rows | |
|---|---:|---|
| `SAME` | **2,552,752** | one symbol either way |
| `NONE` | 506,186 | neither binds (a primitive, a builtin, a member sema resolves) |
| `UNF-ONLY` | **385** | the unfiltered walk bound a symbol the namespace refuses and the filtered walk found nothing: 276 scope heads binding a FIELD (`headers::push_all` inside `Response`, whose field is `headers`: 240), a parameter (`fd::`), a function (`assert::`) or a variable - every one then ignored by `stamp_module_scope` (`symbol_names_type` false) and answered by the module lane, but `record_resolution` had already sent the LSP's go-to-definition to the field; 98 annotation heads (`node::…` under a parameter `node`) the site likewise ignored; **11 identifiers in CALLEE position naming a CLASS** (`Node(1)`, `Parser(…)`), stamped `Def` today and answered by `resolve_direct_call` through the type stamp (`spelling_type`) - the value namespace refuses a `Type` symbol, so under `resolve_path` these are E0202 |
| `DIFF` | 32 | the annotation's generic-parameter probe: an enum VARIANT declared bare in the module scope (`JsonValue::String`, `::Array`) shadows the IMPORT of the same leaf; the site asked only "is it a generic parameter" and both say no, and the leaf lane then resolved the import from the module scope |
| `FIL-ONLY` | **0** | the filter never bound past a refused nearer rib to a different declaration |

So the namespace filter changes no stamp on the corpus except the 11
constructor calls, and those are a language-model question, not a
resolver's: Rust binds a tuple struct's constructor in the VALUE namespace
beside the type - two bindings, one declaration - and this symbol table
binds one `Type` symbol and cannot tell a class from a struct.  **§9 Q13.**

#### What is there now

* `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` is deleted.  Its two callers ask
  `leaf_in_module_scope(module_scope, name)` on the `NameResolver`, which
  calls `resolve_path(&[name], Namespace::Type, ScopeID { id })` and stamps
  the `Def` it answers DIRECTLY - a walk from a module scope crosses no rib
  binding a generic parameter, so the answer is a definition or nothing,
  and nothing is `Pending` as before.  The string projection was one
  `DefId::of_definition(q.qualified_name())` round trip (`DEFID_UNWRAP` 32
  → 31, `DEFID_MINT` 23 → 21).  A pure refactor by construction: the
  function answered a string exactly when `resolve_path` answered `Def`.
* The other seven `lookup` sites and `bare_name_res` are NOT converted.
  The shape that makes `resolve_path` the one door is recorded here and
  not built: (1) `resolve_path` records the span's binding for the LSP
  (`record_resolution`), since seven of the nine sites exist to feed the
  resolution map and a `Res` carries no `SymbolID`; (2) `res_for_head`
  absorbs `bare_name_res`'s classification - `Local` for a parameter and
  a function-local variable, nothing for a member kind (a method, field
  or variant symbol is named through its owner, and `module::leaf` is a
  name nothing is registered under); (3) Q13's ruling for the constructor
  call; (4) the annotation lane's two scopes - the rib chain for a generic
  parameter, the writer's MODULE scope for the leaf, because annotations
  are re-resolved under other modules' cursors - become one explicit scope
  when the site passes the annotation's own rib.  Each is measurable with
  this entry's instrument; none is a unit on its own.

#### Objects and gates

`hash-tree.sh Z` against half `Y` (`7d6705ac`): examples **0 of 1,126**,
tests **0 of 2,665** (`comm -3 .objcmp/ex-Y.s .objcmp/ex-Z.s`; `comm -3
.objcmp/t-Y.s .objcmp/t-Z.s`) - predicted, the conversion being a
refactor.  `make test` (inside `hash-tree.sh`): `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok;
compile-fail: 193 passed; projects: 64 passed)` (`.objcmp/t-Z.txt.log`).
`make lsp-check`: `OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490 warning(s)`
(`.objcmp/z2-lsp.log`).  `make cross-check`: `OK -- x86_64-pc-linux-gnu …
0 errors` (`.objcmp/z2-cross.log`).  `lane-check`: `DEFID_MINT` 23 → **21**,
`DEFID_UNWRAP` 32 → **31**, re-pinned.  `ns-status-check`: the
`DEFID_UNWRAP` row 32 → 31; the `resolve_path` row re-worded with the
route table and three new checks; §5.2's and §7's status blocks corrected
(the lane golden has had ten buckets since §8.230, both said eight).

Outside the ledger: `resolver/resolver.cryo`, `resolver/name_resolution.cryo`,
`tests/lane-baseline.txt`, `scripts/ns-migration/8.239/` (`shadow.patch`,
README row).

**Tally: 82 shadowed, 82 old paths deleted, 82 at zero; 152 artifacts
gone** (+1 artifact, `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from`).

### 8.240 A placed specialization has ONE registrar: the monomorphizer registers the type, its bare-name mapping, the methods it carries and its impl blocks' at the seam, and the pass registers nothing for a named specialization - its four `register_methods` calls found every method already registered (190,183 of 218,521 over six halves) or skipped by the same guard at both writers (28,338: self-returning defaults, and `Result<T, E>::as_ref` whose return is unresolved at either moment) - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.238 moved the specialized TYPE's registration to the monomorphizer's
seam and left the methods where they were: `SpecInjector::register`'s
struct / union / class arms registering the clone's inline methods,
`register_spec`'s loop registering each cloned impl block's, and the
bare-name mapping (`register_name_mapping(spec_name, arena_qname)`), all
in the pass that walks the entries after the module's monomorphization.
Two writers for one placed entry - and since §8.238 the pass's write of
every generic-method spec materialized at the walk was a second
registration of an entry already stamped.

Audit 11's "dead index API" was checked on the way here and is not dead:
`global_slot` is the private funnel of six live accessors
(`is_global_thread_local`, `global_extern_symbol`, `find_global_in_
namespace`, `find_global_by_qualified`, `record_global_extern_symbol`,
`mark_global_thread_local` - 2/2/2/1/2/1 external readers); `resolved_or`
and `lookup_qualified_alternatives` are the LSP's `bare_alts` lane, LIVE by
the ruling on §0's two `bare_alts` rows and pinned there.  The stale
`module_types` comment went in §8.236.  Nothing to delete; the audit's
§7 item is retired by this paragraph.

#### Measured

The seam registering everything the entry carries, the pass's
registrations kept, and a print at each of the pass's four
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.240/shadow.patch` over `5a464de4`, `corpus2.sh
w2`, `.objcmp/w2-lines.txt`, **218,521** `PM` lines, `failing halves: 0`,
`OVERALL PASS … projects: 64 passed`; `awk -F'\t' '$3=="PM"' | cut -f4,5,7
| sort | uniq -c`):

| at the pass | rows | |
|---|---:|---|
| `ALREADY` - the method carries the entry registration stamps | **190,183** | 156,875 impl-block methods, 32,761 struct inline, 2 union inline (registered at the seam); 545 generic-method specs (registered at the walk, §8.238) |
| `NEW`, self-returning default | 19,980 | `register_methods_by_key` skips `is_self_returning_default` at EVERY writer - a deferred template instantiated per call site - so neither the seam nor the pass registers one |
| `NEW`, return type unresolved | 8,358 | every one `Result<T, E>::as_ref(&this) -> Result<T*, E*>` (`SEAM` rows: 8,358, all `as_ref`, trait empty): the clone's return annotation names its own template over pointer arguments and is unresolved both at the seam and when the pass walks the entry; the guard (`!resolved_return_type.is_valid()` → `continue`) skips it at both, so the pass registered nothing here either.  `Option<T>::as_ref -> Option<T*>` does not appear: the one-parameter self-instantiation resolves.  Pre-existing and outside this entry: no `Result::as_ref` call exists in the corpus, and a control that makes one (`.objcmp/asref-ctl`, `Result<i32, i32>::as_ref` then `*v + 1`) builds and exits 42 under this tree, the previous half and the pin, so the method binds by a route this entry did not measure |
| `NEW`, anything else | **0** | |

So the pass's four registrations wrote nothing the seam had not.

#### What is there now

* The seam (`Monomorphizer::specialize_request`, after `resolve_specialized_ast`,
  before the entry is pushed) registers the type (§8.238), the bare-name
  mapping, the clone's inline methods (`register_carried_methods`) and
  each kept impl block's methods, all under the type.
* `SpecInjector::register(node, spec_type, ctx)` registers a placed
  specialization with NO named type - a function template's clone - as an
  injected declaration, and nothing for a named one; the `spec_name`
  parameter is gone with the mapping.  `register_spec` still rewrites each
  clone's impl head to the qualified spec name, records `spec_owner`, and
  registers the clone as a head under the specialization's key in the
  generic registry - a registry write, not an index one, and one whose
  timing the selector reads (a placed clone applies outright), so it is
  deliberately NOT moved with the index writes.
* The lane gate's `REGISTER` total is unmoved at 66: the mapping's
  name-keyed write moved file (`specialization` 2 → 1, `monomorphizer`
  1 → 2), re-pinned.

#### Objects and gates

`hash-tree.sh W` against half `Z` (`5a464de4`): tests **0 of 2,665**;

### 8.241 Every declaration-holding store is under the lane gate's rule: a store is what the context carries, a name-keyed method is any a store declares in any file with `SymbolStr` or `string` in its signature, and a call is placed by its receiver's declared type - eight per-store rows, three audit mutations the old gate accepted and the new one refuses, a committed self-test of seventeen - 2026-09-17

> **Status:** LANDED.  `scripts/lane-gate.py` rewritten under three
> definition-derived rules; `tests/lane-baseline.txt` re-pinned at 18
> buckets; `scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py` in `check-fast`; §0.2 gains a row
> per store and one for the context's members that are not stores; §0.3's
> `lane-check` row rewritten and `lane-selftest` added; §5.2's and §7's
> status blocks say eighteen; §0's two corrupted cells (D5, the trait-registry
> row) restored.  No compiler source changed.

#### Why

Audit round 12 measured the old model 93% gutted and the new 78% complete,
and judged that eleven rounds had each found new surface for one reason:
every gate, row and shadow watched ONE store, `DeclarationIndex` (with
`TypeUtils` in front of it).  It proved three holes in `lane-gate`'s rule by
building the mutation each time:

1. **A cross-file `implement struct` block is invisible.**  The parser read
   the `type struct` block's inline methods only.  Cryo lets a method be
   added to a type from another file (`implement struct Point { ... }` in
   `docs/cryo.md`; three `implement struct` blocks in the stdlib), so a
   reader declared that way is outside the set.  0 such blocks in
   `compiler/src` - a control, not a guarantee.
2. **The key type is a token match.**  `NAME_TYPE = "SymbolStr"`, so a
   reader keyed by `string` is outside the set, and the index already took
   `string` parameters (`impl_owner(node, site: string)`).
3. **Every other store is invisible by construction.**  `GenericRegistry`
   held 22 name-keyed methods and 87 external sites under the gate's own
   rule, and §8.233 moved trait-impl selection into it; nothing enumerated
   it.

#### The three rules

The old gate had one definition-derived rule (which methods, §8.230) and two
lists: the store (one, by name) and the receiver spellings (`di`,
`*.decl_index`, `types`, `*.types`, `this`, `arena`, `*.arena`, `*_arena`).
Every list is the same hole as the `lookup_*` name pattern §8.230 removed.
Now:

* **A store is a declaration-holding type the `CompilationContext` carries
  by pointer**, plus `TypeUtils`.  The context's members were measured under
  the method rule one by one (`.objcmp/`-free; the inventory script is
  reproduced by `lane-gate.py --names` for the stores and was run over the
  rest by hand):

  | type | methods under the rule | external sites | store? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `DeclarationIndex` | 55 (52 `SymbolStr` + `impl_owner`, `type_of_decl`, `register_methods` by `string`) | 224 | yes (LOOKUP / LOOKUP_OTHER / REGISTER) |
  | `TypeUtils` | 11 (9 + `def_type`, `type_display_name`) | 61 | yes, the funnel (LOOKUP_ROUTED) |
  | `TypeArena` | 29 (21 `SymbolStr` + 8 display formatters returning `string`) | 125 | yes (LOOKUP_ARENA / ARENA_READ / ARENA_WRITE) |
  | `GenericRegistry` | 23 (22 + `is_wellknown_trait_path(s: string)`) | 92 | yes (REGISTRY_READ / REGISTRY_WRITE) |
  | `ModuleGraph` | 6 (4 + `find_module_by_path`, `paths_equal_ignore_case`) | 32 | yes (GRAPH_READ / GRAPH_WRITE) |
  | `ConstantTable` | 4 (`register`, `register_enum`, two static key helpers) | 5 | yes (CONST_READ / CONST_WRITE).  **Audit 12 wrote `ConstTable 0`: the type is `ConstantTable`, so its zero was over the wrong population** |
  | `Resolver` | 33 | 11 on a `Resolver` receiver outside `compiler/resolver/`, `instance.cryo`, `compilation_context.cryo` | yes, as REENTRY: an ask from outside the pass is the re-entry §7.2 names |
  | `InternTable` | 4 (every one, by construction) | 1,622 by name | **no** - it holds strings, not declarations; it IS the boundary |
  | `TypeResolver` | 11 | 18 | **no** - pointers to the stores above and no table; a name it answers it answers by asking one of them |
  | `Monomorphizer` / `MonoState` | 7 / 5 | 10 / 10 (all `this.state`) | **no** - spec bookkeeping keyed by mangled symbol, a stamp derivation |
  | `TypeChecker` | 3 (`check_binary_op(op: string)`) | 5 | **no** - an operator spelling, no table |
  | `ModuleLoader` / `PhaseArtifacts` | 24 / 1 | 9 / 3 | **no** - keyed by filesystem path |
  | `DirectiveRegistry` | 3 (`has(kind: string)`) | - | **no** - keyed by directive kind |

  Each exclusion is stated in the script beside `STORES`.  [The sentence
  that stood here - "so the next type added to the context is a question the
  script asks rather than one an audit finds" - was FALSE of the script:
  `STORES` was a hand-written dict of seven that the script never checked
  against the tree, so a new store was exactly what an audit finds, and
  audit 13 found one (`DefaultRegistry`) by adding a map-keyed member to the
  context and reading OK.  §8.253 derives the store list from the tree.]

* **A name-keyed method is any a store declares - in its `type struct`
  block or in an inherent `implement [<G>] [struct] Store {` block in ANY
  file - whose signature mentions `SymbolStr` or `string` as a whole
  token.**  The widening sweeps in `string` parameters that are labels
  rather than keys (`impl_owner(node, site: string)`,
  `type_of_decl(d: DefId, site: string)`) and `string` returns that are
  display text (`format_display`, `resolve_display_name`).  They are pinned
  like keys: the rule cannot tell a label from a key and does not try, and
  a row that moves for one of them is explained at the re-pin like any
  other.  The alternative - a list of parameter names to ignore - is the
  hole again.

* **A call is placed by its receiver's DECLARED TYPE.**  `this` is the
  enclosing `type`/`implement` block's type; a bare identifier is what its
  nearest preceding annotation says (a parameter, a `const`/`mut` binding,
  a field - a struct-literal initializer's lowercase token is skipped);
  each `.field` is the field's declaration; `x()` is the method's declared
  return type; `x[...]` is the element type.  All read from the tree.  A
  receiver any hop of which cannot be read is a hard failure, as before.
  Over the real tree the placer refused three receivers on its first run -
  `this.get_arena().resolve_display_name(…)`, `this.scopes[i].is_ambiguous(…)`,
  `pm_prior: build_manifest::ModuleKeyTable` - each a grammar it did not yet
  read, none a store under a new alias; the accessor, index and qualified
  forms were added and it places every call in the tree.  A set name on a
  receiver whose type is NOT a store lands in `LOOKUP_LOCAL`, which is now
  the control on placement: all 59 were read by eye
  (`FunctionRegistry.register` 9, `ScopeManager.restore_scope` 7 /
  `lookup_local` 5, `DropInserter.lookup_type` 5, `MoveChecker.lookup_type`
  4, `OwnershipQuery::qualified_name_of` 4, `GlobalRegistry.register` 4,
  `DeclarationEmitter.declare_method` 4 / `declare_function` 1,
  `SpecializationPasses::register_inherent_owner` 3 / `register_impl_block`
  1, `DefaultRegistry.lookup` 2 / `register` 1, `TypeMapperCache.lookup`,
  `TraitChecker.template_key_of` 2, `MonoTraitSpecializer.template_key_of`,
  `Scope.is_ambiguous`, `Parser.enter_scope`, `ModuleKeyTable.lookup`,
  `SpecInjector::register`, `AsyncLower.declare_method`), every one a
  same-named method on a type that holds no declarations of the program.

`REENTRY`'s field-reached half was a three-name list (`set_module`,
`find_module_scope`, `restore_scope`, §8.189).  It is now the `Resolver`'s
whole set under the method rule, on a `Resolver`-typed receiver outside the
resolver's directory and the two driver files (`compilation_context.cryo`
joins `instance.cryo`: its `switch_to_module` moves the cursor for the
driver).  Predicted before the run: 6 → 12, mono 3 unmoved, sema 2 → 5
(three asks on the `get_resolver()` local), `dead_code` 1, `types/resolver.cryo`
+2, `passes/type_resolution.cryo` +1.  Measured: exactly that.  The two in
`types/resolver.cryo` are a finding: `resolve_named` asks
`this.name_resolver.is_ambiguous(name)` and `get_ambiguous_modules(name)` by
SPELLING - type resolution reading the name resolver's ambiguity table under
a bare leaf to render E0155's "imported from two modules" - a spelling ask
no list named and no row counted.  Recorded, not moved; it is diagnostic
text, and the entry that converts it should say what stamp the annotation
carries at that point.  The one in `type_resolution.cryo` is
`Resolver::ns_written_as(mod_str, written)`, a static string comparison
asking whether a module's canonical name was written as a given spelling.
