#### Measured first (`.objcmp/pd-cascade/`, `.objcmp/pd-cascade2-w6.log`)

§8.259 recorded the class as "E0233 at the call" and §8.258 as the one
cascade left on the refused corpus.  Seven call shapes to five refused
declarations, under `2da4f155`'s compiler (`cryo-W6.exe`):

```cryo
function ret_bad(v: i32) -> Nope { ... }               // E0203 here - right
function param_bad(v: Nope) -> i32 { ... }             // E0203 here - right
implement Holder { static make_bad() -> Nope { .. }  method_bad(&this) -> Nope { .. }  param_bad(&this, v: Nope) -> i32 { .. } }

ret_bad(1);                        // E0202 cannot find function `ret_bad` - it exists
param_bad(1);                      // E0215 `param_bad` takes 0 argument(s) - the refused parameter was dropped
PdCascade::Main::ret_bad(1);       // E0233 cannot find
Holder::make_bad();                // E0233 cannot find
h.method_bad();                    // E0358 no method named
h.param_bad(1);                    // silent - accepted against `param_bad(&this)`
ret_bad(1) + 1;                    // E0202 again
const x: Nope = 1;  x.v;           // E0204 no field `v` on type `i32` - the initializer's type
```

**13 errors**: the six refusals and seven more, two of them false
statements and one an acceptance.  The mechanism: `register_decl_in_index`
registered a function only when `resolved_return_type` was valid, and
collected only the parameters whose `resolved_type` was valid - so a
refused return unregistered the function and a refused parameter
registered a DIFFERENT function's signature; `register_methods` did the
same for a method, and its arity check accepted the call that fit the
dropped-parameter signature.  A binding whose annotation was refused
adopted its initializer's type through the inference branch, which did
not ask.

Not "correct as is".  Rust's answer is `ty::Error` in the signature and
silence at every use; §8.250's boundary is that the type layer has no
such answer.  What this landing does not do is add one: a poisoned
declaration is a FACT about the declaration, and the index is where facts
about declarations live.

#### The shape

```cryo
// registration: a refused signature registers nothing, under a key that says why
if (decl_index::DeclarationIndex::signature_is_refused(func)) {
    ctx.decl_index.mark_signature_refused(ctx.decl_fn_key(func.name, func.span.file));
} else if (func.resolved_return_type.is_valid()) { ... register as before ... }

// a call-miss reporter, before it speaks
if (this.ctx.decl_index.signature_refused_of_def(stamped_r.def_id())) { return TypeRef::invalid(); }
```

`signature_is_refused` asks `TypeAnnotation::refused` only of a slot
that resolved to NO type: a resolved slot was not refused, and `refused`
reads the stamp through `require`, which a synthesized declaration's
annotation may not carry - asked of every slot, the pin's build of the
compiler reported 6 pending nodes (`.objcmp/pd-build.log`).  The key is
the declaration's own (`decl_fn_key`, `Type::method`), so the reporters
ask by what they hold: the bare call by its stamp
(`signature_refused_of_def`), the module path by the qualifier's stamp
and the written member (`signature_refused_in_module`, composed inside
the index as `global_entry_in_module` composes a global's - not through
`resolve_module_qualified_symbol`, which answers only a REGISTERED
function and so answered nothing here), the static path and the method
by the owner's registered name and the member.  The reporters ask after
every resolution attempt and before the diagnostic, so a name that
genuinely does not exist is refused exactly as before - the E0202, E0233
and E0358 negatives are the control, unchanged and passing.

### 8.266 The bound-directed static path: `T::make()` under `where T: Beta` names Beta's `make` after `T` is substituted with a type two traits provide it for, as `t.go()` under the same bound already named Beta's `go` - the pre-mono dispatch annotator's third rule stamps the bound's identity on the path, the pin reads it as a direction beside D25's refusal; the call, the receiver-argument call, the value and a generic impl's method all run the bound trait's body, a two-bound parameter still ties, a bound lacking the member falls to the bare reading; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-19

> **Status:** LANDED.  `AST/expression.cryo`
> (`ScopeResolutionNode.resolved_trait`, `set_resolved_trait`),
> `AST/cloner.cryo` (copied), `mono/dispatch_annotator.cryo` (rule 3,
> `annotate_dispatch_path`, at every `ScopeResolution` the walk meets),
> `sema/call_resolver.cryo` (`pin_scope_callee_combined` and
> `pin_scope_value_static_method` read the direction), `docs/cryo.md`
> §13.4, `tests/tests/projects/bound_directed_static_path` (run, exit 19),
> `tests/test-roster.txt` (`--merge`, one row).

#### Why this unit

D25's own control (§8.263) found it: `via_bound<P>()` with
`function via_bound<T>() -> i32 where T: Beta { return T::make(); }` was
the E0156 tie once `T = P` and `P` implements Beta and Gamma - the
receiver form `t.go()` under the same bound was directed
(`MemberAccessNode.resolved_trait`, rule 1 of the pre-mono annotator) and
the static path was not.  Rust resolves `T::make()` to `<T as
Beta>::make` because the bound names the trait; §13.4 already said so of
`x.m()`.  D25 gave the shape a spelling; this gives the bare path the
meaning the bound already carries, so the head is needed where Rust
needs it - a concrete type, or a two-bound parameter - and nowhere else.

#### The shape

```cryo
// mono/dispatch_annotator.cryo, rule 3 - the bound list is the one question:
// a where-clause bounds the function's or the impl's parameters and nothing else
annotate_dispatch_path(sr, bounds) {
    if (sr.impl_trait != null || sr.resolved_trait.is_valid()) { return; }
    const tr = this.single_bound_trait_for(sr.scope_name, bounds);
    if (tr.is_valid()) { sr.set_resolved_trait(tr); }
}
// sema, at the pin - a direction, not a refusal
if (scope.resolved_trait.is_valid()) {
    const directed = this.trait_delivered_entries(scope_sym, scope.resolved_trait, member_sym);
    if (directed.length > 0 && this.pin_trait_delivered_call(call, scope, &directed)) { return; }
}
```

The stamp is made before monomorphization erases the parameter and
copied by the cloner onto every specialization, exactly as rule 1's is;
the pin reads it after the substituter has rewritten `T` to the concrete
owner, through the same `trait_delivered_entries` D25 and the
`Trait::m(recv)` form select by.  The value form (`const f = T::make;`)
reads it at `pin_scope_value_static_method` - the walk's first version
stamped only a call's callee and the value control drew the tie
(`.objcmp/pe-ctl.log`: 1 of 5), so the rule runs at every
`ScopeResolution` the annotator's walk reaches.

#### Control (`.objcmp/pa-d25/`, `.objcmp/pe-ctl2.log`; `.objcmp/pb-edge/`, `.objcmp/pe-inv.log`, `pe-inv2.log`)

```cryo
implement trait Gamma for P { go(&this) -> i32 { return this.v * 5; } static make() -> i32 { return 5; } }

Wrap<P>::via_impl_bound()                  // the impl's bound  5

no_member<Q>()         // where T: Delta (no make) -> T::make()  3, Beta's alone for Q
```

**D28 - overlapping impls are refused outright (E0119), Rust's rule.**

**D29 - `implement trait Tick for struct Holder<S>` with `S` undeclared
keeps E0302.**  E0203 (Rust's E0412, the code for any undeclared type

**D30 - a generic parameter that shadows an enclosing one is refused**

builder's to propose):

```cryo
type struct Box<T> {
    size_of_param<T>(&this, x: T) -> u64 { sizeof(T) }   // refused: shadows the owner's T
    do_something<K>(&this) -> int { ... }                 // fine: a distinct name
```

Today the owner's `T` wins silently - `Box<u8>::new(1).size_of_param<i64>(5)`
answers 1 - because the substitution tables are keyed by the parameter's
SPELLING.  In-tree population 0, so nothing breaks.  It rides with audit
14's `GenericParam` identity fix: the resolver binds each parameter to a
`SymbolID` and the stamp arm (`name_resolution.cryo`, `Res::GenericParam(s.name)`)
discards it; stamp the id, key the tables by it, and the shadowing is a
second declaration in a scope that holds the first - refused at the
declaration, by the resolver.

**D31 - the turbofish is required for generic arguments in expression
position.**  `foo::<i32>(y)` opens type arguments; `g(LIMIT < x, MAXV >
(y))` is two comparisons, always.  **`<` immediately after `::` opens
generic arguments; `<` anywhere else is a comparison.**  As Rust's
`Vec::<i32>::new()`, where every `::` after the turbofish is a path step -
there is no `::()` form; `foo::<i32>(y)` is the shape Jake confirmed.  It
retires the parser's `ident <` lookahead tables (`parser_base.cryo`
872–912 and `expr_parser.cryo` ~1190), which decide from the module's OWN
locals, globals and generic declarations and by their own comment cannot
see an import - so one expression means two things by where its
constants came from.  **Source-breaking; the population is unmeasured.
The first task of whoever builds it is the count of bare generic
arguments in expression position over the stdlib, the projects, the
examples and the compiler's own source**, module by module, and Jake
wants that number before it lands.  Not measured here: not this
session's work, and the budget was spent.

#### The defect, as measured before the change

```cryo
type struct Box<T> {
    v: T;
    static new(v: T) -> Box<T> { return Box<T> { v: v }; }
    size_of_param<T>(&this, x: T) -> u64 { return sizeof(T); }   // the method's T
    size_of_other<K>(&this, x: K) -> u64 { return sizeof(K); }
}
function free_size<T>(x: T) -> u64 { return sizeof(T); }

Box<u8>::new(1).size_of_param<i64>(5)   // 1: the owner's u8, not the method's i64
Box<u8>::new(1).size_of_other<i64>(5)   // 8
free_size<i64>(5)                       // 8
```

`.objcmp/qa-d30` under `b0327a49`'s compiler (`.objcmp/cryo-QA0.exe`):
`shadow=1 distinct=8 free=8`.  The owner's specialization substitutes
`T = u8` through every method body it holds, the substituter matching
`Named("T")` by spelling (`substituter.cryo`, `named.name.equals(param_names[i])`),
so the method's own `T` was rewritten to `u8` before the method's
specialization ever asked for it.  Nothing reported anything.

#### The refusal

`declare_generics` declares one parameter at a time, and before each asks
the scope chain from the current scope (`Resolver::lookup`); a
`SymbolKind::GenericParam` answer is E0311 at the parameter's span, the
first declaration labelled "first declared here", with a note.  One at a
time is what makes `<T, T>` meet its first as an enclosing symbol.  Any
other answer - a type of that spelling, a value parameter, nothing - is
the ordinary nearer-rib shadowing and declares as before.  An impl's
`<T>` beside `struct Holder<T>`'s is two scope chains (the impl's parent
is the module) and is not asked about.

Control `.objcmp/qa-d30` (`src/main.cryo` with the shadow renamed `<U>`,
`src/edge.cryo` holding the three other shapes): predicted 3 refusals
under the tree's compiler and 0 under `cryo-QA0.exe`; measured 3
(`.objcmp/qa-ctl3.log`: `edge.cryo:5:19`, `:9:10`, `:17:11`) and 0
(`.objcmp/qa-ctl3-qa0.log`, exit 0, the program printing
`renamed=8 distinct=8 free=8 valparam=2 impl=4`).  The renamed program
prints the same under the tree's compiler (`.objcmp/qa-ctl2.log`).

The code: **E0311 is proposed, not confirmed.**  Rust's E0403 is taken in
Cryo by "Missing Return"; E03xx is the generics family (E0302 the head's
parameter list against its target, E0306 a bound) and E0311 is its next
free number.  Jake to confirm or renumber.

#### The stamp carries the id

`Res::GenericParam(SymbolStr)` was the one `Res` variant naming a
definition by its spelling.  The resolver had the id at every writer
(`bare_name_res`'s `sym_id`, the scope segment's `scope_sym`, the
qualified head's `hs.id`, `res_for_head`'s `sym.id`) and threw it away.
Now the variant and `ResBase::GenericParam` carry the `SymbolID`, the
node the resolver bound records it (`GenericParamNode.sym_id`), the
cloner copies it (a `Res` names a definition, and a clone's is the
template's), and the async lowering's synthesized trait head stamps
`gp.sym_id`.  Readers of the payload: none in the tree took the name from
a `GenericParam` stamp except `ResBase::name()`, whose one caller
(`scope_owner_key`) excluded that variant first; the method is deleted and
the caller reads `Def` and `PrimTy` by kind.  lane-check: `DEFID_UNWRAP`
30 unchanged in total, the one unwrap moved from `res.cryo` (1 → 0) to
`call_resolver.cryo` (2 → 3) - not predicted (the prediction was no row
moved; the door moved from the enum's method to its caller and the gate
counts by file), re-pinned.

#### The tables stay by spelling: one chain, measured

The row asked for the substitution tables keyed by the id.  They are one
system fed from one end, and re-keying one table leaves it with two keys:

* `TemplateEntry.param_names` (`generic_registry.cryo`), built from
  `gp.name` (`specialization.cryo` ×2, `async_lower.cryo`): 15 `equals`
  sites in `sema/call_resolver.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo` and
  `types/resolver.cryo`'s where-bound binder (`param_name_slot`);
* they fill `ResolutionContext.generic_bindings` (33 `add_binding`, 8
  `lookup_binding`) which `resolve_named` asks by the WRITTEN name before
  it reads the stamp, and whose other readers ask by `bound.type_parameter`,
  a projection's member and the prefix of a flat `I::Item`;
* whose names become `ImplBlockNode.derived_param_names` (3 writers, 2
  readers, `trait_specializer.cryo` copying the bindings' names);
* which with the entry's names feed `ASTTypeSubstituter.param_names` (6
  compares: `Named.name`, `args_are_outer_param_refs`, a scope segment's
  spelling, and `ArrayLiteralNode.element_type` - a plain string with no
  stamp to read);
* and `TraitBound.type_parameter` is a spelling with no stamp anywhere (9
  compares).

With the shadow refused, one spelling names one parameter in any scope
chain the resolver sees, so the spelling-keyed tables are unambiguous
over everything the resolver stamped.  What the resolver does not see is
a trait default's body synthesized under an impl whose own parameter
spells the body's method parameter - the body was resolved in the trait's
file, the impl's parameter was not in its scope - and that is the shape
the id tells apart and the spelling cannot.  Population unmeasured; the
re-key is a unit over the whole chain with that as its control.

### 8.270 D28 built: two implementations of one trait whose heads unify are refused at the later head where it is declared - `Show for Wrap<T>` beside `Show for Wrap<i32>`, and two `Emit for Holder<T>` heads told apart only by their where-bounds - under E0308, Rust's rule and Rust's one code for the identical pair and the overlap; §8.261's unifier lands keyed by the parameter's symbol, `select_trait_impl`'s "registration-time report" comment becomes a mechanism, the one green overlap in the tree is converted to a `compile_fail` that keeps its leaf-collision property from the other side; 1 in-tree refusal, 0 objects moved - 2026-09-19

#### The rule, and the code it lands under

```cryo
implement<T> trait Show for struct Wrap<T>   { show(&this) -> i32 { return 1; } }
implement    trait Show for struct Wrap<i32> { show(&this) -> i32 { return 2; } }
//           ^ E0308: `Show for Wrap<i32>` overlaps `Show for Wrap<T>` - a Wrap<i32> selects both

implement<T> trait Emit for struct Holder<T> where T: Alpha { .. }
implement<T> trait Emit for struct Holder<T> where T: Beta  { .. }
//           ^ E0308: two `Emit for Holder<T>` heads differ only in their where-clauses

implement<T> trait Show for struct Pair<T, T>     { .. }   // accepted beside
implement    trait Show for struct Pair<i32, u8>  { .. }   //   one T cannot be both
implement    trait From<i8> for struct Wrap<u64>  { .. }   // accepted beside
implement    trait From<u8> for struct Wrap<u64>  { .. }   //   distinct trait arguments
```

Before (`.objcmp/cryo-QA0.exe`, `6f404d8a`'s compiler): all five pairs
compiled, `w.show()` on a `Wrap<i32>` answered whichever head was written
first, the bound pair dispatched by bound where one held and by order
where both did (§8.261).  Now (`.objcmp/qc-d28`, `qc-ctl1.log`):
predicted 3 refusals at the later heads of pairs 1, 2 and 5 and 0 for 3
and 4; measured 3, at lines 16, 20 and 32, and `cryo-QA0.exe` exit 0 with
0 errors on the same file (`qc-ctl1-qa0.log`).

**E0308, not E0119.**  The row and the ruling name Rust's E0119 as the
rule; as a NUMBER it would file under Cryo's parser family (E0100–E0116
are the parser's), and `E0308_CONFLICTING_TRAIT_IMPL` already is
"Conflicting Trait Implementation" - Rust's E0119 is one code for the
identical pair and the overlap, and so is this.  The sentence tells them
apart: the identical pair keeps "a trait may be implemented at most once
per type, including across modules"; an overlap says "`A` overlaps `B`,
so a type both heads accept would select both"; two heads spelled alike
say they "differ only in their where-clauses, which do not separate
them".  Jake to say if he wants a number of its own.

#### Where it is asked

Type resolution's impl arm registers a source head under its (trait,
target) key, then asks the coherence key for an IDENTICAL earlier head
(E0308 as before); only when there is none does it ask
`overlapping_head(trait, target, node)`: the heads under the key
registered before this one, written ones only (a placed clone is one
written head's instantiation), the first that `heads_overlap`s it.  The
report is at the later head with the earlier labelled "overlaps this
one", once per pair, and never at a use: the use is innocent, and a pick
by order or by bound would make a program's meaning depend on which
impl came first.  `select_trait_impl`'s comment - "the overlap is a
registration-time report, not one per use" - was a hypothesis with no
report behind it (D28's row); it now names the mechanism.

The unifier is §8.261's, with one change: `HeadBinding` is keyed by the
parameter's `SymbolID` off the `Res::GenericParam` stamp (§8.268), so a
head's `T` and the other head's `T` are two variables by identity and
the `side` the measurement's copy carried to keep spellings apart is
gone; `head_names_agree` compares `DefId`s by `equals` rather than
unwrapping two names.  `scripts/ns-migration/8.261/` keeps the
measurement's copy as it was run.

#### The converted pair

`where_bound_leaf_collision` was written for a different defect: the
coherence key once truncated a bound's trait to its LEAF and searched
the program for a qualified name, a search that declined when two
declarations shared the leaf, so `Alpha::Render` and `Omega::Render`
folded to one bound and the pair was refused as a DUPLICATE.  Under D28
the pair is refused either way, so the property is kept from the other
side: the project is `compile_fail` asserting E0308 at `main.cryo:19:1`
with "differ only in their where-clauses" and EXCLUDING "at most once per
type" and `main.cryo:15:1` - a leaf-collapsed key would report the
duplicate sentence, and a use-site report would name the wrong line.
`E0308_overlapping_impls.cryo` pins the three refused shapes by `//~`
and the three accepted ones by the suite's exhaustiveness.

The pairs for the gate: the tree's compiler passes both
(`qc-neg.log`, compile-fail 1 passed; `qc-proj.log`, projects 1 passed)
and `cryo-QA0.exe` fails both - "[FAIL] (expected E0308)" and "[FAIL]
(expected build to fail (exit non-zero))" with `Compiled ->` in its
output (`qc-neg-qa0.log`, `qc-proj-qa0.log`).

* **the new gate over the same tree, refusing**: `grep -rho
  'ErrorCode::E0240_' ... | wc -l` reads **2** against the row's **3**,
  `ns-status-check: DRIFT` (`.objcmp/qd-mut-new.log`).

The same on a name row: one `decl_fn_key(` call renamed `dfk_mut(` and a
`// decl_fn_key` line appended; the old form still read **17**, the new
form (`grep -rh .. | grep -v '^\s*//' | grep -o .. | wc -l`) **14** against
the row's **15**, DRIFT (`.objcmp/qd-mut2-new.log`).  Both mutations
restored (`git checkout -- compiler/src`).

`ecode_rows.py` reads §0, parses the two check forms (240 checks, 228 over

by whether the line begins with `//`.  16 of 228 included a comment hit
(`.objcmp/qd-audit.txt`):

|---|---|---|---|

| `binding_namespace` | 18 | 12 | 6 |

A control on the instrument: for every one of the 228 whose pattern holds

A bare error code (`'E0240'`, `'E0353'`) now greps the emitter's constant,

absence check and stays bare (a comment would move it TOWARDS drift).
§0.4 carries the bullet: a new grep row has the same hole until it is

#### The defect, as measured before the change

```cryo
type trait Conv {
    conv<U>(&this, x: U) -> u64 { return sizeof(U); }   // the method's own U
}
type struct Holder<U> { v: U; }
implement<U> trait Conv for struct Holder<U> { }        // the impl's U spells it

Holder<u8> { v: 1 }.conv<i64>(5)   // 1: the impl's u8, not the method's i64
```

`.objcmp/ra-d30id` under c9a762f0's compiler (`.objcmp/cryo-RA0.exe`):
`same=1 same_k=8 distinct=8 distinct_k=8` (`.objcmp/ra-ctl1.log`).  The
default's body is resolved in the trait's file, where no enclosing `U`
exists, so E0311 cannot fire; it is then copied under the impl, whose
specialization substituted `U = u8` through it by spelling
(`substituter.cryo`, `named.name.equals(param_names[i])`) before the
method's own specialization ever asked.  The `<K>` sibling and the same
two shapes under `implement<T>` answer 8: only the shared spelling fails.

In-tree population of the shape (`.objcmp/ra/default_shadow.py`, a scan of
every `type trait` default with its own `<P>` against every
`implement<..P..> trait` of it): **2** - `Iterator`'s `chain<J>` and
`zip<J>` under `implement<I, J, A> ... ChainIter<I, J>` (`iter.cryo:328`)
and `implement<I, J, A, O> ... ZipIter<I, J>` (`:380`).  Nothing in the
corpus calls `.chain`/`.zip` ON a `ChainIter`/`ZipIter` receiver (grep over
stdlib, tests, examples, compiler, tools: 0), so the conflation is never
demanded, which is why the object comparison below can be 0 and is not
evidence of nothing.  `a.chain(b).chain(c)` on a `ChainIter` fails TODAY
with E0636 "no method 'chain'" even when `c`'s type IS the impl's `J`
(`.objcmp/ra-ctl3.log`, `ra-d30same`).  [This entry called that "a
separate defect ... which the id does not touch": WRONG, corrected in
§8.275 - it IS this shape, and the id fixes the same-`J` case; the
differing-`J` case is the ARENA's half of the same conflation.]

#### The chain, re-keyed as one unit

The stamp already carried the id (§8.268); every table that matched a
spelling now matches the symbol, and no table keeps a spelling as a key:

* **`TemplateEntry.param_syms`** beside `param_names`, filled by the three
  registrars (`specialization.cryo` ×2, `async_lower.cryo`).  The names
  stay for what only a name can do - mint the arena's parameter type
  (`create_generic_param(name, index)`, untouched by the brief's own
  exclusion) and display.
* **`ResolutionContext.generic_bindings: GenericBinding { sym, name, ty }`**,
  `add_binding(sym, name, ty)` (an invalid symbol binds nothing - a
  written arg that is a type, a node nothing stamped), `lookup_binding(sym)`.
  27 writers converted: a `GenericParamNode` gives `gp.sym_id`, a written
  `Named` gives `n.param_sym()`, an entry slot gives `entry.param_syms[j]`,
  a derived parameter gives `derived_param_syms[di]`.  `resolve_named`
  asks step 1 by `slot.generic_param_sym()` and the flat `I::Item` case by
  `slot.relative_param_sym()` (the stamp is `TypeRelative(GenericParam(I),
  1)`), so the spelling is never split to find a prefix.
* **`This::Member` in `assoc_bindings`**, its own table with
  `add_assoc_binding` / `lookup_assoc_binding` by the member's spelling:
  `bind_trait_args_for_impl`'s positional sugar wrote `Item -> T` into
  the generic table and `resolve_projection` read it back by `proj.member`.
  An associated type is no symbol the name layer declares - its identity is
  the trait's and the member's name - so it cannot share the parameters'
  key, and a second table for a second question is not two keys on one.
* **`ImplBlockNode.derived_param_syms`**: `add_derived_param(sym, name,
  ty)`, `lookup_derived_param(sym)`; `cache_derived_trait_params` copies
  the binding's symbol and name.
* **`ASTTypeSubstituter.param_syms`** with `param_slot(sym)`: the `Named`
  arm by `named.param_sym()`, the flat projection prefix by
  `named.relative_param_sym()`, `args_are_outer_param_refs` by the arg's
  symbol, the scope segment (`T::default()`) by `scope_res.relative_param_sym()`.
* **`TraitBound.subject_sym`**, stamped by `stamp_trait_bounds` through
  `bare_name_res(lookup(type_parameter))` in the clause's own scope (the
  one kind-to-`Res` mapping; the `resolve_path` row's `this.resolver.lookup(`
  count moves 11 → 12 and `bare_name_res(` 3 → 4 for it).  Read by the
  where-bound binder (`param_slot(param_syms, bound.subject_sym)`), the
  E0306/E0358 bound checks, `derive_where_assoc_bindings`, and the dispatch
  annotator's rules 1 and 3 (`single_bound_trait_for(param: SymbolID)`,
  the receiver by `param_head_of_ann -> SymbolID`, the static path by the
  segment's `relative_param_sym`).
* **`rewrite_trait_params_annotation`** (a trait's own parameters in a
  default's cloned signature) by `n.param_sym()` against the trait's
  `gp.sym_id`s.

#### What the re-key exposed: an impl block was specialized under the OWNER's parameters

`ASTSpecializer::specialize` ran ONE substituter, built from the struct's
`param_names`, over the struct's clone and over every impl block's clone.
By spelling that worked exactly as long as an impl spelled its parameters
as the struct did, which every in-tree impl does (`.objcmp/ra/impl_params.py`:
the differently-spelled heads are the partially-concrete ones, `Box<T,
GlobalAlloc>`, and the E0302/E0308 negatives).  By symbol the impl's `T`
is a different declaration from the struct's `T`, and the first build
lost every trait default synthesized into a generic impl (`ra-t1`: "no
method 'plain' found on type Other<u8>").  Now each impl clone gets
`impl_substituter`: the impl's own parameters, each bound to the
specialization's argument at the position the head writes it, in head
order, a parameter written twice bound once (`Pair<T, T>`), an argument
written as a type binding nothing (the head was selected against the
arguments by `head_matches_args` already), a where-derived parameter left
to the bounds as before.  The receiver check
(`method_has_modified_self_type`) compares a `this: Owner<..>` annotation
against the parameter the HEAD writes at each position (`head_syms`, via
`GenericRegistry::head_param_of`) rather than the entry's - a default's
`&this` is rewritten to `Reference(Generic(Owner, [the head's args]))`
by `rewrite_this_type_annotation`, and against the entry's symbols every
such default read as "modified" and was dropped.

#### The async lowering spelled parameters with no stamp

`named_ann(name)` minted `Named("T")` unstamped, its own comment saying
"the binding in the resolution context answers it" - by spelling.
`type_ann_for` rebuilds a frame field's type from the ARENA, whose
parameter types carry a spelling and no symbol.  Now `named_ann(gp)`
stamps `Res::GenericParam(gp.sym_id)`, and `type_ann_for(ty, params)`
finds the parameter among the future's own (`d.fut_params`: the owner's,
then the function's - the scope the arena spelling was resolved in, where
D30 makes one spelling name one parameter) through `param_spelled`; a
spelling that is none of them is a type the lowering cannot spell and is
reported as such, where before it was a `Named` nothing would answer.

#### The mono fallback: measured dead, deleted

`ast_resolver.cryo`'s `resolve_func_and_body` re-resolved a still-invalid
return or parameter type under a context binding every ARENA parameter
name of the substitution to its replacement - "the ASTTypeSubstituter
doesn't always reach every spot", by its comment.  A comment is a
hypothesis.  Probed under the re-keyed compiler (`SHADOW D30ID-FALLBACK`
at each successful resolution, `SHADOW D30ID-ENTRY` at each unresolved
slot, `SHADOW D30ID-BLOCK` at the block): over the six-half corpus
(`corpus2.sh ra`, `.objcmp/ra-corpus.out`: LSP direct exit 0, make test
OVERALL PASS 204 / 68, 0 failing halves) **0 resolutions**; over the LSP's
264 modules (`.objcmp/ra-entry-lsp.log`, 486 warnings in the same file as
the control that stderr is captured) **0 entries**; the block itself entered
1,290 times in a one-file program (`.objcmp/ra-block.log`), so the probe
prints.  Its precondition - a signature slot the substituter left
unresolved - never holds; a parameter left in a signature after
substitution names a declaration the clone cannot see, and there is no
second context to try it under.  Deleted with its `entry`/`subst`
threading (`resolve_func_and_body(func, ctx, this_type)`,
`resolve_methods(methods, ctx, this_type)`), and the `full_subst` its
one outside caller built for it.

#### Left keyed by spelling, by design

Four compares in `call_resolver.cryo` (590, 597, 706, 5134) match an
arena `GenericParamType.param_name` / `BoundedParamType.param_name`
against `entry.param_names`, and five callers (`trait_checker.cryo` ×3,
`trait_specializer.cryo`, `method_binding.cryo`) ask
`lookup_subst_for_param(bound.type_parameter, subst)` - a bound's subject
against the arena substitution by spelling.  Both sides are the TYPE
layer's identity, which is the spelling alone (`create_generic_param`
caches by the name; this entry said "name+index", corrected in §8.275)
and carries no symbol; the brief excludes it, and it is the same identity by which
`implement<U>`'s `U` and `conv<U>`'s `U` are one arena type.  The AST
tables no longer conflate them, and that is what the control measures;
`method_binding.cryo` 385/443/1141/1152 read an arena parameter's spelling
against a bound's `type_parameter` for the same reason.  A differently-
spelled impl's where-bound (`implement<X, A> .. for ChainIter<X, J> where
X: Iterator<A>`) still derives through the owner's arena substitution by
spelling, as it did.  `ArrayLiteralNode.element_type` had no writer but
the substituter and no reader but the dumper - always `""` - and is gone.

#### Gates

Control `.objcmp/ra-d30id`: `same=8 same_k=8 distinct=8 distinct_k=8`

The brief named this class as "the only cascade left": a call to a

```cryo
implement Holder { static make_bad() -> Nope { return 1; } }   // E0203 - right

const fv: (i32) -> i32 = ret_bad;                  // E0201 cannot find value `ret_bad` - it exists
```

### 8.274 The trait arm's bare-leaf `method_returns` write, measured and deleted: every trait method's return was registered twice, under the trait's canonical name and under its written leaf, "so bound-aware dispatch can find the method by leaf name"; over the six-half corpus 25,374 bare writes were read 0 times, the control read by the leaf hits every time, so the leaf key is gone and the canonical write stays; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-19

#### The finding

Audit 13 named it and audit 14 recorded it as still unmeasured and not in
the ledger: the trait arm registered `node.name::method` beside
`<module>::Trait::method` in `method_returns`, and it registered a return
with no signature.  The second half is by design - a trait declares what
its methods return and nothing checks a call's arguments against a trait
(the selected implementation is checked, §8.267) - so the question was
the leaf key: two modules' same-leaf traits would be one key under it,
and a reader that asked by it would take whichever registered last.

#### Measured

A probe compiler recorded every key the bare write produced
(`register_method_bare_probe`, a set beside the table) and printed
`SHADOW MR-BARE-HIT` at every `lookup_method_return` whose key was in the
set - a hit is a read the bare write alone could have answered, because a
trait whose canonical name IS its leaf is skipped by the write's own
guard.  Over the six halves (`corpus2.sh rc`, `.objcmp/rc-corpus.out`:
LSP direct exit 0, make test OVERALL PASS 204 / 69, 0 failing halves):
**25,374 bare writes** (`SHADOW MR-BARE-WRITE`, 263 per trait method
across the compilations), **0 hits**.  Control by inversion: one read by
the leaf added at the write (`.objcmp/ra/probe_mr_ctl.py on`), a one-file
program: 96 writes, **96 hits** (`.objcmp/rc-ctl1.log`); removed.  The
readers: `resolve_method_owner`'s contract is a registered name, and a
bound's trait is `tr.identity()`, the stamped canonical name - the leaf
the comment said would be asked for was never asked for.  The LSP holds
no reader of its own.

### 8.275 The arena's half of D30's conflation, found by the id's own control: with the AST tables keyed by symbol, `a.chain(b).chain(c)` on a `ChainIter` - E0636 before - runs when `c`'s type is the impl's `J` and iterated over GARBAGE when it was not, because the arena keys a generic parameter by its spelling alone and a substitution holding the method's `J` and the impl's `J` answered whichever was added first; `TypeSubstitution::get` now answers nothing for a parameter bound to two different types, so the differing case is refused where its specialization is missed; §8.272's two wrong sentences corrected; the arena keyed by symbol is Jake's design unit - 2026-09-19

> **Status:** LANDED.  `types/substitution.cryo` (`get` refuses a parameter
> bound to two different types), `tests/tests/projects/chain_default_same_param`
> (run, exit 25), `tests/tests/projects/chain_default_param_conflict`
> (`compile_fail`, E0636 "cannot resolve 'ChainIter::new'"),
> `tests/test-roster.txt` (`--merge`, two rows); §8.272's "a separate
> defect which the id does not touch" and "name+index" corrected in place,
> marked.

#### Found by the control, not claimed by it

§8.272's control measured the trait-default shape and its entry set the
in-tree instance aside: `a.chain(b).chain(c)` on a `ChainIter` receiver
failed with E0636 under the old compiler even when `c`'s type was the
impl's `J`, so it read as "a separate defect".  Re-run under `c596a14b`'s
compiler (`.objcmp/rd-ctl1.log`): `chained_same=25` - the id had fixed it.
Then the differing-`J` case (`.objcmp/rd-ctl3.log`):

```cryo
mut c: TakeIter<Range<i32>> = r.take(2);            // a J the impl's J is not
sum_it(a.chain(c))             // Range.chain(TakeIter):     4  right
sum_it(a2.chain(b2).chain(c2)) // ChainIter.chain(TakeIter): 0  WRONG (25)
sum_it(a3.chain(b3).chain(c4)) // ChainIter.chain(Range):    25 right
```

A silent wrong answer where a refusal had stood - the outcome the house
rules name as a failure - and the mechanism, from the IR
(`.objcmp/rd-chain`, `ops.ll`): the spec'd `chain` built
`ChainIter<ChainIter<Range, TakeIter>, TakeIter>` - `This`'s own second
argument rebuilt with the METHOD's `J`.  The stash probe
(`.objcmp/ra/probe_stash.py`, `.objcmp/rd-ctl5.log`) showed the stash
already held `ChainIter<Range, TakeIter>` when mono read it, i.e. the
substituter's `subst.apply` over sema's abstract stash had answered the
impl's `J` with the method's binding.

#### The arena keys a parameter by its spelling alone

`TypeArena::create_generic_param(name, index)` caches by `name.id`; the
index is whatever the first creation passed.  §8.272 wrote "name+index":
wrong, and corrected there.  So `implement<I, J, A> .. ChainIter<I, J>`'s
`J` and the default's `chain<J>`'s `J` are ONE arena type, and
`specialize_method`'s substitution held it twice - `J -> TakeIter` (the
method's, added first) and `J -> Range` (the owner's) - and `get` answered
the first.  The old compiler's E0636 was the AST half of the same
conflation reaching first (the impl's substituter rewrote the default's
`J` by spelling, so the method had no parameter left to specialize); the
AST half is fixed, and the arena half was exposed.

#### The shape

`TypeSubstitution::get` answers nothing for a parameter it holds two
different types for (the same type twice is one answer); nothing in the
compiler can apply such a substitution correctly, and an invalid answer
leaves the type unresolved, so the nested `ChainIter::new` is not
specialized and codegen reports the miss.  A refusal in codegen's terms,
as before, and not a diagnostic of its own: a code for "the method's `J`
cannot be told from the implementation's" would describe the arena's
limit to the user, and the fix is the arena keyed by symbol - a design
unit the brief excluded and that is Jake's.  The `conv<U>` control keeps
its 8: its `sizeof(U)` is rewritten by the AST substituter by symbol
before any arena parameter is asked.

Measured: `ra-d30id` 8 / 8 / 8 / 8, `ra-d30same` 25, `rd-chain` refused
(`.objcmp/rd-ra-d30id.log`, `rd-ra-d30same.log`, `rd-rd-chain.log`).

(E0636 "cannot resolve 'ChainIter::new'") pass under the tree's compiler

"(exit 1, expected 25)" and "(output missing "cannot resolve

#### The ruling

Jake set the gate on merging `naming-impl` to `main`: the migration is
**100% complete** - not "correct with known items rowed" - when there are
zero name-keyed reads outside an enumerated, justified residue, every
member named with a one-line reason it is correct where it is, and the
residue pinned by count so it cannot grow.  The by-design sites are "the
maximum allowed": a residue above that set either moves the ceiling with a
justification per extra site or converts the sites.

#### The count is not fixed here, deliberately

The figure in circulation - "about sixteen" - was a paraphrase of audit
12's bucket D.  Audit 14 remeasured the whole population at 55 sites with
the buckets redistributed, so the justified residue may be more or fewer,
and a number traced to a recollection rather than a measurement is the
defect class this ledger keeps finding (§8.271's fifteen rows counted
comments; §8.272's "name+index" was a guess, §8.275).  The row therefore
states the SHAPE and leaves the count to the enumeration: one list,
`scripts/ns-migration/residue.md`, each site with its justification -
member lookup inside an owner is the canonical member, name-keyed in Rust
too - and Jake rules on the final number.  The enumeration is a unit of
its own, for a later session, after the id-move's remaining buckets land,
since those are still shrinking the population it would count.

> **Status:** LANDED, the first third.  `compiler/parser/expr_parser.cryo`
> (`at_turbofish`, `parse_generic_head`, `parse_identifier_tail`; the
> member and scope-member arms), `tests/tests/lang/turbofish_expression_generics.cryo`

#### Why three landings and not one

The pin (`bin/cryo`, `bin/cryo.exe`, at `db5af63c`) compiles the stdlib
and the compiler.  A tree spelled `Array::<i32>::new()` is refused by it:

```
error[E0100]: expected member name after '::', found '<'
```

(`.objcmp/sb-tf3.log`: the scratch below under `.objcmp/cryo-SA0.exe`,
HEAD's compiler, which parses as the pin does).  So the rewrite cannot
land before a pin that reads `::<`, and a pin cannot be built from a
compiler that does not; the order is forced: (1) the parser reads both
spellings, (2) the pin is refreshed from it, (3) the tree is rewritten and
the lookahead deleted.  The two spellings coexist for exactly one commit
of the pin's life, in this tree, and nowhere else.

#### The rule as parsed

`<` opens generic arguments in expression position only immediately after
`::`; every `::` after the arguments is an ordinary path step.

```cryo
Wrap::<i64>::new(7)                 // owner argument, then a path step
Pair::<i32, i64> { first: 1, second: 2 }
free_size::<i64>(5)                 // a free generic function
tramp::<i32>                        // the specialization as a value
Plain::make::<u16>(1)               // a static method's own argument
w.size_of::<u32>(1)                 // a method's own argument
g(LIMIT < x, MAXV > (y))            // two comparisons, whatever LIMIT and MAXV name
(Beta for P)::make::<T>()           // the impl-qualified path's member
```

Type position is untouched (`Array<i32>` in an annotation, a where-bound,
a static-match arm, `new Type<T>(..)`): a `<` after a type name is never a
comparison.  One method, `ExprParser::at_turbofish`, answers the question
at the three places it arises - the identifier (`parse_identifier_or_call`),
the scope member (`parse_scope_member`, which also serves the
impl-qualified path and the postfix `::` chain) and the member access
(`parse_member_access_expr`); the identifier's four followers (`(`, `{`,
`::`, a value) moved whole into `parse_generic_head`, and what may follow
any name into `parse_identifier_tail`, so both spellings run one body.  The
lookahead arm at each site is marked for the retirement.

The 2×2 (`.objcmp/sb-tf/`, `.objcmp/sb-tf-old/`: one program in each
spelling, every shape above): old spelling under `cryo-SA0.exe` runs and
prints `7 1 2 4 8 1 1 3 1`; the turbofish under this compiler prints the
same; the old spelling under this compiler prints the same; the turbofish
under `cryo-SA0.exe` is refused with the E0100 above.  While building the
scratch a pre-existing refusal surfaced and was removed from it:
`Wrap<i64>::make<u8>(1)` - a generic static method reached THROUGH a
generic owner - is E0636 (`codegen: cannot resolve 'Wrap::make'`) under
HEAD's compiler in the old spelling too (`.objcmp/sb-tf-old.log`).  That
is D24's shape, ruled and unbuilt, not this entry's.

#### The rule

Audit 14 (its report and `nomap_owners.py`, copied to
`.objcmp/sa/nomap_owners_r14.py`) attacked rule 1 - "a store is a type
that owns a map" - and found the two by-name lanes then live in the tree
were in types that own NO map: `Res::GenericParam(SymbolStr)` with the
substitution chain's parameter arrays beneath it (D30, §8.272), and the
parser's `local_names` / `global_value_names` / `generic_decl_names`
(D31, §8.278).  Its mutation `m8` - an array-backed store,
`entries: Pair<SymbolStr, TypeRef>[]` with a linear `lookup_leaf(name)`,
carried by the context, with a caller - read `lane-gate: OK`.  A linear
search over an array of names answers "which declaration is spelled X"
exactly as a map does; the rule saw the map and not the question.

Rule 1b, beside rule 1 and derived the same way: a type block that owns no
map, owns an ARRAY OF NAMES (`SymbolStr[]`, `string[]`, or
`Pair<SymbolStr|string, ..>[]` - the shape that stores an answer beside
each name), and declares a method taking a name (a key type in PARAMETER
position, never `SymbolStr[]`, which is a table handed in) is a candidate,
and every candidate is placed: a store, or an entry in `EXCLUDED_ARRAYS`
with the file and the reason its array holds no declaration a stage looks
up by that name.  A candidate in neither is refused; an entry that is no
longer a candidate is a stale exclusion, refused; an entry that owns a map
is rule 1's and is refused here.  An array owner nothing asks by name is
data, not a table, and is not a candidate - the signature test is what
makes the array a table (audit 14's own formulation).

```cryo
type struct LeafTable {                          // audit 14's m8
    entries: Pair<SymbolStr, TypeRef>[];
    lookup_leaf(&this, name: SymbolStr) -> TypeRef { .. }   // refused now
}
type struct NameTables {
    generic_decl_names: SymbolStr[];
    count(&this) -> i64 { .. }                   // data: accepted
}
```
