### 8.328 A call through a trait's path, or an impl-qualified path, that hands a shared reference where the method takes an exclusive one is refused where it is written (E0214), naming the argument and giving the spelling that borrows exclusively; it was the one mismatch nothing reported, and it failed later in code generation as "cannot resolve"; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

#### The class, measured first

```cryo
mut r: Count = Count { n: 0 };            // Count implements Iterator
const a = Iterator::next(&r);             // next(mut &this): refused now
const b = (Iterator for Count)::next(&r); // same, impl-qualified: refused now
const c = Iterator::next(r);              // accepted: borrows r exclusively
const d = r.next();                       // accepted: the method form
```

The brief's premise was "no error, no result". Measured, it was not silent end
to end: sema said nothing, the call reached code generation unpinned, and the
build failed there with E0636 `codegen: cannot resolve 'Iterator::next'`
(`(Iterator for Count)::next(&r)`: `cannot resolve 'Count::next'`), before
§8.327 buried under 43 false "codegen failed for module" lines. Nothing named
the receiver.

Where the silence came from: a call through a trait's path pins the entry its
arguments select (`pin_trait_delivered_call`), and the selector compares
argument and parameter types exactly - a shared reference `&Count` is not a
`mut &Count`. When no entry fits it answers false and "leaves the report to
the caller", and two of its three callers (`pin_trait_qualified_call`,
`pin_impl_qualified_call`) dropped that answer. Other mismatches are reported
anyway, by the argument checks that run after (E0215 for a count, E0214 for a
type); a mutability-only one is not, because those checks do not compare
reference mutability at all (see "found on the way").

Instrumented before fixing (a print at every give-up of
`pin_trait_delivered_call`: the reason, and whether some entry fits once
reference mutability is set aside; not committed). Controls first, one
program per shape: `Iterator::next(&r)` and `(Iterator for Count)::next(&r)`
gave up with `fits=0 blind=1`; an extra argument, a wrong-type argument and an
impl-qualified extra argument gave up with `fits=0 blind=0` and were reported
(E0215, E0214, E0215). Then the corpus (`scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh s43u2`, six
halves, 0 failing halves, `.objcmp/s43u2-lines.txt`):

| give-up | count | where |
|---|---|---|
| no entry fits, a mutability-only difference | **0** | - |
| no entry fits, a count or type difference | 4 | all in negatives (`E0215_impl_qualified_arity` ×3, `E0233_trait_qualified_unselected` ×1), each reported |
| several entries fit | **0** | - |
| an argument with no type | **0** | - |

So the silent class is exactly one mismatch, in any argument position and in
both path forms: an argument that differs from its parameter only in being a
shared reference where the parameter is exclusive. No program in the tree
reaches it.

#### What is there now (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`)

`pin_trait_delivered_call` reports that mismatch itself when no entry fits
(`report_shared_for_exclusive`): it looks for an entry every argument fits
once a shared-for-exclusive reference is set aside, and refuses the first such
argument as E0214, the existing "Argument Mismatch" code:

```text
error[E0214]: `next` takes its receiver as an exclusive reference (`mut &`), and this is a shared one
    const v: Option<i32> = Iterator::next(&r);
                                          ^~ a shared reference; the parameter is `mut &`
 help: pass `r` itself, which the call borrows exclusively, or call the method: `r.next()`
```

Any other no-fit is left to the argument checks, as before, so nothing is
reported twice. Silent during a symbolic generic-body walk, as every report
in this family is.

Jake's ruling (2026-09-24, relayed in plain text): refuse, as Rust does -
Rust's fully-qualified `Iterator::next(&r)` does not auto-reference and a
shared reference where `&mut` is wanted is a type error. Accepting `&r` is off
the table.

**The spelling the help gives is Cryo's, not Rust's.** Cryo has no expression
for an exclusive borrow: `&` is the only borrow operator (`expr_parser.cryo`
`parse_unary`), and nothing in the tree writes `mut &x` or `&mut x` as an
expression. Passing the value itself is what borrows exclusively in the path
form - the selector's auto-reference pass admits a value for a reference
parameter - and it borrows rather than moves: `Iterator::next(r)` twice
yields 2 and leaves `r.n == 2`.

#### Controls

* `negative/E0214_trait_path_shared_for_exclusive` pins three refusals - the
  trait path, the impl-qualified path, and an argument after the receiver
  (`Fill::fill(&s, &t)` with `into: mut &Tally`) - and compiles the three
  spellings that are accepted beside them. **`32be5028`'s compiler fails it
  (`[FAIL] (expected E0214)`); this tree passes it.**
* The shapes reported by the argument checks are unchanged: E0215 for an extra
  argument in either path form, E0214 `mismatched types` for a wrong-type one.

#### Measured

Predicted: 0 objects move - no program in the tree reaches the new report.

| what | result |
|---|---|
| objects (`objcmp.sh`) | **0 of 1,126** examples, **0 of 3,017** tests; `OVERALL PASS` |
| residue, lane gate | unchanged: residue 359, J 150, convertible 93; lane gate OK (the report asks the index for an entry's signature by the entry id it already holds) |
| roster | +1 compile-fail (3 annotations) |
| `lsp-check`, `cross-check` | OK, OK |

#### Found on the way, not acted on (Jake's)

**No call form checks reference mutability.** Each of these compiles and runs
on this tree, pin and HEAD alike:

```cryo
function bump(c: mut &Count) -> void { c.n = c.n + 1; }
implement struct Count {
    static poke(c: mut &Count) -> void { c.n = 5; }
    bump2(mut &this) -> void { this.n = 5; }
}

bump(&r);              // a shared reference into `mut &Count`: accepted
Count::poke(&r);       // the same through a type's path: accepted
Count::bump2(&r);      // a method through the type's path: accepted

const k: Count = Count { n: 0 };
k.next();              // a `const` binding mutated through `mut &this`: accepted
Iterator::next(k);     // likewise, through the trait's path
```

The trait path was the only form where the absence showed, because its
selector happens to compare exactly. Refusing these is a language rule (what
`const` and `&` promise), source-breaking at an unmeasured scale, and not this
unit's.

### 8.329 The thirteen bit-operation intrinsics are declared (`bswap`, `popcount`, `clz`, `ctz`, the rotates), so a program can call them; three of the drafted declarations had the wrong result width and are corrected to what the lowering produces; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

#### What was there

The lowering for 13 bit operations existed and was correct
(`codegen/ops/intrinsic_emitter.cryo`), and §8.325 gave each a kind decided
once, where its declaration registers. Nothing declared them, so nothing could
call them. Jake approved declaring them as public API (2026-09-24, relayed in
plain text).

#### The drafted declarations were checked against the lowering, not pasted

The previous handoff drafted all 13. Read against the emitter, **three were
wrong**: `popcount64`, `clz64` and `ctz64` were drafted `-> u64`, but the
emitter truncates each count to `i32` (`emit_unary_llvm(..., narrow_to_i32:
true)` for `llvm.ctpop.i64`; `emit_clz_or_ctz` narrows every width that is not
32). A `u64` declaration over an `i32` value is a signature LLVM rejects or a
value read at the wrong width. They are declared `-> u32`, which is also what
Rust's `count_ones` / `leading_zeros` / `trailing_zeros` return. The byte swaps
(same width in and out) and the rotates (`(value, n: u32)`, the count widened
to 64 bits for the 64-bit forms by `emit_rotate`) matched the draft.

```cryo
import std::core::intrinsics;

const a: u32 = intrinsics::popcount64(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF);   // 64, a u32
const b: u32 = intrinsics::clz32(0);                         // 32: zero answers the width
const c: u64 = intrinsics::rotl64(0x8000000000000001, 4);    // 0x18
```

#### What is there now

`stdlib/core/intrinsics.cryo` declares the 13, with what each lowers to and
the zero-input and width rules. The kind is decided once, where the
declaration registers (`IntrinsicKind::from_name`, §8.325); code generation
reads it off the call's pin and never sees the name. A declared intrinsic is
argument-checked like any function: `intrinsics::bswap32(1, 2)` is E0215 and
`intrinsics::popcount32(3.5)` E0214 at the call - the "arity mismatch falls
back to a call to an undefined symbol" the previous handoff warned of is not
reachable from a declared intrinsic.

#### Controls

* `lang/bit_intrinsics.cryo` (5 tests, all 13 intrinsics against values worked
  by hand, including a zero input to each count and a rotate by the full
  width): **passes 5/5**.
* **The mechanism broken on purpose** (run alone): `from_name` made to answer
  `IntrinsicKind::Call` for `popcount32` - the registration deciding it is an
  ordinary call. The test then fails to LINK with `undefined reference to
  'popcount32'`, at that intrinsic's two call sites and nowhere else; the
  other twelve lowered inline. Restored, rebuilt clean (346 warnings,
  unchanged).

#### Measured

Predicted: 0 objects move - a declaration nothing calls emits nothing.
`objcmp.sh` stashes only `compiler/src`, so the comparison was its two hash
halves with HEAD's `intrinsics.cryo` against this one, one compiler, the new
test set aside on both sides (`.objcmp/s43u3`).

| what | result |
|---|---|
| objects | **0 of 1,126** examples, **0 of 3,017** tests; `OVERALL PASS` |
| `^intrinsic function` in `stdlib/core/intrinsics.cryo` | 58 → **71** |
| declared-by-nothing kinds | 13 → **0** |
| residue, lane gate | unchanged (no compiler change) |
| `lsp-check`, `cross-check` | OK, OK |
| roster | +5 unit tests |

#### Found on the way, not acted on

* **`docs/stdlib-api.txt` lists no intrinsic** - not these 13, and none of the
  58 before them - so the "grep the API index before writing a helper" rule
  cannot find an intrinsic. `make api-index` produced no diff for this change.

§0.0 now states Jake's four conditions (relayed in plain text) and the state
of each, with `scripts/ns-migration/done.py` as the instrument:
`--outstanding` lists condition one's functions (the residue's convertible
rows grouped by lookup function, refusing to answer unless `residue.py
--check` is OK); `--name-taking` lists every function in `compiler/src` with

the second: `report_impl_qualified_miss` and `check_static_scope_method_args`
(signatures wrapped over two lines) are listed; `find_module_index`, which

callers, 9 hand-written scans), 93 call sites. Condition two's population was
**1,136** at the tip and is **1,113** after this change.

#### What changed

One fact - which trait - was carried as a string in eight places. Each is a
`DefId` now:

| carrier | was |
|---|---|
| the registry's trait lookups: `get_trait_decl`, `heads_for`, `select_trait_impl`, `template_head_for`, `overlapping_head`'s trait half, and the private `heads_under` / `register_trait_impl` / `register_trait_decl` beneath them | `SymbolStr` |
| `TraitChecker::type_implements_trait`, `select_impl`, `type_satisfies_opaque_bound`; `TypeResolver::concrete_trait_slots` | `SymbolStr` |
| `GenericRegistry::wellknown(LangItem)`'s answer | `SymbolStr` |
| an impl head's trait (`ImplBlockNode.trait_def`) | `qualified_trait_name: SymbolStr` |
| a method's providing trait (`FunctionDeclNode.origin_trait`) | `SymbolStr` |
| a call's stamped trait (`resolved_trait` on a member access and on a path) | `SymbolStr` |
| an overload entry's trait (`DeclarationIndex::entry_trait`) | `u32` |
| `call_resolver`'s `trait_sym` / `only_trait` / `found_trait` through the trait- and impl-qualified paths | `SymbolStr` |

```cryo
// before - compiled; any interned string was accepted, a leaf included
registry.get_trait_decl(intern.intern("Iterator"))
// after - E0214, expected `DefId`, found `SymbolStr`
registry.get_trait_decl(bound.definition())
```

Every caller already held the definition: `TypeAnnotation::trait_def`,
`TraitRef::definition`, the impl head's stamp. None needed a new mint except
two inside the registry (a language item's claim, a trait's `TypeRef`) and one
the parser already made by spelling (below). Where a consumer still takes a
name, the id is unwrapped there (`DEFID_UNWRAP` 31 → 60): 5 inside the
registry packing its own keys, 11 for text, 14 at a lookup or compare that
still takes a string - codegen's `resolve_function` ×3, the test runner's
`lookup_sole_entry` ×3, `get_template` for `Array` ×3, the async lowering's
`Poll`/`Option` spelling ×2, `EnumType.qualified_name` ×2, the thread-safety
deny list ×1.

#### Measured

| what | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|
| objects, `objcmp.sh` (`.objcmp/s44u1/run.out`) | 0 | **0 / 1,126** examples, **0 / 3,018** tests; OVERALL PASS |
| residue population (`residue.py --count`) | 359 → 337 | **333** - see the miss below |
| B / S / J / convertible | 51→29 / 19 / 150 or 149 / 93→71 | **27 / 18 / 149 / 68** |
| `done.py --outstanding \| wc -l` | 30 → 26 | **25** |
| `REGISTRY_READ` | 87 → ~65 | **33** - see below |
| compiler warnings, clean build | 346 | **346** |
| `lsp-check`, `cross-check` | OK | OK, OK |

**The misses, explained.** The prediction was made for the registry lookups
alone. Converting them turned `local::ImplBlockNode[]`'s two scans
(`block.qualified_trait_name.equals(only_trait)`) into
`block.trait_def.qualified_name().equals(only_trait)` - and the lane gate
REFUSED the tree, the scan table naming an entry nothing scanned. The
instrument had gone blind to two unconverted reads. The unit was widened to
the carriers they compared against (`only_trait` ← `resolved_trait` /
`origin_trait` / `entry_trait`), after which both compare `DefId` to `DefId`
and the table entry is stale for a true reason: B 29 → 27, outstanding
26 → 25. The other two rows: a trait's type asked by name
(`method_binding.cryo`, S) and a language item's type
(`async_lower.cryo`, J) both ask `type_of_def` now. `REGISTRY_READ` fell by
54, not ~22: the gate counts a store method as name-keyed when a `SymbolStr`
is anywhere in its signature, the return included, and `wellknown` returned
one - its callers left the row with it.

**Control.** The property is that the compiler refuses a spelling. Build 3
(`.objcmp/s44/build3.log`) failed at `mono/call_specializer.cryo:914` with
`expected DefId, found SymbolStr` - a caller handing `SymbolStr::empty()` to
a converted lookup - and at `sema/call_resolver.cryo:2845` the same.

#### Found on the way, not acted on

* **The parser names `Iterator` by spelling its path.**
  `parser/parser.cryo:3401` stamps the `for` loop's `next` call with
  `LangItem::Iterator.path()` interned - an identity built from a string at
  parse time. It was a `SymbolStr` and invisible; it is a `DefId::of_definition`
  now, and `DEFID_MINT` counts it (24 → 25 net).
* **Rule 1c goes blind when a key field becomes an id and is unwrapped for a
  compare.** `x.def.qualified_name().equals(n)` in a loop is a name-keyed
  scan the gate does not recognise. Here it refused the tree (a stale entry);
  a scan newly written in that shape would not be seen at all.
* **The gate's name-keyed test reads the return type.** A store method that
  takes an enum and returns a name was a "read"; the rule and its golden
  should say which they mean.

### 8.331 The last lookups whose callers already held the identity take it: the self-growth check is handed the owner's `DefId`, and an identifier is matched to a parameter by the binding its stamp names; condition one's remaining 23 lines all wait on two design units - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

#### What changed

| site | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `TypeArena::is_self_growing_instantiation` (2 calls, `types/resolver.cryo`) | the owner's name, unwrapped from a `DefId` by the caller or an impl head's `target_key` | the `DefId`; an impl head's through `ImplBlockNode::target_def` |
| `mono/dispatch_annotator.cryo` rule 1 | `param.name.equals(id.name)` | `param.sym_id` against `id.res.local_sym()` |
| `sema/async_lower.cryo` combinator field map | the literal's identifier and the parameter by spelling | the same, by binding |

An impl head whose target is a primitive or a monomorphized clone has no
`DefId`; `target_def` answers invalid there and the check is skipped. It
could never match either way: the check compares against a generic
instantiation's BASE, which is never a primitive or a specialization.

```cryo
implement<T> struct Wrap<T> {
    pointed(&this) -> Wrap<T*> { ... }   // self-growing: the owner is Wrap's DefId, not "Wrap"
}
```

The two identifier sites were shadowed first - both compares computed, a
line on every match - over the six halves (`corpus2.sh w`,

|---|---|---|---|
| dispatch rule 1 | 38,725 | **0** | 73,141 |
| combinator field map | 22 | **0** | 0 |

| `lsp-check`, `cross-check`, warnings | OK, OK, 346 | OK, OK, **346** |

| `ARENA_READ` | 75 → 73 | **73** |
| `done.py --outstanding` / `--name-taking` | 23 / 1,110 | **23 / 1,110** |

`done.py --outstanding` lists 23 lines, 64 call sites. None has its
identity at the caller:

* **The registry's template and inherent-impl keys** - `get_template`,

  `find_inherent_impl_generic_method`, `inherent_impl_has_method`, `inherent_impl_blocks`, `overlapping_head`'s target half: 7 lines. The key
  is a type's canonical name OR a specialization's; which identity names a

### 8.332 A template is asked for by the declaration it is or by its own type, never by a name built at the call, and a function declaration carries its identity the way a type declaration does; the design review ratifies §8.330 and corrects its stated reason - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

The registry re-key's first stage. The design and its measurements are in
`docs/name-resolution-rekey.md` (untracked); Jake approved them in plain text
(relayed 2026-09-24): the key is the handle, created at first mention;
`CalleePin::Instance`, `template_in`, `template_of_type` and `def_of` are the
names; a function declaration gets an identity the way a type declaration
has one; the negative suite is measured before the stage that creates a
generic function's handle in sema.

#### What changed

| site | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `GenericRegistry::get_template(SymbolStr)` - 18 of its 20 callers | a template by a name the caller unwrapped, composed or read off a type | `template_of(DefId)` for a declaration's stamp; `template_of_type(TypeRef)` (renamed from `get_template_by_type_id(u64)`, 26 callers) for a type in hand; `template_in(ResBase, member)` for a template declared inside a module or a type |
| `CallExprNode.resolved_template` | the winning template's name | the template's own type (`TemplateEntry.base_type`) |
| `register_impl_block` (3 callers) | the target's name | the head's `DefId` (`target_def`) |
| `FunctionDeclNode.def` | absent; a function's key re-derived from its name and file (`decl_fn_key`) | stamped by the name layer when it declares the function, the same id every reference resolves to |
| function template registration | `decl_fn_key` when the declaration had no stamp | the stamp; an unstamped declaration is recorded (`record_pending_bug`) and registers nothing |
| `GenericRegistry::trait_decl_of(TypeRef)` | a trait type named back to a `DefId` through the arena | deleted; `get_trait_decl(def_of(ty))` |
| `CompilationContext::definition_id_of` (12 callers) | a type's definition, on the context | `DeclarationIndex::def_of(ty, arena)` - the one door from a type to its definition, where the type resolver can reach it too |

```cryo
implement<S> struct BufStream<S> { ... }
// codegen's "is this head a template's?" - was a string, is the stamp:
greg.template_of(node.target_def())            // BufStream's DefId; invalid for a primitive or a clone

mem::offset(this.ptr, count)                   // mono: the template declared in `std::core::mem`
registry.template_in(ResBase::Def(scope_def), name)

implement string { static f<T>() -> T { ... } }
string::f<u8>()                                // a primitive container is `ResBase::PrimTy`
```

`template_in`'s container is a `ResBase`, not a `DefId`, because a static
generic method may be declared on a primitive (`implement string`); none is
in the tree (a scan of `stdlib`/`tests`: 19 primitive blocks, 29 static
methods, 0 generic), but the program is legal today and a `DefId`-only door
would have dropped it silently.

#### The review of §8.330

Ratified. §0.0 recorded its reason as "a trait has no type arguments"; that
was wrong - `type trait From<T>` has one. It is sound because every lookup
it converted asks for a trait's DECLARATION, which has no arguments in any
language (Rust's `TraitRef { def_id, args }` carries them on the use), and
the keys it replaced, `tr.identity()`, never included them. §0.0 now says so.

#### Two findings

* **A local named `module` is miscompiled, silently.** `module` is a keyword

  { module = q; } _ => {} } return module...` built with the pin reads

  stage's first build used that name in `scoped_template_from_stamp` and
  failed `E0636 cannot resolve 'mem::offset'` in every example; renamed.
  Nothing else in the tree declares a local of that name. The fix - refuse
  the keyword as a binding, or bind it correctly - is not this stage's.
* **An incremental `make cryo` after a field is added to an AST class reuses
  objects built against the old layout** (`reusing 85 cached object(s)`),
  and the result runs. The first shadow corpus ran on such a binary and is
  void; everything above is from clean builds.

#### What this does not do

* `get_template(SymbolStr)` keeps two callers, both in
  `scope_is_generic_template`, asked with a specialization's built name -
  the re-key's third stage.
* `decl_fn_key` keeps 14 readers: a function's registration key for
  monomorphized clones and synthesized functions, which by design carry no
  stamp. A method carries none either; a generic static method stays a
  member of its owner, found by `template_in`.
* Finding 2 of the forty-fourth handoff - the arena interns a generic
  parameter by spelling, so `Pair<A, i32>` written in two templates is one
  handle - is untouched and does not bear on this stage: its keys are a
  declaration's `DefId` and a template's own type, and no type argument goes
  into either. The names the later stages replace collapse exactly the same
  way (`4Pair$LN$L1A$G...` carries the parameter's spelling), so converting
  them to handles keeps today's identity; Jake's option B for impl
  parameters needs the arena to tell parameters apart first.

### 8.335 A keyword that opens a declaration cannot name a binding anywhere one is written - a variable, a parameter, a pattern element, a destructured local - and the lane gate keeps watching the trait-head table, for being scanned by identity; §8.333-§8.335 land together - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

#### The keyword refusal

§8.332 found a local named `module` read garbage with no diagnostic. The
mechanism: a statement that begins with a keyword opening a declaration is
parsed as a declaration, so `module = q;` was never an assignment. Jake ruled
(plain text, 2026-09-24) that `module` is refused as a variable name. The
refusal covers the class the mechanism defines - the 19 keywords
`ParserBase::opens_declaration` answers for (`function const mut type struct
class enum trait import module extern implement public private protected
namespace intrinsic static async`) - not the one spelling. **The scope grew
from Jake's ruling on one keyword to nineteen; §8.338 records his ruling
that it stays at nineteen.** A keyword
that opens nothing (`default`, `string`) stays a legal name.

```cryo
function take(module: i32) -> i32 { ... }          // E0100: expected a parameter name, found `module`
const module: i32 = 42;                            // E0100: expected a variable name
match (r) { R::D(static) => { ... } }              // E0100: expected a binding name
const { v: module, struct }: P = p;                // E0100 twice: the rename, and the shorthand's field
```

`ParserBase::refuse_declaration_keyword_name`, called where a binding's name
is read: `parse_variable_declaration`, `parse_parameter`, an enum pattern's
element (`expr_parser.cryo`), a destructuring entry (the rename, or the field
itself for the shorthand). `for` variables and lambda parameters already
refuse every one of the 19 - the keyword is not an identifier there. 28
compiler parameters named `module` / `namespace` renamed
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.335/rename_params.py`, run once from the repo root
at `fad94370`).

Measured with one tiny program per keyword and shape, `m` as the control
(`C:/t/kw47/sweep*.sh`; before = `sweep.txt`, `sweep2.txt`,
`sweep3-before.txt`, from this commit's compiler without the pattern and
destructuring sites; after = the `-after` files):

| shape | accepted before | accepted after |
|---|---|---|
| pattern element, read in the arm | 18 of 19 (`mut` is E0113) | **0** |
| pattern element, a statement beginning with it (`static.put(&out);`) | 0 compile - 14 fail in CODEGEN, E0636 "type `<unknown>`", after sema passed them; `function const mut type intrinsic` in the parser | **0**, all E0100 at the binding |
| destructured local, shorthand / rename | 12 / 16 | **0 / 0** |
| `for` variable, lambda parameter | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| control `m`, every shape | compiles, prints 42 | compiles, prints 42 |

The negative test `E0100_declaration_keyword_as_binding_name.cryo` carries 5
annotations. The pair: the compiler without the two new sites runs it
`OVERALL FAIL (compile-fail: 0 passed, 1 failed)`, "expected error[E0100] at
line 25 containing `expected a binding name, found \`static\``"; this commit's
passes it.

#### The trait-head table's gate entry: updated, not removed

`GenericRegistry.trait_heads` still exists and is still scanned inline in its
own file - by the target's `TypeRef` and the trait's `DefId` since §8.333
(`TraitImplHead { trait_id: DefId; target: TypeRef; block }`). Rule 1c only
recognises a compare of a NAME-typed field, so the entry went stale and the
gate refused the tree. Deleting it would have left nothing recording that the
table exists and how it is keyed, and a later by-name scan would have been
invited back as an ordinary TABLE entry.

The entry changes kind instead: `IDENTITY` (`scripts/lane-gate.py`,
`IDENTITY_TYPES = DefId, TypeRef`). An identity entry must still be scanned by
an identity-typed field, or it is stale; a scan of it by a name is refused
outright, naming the site. The same justification as the earlier removals
(`local.ImplBlockNode`, §8.330): the scans compare identities now, so this is
a conversion, not the instrument going blind - and here the instrument keeps
watching.

The pair, over this tree with `generic_registry.cryo` put back to HEAD's
name-keyed table (`C:/t/s47pair`, golden pinned by the old gate): the OLD gate
prints `lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 5 ...` exit 0; the NEW gate exits 1,
"`GenericRegistry.trait_heads` is listed in SCANNED_ARRAYS as keyed by
identity (DefId / TypeRef) but is scanned by a name
(compiler/types/generic_registry.cryo:911 `.target_key`, 3 sites)".
`lane-gate-selftest` 38 → 40 mutations: an identity entry scanned by a name,
and one no longer scanned by identity, both refused.

### 8.336 `private` and `protected` on a member mean a module, as they already did on an item: `private` reaches the declaring module only, `protected` that module and every module under it, and a struct literal may be written only where every field is visible - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-24

Jake's rulings (relayed in plain text 2026-09-24), all built here:
`private` = the declaring module only; `protected` = the declaring module and
everything under it; a struct literal requires every field visible to the
writer, with no exception for construction. Considered and **rejected**:
letting outsiders set private fields at construction - setting a private
field is the more dangerous operation, since reading one leaks information
while setting one breaks the invariant the field exists to protect. Types
and functions stay public by default.

```cryo
// module app::vault
type struct Chest { private: secret: i32; public: static issue() -> Chest { .. } }
function peek(c: Chest) -> i32 { return c.secret; }       // now fine: same module

// module app::forge
implement struct Chest {
    static forge(k: i32) -> Chest { return Chest { secret: k }; }   // now E0353
}

// module app::report
type struct Stamped { private: stamp: i32 = 7; public: tag: i32; }   // (declared in app::vault)
const t: Stamped = Stamped { tag: 3 };   // E0353: the literal sets `stamp` too
```

#### What changed

`MemberResolver::member_reachable(decl: ModulePath, is_protected, span)` is
the one question both member gates ask: the use site is the module owning the
syntax's own file (`module_ns_sym_of_file(span.file)`, the callee gate's
source of truth), never the type the walk is inside. A field's module is its
type's (`module_name`); a method's is the file its declaration is written in,
so a `private` method in an `implement` block belongs to the block's module.
`protected` asks `ModulePath::is_within` (new: the module itself, or a path
continuing it past `::`). Deleted: the subclass walk (`is_subclass_of` in the
member resolver) and `async_origin_owner`, the special case that lent a
lowered future its origin type's access - a lowered body keeps the spans it
was written with, so it keeps its module. A struct literal now checks every
field it sets, the defaulted ones included (`sema.cryo`, the missing-field
loop). The labels name the module: "private field reached outside module
`M`", "private method called outside module `M`" - **new wording, Jake's to
change**; the messages the tests pin are unchanged.

`docs/cryo.md` §8.2 and §14.4 and this document's §3.1 say so.

#### Measured before the change: a shadow of the rule

Every non-public member check computed the type rule and the module rule side
by side over the six halves (probe reverted; runner `C:/t/vis-corpus.sh`,
`.objcmp/vis/s1-*`), 0 failing halves:

| | count |
|---|---|
| field, both allow | 807 |
| method, both allow | 3,338 |
| method, both refuse | 2 (`visibility_static_gate`) |
| **type rule refuses, module rule allows** | **4** - exactly the four single-file negatives below |
| type rule allows, module rule refuses | **0** |
| use site with no module | 0 |
| a literal leaving a private field to its default | 0 |
| a private method declared outside its type's module | 0 |

Control on the probe: the Token forge (`C:/t/dp/forge`, an `implement` block
in another module building the type's private field) printed 2 x `differ
old=1 new=0 use=Forge decl=Forge::vault`.

#### Tests

The four single-file negatives became legal programs under the ruling - their
outsider sat in the declaring module - so each assertion moved into one
two-module project, `projects/visibility_module_private`, beside the cases
the old rule could not express: `E0353_private_field_access` (`secret`),
`E0353_private_field_literal` (`sealed`), `E0353_private_field_async_foreign`
(`hidden`, from an `async` method in another module),
`E0353_protected_outside_subclass` (`for_sibling`, from a sibling module);
new: a foreign `implement` block building a type (`seal`), a literal leaving
a private field to its default (`stamp`), a private method declared in
another module's `implement` block (`tuck`). Controls, asserted absent: a

### 8.337 An identity type stays sealed only while one of its fields is private, and the lane gate now refuses a tree where `DefId` or `OverloadId` has none; what the identity index needs before it can be built - no compiler behaviour changed - 2026-09-25

#### The guard

Since §8.336 a member field is private to its declaring module, so
`DefId { .. }` and `OverloadId { .. }` can be written only in
`compiler::resolver::res`. That holds only while a field IS private, and
members are public by default: a refactor that drops the `private:` label
reopens construction to every module with no error at any caller - and the
`DEFID_MINT` row, which greps `DefId::of_definition(`, would never see a
literal.

`scripts/lane-gate.py` `SEALED_TYPES` names each sealed type, its declaring
file and why it must stay sealed; `check_sealed_types` refuses a listed type
with no private field (under a label or inline), and an entry whose type is
gone.

```cryo
type struct DefId {
private:            // drop this line and lane-check refuses the tree
    qn: SymbolStr;
public: ...
}
```

The pair, this tree with `DefId`'s `private:` label removed (`C:/t/s47seal`):
the OLD gate (HEAD's `lane-gate.py`) printed `lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 5
...` exit 0; the NEW gate exits 1, "`DefId` (compiler/resolver/res.cryo) has
no private field, so any module can write its literal". Control on the
instrument: over the real tree it reads `qn: SymbolStr;` for `DefId` and
`pos: u32;` for `OverloadId` - its first version read neither (its regexes
shared names with two later definitions in the script, which replaced them)
and refused the real tree, which is how that was caught. `lane-gate-selftest`
40 -> 43 mutations. `res.cryo`'s comment on `DefId`, which said visibility
was type-scoped and so could not narrow minting, is corrected.

`DEFID_MINT` stays: the literal is sealed, but `of_definition` still takes
any interned string, so the row still counts something that can happen.

#### What the identity index needs first (measured at the tip, 25 mints, 56 reads)

`docs/defid-index-plan.md` (untracked, approved) makes `DefId` an index into
a `DefTable`. Three things found while sizing it:

1. **The table has to live in `res.cryo`**, because only that module can
   write the literal - and the AST imports `res`, so the table cannot take
   an AST node. "The mint takes a resolved declaration" can therefore be the
   plan's `register(parent: DefId, leaf, kind, span)`, append-only with no
   lookup by path: a string can make a NEW id that nothing uses, never an
   existing declaration's.
2. **Every declaration must then be registered exactly once**, and today
   nothing is: the name layer mints from `module + "::" + leaf` on every
   answer (9 sites, `DefId::of_definition(qualified_name_of(&s))`), an
   imported name is its own `Symbol` (so the id has to be copied at import),
   type registration mints again from a string (`decl_index.cryo:642`), a
   type's id is recovered from its name (`def_of`, 2), modules from their
   namespace (2), the parser mints three language items before any
   declaration exists, and the async lowering (6) and bindgen (1) mint for
   what they synthesize.
3. **Registering per declaration changes two identities today's names
   collapse**, and both are open questions for Jake: two free functions `f`
   in one module share `DefId("ov::f")` now and would get two ids (question
   3 of the plan), and 1,650 monomorphized instantiations get a `DefId` in
   the self-build (question 4). Neither was acted on here.

Proposed order, so a representation change and a behaviour change never land
together: first move every mint to a registration point with `DefId` still
holding its path (values identical, 0 objects, a shadow can prove it - the
`DEFID_MINT` count falls to the registration points); then swap the
representation to an index, when every id already comes from one place.

#### Reproduce

```
python3 scripts/lane-gate.py && python3 scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py
git grep -n "DefId::of_definition(" -- compiler/src | grep -v "static of_definition" | grep -v ":\s*//" | wc -l   # 25
git grep -n "\.qualified_name()" -- compiler/src | grep -v ":\s*//" | wc -l                                      # 56
```

### 8.339 An identity is made where its declaration is registered and read everywhere else: the name layer stamps each binding once, a module gets its id when it is discovered, a type's id comes from its registration - mints 25 → 9, 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

The groundwork §8.337 proposed for the identity index, with `DefId` still
holding its path, so every value is the one the tree had.

#### What moved

Before, the name layer built a declaration's id again at every answer it
gave for it - nine places, each gluing the module to the leaf:

```cryo
// before - the same id rebuilt at each use
return Res::Def(DefId::of_definition(this.resolver.qualified_name_of(&s)));
// after - read off the binding, stamped once when the binding was made
return Res::Def(s.def);
```

| where an id is made now | what it covers | replaced |
|---|---|---|
| `Resolver::admit` (`resolver.cryo`) | every binding, as it enters the symbol arena (`Symbol.def`); the three ways in - `declare`, `declare_import`, `declare_module_symbol` - all go through it | 9 name-layer mints: `stamp_function_def`, `bare_name_res` ×2, `walk_module_rooted_type` ×2, the scope segment's base, the path head's type, `res_for_head` ×2 |
| `ModuleInfo::with_namespace` (`module_graph.cryo`) | a module, when the loader discovers it; read by `ModuleGraph::module_def` and `ModuleSpellingMatch.found_def` | the module owner of a `Module::member` path (`name_resolution.cryo`, was `DefId::of_definition(owner)`) |
| (no mint) | an `extern module` alias in the scope position reads the alias symbol's own stamp, through the new `alias_of` (`alias_module_of` is now its name) | `DefId::of_definition(alias_ns)` |
| `register_type`, `register_type_reverse_only` (`decl_index.cryo`) | a type; the reverse map now holds the `DefId` the registration made, and `def_of` / `lookup_type_name` read it | `def_of`'s two mints from the type's registered name |
| (no mint) | `claim_wellknown` takes the registration's `DefId`: a type declaration's `node.def`, a function's name-layer stamp `func.def` | the claim's mint from a name |
| (no mint) | the async lowering registers its future struct BEFORE building anything that names it, and the impl head, the future's annotation and the constructor literal read `struct_decl.def`; `Poll` is `wellknown(LangItem::Poll)`; an instantiation's base is `def_of(generic_base)` | 5 async mints |

**Left (9):** the five registration points above, and five references built
before their declaration is registered - so no registration exists to read
from yet:

- the parser's three language-item stamps (`lang_variant_pattern`, the range
  constructor, `for`'s `Iterator::next`). The plan's answer ("the parser
  records the item, name resolution stamps it after registration") does not
  fit the pass order: language items are claimed in `TypeDeclaration`, which
  runs AFTER `NameResolution` (`pass_registry.cryo`,
  `build_standard_pipeline`). Stamping them needs a point after the claims.
- bindgen's `named()` (a reference to a C record the importer emits; the
  record is registered later, by `TypeDeclaration`).
- the async `main$async` callee. Found while measuring: the renamed function
  keeps the name layer's stamp for `main` (`M::main`) after
  `node.set_name("main$async")`, and the synthesized wrapper `main` carries no
  stamp at all. Nothing reads the stale stamp in a way that moved an object;
  not acted on.

#### Evidence

- **Shadow, six halves** (`scripts/ns-migration/8.339/mint-move-shadow.py`;
  `.objcmp/u1/mint-lines.txt`, 3,418,661 lines; 0 failing halves; the suite
  under the shadow `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 227 passed;
  projects: 74 passed)`). At each moved site the stamp now read and the mint
  the site used to make, side by side:

  | site | agree | differ |
  |---|---|---|
  | `res_for_head` (no trailing segment) | 902,124 | 0 |
  | `stamp_function_def` | 293,520 | 0 |
  | scope segment's base | 250,525 | 0 |
  | `bare_name_res` (both) | 132,971 | 0 |
  | module owner of `Module::member` | 94,760 | 0 |
  | module-rooted path member / alias member | 3,216 / 12 | 0 |
  | `extern module` alias in the scope position | 507 | 0 |
  | path head naming a type | 62 | 0 |
  | async: impl head / future annotation / constructor / `Poll` / generic base | 759 / 459 / 747 / 230 / 818 | 0 |
  | **function language-item claim** | 49,621 | **8,857** |
  | `res_for_head` with a trailing segment | never entered | |

  The claim's disagreements: 8,840 are monomorphized function clones, whose
  node carries no stamp (the old key was the clone's mangled name, which
  contains `$`); 4 are async `main` wrappers and renamed bodies (above); 15

  **Control on the instrument:** the same helper prints `differ` at 8,857

### 8.340 `Module::f` cannot yet be named by the name layer's binding: intrinsic functions have none, and a private member's refusal depends on the name sema composes - BLOCKED on Jake, measured, nothing built - 2026-09-26

Condition one's two visibility lines (`DeclarationIndex::is_candidate_public`
and `namespace_of`, both called from `CallResolver::enforce_callee_visibility`)
convert only if a module-qualified call hands the gate the function's
identity. The unit tried the direct route: the name layer already finds the
member when it stamps the scope segment (the symbol the module offers under
the leaf, whose stamp is `Symbol.def` since §8.339), so it records it on the
node, and sema reads it instead of composing a name.

```cryo
// today - sema glues the module's stamp to the written leaf
const q: SymbolStr = intern(stamped_ns + "::" + member);      // std::core::mem::swap
// tried - the binding the name layer made for `mem::swap`
const callee: DefId = scope.member_def;
```

The patch (`.objcmp/u3/unit3.patch`, on `46466528`: `ScopeResolutionNode
.member_def`, stamped beside the scope segment; `resolve_module_qualified_def`
in place of `resolve_module_qualified_symbol`; `enforce_callee_visibility`,
`enforce_value_ref_visibility` taking a `DefId`, with `namespace_of_def` /
`is_public_def` in the index) builds, and then **every program that calls an
intrinsic by path fails**: `examples/05-todo-cli` stops with E0233 "cannot
find `intrinsics::fpclass`" and 452 like it.

#### Measured (`scripts/ns-migration/8.340/member-def-shadow.py`, six halves, the OLD answer returned so the build is the tree's)

At every module-qualified function the call resolver names, the binding
against the composed name (`.objcmp/u3/u3-lines.txt`):

| outcome | count |
|---|---|
| both name the same function | 277,526 |
| neither names a function | 22,720 |
| they name different functions | **0** |
| no binding, but the composed name is a function | **15,872** |

The 15,872 are two populations, and nothing else:

1. **15,849 intrinsic functions** (`std::core::intrinsics::…`). The name
   layer declares an intrinsic function and never exports it
   (`name_resolution.cryo`, the `IntrinsicDeclaration` arm has no
   `export_symbol`; the `IntrinsicConstDeclaration` arm does), so the module
   offers nothing under the leaf and `intrinsics::f` resolves today only
   because sema composes `std::core::intrinsics::f` and finds the signature
   the declaration index registered. §8.65 tried exporting them: it
   ambiguated 87 leaves and broke the build on `panic` (an intrinsic and a
   real function share the leaf), and the endgame plan's §1 treats the
   intrinsics as a design of their own.
2. **Private members called by path** - `VisibilityGate::Vault::latch` (6),
   `PrivExt::Ffi::llabs` (3), `VisibilityValueGate::Vault::tapped` (1): the
   three negative projects that pin E0353 "is private and cannot be called".
   The module offers only public members, so the refusal they pin fires only
   because the composed name reaches a declaration the name layer did not
   bind. Keeping it needs the name layer to bind the private declaration
   (`Resolver::private_declaration`, which imports already use) and leave the
   refusal to sema's gate - an answer the tree gives, not a question.

**Question for Jake:** should an intrinsic function be offered by its module
- reachable as `intrinsics::f` through the name layer's binding - and if so,
by being exported (so a glob import brings it, which §8.65 showed collides),
or by path only (a set a path reaches that an import does not)? Until one of
those holds, condition one's two F lines cannot be converted without minting
the callee's id from the composed name, which §8.339 just removed.

asserts its output does not contain `VisibilityGate::Vault::door`, and the
probe prints the names it compares. The same caveat §5 of the identity-index

### 8.341 A generated `implement` block is told from a written one by `spec_owner`, already: every instantiation clone carries it, no written block does - measured, nothing changed - 2026-09-26

An audit found the compiler places `implement` blocks for generic
instantiations into the same statement lists that bare-name finders walk,
242 of them unstamped beside 312 written and stamped, and no mark to skip the
generated ones by. Whether converting those finders needs a mark ADDED
decides that later unit's shape.

**It does not: the mark exists.** `scripts/ns-migration/8.341/impl-origin-probe.py`
tags each `ImplBlockNode` with where it was created (a field for the
measurement only) and prints, just before code generation, every block in
each compiled module's top-level statement list with the fields a consumer
could tell them apart by. Six halves (`.objcmp/u3/u3-lines.txt`; the
population counts one block once per module compilation that holds it):

| created by | blocks | head stamped | `spec_owner` set | `target_type_span` set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the parser (written) | 23,065 | all: 9,817 a definition, 13,248 a primitive (`implement … for i32`) | **0** | all |
| the AST cloner (the monomorphizer's instantiation blocks) | 24,857 | **none** | **all** | none |
| the async lowering (a future's `Future` impl) | 733 | all | 0 | none |
| the C++ binding importer | 0 (no corpus reaches it) | | | |

```cryo
// what a finder that must pass over instantiation blocks asks
if (ib.spec_owner.is_valid()) { continue; }   // the block is a clone placed for an instantiation
```

- `spec_owner` splits the population exactly: set on 24,857 of 24,857
  clones, on 0 of 23,798 others. It is the designed carrier: the
  monomorphizer sets it on every kept clone as soon as the concrete type is
  decided (`monomorphizer.cryo`, before `resolve_specialized_ast`), and the
  placement pass sets it again when the clone goes into a module
  (`specialization.cryo`). From the code (not measured at the finders' own
  point): both writes precede the clone's arrival in any statement list.
- The head stamp splits it too, and by design: the cloner withholds `res`
  (`cloner.cryo`, the `ImplBlockNode` visit), so a stamp-keyed finder never
  matches a clone at all.
- `target_type_span` does NOT: the async lowering's blocks lack it as well.

So the audit's "no mark" held for the fields it looked at, not for the
node: nothing needs adding, and a finder converted to stamps can skip
generated blocks by `spec_owner`, or needs nothing when it matches by stamp.
The measurement point is code generation, after every placement; the
audit's populations (242, 312) were counted elsewhere and are not comparable
one to one.

### 8.342 An import carries the identity of the declaration it binds, copied, instead of an identity built from the import's own module and leaf - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

§8.337 recorded that an imported name is its own `Symbol`, so under the
identity index an import's id has to be copied from the declaration: an
index minted for the import would be a second id for one declaration.
§8.339 measured that copying is value-identical today; this makes it so.

```cryo
// module App - `import std::fmt::{ println };`
// before: the import symbol was admitted like a declaration, and its id built
//         from its own fields - "std::fmt" + "::" + "println"
// after:  it carries the stamp std::fmt's own `println` declaration has
println("x");   // Res::Def(<the declaration's id>) either way; now by copy
```

- `Symbol::import_sym` takes the `DefId` of the declaration the import binds;
  the four import forms pass the exported symbol's own stamp (a glob's export,
  a re-export's, a named entry's - offered by the module or through its
  `export` closure - and a sub-module's export).
- `Resolver::declare_import` no longer admits the symbol as a definition;
  `admit`, the one mint in the name layer, now runs for declarations only.
- `import M as X` still goes through `declare`, so `X` is admitted and
  stamped as the declaration of a new name (`M::X`) exactly as before:
  copying would give it the module's id, and that form is refused downstream,
  so what it names is not changed here.

#### Evidence

- The value question was measured in §8.339's shadow, at these five sites
  with the import's own stamp against the declaration's: **88,022 of 88,022
  agree** (glob 67, named 80,844, sub-module 7,111); the re-export form was
  never entered, and for it the two are equal by construction (the import's
  module is the re-exported symbol's own `source_module`, and an exported
  symbol always has one - only a refused import's binding has none, and it is
  never exported).
- Objects: `objcmp.sh` tip → tree, **0 of 1,126 example objects, 0 of 3,018
  test objects** (predicted 0). `lsp-check` OK (0 errors, 478 warnings),
  `cross-check` OK, 346 compiler warnings, `test-census` OK.
- Rows: `lane-check` unchanged (predicted: the mint in `admit` stays, it runs
  for fewer symbols); residue and `done.py` unchanged.

### 8.343 Option B priced: nine places read an implement block's own parameters through the type's, seven more compare by spelling, and the bottom is visible - measured, nothing landed - 2026-09-26

Jake ruled option B (§8.332's re-key review, `docs/name-resolution-rekey.md`
§9): a parameter an `implement` block writes is the block's own, related to
the type's parameter only through the block's head, as in Rust. The type
table still gives every parameter spelled `T` one type, so today the block's
`T` and the type's `T` ARE one type, and code relating them works without
ever looking at the head. The approved route is converge first, flip last,
and his gate was a count of the places before any flip. This is that count,
measured rather than grepped.

```cryo
type struct Wrap<T> { inner: T; }

implement<T> trait Show for struct Wrap<T>   // this T is the impl's own
where T: Show {
    show(&this) -> i32 { return this.inner.show() + 1; }
}
// Wrap<Num>: every place below that asks "what is the impl's T?" today
// finds Wrap's T bound to Num - by spelling, never through the head.
```

#### The instrument

`scripts/ns-migration/8.343/option-b-probe.patch` (applies to `0aa16644`):

- the flip itself - the forty-fourth session's arena keyed by the
  parameter's declaration (`create_generic_param(sym, name, index)`,
  `GenericParamType.param_sym`, every creator passing its symbol), taken
  from its saved patch WITHOUT its two consumer fixes;
- every lookup the flip makes answer by identity answers by SPELLING
  instead - the answer the table gave before the flip - and prints
  `SHADOW BSPELL <kind> <place>` wherever the identity answer differs. That
  is the substitution (`TypeSubstitution::get`, tagged with the function
  that built the substitution), `lookup_subst_for_param` (tagged with its
  caller), and the ten scans the flip converted from spelling to symbol;
- env `B_STRICT` makes named places answer by identity instead (a list,
  `-list` for all but, or `all`), so each place can be flipped alone.

#### What it measured

1. Six halves under the probe, every place by spelling: **0 failing halves**,
   `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 227 passed; projects: 74 passed)`,
   185,175 BSPELL lines in 14 rows (substitutions by the function that
   built them, `lookup_subst_for_param` as one row; split by caller below).
   `objcmp`, tip against the probe:
   **0 of 1,126 example objects, 0 of 3,018 test objects moved.** So the
   types really are distinct (the lines prove the identity answers differ)
   and nothing but these lookups depends on their being one type: interning,
   id equality and everything else the flip touches changed no object.
   **The bottom is visible** - in this corpus there is no layer below these
   places.
2. Controls, each alone, over the 14 examples: every substitution by
   identity - 14 of 14 fail (E0200 at `net/http/server.cryo:245,266`,
   `json/parser.cryo:326`); every scan by identity - 14 of 14 fail (E0306
   at `io/buf.cryo:541,593`, E0600 at `net/http/conn.cryo:69,108`). These
   are the forty-fourth session's eight locations in its shapes.
3. Each place by identity alone (`per-place.sh`, 01-hello and the shapes),
   then the rest together by `objcmp`'s hash over both populations.

**Places that must bind through the head** - identity breaks a build or
moves an object:

| place (function) | alone by identity |
|---|---|
| `TraitChecker::bounds_satisfied`, fed the template's substitution by the monomorphizer's filter of kept impls | every program fails (`core/result.cryo:190`, `fmt/display.cryo:584`: an impl whose `where T: Eq` fails is kept) |
| `MonoTraitSpecializer::derive_impl_where_generics` | every program fails (`collections/array.cryo:926`) |
| `MethodBinding::subst_method_return_from_receiver` | 01-hello fails (`server.cryo:245`: a combinator's `O` stays abstract) |
| `MethodBinding::scan_param_bounds` | 01-hello fails (`buf.cryo:541`) |
| `MethodBinding::scan_param_bound_param_types` | 01-hello fails (`buf.cryo:541`) |
| `AsyncLower::param_bound_by` (`param_spelled`) | 01-hello fails (`conn.cryo:69`) |
| `CallResolver::try_resolve_generic_return` | `Array::<i32>::default()` fails (shape `f`) |
| `ASTSpecializer::impl_substituter` | builds; with the next, E0636 in `async_receiver_refresh` |
| `Monomorphizer::specialize_with_entry`, its substitution applied to kept impls | moves `AsyncReceiverRefresh.o`; with the previous, E0636 |

The last two are one question answered twice: either alone covers the
other's miss. That is the forty-fourth session's "each layer exposed
another" in miniature, and why a flip-first attempt could not see where it
stood.

**Places that need only their comparison switched** - identity answers
differently, no object moves (all together, hash `x9`: examples 0 of 1,126;
tests: only `AsyncReceiverRefresh.o`, the pair above, and the canary):
`MonoTraitSpecializer::bind_where_arg_param`,
`MonoCallSpecializer::specialize_method_call`,
`MethodBinding::find_generic_method_on_receiver_bounds` (two scans),
`SymbolicChecker::symbolic_name_is_generic_param`, the call resolver's owner
numeric hints, and `MonoCallSpecializer::specialize_method` - whose
identity answer is the intended fix: `chain_default_param_conflict` stops
failing E0636 and builds (its 45 objects are the only other movers).

Listed by the static census (`rekey.md` §9) and never entered by this
corpus: `for_specialization`, `args_are_outer_param_refs`,
`substitute_derived_params_in_method_bodies`, `refuse_elided_template_params`,
`synthesize_default_trait_methods`, `TemplateEntry::new`,
`resolve_trait_impl_method_return`, `ASTSpecializer::specialize`. Absent, not
starved - no identity answer differed there; that they need nothing is not
shown.

#### A live bug the ruling fixes

```cryo
type struct Wrap<T> { inner: T; }
implement<U> trait Show for struct Wrap<U>
where U: Show {
    show(&this) -> i32 { return this.inner.show(); }
}
const w: Wrap<Plain> = ...;   // Plain has no Show; nothing calls show()
```

fails E0358 (`no method named show found on type Plain`) with the pin; the
same program spelling the impl's parameter `T` compiles (shapes `d`, `e`).
The where-clause filter reads the impl's bound through the TYPE's parameter
names, so a different spelling makes the bound vacuous and the impl is kept
for a type it excludes. Under option B the first place in the table binds
`U` through the head and the filter drops the impl.

#### What the count means for the plan

- The flip, from the saved patch: about 150 lines added and 130 removed in
  15 compiler files, mechanical (every parameter creator passes its symbol).
- Converge: nine places to bind through the head. Two of them
  (`scan_param_bounds`, `scan_param_bound_param_types`) and two of the
  seven below (the `find_generic_method_on_receiver_bounds` scans) share
  one shape - a field of `this` typed with the TYPE's parameter, a bound
  written on the impl's - and may have one upstream fix: `this` inside an
  impl body typed through the head. That is a hypothesis; the table is the
  measurement.
- Seven places switch their comparison to the symbol at the flip. The
  `lookup_subst_for_param` callers never seen in 01-hello and the shapes
  (`unsatisfied_trait_ref`, `bounds_satisfied_at_depth`, method binding's
  two) answered by identity in the hash runs and moved nothing.
- A converge step can land while parameters are keyed by spelling: binding
  the impl's parameter through the head gives the same type the spelling
  gave, so a program spelling both alike cannot move. A program spelling
  them differently (the bug above) CAN change - from refused to compiled.

Population caveat: the corpus is the six halves; a place no program here
reaches is not measured.

Reproduce: `git apply scripts/ns-migration/8.343/option-b-probe.patch`,
`make cryo`, copy the compiler out, run the corpus
(`scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh`), `objcmp.sh`, and
`scripts/ns-migration/8.343/per-place.sh <compiler> <B_STRICT values>`.
The "seven" hash ran `hash-tree.sh` under `B_STRICT=-` followed by the
first eight places of the table (the pair's `specialize_with_entry` left
answering by identity), and compared it to the probe's own hash.

### 8.344 Reference mutability at a call, priced: no written code passes a shared reference where an exclusive one is wanted; 171 places would need the new borrow operator, about 30 hand-written calls mutate through an immutable receiver, and the async lowering writes several hundred more - measured, nothing built - 2026-09-26

Nothing checks reference mutability at a call. Jake asked for the blast
radius before deciding whether the check and its operator are a unit or a
project. Cryo has the type `mut &T` but no expression that borrows
exclusively, so the operator and the check land together; this measures
what both would meet.

```cryo
function bump(c: mut &Count) -> void { c.n = c.n + 1; }

const k: Count = Count { n: 0 };
bump(&k);      // accepted: `&k` is shared, the parameter exclusive
k.next();      // accepted: `next(mut &this)` on a const binding
```

#### The instrument

`scripts/ns-migration/8.344/mutref-probe.patch` (on `0aa16644`) prints one
`SHADOW MUTREF` line, with the source position, for:

- `arg` - an argument checked against a `mut &T` parameter whose type is a
  SHARED reference (`&x` is typed shared at a call, so this is where
  `bump(&k)` lands), with what `x` is;
- `recv` - a call of a `mut &this` method, with what its receiver is;
- `amp` - `&x` typed `mut &T` from an expected `mut &T` (never fired).

A place is classed by its root binding: a `mut` or `const` local, a shared
or exclusive reference, a raw pointer, a field of one of those. The control,
`scripts/ns-migration/8.344/control/`, has every shape once and is classed
correctly: `bump(&k)` const, `bump(&m)` mut, `bump(r)` with `r: &Count`,
`k.next()`, `r.next()`, `this.next()` in a `&this` and in a `mut &this`
method.

Population: the compiler compiled by the probe (`compiler/`, which the LSP
also links) and the six-half corpus (LSP, unit suite, projects, project
tests, examples, negatives; every program compiles the stdlib it imports).
`OVERALL FAIL` in the corpus's `make test` half is the probe's own output
tripping `projection_bound_leaf_collision`'s `output_excludes` ("iter.cryo");
built alone it passes, and the run reports 0 failing halves.
Tally: `mutref-tally.py`, distinct source positions, the populations that
compile one file merged.

#### What it found

| what the check would meet | distinct places |
|---|---|
| a shared-reference VARIABLE passed for `mut &T` (`bump(r)`) | **0** |
| `&x` of an immutable binding passed for `mut &T` (`bump(&k)`) | **0** |
| `&x` of a mutable place passed for `mut &T` - legal, but needs the new operator | **171** (compiler 11, stdlib 56, tests 102, examples 12, LSP 54 before merging) |
| a written call mutating through an immutable receiver | **30**: 15 in methods that write no receiver (the parser supplies `&this`), 9 in methods written `&this`, 6 on a `const` local or a shared reference |
| explicit `x.drop()` on a binding read as immutable | **73** (some are `mut` pattern bindings the probe cannot see as mutable; all are W0015's explicit destructor calls) |
| calls the async lowering synthesizes on an immutable receiver | **541**, plus 155 unclear |
| unclear (raw-pointer deref, call results, indexing, globals) | 113 |

```cryo
// the 15: a method with no receiver written gets `&this` from the parser
collect_doc_comments() -> void {     // compiler/src/compiler/parser/parser_base.cryo
    this.push_doc(tok);              // push_doc(mut &this)
}
// the 9: written `&this`, mutating anyway
advance(&this) -> char {             // compiler/src/compiler/lex/lexer.cryo
    this.current_location.increment_char(c);   // increment_char(mut &this)
}
```

The split between those two rows reads each method's header line with a
regex and is approximate; the 24 together are the measurement.

The 541 are not 541 edits: they are the calls the async lowering writes
into poll bodies (the probe gives them the nearest source span - an `async`
header, an `await` operand, even a comment). And the 74 `field<deref<ptr>>`
places are written code inside `async` methods (`this.conn.queue_frame(..)`),
where the lowering has already turned `this` into a raw pointer - a check
run after lowering cannot see the method's declared receiver at all.

#### What it means

- The core hole Jake named - a shared reference accepted for an exclusive
  one - occurs in NO written code measured: 0 `bump(r)` shapes, 0
  `bump(&k)` shapes.
- The operator is 171 rewrites, mechanical.
- The check itself meets three things that are not edits: what a method
  with no written receiver means (15 places, all in the compiler - a
  language question), the async lowering (its synthesized receivers, and
  checking an `async` method's body before `this` becomes a pointer), and
  `x.drop()` (73, already slated by W0015). Around 30 hand-written calls
  need a receiver or binding made `mut`.
- So it is a project, not a unit - for the async lowering and the implicit
  receiver, not for the edit count.

Classifier limits, measured on the control and the samples: a `mut this`
by-value receiver reads as const (3 places, set aside), and a `mut` pattern
binding reads as const (inside the 73). Places no program here compiles are
not measured.

### 8.345 The eight bare-name finders are convertible without a definition table, but every caller is in the editor's handlers - assessed, not converted, BLOCKED on Jake - 2026-09-26

Eight functions in `compiler/src/compiler/AST/node_locator.cryo` find a
declaration by the LAST segment of its name, first match wins; with `Item`
declared in two modules, go-to-definition on one lands on the other's. They
were blocked on a "declaration from this identity" lookup.

```cryo
// module A: type struct Item { .. }     module B: type struct Item { .. }
const x: B::Item = ...;   // hover / go-to-definition on `Item`
// find_type_decl_in_modules(graph, intern, "B::Item") matches the leaf
// "Item" and returns whichever module's declaration it walks first
```

Read, not probed (the counts are greps: `grep -rn "<finder>(" tools/CryoLSP
compiler/src --include=*.cryo`):

- The eight: `find_type_decl_in_modules` (16 calls), `find_method_in_modules`
  (6), `find_field_in_modules` (5), `find_function_in_modules` (2),
  `find_const_in_modules`, `find_trait_method_in_modules`,
  `find_impls_of_type`, `find_impls_of_trait` (1 each) - **33 calls, every
  one in `tools/CryoLSP/src/handlers/`** (`definition.cryo`, `hover.cryo`,
  `code_lens.cryo`); none in `compiler/src`. The ninth copy of the matcher is
  `HoverEngine::format_impl_methods` (`hover.cryo`).
- **No DefId -> declaration table is needed.** Every type and function
  declaration carries its own `.def` (stamped at registration), so a finder
  keeps its walk and matches `d.def.equals(def)`; a method or field matches
  its owner by `def` (an implement block by `target_def()`) and the member by
  its name within that one owner. Generated implement blocks drop out by
  construction (the cloner withholds the head's resolution), except for
  `find_impls_of_trait`, which must skip a block with `spec_owner` set -
  §8.341's mark.
- **Most callers hold an identity already**: a member access's receiver type
  answers `DeclarationIndex::def_of`; a scope segment carries `scope_res`; a
  named annotation, an enum pattern and a struct literal carry their
  resolution; an implement head has `target_def()`; code lens holds the
  declaration node.
- **Not mechanical**: about seven hover fallbacks whose name has no identity
  behind it (a generic parameter's spelling, annotation text, the owner
  returned as a name by `find_enclosing_method_owner`),
  `find_function_in_modules` (the callee's identity would come from an
  `OverloadId`, not checked), and `find_const_in_modules`, called for a
  fresh match-arm binding with no referent at all.

**Why nothing was converted.** Changing a finder's parameter from a name to
an identity changes all 33 call sites, and they are the editor's own
handlers - which Jake ruled out of scope until the compiler's migration is
done - and whether the finders land before merge at all is an open question
of his. Converting the finders alone would leave identity-taking functions
nobody calls. The lookup the earlier sessions were waiting for is not the
obstacle any more; the scope ruling is.

### 8.346 A definition's identity is a position in a table only its own module can extend, and its name is a lookup: `DefId` is an index into `DefTable` - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

The identity index `docs/defid-index-plan.md` proposed, built to the four
properties Jake approved. Before, a `DefId` WAS its path, so anything holding
a string could make one and anything holding one could read the string back
out. Now it is a number that only the table in `compiler/resolver/res.cryo`
can hand out, and its path is something you ask the table for.

```cryo
// before: the id was the name
const d: DefId = DefId::of_definition(intern("std::fs::Path"));
const s: SymbolStr = d.qualified_name();

// after: registered once where the declaration is, named by a lookup
const d: DefId = defs.register(fs_module, intern("Path"), DefKind::Type, span);
const s: SymbolStr = defs.path_of(d);            // "std::fs::Path"

// anywhere outside compiler/resolver/res.cryo:
const forged: DefId = DefId { index: 3 };
// error[E0353]: field `index` of `compiler::resolver::res::DefId` is private
//   private field reached outside module `compiler::resolver::res`
```

#### The four properties

1. **The type and its creator share a module; the field stays `private`.**
   `DefTable` sits beside `DefId` in `res.cryo`. This needed the pins
   refreshed first (`55bdd2cc`): the old pin was built before `private`
   became module-scoped, and refused `DefTable` building a `DefId` with the
   old type-scoped wording. No field was widened.
2. **The creator takes a declaration's place, not a path.**
   `register(parent: DefId, leaf, kind, span)` always appends and composes
   the path itself from the parent's path and the leaf; it never looks
   anything up. As far as the approved shape allows: the leaf is still a
   string. There is no "find by path".
3. **No accessor for the insides.** `DefId::qualified_name()` is deleted;
   the 58 places that read a name out of an id ask `defs.path_of(d)`
   (`scripts/ns-migration/8.346/name_reads_to_table.py`; one continuation
   line in `call_resolver.cryo` was joined by hand). Nothing returns the
   number.
4. **A guard that both types keep a private field.** `DefId` was already in
   `lane-gate.py`'s `SEALED_TYPES`; `DefTable` is added, with the reason: with
   its arrays public, any module could rewrite a path and an existing id
   would name something its registrar never declared.

**The rule written on `DefId`: the number never reaches output and is never
persisted or compared across builds** - it follows registration order, which
follows module discovery, which follows the filesystem and differs between
hosts.

#### Who registers, and who copies

| registers an id | what |
|---|---|
| `ModuleGraph::add_module` | each module (a root; its leaf is the namespace path it declares) |
| `Resolver::admit` (name layer) | each module-level declaration: type, function, method, intrinsic, constant, global, module symbol. **A local, parameter or generic parameter gets none** - named by its `SymbolID` |
| `PassRegistry::primitive_def` | the 19 primitives, once per compilation (the stage runs per module; it now registers only when `void` has no id yet) |
| `CompilationContext::register_in_module` | what a lowering creates: a closure's struct, an async future, the body an `async main` is renamed to |
| the monomorphizer | each instantiation, beside its template (`DefKind::Instance`) |

Everything else copies: `register_type` takes the id the name layer stamped
on the declaration node (it made one of its own before, equal only by
name); the reverse-only registration takes the specialized type's
registered id; an import copies (§8.342).

A C import's module (`extern module llvm := "C" { .. }`) is a module no file
holds, so the graph did not know it and its functions had no parent; the
graph's module-by-path table (`module_defs`) now holds both kinds, the second
written where the name layer declares the import's alias
(`bind_c_import_module`).

#### References written before their declaration exists

Jake's wrinkle: the parser writes three references to language items (a
desugared `for` names `Iterator::next`, `a..b` names `Range`, `x ?? d` names
`Option`'s variants) before any declaration is registered, and items are
claimed in the type-declaration stage, after name resolution.

```cryo
for (x in xs) { }        // the parser writes `__it.next()` naming Iterator::next
const r = 0..n;          // `Range::new(0, n)`, naming the language's Range
```

The slot now holds the item (`ResSlot::Lang(LangItem)`, which no resolver
may answer by looking the leaf up), the node goes on a list on the context,
and the end of each module's type declarations answers every listed
reference whose item has been claimed with the claimed id
(`PassRegistry::settle_lang_refs`). `LangItem` moved to
`compiler/resolver/lang_item.cryo` so the name layer's slot can hold one
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.346/move_lang_item.py`).

The C importer had the same shape: it builds a record's field and alias
types before anything is declared. Each such reference is listed with its C
tag; the importer pins it to the declaration it emitted for that tag (the C
header's namespace is the importer's own), and the end of name declaration
answers it with that declaration's id (`NameDeclarationPass::settle_c_refs`).
A first cut left these unanswered, and the shadow corpus caught it:
`ffi_c_import`'s tests failed with E0900.

#### Evidence

- **Shadow, six halves** (`scripts/ns-migration/8.346/index-shadow.patch`
  on this commit; `.objcmp/s50a-lines.txt`): the new id carried the old
  name beside it, the old answer was returned everywhere, and a SHADOW line
  was printed at any registration whose composed path differed from the old
  string, any `path_of` whose table path differed, any `equals` whose index
  answer differed from the name answer, and any copied registration whose
  path differed. **Every count of a difference is 0**, over: 26,272,370 path
  reads, 21,760 type registrations, 7,426 modules, 16,331 instantiations,
  16,331 reverse registrations, 740 async futures, 43 closure structs, 4
  renamed async mains, 153 language-item references, 2,166 primitive
  registrations (19 per compilation). Suite under the shadow: `OVERALL FAIL
  (unit: ok; compile-fail: 227 passed; projects: 73 passed, 1 failed)` - the
  one failure the C-import gap above; after the fix, `ffi_c_import`'s tests
  19 passed, 0 failed, both of its references answered with ids whose paths
  agree.
- **Locals**: the shadow registered 682,359 locals, parameters and generic
  parameters; not one was read by path, compared or asked whether valid.
  They are no longer registered.
- **Objects**: `scripts/objcmp/objcmp.sh` `55bdd2cc` → tree: **0 of 1,126 example objects, 0 of 3,018 test objects** (`.objcmp/s50/objcmp.out`), and the suite under it `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 227 passed; projects: 74 passed)`.
  Predicted 0.
- `lsp-check` OK (0 errors, 478 warnings); `cross-check` OK; compiler
  warnings 346 (unchanged).
- **Control on the seal**: `DefId { index: 3 }` written in `sema.cryo` is
  refused, E0353 above, by the compiler under test.

#### Rows

`make lane-check`, re-pinned. Predicted `REGISTER` 70 → 41 (every
`register_type` call now passes an id): held. Not predicted, each a
registration point: `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 50 → 55 (the table's five callers - the
creator takes a leaf), `GRAPH_READ` 32 → 34 (a declaration's parent module
asked of the graph by path, in the name layer and for a lowering's
declaration), `GRAPH_WRITE` 0 → 1 (`bind_c_import_module`).

The gate itself changed, as the brief asked: **the row counting the
creator's callers is deleted** (`DEFID_MINT`, which counted
`DefId::of_definition(`): construction is now refused by the language, so it
counted something that cannot happen. The row counting names read back out
is retargeted, `DEFID_UNWRAP` (`.qualified_name(`) → `DEFID_PATH`
(`.path_of(`), **61**. Mutation pairs (a copy of `compiler/src`, each
mutation alone):

- `DefTable`'s `private:` label deleted: the OLD gate's sealed-type check
  says OK; the NEW gate refuses (`DefTable ... has no private field`).
- one extra `defs.path_of(..)` read in `sema.cryo`: the old row's regex
  matches 0 in the tree either way; the new row reads 61 → 62.

`lane-gate.py`'s placement tables gained three entries, each placed rather
than counted: `DefTable` as an array exclusion (indexed by position, never
searched), and two inline scans as DATA - `Importer.type_decl_tags` (the C
header's own tags) and `CompilationContext.c_ref_alias` (which import made a
pending reference).

#### Overloads

Two overloads of `f` are two declarations, so now two registrations and two
ids with one path; before, they were one id. The shadow's `equals` check
says nothing compared two such ids in this corpus. Jake has ruled both kinds
of overloading stay (§0.1 D35): the composed-name lookups on condition
one's list will return the SET of candidates, which is what separate ids
make expressible.

#### Rulings recorded

§0.1 gains D33-D39 for the rulings relayed at the start of this session, and
condition one gains the finders' written exception with its reason and the
condition that lifts it (D38).

#### Found, not acted on

- **A module has two ids.** The graph registers `a::b`; the name layer's
  module symbol for it is registered too, with the parent `a::b` and the
  leaf `a::b`, so its path is `a::b::a::b`. That is what the old code
  computed (the shadow agreed), and 3,985 path reads over the corpus read

- **Instantiations are still registered** (16,331 in the corpus). Jake has
  ruled they stop getting identities; the clone's readers need the
  instantiation's own handle first. `DefKind::Instance` marks them.
- The renamed `async main` body's node still carries the name layer's stamp

  where it was renamed.
- `make check-fast` takes about seven minutes on this host, not ten

#### Reproduce

### 8.347 The monomorphizer's filter of kept implement blocks checks an impl's `where` bounds against the parameters its own head binds - converge step one of nine, one kind of program goes from refused to compiled - 2026-09-26

The first place §8.343 priced, taken as Jake ruled (§0.1 D39): an implement
block's parameters are its own and relate to the type's only through the
block's head.

```cryo
type struct Wrap<T> { inner: T; }

implement<U> trait Show for struct Wrap<U>     // U is the impl's own
where U: Show {
    show(&this) -> i32 { return this.inner.show() + 1; }
}

const p: Wrap<Plain> = ...;   // Plain has no Show; nothing calls p.show()
// before: error[E0358]: no method named `show` found on type `Plain`
//         (the filter looked `U` up among Wrap's parameter NAMES, found no
//         `U`, read the bound as vacuous, and kept the impl for Wrap<Plain>)
// after:  U is bound to Plain through the head `Wrap<U>`, the bound fails,
//         and the impl is dropped for Wrap<Plain> - kept for Wrap<Num>
```

Spelled `T` like the type's parameter, the same program always compiled:
the filter's bindings were the type's, and a same-spelled impl parameter
happened to find them.

- `TraitChecker::add_head_param_bindings(impl, args, subst)`: each
  parameter the head writes as a target argument, bound to the
  instantiation's argument in that position. The trait checker's own
  nested check (`impl_bounds_hold`) already bound this way, inline; it now
  calls the helper.
- `MonoTraitSpecializer::filter_bounds_violating_impls` checks
  `impl.where_bounds` against those bindings instead of the template's
  substitution.

Parameters are still keyed by spelling (the arena flip has not happened),
so for a head spelling its parameters as the type does, the bindings are the
ones the template's substitution gave - nothing that compiled can move. What
can change is the other spelling, from refused to compiled.

#### Evidence

- New project `tests/tests/projects/impl_param_bound_through_head` (the
  program above plus a `Wrap<Num>` whose `show()` runs; `run`, exit 7).
  Under the compiler without this change: `E0358 no method named show found
  on type Plain`. With it: builds, exits 7. Roster golden merged, +1
  (`make roster-check ARGS=--merge`).
- `objcmp.sh` `88be88be` → tree: **0 of 1,126 example objects**; test
  objects: 54 changed, **every one the new project's own** (the old
  compiler cannot build it); suite `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
  227 passed; projects: 75 passed)`. Predicted exactly that.
- `lsp-check` OK (0 errors, 478 warnings); `cross-check` OK; 346 compiler
  warnings.

#### Where converge stands

Eight places of §8.343's nine remain, then the seven comparisons, then the
arena flip that retires condition one's six parameter scans
(`TemplateEntry::param_names[]` and the rest). This step retires none of
them by itself.

Reproduce: `bash scripts/objcmp/objcmp.sh`; the project alone with
`cryo build tests/tests/projects/impl_param_bound_through_head`.
