### 8.348 Converge, the other eight places: an implement block's parameters are read through its head everywhere §8.343 counted, and three more kinds of program go from refused to compiled - 2026-09-26

The rest of §8.343's table, taken as Jake ruled (§0.1 D39) and as one
mechanism: an implement block's parameters are its own and relate to its
owner's only through the head, so every place that related them by
spelling now relates them by position in the head.

```cryo
type struct Wrap<T> { inner: T; }

implement<U> trait Make for struct Wrap<U> where U: Make {
    static make() -> Wrap<U> { return Wrap::<U> { inner: U::make() }; }
}
const w: Wrap<Num> = Wrap::<Num>::make();
// before: error[E0200]: expected `Wrap<Num>`, found `Wrap<U>` - the turbofish
//         bound Wrap's `T`, and nothing related `T` to the impl's `U`
// after:  `U` is `T`'s position in the head `Wrap<U>`, so the return is Wrap<Num>
```

#### The mechanism, three directions of one relation

`TraitChecker::head_param_type(impl, i)` - the parameter the head writes
at position `i` - is the one creator; everything below goes through it.

1. **The impl's parameters bound to an instantiation's arguments**
   (`add_head_param_bindings`, step one's helper).  The monomorphizer
   (`MonoTraitSpecializer::head_bindings`) now filters an impl's METHODS by
   it as well as the impl, and resolves each kept impl's clone under it
   rather than under the template's substitution - which is all
   `derive_impl_where_generics` ever read.  Places:
   `MonoTraitSpecializer::derive_impl_where_generics`,
   `Monomorphizer::specialize_with_entry`.  `ASTSpecializer::impl_substituter`
   already bound through the head; its pair's miss was the other half, now
   gone.
2. **The impl's parameters bound to the owner's own**, for the declaration
   index.  A method's return is written in the impl's parameters and every
   reader of the index substitutes the OWNER's into it (a receiver's
   arguments, a turbofish).  `TypeResolutionPasses::register_returns_through_head`
   re-registers each return with the impl's parameters bound to the owner's
   through the head - after the block's methods are registered, and again
   after the `async` lowering re-registers a method with its future type
   (`repoint_method`), which is the half the first build missed (below).
   Places: `MethodBinding::subst_method_return_from_receiver`,
   `CallResolver::try_resolve_generic_return`.
3. **The owner's parameters read as the impl's**
   (`add_owner_to_head_bindings`, `owner_type_through_head`).  Sema walks a
   generic impl's methods with `this` typed as the bare TEMPLATE
   (`Sema::visit(ImplBlockNode*)`: `impl_owner(node)`), so a type computed
   from a field of `this` names the owner's parameters while the impl's
   bounds - its own and its methods' - name the impl's:

   ```cryo
   implement<S> trait AsyncWrite for struct BufStream<S> {
       async flush(mut &this) -> .. where S: AsyncTransport {
           await this.inner.write_from(out);   // this.inner: BufStream's S
   ```

   The two bound scans and the `async` lowering's frame fields read such a
   type through the head first.  Places: `MethodBinding::scan_param_bounds`,
   `MethodBinding::scan_param_bound_param_types` (both entered through
   `lookup_method_through_param_bounds` / `param_types_through_param_bounds`,
   which now take the parameter's TYPE, not its spelling), and
   `AsyncLower::param_spelled` (through `through_owner_head`, the record
   carrying the owning block).  Retyping `this` as `Wrap<U>` in sema is the
   upstream alternative; it was not taken - it changes every generic body's
   field types, not only an impl's.

   One ambiguity is left in place while parameters are keyed by spelling: a
   head that SWAPS them (`implement<B, A> .. for Pair<B, A>` over
   `Pair<A, B>`) makes the arena type `A` both the owner's first parameter
   and the impl's second, and no type can say which it means.  Such a
   position is skipped (the reading stays as before); after the arena flip
   the two are two types and nothing is skipped.

#### Evidence

- **Shapes** (`scripts/ns-migration/8.348/shapes`, each with a

### 8.350 The arena flip, measured with no build: one layer below option B's count - a method's owner parameters are returned unsubstituted when the receiver's arguments are abstract - STOPPED, a live bug recorded - 2026-09-26

The combined compiler of §8.348 (the probe plus the nine places) under
`B_STRICT=all` IS the flip, every comparison by identity.  Six-half corpus
(`corpus2.sh`, run in a second worktree): every project builds except the
canary `chain_default_param_conflict`, which COMPILES (the predicted
mover); no parameter reaches the arena without a symbol (0 `BNOSYM`).  But
the unit suite does not build: 27 x E0600, e.g. `stdlib/net/ws/conn.cryo:222`.

```cryo
async function run<X>(x: X) -> i64 where X: Tick {
    mut h: Holder<X> = Holder::<X> { inner: x };    // Holder is `Holder<S>`
    const a: i64 = await h.drain();
    return a;
}
// error[E0600]: a generic async function cannot carry a value of type
//   `Option<Holder$drain$Future_0<S>>` across a suspend
```

`MethodBinding::subst_method_return_from_receiver` returns the callee
OWNER's parameters unsubstituted when the receiver's arguments are
abstract (its "symbolic walk" early return), so the awaited future is typed
with `Holder`'s `S`, not the caller's `X`.  By spelling it works only when
the caller spells its parameter as the owner does.  **A live bug today,
independent of the flip**: the program above is E0600 under `cf230067` and
under `fb6114bd`; spelled `S`, it builds and exits 42 under both.  The
probe of §8.343 could not see it: it prints where an identity answer
DIFFERS from the spelling's, and this place does not answer.  Not routed
around; the arena flip waits on it.  The fix it suggests - substitute the
receiver's arguments even when abstract, as they are the caller's own
parameters - is not built: whether it is in scope is Jake's.

`corpus2.sh` reported "failing halves: 1" over the unit half's build
failure: its unit half prints `make test exit=2` and counts nothing when
the suite fails before its summary line.  Recorded, not changed.

### 8.352 A receiver whose arguments are the caller's parameters substitutes them: a generic caller spelling its parameter unlike the owner's compiles - 0 objects moved; the arena flip then stops one layer further down - 2026-09-26

§8.350's live bug, taken as Jake answered in plain text ("if scoping it out
unblocks completing unit 2, sure" - read as: in scope because it unblocks
the flip; said back to him).

```cryo
async function run<X>(x: X) -> i64 where X: Tick {
    mut h: Holder<X> = Holder::<X> { inner: x };    // Holder is `Holder<S>`
    const a: i64 = await h.drain();
    return a;
}
// before: E0600 - the awaited future typed `Holder$drain$Future_0<S>`
// after:  typed with `X`; builds, exits 42
```

`MethodBinding::subst_method_return_from_receiver` gave up when the
receiver's arguments were abstract and handed back the callee owner's own
parameters.  They are the CALLER's parameters, so they are substituted like
any others; for a concrete receiver an answer that stays abstract still
yields the return unchanged, as before.

#### Evidence

- Project `generic_caller_receiver_args` (exit 42): E0600 under the
  compiler without the change, 42 with it.  Spelled `S` like the owner,
  the same program builds under both.  Roster merged (+1).
- Objects against `58963767`: **0 of 1,126 example and 0 of 3,234 test
  objects** (the suite before the project was added); suite `OVERALL PASS`.
  lsp-check OK (478 warnings), cross-check OK.

#### The flip, measured again: the next layer

The combined compiler (§8.348's, plus §8.349 and this) under
`B_STRICT=all`, six halves: the 27 E0600 are gone; every project builds
but the canary `chain_default_param_conflict`, which compiles (the
predicted mover); one error in the unit suite:

```cryo
implement struct GenConn<S> {
    async wrapped(mut &this, n: i64) -> i64 where S: GenTick {
        const v: i64 = await GenCombine::boxed(0, this.pump(n));
// error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve 'GenCombine::boxed'
//   (tests/lang/async_receiver_refresh.cryo:282)
```

The same root as §8.348's three consumer-side translations: sema walks a
generic impl's methods with `this` typed as the bare TEMPLATE, so a type
computed from `this` - a field, and here a method's return - names the
OWNER's parameters.  `boxed`'s `F` is inferred as `pump`'s future over
`GenConn`'s `S`; keyed by declaration, the monomorphizer binds the impl's
`S` and not the owner's, the call's bindings stay abstract, and `boxed` is
never specialized.  This is §8.343's `impl_substituter` /
`specialize_with_entry` pair's E0636, now with a mechanism.  The fix it
points at is typing `this` in a generic impl as its head's instantiation
(`GenConn<S>` over the impl's own `S`), which would make §8.348's
owner-to-head translations unnecessary.  Not built: a change to how sema
walks every generic impl, a layer §8.343 did not count, recorded as the
brief requires.

Reproduce: `git apply scripts/ns-migration/8.348/combined.patch`
on `cf230067`, then this commit's and §8.349's compiler diffs, `make cryo`,
and `B_STRICT=all bash scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh all`.

#### The corpus script's unit half

`scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh` echoed the unit suite's and the direct LSP
build's exit codes but counted neither: `failing halves` counted only the
halves run through `run_half`.  The unit suite is ONE program, so a build
error aborts it before any test runs - after it has printed the SHADOW

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `.objcmp/s51/corpus5` | exit 2, `(1 errors ..)` | none | 3,423 | `failing halves: 1` | `failing halves: 2`, same line with `(1 errors)`; exit 1 |

#### A compiler warning total is not evidence from an incremental build

`instance.cryo:1989`: a module reused from cache skips the stage after
monomorphization - generic validation, the move check, the dead-code lint,
drop insertion - and its warnings are never replayed.  The front end's
warnings are reported for every module, so only that stage's move.  On
`3093959d` (a copy outside the repo, the pin building the compiler):

| build | warnings | unused-variable |
|---|---|---|
| clean | 346 | 9 |
| clean again | 346 | 9 |
| comment added to `diag/_module.cryo` (imported everywhere) | 346 | 9 |
| comment added to `CLI/commands.cryo` (a leaf) | **337** | **0** |

The count is deterministic per source; what varies is which modules the
edit made the build recompile.  §8.348's "one intermediate build printed
342 .. the W0001 total is not a stable instrument" is this, misread: its
two builds differed in `type_resolution.cryo` and `async_lower.cryo`, and
the warnings that vanished were in modules that edit did not make it
recompile (inferred from the mechanism; that build's log is not kept per
module).  §8.320 had diagnosed it correctly -
"an incremental build loses warnings of modules it does not recompile; it
is not a count to read" - and it was lost, because a finding that lives
only in an entry's prose is not read by the next session.  It now lives
in §0.3 as a gate row, with a check that reads the skip itself, so the row
fails the day the skip changes.

Every earlier entry that cites a compiler warning total (§8.60, §8.73,
§8.299, §8.323, §8.325, §8.329, §8.347, §8.348) rests its conclusion on
objects moved and the suite, not on the total, so none changes.  The
editor's totals (478, 486, 490) are clean: `lsp-gate.py` deletes its build
directory first.

Not fixed here, and not in this unit: an incremental and a clean build
disagree about the same source for a user too - a comment edited in one
file and nine real warnings vanish.  Replaying a reused module's warnings
is a compiler change, and reaches `make cryo` only through a re-pin.

### 8.354 Section 0's rows share one parse of `compiler/src` per run: `ns-status-check` 305 s -> 120 s, every row's output byte-identical; and the rows run in WSL's bash - 2026-09-25

Approved by Jake (relayed in plain text 2026-09-25) as a script change
that relaxes nothing.

#### Where the time went

Timed per row (each command `ns-status-check` runs, wall clock, over
`3840f8c3`): 305.5 s for 411 rows, of which 19 `lane-gate.py` rows, 4
`residue.py` rows and `done.py --outstanding` (which runs `residue.py
--check`) each spent ~10 s in the same work - `lane-gate.py`'s `scan()`
(10.5 s alone: `place_inline_scans` 4.5 s, `place_array_owners` 2.1 s) or
`residue.py`'s `population()`, over the same unchanged tree.

#### The change

`scripts/parse_cache.py`: `memo(label, scripts, src, compute)` returns
`compute()`, or the answer an earlier call in the same run computed from
byte-identical inputs - the key is a SHA-256 over the scripts' bytes and
every `.cryo` file's path and bytes under the source tree, so a tree or a
script changed mid-run is parsed afresh.  It is inert unless
`CRYO_PARSE_CACHE` names a directory; only `ns-status-check` sets it, to a
directory it makes for the run and deletes after.  `lane-gate.py` memoizes
`scan()`, `residue.py` memoizes `population()`; nothing else changed in
either.

#### The rows run in WSL, and the first cut cached nothing

The first cut made the directory with `tempfile.mkdtemp` and measured
**299.9 s - no faster**.  The cause: `ns-status-check` refuses unless
`shutil.which("bash")` finds a bash (Git Bash here), then runs
`subprocess.run(["bash", ..])`, which Windows resolves by its own search
order - System32 first - to **WSL's** `bash.exe`
(`uname -sr` from inside: `Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`;
`command -v python3`: `/usr/bin/python3`).  Every §0 row on this host runs
in WSL, over `/mnt/c`.  A Windows environment variable reaches WSL only
when `WSLENV` names it, so the rows never saw `CRYO_PARSE_CACHE`, and a
`C:\..` directory would not have opened there anyway.  Now: the directory
is made by the rows' own shell (`bash -c 'mktemp -d'`), the variable is
passed with `WSLENV=CRYO_PARSE_CACHE/u` (any other bash ignores
`WSLENV`), and the run checks that the rows' shell can SEE it
(`test -d`), printing a note and parsing per row when it cannot - so a
cache that silently does nothing, which is what the first cut was, now
says so.  Which shell runs the rows is recorded in §0.4; changing it is
not this unit.

#### Evidence

Both sides in a clone of `3840f8c3` outside the repository, every row's
full output recorded (`scripts/ns-migration/8.354/nsdump.py`; `compare.py` beside it diffs two recordings):

| tree | scripts | exit | total | rows | rows whose full output differs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `3840f8c3` | before | 0, `OK -- 411 §0 row(s)` | 305.5 s | 411 | - |
| `3840f8c3` | after | 0, `OK -- 411 §0 row(s)` | **120.1 s** | 411, same commands in order | **0** |
| one `defs.path_of(` line deleted from `call_resolver.cryo` | before | **1** (DEFID_PATH row 61 -> 60) | 317.5 s | 411 | - |
| the same mutation | after | **1** | 122.1 s | 411 | **0** |

The remaining time is two first parses (~11 s each), `impl-head-elided-params.py`
(3.2 s), one `git ls-files | xargs grep` (2.6 s) and ~0.2 s of WSL start-up
per row.  `ns-guard-selftest.py` with the new scripts: `OK -- 19 case(s)`.

`parse_cache.py --selftest` (a §0 row): 8 cases - inert without the
variable, a hit on an identical tree, a miss on a changed / added / removed
source file and on a changed script, a non-`.cryo` file ignored, a failed
computation not stored - **8 of 8** under Windows Python and under WSL's

#### Condition three's written reasons, counted

### 8.355 Warnings an incremental build does not report: the mechanism, and why a warning total is evidence only from a clean build - FILED (D40) - 2026-09-25

This is the third description of one defect.  §8.320 found it and said
"it is not a count to read"; §8.348, twenty-eight entries later, saw it
again and called the unused-variable total "not a stable instrument" - a
wrong mechanism (noise) for a deterministic one.  The first description
lived only in an entry's prose, which the next session did not read.  This
entry is the mechanism; D40 in §0.1 is the ruling and carries the check;
§0.3's warning row is the rule, where the gates are read.

#### The mechanism

A project build is incremental per module.  `instance.cryo` computes a key
for each module (`instance.cryo:1800-1931`): the module's source hash
folded over the source hashes of its transitive import closure, plus a
toolchain fingerprint (the compiler, the optimization level, debug info).
A module is REUSED when the previous build's manifest holds the same key
and its object file is still on disk (`:1934-1947`); anything the key
cannot prove - an unattributable specialization, a short import closure -
disables reuse.

Every module is still parsed, name-resolved and type-checked: the front
end's warnings are reported for all of them.  The stage after
monomorphization - `GenericValidation`, `FunctionBodyTypeCheck`,
`MoveCheck`, `DeadCodeAnalysis`, `DropInsertion`, `TypeLowering`
(`:1963-1968`) - is SKIPPED for a reused module:

```cryo
if (pm_active && pm_cached[order[i] as i64]) { continue; }   // instance.cryo:1989
```

The comment above it is right about errors (a reused module compiled
clean the build that produced its object) and silent about warnings: the
warnings that stage emitted for the module in the earlier build are not
stored, so they are not replayed.  So the unused-variable (W0001),
unused-function (W0002) and unreachable-code (W0009) lints of
`passes/dead_code.cryo`, and any warning the other passes of that stage
emit, are reported ONLY for the modules this build recompiled.
Measured for W0001; the other passes' warnings are inferred to be lost by
the same `continue` and were not measured (the tip emits none of them).

#### What it looks like

The pin building `3093959d`'s compiler, in a copy outside the repository:

| build | warnings | W0001 |
|---|---|---|
| clean (`rm -rf compiler/build`) | 346 | 9 |
| clean again | 346 | 9 |
| incremental, a comment added to `diag/_module.cryo` - in every module's closure, so nothing is reused | 346 | 9 |
| incremental, a comment added to `CLI/commands.cryo` - in almost no module's closure, so almost everything is reused | **337** | **0** |

The count is deterministic per source; what an edit decides is WHICH
modules recompile, and so which modules' post-monomorphization warnings
appear.  The last session's builds read 9, 5, 3 and 0 on sources that
differed only in files unrelated to the warnings that vanished.

For a user it is the same inconsistency: edit a comment, rebuild, and nine
real warnings are gone until something in their modules' closures
changes.  `make incremental-check` does not see it - it compares object
files, not diagnostics.

#### The rule, until it is fixed

1. **A compiler warning total is evidence only from a clean build** -
   `rm -rf compiler/build` (or the project's `build/`) first.
2. **Two builds' warnings compare as SETS** - (code, file, line), e.g.
   `grep -A1 '^warning\[' LOG | paste - - - | sed -E 's/^warning\[(W[0-9]+)\].*--> ([^:]*:[0-9]+).*/\1 \2/' | sort`
   - not as totals: a total can hold still while one warning replaces
   another.
3. The editor's totals from `lsp-check` are clean builds already
   (`lsp-gate.py` deletes its build directory first).

#### Filed, not fixed (D40)

The fix is the compiler storing each module's post-monomorphization
warnings beside its reused object and replaying them on reuse; re-running
the dead-code lint on a reused module alone would not do, since it reads
method targets the skipped stage sets and would report unused methods
falsely.  Because `make cryo` builds the compiler with the pin, a fix
reaches that build's warnings only after a re-pin.  D40's check reads the
skip line, so the day it changes the row fails and this entry is re-read.

### 8.356 The symbolic walk's owner-field and owner-method readers substitute the receiver's arguments: an implement block spelling its parameter unlike the type's compiles - 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

```cryo
type struct Conn<S> {
    inner: S;
    async pump(mut &this, n: i64) -> i64 where S: Tick { .. }
}
implement struct Conn<U> {
    async wrapped(mut &this, n: i64) -> i64 where U: Tick {
        const v: i64 = await Combine::boxed(0, this.pump(n));
        return v;
    }
}
// before: error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve 'Combine::boxed'
// after:  builds, exits 42.  Spelled `implement struct Conn<S>`, both build.
```

`SymbolicChecker::symbolic_resolve_owner_field` and
`symbolic_resolve_owner_method_return` read a field's type or a method's
return off the owner template's AST and handed it back as declared - in the
owner's parameters.  Inside `implement struct Conn<U>` the receiver is
`Conn<U>` (`symbolic_owner_instance`), so `this.pump(n)` was typed with
`S`, a parameter the body does not have; `boxed`'s `F` was bound to it, the
call's bindings stayed abstract, and `boxed` was never specialized.  Both
readers now substitute the receiver instantiation's arguments for the
owner's parameters.  The substitution already existed as
`MethodBinding::subst_method_return_from_receiver` (§8.352); it moved to
`TypeUtils::subst_owner_params_from_receiver` so the symbolic checker, which
`MethodBinding` holds and cannot hold back, calls the same one.  Its five
callers follow it.  Compiler: 54+ / 49- in 5 files.

#### Which further sites share the mechanism: measured

The brief's ~15 further unsubstituted sites were found by reading; that
list is not in the tree, so the population was measured instead.  Probe
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.356/probe.patch`, reverted): after every
expression sema types during a symbolic walk, print the expression when its
type holds a generic parameter whose arena identity is NOT one of the walk's
in-scope parameters.  Control: shape `g` (the program above) prints 17
lines at `main.cryo:37-38` under the compiler without the fix and none with
it.  Corpus (`corpus.sh`: the unit suite and the 14 examples), before and
after the fix: the SAME **20 sites**, three other mechanisms, none a
receiver read:

- a trait method reached through a where-bound keeps the trait's own
  parameter - `x.deref()` with `T: Deref<U>` typed `Target*`, not `U*`
  (`operator_overload.cryo:40`; `fluent_default_method_combinator.cryo:68-69`);
- a generic static on a generic owner whose arguments are inferred keeps the
  owner's parameter - `TakeIter::new(this, n)` in `Iterator`'s defaults
  (`core/iter.cryo` x7, `fluent_default_method_combinator.cryo:36`);
- a method-level generic on a bound receiver keeps the method's parameter -
  `rng.next_range(lo, hi)` typed `T` (`random/distribution.cryo` x8).

None changes what compiles, measured: the first respelled so the trait's
parameter and the caller's collide by name and position (shapes `h`, `i`,
`implement<Item, I> trait MyIter<Item> ..` and `deref_ptr<Target, U>`)
builds and runs 42 under the compiler without the fix, as the controls do;
monomorphization retypes each.  Not taken.  The probe's blind spot, stated:
a leaked parameter spelled and positioned like an in-scope one IS the
in-scope one by today's arena key, so it cannot print - which is exactly
what the flip changes.  A receiver of the owner with OTHER arguments inside
the owner's own body (`other.inner` for `other: &Conn<i64>` in `Conn<S>`,
shapes `j`..`m`) was typed `S` before and `i64` now; every such shape
compiled both ways.

#### Evidence

  compiler without the change, 42 with it.  Roster merged (+1).
- `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD"` over the population without the new

- Warnings, clean builds: 346 before and after.
- §0: projects 82 -> 83; D15's `::{` count 629 -> 634 (the project's

### 8.357 The arena flip: a generic parameter's type is its declaration's, every comparison of two parameters is by identity, and the owner-to-head translation is deleted as redundant - condition one's list 14 -> 8; 0 objects moved outside the one program the flip makes compile - 2026-09-26

```cryo
mut a: Range<i32> = Range::new(0, 3);
mut b: Range<i32> = Range::new(10, 12);
mut c: TakeIter<Range<i32>> = r.take(2);
for (x in a.chain(b).chain(c)) { sum = sum + x; }
// before: error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve 'ChainIter::new'
// after:  exits 25
```

`Iterator::chain<J>` is walked under `implement<I, J> .. for ChainIter<I, J>`,
and both parameters are spelled `J`.  `TypeArena::create_generic_param`
cached a parameter's type by its NAME alone, so the two were one arena type
with two answers, and §8.275 had `TypeSubstitution::get` answer neither.  The
arena now keys a parameter's type by the `SymbolID` its declaration bound
(`GenericParamType.param_sym`); a parameter with no symbol names no
declaration and gets no type, and the `This` placeholder, which no
declaration binds, is its own one type (`TypeArena::this_placeholder`).

Every place that compared two parameters by spelling compares by
declaration (`GenericParamType::declared_by`): the enum payload and
constructor compares and the owner's numeric parameters in the call
resolver, method binding's four where-bound scans, the symbolic checker's
in-scope test (deleted for the existing `symbolic_param_in_scope`), the async
lowering's parameter lookup, and `lookup_subst_for_param` (a bound's subject,
asked by the bound's symbol: 7 calls).  Those were the six hand-written
scans on condition one's list - `TemplateEntry::param_names[]`,
`local::TraitBound[]`, `FunctionDeclNode::trait_bounds[]`,
`ImplBlockNode::where_bounds[]`, `SemaState::symbolic_method_param_nodes[]`,
`SemaState::symbolic_owner_param_nodes[]` - and the list is now the eight
lines of candidate sets and visibility.

How the diff was made is `scripts/ns-migration/8.357/README.md`: §8.343's
probe applied to the tip, its answer-both-ways comparisons turned into the
identity answer by `convert.py`, its scaffolding cut.  Compiler: 134+ / 235-
in 15 files.

#### The owner-to-head translation: measured redundant, deleted

§8.348 read a type computed in an impl body through the impl's head (the
owner's parameter at each position as the impl's), because `this.<field>`
came back in the owner's parameters.  §8.356 substitutes it through the
receiver, and a parameter is now its declaration.  Measured before deleting:

### 8.358 Intrinsic functions exported through their module; a module-qualified call carries the declaration the name layer bound, looked up in the value namespace; the visibility store keyed by the definition - condition one 8 -> 6; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

D34, landed with Jake's three rulings (relayed in plain text): intrinsics are
exported and the `panic` collision is the prelude's glob, not the export;
the private-call hole is closed by the name layer stamping the private
function, keeping "is private"; the visibility table is re-keyed by
identity, and the two gate increases are accepted with written reasons.

```cryo
namespace Vault;
public type struct latch { v: i32; }
private function latch() -> i32 { return 7; }

namespace Main;   // another module
const n: i32 = Vault::latch();
// error[E0353]: `Vault::latch` is private and cannot be called from `Main`
```

#### The unit

- §8.351's patch (`scripts/ns-migration/8.358/unit3-ready.patch`):
  `IntrinsicDeclaration` exports its symbol; the prelude no longer globs
  `core::intrinsics`, so bare `panic` is `std::core`'s function and an
  intrinsic is reached as `intrinsics::f` after an import; the name layer
  stamps `ScopeResolutionNode.member_def` and sema's
  `resolve_module_qualified_def` reads it where `resolve_module_qualified_symbol`
  composed `module + "::" + leaf`.
- The visibility store: `DefTable` records each definition's verdict
  (`DeclVisibility`: `Unrecorded`, `Public`, `Private`), written by
  `register_type` and by type resolution's three function registrars through
  the definition they hold (`IntrinsicDeclNode.def` is new, stamped as a
  function's is).  `DeclarationIndex::hidden_from(d, use_module)` compares the
  declaring module's definition (`DefTable::module_of`) with the use site's;
  `decl_visibility`, `is_candidate_public` and `namespace_of` are deleted.
- The stamp: a path's member is looked up in the namespace the path is
  written in.  The module scope holds one slot per name, a same-leaf function
  sitting in the type's overload set, and `lookup_in_module` answered the
  first public export whatever its kind.  `Resolver::exports_named` and
  `private_declarations` return every declaration under the leaf;
  `NameResolution::export_in` / `private_in` choose by `Namespace::accepts`.
  A module-rooted type path asks `Type`, `M::f` in an expression and the
  extern-module alias ask `Value`.  `lookup_in_module` is `exports_named`'s
  first, so there is one path; the import checks ask whether any private
  declaration carries the name, as before.

Compiler 227+ / 126- in 11 files; `stdlib/prelude.cryo` 4+ / 1-.

#### The hole, shown as a pair

`scripts/ns-migration/8.358/shapes/` (v1: public type then private function;
v4 the other order; v2 both public; v3 private type, public function):

| compiler | v1 | v2 | v3 | v4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the parent commit | E0353 | runs 7 | runs 9 | E0353 |
| patch + store keyed by definition, stamp as saved | **runs 7** | runs 7 | runs 9 | **runs 7** |
| this change | E0353 | runs 7 | runs 9 | E0353 |

With the saved stamp, `Vault::latch` is stamped with the public TYPE's
definition; the function type is found by that definition's path, which is
the private function's too, and the store keyed by the definition answers
"public".  The parent commit refused it only because the path-keyed store
held one verdict for the path and the function's registration wrote it
last.  Project `visibility_function_beside_type` pins v1 (E0353 with its
text); it fails under the middle compiler and passes under this one.

#### Evidence

- Predicted: 0 of 1,126 example and 0 test objects move; the visibility
  projects keep their text.  Measured (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD"`,
  before the new project): **0 of 3,407 test and 0 of 1,126 example
  objects moved**; census OK (the six `visibility_*` projects and
  `extern_private_function_is_private` with their exact text), 14/14
  examples, lsp-check OK (478 warnings), cross-check OK.  The new project
  passes under `cryo test`.  346 warnings, clean build, the same set by
  (code, file).
- Lane, predicted and measured: `DEFID_PATH` 61 -> 62 and `GRAPH_READ` 34 ->

  printing the private callee's path (diagnostic text a person reads and a

- Residue 301 -> 298 (predicted 297: the two F sites and two

### 8.359 A refused signature is recorded by identity: a function's on its definition, a method's by its owner type and leaf - condition one 6 -> 5; 0 objects moved; and the five lines left are BLOCKED on one design question - 2026-09-26

```cryo
function ret_bad(v: i32) -> CfNope { return v; }   // E0203, where it is written
function user() -> i32 { return ret_bad(1); }        // nothing more: the call is silent
```

A declaration whose signature names something the name layer refused
registers no signature, and a call to it reports nothing more (§8.265).
The refusal was one map from a composed string to a flag - a free
function's path, or `Type::method` - read four ways: by a stamp's path, by
`module + "::" + leaf`, by `type_sym + "::" + method`, by
`scope_owner_key + "::" + member`.  Now a free function's refusal is a
`DefTable` column (`record_signature_refused`, `signature_refused`) written
by type resolution through `func.def`, and a method's is
`refused_methods`, keyed by `pack_method_key(owner, leaf)` exactly as
`method_returns` is, written in `register_methods_through` beside the
return.  The readers: a stamp asks its definition; `Mod::f(..)` asks the
definition the name layer bound for the member (§8.358's `member_def`); a
method call asks the receiver's registered owner
(`TypeUtils::method_owner_ref`, the owner the method-return lookup uses);
`Type::f(..)` asks `spec_owner` when set, else the type the scope's stamp
names.  Deleted: `mark_signature_refused`, `signature_refused`,
`signature_refused_of_def`, `signature_refused_in_module`, the map.
Compiler 45+ / 48- in 5 files.

#### Shadow, then delete

Shadow build (`scripts/ns-migration/8.359/shadow.patch`, made by

#### BLOCKED on Jake: the family door

Condition one's five lines are now all one thing - an overload FAMILY asked
by a composed key string: `lookup_family_entries` (6), `lookup_func_type_overloads`
(2), `lookup_func_type_exact` (2), `family_intrinsic_kind` (1),
`lookup_func_type` (1).

```cryo
// today: the family is a string, composed at the call site
const q: SymbolStr = intern(owner_key + "::" + member);   // `Beacon::make`
const entries: OverloadId[] = di.lookup_family_entries(q);
```

The endgame plan's door was `entries_of(def: DefId)` - "the family IS the
declaration" - but D33 gives every overload its own `DefId` (two
declarations of `f` are two ids), and D35 keeps both function and method
overloading, so a family is a SET of definitions and needs an identity of
its own.  The question is which: (a) the family keyed by `(owner, leaf)` -
the owner a module's `DefId` or a type's `TypeRef`, the leaf the written
name - as `method_returns` and the refusals are now, which is a member read
by leaf inside an owner (a J by D32); or (b) a family id minted at
registration, one per `(owner, leaf)`, that every overload's definition
records and a call's stamp carries.  (a) needs no new identity and leaves
the leaf as the key; (b) makes a pin name the family without a string.
Not decided here: it is a design question the plans leave open.

### 8.360 An overload family is keyed by its owner's identity and the written leaf: the five family doors take a `FamilyOwner` and the leaf, the pin carries them, and each door is on the approved list with a checking command - condition one's list 5 -> 0 lines; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

```cryo
type struct Beacon { v: i32; }
implement struct Beacon {
    static make() -> Beacon { return Beacon { v: 1 }; }
    static make(v: i32) -> Beacon { return Beacon { v: v }; }
}
// `Beacon::make(2)`: the family is (Beacon's definition, "make") - two entries,
// the arguments pick one.  It was the string "main::Beacon::make", composed at
// the call and again at registration.
```

Ruling (D35, relayed in plain text): key the family by the owner's identity
plus the written name, the owner a module or a type, as a method's return
and a refused signature are keyed; no family identity type.

#### Step one: the twelve sites, classified before any change

Reading only, at the parent commit.  "Resolution" is an early,
once-per-call-site lookup turning written text into a meaning (selecting
the callee); "late" is a consumer reaching back for a family by name after
the callee was settled - a pin or a stamp already exists.

| site (parent commit) | door | what it asks | class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_resolver.cryo:315` `lookup_callee_function_type` | `lookup_func_type_exact` | `Type::member(..)`'s signature, to type the arguments before the pin | resolution (a type question asked early) |
| `call_resolver.cryo:933` `resolve_call` | `lookup_func_type` | a call already pinned to a family, on a re-walk | late |
| `call_resolver.cryo:1852` `check_call_arity` | `lookup_func_type_overloads` | the stamped callee's signatures, for the arity check | late |
| `call_resolver.cryo:2485` `try_pin_overload_mangled_callee` | `lookup_family_entries` | a bare call's overload, selected by the arguments | resolution |
| `call_resolver.cryo:2610` `family_return_type` | `lookup_func_type_exact` | the return of a specialization's family just pinned | late |
| `call_resolver.cryo:3706` `pin_scope_callee_combined` | `lookup_family_entries` | a static call's single entry | resolution |
| `call_resolver.cryo:3793` `trait_delivered_entries` | `lookup_family_entries` | the entries a named trait delivers for a type | resolution |
| `call_resolver.cryo:4043` `entry_of_signature` | `lookup_family_entries` | `Type::method` taken as a value, the entry of its selected signature | resolution |
| `call_resolver.cryo:4161` `try_pin_static_method_overload` | `lookup_family_entries` | a static call's overload, selected by the arguments | resolution |
| `call_resolver.cryo:5653` `check_scope_call_arg_types` | `lookup_func_type_overloads` | a pinned `Scope::member(..)`'s signatures, for the argument check | late |
| `codegen/ops/symbol_resolver.cryo:227` `family_answer` | `lookup_family_entries` | a `CalleePin::Family`'s one symbol | late |
| `codegen/visit/call_emitter.cryo:1139` `pinned_intrinsic_kind` | `family_intrinsic_kind` | the intrinsic kind of a family pin | late |

Six resolution, six late.  Every late one reads a family that a pin or a
stamp already identified, and received it as a string only because the pin
held one (`CalleePin::Family(SymbolStr)`) or the reader rebuilt it from the
stamp (`callee_family` = `path_of(def)`).  The same store had eleven more
readers outside the twelve, all late: codegen's `resolve_function` (the
lang items `set_args`, `set_env` and the allocator by a stamp's path,
`"string::append"`, the AST arena's allocator by a literal path), three
class-constructor lookups by `<type name>::<ctor>`, the test runner's three
`lookup_sole_entry`, and `func_type_of_def`.

#### The change

- `FamilyOwner` (`resolver/res.cryo`): `Def(DefId)` - the owner's
  definition, a module or a type, the invalid id being the root that owns
  a specialization's minted identifier - and `Type(TypeRef)`, for an owner
  held as a type (the monomorphizer pins a family on an instantiation
  before that instantiation is registered, so the owner's definition is
  read when the family is asked).
- The index's store is keyed by `family_slot(owner, leaf)`: the owner's path
  and the leaf's intern id, packed; the owner's path is read inside the
  index (`family_owner_path`), nowhere a caller stands.
  `register_signature`, `register_function_signature`, `reset_family`,
  `lookup_family_entries`, `lookup_func_type_overloads`, `lookup_func_type`,
  `family_intrinsic_kind` and `TypeUtils::lookup_func_type_exact` take
  `(owner, leaf)`; `lookup_sole_entry` and codegen's `resolve_function`
  take the definition; `func_type_of_def` asks the definition's parent and
  leaf.  `entry_key` and `overload_func_keys` (read by nothing) are gone.
- `CalleePin::Family(FamilyOwner, SymbolStr)`.  Every pin writer hands the
  owner it holds: a stamp's parent (`sema.cryo`, the module-qualified pins),
  the owner type (`Type::method` values, mono's instantiation), the root
  (a function specialization's minted identifier).
- Registration names a declaring module's family through three context
  helpers: `decl_fn_family` (the module `decl_fn_key` qualifies under, and
  the leaf), `minted_family` (a minted name as minted: bare -> root,
  qualified -> its module), `module_family` / `module_def_of` (one reader of
  a module's definition by namespace, shared with `register_in_module`).
- Late readers: codegen reads the pin's owner and leaf; the lang items hand
  over their definition; `string::append` asks `append` in the family of
  the primitive `string`, held by its arena identity (`get_string()`); a
  constructor is the class's family under the class's own leaf.
- Deleted: `callee_family` (now `callee_def`), `module_qualified_path`,
  `pin_scope_callee_qsym`, `reset_function_overloads`,
  `reset_method_overloads`, `family_name()`.

said "key" or "canonical name" for a family was rewritten.

`scripts/ns-migration/approved-names.tsv` - D41's form, one entry per line:

stand-in for an identity (Rust's resolver keys the same set by parent
module, identifier and namespace), and the leaf is a stamp's leaf, a written
member name or a minted identifier, never a path composed at the call.

helper's body.  `make approved-check` (self-test, 12 cases, then the list)

#### Where a generated name meets a written one - measured, carried to the next entry

The brief asked that the family key record where its leaf came from.
Measured over the self-build (a probe logging every key registered and
asked): 31,314 distinct keys registered, 5,448 asked; every key whose leaf
the compiler minted carries `$` (`9transmute$Lf_j$G`,
`Child$join$Future_0::poll`), which no source can spell, and every
synthesized call is stamped with the definition it means
(`set_synthesized_ref`).  So no family key in the tree can collide with a
written one, and an origin field on the family key would change no answer.

The one generated name a user CAN write is the closure's: its struct is
`<module>::__Closure_<N>` with a method `__call__`
(`sema/lambda_synth.cryo` `mint_closure_def`).  It collides one level up,
at the type, before any family is keyed - `TypeArena::create_struct`
caches a struct by its qualified name (`types/arena.cryo:548`), so the
closure's struct and a user's struct of that name are ONE arena type:

```cryo
type struct __Closure_0 { v: i32; }
implement struct __Closure_0 {
    __call__(&this, x: i32) -> i32 { return 1000; }
}
function main() -> i32 {
    const bias: i32 = 10;
    const add_bias = (x: i32) -> i32 { return x + bias; };
    return add_bias(32);        // exits 232 (1000 mod 256), not 42 - no diagnostic
}
```

Where the origin must be recorded is therefore the generated DEFINITION,
not the family key.  That is the next unit; this entry records the
collision as found.

### 8.361 A definition the compiler generates records its origin, and its path is one no written declaration can have: a program's own `__Closure_0` no longer becomes a closure's struct - 122 objects moved, every one carrying a generated definition's symbol - 2026-09-26

```cryo
type struct __Closure_0 { v: i32; }
implement struct __Closure_0 {
    __call__(&this, x: i32) -> i32 { return 1000; }
}
function main() -> i32 {
    const bias: i32 = 10;
    const add_bias = (x: i32) -> i32 { return x + bias; };
    return add_bias(32);        // 42 now; exited 232 (1000 mod 256), no diagnostic
}
```

The brief for §8.360 asked that the family key record where its leaf came
from, so that a name the compiler generates cannot collide with one the
program wrote.  §8.360 measured that no family key can collide - every
minted family leaf carries `$` and every synthesized call is stamped - and
that the one generated name a program can write, the closure's struct,
collides at the DEFINITION: its path `main::__Closure_0` is a path the
program can declare, and every store keyed by a path merges the two (the
arena's struct cache first, `types/arena.cryo:548`).  So the origin is
recorded where a definition's path is composed.

#### The change

- `NameOrigin` (`resolver/res.cryo`): `Written`, `Generated`.
  `DefTable::register` records `Written`; `DefTable::register_generated`
  records `Generated` and composes the path with the leaf marked `$` -
  `main::$__Closure_0` - which begins no identifier a program can write
  (`$` lexes as its own token).  `leaf_of` answers the leaf as minted, so a
  family keyed by the definition's parent and leaf is unchanged.
  `origin_of(d)` answers the recorded origin; nothing reads it yet.
- `CompilationContext::register_in_module`, the one registration every
  synthesizer goes through (a closure's struct, an async function's future,
  the body `async main` is renamed to), calls `register_generated`.
- An instantiation still registers through `register`: its leaf is the
  template's written name mangled with its arguments, not a declaration the
  lowering minted, and D33 moves instantiations out of the table.  Marking
  them would rename every generic instance's symbols for no answer changed.

#### What carrying origin on every identifier would take

Rust carries a syntax context on every identifier.  Here, a synthesized
REFERENCE already carries the definition it means - 37 sites stamp one
(`set_synthesized_ref`, `set_synthesized_res`, `alloc_synthetic_binding`),
so a desugared `Option::Some` or `Poll::Ready` is not resolved by its
spelling in the program's scope.  What remains spelled is what the
synthesizers BUILD: 28 `IdentifierNode`, 10 `ScopeResolutionNode` and 26
`MemberAccessNode` constructions outside the parser.  Carrying origin on
all of them means an origin field on those nodes, set at each of the 64
sites, and every lookup that can reach one asking by (leaf, origin);
today no lookup found a synthesized spelling colliding with a written one
except through a definition's path, which this entry closes.  Two readers
still decide "generated" by spelling and would move to `origin_of`: the
editor's `is_synthesized_closure_name` (the substring `__Closure`,
`tools/CryoLSP/src/handlers/semantic_tokens.cryo:354`, inside the editor
exception) and `SpecializationPasses::owner_of_type`, which takes a type
name containing `$` for a monomorph (`passes/specialization.cryo:532`) -
harmless for a generated struct, which has no type arguments to look in,
but a classification by spelling.

### 8.362 An incremental build no longer reuses an object that lacks a generic instance an edit newly requires, and a failed link's error carries the linker's own report - reproduced as a verify gate; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

```cryo
import std::thread;
type struct JobA { n: i32; }
type struct JobB { m: i64; }                 // added by the edit
function run_a(j: JobA) -> void { }
function run_b(j: JobB) -> void { }
function main() -> i32 {
    {
        mut scope: thread::Scope = thread::Scope::new();
        scope.spawn::<JobA>(JobA { n: 1 }, run_a);
        scope.spawn::<JobB>(JobB { m: 2 }, run_b);   // added by the edit
    }
    return 4;
}
```

Built once without the two marked lines, then again incrementally with
them: the second build failed to link, `undefined reference to
C$3std.6thread.5Scope-5spawn$F$m_N$L4main.4JobB$G...`, where a clean build
links and exits 4.  Filed in the fifty-second session with
`Scope::spawn<ShellJobs>` in the compiler's own build.

#### The cause: a spec method's owning module misattributed

`nm` over a clean build: both `Scope::spawn<JobA>` and `spawn<JobB>` are
DEFINED in `std/thread.o` and referenced from `main.o` - a generic method
instantiated on a non-generic owner is emitted with the owner's
declaration.  The per-module cache keys a module that owns a specialization
by a digest of every source, and any other module by its import closure
only (`instance.cryo`, `pm_owns_spec`).  `spawn<C>` is written inside
`type struct Scope { .. }`, with no impl block, so its specs go through
`register_spec_method_in_di_inherent` (`mono/call_specializer.cryo`), which
recorded the owning module as `current_module` - the module whose CALL was
being walked, `main`.  `std::thread` was never flagged, kept its
import-closure key, and its object from the first build - without
`spawn<JobB>` - was reused.  Fix: the owning module is the one whose file
declares the owner (`owner_ast.span.file`), which is where the definition
is emitted.  The impl-block path already records the block's own module.

Checked for the right reason: after the fix the second build still reports
`reusing 37 cached object(s)` (38 in the failing build - `std/thread.o` is
the one no longer reused, and its timestamp moved), so the cache was in
effect and the link succeeded because the stale object was rebuilt, not
because the cache was off.  A key the module graph could not resolve would
have switched the cache off for the whole build (`pm_active = false`) and
passed for the wrong reason; the reuse count is what rules that out.

#### The swallowed report

The linker's output was printed as it ran, while the compiler's diagnostics
render after every pass: the reason (`undefined reference to ...`) sat 290
lines above the one error, `E0900 linker invocation failed (gcc exited with
1): <command>`, which did not contain it - and any reader of the last
screen, or of a log's tail, never saw it.  `CodegenPasses::run_tool` now
runs a toolchain command with its output captured to a log beside the
response file, and `tool_failure` puts that output in the error as a note
(`the tool reported:`); a command that succeeds has its output printed as
before.  The project link, the single-file link and the archiver go
through it.

  `tests/started-compiling`, where refused-then-built is the claim.

#### Not done

The fix rests on attributing every emitted specialization to the module
that emits it.  A direct guard - each module's cached key or sidecar
recording the specialization symbols its object defines, and reuse refused
when the set now required of it grows - would hold whatever the
attribution; it would also be a second answer to the question the
ownership flag answers, so it is not built here.

### 8.363 The three identity types a caller could build from raw input are sealed: an `OverloadId`, a `SymbolID` or a `ModulePath` written outside its owning module no longer compiles, and the lane gate refuses a public static that mints one; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

## Why

A read-only audit showed that the conversions to identities could be
bypassed by an ordinary call: three identity types had a public
constructor taking the raw payload, so

```cryo
const o: OverloadId = OverloadId::at_position(7);             // any registry slot
const s: SymbolID   = SymbolID::new(7);                        // any resolver symbol
const m: ModulePath = ModulePath::of(intern("not::a::module")); // any text
```

all compiled anywhere, and every lookup keyed by those types answered for
them. Cryo's `private` is scoped to the declaring module, so the fix is the
same for each: the payload and the constructor are private to the module
that registers the things the type names, and that module publishes only
doors that can answer something real.

## What changed

**`OverloadId`** moves from `resolver/res.cryo` into `decl_index.cryo`, the
index that registers signatures; `pos`, `at_position` and `position` are
private there. Making them private refused nothing: no code outside the
index had ever built or read one.

**`SymbolID`**: `id` and `new` are private in `symbol_id.cryo`. The compiler
refused 67 sites (`scripts/ns-migration/8.363/refused-symbolid.lst`):

| what the site did | sites |
|---|---|
| read the number as a key in the pass's OWN table (`drop_insertion` 39, `move_check` 18, `dead_code` 2, `sema` 2, `resolver` 2 arena indexes and 2 log lines, `arena` 1) | 63 |
| REBUILT an id from a stored number (`drop_insertion` 2, `move_check` 1) | 3 |
| minted the next id (the resolver) | 1 |

The reads use a public read-only `key()`; nothing turns a number back into
an id outside `symbol_id.cryo`. The three rebuilds are gone: each helper has
a body taking the key, and its `SymbolID` signature is a thin wrapper over
it, so its other callers are unchanged -

```cryo
mark_moved(mut &this, sym: SymbolID) -> void { this.mark_moved_key(sym.key()); }
// the recursion over a stored link calls mark_moved_key(this.link_subject[i])
// where it used to call mark_moved(SymbolID::new(this.link_subject[i]))
```

The one mint is `SymbolIds::next()`, an allocator beside the type that the
resolver holds instead of a counter. A second `SymbolIds` can still be
created and would hand out colliding ids - the same hole `DefTable::new`
has; not closed here.

**`ModulePath`** moves into `module_graph.cryo` (and
`resolver/module_path.cryo` is deleted); the payload and `of` are private.
The graph registers every module, so it is the only minter, through three
doors:

```cryo
info.path()                         // a registered module's own path
graph.module_of_file(span.file)     // the module a source file declares
graph.module_named(ns)              // THE text-to-module door: a module the
                                    // graph holds under `ns`, or none
```

`module_named` answers for a module in either of the graph's tables: an
aliased C import (`extern module libc as cit`) is recorded in `module_defs`
and not in the module list, so answering from the list alone would have
lost it. A site that asked `find_module_index(...) < 0` still asks it, and
still answers "no" for an alias-only module.

Making `of` private refused 40 sites (`refused-modulepath.lst`: 39 in the
compiler, 1 in the editor; 4 more inside the graph stay). Each was
rewritten by what it meant:

| meaning | sites | now |
|---|---|---|
| already held a registered module | 4 | `info.path()` |
| the module a file declares | 4 + the editor's | `module_of_file`; the editor passes the edited module's `path()` |
| a module's definition, by the DECLARATION in hand | 1 | `defs.module_of(hs.def)` - the one that split a qualified name's parent back out of its text |
| written text naming a module - imports, exports, the prelude, a C import's alias | 13 | `module_named` |
| a namespace another structure stored as text earlier | 13 | `module_named` |

`bind_c_import_module` now takes the C import's namespace and the graph
mints its path. The overload family's owner at registration
(`CompilationContext::decl_fn_family`, the owner half of the family key)
now comes from the declaring file's module (`module_of_file`), not from a
namespace string; a name minted already qualified still names its module
through `module_named`.

**Every rewritten site answers as before**, and that was measured, not
argued. Where the path goes into the graph's own tables
(`find_module_index`, `module_def`, `reexport_closure`) the answer is equal
by construction: `module_named` is valid exactly when one of those tables
holds the key. The rest - the resolver's module scopes (four sites), the
declaration index's import relation, a struct's declaring module in the
member visibility check, and the owner rewrite - were given temporary
probes (`scripts/ns-migration/8.363/probe_mp.py`) that exit 97 whenever
the new answer could differ from `ModulePath::of(text)`'s: for a scope,
when the resolver holds a scope under the text and the graph does not know
it. Over the census (2,209 unit, 227 compile-fail, 83 projects), the 14
examples and the editor's build (265 modules, the compiler's 160 among
them) **no probe fired**. Control: with `CRYO_SEALPROBE_CONTROL=1` the probes
print instead of judging - on `examples/07-shapes` the use-site probe was
reached 1,282 times, the template-scope probes 748 and 330, all answering
a registered module. The single-file risk - a resolver scope keyed by a
name the graph never registered - does not occur: a single file is
compiled as a one-module project, and its module name is registered.

## The text-to-module door is unconfirmed

`module_named(text)` cannot forge a module, but it names a REAL one from
text, so

```cryo
const m: DefId = graph.module_def(graph.module_named(intern(user_text)));
```

still compiles. An import begins as text, so a text-to-module door has to
exist; this commit makes it one named door that can return only a
registered module. **This is a recommendation carried by the task, not a
ruling** - Jake has not confirmed it. The alternative is that every
structure storing a namespace as text (`StructType.module_name`,
`TemplateEntry.module_name`, `Symbol.source_module`, the `use_ns` strings
and the rest of the 13 in the last row above) holds an identity instead: a
separate, larger unit.

## The lane gate's seal check

`check_sealed_types` asserted a type was sealed when one of its fields was
private. `OverloadId` passed it with a private `pos` and a PUBLIC
`static at_position(pos)`: the literal was sealed, the constructor was not.
A second rule now refuses, on an identity type, a public static that takes
an argument and returns the type; a parameterless one (`invalid()`,
`none()`) is a sentinel and passes, and `DefTable` is exempt because its
constructor makes an empty store, not a value naming an entry.
`SymbolID` and `ModulePath` are added to the sealed list, and `OverloadId`'s
entry names its new file.

Pair, over a copy of this tree with `at_position` made `public`
(`.objcmp`-local, reproduced by hand): the gate's previous check (its
code at the parent commit, with this commit's table) printed `lane-gate:
OK`; this commit's printed `` `OverloadId` (compiler/decl_index.cryo) has a
public `static at_position(pos: u32)` returning it ``; on the unmutated
copy, OK. The self-test gains three cases (one-line mint refused, two-line
mint refused, private mint beside a public sentinel accepted): 46 cases.

## Proof by inversion

Three scratch projects depending on the compiler library, each built alone
with this compiler:

```
error[E0353]: method `of` of `compiler::module_graph::ModulePath` is private
 7 |     const m: ModulePath = ModulePath::of(SymbolStr::from_id(7));
error[E0353]: method `new` of `compiler::resolver::symbol_id::SymbolID` is private
 6 |     const s: SymbolID = SymbolID::new(7);
error[E0353]: method `at_position` of `compiler::decl_index::OverloadId` is private
 6 |     const o: OverloadId = OverloadId::at_position(7);
```

and the literal forms, `ModulePath { sym: .. }`, `SymbolID { id: 7 }`,
`OverloadId { pos: 7 }`, each `error[E0353]: field ... is private`.
Control through the same harness: `ModulePath::none()` passes every check
and reaches the link (which then fails only because the scratch project
does not link the compiler's LLVM libraries).

## Out of scope

- A raw pointer cast still turns the number 7 into a valid-looking sealed
  id, and the program runs. Closing it is a language decision, parked.
- `TypeRef` is unsealed (public `id`, `arena` and `new(id, arena)`); it is
  measured, not converted, in the report that accompanies this commit.

### 8.365 The compiler reports its own calls: `cryo build --emit=facts` writes one record per argument a call passes to a parameter taking a name as text, and per comparison of such names, from what the body check resolved; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

## Why

Every gate measuring this migration is a Python pattern-match over Cryo
source text, and every blind spot found in them came from that approach: a
reader under another name, a reader in another file's `implement` block, a
`string` key where the rule looked for `SymbolStr`, a store the rule did not
know was a store, a read written as a loop, a name turned into text and then
compared, a `ModulePath::of(text)` on a type that was not a store. D42 rules
that the compiler, not the scripts, is the authority, and that the report is
an output of the ordinary build command rather than a separate mode, so it
cannot take a different path from the code that ships.

## What changed

`compiler/src/compiler/sema/call_facts.cryo` (new). The body check before
monomorphization - which runs on every module on every build, a module the
incremental cache reuses included - records, at its one call-resolution
entry (`resolve_call_recorded`, `sema.cryo`) and its binary-expression
entry (`resolve_binary_recorded`):

- `arg`: one record per argument a call passes to a parameter whose type is
  a KEY - `string`, `SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName` or `ModulePath`, by value,
  by reference or as an array. The parameter types come from the pinned
  declaration's signature; the receiver is skipped by the arity difference,
  and a call where that difference is not 0 or 1 is written as `unaligned`
  rather than guessed. A call sema did not pin uses the types sema itself
  classified its arguments against, and one with neither is `noparams`.
- `cmp`: one record per `==` / `!=` whose operand is a key, or a number read
  off one (`name.id == other.id`).

Tab-separated, sorted by file then line and column as numbers, without
repeats. Two real records from the compiler's own facts, fields split for
reading:

```
arg  src/compiler/Instance.cryo  906  13
     index 0   type compiler::resolver::symbol_str::SymbolStr
     provenance  call:compiler::resolver::intern_table::InternTable.intern(mut &this, string) -> ...SymbolStr
     receiver    field:compiler::compilation_context::CompilationContext*.module_graph<-param:ctx
     callee      C$8compiler.12module_graph.11ModuleGraph-12module_named$F...   pin call
     callee-decl src/compiler/module_graph.cryo:379
     enclosing   C$8compiler.8instance.16CompilerInstance-21mark_implicit_closure$F...
     (then both rendered: ModuleGraph.module_named(&this, SymbolStr) -> ModulePath,
      CompilerInstance.mark_implicit_closure(&this, ...))

cmp  src/CLI/_module.cryo  178  39   ==   string
     right  literal
     left   local:value=field:cli::Argument.default_value<-field:Pair<string, cli::Argument>.second
            <-element:field:cli::ParsedArgs.args<-param:this
     enclosing  cli::ParsedArgs.validate(&this) -> boolean
```

The first is a text-to-module lookup whose key was freshly interned from a
string; the second compares a stored field with a literal. Provenance is
the part no regex could give: `literal`, `param:<name>` (the enclosing
function's own parameter), `local:<name>=<its initializer's provenance>`
(`local:mut` when it can be reassigned - only the initializer is known),
`global:<path>`, `field:<type>.<member><-<where the value came from>`,
`call:<callee>`, `element:<array's provenance>`, `sourceloc:FILE`,
`expr:<kind>`. How far it goes: one level per expression, through `&`, `*`
and casts, following a local to its initializer; it does not follow a
reassignment, a return value into its callee, or a parameter into its
callers - `param:` is where a record hands over to the caller's records.

The key types are named by their declarations' paths in `carries_key`: they
are the report's subject, not a language rule, and a program declaring none
of them gets `string` records only. Condition two's population (`string`,
`SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName`) and D32's (`string`, `SymbolStr`,
`ModulePath`) are both read off the same file by the parameter type each
record carries.

`--emit=facts` sets `CompilerConfig.emit_facts`; the build writes
`<output_dir>/<project_name>.facts` after the body check and bypasses the
up-to-date short-circuit, which would skip it. Any other `--emit=` value is
refused. `make facts` (`scripts/facts.py`) runs it with the compiler under
test over the compiler, the stdlib and the editor into `.facts/`, refusing a
build that stated no population or wrote no facts, and records a hash of
every source the facts depend on; `scripts/facts.py --check` refuses a
missing or stale file.

## Coverage

`make facts`, 79 s for all three: compiler 12,202 records (10,147 `arg`,
681 `cmp`, 1,374 `noparams`); stdlib on its own 947; editor 11,983, of which
865 are the editor's own files - the old counter aborted on the editor, so
"zero rows" there meant never walked - 10,599 the compiler it is built with,
519 stdlib. Of the compiler's own `arg` records, 7,145 pass a `string`,
2,464 a `SymbolStr`, 42 a `ModulePath`, 27 a `QualifiedName`, the rest
arrays and references; by provenance 4,425 literal, 1,714 local, 1,308
field, 1,271 param, 892 call, 113 element, 50 other, 13 global. The 1,374
`noparams` are calls sema left unpinned and untyped before
monomorphization: 1,229 `Array.push`, then `compare`, `write_uint`,
`unwrap_or` - generic methods taking `T`, outside both populations.

## Findings

- Of the 9,787 `arg` records in the compiler's own files, 9,766 name a
  callee, and every one of those was the call's own `resolved_callee`; the
  pin on the callee expression and `resolved_method` never answered first.
  21 had no pin.
- Sema's own aligned parameter list is empty for many calls it DID pin:
  with it as the source, `ParserBase.consume(.., string)` (166 calls) and
  `string.eq` (217) were invisible. The signature is the source for that
  reason.
- On Windows a record's path is the loader's spelling, which follows the
  module name's case (`src/compiler/parser/Parser.cryo` for
  `parser.cryo`); a consumer matches paths case-insensitively here.

`scripts/ns-migration/8.365/facts_inversion.py --cryo <compiler>`: a scratch

| shape | records |
|---|---|
| s00 control, empty body | 0 |
