### 8.366 The residue's population is read from the compiler's facts, and its text-pattern counting is deleted: 317 -> 319 sites, every difference traced to a loop the text reader could not follow or over-counted; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

## Why

D32's instrument found its sites by pattern-matching `compiler/src`: a
regular expression for each call shape, the receiver's type read off its
declaration, and a separate reader for loops that search a member table by
a name. Every blind spot the ledger records in it came from that approach.
D42 rules that the compiler is the authority; §8.365 built the report.

## What changed

`scripts/ns-migration/residue.py` reads `.facts/compiler.facts` (`make
facts`; refused when missing or stale). Which types HOLD declarations is
still placed by the lane gate over declarations - the stores and the member
tables. Everything that FOUND sites is deleted: the call patterns, the
receiver-type placement, the loop-scan reader's use, the two refusals for
receivers it could not type or reach, and the "elsewhere" table, which
existed to catch a receiver placed on the wrong type. A callee named by the
compiler cannot be placed on the wrong type. Its one remaining refusal is a
call into a holder that sema left unpinned.

A METHOD site is an `arg` record passing a key (`SymbolStr`, `string`,
`ModulePath`) to a holder's `&this` or static method, outside the holder's
file and the files its store owns. A SCAN site is a comparison (a `cmp`
record, or a key type's `equals`) whose operand is a key read off an
element of an array placed as a table, where the INNERMOST loop around the
comparison reads that element:

```cryo
for (mut si: i64 = 0; si < src.reexports.length; si++) {
    const re_ns: SymbolStr = src.reexports[si];          // declared at depth 4
    for (mut qi: i64 = 0; qi < imi_visible.length; qi++) {
        if (imi_visible[qi].id == re_ns.id) { .. }       // depth 5: searches imi_visible
    }
}
```

The inner loop searches `imi_visible` (a list of names, data) for a key that
came from the `reexports` table. That is not a read of `reexports`. The facts
tell the two apart because the compiler now records loop depth. A local
carries the depth it was declared at (`local:re_ns@4=...`), and so does a
counter declared in a `for` header (at the depth of the loop it drives). An
element carries its index's depth (`element@5:...`), and every record
carries its own depth as a fifteenth field. An element read at the record's
depth is the array being searched; one bound further out is the source of
the key.

Two more changes to the emitter:

- Provenance now includes a literal's text (`literal:"iter"`) and, for a
  call's result, where its first argument came from (`call:InternTable.intern(..) of literal:"iter"`).
  The classifier's per-site overrides were keyed by the argument's source
  text (`this.intern.intern("iter")`); they are now keyed by this provenance,
  which keeps them apart.
- A comparison of an array-of-names' `length` is no longer recorded as a
  comparison of keys (62 records): a number counts only when read off one
  key, not off an array of them.

`residue.md` gives each site's key as provenance, so a row now says where
its name came from:

```
| compiler/sema/sema.cryo:1284 | TypeUtils::lookup_method_return |
  call:InternTable.intern(mut &this, string) -> SymbolStr of literal:"iter" | J | member: the for-in protocol's `iter` ...
| compiler/sema/sema.cryo:2696 | ResolutionContext::new | literal:"" | N | a constructor: the string is the SOURCE file ...
```

`residue_selftest.py` drives a synthetic facts file and throwaway lists. It
has 13 facts mutations, each refused or allowed as the rule says: a planted
read, a static read, an unpinned call, a record of the wrong shape, an
unclassified method, a registrar, a store's own call, a call passing no key,
a call outside `compiler/src`, a scan at the innermost loop, the same element
bound outside it, a data array, and two members of one element. It keeps the
five list mutations.

`check-fast` runs `facts-fresh` first, which builds the compiler and the facts
only when stale. CI runs `make facts` after `make cryo`, and runs
`ns-status-check` after it; it used to run before the build.

## Every difference, old against new

Over one tree, the regex population (the parent's `residue.py`) and the facts
population:

- **Method calls: 250 and 250, identical to the line.** Nothing the regex
  counted is missing, and nothing new appeared. The first draft of the facts
  reader found 49 more, all calls inside the resolver's own files; the regex
  excluded those as a store's machinery. With the same rule the two agree.
- **Scans: 67 -> 69.** An early draft found 14 extra rows. Each was traced to
  a bug in the draft or in the facts, then fixed:
  - The draft took every element anywhere up a chain, not the nearest.
  - The facts recorded an array's `length` compare as a key compare.
  - A comparison with both sides read off table elements counted both sides.
    Loop depth decides which side is being searched.
  - An element indexed by an outer loop's counter was read at the inner
    depth. The fix was the index's own depth.

  Four remain, and the source settles each one:

| site | shape | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `sema/call_resolver.cryo:2380` | `mn = block.methods[bmi]; fn_node = mn.func; if (fn_node.name.equals(member.member))` | regex BLIND: a local bound to a member of the element |
| `sema/call_resolver.cryo:2978` | the same shape | regex BLIND |
| `instance.cryo:1476` | `src = &ctx.module_graph.modules[reexporters[ri]]; if (src.name.id != via.id)` | regex BLIND: an element bound through `&`, indexed by another array's value |
| `passes/ast_validation.cryo:213` | `f = fields[i]` outside; inside `for k { if (seen[k] == f.name.id) }` | regex OVER-COUNT: the loop searches `seen`, a list of ids, for a key from `fields` |

Two members of one element compared (`dumper.cryo:789`,
`b.source_field.id == b.local_name.id`) is one site, as it was.

## Proof the new gate sees what the old could not

The pair was run over one probed tree. The probe is
`probe_blind_scan` in `sema/call_resolver.cryo`: the loop shape from the
table above, searching an impl's methods through `fn_node = mn.func`. It was
built with `make cryo` and `make facts`, then reverted.

- The OLD gate - the parent's `residue.py`, classifier and list - printed
  `residue: OK -- 317 sites, list, tree and classifier agree; J 190, N 127; convertible 0; elsewhere 20`.
- The NEW gate printed
  `residue: compiler/sema/call_resolver.cryo ImplBlockNode::methods[] (param:n): tree 1, list 0`
  and `residue: DRIFT - tree 320, list 319`.

Self-test controls, each mutation run alone:

- With the innermost-loop rule removed from `residue.py`, the self-test failed
  "the same element bound outside the innermost loop ... expected exit 0".
- With the unpinned refusal removed, it failed "a call into a holder that sema
  left unpinned is refused ... got exit 0".
- Restored, it printed `residue-selftest: OK -- baseline accepted, 13 facts and 5 list mutations behaved`.

## Provenance and condition three

Keys by class, first key argument:

| class | param | local | field | call | literal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| J (192) | 71 | 30 | 60 | 31 | 0 |
| N (127) | 10 | 9 | 8 | 2 | 98 |

Of the N literals, 49 are `""`. No justified read passes a bare literal, and
98 of the 127 "not a key" rows do. A rule over provenance could therefore
check most N reasons mechanically. That is the self-checking reason condition
three asks for. This entry does not build the rule; it shows the facts can
support one.

## Evidence

- Predicted before the switch: 250 method sites identical, scans 67 -> 69
  (+3 blind, -1 over-count), residue 317 -> 319, J 190 -> 192. Measured the
  same: `residue: OK -- 319 sites ... J 192, N 127; convertible 0`.
- The table `local::FieldDeclNode[]` is now "called from nowhere". Its only
  scan was the over-count.
- §0 rows: residue 317 -> 319, J 190 -> 192, `check-fast`'s prerequisite
  row, D32 and D42.
- Facts after this change: compiler 12,197 records. That is 12,138 before
  literals carried their text. A few distinct calls share one source span:
  one expression desugared into several calls. When their records were
  otherwise identical, de-duplication had merged them. That was a small
  undercount, which the literal's text now separates.

### 8.367 An import binds every declaration a module offers under the leaf, and each later use chooses among them by namespace: a type declared after a same-leaf function no longer escapes the module/type collision; the first-match export lookup is deleted; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

## Why

An import kept one binding per name, holding whichever declaration the
module's export list gave first, and four places in the name layer followed
an import by looking the name up again in the module whose path the import
stored as text, again taking the first public export whatever its kind
(`Resolver::lookup_in_module`). A module may declare a type and a function
under one leaf. Which of the two came first then decided the answer. This
program compiled and ran, printing the module's constant:

```cryo
namespace Pcf::Vault;
public function Color(x: i32) -> i32 { return x + 100; }
public type enum Color { Red; Green; }

namespace Pcf::Color;
public const Green: i32 = 42;

namespace Pcf::Main;
import Pcf::Color;
import Pcf::Vault::{ Color };
function main() -> int {
    const v: i32 = Color::Green;   // ran, exit 42
    return v as int;
}
```

With the two declarations in `Vault` swapped, the same program is refused
with E0205 (`Pct::Color` is a module) - §4 rule 5: a type imported under a
module's name is a redeclaration. The collision check asked "does this
import name a type", followed the import to the first export, found the
function, and answered no.

## What changed

- `Resolver::declare_import(sym, target)` records the declaration each
  import binding names. An import of a leaf binds EVERY declaration the
  module offers under it, one binding each: the braced form binds all of
  `exports_named`, and the glob forms already walked each export. A second
  declaration from the same module is a second binding in the scope's
  overload set, as the declaring module's own scope holds a type beside a
  same-leaf function; the same declaration imported twice binds once.
- `Resolver::import_target(sym, ns)` answers what an import binding names
  in a namespace: among the bindings its scope holds under its name, the
  target whose kind `ns` accepts. The four followers ask it by the
  namespace they mean - the `extern module` alias an import names (type),
  whether an import names a type (type; this is the collision check and
  the did-you-mean type list), the functions visible by a bare name
  (value), and a path's head (type). None of them reads the stored module
  text any more.
- `Resolver::resolve_path` follows an import head the same way. An import
  that binds nothing in the asked namespace keeps its own answer, as
  before, and the stage that needs the kind reports the mismatch.
- `lookup_in_module` is deleted. `NameResolution::export_in` moves into the
  resolver as `Resolver::export_in`, the one namespace-aware question; an
  `extern module` alias's member in a type path asks it in the type
  namespace; the two existence checks ask whether `exports_named` is
  non-empty. The prelude tier asks each prelude module in the namespace
  `resolve_path` was asked in; asked in none (`lookup`), a prelude module
  offering several declarations under a leaf is unanswered, as two prelude
  modules offering one are.
- Nothing reads a scope's overload set of imports except `import_target`:
  `private_declarations` skips imports, and the call-site overload record
  (`record_overloads`) has no reader.

## Evidence

- The shape, six programs (`.objcmp/s57/imp/`, not committed; the pair is
  the committed project): function-first and type-first, each with a
  type use (`Color::Green` through the enum), a call (`Color(5)`), and the
  module collision. Before: 2, 2, 105, 105, **runs 42**, E0205. After: 2,
  2, 105, 105, **E0205**, E0205.
- Project `import_type_beside_function_meets_module` (in
  `tests/started-passing`): the parent commit builds it and it exits 42;
  this change refuses it with E0205 and the text it pins.
- Population: a print in `exports_named` whenever it returned two or more
  declarations fired 4 times on the program above and **0** times over the
  compiler (164 local modules), the standard library (154) and the editor
  (25 local, 161 dependency), each build stating its population and
  exiting 0. No shipped code has a type and a function under one exported
  leaf, so no answer outside the new project could move.
- Predicted and measured (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD
  --require-identical"`): 0 of 3,515 test and 0 of 1,126 example objects
  moved; the baseline's census fails on exactly the declared project.
- References to `Symbol.source_module` in `compiler/src` outside comments:
  37 -> 31.

## Still open

- A bare identifier in an expression (`bare_name_res`) and the namespace-
  less `lookup` still read the binding a scope holds FIRST for a name, so
  `Color(5)` is stamped with the type's definition when the module
  declared the type first. Later stages recover the function by the
  definition's path, which the two share, and the program runs correctly
  in both orders (105), so no wrong answer is known; the stamp is wrong.
- Two imports of one leaf from DIFFERENT modules are still ambiguous even
  when one is a type and the other a function.
- The import still stores its module as text (`source_module`), read by
  `declare_import` to tell a re-import from a clash and by
  `qualified_name_of`.

### 8.368 The lane gate's buckets are counted from the compiler's facts, and its receiver-pattern counting is deleted: 15 of 16 buckets identical site for site, `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 56 -> 51, every difference traced; two shapes the patterns could not see are now counted; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-26

## Why

The lane gate was the last counter reading source text: it found calls with
regular expressions and placed each by its receiver's declared type, read
from annotations above the call. D42 makes the compiler the authority;
§8.366 moved the residue onto the facts. This moves the lane gate's
counting.

## What changed

- The facts emitter (`sema/call_facts.cryo`) writes a `call` record for
  every call sema binds - zero-argument calls included - with the linker
  symbol and rendered declaration of what it reached. The `arg`/`cmp`
  records are unchanged: over every file but the emitter's own, the 12,119
  records are byte-identical before and after. The compiler's facts grow
  from 12,197 records (8.8 MB) to 48,913 (32 MB); 36,729 are `call`.
- `scripts/lane-gate.py` counts from `call` records. A call is a store's
  when its declaration is a method of the store's type - the symbol names
  a member (`-`, the mangling spec) and the rendered owner is the store's
  path, `compiler::` plus its file's path. It is name-keyed when that
  signature names `SymbolStr`, `string` or `ModulePath`, read by each
  type's last path segment, so `std::collections::string::String` is not
  `string`. The receiver's kind picks the row: `mut &this` the write row,
  `&this` or static the read row. `get_resolver`, `DefTable::path_of` and
  `set_home_module` are matched by their declaration. A store's own files
  are excluded as before.
- Refusals: an unpinned call whose written method is one a row counts; a
  store no call in the facts reaches (a store whose path the reader renders
  differently would otherwise count zero); a record of another shape;
  missing or stale facts.
- Deleted: the call patterns (`call_patterns`, the cast and static-owner
  patterns), the receiver placement's use, the declared name-keyed sets
  (`store_methods`) and the three door regexes. Rules 1, 1b and 1c (stores,
  array owners, inline scans) and the sealed-type check still read the
  tree.
- `lane-check` depends on `facts-fresh`; CI runs it after `make facts`.

## Evidence

Old gate (the parent's script) and new, every counted site listed, the
old gate instrumented to name each site
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.368/diff_lane.py`, which reads the parent's gate
from git):

| bucket | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| LOOKUP | 5 | 5 |
| LOOKUP_OTHER | 92 | 92 |
| REGISTER | 31 | 31 |
| LOOKUP_ROUTED | 36 | 36 |
| LOOKUP_LOCAL | 56 | **51** |
| ARENA_READ | 61 | 61 |
| ARENA_WRITE | 44 | 44 |
| REGISTRY_READ | 12 | 12 |
| REGISTRY_WRITE | 8 | 8 |
| GRAPH_READ | 62 | 62 |
| GRAPH_WRITE | 1 | 1 |
| CONST_READ | 3 | 3 |
| CONST_WRITE | 2 | 2 |
| REENTRY | 13 | 13 |
| HOME_WRITE | 0 | 0 |
| DEFID_PATH | 52 | 52 |

Five site differences, one cause. `ScopeManager.lookup_local` at
`sema/call_resolver.cryo:287`, `:2648`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo:252`,
`:540`, `sema/sema.cryo:1696` were `LOOKUP_LOCAL` because the resolver
DECLARES a name-keyed `lookup_local` - which nothing calls. The facts know
only methods that calls reach. The old declared sets and the sets the facts
reach agree for every store but that one method (35/35, 7/7, 24/24, 8/8,
10/10, 5/5, 36/35).

The re-pin, `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 56 -> 51, is a decrease on a floor row and is
not ratified.

The pair - each probe planted alone next to `type_resolution.cryo`'s one

- a per-kind lookup after `const probe_b: string = "a//b";` on the same

Controls:

- The self-test (`scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py`): 28 tree mutations (the

### 8.369 A residue site whose every key argument is a string literal is classified from the compiler's facts, with no written reason: 98 of the 127 "not a key" sites, none of the 192 justified ones; 29 sites remain whose reason is prose; no compiler source changed - 2026-09-27

## What changed

`residue_classify.py` has a rule decided from the facts rather than from a
table. A site is class **L** (constant key) when every key argument's
provenance, as the compiler reports it, is one string literal:

```cryo
// L: the key is a literal in the compiler's source. Nothing the program
// being compiled wrote can reach it.
const type_ref: TypeRef = this.ctx.decl_index.type_of_decl(node.def, "codegen/declare struct type");

// Not L, stays in the remainder: the string comes from the context.
const idx: i64 = ctx.module_graph.find_module_by_path(ctx.source_file);
```

The records behind those two lines (`.facts/compiler.facts`, fields 1-3,
5-7, 13):

```
arg  src/compiler/codegen/Ops/declaration_emitter.cryo  235  1  string  literal:"codegen/declare struct type"  DeclarationIndex.type_of_decl(&this, DefId, string) -> TypeRef
arg  src/compiler/codegen/passes.cryo  1408  0  string  field:CompilationContext*.source_file<-param:ctx  ModuleGraph.find_module_by_path(&this, string) -> i64
```

The match is `literal:"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"` repeated with `, ` over the whole
joined key (`CONSTANT_KEY.fullmatch`). The compiler escapes a quote or
backslash inside a literal's text (`CallFacts::literal_text`), so a literal
cannot end early or run into the next argument. An f-string is a chain of
`fmt` calls and a concatenation is `expr:BinaryExpression`, so neither
reads as a literal.

The rule is checked before the site overrides and the method table. A new
call passing a literal is classified with no row, even into a method the
tables never saw. A site override naming a literal site refuses both
`residue_classify.py` and `residue.py --check`.

What the rule does NOT take, on purpose: a literal through a local
(`const l = "x"; f(l)`), through a call (`intern("Ready")`, which the `lang`
reads use and which stay J), beside a key that is not a literal, a
non-string literal. Each step in between is a place a program's spelling
could enter.

## Why it is correct

A literal key asks the same question for every program compiled. The
defect this migration removes is a program's spelling finding the wrong
declaration by text, and no spelling from the program reaches such a call.
The rule does not tell a diagnostic label from a name the compiler fixes (a
lookup passed `"std::ops::Drop"` directly would read L); none does that
today, and both are outside the population's question either way.

## Measured

Prediction before editing: 98 sites move N -> L, 0 from J, population 319
and J 192 unchanged; wrong if any J site moved or the count was not 98.
Result: exactly 98, every one N -> L, nothing else moved (per-site
comparison of the list before and after by (file, method, key); a first
comparison with `awk -F'|'` reported J rows changing, because cells contain
escaped pipes - the instrument, not the list).

`python scripts/ns-migration/residue.py --check` -> `J 192, L 98, N 29;
convertible 0` (was `J 192, N 127`).

The 29 left, each where the string came from somewhere with steps:

| sites | what | provenance |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | `ModuleGraph::find_module_by_path` | a file path: a parameter, a span's file, the context's source file, `resolve_import_path` of an import path, `intern.resolve` of a spec owner's source |
| 3 | `ModuleGraph::module_of_file` | a span's file, a parameter |
| 1 | `ModuleGraph::ns_sym_of_file` | a parameter file path |
| 2 | `ResolutionContext::new` | the context's source file |
| 3 | `DeclarationIndex::lookup_type` / `lookup_func_type` / `lookup_method_return` in `type_utils.cryo` | the funnel's own parameters (its callers are the sites) |
| 2 | `ImplBlockNode::set_target_type` | a write: a specialized identifier; an if-expression |
| 1 | `TraitType::add_assoc_type` | a write: a trait's associated-type name |
| 2 | `ConstantTable::intern_qualified` | a declaration's namespace and name, registering it |
| 1 | `ConstantTable::parse_int_literal` | a literal node's value text |
| 1 | `GenericRegistry::member_template_key` | an owner key and a method's name |
| 1 | `DestructureDeclNode::bindings[]` in the dumper | a binding's own name |

## The rule's inversion

`scripts/ns-migration/8.369/rule_mutations.py` applies five mutations to
the classifier, each alone, and runs the self-test and the real-tree check:

- the key's PREFIX is enough (`match` for `fullmatch`): the rule fires on
  `literal:"std", param:name`. Real-tree check `residue: OK -- ... L 98, N 29`;
  self-test refuses: `rule case (a literal beside a parameter): ... classed L, want N`.
- the rule never fires: self-test refuses 7 cases; real-tree check refuses
  98 rows.
- an escaped quote ends the literal: real-tree check OK; self-test refuses
  `literal:"a\", param:name`.
- a site override may reclass a literal site: real-tree check OK; self-test
  refuses.
- the method table outranks the rule: self-test refuses 5 cases; real-tree
  check refuses 98 rows.

Three of the five pass the real-tree check, because no site in the tree has
the shape; the self-test's cases are the only thing that sees them.

`residue_selftest.py` gains 12 classification cases, the override refusal
and one end-to-end case (a literal key into a method no table classes is
drift, not refused as unclassified).

## Still open

- 29 sites carry a prose reason and no command.
- A new read METHOD still needs a row in `CLASS_OF_METHOD`, unless every
  call to it passes literals. A new call to an existing method takes that
  method's row, so an interesting provenance lands in its class with no
  edit - and moves the pinned count, which is how it is seen.

### 8.370 The lane gate's inline-scan rule reads the compiler's facts, and its source-pattern reader is deleted: 19 arrays it could not see are placed, 2 stale entries go, the facts learn which loop a `while` counter drives; residue 319 -> 320; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What changed

Rule 1c of `scripts/lane-gate.py` - every array a caller searches inline by
a key must be placed as a TABLE or as DATA - found those loops with regular
expressions over source lines. It now reads them from the facts
(`facts_scans`): a `cmp` record, or the `arg` record of a key type's
`equals`/`eq`, one of whose operands is read off an element the innermost
loop around the comparison reads. The regex reader (`inline_scans`, its
eleven patterns and helpers, and the tree's receiver-typing methods only it
used) is deleted, in this commit.

```cryo
for (mut i: i64 = 0; i < methods.length; i++) {
    const mnode: MethodNode* = methods[i];
    const fn_node: FunctionDeclNode* = mnode.func;
    if (!fn_node.name.equals(method_name)) { continue; }   // a scan of `methods`
```

The record behind that comparison (`call_resolver.cryo:388`; operands and
depth):

```
arg ... param:method_name
        field:FunctionDeclNode*.name<-local:fn_node@1=field:MethodNode*.func<-local:mnode@1=element@1:param:methods
        depth 1
```

`element@1` is read by the loop at depth 1, the record's own depth, so the
array searched is `methods`, labelled `local.MethodNode` by the element's
type. The residue's own reader could not follow the second local; the
residue now reads scans through the same function (one definition of "a
scan"), and this site joins it: population 319 -> 320, J 192 -> 193.

What stays read from declarations, because the facts record calls and
comparisons and say nothing about declarations: which types own a map or an
array of names (rules 1 and 1b), the file a scanned array's owner is
declared in, the class that declares an inherited array, and the sealed-type
check. A class's base is now read from its head (`type class X : Base`) so
an array read through a derived class's value is placed under the class
that declares it.

## The facts defect found on the way

A counter declared before a `while` was recorded at the depth it was
declared, not the loop it drives:

```cryo
mut i: i64 = 0;
while (i < ctx.orig.length) {
    if (ctx.orig[i].equals(name)) { return ctx.repl[i]; }   // async_lower.cryo:6041
    i++;
}
```

read `element@0` at depth 1, so no reader could see the scan. The compiler
now claims, for a `while` or `for` loop, a local its condition compares
directly AND the loop steps (`i++`, `i += 1`, `i = ..`) in its update or a
statement directly in its body; for the body it counts that loop, and the
old depth is handed back after (`CallFacts::claim_counters`,
`release_counters`, `stepped_locals`). A local the condition only compares
is a bound and is not claimed - the first draft claimed both operands, and
`j < i` inside a loop over `i` made the outer element read as the inner
loop's (`name_resolution.cryo:609` re-keyed); the draft was measured and
fixed before this lands. A counter stepped only inside a nested `if` is not
seen: the limit, pinned by `scripts/ns-migration/8.370/loop_counter_facts.py`.

Facts before and after, compiler: the same 46,892 records outside the two
edited files, 107 of them differing only in a depth mark (0 once `@d` is
normalised); +37 records inside the edited files, all in the new code.

## Old against new, site by site

`python scripts/ns-migration/8.370/diff_scans.py` (the old reader loaded
from `29b46dad`): key-scan records 170 old, 211 new; 17 lines only the old
reader counted, 50 only the new one.

Old only (17): 14 reads by POSITION outside any loop (`dir.args[0]`, eleven
in `directive_processing.cryo`; `pending_doc_comments[0]`; two
`reg.entries[idx]` in `autovendor.cryo`) - the regex had no notion of a
loop; 3 comparisons of two elements where it took the left one and the
innermost loop reads the other (`commands.cryo:1839`, `instance.cryo:1476`,
`ast_validation.cryo:213`).

New only (50): those 3 other sides; 1 join both of whose elements the
innermost loop reads (`instance.cryo:3502`); 8 tables whose element is a
`Pair` (the regex typed only elements declared in the tree); 17 arrays of
interned ids (`u32[]`) compared with a key's `.id`; 13 `string[]` locals and
parameters; 6 keys read through a local bound to a member of the element or
through two locals; 2 `while` loops visible only after the facts fix
(`test_main_codegen.cryo:234`, `:235`).

Identity scans (the check that an IDENTITY entry is searched by an identity
and never by a name): 12 lines only the old reader saw, each an element on
the ARGUMENT side of `TypeRef.equals` (`np.equals(f.param_types[i])`) - a

### 8.371 The gates refuse stale facts instead of rebuilding them, and eight rulings are recorded: five lane re-pins and the import rule ratified, the text-to-module door ruled against, five decisions for later units - 2026-09-27

## Stale facts are refused

`lane-check` and `check-fast` depended on `facts-fresh`, which ran
`scripts/facts.py --if-stale`: when any source had changed since the facts
were written, the gate first built the compiler and re-ran `--emit=facts`
over three projects - minutes of work a one-minute gate paid silently.
Ruled: refreshing the facts is a deliberate act, not a hidden cost.

Now:

* `facts-fresh` and `--if-stale` are deleted. `make facts` is the only
  refresh.
* `facts-check` runs `facts.py --check` and builds nothing; `lane-check` and
  `check-fast` run it first. Over a stale tree check-fast stops in 0.3 s:

  ```
  facts: STALE -- .facts/lsp.facts was written from other sources; run `make facts`
  make: *** [Makefile:735: facts-check] Error 1
  ```

  The readers were already refusing on their own (`facts_path`, which
  `lane-gate.py` and the residue call, raises on a stale file); what
  changed is that nothing regenerates behind them.
* `scripts/verify.py` refuses up front when its `fast` gate is selected and
  the facts are stale, instead of running five minutes of other gates first.
* `scripts/facts-selftest.py` (`make facts-selftest`, in check-fast and in
  CI's self-test step): the freshness check over a throwaway tree through
  both entry points (`--check`, `facts_path`) - an edited source, an added
  source, a missing inputs record refused by name; fresh facts and an edit
  to a non-source file accepted - and `make -n` of `lane-check` and
  `check-fast` in the repository, which must run the check and print no
  compiler build and no facts generation. A dry run prints a regenerating
  prerequisite's recipe whether or not the facts are stale, so this half
  does not depend on the tree's state.

Inversion, each mutation alone:

| tree | self-test |
|---|---|
| the Makefile and `facts.py` before this change | `FAIL (2 of 12 cases)`: both targets' dry runs print the stage-2 build and `facts.py --cryo ... --if-stale` |
| this change | `OK (12 cases ...)` |
| this change, staleness comparison deleted from `check()` | `FAIL (4 of 12 cases)`: the edited and added source accepted, through both entry points |
| this change, `lane-check: facts` (regenerating) | `FAIL (2 of 12 cases)` |

`CLAUDE.md`'s command list and its check-fast paragraph said a stale
`.facts/` is rebuilt first; they now say it is refused, and that `make
facts` is run after a source change. The cost moves, it does not vanish:
a session that edits compiler source runs `make facts` before `check-fast`
or `verify`.

### 8.372 A type's and a template's module are stored as a module identity, not as text: the arena's four type records, the template registry's entries, the specialization table and the injected-origin table; four text-door sites and one qualified-name split go; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What was stored, and what read it

The arena's struct, class, enum and trait records and the template registry's
entries each carried `module_name: SymbolStr` - the text of a namespace, or,
for a unit declaring none and for every closure and async-state struct, the
text of a SOURCE FILE PATH. Every reader that needed the module turned the
text back into one, or split a qualified name to find it:

```cryo
// member_resolver.cryo, the field visibility check (before)
type_module(&this, t: Type*) -> ModulePath {
    if (t.kind == TypeKind::Struct) {
        return this.ctx.module_graph.module_named((t as StructType*).module_name);
    }
    ...
}

// specialization.cryo, which file owns a specialization's type argument (before)
const qname: QualifiedName = QualifiedName::parse(ctx.intern_table, qs);
const parent_str: string = qname.display_parent(ctx.intern_table);
fallback = ctx.module_graph.source_file_for_owner_key(
    ctx.intern_table.intern(parent_str), ctx.intern_table);
```

The facts record for that last argument, before:

```
arg  specialization.cryo  528  ...  SymbolStr
     call:InternTable.intern(..) of local:parent_str@0=call:QualifiedName.display_parent(..) ...
```

and after, the same question asked of the record:

```
arg  specialization.cryo  522  ...  ModulePath
     call:TypeArena.declared_in(&this, Type*) -> ModulePath of local:t@0=call:TypeArena.lookup(..) ...
```

## What is stored now

* `StructType`, `ClassType`, `EnumType`, `TraitType`: `declared_in:
  ModulePath`, set from the declaration's DEFINITION -
  `ModuleGraph::declaring_module(def)`, the nearest module on the
  definition's parent chain (`DefTable::module_of`), answered as the path the
  graph registered that module under. Identity to identity: no spelling is
  read. A C import's types get the C import's module this way (its
  definition is the alias's), which the text route reached only through the
  text door.
* `TemplateEntry.declared_in: ModulePath`, set from the unit writing the
  template's body (`CompilationContext::current_module`, the module the
  unit's source file declares) - the module whose scope the monomorphizer
  resolves the body in. A static method written in another module's
  `implement` block is resolved in the impl's module, not the owner type's,
  so this is deliberately not the definition's module.
* `SpecializationEntry.template_module: ModulePath`, copied from the entry.
* The context's injected-origin table holds `ModulePath[]`;
  `lookup_injected_origin` and `TypeUtils::find_template_module` return one.
* `ModuleGraph::source_file_of(m: ModulePath)`: a module's file by its
  identity. `source_file_for_owner_key` stays for its last caller (the
  incremental build's spec-owner list, still text).
* Readers: the field visibility check reads `TypeArena::declared_in`; the
  monomorphizer and sema switch into the template's module by the stored
  path; the file-ownership walk reads the type's record instead of splitting
  its qualified name. `spec_base_name` and `is_free_function` still read the
  module's TEXT (`declared_in.as_sym()`) to measure a qualified name - an
  owner segment found by string length, left for its own unit.
* Deleted: `MemberResolver::type_module`; an unread `module_name` local in
  `ast_resolver.cryo`; `AsyncLower::repoint_method`'s unread namespace
  parameter; three writers' `if has_namespace { namespace } else { source

* An import turns its written path into the module ONCE, at the top of

## What was text

The resolver answers four questions about a module's declarations -

each took the module as `SymbolStr` text. Its export table is keyed by the
module's interned id, so the text was only ever a key, but every caller

`ModulePath` and answered `SymbolStr[]`, so every walk over a re-export

```cryo

reexport_offering(&this, m: SymbolStr, name: SymbolStr) -> SymbolStr {
    const via: SymbolStr[] = this.ctx.module_graph.reexport_closure(this.ctx.module_graph.module_named(m));
    ...
}
```

and `CompilationContext::modules_written_as` found a module by walking the

`any`), which the qualified-path walks handed to those questions.

## What they take and answer now

* `Resolver::get_exports`, `exports_named`, `export_in`,
  `private_declarations` take `m: ModulePath`; the table is keyed by
  `m.as_sym().id`, the same key as before.
* `ModuleGraph::reexport_closure` answers `ModulePath[]`. It walks the
  re-export lists the loader recorded - text, the declarations'
  spellings - and hands out each one the graph holds as a module, turning
  it once, at the end of the walk. A recorded namespace the graph does not
  hold is left out; no export question could answer anything for it.
* `ModuleSpellingMatch.found`, `other` and `any` are `ModulePath`s

  definition (`ModuleGraph::declaring_module`, identity to identity), where
  it was the alias's qualified name composed as text.
* The resolver's prelude list is `ModulePath[]`, turned from the
  namespaces the prelude's declarations spell once, where it is installed
  (`set_prelude_modules`).

```cryo
// compilation_context.cryo (before)
module_def_of(&this, ns: SymbolStr) -> DefId {
    if (!ns.is_valid() || this.module_graph == null) { return DefId::invalid(); }
    return this.module_graph.module_def(this.module_graph.module_named(ns));
}
```

`module_ns_sym_of_file`), then handed to the spelling match, the E0240
reachability check and the callee visibility check, each of which turned
it back into a module:

```cryo

enforce_callee_visibility(mut &this, callee: DefId, use_ns: SymbolStr, span: SourceSpan) -> void {
    const use_module: DefId = this.ctx.module_graph.module_def(this.ctx.module_graph.module_named(use_ns));
    ...
}
```

```cryo
    if (this.state.in_symbolic_check) { return; }
    if (!this.ctx.decl_index.hidden_from(callee, this.ctx.module_def_of(use_module))) { return; }
```

### 8.376 The module graph's edge lists and the prelude list are module identities: the loader records edges as text during discovery, the graph turns them into modules once when discovery finishes, and every reader - build order, the dependency closure, the re-export closure, the import registration, the prelude - reads identities; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What was text

Each `ModuleInfo` carried four lists of namespaces as text:
`dependencies` (build order), `imported_namespaces` (what the module can
see), `submodules` (its `public module` declarations) and `reexports` (its
`export` declarations). The loader records them while it discovers
modules, and an import inside a cycle names a module still being loaded,
which the graph does not hold yet - so an edge could not be a module when
written. Every reader turned the text back into a module, each time it
read it:

```cryo
// module_graph.cryo, build order (before)
const deps: &SymbolStr[] = &this.modules[i].dependencies;
for (mut d: i64 = 0; d < deps.length; d++) {
    const dep_idx: i64 = this.find_module_index(ModulePath::of(deps[d]));
```

and the orchestrator handed the prelude's sub-modules and each module's
visible set to the declaration index as text, which handed the prelude to
the resolver as text, which turned each into a module through the text
door (`set_prelude_modules`).

## What it is now

* `dependencies`, `imported_namespaces`, `submodules` and `reexports` are
  `ModulePath[]`.
* The loader's `add_dependency`, `add_imported_namespace`, `add_reexport`
  and `add_submodule` are unchanged in what they take - the namespace each
  target declares - and record it in `written_dependencies`,
  `written_imported`, `written_submodules`, `written_reexports`, with the
  same self-edge and duplicate rules as before.
* `ModuleGraph::resolve_edges`, called once by the orchestrator right
  after discovery finishes, turns each recorded list into modules through
  `modules_of` - the one place the recorded text meets the text door - and
  empties the recorded lists. A recorded namespace the graph holds no
  module for is left out; a DEPENDENCY left out is counted
  (`unresolved_dependencies`), and `compute_import_closure` reports a
  closure through that module as incomplete, exactly as it did when it met
  the unresolvable text, so the incremental cache still declines to reuse
  an object keyed on it.

```cryo
// module_graph.cryo, build order (after)
const deps: &ModulePath[] = &this.modules[i].dependencies;
for (mut d: i64 = 0; d < deps.length; d++) {
    const dep_idx: i64 = this.find_module_index(deps[d]);
```

* `reexport_closure` walks identities end to end; its final pass turning
  the walked text into modules is gone.
* `DeclarationIndex::register_module_imports(m: ModulePath, imports:
  &ModulePath[])` and `register_prelude_namespaces(prelude: ModulePath[])`;
  the index keeps the prelude as `prelude_modules: ModulePath[]` and hands
  it out as `ModulePath[]`; `Resolver::set_prelude_modules` takes
  `ModulePath[]` and no longer asks the door.
* The orchestrator's visible-set walk compares modules (`src.path().
  equals(via)`) where it compared namespace ids.

**An array's methods are not argument-checked before codegen.** In a

## One allocator per table (D48): measured, blocked

The ruling: nothing outside a table can construct a second `SymbolID`
allocator (`SymbolIds`) or a second `DefTable`. Each alone, `cryo check`
over a copy of `compiler/` (control: no errors):

* A second allocator in an unrelated module - `mut ids: SymbolIds =
  SymbolIds::new(); return ids.next();` added to `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`
  - **compiles, no error.**
* A second table in that module - `mut t: DefTable =
  DefTable::new(intern); return t.register(DefId::invalid(), ...);` -
  **compiles, no error.** Its `DefId` names position 0 of its own table,
  which is some other definition in the real one.
* `SymbolIds::new` made private -> `error[E0353]: method new of
  compiler::resolver::symbol_id::SymbolIds is private ... private method
  called outside module compiler::resolver::symbol_id`, at
  `resolver/resolver.cryo:129` - the resolver, its one owner.
* `DefTable::new` made private -> `error[E0353]: method new of
  compiler::resolver::res::DefTable is private`, at
  `compilation_context.cryo:309` - the context, its one owner.

Cryo's `private` reaches the declaring module and nothing else; `protected`
(which also reaches nested modules) exists for classes only. Each owner
lives in another module than its table, and neither can move: `Symbol`
(`symbol.cryo`) imports `SymbolID`'s module and the resolver imports
`Symbol`, so `SymbolID` cannot live in the resolver's module; the module
graph imports `DefTable`'s module and the context imports the module
graph, so `DefTable` cannot live in the context's. So "constructible by its
owner only" cannot be written in the language as it stands. The ways
forward are a choice, recorded in D48's row: a visibility that reaches one
named module; D47's generation tags, which would catch an identity from a
second table where it is read; or the allocator folded into a table type
in the identity's own module, which makes a second ALLOCATOR impossible
but leaves a second table constructible.

### 8.378 A C import's module is registered once by the importer and every declaration it synthesizes carries the module, not its namespace text; the declaration index's global table is keyed by the declaring module; the name layer's C-import door and the global table's name splitter are deleted; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What was text

The C-header importer composes a namespace for each `extern module cit :=
"C" { ... }` - the declaring module's namespace with the alias under it
(`app::cit`) - and wrote it as TEXT on the extern block and on every
struct, union, enum, alias and global it synthesized
(`binding_namespace: SymbolStr`). Everything downstream turned it back
into a module: the name layer through its own door
(`c_import_module(binding_ns)` -> `module_named`), the function
registration through the context's `module_family_named`, the type mapper
by splicing it into `app::cit::Tag` spellings.

The declaration index kept every module-level global in a slot keyed by
`(leaf, namespace text)`, and a definition's global was found by
splitting its canonical name back into that pair:

```cryo
// decl_index.cryo (before)
global_entry_of_def(&this, d: DefId, intern: InternTable*) -> GlobalEntry {
    mut leaf: SymbolStr = SymbolStr::empty();
    mut ns: SymbolStr = SymbolStr::empty();
    DeclarationIndex::split_global_key(this.defs.path_of(d), intern, &leaf, &ns);
    return this.global_entry_at(this.global_slot(leaf, ns));
}
```

and a qualified path's global (`libc::FIONBIO`) was asked by the text of
the module definition's path (`global_slot(name, this.defs.path_of(module_id))`).

## What it is now

* `ModuleGraph::register_c_import_module(ns) -> ModulePath` - called by
  the importer at the one place it composes the namespace - enters the
  module in the graph and answers its identity. The block and every
  declaration the importer synthesizes hold `binding_namespace:
  ModulePath`. When the name layer binds the alias it hands the graph that
  identity (`bind_c_import_module(m: ModulePath, def)`), no longer text,
  and declares the import's types and globals in it directly: the
  `c_import_module` door is deleted.

```cryo
// bindgen/importer.cryo (after)
extern_node.binding_namespace = ctx.module_graph.register_c_import_module(ctx.intern_table.intern(
    mod_name + "::" + ctx.intern_table.resolve(extern_node.namespace_alias)));

// resolver/name_resolution.cryo (after)
declare_c_imported_global(&this, c_module: ModulePath, node: VarDeclNode*) -> void {
```

* The type mapper and the pending record references (`c_ref_alias`) hold
  the module; the mapper reads its text only to spell `app::cit::Tag`.
* The global table's module column is `module_global_declared_in:
  ModulePath[]` (the file column is renamed `module_global_files`, which
  is what it always held). `GlobalEntry` carries `declared_in: ModulePath`
  and `source_file`. `global_slot`, `global_entry_in_module`,
  `record_global_extern_symbol` and `mark_global_thread_local` take a
  `ModulePath`; the registration key's module comes out of
  `decl_global_key` as the identity it already was (the file's module, the
  unit's, or the C import's).
* A definition's global is asked by the compilation context, which holds
  the graph: its leaf under the module its PARENT is
  (`CompilationContext::global_entry_of_def`, through the new
  `module_of_def` - the module a definition IS, none for any other
  definition). A definition nested in a type asks under no module a global
  is registered in, exactly as the split name of `Mod::Type::x` named no
  global's namespace before. `split_global_key` is deleted.
* A qualified path's global is asked under `module_of_def(stamp)`: a stamp
  naming a type or nothing asks under no module.
* Codegen mangles and caches a global under `declared_in.as_sym()` - the
  same text as before, so no symbol moved.

One behaviour differs, on a population the corpus does not have: a C
import in a unit with no `namespace` declaration. Its globals register
under `<file>::cit`, while the alias's definition path is `cit`, so the
split reader asked under `cit` and found nothing; the module a definition's
parent is answers `<file>::cit`, where they registered.

### 8.379 The monomorphizer's remaining "module" stores held a source file or nothing: the method-spec owner list, the call specializer's current module and an impl block's `source_module` are named for the file they hold, the namespace-or-file owner lookup is deleted, and the registry's per-module demand list and the specialization table's origin module - written, never read - are deleted; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What the stores held

The last stores on D45's list were measured before converting them, and
none holds a module:

* `MonoState.spec_owner_modules` - the unit that emits each generic-method
  specialization, for the incremental cache. Its two writers
  (`CallSpecializer::register_spec_method_in_di` and
  `register_spec_method_in_di_inherent`, the only callers the type checker
  finds) record `impl_node.source_module`, the call specializer's
  `current_module`, or `owner_ast.span.file`.
* `DeclarationNode.source_module` is written once, by the type-resolution
  pass, as `ctx.source_file`; the cloner copies it. A FILE.
* The monomorphizer's and call specializer's `current_module` are set in
  three places, all `ctx.intern(ctx.source_file)`. A FILE.

So every key in the owner list is a source file, and
`ModuleGraph::source_file_for_owner_key` - which asked first whether a key
was some module's NAMESPACE, then whether it was a module's file - could
answer only through its second loop: a namespace never equals a file path.
Its first loop is a text-to-module lookup that no key reached.

Two more were never read at all:

* `GenericRegistry.demand`, a `(instantiation, module text)` pair pushed by
  `instantiate_for_module` - which is `instantiate` plus that push - on
  every instantiation from seven call sites. Nothing reads the list.
* `SpecializationEntry.origin_module`, written from the current module
  once per specialization and read nowhere.

## What changed

```cryo
// instance.cryo, the method-spec owners (before)
const key: SymbolStr = ctx.monomorphizer.spec_owner_module_at(s);
if (!key.is_valid()) { pm_active = false; continue; }
const src: SymbolStr = ctx.module_graph.source_file_for_owner_key(key, ctx.intern_table);
if (!src.is_valid()) { pm_active = false; continue; }
const midx: i64 = ctx.module_graph.find_module_by_path(ctx.intern_table.resolve(src));

// after - the same lookup the type/free-function specs' owners already use
const src: SymbolStr = ctx.monomorphizer.spec_owner_file_at(s);
if (!src.is_valid()) { pm_active = false; continue; }
const midx: i64 = ctx.module_graph.find_module_by_path(ctx.intern_table.resolve(src));
```

* `spec_owner_modules` -> `spec_owner_files`, `record_spec_owner_module`
  -> `record_spec_owner_file`, the monomorphizer's count/at readers
  likewise; `source_file_for_owner_key` deleted.
* `current_module` -> `current_source_file` in the monomorphizer and the
  call specializer (`set_current_source_file`).
* `DeclarationNode.source_module` -> `source_file` (`set_source_file`).
* `instantiate_for_module` and `demand` deleted; the seven callers call
  `instantiate` with the same base and arguments, and the three locals
  that interned the source file only to hand it over go with them.
* `origin_module` deleted.

## Measurements

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: tests 3,515,
  moved 0; examples 1,126, moved 0; census, examples, editor, other-OS and
  incremental gates OK. Predicted 0.
* `cryo check src/main.cryo`: 346 warnings, same (code, file) set.
* Name-taking functions 1,095 -> 1,093 (predicted: `instantiate_for_module`
  and `source_file_for_owner_key`; the renamed setters still take text,
  which is a file); `module_named(` unchanged at 14 (predicted).
* Residue 303 -> 302, J 179 -> 178: the orchestrator's
  `source_file_for_owner_key` site; its classification is removed from
  `residue_classify.py` with the method. The `find_module_by_path` row
  beside it is re-keyed (its argument no longer passes through the deleted
  lookup), class N as before.
* Lane gate, decreases only: REGISTRY_WRITE 8 -> 1 (the seven
  `instantiate_for_module` calls, each handing the registry a module's
  text), GRAPH_READ 49 -> 48 (`source_file_for_owner_key`).

## Does any gate watch the owner loop?

The change is to what the incremental cache reads, which no object
comparison sees: a clean build never reuses an object. So the loop was
broken on purpose - the owner it reads left unflagged
(`pm_owns_spec[midx] = false`) - and a compiler built from that tree was
handed to the incremental gate (`scripts/incremental-instance-check.py
--cryo <that compiler>`): `incremental-instance-check: FAIL -- the
incremental build after the edit: build exit 1, run exit None (want 0 and
4)`, the link refused (`error[E0900]: linker invocation failed`) because
the owner's cached object predates the spec. The unmutated compiler over
the same script: `incremental-instance-check: OK -- first build ran 3;
after the edit the incremental build reused 37 cached object(s), linked
and ran 4`. The gate covers this reader.

## Not an inversion, and why

These stores still hold text, because a file path IS text: nothing here
makes a wrong key fail to compile. The claim is narrower - that none of
them holds a module - and its evidence is the enumeration above (every
writer the type checker finds), the deletions compiling (no reader was
left), and 0 objects moved.

### 8.380 Definition and symbol identities carry the tag of the table that made them, and each table refuses, where it reads, an id another table made or one made before a rebuild; the resolver refuses a symbol admitted at a slot its id does not name; 0 objects moved, no measurable cost - 2026-09-27

## The hole

A `DefId` was a bare position in the `DefTable`, and a `SymbolID` a bare
number from the resolver's `SymbolIds`. §8.377 showed a second allocator
and a second table both compile from an unrelated module. What that costs
is a wrong answer, not an error: an id from the second table is a valid
position in the first, and the first answers whatever it holds there. The
same holds for an id kept across a table REBUILD. Measured over the tree
before this change (the harness below, built against the previous
commit's compiler source):

```
foreign           exit   0  foreign: 'alpha'            # B's id for 'beta', read by A
stale             exit   0  stale: 'gamma'              # the id made for 'alpha', read after a rebuild
sym_foreign       exit   0  sym_foreign: 'x_one'        # resolver 2's id for 'y_two', read by resolver 1
synth_interleave  exit   0  synth_interleave: 'b_second'   # see below
```

Every one exits 0 having answered a different declaration.

## What changed

```cryo
// resolver/res.cryo
type struct DefId {
private:
    index: u32;
    table: u32;          // the tag of the table that made it; 0 = invalid
}
// DefTable: `tag` from a process-wide counter at `new`, stamped by `append`;
// every read goes through
slot(&this, d: DefId) -> i64 {
    if (d.table != this.tag) { DefTable::refuse(d.table, this.tag); }
    return d.index as i64;
}
```

* `DefTable` - `path_of`, `parent_of`, `leaf_of`, `kind_of`, `module_of`,
  `origin_of`, the visibility and refused-signature reads and writes, and
  `append`'s read of the parent's path: each indexes through `slot`.
  `DefId::equals` compares the tag too.
* `SymbolID` is a 32-bit sequence number and a 32-bit tag (8 bytes, as
  before); `SymbolIds::slot_of` refuses an id another allocator made and
  the invalid id. `key()` is unchanged - still the sequence number the
  passes key their own tables by.
* The resolver's arena reads (`get_symbol`, the import-target read, the
  existing-binding read) go through `slot_of`; the dead-code pass, which
  indexed the arena directly by `key() - 1`, asks `get_symbol`.
* `Resolver::admit` checks that the symbol it pushes lands at the slot its
  id names. It did not: an id handed out with no symbol behind it
  (`alloc_synthetic_binding`) followed by a declaration made every later
  `get_symbol` read the NEXT symbol - the harness's `synth_interleave`
  answers `b_second` for `a_first` over the old tree. The corpus never
  interleaves them (the census passes with the check in place); the check
  is what keeps that true.
* A refusal is a panic: `internal compiler error: a definition id made by
  table 2 was read against table 1 (the invalid id carries 0)`, exit 101.

## Evidence

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: tests 3,515,
  moved 0; examples 1,126, moved 0; census, examples, editor, other-OS,
  incremental gates and check-fast OK. Predicted 0: no id reaches output.
* `cryo check src/main.cryo`: 346 warnings, same (code, file) set.
* Editor answer harness (`scripts/ns-migration/8.377/editor_answers.py`,
  the server `make verify` linked): `wrong-or-missing 18 of 25`, the same
  as §8.377, no panic - the server holds contexts across requests and
  none reads another's ids.
* `python3 scripts/ns-migration/8.380/tag_harness.py --cryo <compiler>`
  builds `harness/` against `compiler/src` and runs each mode alone:

  ```
  ok    own               exit   0  own: 'alpha'
  ok    foreign           exit 101  ... a definition id made by table 2 was read against table 1 ...
  ok    stale             exit 101  ... a definition id made by table 1 was read against table 2 ...
  ok    sym_own           exit   0  sym_own: 'x_one'
  ok    sym_foreign       exit 101  ... symbol id 1 made by allocator 2 was read against allocator 1 ...
  ok    synth_interleave  exit 101  ... symbol admitted at arena slot 0, its id names slot 1
  tag-harness: OK -- 6 modes: every foreign or stale id refused, every own id answered
  ```

  The same script over a copy of `harness/` depending on the previous
  commit's compiler source (`--project`): `tag-harness: FAIL -- 4 of 6
  modes did not do what they must`, the four wrong answers quoted above.
  The own-table modes answer on both, which is the control.

## Cost

Whole-compiler type check (`cryo check src/main.cryo`), four rounds
alternating the previous commit's compiler and this one, each from a clean
build: median 22.40 s both (min 22.21 s / 22.32 s). One comparison per
read, and `DefId` grows from 4 to 8 bytes.

A first version kept `SymbolID`'s 64-bit number and added the tag beside
it, making it 16 bytes: median 22.99 s against 22.29 s, slower in every
round (+3%). Moving the panic out of the read path changed nothing (23.22
s against 22.34 s); packing the id back into 8 bytes removed the whole
difference. The cost was the size, not the comparison.

## What the tags do not do

They do not stop a second table or allocator being BUILT - §8.377's
mutations still compile. They make every id such a table hands out useless
against the compiler's own: refused at the first read, not answered. The
one-allocator ruling asks for construction itself to be refused; whether a
refusal at use is enough, and so whether a visibility level reaching one
named module is still wanted, is not this ledger's to decide.

`OverloadId`, `TypeRef` and the other arena positions carry no tag.

`dead_code.cryo`. New: `scripts/ns-migration/8.380/` (the harness project
and its runner; no gate runs it - it builds the compiler library, about
thirty seconds).

```cryo

    const m: i32 = Nope::make();      // Nope exists nowhere
```

answered, with the compiler at the previous commit:

```
error[E0900]: 15 path-bearing node(s) reached a stage requiring name resolution with no `Res` recorded; first required at default_expansion:scope segment
```

- no file, no line, and an internal-error code for a typo. The same for a
type whose MODULE is imported but which is not itself
(`import std::collections::hashmap;` then `HashMap::<i32, i32>::new()`:

compiler's own source when a file called `ModulePath::none()` without
importing `ModulePath` (§8.378).

The name layer's scope-segment stamp (`stamp_module_scope`) left a segment
that binds nothing in scope, spells no primitive and no module, UNANSWERED,

later stage actually needs it - with a location". The later stage is the
unanswered-slot counter, which has no location to give.

That branch now asks `refuse_unbound_type` - the reporter an unbound type
spelling already gets in a declaration - and answers `Err`:

```cryo
    if (canon.is_valid()) { ...; return; }
    if (this.refuse_unbound_type(node.scope_name, node.scope_span)) {
        node.set_scope_res(Res::Err);

    return;
}
```

It explains the name from what the program declares under it: none - E0203
with a did-you-mean; one, out of the writer's reach - E0240 with the import
that reaches it; two - E0155. Both repros now read:

```

 --> src/main.cryo:4:20
  |
4 |     const m: i32 = Nope::make();
  |                    ^~~~ not found in this scope
```

and `cannot find type HashMap in this scope` at `src/main.cryo:6:20`, one

### 8.382 The type arena is read by the handle it handed out, never by a number, and the generic-parameter lists hold handles; a `TypeRef` seal now refuses 205 sites where it refused 822; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## Why

`TypeRef` is to be sealed (D46): its number and constructor private to its
module, so no code can build a handle from a raw number. Tried at the
parent commit, with a compiler whose diagnostic cap was switched off
(`max_errors: 0` in `compiler/diag/config.cryo`, a measuring build only; the
shipped cap of 500 is what stopped the earlier count), the seal refuses
**822** sites in 59 files: 816 reads of `.id` and 6 calls of `TypeRef::new`;
no code outside the module reads `.arena`.

Of the 816 reads, about 600 were one shape: the arena's read took the
handle's number, so every caller unwrapped the handle it already held.

```cryo
// before
lookup(&this, id: u64) -> Type* { ... }
const t: Type* = this.arena.lookup(ty.id);

// after
lookup(&this, ty: TypeRef) -> Type* { ... }
const t: Type* = this.arena.lookup(ty);
```

A read that takes a number accepts any number - a stored one, a computed
one, one from another arena - and answers whichever type sits at that
position. A read that takes the handle accepts only a handle.

## What changed

* The arena's five number-taking reads take the handle: `lookup`,
  `pointer_pointee_of`, `array_element_of`, `resolve_display_name`,
  `resolve_display_name_short`. Codegen's three forwarders
  `lookup_type_by_id(id: u64)` are `arena_type(ty: TypeRef)` (not
  `lookup_type`: the declaration index has a name-keyed `lookup_type`, and
  sharing its name would count every forwarder call as a local lookup in
  the lane gate).
* The call sites were rewritten from the compiler's own refusals by
  `scripts/ns-migration/8.382/strip_id_args.py` (recipe in its README):
  every argument the check refused as `u64` where a `TypeRef` was wanted,
  and which read `<expr>.id`, lost the `.id` - 608 in the compiler, 28 in
  the editor; 90 forwarder calls renamed.
* Two arguments were not a handle's `.id` but a STORED number, and each
  was a real store, not a rewrite:
  - the generic-parameter lists held the parameters' numbers:
    `TemplateEntry.param_type_ids: u64[]`, `TypeSubstitution.param_ids:
    u64[]`, `InferCtx.param_ids: u64[]`. They hold the handles now
    (`param_types`, `params`, `params`: `TypeRef[]`), and
    `TypeSubstitution::add/get` and `InferCtx::binding_index` take the
    parameter's handle. This removed one of the six in-compiler forgeries
    the seal found:

    ```cryo
    // before - a handle rebuilt from a stored number
    owner_params.push(TypeRef::new(tmpl.param_type_ids[i], arena));
    // after
    owner_params.push(tmpl.param_types[i]);
    ```
  - the monomorphizer's scan for standalone dynamic arrays counted type
    numbers from 1 and read each through the arena; it walks the arena's
    type list, as the specialization pass and codegen's pass already do.
    It never needed the array type's handle, only its element's.
* 14 `u64[]` locals that feed those stores became `TypeRef[]`, and their
  pushes dropped `.id`. **No check lists those**: an array push is not
  argument-checked before code generation, so they were found by reading
  every writer of each store.

## Evidence

  build: census, examples, editor, other-OS, incremental all OK; tests
  3,515 objects moved 0, examples 1,126 moved 0; 346 warnings.

* Residue: 302 sites before and after, J 178; 13 rows re-keyed, because a
  row's provenance spells the chain its key came through
  (`lookup(&this, u64) of field TypeRef.id<-param:tref` now reads
  `lookup(&this, TypeRef) of param:tref`). With line numbers and that hop
  normalised the two lists are identical; before normalising the same
  comparison reports them different. Not predicted - the provenance was not
  in view when the prediction was made.
* Inversion, each mutation alone over a copy of this tree, with the
  unmutated copy as control (control: 346 warnings, exit 0):
  - the arena read handed a number (`arena.lookup(ty.id)` in
    `substitution.cryo`), `cryo check`:
    `error[E0214]: mismatched types --> src/compiler/types/substitution.cryo:107:39 ... expected `compiler::types::type_ref::TypeRef`, found `u64``.
  - a number pushed into a converted store (`pids.push(pref.id)` in

    The unmutated copy builds (exit 0).

### 8.383 `TypeRef` is sealed: its number is read one way through `key`, handles are compared through `equals`, and only the arena's allocator makes one; a handle forged from a number no longer compiles; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## Why

After §8.382 a seal of `TypeRef` refused 205 sites (uncapped): 200 reads of
`.id` and 5 calls of `TypeRef::new`. A handle anyone can build from a number
names whatever type sits at that position:

```cryo
// compiled before this entry, anywhere in the compiler
const t: TypeRef = TypeRef::new(5, arena);
const u: TypeRef = TypeRef { id: 5, arena: arena };
```

## What changed

* `type_ref.cryo`: the number, the arena pointer and the constructor are
  `private`. The number is read through `key()` - one way, for a pass's own
  table, a hash, or a debug line; there is no way back from it to a handle.
  A new allocator `TypeRefs` beside the handle is the one maker: `next`
  answers a fresh handle, `upcoming` the number the next one will carry (a
  `Type` records its own number when it is built, before the arena stores
  it). The arena holds its `TypeRefs` as a PRIVATE field in place of its
  `next_id` counter, and `alloc_type` mints through it.
* The 200 reads, rewritten where the compiler pointed by
  `scripts/ns-migration/8.383/seal_reads.py` (recipe in its README):
  - two handles compared by number, 54 comparisons, became `equals`:
    ```cryo
    // before
    if (e.specialized_type.id != target_type.id) { continue; }
    return (pt as PointerType*).pointee.id == (at as ReferenceType*).referent.id;
    // after
    if (!e.specialized_type.equals(target_type)) { continue; }
    return (pt as PointerType*).pointee.equals((at as ReferenceType*).referent);
    ```
  - every other read, 92, became `key()`: table keys
    (`type_reverse.insert(ty.key(), def)`), hashes, packed keys, debug
    prints.
* The 5 constructions, by hand:
  - the arena's own mint: through its allocator;
  - the mangler rebuilt the handle of the `Type*` it was encoding
    (`TypeRef::new(ty.id, this.arena)`) and took an instantiation's owner as
    a number; its `encode_type` now takes the handle its only caller,
    `encode_type_ref`, already holds, and `encode_instantiation_of` takes
    the owner's handle;
  - the symbolic checker rebuilt a receiver's base handle from the
    `Type*` a peeler answered (twice). `TypeUtils::unwrap_to_base_ref` is
    now the one peeler, answering the handle; `unwrap_to_base_type` reads
    through it, and the checker keeps the handle.

### 8.384 Type handles and signature ids carry the tag of the allocator or index that made them, and the arena and the declaration index refuse, where they read, one made elsewhere or before a rebuild; `TypeRef` shrinks from 16 bytes to 8; 0 objects moved, no measurable cost - 2026-09-27

## The hole

§8.380 tagged `DefId` and `SymbolID`. The other two identities were still
bare positions:

* A `TypeRef` held a position in its arena's sequence and a pointer to the
  arena (16 bytes). The arena read its storage by the position alone. Every
  arena holds the same 21 primitives at positions 1-21, so a first user type
  is number 22 in EVERY arena, and a handle from any arena names something
  in any other.
* An `OverloadId` held a position in the declaration index's registry
  (4 bytes). A second index's positions also start at 0.
* §8.383 left a live consequence: the allocator `TypeRefs` is public, so a
  second one compiles anywhere, and its first handle is number 1 - the
  arena's `void`.

Measured over the tree before this change - the harness below built against
the parent commit's compiler source (`tag_harness.py --before HEAD`):

```
sizes         exit   0  sizes: TypeRef 16, OverloadId 4
ty_own        exit   0  ty_own: 'i32*'
ty_foreign    exit   0  ty_foreign: 'u8*'        # arena B's `i32*`, read by arena A
ty_stale      exit   0  ty_stale: 'u8*'          # the handle made for `i32*`, read after
                                                 #   the arena was rebuilt IN THE SAME
                                                 #   VARIABLE - the same address
ty_allocator  exit   0  ty_allocator: 'void'     # a free-standing allocator's first handle
ovl_own       exit   0  ovl_own: 'sym_alpha'
ovl_foreign   exit   0  ovl_foreign: 'sym_alpha' # index Y's `sym_beta`, read by index X
ovl_stale     exit   0  ovl_stale: 'sym_gamma'   # the id made for `sym_alpha`, read after
                                                 #   a rebuild
```

Five of the eight exit 0 having answered a different type or a different
signature. `ty_stale` is the case only a tag can catch: the arena was
rebuilt at the same address, so even the arena pointer the old handle
carried still matched.

## What changed

```cryo
// types/type_ref.cryo - before
type struct TypeRef {
private:
    id:    u64;
    arena: TypeArena*;
}
// after
type struct TypeRef {
private:
    id:  u32;
    tag: u32;       // the tag of the TypeRefs that made it; 0 = invalid
}
// TypeRefs: `tag` from a process-wide counter at `new`, stamped by `next`
slot_of(&this, ty: TypeRef) -> i64 {
    if (ty.id == 0) { return -1; }
    if (ty.tag != this.tag) { TypeRefs::refuse(ty.id, ty.tag, this.tag); }
    return (ty.id - 1) as i64;
}
```

* The arena pointer was read by nothing but `is_valid` (§8.383 measured no
  reader outside the handle's module), and every handle already came from
  `TypeRefs::next(arena)` with a non-null arena, so `is_valid` is `id != 0`
  exactly as before. `next` no longer takes the arena.
* The arena's two reads of its storage - `lookup` and
  `swap_wrapper_to_concrete` - index through `refs.slot_of`. `key()` is
  unchanged: still the sequence number, which passes key their own tables
  by. `equals` compares the tag too.
* `OverloadId` is a 32-bit position and a 32-bit tag (8 bytes). The
  `DeclarationIndex` takes a tag from a process-wide counter at `new` and
  holds it privately; its three mints stamp it, and its six registry reads
  go through `DeclarationIndex::slot_of`, which refuses another index's id.
  `position()` is deleted. The invalid id carries tag 0 and never reaches
  `slot_of`: every read answers its default for it first, as before.
* A refusal is a panic, as §8.380's are:

```
internal compiler error: a type handle made by allocator 2 (number 22) was read against allocator 1
internal compiler error: a signature id made by index 2 (position 0) was read against index 1 (the invalid id carries 0)
```

The harness over this tree (`tag_harness.py`):

```
ok    sizes         exit   0  sizes: TypeRef 8, OverloadId 8
ok    ty_own        exit   0  ty_own: 'i32*'
ok    ty_foreign    exit 101  ... a type handle made by allocator 2 (number 22) was read against allocator 1
ok    ty_stale      exit 101  ... a type handle made by allocator 1 (number 22) was read against allocator 2
ok    ty_allocator  exit 101  ... a type handle made by allocator 2 (number 1) was read against allocator 1
ok    ovl_own       exit   0  ovl_own: 'sym_alpha'
ok    ovl_foreign   exit 101  ... a signature id made by index 2 (position 0) was read against index 1
ok    ovl_stale     exit 101  ... a signature id made by index 1 (position 0) was read against index 2
tag-harness: OK -- 8 modes: every foreign, stale or free-standing handle refused, every own one answered
```

## What it costs

Size was the cost last time (§8.380: a 16-byte `SymbolID` was 3% slower in
every round). Here `TypeRef` SHRINKS 16 -> 8 and `OverloadId` grows 4 -> 8,
as `DefId` did. `cryo check src/main.cryo` in `compiler/`, five rounds,
alternating the parent's clean-built compiler and this one's
(`.objcmp/s61/timing.py`): median **22.02 s** before, **22.00 s** after
(min 21.84 / 21.96). No measurable cost.

## What it does to D48

All four identities a table hands out - `DefId`, `SymbolID`, `TypeRef`,
`OverloadId` - now carry their maker's tag, and every table refuses an id it
did not make where it reads it. A second `TypeRefs`, `SymbolIds`,
`DefTable` or `DeclarationIndex` still COMPILES; none of its ids is
answered by the compiler's own. Construction is still open; the harm D48
names (a colliding id silently answering) is closed for all four.
`ModulePath` is not a table position and is not tagged.

## Not covered

The process-wide LLVM type cache in `codegen/type_map.cryo` is keyed by
`key()` alone and reset per compile; a tag does not reach it.

## Measured

* Objects: `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` - tests
  3,515, moved 0; examples 1,126, moved 0. Census, examples, editor
  (`lsp-gate: OK -- compiled 267 module(s) ... 0 errors`), other-OS,
  incremental: OK.
* Warnings, clean build: 346 -> **344**, compared as sets: the only change
  is two `W0005` (implicit `u64`/`i64` conversion) in `arena.cryo`, in the
  two reads rewritten above, which now index with `i64` throughout. Not
  predicted; explained.
* Lane counts: unchanged (LOOKUP_LOCAL 71, ARENA_READ 63, LOOKUP_OTHER 93,
  GRAPH_WRITE 2). Predicted.
* §0's braced-import file count 639 -> 638: `type_ref.cryo` no longer
  imports the arena.

## Blast radius

Compiler 3 files (+107/-57): `type_ref.cryo`, `arena.cryo`,
`decl_index.cryo`. Harness `scripts/ns-migration/8.384/` (project,
`mint_before.cryo` for the parent's `next(arena)`, runner). Gate cycles: 1
clean build + facts + verify, 1 uncapped check, 3 harness pairs, 1 timing
run of 5 rounds.
