### 8.386 Message text has its own type, `Text`: 72 functions whose only spelling-typed parameters were a message leave the name-taking population by construction (1,093 -> 1,022); the one-allocator ruling is closed by the tags; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## Why

Condition two's lint needs the compiler to know which parameter types ARE
spellings. A marker can go on `SymbolStr`; it cannot go on the primitive
`string`, and 632 of the 1,093 name-taking functions take only `string`
(§8.385's handoff measurement). So text and names have to be told apart by
type first: whatever takes text leaves the population with no written
reason, and whatever still takes `string` is a name, markable once converted.

## The population, re-measured

`done.py --name-taking` -> 1,093 functions; 653 take a `string`, through 801
`string` parameters (the recipe is in `scripts/ns-migration/8.386/`).
Joined against the compiler's own facts (`.facts/compiler.facts`, each `arg`
record's callee declaration), those parameters receive **4,701 call-site
arguments** inside `compiler/src` (literal 4,290, local 1,849, call 1,267,
param 888, field 656); 47 parameters have no call in this host's build. A
first join read 3,825 - the facts spell some paths with a different case
(`Diagnostic.cryo` for `diagnostic.cryo`), and a case-sensitive join missed
them; the 4,701 is case-insensitive.

A first pass by parameter name and file (hand-read where it said nothing):

| kind | parameters | call sites |
|---|---|---|
| diagnostic / log message | 112 | 1,791 |
| file path | 165 | 452 |
| backend label (an LLVM value name) | 101 | 653 |
| command line | 60 | 268 |
| source text being lexed or rendered | 50 | 346 |
| not classed by name (read by hand) | 313 | 1,191 |

## One type, not four - a choice made by the session, recorded here

The goal is only that a name is distinguishable from text. Separate types for
paths, messages, backend labels and command lines would add a check the
property does not need - an argument-order check between two kinds of text -
and it would pay for it at every place one kind flows into another (a path
rendered into a message, a command-line argument that is a path). Measured:
27 of the classified signatures take two different kinds of text, the only
places a second type could catch a swap. So one type: `Text`, "bytes the
compiler writes or hands on and never looks anything up by".

The standard library's `str::Str` is already outside the population and was
the other candidate. It was rejected: it is a length-carrying view, so each
wrap is a `strlen`, and the way back to a NUL-terminated `string` - which
most of these parameters are handed on as, to C or to a `string` field - is
not guaranteed without a copy. `Text` holds the `string` itself: one pointer,
`Copy`, passed in one register on both hosts' ABIs, lossless both ways.

```cryo
// before: a message and a name's spelling are the same type
consume(TokenKind::Semicolon, "expected `;`");
ctx.emit_error_at(code, fmt::format("unknown type `%s`", name_str), span);

// after: the message is marked, the spelling is not interchangeable with it
consume(TokenKind::Semicolon, Text::new("expected `;`"));
ctx.emit_error_at(code, Text::new(fmt::format("unknown type `%s`", name_str)), span);
```

## What changed

`compiler/src/utils/text.cryo`: `Text { private raw: string }`, `Text::new`,
`as_string`, and `Display` (so `f"{t}"` writes the text). The first slice is
message text: 89 parameters in 80 functions - the diagnostic builders
(`Diagnostic::error/warning/note`, `with_note`, `help`, `also_at`,
`SpanLabel`, `Suggestion`), the context's and the parser's error reporters,
`DiagSink::emit_raw`, the logger and `cdebug`, the failure-report site labels
(`Res::require`, `DeclarationIndex::type_of_decl` / `impl_owner` /
`register_methods`), and the project config's key reports
(`slice1.tsv`). The edge functions that turn text INTO a name (`intern`,
`QualifiedName::push`, the mangler's `encode_ident`) are not in it.

## Measured (predicted before the check)

* Refusals, uncapped (`max_errors: 0` compiler, `.objcmp/s64/cryo-nocap.exe`):
  **1,728** - 1,685 arguments `string` where `Text` is wanted, 13 `Text`
  where `string` is wanted, 30 others. Predicted 1,731 call sites from the
  facts; the difference, 46, is every call inside a retyped function that
  forwards its own parameter to another retyped function (the logger's six
  `trace` ... `fatal` -> `write_log(msg)`, `emit_error_at` ->
  `Diagnostic::error(message)`, ...): already `Text`, nothing to refuse.
  Per file, refused-and-not-in-the-facts is 0.
* The other OS (`--target=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`): 2 more, both `cdebug` under
  `![target(unix)]`.
* **Uses the check does not see: 22.** A `Text` handed to a C-variadic
  argument list (`fmt::format("%s", message)`, `printf`) or to an array's
  `push` compiles, because a variadic takes anything and an array method's
  argument is checked only at code generation; only `String::push<T>` was
  caught, as E0645 inside `stdlib/collections/string.cryo` with no call site.
  All 22 found by listing every use of each retyped parameter
  (`uses.py`) and reading it.
* Name-taking: 1,093 -> **1,022** - 72 leave (predicted 72), and
  `Text::new(s: string)` enters: it is the one door where bytes become text,
  and will carry its reason on the approved list.
* Lane gate, NOT predicted - explained, a decrease, re-pinned:
  LOOKUP_OTHER 93 -> **44**, REGISTER 31 -> **18**. The gate's rule 2 calls a
  store method name-keyed when its signature mentions `string`;
  `type_of_decl(d: DefId, site: string)` and `impl_owner(node, site: string)`
  qualified only through their failure-report label. Per file, the drop is
  exactly those methods' callers (`type_of_decl` 35 + `impl_owner` 14 = 49;
  `register_methods` 11 + `register_methods_through` 2 outside its own file =
  13). None of those calls was ever a lookup by name: the gate was
  over-counting, and the type now says so.
* Rule 1b: `Suggestion` and `ErrorType` were excluded by hand as holding
  "TEXTS"; they take `Text` now, the gate refused both entries as stale, and
  they are removed (array exclusions 48 -> **46**).
* Residue: 300 -> **251**; J 176, N 26 unchanged, L (literal key) 98 -> 49 -
  the 49 `type_of_decl` / `impl_owner` rows, every one a literal label like
  `"codegen/declare impl"`. The classifier's two hand-written reasons for
  them ("the string is the diagnostic label of the asking site") are
  deleted; normalised for line numbers, nothing else in the table moved.
* Warnings (clean build): 344, the same set.
* Objects: `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` - 0 of
  3,515 test and 1,126 example objects moved; see the commit message.

## Proof by inversion (`scripts/ns-migration/8.386/invert.sh`)

Each mutation alone in `DeclarationIndex::impl_owner`, the control the
restored tree:

* A name where text is expected - `record_unregistered_def(n)` with
  `n: SymbolStr`:
  `error[E0214]: mismatched types ... expected `utils::text::Text`, found

* Text where a name is expected - `this.lookup_type(site)` with `site: Text`:

A raw `string` where `Text` is wanted is refused the same way - the 1,685

## The one-allocator ruling (D48)

Closed: the generation tags are the answer, and the work stops there (Jake,

### 8.387 File paths, command lines, hashes and file contents take `Text`: 119 more functions leave the name-taking population by construction (1,022 -> 903); three more hand-written "TEXTS" exclusions retire; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What changed

The second slice of §8.386's type: every scalar `string` parameter of the
functions that hand text to the file system, an external tool or the backend
- file and directory paths, command lines, URLs and commit hashes, target
triples, file contents, the lockfile and manifest paths, the LSP entry
points' virtual path and buffer - 186 parameters in 135 functions
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.386/slice2.tsv`), across the CLI's executor, the
dependency resolver, git and cache, the build manifest, codegen's link and
tool passes, the project config's directories, the vendor registry, the C

Left out on purpose, because they turn text into something they then look

retyping the store that feeds it.

Most of these bodies work on the bytes (lengths, indexing, `+`, `contains`),
so 182 of the 186 parameters are unwrapped once where the body opens and the
body is untouched:

```cryo
// before
static job_tmp_path(tmp: string, k: u64) -> string {
    return fmt::format("%s.%llu", tmp, k);
}
// after: the caller hands text; the body still formats bytes
static job_tmp_path(tmp_text: Text, k: u64) -> string {
    const tmp: string = tmp_text.as_string();
    return fmt::format("%s.%llu", tmp, k);
}
```

```cryo

build_load(&this, ty: LType, ptr: LValue, name: string) -> LValue {
    ...
    return LValue { raw: llvm::LLVMBuildLoad2(this.raw, ty.raw, ptr.raw, name) };
}
// after: the C function still gets the bytes
build_load(&this, ty: LType, ptr: LValue, name: Text) -> LValue {
    ...
    return LValue { raw: llvm::LLVMBuildLoad2(this.raw, ty.raw, ptr.raw, name.as_string()) };
}
```

way (`error_eof`'s context, `emit_use_after_move`'s headline). 68 parameters
in 64 functions (`scripts/ns-migration/8.386/slice4.tsv`).

Left out on purpose: anything that maps a spelling to a keyword, a type, a
suffix type or an enum variant (`Token::from_keyword`,

```cryo

if (ParserBase::is_float_lexeme(num_tok.lexeme)) { ... }
// after: the token's lexeme is handed on as text to be scanned
static is_float_lexeme(s_text: Text) -> boolean {
    const s: string = s_text.as_string();
    ...
}
if (ParserBase::is_float_lexeme(Text::new(num_tok.lexeme))) { ... }
```

## The LLVM type cache and the tags

`codegen/type_map.cryo`'s `TypeMapperCache` maps a handle's bare number
(`ty.key()`, and a struct type's own `t.id`) to its LLVM type; the tag does not
reach it. Read, not changed: it is reset by `reset_shared_type_cache` at every
compile entry point that reaches code generation (`compile_raw`,
`compile_for_lsp_content_into`, `compile_project_with_config`) and once per
module in the project loop, together with a fresh LLVM context
(`instance.cryo`). One compile has one arena and one allocator, so within a
cache's lifetime a number cannot name two types. One caveat for the record:
`map_type` consults the cache BEFORE reading the arena, so it is the one read
where a handle from a second arena with a colliding number would be answered
without the tag check. No second arena reaches code generation today.
Keying the cache by the whole handle would close it; codegen was not
redesigned here.

## The bare-call stamp - skipped, not small

`visit(IdentifierNode)` in `name_resolution.cryo` asks the namespace-less
`Resolver::lookup`, and `bare_name_res` stamps whatever binding the scope
holds first, so `Color(5)` records the type's definition when the module
declared the type before the function (§8.367). Fixing it means asking the
value namespace for an identifier in expression position. Whether a bare
identifier may still name a TYPE there - `Color(5)` with only the type
declared - is a language rule the spec does not state, and "ask the values,
then the types" is a fallback chain. Left open.

### 8.391 A literal or range pattern whose kind is not the match subject's own type is refused at the pattern; a string pattern on a struct compiled to an arm that never matched; seventeen rulings recorded - 2026-09-27

## The defect

`cryo check` accepted this, the build produced a program, and the program
returned 0 - the arm written for `"yes"` could never be tested against a
struct, and nothing said so:

```cryo
type struct Word { text: string; }

function classify(w: Word) -> i32 {
    return match (w) {
        "yes" => { 1 }      // never matches, no diagnostic
        _     => { 0 }
    };
}
```

Now:

```
error[E0200]: string pattern requires a `string` subject, found `MatchStringPatternOnStruct::Main::Word`
 --> src/main.cryo:13:9
```

Cause. Sema checked a RANGE pattern's kind against the subject
(`check_range_patterns`) and never checked a single literal pattern at all.
Codegen compares a literal pattern with the subject's own value - a string by
content when the subject's type is `string`, anything else as an integer
compare - and a string literal against anything else lowers to no value; the
arm emitter then took its "pattern produced no comparison (a codegen gap);
treat it as an unconditional miss" branch. The range check had a second hole
of the same shape: it peeled the subject through references and pointers
(`TypeUtils::unwrap_to_enum`) before comparing kinds, and codegen peels
nothing, so `match (c: &char) { '0'..'9' => .. }` passed the check and died
at LLVM module verification (E0900).

Measured on the compiler at the parent commit, each shape in its own scratch
program:

| subject | pattern | parent compiler |
|---|---|---|
| a struct | `"yes"` | builds, returns 0: never matches |
| `&string` | `"yes"` | builds, returns 0: never matches |
| `u32*` / `&u32` / `string` | `0` / `7` / `5` | passes the check; the three built together (with the `&string` case) fail LLVM module verification, E0900 - not isolated one by one |
| `&char` | `'0'..'9'` | passes the check, E0900 LLVM verification failure |

## Refuse, not match

A literal pattern "matches exactly that value" (`docs/cryo.md` §7.1); a
string literal is never exactly a struct's value, and there is no field it
could mean. Rust refuses the same program (mismatched types in a pattern).
The reference case could be made to match by loading through the reference,
but the program can say that itself (`match (*s)`), and the corpus holds no
program wanting it; refusing is the safe default where the current behaviour
is silently nothing.

## What changed

* `PatternResolver::check_range_patterns` becomes `check_literal_patterns`,
  called from the same two places (the statement and expression forms of
  `match`), and checks every literal AND range pattern through the new
  `check_pattern_fits_subject` against the subject's OWN type, peeling
  nothing: a string pattern needs a `string` subject, a char pattern or range
  a `char` one, an integer pattern or range an integer or `char` one,
  `true` / `false` a `boolean` one. E0200, the code the range check already
  used; the two range messages keep their old text as a prefix and gain
  "found `T`".
* Codegen's silent miss becomes an internal error: E0900 "codegen: a match
  pattern produced no comparison against its subject", at the pattern, still
  branching to the miss so the block stays terminated. Measured to fire 0
  times over the corpus below before the change.

## Blast radius: 0 programs

A probe compiler (the parent tree plus one line printed per literal pattern
in sema - literal kind and subject type - and one per codegen silent miss;
not committed) built every corpus in the tree: the standard library, the
compiler, the editor, the 14 examples, and the whole test run (2,209 unit,
227 compile-fail, 85 projects). Every literal pattern's kind agreed with its
subject: string on `string` 700 distinct sites, char on `char` 142, integer
on `u32` 83 / `u16` 52 / `u8` 6 / `i32` 6, boolean on `boolean` 12 (library
and tools); the test suites added integer on `u32` / `u16` / `i64` / `i32` /
`u8` / `u64`, string, char and boolean, all on their own types. The silent
miss fired 0 times. The control that the probe can report the defect: the
struct program above printed `lit src/main.cryo:9 String M1::Main::Word` and
`miss src/main.cryo:9`. With the fix, the same corpora all build and the
test run passes (2,209 unit, 227 compile-fail, 88 projects with the three new
ones, in verify's census) - no program that was in the tree is refused.

## Proof

Three compile-fail projects, one per shape, each declared in
`tests/started-passing` (the parent compiler built or mis-reported each):
`match_string_pattern_on_struct`, `match_string_pattern_on_reference`,
`match_char_range_on_reference`. Each asserts E0200, the pattern's
`file:line:col` and the message, and excludes E0900 and a successful build.
`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` runs the census
with the parent's compiler over this tree's tests and asserts it fails on
exactly the declared projects:

* parent: `census FAIL ... suite exited 1`, and per project `baseline exit
  0, tree exit 1` (the struct and the `&string` program BUILT on the parent)
  and `baseline exit 1, tree exit 1` for the `&char` range (E0900 on the
  parent, not the E0200 the project asks for)
* this tree: `census ok ... suite exited 0`; `verify: OK in 264 s`

The first cut put the two reference shapes in single-file negatives, and
verify refused it - "the baseline failed 0 unit and 2 compile-fail test(s);
only declared projects may fail there": a new negative that fails on the
parent cannot be declared. They are projects now; the programs and the
assertions are the same.

Each mutation built alone, reverted before the next, against the unmutated
tree as control (all three cases pass there). Run while the reference cases
were still single-file negatives with the same programs and messages:

* A - a string pattern fits any subject: the `&string` case FAILS, the
  `&char` range case passes, and the struct project's build stops at the
  codegen line instead of producing a program: `error[E0900]: codegen: a
  match pattern produced no comparison against its subject -->
  src/main.cryo:13:9` - the second line of defence reports what sema let
  through.
* B - the subject peeled through references and pointers again: both
  reference cases FAIL; the struct project still refuses (E0200 at 13:9).

## Counts

* Objects: 0 of 3,515 test objects and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved

### 8.392 Link symbols take `MangledName`, which now carries the symbol's bytes: 27 functions leave the name-taking population by construction (748 -> 722); 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What a link symbol is here

A symbol as the linker and the backend see it: a Cryo-mangled name
(`C$8compiler.7codegen...`), a C function's own name (`abort`, `strcmp`), a
runtime entry point (`__cryo_panic`), an LLVM intrinsic (`llvm.trap`). The
backend's symbol table is looked up by these bytes; nothing else looks
anything up by them. They reached the backend as `string`, the type a name's
spelling also travels as, so 27 functions that only ever hand a symbol to
LLVM counted as taking a spelling.

Before and after, at the backend's symbol table and one of its callers:

```cryo
get_named_function(&this, name: string) -> LValue { ... }
mut fn: LValue = this.llvm_module.get_named_function("abort");
```

```cryo
get_named_function(&this, name: MangledName) -> LValue {
    return LValue { raw: llvm::LLVMGetNamedFunction(this.raw, name.as_string()) };
}
mut fn: LValue = this.llvm_module.get_named_function(MangledName::new("abort"));
```

## The type

`MangledName` already existed, in the mangler, and was already outside the
population as "an opaque link symbol" - but it held an interned `SymbolStr`,
and every factory's result was resolved back to a `string` on the next line
(8 sites) before it reached the backend, which has no intern table (two of
its entry points, `LType::named_struct` and `struct_by_name`, are static).
Now it holds the bytes, privately, like `Text`: `MangledName::new(s)` marks
bytes as a link symbol, `as_string()` hands them to a C function or a
`string` store, and the factories build the bytes without interning them. The
two stores that key by an interned symbol - the declaration index's
signature and the specializer's pin for a generic method - intern the bytes
where they store (`intern.intern(mangled.as_string())`, 3 sites). The design
choice (bytes rather than an interned handle) is mine: the interned form
would have made every backend call intern `"abort"`.

## The slice

27 parameters, one per function, listed with the reason class in
`scripts/ns-migration/8.391/mk_slice.py` (the tree's own line numbers are
read from `done.py --name-taking`; `slice-mangled.tsv` is the list):

* the backend's symbol table, read and written by symbol: `LModule`'s
  `get_named_function`, `get_named_global`, `add_function`, `add_global`,
  `LType::named_struct`, `struct_by_name`, the type mapper's
  `forward_declare_struct`, the test harness's `add_extern_test_function` (8)
* a symbol's linkage and COMDAT: `apply_spec_linkage`,
  `apply_directive_effects` (2)
* the set of symbols stripped from a module: both `is_stripped` (2)
* LLVM intrinsics and runtime check handlers declared by symbol: the
  intrinsic emitter's `get_or_decl_*` (7), `emit_*_llvm` / `emit_clz_or_ctz`
  / `emit_rotate` / `emit_addr_intrinsic` (5), the check handler's three (3)

Not in it: link symbols already typed `SymbolStr` - the codegen function and
global registries' keys, `declare_extern_function_as(.., symbol)`,
`held_symbol` - which key interned stores; converting them means retyping
the stores (see the handoff).

## How

`retype.py` (committed with the `Text` work) gains `--as MangledName`: the
same modes with that type's import, `::new` and qualified name. Uncapped
check (`.objcmp/s64/cryo-nocap.exe`, `max_errors: 0`) after `--params`: 112
refusals - 99 arguments refused as `string` where a `MangledName` is wanted
(wrapped by `--refusals`), and 13 that are not arguments, fixed by
`fix_mangled_sites.py` (committed): 3 reads of the old interned `.value`, 8
`.resolve(intern)` of a factory's result (now held as the `MangledName`
itself), and 2 comparisons of the symbol with a `string`. Second check: 16,
each an argument already wrapped `MangledName::new(x)` whose `x` had become a
`MangledName`; unwrapped by `--refusals` and collapsed by `--round-trips`
(14; the 2 others are `mangled.as_string()` handed to the diagnostic that
names a struct). Third check: 0 errors.

`uses.py` over the 27: every use is a checked call into another retyped
function, except one `if (name == null)` in `CodegenPasses::is_stripped`.
`cryo check` accepted comparing the struct with `null`; the full build for the
other OS then refused it as a codegen defect - "E0633: codegen: function
'...is_stripped' ... left 1 of 3 basic block(s) unterminated; body
discarded" - so it reads `name.as_string() == null` now. That a struct value
compared with `null` passes the check is a type-check hole, recorded, not
fixed here.

One ordering slip, caught and redone: the hand edits ran before
`--refusals` and merged two lines in `declaration_emitter.cryo`, so the 4
refusals below that point would have been applied one line off; the file was
restored and redone with the refusals first (`filter_log.py`, committed, cuts
a check log to one file).

## Proof by inversion

`CRYO=<this tree's compiler> bash scripts/ns-migration/8.391/invert.sh`,
each mutation alone:

* A - a raw string literal where a link symbol is expected
  (`get_named_function("abort")`): E0214 at `intrinsic_emitter.cryo:1121:62`,
  "expected `...MangledName`, found `string`"
* B - a name where a link symbol is expected
  (`get_named_function(symbol)`, `symbol: SymbolStr`): E0214 at
  `symbol_resolver.cryo:132:66`, "expected `...MangledName`, found
  `...SymbolStr`". A first B, using `SymbolStr::empty()` in a file that does
  not import it, was refused for that reason instead (E0240) and was moved -
  it showed nothing about the type.
* C - the link symbol where the declaration index's interned symbol is
  expected: E0214 at `decl_index.cryo:1075:88`, "expected `...SymbolStr`,
  found `...MangledName`"

### 8.393 Spellings matched against a fixed table take `Keyword`: 7 functions leave the name-taking population by construction (722 -> 716); the literal-pattern check refuses the conversion's one silent miss; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-27

## What these are

Seven functions take a spelling only to match it against a table written into
the compiler - never against a program's declarations: the lexer's keyword
table (`TokenType::from_keyword`), the numeric-literal suffix tables
(`Lexer::is_valid_numeric_suffix`, `sema_numeric_suffix_type`), the primitive
numeric spellings (`is_numeric_type_name`), the syntax highlighter's keyword
list (`lex_eq(.., kw)`), and the fixed values of two project settings
(`TargetType::from_string`, `PanicStrategy::from_string`). They took
`string`, so they counted as taking a spelling.

```cryo
// before
static from_keyword(s: string) -> TokenType {
    return match (s) { "if" => { TokenType::KwIf } ... };
}
const kw_kind: TokenType = TokenType::from_keyword(text);

// after
static from_keyword(s_text: Keyword) -> TokenType {
    const s: string = s_text.as_string();
    return match (s) { "if" => { TokenType::KwIf } ... };
}
const kw_kind: TokenType = TokenType::from_keyword(Keyword::new(text));
```

`compiler/src/utils/keyword.cryo`: `Keyword`, one private `string`,
`Keyword::new`, `as_string` - `Text`'s shape. The name is mine, flagged: the
ruling asked for "a keyword type"; the suffixes, the numeric spellings and
the settings' values are keywords only in the loose sense of a fixed table.

## How

The `Text` recipe, with `retype.py --as Keyword` and the slice in
`scripts/ns-migration/8.391/mk_slice.py keyword` (`slice-keyword.tsv`).
Every body works on the bytes, so all seven are unwrapped once at entry
(`--prologue`, the parameter renamed `<p>_text`); 87 call arguments wrapped
by `--refusals`; `--collapse` found nothing to collapse. Checks: 204
refusals, then 87, then 0.

**The measuring compiler mattered.** The first uncapped check used the
session-64 no-cap build, which predates §8.391, and reported 120 refusals -
none of them in `from_keyword`, whose body is `match (s) { "if" => .. }`:
retyped to a struct, all 84 keyword arms would have compiled to arms that
never match, a lexer recognising no keyword, with no diagnostic. The same
check with this tree's compiler reported 204: those 84 are E0200 "string
pattern requires a `string` subject, found `utils::keyword::Keyword`". 204
is under the shipped cap of 500, so this tree's own build measured it. The
full cross build and the editor build then passed.

## Proof by inversion

`scripts/ns-migration/8.391/invert.sh`, modes D-F, each alone with the
restored tree as control:

* D - a raw string where a keyword spelling is expected
  (`from_keyword(text)`): E0214 at `lexer.cryo:196:60`, "expected
  `utils::keyword::Keyword`, found `string`"
* E - a name where a keyword spelling is expected
  (`from_keyword(SymbolStr::empty())`, in a file that imports it): E0214 at
  `parser.cryo:886:41`, "expected `utils::keyword::Keyword`, found
  `...SymbolStr`"
* F - the keyword table matched on the `Keyword` itself (`match (s_text)`):
  this tree's compiler, E0200 at `lex/_module.cryo:877:13` and every arm
  after it; the session-64 compiler over the same mutation, "No errors
  found." - the pair for §8.391's check on a real body
* control: "No errors found."

## Counts

* Name-taking 722 -> **716**, as predicted (7 out, `Keyword::new` in).
* Warnings (clean build) 344, the same set. Editor 476, builds. Cross full
  build OK.
* Lane, residue, braced-import files: unchanged.
* Objects: 0 of 3,515 test objects and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved
  (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`, OK in 306 s;
  the census passing is also the lexer still recognising every keyword).

## What the two conversions teach about the lint's population

716 functions still take a spelling. What this session's two slices say
about them:

* A marker type removes a function only when EVERY spelling-typed
  parameter it has is the marked kind; both slices here had one parameter
  each, which is why they were clean. The rest of the codegen population is
  mostly `SymbolStr`-keyed stores (the function and global registries, the
  value table, `held_symbol`, `declare_extern_function_as`) - link symbols
  or local names held interned. Retyping them means retyping the stores,
  not the parameters.
* Retyping a parameter to a struct makes every `match` on it with string
  patterns a silent miss unless the checker refuses it; it does now
  (§8.391). Any future marker-type slice must be measured with a compiler
  at or after `6c1e2a6b`.
* `cryo check` still accepts a struct compared with `null` (found in
  §8.392); a full build is the evidence for such a body.
* The config enums' `from_string` were in the ruling's list; `is_numeric_type_name`
  compares a type's DISPLAY name, and moves with the primitive-keyword work
  (D66) - if the primitive spellings stop being keywords, its table is the
  thing to revisit.

## Blast radius

Scripts: `retype.py` +1 (`Keyword` in its table), `mk_slice.py` two slices,
`invert.sh` modes D-F. Gate cycles: 4 checks (one wasted on the pre-fix
compiler, above), 1 cross full build, 1 editor build, 1 clean build, 1
facts, 1 check-fast, 4 inversion checks, 1 verify.

### 8.394 A lint level takes a `reason`, and allowing `lookup_by_spelling` requires one; the lint itself follows a re-pin (D52-D55) - 2026-09-28

## What changed

`![allow(..)]`, `![warn(..)]` and `![deny(..)]` parsed a `key = value`
argument already, and refused it: they took identifiers only. They now take
lint names and at most one `reason = "..."`, a non-empty string literal.
Allowing `lookup_by_spelling` - the lint condition two asks for, ruled
D52-D55 - needs that reason and a function or method to sit on:

```cryo
![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "the parser hands this a bare leaf; no identity exists yet")]
function find_leaf(name: SymbolStr) -> Decl { ... }        // accepted

![allow(lookup_by_spelling)]                               // E0152: needs a reason
![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "   ")]               // E0152 at the reason: empty
![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reasn = "x")]                  // E0152: unknown key (once)
![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = 42)]                  // E0152: not a string literal
![warn(lookup_by_spelling)]                                // E0152: no warning level
![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "x")] type struct S   // E0151: function or method only
```

Every refusal is E0152 (or E0151 for the placement), as D54 rules; the
wording is mine. A type- or module-wide allow is refused because it would
cover declarations written after it, which never had a reason of their own;
`warn` is refused because it lowers the level without one. Both are my
choices, not rulings.

## Why a commit of its own

The lint refuses every declaration in the compiler that takes a spelling
type, 527 of them, and landing it without writing 527 reasons means marking
those declarations with an allow - in `reason = ...` form. The pinned
compiler that builds the compiler is the previous one, which refuses that
form (measured: `make cryo` over the marked tree, 488 errors, each
"directive `![allow]`: argument 2 must be an identifier"). So this syntax
lands first, the pins are refreshed from it, and the lint and the marks land
after, as the turbofish did (`3ab83793`).

## Proof

Two projects, each failing on the parent compiler and passing on this one
(declared in `tests/started-passing`):

* `spelling_lint_empty_reason` - parent: "E0152: directive `![allow]`:
  argument 2 must be an identifier" at 10:1, the right code for the wrong
  cause, which the project's `output_excludes` refuses; now: "E0152:
  directive `![allow]`: `reason` is empty; say why the lint does not apply
  here" at `src/main.cryo:10:29`.
* `spelling_lint_missing_reason` - parent: built, and returned 3; now:
  "E0152: `![allow(lookup_by_spelling)]` needs a reason: write `reason =
  "..."` saying why this takes a spelling rather than an identity" at
  `src/main.cryo:9:1`.

## Counts

* Name-taking 716, unchanged, as predicted: the one new helper,
  `emit_bad_arg`, takes its message as `Text`.
* Warnings (clean build) 344, the same set.
* Test projects 91 -> 93. Roster merged (+2).
* Lane, residue: unchanged.
* Objects: 0 of 3,515 test objects and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved
  (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`, OK in 256 s;
  the two projects: baseline exit 1 and 0, tree exit 1 - the census
  checks the message).

### 8.395 The spelling lint: a declaration taking `SymbolStr` or `QualifiedName` is E0157 unless an allow gives a reason; the 527 declarations it refused carry a pending reason (D52-D54) - 2026-09-28

## What it does

In the directive pass, after each module's directives are validated, every
function and method the module declares is linted: a parameter whose type is
one of the compiler's spelling types - by value, behind a reference, or as
an array's element - is E0157 at the parameter, unless the declaration's own
`![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "...")]` says why (§8.394 for the
reason's rules). A receiver is not linted: it is the method's owner, not a
spelling it was handed.

```cryo
function find_leaf(name: SymbolStr) -> Decl { ... }
// error[E0157]: `find_leaf` takes a spelling: parameter `name` carries a `SymbolStr`
//  help: take the identity the spelling names, or say why it cannot:
//        `![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "...")]` on the declaration

![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "the parser hands this a bare leaf; no identity exists yet")]
function find_leaf(name: SymbolStr) -> Decl { ... }        // accepted
```

The list is hardcoded (D52), in `DirectiveProcessingPasses::spelling_type_of`:
`compiler::resolver::symbol_str::SymbolStr` and
`compiler::resolver::qualified_name::QualifiedName`, by the qualified names
their declarations give them. It is the declaration that is linted, never a
call (D53); the residue's literal-argument rule is untouched. The code is
E0157 (D54); the number and all wording are mine, flagged.

## Landing without writing 527 reasons

The lint refuses **527 declarations**: 488 in the compiler (61 files), 39 in
the editor (4 files), 1,125 parameter reports across the two builds (539 in
`cryo check src/main.cryo`, 586 in the editor's build, which compiles the
compiler library too). Writing their reasons is condition two's migration,
a unit of its own. Landing the lint as "deny by default" without them would
leave the compiler unbuildable by its own stage-2, so each carries

    ![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "pending: this took a spelling before the lint existed, and why is not written yet")]

inserted by `scripts/ns-migration/8.395/pending_allows.py` from the
compiler's own E0157 report - it finds each reported parameter's
declaration head and writes the allow above it at its indentation; it does
not parse signatures. The §0 row counting these lines is the ratchet: a
reason written replaces one, so the count only falls. What this buys over a
module-wide allow: a function written tomorrow, in any file, is refused
until it has a reason of its own.

Control on the generator: every marker stripped, the uncapped compiler
rebuilt from the final sources, both reports taken again, the generator run
- the tree came back byte-identical (all 527, and `directive_processing.cryo`).
Its refusal was exercised too: re-run over a report whose line numbers the
insertions had moved, it found no head for any site and wrote nothing.

## Proof by inversion

On the compiler tree itself (`.objcmp/s66/mut.py`, one function appended
to `resolver/scope.cryo` per run, restored after), each against the
unmutated control "No errors found.":

* no allow: "error[E0157]: `mutation_find_leaf` takes a spelling:
  parameter `name` carries a `SymbolStr`" at `scope.cryo:369:29`
* allow and a reason: no errors
* `reason = ""`: "error[E0152]: directive `![allow]`: `reason` is empty;
  say why the lint does not apply here" at `scope.cryo:369:29`
* no reason: "error[E0152]: `![allow(lookup_by_spelling)]` needs a
  reason: ..." at `scope.cryo:369:1`

Three projects, and the two of §8.394 now also asserting no E0157:

* `spelling_lint_refuses_unallowed` (declared: parent builds it, exit 6): a
  `SymbolStr` by value, by reference, as an array, a `QualifiedName`, and a
  method's non-receiver parameter - five E0157, each at its parameter; a
  receiver-only method and a function taking `i32` are not reported.
* `spelling_lint_allows_with_reason`: the same program with five allows
  and reasons, built and run (exit 6), on both compilers.
* `spelling_lint_directive_shapes` (declared: the parent reports the four
  malformed directives and not the `deny`'s parameter): an allow on a type
  (E0151), a `warn` (E0152), a misspelt key (E0152, once - not also "needs a
  reason"), a number as the reason (E0152), each without a second refusal
  of the declaration under it; and `deny` refuses the parameter (E0157).

The program types are declared at the compiler's qualified names, since the
list names types by them.

## The lint against the listing

`done.py --name-taking` = 716: 461 declarations with a spelling type and
255 with only a `string` (`.objcmp/s66/split_rows.py`). Reconciled by
declaration line (`.objcmp/s66/recon2.py`), the lint's 488 compiler
declarations are the listing's 461 **less one** - `opaque_assoc_item_mismatch`,
whose `SymbolStr*` out-parameters the listing's matcher counts and the lint,
by the definition "by value, by reference or as an array", does not - **plus
28** class constructors (`VarDeclNode(name: SymbolStr, ..)`,
`StructType(.., qualified_name: SymbolStr, ..)` and 26 more) that the
listing's matcher never sees: it requires a lowercase name. The 255
`string`-only declarations are outside the lint: D52's list names the
compiler's types, and `string` is the language's.

## Pinning the list - considered, not built

Nothing refuses a spelling type added to the compiler and left off the
list, which would narrow the lint silently. A pin would need to recognise a
spelling type some other way than the list, and there is none to use:

* the types do not share a module (`SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName` and the
  exempt `MangledName` in `resolver/`, the exempt `Text` and `Keyword` in
  `utils/`, the exempt `ModulePath` in `module_graph.cryo`);
* the shape does not tell: `SymbolStr` is one `u32`, as `DefId` is; a scan
  for structs whose every field is text or a spelling
  (`.objcmp/s66/wrappers.py`, which first missed `QualifiedName` behind a
  doc comment holding a parenthesis, fixed) finds 19 - both exempt kinds,
  `QualifiedName`, and records such as `LockedDep` and `VendorLink` - and
  never `SymbolStr`;
* a marker on the type would recognise it, and D52 ruled a marker out.

So a pin would be a second hand-kept list checked against a candidate set
that cannot contain the main spelling type - a pattern-matcher that proves
less than it appears to. Not built; the question is Jake's.

## Counts

* Name-taking 716, unchanged, as predicted: no new function takes a
  spelling.
* Lane: unchanged. The first build moved ARENA_READ 64 -> 65 (predicted
  +2, one `lookup` and one display read; `lookup` is not counted there):
  the E0157 message named the parameter's type with
  `resolve_display_name_short`. The message now names the listed type the
  lint matched, which it already holds, and the count is back to 64.
* Warnings (clean build) 344, the same set.
* Test projects 93 -> 96; roster merged (+3). Files with brace imports
  643 -> 645 (the two fixtures import their `QualifiedName`).
* Objects: 0 of 3,570 test objects and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved
  (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`, OK in 272 s;
  3,570 is 3,515 plus the 55 of `spelling_lint_allows_with_reason`, which
  builds on both sides). The editor gate compiled the marked compiler and
  editor with 0 errors, and so did the other-OS gate.

## Blast radius

`directive_processing.cryo` +110 / -5 and `diag/_module.cryo` +7 (the
lint); 527 generated lines in 65 files (61 compiler, 4 editor);

### 8.396 A dynamic array's method arguments are checked by the type check, so `cryo check` refuses what only code generation refused (D61) - 2026-09-28

## The hole

`cryo check` passed an argument of the wrong type to a method of a dynamic
array; only a full build refused it, in code generation, with a message
about the wrong thing:

```cryo
mut nums: i64[] = [];
nums.push("not a number");
// before: cryo check -> "No errors found."
//         cryo build -> error[E0636]: codegen: no method 'push' found on type 'i64[]'
//                       (then E0633, a block left unterminated, and E0900)
// after:  cryo check -> error[E0214]: mismatched types, at the argument:
//                       expected `i64`, found `string`
```

A struct's method was checked (E0214), an unknown array method was refused
(E0358), and an array method's return was typed right: only the ARGUMENT
check missed the array.

## Cause, and why it is one arm

`CallResolver::check_method_call_arg_types` peels pointers, references and
instantiations to the type whose methods it checks against, and had no arm
for a dynamic `T[]`, so it found no candidate and reported nothing. The
binder beside it (`bind_method_on_receiver`) and `TypeUtils::method_owner_ref`
both reach a `T[]`'s methods through the `Array<T>` specialization
registered for its element (`decl_index.lookup_array_type`); the check now
does the same.

That map is filled by the specialization pass, after mono. Measured with a
probe line at the new arm over the repro: sema runs twice under
`cryo check`; the pass before mono found no specialization (1 time for
`i64[]`, 8 for `string[]` inside the stdlib) and the pass after it found
`Array<i64>` and reported E0214. So the pass before mono returns early, as
the arm for an unresolved instantiation already did, and the check happens
in the pass after it - still inside `cryo check`, before code generation.

## The message

Code generation does not look methods up: it calls the one the type check
bound, and E0636 fires when there is none. Its member-call text claimed
"neither the concrete type nor any base defines this method" - which it
never checked, and which was false here. It now says what it knows: "the
call to method 'push' on type 'i64[]' was never bound to a method", with a
note that the type check accepted the call without binding it, which is a
compiler defect. The array shape no longer reaches it. The wording is mine.

## Proof

`array_method_argument_mismatch` (declared in `tests/started-passing`):
`push`, `insert`, `set` and a borrowed `contains` argument on an `i64[]`.

* parent compiler: `cryo check` - "No errors found."; `cryo build` - four
  E0636 "codegen: no method '...' found on type 'i64[]'", then E0633 and
  E0900.
* this tree: `cryo check` and `cryo build` - four E0214 at `9:15`,
  `10:20`, `11:17`, `13:23`, "expected `i64`, found `string`" (and
  "expected `&i64`, found `&string`" for `contains`), no E0636.

## Not taken

`cryo check` also accepts a struct compared with `null`, and the build then
dies with an unterminated block. It is a separate rule, not this one:
`TypeChecker::check_binary_op` (`compiler/src/compiler/types/checker.cryo:857`)
accepts `==` / `!=` whenever either side is `void` - the type of the `null`
literal - whatever the other side is. Recorded, left.

## Counts

* Warnings (clean build) 344, the same set. `cryo check` of the compiler
  itself: no errors.
* Lane: unchanged (predicted a possible +1 for `lookup_array_type`; the
  gate does not count it). Name-taking 716.
* Test projects 96 -> 97; roster merged (+1).
* Objects: 0 of 3,570 test objects and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved
  (`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`, OK in 322 s):
  the check, now reaching every array method call after mono, refused
  nothing in the stdlib, the compiler, the editor or the corpus, and
  converted no argument.

## Blast radius

`sema/call_resolver.cryo` +9, `codegen/visit/call_emitter.cryo` +8 / -2.
Gate cycles: 2 builds (1 probe), 2 repro checks, 1 facts, 1 check-fast,
1 verify.

### 8.397 An operator is dispatched by its token kind, not its spelling: 6 functions leave the name-taking population by construction (716 -> 710); the 255 `string`-takers measured by what their bodies do; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-28

## What the 255 are

Condition two's lint reaches `SymbolStr` and `QualifiedName` only; 255 of the
716 name-taking functions took a spelling as a plain `string` and nothing
governs them. The working assumption was that most of them read a name-keyed
store, so that retyping the store would carry its readers with it. Measured,
it is not so.

`scripts/ns-migration/8.397/uses.py` reads each body and classes every use of
each `string` parameter (308 parameters in the 255 functions): handed to an
intern or parse edge, looked up in a store reached through `this.` or an
element, compared with a literal, rendered into a message or log, forwarded
to another call, or anything else. Its control is the loader's own
`is_loaded` / `mark_loaded` / `is_loading`, which it classes as store reads.
By the strongest use of each parameter:

| use | parameters |
|---|---|
| forwarded to another call | 93 |
| other (a field set, string arithmetic, a constructor) | 81 |
| rendered into a message or log | 45 |
| compared with literals (a fixed table) | 42 |
| handed to an intern / parse edge | 24 |
| looked up in a store | **23** |

The 23 store reads are the CLI's parsed-argument map (6), the module loader's
loading and loaded sets and its namespace map (8), the intern table itself
(3), the build manifest's module keys, the lockfile's find, the directive
set, the C include paths and the inline-asm clobbers. Fewer than one
parameter in ten reads a store, so a store-by-store conversion cannot be
the route for most of this population.

`scripts/ns-migration/8.397/group.py` then assigns every function to one
mechanism by hand-written rule, refusing to finish while a row is unclaimed.
After this entry (249 functions):

| mechanism | functions | what the `string` is |
|---|---|---|
| file-path | 49 | a file or directory path used as a key (the loader's sets, `module_of_file`, `find_module_by_path`, the editor locator's file match) or an array of paths (link objects, include dirs, artifacts) |
| display | 32 | a name only rendered: a diagnostic's subject, a scope's debug label, a type's display name, bindgen's emitted source |
| cli | 31 | a command-line flag, command or help topic matched against the compiler's own table, and the parsed-argument map keyed by flag |
| edge | 28 | where bytes become an identity: `InternTable::intern` / `lookup` / `contains`, `QualifiedName::parse` / `single` / `child` / `push`, `mint_temp`, `Text::new`, `Keyword::new`, `MangledName::new`, synthesized calls built by method name |
| module-name | 26 | a module's namespace held as text: the loader's namespace map and `resolve_import_path`, the build manifest's module keys, codegen's module name, the resolver's written-module helpers |
| fixed-table | 26 | a spelling matched against a table the language or a format fixes: primitive spellings, intrinsic names, cfg atoms, directive names, float suffixes, C backing types, mangling operator codes |
| deps-vendor | 21 | a dependency or vendored library's name, a target triple, a JSON key |
| qname-text, mangle-text | 9 + 6 | string arithmetic over `a::b::c` text (`leaf_of`, `parent_of`, ...) and the mangler / demangler's text |
| literal-text | 9 | a lexeme or a literal's text |
| type-display | 6 | the specializer's type-argument DISPLAY strings, compared with each other |
| vestigial-owner | 4 | the call resolver's `owner_str`, threaded through four functions and read only by an emptiness guard |
| operator | 2 | the trait method name an operator lowers to (`OperatorTraitMap::mk`, `mk_ord`) |

## What changed

Every operator token carries its identity - `TokenType::Plus`, `LAngle`,
`EqualEqual`, ... - and code generation already dispatched on it. The type
checker, the operator-to-trait map, the constant folder and the sema helpers
that decide whether an expression is a constant numeric one asked the same
question of the token's SPELLING instead:

```cryo
// before
const op: string = b.op.lexeme;
if (op == "<<") { ... }
static for_binary(op: string) -> OperatorTraitMap {
    if (op == "+") { return OperatorTraitMap::mk(LangItem::Add, "add", false); }
// after
const op: TokenType = b.op.kind;
if (op == TokenType::LessLess) { ... }
static for_binary(op: TokenType) -> OperatorTraitMap {
    if (op == TokenType::Plus) { return OperatorTraitMap::mk(LangItem::Add, "add", false); }
```

* `TypeChecker::check_binary_op` / `check_unary_op`,
  `OperatorTraitMap::for_binary` / `for_unary`, `ConstEval::apply_binary` and
  `SemaVisitor::emit_operator_missing_impl` take a `TokenType`. A message that
  names the operator renders it with `TokenType::to_string`, which gives the
  same spelling, so no message changed.
* `TokenType::compound_base_lexeme() -> string` is
  `TokenType::compound_base() -> TokenType` (`Unknown` for a non-compound
  token). Code generation carried two private copies of that table (the
  overloaded-compound store and the compound emit); both now ask it, so sema
  and codegen cannot disagree about what `a op= b` computes.

`mk` and `mk_ord` still take the trait method name an operator lowers to as a

### 8.398 A directive's name is a `Keyword` where the parser records it: 18 functions leave the name-taking population by construction (710 -> 692); a class constructor's arguments under `new` are not type-checked; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-28

## The store

A directive's name - `inline` in `![inline]`, `repr` in `![repr(C)]`,
`windows` in `![config(windows)]` - is recorded once, by the parser, in
`DirectiveNode.directive_kind`, and copied into the module's directive set
(`DirectiveRecord.kind`). Every reader matches it against a table the
compiler fixes (the built-in directives, the platform and feature atoms) or
renders it into a message; no reader finds a declaration with it, and an
unknown directive is recorded and otherwise inert. Both fields held a
`string`, so every function the name flowed into took a `string`, outside the
spelling lint and counted in condition two's population.

Both fields are now `Keyword`, the type whose definition is exactly that
("a spelling matched against a table the language or its configuration
format fixes ... no declaration in a program is ever found through one"),
and the parameters follow the store:

```cryo
// before
directive_kind: string;
find_directive(&this, name: string) -> DirectiveNode* { ... d.directive_kind.eq(name) ... }
if (func.has_directive("test")) { return true; }
static is_known_builtin(name: string) -> boolean { return match (name) { "inline" | ... } }
// after
directive_kind: Keyword;
find_directive(&this, name: Keyword) -> DirectiveNode* { ... d.directive_kind.as_string().eq(name.as_string()) ... }
if (func.has_directive(Keyword::new("test"))) { return true; }
static is_known_builtin(name: Keyword) -> boolean { return match (name.as_string()) { "inline" | ... } }
```

* The 18 functions: `DeclarationNode::find_directive` / `has_directive`,
  `DirectiveRegistry::has`, `is_known_builtin`, `is_cfg_os_atom`, the four
  `apply_layout_effects_*`, `emit_arity_error`, `emit_arg_kind_error`,
  `emit_placement_error`, `emit_layout_conflict` and
  `validate_test_module_placement` in the directive pass, and the platform
  gate's `HostOS::matches` / `is_os_atom`, `CfgEnv::is_feature_atom` /
  `feature_active`. The directive pass's helpers are handed the store's own
  `dir.directive_kind` (57 calls), not a copy re-wrapped; the free-text labels
  beside it (`"a string literal"`, `"function or method"`, the conflict
  pair `"repr(packed)"` / `"align"`) are message text and take `Text`.
* Where a name enters from source, it is wrapped: the parser's two
  `new DirectiveNode(Keyword::new(tok.lexeme), ..)`, the literal directive
  names callers ask for (`has_directive(Keyword::new("entry"))`, 6), and
  the gate's atoms. A gate atom is an identifier ARGUMENT
  (`DirectiveArg.name`), and that store also carries `derive(Trait)`'s
  trait names - real names - so it is not retyped; the wrap is at the eleven
  places an identifier argument is read as a platform atom.
* Uses `cryo check` does not verify, audited by hand: the directive name
  passed into a C-variadic `fmt::printf` (the AST dumper), three `cdebug`
  traces and one `fmt::format` (the test-placement message) - each now
  `.as_string()`. The last would have compiled and printed a struct's
  bytes as the directive's name.
* The lane gate refused its two hand-written array exclusions whose reason
  was "a spelling the language fixes, TEXTS" (`DeclarationNode`,
  `DirectiveRegistry`) and three inline-scan entries for the same arrays as
  stale; all five are removed (array exclusions 42 -> 40). Lane buckets
  unchanged.

## Found on the way: `new C(args)` does not type-check its arguments

The two `new DirectiveNode(<string>, ..)` calls were NOT refused when the
constructor's parameter became `Keyword` - the check reported "No errors
found." over them. Reduced:

```cryo
type struct Wrap { raw: string; }
type class Holder { public: w: Wrap; Holder(w: Wrap) { this.w = w; } }
function take(w: Wrap) -> i32 { return 0; }
// new Holder("not a Wrap");  -> cryo check: No errors found; cryo build: builds, runs, exit 0
// take("not a Wrap");         -> error[E0214]: mismatched types ... expected `CtorArg::Wrap`, found `string`
```

So retyping a class constructor's parameter gets no refusal at its `new`
sites, and a wrong argument compiles whenever the layouts happen to agree.
This matters to this population: about 38 class constructors take a
spelling (28 as `SymbolStr`, found by the lint; about 10 as `string` -
`ImportDeclNode(module_path: string, ..)`, `ModuleDeclNode(path: string,
..)`, `LiteralNode(value: string, ..)`, `ExprParser` / `Parser` /
`ParserBase(.., source_file: string, ..)`, `ErrorType(.., reason: string,
..)`, `ExternBlockNode(linkage_type: string, ..)`, `AsmPiece(.., text:
string, ..)` - by a grep whose control finds 27 of the lint's 28, the
28th being wrapped over two lines). `done.py --name-taking` lists none of
them. Not fixed: a type-checker change of its own, and not this slice's
mechanism.

### 8.399 The compiler reports its declarations as it reports its calls: the sealed-type check reads them, its source parser deleted, and the move checker's rows read its field records (D62); what still judges code from source - 2026-09-28

## What changed

`cryo build --emit=facts` wrote one record per call that passes a key and
per comparison of keys. It now also writes one record per DECLARATION each
module makes, in the same file and the same fifteen columns, from the same
check (sema's per-module walk, before monomorphization, after the bodies so
an `async function` is recorded as it compiles):

```
type   src/compiler/resolver/res.cryo  92  1  2  -    public   struct  -  -  -  -  compiler::resolver::res::DefId  -      0
field  src/compiler/resolver/res.cryo  95  5  0  u32  private  -       -  -  -  -  compiler::resolver::res::DefId  index  0
fn     src/compiler/resolver/res.cryo 103 12  0  compiler::resolver::res::DefId  public  static  C$...invalid...  -  -  -  compiler::resolver::res::DefId  invalid  0
param  ...  <index>  <type>  <visibility>  <role>  <symbol>  <key>  -  -  <owner>  <fn>:<param>  0
```

A type's record carries its field count, visibility and kind; a field's,
its resolved type, visibility and the key type it carries (`string`,
`SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName`, `ModulePath`, or `-`); a function's, its
parameter count (the receiver not counted), resolved return, visibility,
role (`free`, `method`, `static`, `constructor`, `destructor`) and linker
symbol; a parameter's, its resolved type and key. The owner of a method is
the type whose block declares it, or the type an `implement` block's head
was resolved to; of a free function, its module. The key column is decided
by the function that already decided it for calls: `carries_key` is now a
test on `CallFacts::key_of`, which names the key rather than answering yes.
The records are sorted with the rest and are byte-identical across two
`make facts` runs. Compiler facts 51,982 -> 70,726 records (688 `type`,
2,387 `field`, 6,455 `fn`, 9,034 `param`).

## The sealed-type check

The lane gate's sealed-type check read each SEALED type's block from source
with five regexes and a brace counter: find the type, its private fields,
and any public static taking an argument and returning the type. It now
asks the records, by the type's definition path: a `type` record, at least
one private `field`, and no public `static` `fn` with a parameter whose
resolved return is the type (a store exempt). The source reader
(`SEALED_HEAD_RE`, `private_fields`, `public_mints` and three more
patterns) is deleted in this commit.

Side by side over the tree first (`scripts/ns-migration/8.399/sealed_side_by_side.py`):
all six entries AGREE, with the same declaration line and the same private
field list for each (`DefId`: `index`, `table`; `DefTable`: its ten arrays;
...). Then each breach planted alone in the real tree, the compiler's facts
regenerated, both checks run (`sealed_mutations.py`):

| planted in `res.cryo` | old (source) | new (records) |
|---|---|---|
| `static forge(n: u32) -> DefId` public, in `DefId`'s block | REFUSED | REFUSED |
| the same static in an `implement struct DefId { .. }` block - which compiles | **OK** | **REFUSED** (`forge (src/compiler/resolver/res.cryo:121)`) |
| `DefId`'s `private:` label dropped | REFUSED | REFUSED |
| control, the tree | OK | OK |

The second row is the difference: the source reader looked only inside the
type's own block, so a public door minting identities from integers could
be added in an implement block and the gate read OK.

The self-test's six sealed cases were source mutations; they are record
cases now (`lane-gate-selftest.py`, `SEALED_CASES`), and each rule of the
new check, removed from the gate alone, turns the self-test red on the case
written for it (`sealed_gate_mutations.py`, 9 removals: the private-field
rule, the static rule, a parameterless static or one returning another type
or a method read as a mint, visibility ignored, the store exemption, the
implement-block half, the stale entry; control green).

## The move checker's rows (D62)

The move-state row checked the identity keying with greps: `name\.id`
absent from `move_check.cryo`, and the text `moved_keys:  u64[]` present in
each pass. Two of those become record queries, and two are added:

* `MoveChecker`'s fields carrying a key type: **0** of 22.
* `DropInserter`'s: **1**, `drop_sym` - the method name its synthesized
  `.drop()` calls are written with.
* `moved_keys`' declared type in each pass: **u64[]**.

The pair: with `last_moved: SymbolStr` planted in `MoveChecker` (move state
kept by a binding's spelling, initialized, compiles), both old greps read OK
(`name\.id` 0 lines, `moved_keys:  u64[]` 1) and the record check reads
`last_moved` as a key-carrying field; restored, both read OK
(`move_state_pair.py`).

**What declarations cannot carry.** The move sets are `u64[]` and
`DropInserter.binding_names` is a `u32[]` of interned spelling ids: to the
type system both are integers, so no declaration record can tell a set of
identities from a set of spellings' ids, and the `name\.id` grep (a member
read in a body) stays - it is a question about expressions. What would let
declarations carry it is typing the sets by identity (`SymbolID[]`); that is
a change to the ownership passes, which follow the merge on their own
branch, and is not made here.

## What still judges code from source

Inventory of the scripts `check-fast`, `verify` and section 0 run, by
whether the script itself decides what the code IS:

* **Now on the compiler's records**: the lane gate's call buckets (§8.368),
  its inline scans (§8.370), the residue's sites (§8.366), and the sealed
  types (this entry).
* **Still reading source, and declaration records could carry it**: the
  gate's rule 1 (a type owning a `HashMap` field is a store) and rule 1b (a
  type owning an array of names or keyed records and a method taking a name)
  - both are field types and parameter keys, which the records now hold;
  `done.py --name-taking`, condition two's population (a parameter typed
  `string`, `SymbolStr` or `QualifiedName`) - exactly the `param` records'
  key column, and it would also see the ~38 class constructors the regex
  never lists; the residue's method-kind parse (`read_methods`); two of
  `approved.py`'s assertions (`--signature`, `--owner-is-identity`).
* **Still reading source, and declarations cannot carry it** (they are about
  bodies or spelling): `derived-name-scans.py` (a local derived from
  `resolve`/`leaf_of` compared in a loop), `receiver-spelling-sites.py` (an
  interned `"this"` flowing into a comparison), `approved.py
  --no-composed-leaf` (how a call's argument text was built),
  `qualify-intrinsic-calls.py` (how a call is written), and the ~200
  `grep -c` checks in about 120 section-0 rows, which count text occurrences.
  The first three need argument provenance on more records than the facts
  write today, not declarations.
* **Plumbing, and stays**: `facts.py`, `verify.py`, `verify-pin.py`, the
  census, the status checker, the commit guard, the self-tests, `parse_cache.py`.

So the answer to "can the Python all go" is: not yet, and not all of it by
declarations. Moving rules 1, 1b and the name-taking listing onto the
records is mechanical now that the records exist; the body-level scanners
need more of the call records' provenance; the section-0 greps are a
different kind of thing - checks of a shape, not judgements the migration
depends on - and would each need its own answer.

### 8.400 The lane gate's store rules and condition two's name-taking listing read the compiler's declaration records, their source readers deleted; a bare identifier naming a type measured over the corpus and not built, blocked on Q13 - 2026-09-28

## Why

§8.399 gave `--emit=facts` a record per type, field, function and
parameter and named three readers still judging declarations from source:
the lane gate's rule 1 (a type owning a map is a store), rule 1b (a type
owning an array of names or of keyed records, with a method taking a name,
is a candidate table), and `done.py --name-taking` (condition two's
population). All three are questions about declared types, which the
records answer.

## What changed

* **The compiler**: a class's `type` record carries the path of the class
  it extends in its sixth column (`-` for any other type), so the gate's
  rule 1c can name the class that declares an inherited array without
  reading source. `CallFacts::base_text`; the record header documents it.
* **The lane gate** (`scripts/lane-gate.py`): `Tree` is built from the
  records. Each field's resolved type decides a map owner (`HashMap` /
  `HashSet`), an array of names (`string[]`, `SymbolStr[]`, a `Pair` headed
  by one) or an array of records, and each `param` record's key column
  decides whether a method takes a name. A method of a trait impl is known
  by its linker symbol (`C$tr$...`, docs/cryo-mangling-spec.md) and is not
  the type's own surface; a constructor builds a table rather than asking
  it and is not read; a receiver's kind is its symbol's `$m` / `$s`. The
  tree is read only for which files exist, and a declaration record naming
  a file outside it is refused. Deleted: the brace-counting block scanner,
  `block_methods`, `strip_comment`, and eleven regular expressions
  (`TYPE_HEAD_RE`, `FIELD_RE`, `MAP_FIELD_RE`, `NAME_ARRAY_RE`,
  `RECORD_ARRAY_RE`, `KEY_PARAM_RE`, `METHOD_HEAD_RE`, `IMPL_HEAD_RE`,
  `INHERENT_IMPL_RE`, `CLASS_BASE_RE`, `KEY_RE`).
* **The residue** (`scripts/ns-migration/residue.py`) used the gate's
  scanner for which of a holder's methods are reads; it asks the `Tree`'s
  receiver kinds now.
* **`done.py --name-taking`**: every `fn` record under `compiler/src` with
  a `param` record whose key is `string`, `SymbolStr` or `QualifiedName`,
  refused when the facts are stale. The regular-expression matcher is
  deleted.
* **The self-tests**: the lane gate's fixture is a set of declarations
  rendered as records and as files (`Fixture` in
  `scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py`); its source mutations are declaration
  changes. Three cases are new: an array of `string` asked by a `string`,
  a trait impl's method taking a name (accepted), and records naming a file
  the tree does not hold (refused). The residue's self-test takes the
  fixture's records. `done.py --selftest` drives the reader over records.

## Every difference, old against new

Run side by side over the whole tree before the switch
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.400/stores_side_by_side.py`,
`name_taking_side_by_side.py`, and the residue's sets):

| population | old (source) | new (records) | differences |
|---|---|---|---|
| map owners (rule 1) | 21 | 21 | none |
| array candidates (rule 1b) | 40 | 40 | one, display only: `ParsedArgs`' field printed `pair::Pair<string,Argument>[]` as written, `Pair<string,Argument>[]` resolved |
| types declared, for rule 1c | 454 | 455 | `VendorGenerator` (`bindgen/generator.cryo:735`), which the source reader never saw |
| class bases | 102 | 102 | none |
| residue holders / read methods | 14 / 107 | 14 / 107 | none |
| lane buckets | the golden | the golden | none (`lane-gate: OK`) |
| name-taking | 692 | 721 | 41 new-only, 12 old-only |

`VendorGenerator`: the old scanner stripped string literals with a pattern
that does not know character literals, so `if (c == '"')` at
`generator.cryo:718` opened a "string" that swallowed the `{` after it; the
brace depth read -1 from there to the end of the file, and every type
declared below it was invisible to rules 1, 1b and 1c.

Name-taking, new-only: the 38 class constructors taking a spelling (the
regex required a lowercase name), `LOG_DEBUG` (the same), and
`Executor::run_negative_suite` / `run_projects_suite`, whose return arrow
stands on its own line (the regex read only the rest of the closing line).
Old-only: 12 functions whose only spelling is behind a pointer -
`argv: string*` (3: `cli::parse`, `run`, `main`), `out: string*`
(`run_tool`), `string[]*` (7: `dedup_in_place`, `run_multiprocess_emit`,
`walk_deps`, `resolve_path_dep`, `resolve_git_dep`,
`resolve_stdlib_root`, `collect_from_tu`) and `out_trait: SymbolStr*`
(`opaque_assoc_item_mismatch`). The listing's stated definition is "by
value, by reference or as an array", the compiler's `key_of` follows
references and arrays and not pointers, and so does the spelling lint's
`spelling_type_of` - the regex matched the pointers by accident of `\b`.
Whether a pointer should carry a spelling, for the listing and the lint
alike, is not decided here: `SymbolStr*` is the one lint-relevant case, an
out-parameter.

## Proof the new readers see what the old could not

A table planted past the character literal in `generator.cryo`:

```cryo
type struct PlantedTable {
    planted_names: string[];

    planted_has(&this, n: string) -> boolean { return false; }
    static planted_probe(n: string)
            -> void { }
}
```

With the compiler's facts regenerated: the pre-switch gate read
`lane-gate: OK -- LOOKUP = 5 (3 files), ...`; the new gate refused
``rule 1b - `PlantedTable` (compiler/bindgen/generator.cryo) owns an array
of names or records (planted_names: string[]), takes a name (planted_has,
planted_probe) and is in neither STORES nor EXCLUDED_ARRAYS``. The
pre-switch listing went 692 -> 693 (`planted_has`), the new one 721 -> 723
(both). Restored; facts regenerated.

## Each rule removed

`scripts/ns-migration/8.400/gate_mutations.py` removes each rule of the
gate's declaration reader alone and runs its self-test (control: OK):
a map field no longer a map owner, a `string` array no array of names, a
name-headed `Pair` no array of names, a trait impl's methods read as the
type's, an array of keys counted as a key, a record array counted whatever
its fields carry, the base not read, the declaring file not read, a
foreign-file record dropped - each fails the case written for it (the
declaring-file removal fails the baseline itself: every scanned owner then
reads as declared nowhere). `done_mutations.py` does the same for the
listing's reader: seven removals, each fails its case.

## A bare identifier naming a type: measured, not built

D59 rules that a bare identifier in expression position may not name a
type. Measured first, with a probe in `visit(IdentifierNode)` that asks the
VALUE namespace for each bare identifier - each rib's whole overload set,
an import counted when it binds a value - and prints when nothing answers
there, or when the answer's definition differs from today's stamp. Over
the compiler, the standard library, the editor, the unit suite, every
example, test project and negative file (338 builds), and the 11
project-local test suites:

* **17 sites name a type, and every one constructs a class by value by
  calling the class's name**: 13 in the compiler (`ASTCloner()` 7,
  `Parser(..)` 2, `NameResolver(..)` 2, `ASTDumper(..)`, `SemaVisitor(..)`,
  `IRGeneratorVisitor(cg)`), 3 in `tests/tests/lang/swap_pointer_array.cryo`
  (`Node(1)`), 1 in `E0203_undefined_base_class.cryo`. None in the
  standard library, the examples or the projects. No site names a struct,
  an enum, an alias or a generic parameter.
* **0 sites where the value namespace answers a different definition** than
  today's stamp. The control, a module declaring `type enum Color` before
  `function Color(x: i32)` and a caller importing both and writing
  `Color(5)`, prints the difference; the function-first order does not.
* Every non-class shape is already refused later: `const p = Point;` and
  `g(Point)` E0201 "cannot find value", `const x = T;` E0201,
  `Color(5)` with only the enum E0200 "expected `i32`, found `S2::Color`".
  **`Point(1, 2)` on a struct passes `cryo check` ("No errors found.") and
  fails code generation**: `error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve function
  'Point'`.

So the rule's whole blast radius in this corpus is the class constructor
called by name. Refusing it removes by-value class construction, which has
no other spelling (`new` yields a pointer). That is §9 Q13, still open:
either a class declaration binds its constructor in the value namespace
(Rust's tuple-struct model, which keeps `Node(1)` and is compatible with
D59), or the value namespace accepts a class (which D59 rules out).
Keeping `Node(1)` without the first is "ask the values, then the types",
the fallback §8.390 refused; and the stamp fix needs the value-namespace
lookup, which refuses `Node(1)`. **Neither is built; both wait on Q13.**
Under the first answer the blast radius is 0 programs. The probe is not
committed.

### 8.401 A class's constructor binds in the value namespace, a bare identifier naming only a type is refused where it is written, and an import is stamped with the declaration it binds as a value - `Color(5)` records the function in either order; 0 programs refused; ten rulings recorded - 2026-09-28

## Why

D59 rules that a bare identifier in an expression may not name a type.
§8.400 measured its blast radius: 17 sites named a type as a value, every
one a class built by value by calling its name (`ASTCloner()`, `Node(1)`),
and refusing them would remove by-value class construction. D68 answers
§9 Q13: a class's constructor lives in the value namespace beside the
class, as a Rust tuple struct's does. With that, the rule and the stamp
fix behind it can be built without a fallback from values to types.

## What changed

* `SymbolKind::Constructor`: a class that declares a constructor binds one
  under its name in the same scope, beside the type, carrying the class's
  definition and visibility, and is exported with it
  (`Resolver::declare_constructor`, `Symbol::constructor`). The value
  namespace accepts it; it joins the name's binding set rather than being
  refused as a redeclaration. Its definition is the class's, which is how
  every later stage already reads a call of a class's name, so nothing
  after the name layer changes.
* `Resolver::lookup_value`: the binding a name has in the value namespace
  alone. Each rib is asked for every binding under the name and answers
  with the first a value can be - a declaration the value namespace
  accepts, a refused import, an import that binds a value; a type-only
  binding neither answers nor shadows. The prelude is asked last, in the
  value namespace.
* `visit(IdentifierNode)` asks `lookup_value`. When nothing answers and the
  name binds something else, it is refused at the name
  (`refuse_type_as_value`): E0231 "`Point` is a type, not a function" as a
  callee, E0201 "expected a value, found type `Point`" otherwise, with a
  note on how a type is built. Whether the name binds at all is asked only
  to choose that message.
* The stamp is built from `Resolver::value_target`: an import is stamped
  with the declaration it binds in the value namespace, not with the one
  its module listed first.

## The recorded identity, before and after

A temporary line at the end of `visit(IdentifierNode)` printed the
definition `Color` was stamped with; the previous compiler and this one,
each built with it:

| program | before | after | runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| module declares `type enum Color`, then `function Color(x: i32)`; `main` imports both and calls `Color(5)` | `Ptc::Vault::Color` (type) | `Ptc::Vault::Color` (function) | 105 both |
| the same, all in one module | `Plc::Main::Color` (type) | `Plc::Main::Color` (function) | 105 both |
| the function declared first (control) | (function) | (function) | 105 both |

The program ran correctly before because later stages recovered the
function from the definition's path, which the two share; the stamp was
the type's.

## Each mutation alone, against the unmutated compiler

| compiler | `Node(7)` (a class) | `Color(5)` imported, type first | same, one module | `const p = Point;` | `Point(1, 2)` on a struct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | runs 7 | stamped the type | stamped the type | `E0201: cannot find value `Point` in this scope` | passes `cryo check`; `E0636: codegen: cannot resolve function 'Point'` |
| this change | runs 7 | the function | the function | `E0201: expected a value, found type `Point`` | `E0231: `Point` is a type, not a function` |
| without the constructor binding | `E0231: `Node` is a type, not a function` | the function | the function | E0201, the new message | E0231 |
| with the old namespace-less lookup | runs 7 | the function | **the type** | `cannot find value` (the old, later refusal) | E0636 again |
| without the import's value target | runs 7 | **the type** | the function | E0201, the new message | E0231 |

Each removal undoes its own column and nothing else: the constructor
binding is what keeps `Node(7)` building, the value-only lookup is what
refuses a type and fixes the one-module stamp, and following the import's
value target is what fixes the imported stamp.
