### 8.402 The monomorphizer decides a type argument's shape by its kind and a receiver's instantiation by the type it denotes, never by printed text - four wrong answers fixed, 0 objects moved; the template-by-spelling sites measured, one live wrong answer, not built - 2026-09-28

## Why

D74: the monomorphizer identified generic type arguments by their display
text, including a match on the last `::` segment
(`mono/specializer.cryo`, `annotation_matches_param_or_spec`). It is the
defect this branch was started over - a spelling standing in for a type -
in the place that decides what a specialization contains.

## The population, measured before changing anything

Every place in `compiler/mono/` and `AST/substituter.cryo` that read a
type argument's display text, and what each asked:

| site | question asked of the text | a decision? |
|---|---|---|
| `specializer.cryo` `annotation_matches_param_or_spec` | does a receiver's written argument name the specialization's argument - whole text, or the display's last `::` segment | yes: keeps or drops a method |
| `specializer.cryo` `annotation_is_modified_outer` | is the receiver's base this template - its written name against the template's leaf or qualified name | yes: same filter |
| `substituter.cryo` `substitute_named_annotation` | is the argument unit (`()`), a primitive (a keyword spelling), a pointer (ends in `*`), a dynamic array (ends in `[]`) | yes: the rewritten annotation's shape |
| the same, the projection and path branches; `monomorphizer.cryo`'s three diagnostics | the text written as a label beside the argument's TypeRef, or printed | no |
| `specializer.cryo:155`, `call_specializer`, `trait_specializer` | where the display text was computed and interned for the above - four copies of one rule | feeds the above |

Separately, six sites in `substituter.cryo` recognise the TEMPLATE itself
by its written leaf (`base_name`): a named annotation, a generic
annotation's base, a struct literal, a `new`, a path's scope segment and an
enum pattern. They are measured below and not changed.

## Wrong answers today

Each program beside a control that differs only where the question does:

```cryo
// module A: type struct Point { x: i32; }
// module B: type struct Point { x: i64; y: i64; }
// module G:
import P1::B::{ Point };
type struct Wrapper<T> { val: T; }
implement struct Wrapper<T> {
    get(&this) -> T { return this.val; }
    only_b(this: &Wrapper<Point>) -> i64 { return this.val.y; }  // B's Point only
}
// main: Wrapper<A::Point> built and read through get()
```

| program | before | control (B's type renamed `BPoint`) | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| the above | `E0204: no field or method 'y' on type 'P1::A::Point'` - `only_b` specialized for A's `Point`: the display `P1::A::Point` ends in `Point` | runs, 7 | runs, 7 |
| `only_b` reads `this.val.x as i64` and `main` calls `w.only_b()` on `Wrapper<A::Point>` | **builds and runs, exit 7** | `E0358: no method named 'only_b' found on type 'P1::G::Wrapper<P1::A::Point>'` | E0358, as the control |
| the same through `type W<U> = Wrapper<U>;`, `only_b(this: &W<Point>)` | builds and runs, 7 | - | E0358 |
| `only_i32(this: &Wrapper<i32>)` called on `Wrapper<i32>` | `E0358` - a primitive argument is not a named annotation, so no receiver written with one matched any specialization | - | runs, 7 |
| `only_boxed(this: &Wrapper<Box2<i32>>)` called on `Wrapper<Box2<i32>>` | `E0358`, the same | - | runs, 5 |
| `pick<T>(x: T) -> T` with `T = (i32) -> i32*` | `E0900: unresolved generic instantiation after monomorphization` - the display ends in `*`, so the argument became a pointer to a type named `(i32) -> i32` | `T = (i32) -> i64`: runs, 3 | runs, 3 |
| the same with `T = (i32) -> i32[]` | E0900, the same through `[]` | - | runs, 4 |

No source in the tree writes a typed receiver on a generic owner (`grep`
over `stdlib`, `compiler/src`, `tools`, `examples`, `tests`: 0), and no
program in it instantiates a generic with a function type returning a
pointer or an array - it could not have compiled. So every wrong answer
is reachable only by a user program, and the prediction was that no object
in the corpus moves.

## What changed

* **The argument's shape is its kind.** `substitute_named_annotation` asks
  the arena `kind_of(arg)`: Unit becomes the empty tuple, the seven
  primitive kinds a primitive annotation, a pointer a pointer over its
  pointee's TypeRef, a dynamic array (`dynamic_array_element_of`) an array
  over its element's; anything else stays named and carries the argument's
  TypeRef, as before. The kinds that printed as one of the
  `is_primitive_spelling` names are exactly Void, Bool, Int, Float, Char,
  String and Never (`va_list` is not in that list and is not in this one),
  so every argument that compiled before takes the branch it took before.
* **The label is derived in one place.** The substituter computes the name
  a rewritten annotation carries from the argument's TypeRef
  (`arg_label`: the qualified name, else the display) - byte-for-byte the
  rule the four copies used, which are deleted with the parameter that
  carried their output (`type_arg_displays`) through `specialize`,
  `impl_substituter` and the substituter's constructor.
* **The receiver filter compares types.** A method's receiver written as
  an instantiation (`X<..>`) is resolved by the type resolver, with each
  parameter the impl's head writes bound to the specialization's argument
  at its position; the method is dropped when the result is an
  instantiation of this template (`inst_generic_base` is the entry's base
  type) with other arguments. The template is recognised by the type the
  receiver denotes, so an alias of it is recognised too; the base-name
  comparison and the leaf match are deleted. A receiver written as a bare
  name is not asked: it is the one the parser gives a method that wrote
  none, and it names the owner.

## Each mutation alone, against the unmutated compiler

Three compilers, each built from the change with one mutation and the tree
restored after (`git diff` identical to the change's):

| compiler | leaf-sharing receiver | wrong call | alias | `(i32) -> i32*` | `(i32) -> i32[]` | `Wrapper<Box2<i32>>` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this change | runs 7 | E0358 | E0358 | runs 3 | runs 4 | runs 5 |
| the filter never drops | **E0204** | **runs 7** | **runs 7** | runs 3 | runs 4 | runs 5 |
| a pointer recognised by the label's `*` | runs 7 | E0358 | E0358 | **E0900** | runs 4 | runs 5 |
| an array recognised by the label's `[]` | runs 7 | E0358 | E0358 | runs 3 | **E0900** | runs 5 |

Each undoes its own column and nothing else.

## Found and not fixed

* **A receiver written through a non-generic alias** (`type WI =
  Wrapper<i64>; only_i64(this: &WI)`) is not asked, because only a written
  instantiation is: `only_i64` is callable on a `Wrapper<i32>`, reads an
  `i32` as an `i64`, and the program runs (exit 2) before and after. Asking
  a bare name too would resolve the parser-given receiver, and resolving a
  bare all-default template canonicalises it to its default instantiation
  (`String` to `String<GlobalAlloc>`), which would drop every method of a
  specialization with another allocator. Not a spelling comparison; the
  filter's reach.
* **The template recognised by its spelling** (the six `base_name`
  sites). A generic function and a type sharing a name:
  `type struct Tag { n: i32; }` and `function Tag<T>(x: T) -> Tag` - the
  return annotation `Tag` is rewritten to the function's specialization
  name: `E0200: expected 'P8::Main::Tag', found 'P8::Main::Tag<i32>'`,
  before and after; the control (the function named `make_tag`) runs, 4.
  The fix is to recognise the template by the declaration its stamp names;
  it needs the parser-given receiver stamped first, since that annotation
  is `Pending` and matches today only by spelling. Not built.
* **A function type as a generic struct's field type**: `Holder<(i32) ->
  i32*>` failed with a type-lowering E0900 before; it now fails as its
  control `Holder<(i32) -> i64>` does, `E0622: member access 'get' ...
  carries no field pin` - a separate defect, before and after.
* The old compiler's exit on `generic_receiver_by_type` in the baseline
  run was 3221226356 (a heap-corruption status on Windows), after its
  E0204 - it crashed while refusing. Not investigated.

The LLVM type cache that codegen asks before the arena is not touched:
nothing here reaches codegen or changes how many arenas a compile has.

### 8.403 A construction's arguments are checked against the constructor of their arity, by `new C(args)` and by value `C(args)`; one wrong-typed construction in the compiler's own source fixed; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-28

## Why

D73: `new C(args)` did not type-check its arguments at all (repro in
§8.398). Measured before changing anything, the hole was wider than that:

| program | `cryo check` | build | run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `new Holder("not a Wrap")`, `Holder(w: Wrap)` its constructor | passes | builds | runs, 3 |
| `Holder("not a Wrap")` by value | passes | builds | runs, 3 |
| `new Holder()` and `new Holder(w, 5)` | passes | builds | runs, 3 |
| `take("not a Wrap")`, an ordinary function (control) | E0214 | - | - |

`resolve_new_expr` resolved the arguments and asked nothing of them. The
by-value call reached `check_call_arity`, which looks a callee's family up
under its PARENT and leaf; a class's constructors are registered as the
class's methods, under the class and its leaf (`register_methods`, the key
code generation's `resolve_family(FamilyOwner::Type(..), .., arity)`
uses), so the lookup found nothing and returned. Code generation picks the
constructor by argument count alone and emits no call when none has it.

## What changed

* `family_signatures_of(def)`: the signatures of the family a definition
  names - a function's under its parent and leaf, a type's constructors
  under the type and its leaf. Which of the two is the definition's KIND
  (`DefTable::kind_of`). The first version asked `type_of_def(def)` instead,
  and the census refused `class_constructed_by_name`'s `Tone(4)` with
  "constructor `Tone` takes 0 argument(s)": `type_of_def` looks a type up by
  the definition's PATH, and the function `Shapes::Tone` shares its path with
  the enum `Shapes::Tone`, so it answered the function's definition with the
  enum. The kind answers by identity.
* `check_constructor_args`: the constructor whose parameters, less the
  storage being initialized, number the call's arguments is checked
  argument by argument by the checker every call uses; no such constructor
  is E0216/E0215 naming the one arity the type offers, or "no overload of
  constructor `Two` takes 3 argument(s)" when it offers several; a type that
  declares no constructor takes no arguments. A generic type's constructors
  are registered on its instantiations, so an unregistered one is not
  judged here.
* `check_call_arity` asks `family_signatures_of` - its lookup moved there,
  so the lane gate's count of name-crossing index reads is unchanged - and
  a callee whose definition is a type goes to the constructor check.
  `resolve_new_expr` does the same for `new`.
* `check_args_against_params` and `try_apply_implicit_conversion` work on
  an argument array rather than a call node, so a construction's arguments
  get the same implicit conversions a call's do; `emit_method_arity_error`
  takes the span it points at.

## Found by the new check in the compiler's own source

```cryo
// async_lower.cryo, the async-main wrapper
const exec_id: DefId = this.ctx.generic_registry.wellknown(LangItem::Executor);
mut ex_scope: ScopeResolutionNode* = new ScopeResolutionNode(
    exec_id, this.intern.intern("new"), span);        // scope_name: SymbolStr
```

`E0214 ... expected 'SymbolStr', found 'DefId'`: an 8-byte tagged
definition id was written into a 4-byte spelling slot since `4ff24ea3`, so
the node's written scope name was whatever interned string the low bits
indexed. It compiled and worked because `set_synthesized_ref` carries the
real identity beside it. Now `this.ctx.defs.leaf_of(exec_id)`. No object
moved: nothing reads that name in the programs' code.

## Each mutation alone, against the unmutated compiler

`cryo check` over the three probes (not a build):

| compiler | `new Holder("not a Wrap")` | `Holder("not a Wrap")` | `new Holder()`, `new Holder(w, 5)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | no errors | no errors | no errors |
| this change | E0214 | E0214 | E0216, E0215 |
| `new` not checked | **no errors** | E0214 | **no errors** |
| by-value call not checked | E0214 | **no errors** | E0216, E0215 |

## New wording

The arity messages are the existing ones with the kind word
"constructor" (`constructor 'Holder' takes 1 argument(s) but 0 were
supplied`, `no overload of constructor 'Two' takes 3 argument(s)`). No new
error code. The word is this session's - flagged for review.

## Not covered

`new Box3<i32>("no")` on a generic class is not refused - its
constructors are not registered on the template - and `new Box3<i32>(4)`
itself fails with E0200 at the `new` before and after, a separate defect.
`type_of_def` answering a function's definition with a same-path type is
a lookup by path wherever else it is asked; not audited.

## Tests

### 8.404 A value compared with `null` or another pointer is refused by the type check unless it is a pointer, a function, a string or a reference; the rule that let it through was the pointer rule, not the one the ruling named; 0 objects moved - 2026-09-28

## Why

D77's first hole: a struct compared with `null` passes `cryo check` and dies
in the build. The ruling located it at `types/checker.cryo`'s rule that
accepts a comparison when either side is `void`. Measured, that is not the
rule that fires: `null` is typed `void*` (`LiteralResolver::resolve_null_literal`),
a pointer, and the comparison is accepted by the rule before it - "either
side is a pointer" - whatever the other side is. So the hole was every
non-pointer kind, not structs alone:

| `x == null` with `x` a | `cryo check` before | build before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| struct value | passes | `E0633: codegen: function 'main' ... left 1 of 3 basic block(s) unterminated` | E0229 (`S` does not implement `Eq`) |
| class value | passes | E0633 | E0229 |
| enum value | passes | `E0900: LLVM module verification failed` | E0229 |
| `i32` | passes | builds; compares a number with an address | `E0229: Cannot compare Int and Pointer` |
| `boolean` | passes | builds, the same | `E0229: Cannot compare Boolean and Pointer` |
| `i32` against `&n` | passes | builds, the same | `E0229: Cannot compare Int and Pointer` |
| class pointer, string (controls) | passes | runs | passes, runs |

## What changed

The pointer rule accepts a comparison only when the side that is not the
pointer is a pointer, a function, a string (a `char*`), a reference, or
`void`, and otherwise fails with the message every other unaccepted
comparison already gets ("Cannot compare %s and %s"). It refuses rather than
falling through, because the class rule after it accepts a class value
beside anything. A struct, class or enum value then reaches the operator
traits, whose existing refusal names `Eq` - the message is existing
wording; a struct that does implement `Eq` was already refused at `null`
(E0214 at the `equals` argument), before and after.

## Before and after, `cryo check` itself

The previous compiler over the six programs: "No errors found." each. This
one: the six refusals above. The change is one rule, so the pair is the
whole inversion: the same programs, the rule restored, pass the check.

## Tests

`compare_with_null_refused` (compile_fail, six refusals). Declared in
`tests/started-passing`: the baseline refused it too, but in code
generation (E0633), without the report the project expects. Roster golden
+1.

## Found on the way, not fixed

An `implement trait Eq for struct S` whose method is spelled `eq` instead of
the trait's `equals` passes `cryo check`, and the build fails at `v == w`
with `E0636: codegen: the call to method 'equals' on type 'S' was never
...`. Another place the fast check does not see what the build does.

### 8.405 The monomorphizer recognises the template being specialized by its declaration, not its spelling, in the substituter and in the receiver filter; a generic function named like a type and a receiver written through an alias both get the right answer; 1 object moved, predicted in kind - 2026-09-28

## Why

Two wrong answers found in §8.402 and left open, both in the monomorphizer.

A generic function sharing a type's name was rewritten into itself. The
substituter decided "this written name is the template being specialized"
by comparing the name's spelling with the template's, at six sites (a named
annotation, the base of a generic annotation, a struct literal, `new`, a
path's scope segment, an enum pattern):

```cryo
type struct Tag { n: i32; }
function Tag<T>(x: T) -> Tag { ... }
const t: Tag = Tag(1);
// error[E0200]: mismatched types - expected 'Tag', found 'Tag<i32>'
```

A method whose receiver is written through a non-generic alias of one
instantiation was specialized for every instantiation. The receiver filter
asked only a written instantiation (`Wrapper<i64>`) what it denotes, and
took any bare name to be the owner:

```cryo
type WI = Wrapper<i64>;
implement struct Wrapper<T> { only_i64(this: &WI) -> i64 { return this.val; } }
const w: Wrapper<i32> = ...;
w.only_i64();   // built, and read the four-byte value as eight
```

## One mechanism

Both are the same question - does this written name denote the template
being specialized? - answered without asking which declaration the name
resolves to. The substituter answered it by spelling; the filter answered
"yes" for every bare name. Both now compare the name's stamp with the
template's declaration.

§8.402 recorded a blocker: that the receiver the parser gives a method
(`Parser::receiver_type_annotation`) is `Pending` and could only be matched
by spelling. Measured, that is not so. The name layer stamps it like any
parameter annotation (`stamp_annotation` over every parameter,
`name_resolution.cryo`). A probe compiler printing, at each of the six
sites, whether the spelling matched, whether the stamp named the template
and the stamp's shape (`.objcmp/s70/probe.patch`), building the compiler
itself: 97,122 spelling matches - 36,560 named annotations, 18,076 generic
bases, 1,112 struct literals, 6,020 scope segments, 35,354 enum patterns,
no `new` - every one stamped and every one naming the template; no stamp
naming the template without the spelling; no unanswered stamp. The one
disagreement anywhere was the repro above (`spell=1 ident=0`).

## What changed

* `TemplateEntry` carries `def`, the declaration it is, set by its three
  registrars (generic declarations, generic static methods, async futures).
* `ASTTypeSubstituter` takes that `DefId` instead of the template's name.
  `names_template` answers for a stamp that resolved to the template;
  `scope_names_template` for a scope segment the name layer stopped on as
  the template with only the member left. The two substituters that
  specialize no declaration of their own pass an invalid id, as they passed
  an empty name.
* The receiver filter (`method_has_modified_self_type`): a name whose stamp
  is the template is the owner and is not resolved - a bare template whose
  parameters all default would denote the default instantiation alone - and
  any other name is resolved and compared like a written instantiation.

## Proof by inversion

One mutant compiler (`.objcmp/s70/mutant.py`) restores the old answer at
exactly one site, chosen by an environment variable; each mutation ran
alone, against the same compiler unmutated as the control. Probe programs
in `.objcmp/s70/sites/`, one per shape:

| mutation | probe | control (no mutation) | mutated |
|---|---|---|---|
| named annotation by spelling | return type `-> Tag` | exit 4 | E0200 at the call |
| struct literal by spelling | `Tag { n: 6 }` in the body | exit 6 | E0638 "struct literal field 'n' has no slot" |
| bare receiver name is the owner | `this: &WI` | E0358 "no method named `only_i64` found on type `P6::Main::Wrapper<i32>`" | builds, exit 2 |
| generic base, `new`, scope, enum pattern (each alone) | all probes | right | right |

The named-annotation mutation alone also breaks the `new` (E0200), variant
path (E0200), parameter (E0403 "reaches the end of its body without
returning") and pointer probes: their wrong answer on the previous compiler
came through the annotations around them. Four of the six sites have no
probe in which their spelling answer ALONE changes a result: the generic
base collapses through the named site, so it goes wrong only with it; the
`new`, scope and enum-pattern rewrites are overwritten by later pins in
every probe tried. They are converted because the question is one question.

## Tests

* `generic_function_named_like_type` (run, exit 39): a generic function
  named like a struct (return type, struct literal, `new`), an
  enum (variant path, local, patterns; a parameter typed as the enum), and a
  generic static method named like a generic struct (`static Bag<T>(x: T)
  -> Bag<T>`). The previous compiler refused it: `E0200` at
  `src/ret.cryo:12:20`. Declared in `tests/started-compiling`.
* `generic_receiver_alias_refused` (compile_fail, E0358 at
  `src/main.cryo:17:14`). The previous compiler built it and ran the method
  on a `Wrapper<i32>`. Declared in `tests/started-passing`.
* `generic_receiver_alias` (run, exit 19): the alias's method on its own
  instantiation reads both halves of `2^32 + 7`, and the owner's `get`
  stays on `Wrapper<i32>`. Passes before and after; it guards against the
  filter dropping too much, which no mutation here demonstrated.

Roster golden +3 (`--merge`).

## Measured

* Predicted: 0 objects move in the existing corpus, because the probe found
  no site where the two answers differ and the tree writes no receiver
  through a bare name other than the owner's. Held: 0 of 3,844 existing
  test and 0 of 1,126 example objects moved.
* Not predicted: the new `generic_receiver_alias` project's own object
  moves. It is the fix in kind: the previous compiler emitted
  `Wrapper<i32>::wide(&Wrapper<i64>)`, the alias's method specialized for
  an instantiation it was not written for; this one does not (`llvm-nm`
  over both builds, one symbol fewer, no other difference). So
  `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` reports FAIL on
  that one object; every gate in it passed (census, examples, lsp, cross,
  incremental, check-fast).
* Warnings 344 from a clean build, the same set as the previous commit's.
* Name-taking and pending allows unchanged: the substituter's constructor

## Found on the way, not fixed

* **The template registry is keyed by path.** A generic type and a generic
  function in one module sharing a name share a key, and one of them is
  lost: `type struct Box<T>` beside `function Box<T>(x: T) -> i32` makes
  `Box<i32>` "E0204: no field or method `v` on type `S2D::Main::Box`" with
  no substitution involved. `GenericRegistry::template_of(def)` answers by
  the definition's path, so a non-generic struct beside a generic function
  of its name is taken to be the function's template: `implement struct
  Tag` is "E0302: `Tag` is a template with 1 parameter, and this impl head
  names 0 of them". The same shape as `type_of_def`.
* **A module's own function hides an imported type of the same name**:
  `import M::{ Bag }` beside `function Bag<T>` is "E0203: cannot find type
  `Bag` in this scope" at the signature, and a path `Tag::make` to an
  imported `Tag` beside a function `Tag` is E0233. Not checked against the

### 8.406 The facts record an argument whose value is a spelling whatever it is passed to, and every `match` over one; the places they still cannot see are a committed list checked by a verify gate - 2026-09-28

## Why

Every gate reading `.facts/` counts only what `sema/call_facts.cryo`
records, and a shape it does not record reads as zero. Two shapes it could
not see:

1. An argument was recorded only when the PARAMETER's type carried a key
   (`string`, `SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName`, `ModulePath`). A spelling passed
   as a `Text` or a `Keyword`, the number behind one, or any spelling passed
   to a generic or variadic parameter, was invisible:

   ```cryo
   seen.get(&name.id)        // a lookup keyed by a spelling; no record
   takes_text(t)             // t: Text; no record
   names.push(sym)           // sym: SymbolStr into a generic push; no record
   ```

2. Only `==` and `!=` were recorded. A `match` over a spelling's text - the
   shape special-casing by name is written in - was not:

   ```cryo
   match (intern.resolve(name)) { "Option" => { ... } _ => { ... } }
   ```

## What changed

* `sarg`: one record per argument whose VALUE is a spelling and which no
  `arg` record describes - a key, a `Text` or a `Keyword`, or a number read
  out of one (`name.id`), read through `&`, `*` and casts. Its `type`
  column says what the value is (`Text`, `SymbolStr.id`). It is written on
  every path out of a call's record, `noparams` and `unaligned` included,
  so a call whose parameter types sema never had - 1,240 of the compiler's
  1,384 such calls are an array's `.push` - still shows its spelled
  arguments.
* `match`: one record per `match` statement or expression whose subject's
  value is a spelling by the same test, with the number of arms carrying a
  literal pattern, the subject's provenance, and the literal patterns.
* Both keep fifteen fields; no existing record changes. The standard
  library's facts, whose source this does not touch, are byte-identical in
  every old kind (the new kinds filtered out, `cmp` of the two files).
  Every reader filters by kind, so none needed a change.

## The list of what is still blind

`scripts/facts-blind-spots.py` holds the list; each entry is a probe line in
`tests/fixtures/facts-blind-spots/src/main.cryo`, which declares `Text`,
`Keyword` and `SymbolStr` at the paths the writer knows them by. The script
builds the fixture with `--emit=facts` and requires each SEEN line to carry
the record kind it names and each BLIND line to carry none. It runs as
`make facts-blind-spots` and as a `make verify` gate, `blind`. 14 SEEN
(the controls), 5 BLIND:

| blind | example |
|---|---|
| a spelling's number in a plain integer local | `const k: u32 = name.id; seen.get(&k)` - a value is a spelling by its TYPE |
| a spelling's number in a struct literal's field | `Holder { key: name.id }` - not an argument |
| a generic call's callee | pin `none`, callee `?`: placed by its spelling alone |
| a function pointer call's callee | the same |
| a closure call's callee | the same |

Its arguments are seen for all three kinds of unpinned call: the audit's
"generic, function-pointer and closure calls are not recorded" holds for
the callee's identity, not for the call or its arguments.

## Proof: the old writer over the list, and the list mutated

* The previous commit's compiler over the fixture: `FAIL -- 6 entries no
  longer hold`: `number-to-generic-insert`, `number-to-generic-get`,
  `number-to-number`, `text-to-text`, `keyword-to-keyword`, `match-string`.
  This one: `OK -- 19 entries hold: 14 seen, 5 blind`. The eight other SEEN
  lines hold for both - they are what shows the instrument reports.
* `number-via-local` relisted SEEN: `FAIL -- ... is listed SEEN and the
  facts no longer see it`. A marker deleted from the fixture: `FAIL --
  number-into-field is in the list and marked nowhere in the fixture`. Both

## What the new records reveal

Predicted before measuring (compiler facts): about 3,000 `Text`, 150
`Keyword`, 100 spelling numbers, 8,000 keys into generic or variadic
parameters; about 80 `match` statements, 30 of them over a name.

Measured (`awk -F'\t' '$1=="sarg"' .facts/compiler.facts`, column 6):
3,170 `Text`, 167 `Keyword`, 98 `SymbolStr.id`, 2,323 `string`, 116
`SymbolStr`, 17 `ModulePath` - 5,891 in all. The key count was over-predicted
by a factor of three: most strings already go to `string` parameters and
were `arg` records. The 98 numbers: 31 `.get`, 4 `.contains_key`, 2

are lookups keyed by a spelling's interned number - 39 no record counted

38 `match` over a spelling (predicted 80). Most are fixed tables: the CLI's

`directive_processing.cryo:1430` compares `InternTable.resolve` of a type

`"compiler::resolver::qualified_name::QualifiedName"`;
`types/resolver.cryo:1296` a resolved spelling with the primitive type
names; `res.cryo:488` a name with `"FILE"` / `"LINE"`;
`intrinsic_kind.cryo:118` a name with 68 intrinsic names;

## Provenance across a function boundary

Not chained this session. The records carry what chaining needs: an
`arg`/`sarg` names its callee's linker symbol and the argument's position;

### 8.409 A check traces every spelling through the facts, across calls, to the lookups it reaches: 339 of the compiler's 349 lookups are reached outside a door, and text an identity handed back reaches a lookup or a door by 52 paths; the list is committed and checked in both directions - 2026-09-28

## Why

Rules three and four of `docs/resolution-rules.md` - a spelling reaches a
lookup only through a door; identity text never becomes a lookup key - had
no instrument, and nobody knew whether what remains is dozens of
conversions or hundreds.

## Can the facts chain a call to its callee's parameter?

Yes, for every call sema pinned. Over `.facts/compiler.facts`: of 10,467
spelling arguments passed to a compiler function, 10,466 join a `param`
record by (callee symbol, position); the 72 others are `cdebug`/`LOG_DEBUG`
variadic arguments (no parameter at that position) and 1 an extern. Of
1,346 records whose provenance is `param:<name>`, 1,346 join the enclosing
function's parameter by (symbol, name). Nobody had written the chaining.
What the records cannot chain is the known list: generic, function-pointer
and closure calls (callee `?`), a key held in an integer local or a field,
and composed keys. Probe: `scripts/ns-migration/8.409/chain_probe.py`.

## What changed

`scripts/spelling-flow.py`. A lookup is a spelling used as a map key (read:
`.get`, `.get_ref`, `.get_mut`, `.contains_key`, `.contains`; write:
`.insert`, `.remove`), a spelling compared inside a loop with an array
element (a hand-written search), or a `match` over a spelling. Each key is
traced back: through locals, through `name.id` and through calls that return
the same text (`InternTable.resolve`, `intern`, `Text::new`, ...), and at a
`param:` to every recorded caller. A lookup is allowed when every path ends
inside a door; otherwise each path is a violation at its origin - where the
spelling started. Rule four: any path from `DefTable.path_of`/`leaf_of`,
`ModulePath.as_sym`, a type's display name, a link symbol's text, a
binding's recorded name or a template's path into a lookup or a door's
argument, doors or not.

```cryo
// refused (rule 3): a stored spelling asked of a map outside every door
if (this.types.contains_key(&node.member.id)) { ... }   // origin: field MemberAccessNode.member

// refused (rule 4): identity text handed back into a lookup
const entries = this.lookup_family_entries(FamilyOwner::Def(parent), this.defs.leaf_of(d));
```

`scripts/spelling-flow.outstanding.tsv`: every violation as (rule, lookup
kind, key class, lookup function, origin kind, origin function, origin text)
with a count - no line numbers. `make spelling-flow` (in `check-fast`)
refuses a violation not listed and a listed one the tree no longer has.
`make spelling-flow-selftest` (verify gate `flow`) builds
`tests/fixtures/spelling-flow` with `--emit=facts` and checks 13 marked
lines, then removes each of the nine tracing rules in turn and requires the
case written for it to fail.

`scripts/facts-blind-spots.py`: new BLIND entry `number-composed-key` - a key
composed arithmetically from spellings' numbers, `(owner_path.id << 32) |
leaf.id`, the shape of `DeclarationIndex::family_slot`: no record is
written, so the family door's own key - built from a definition's PATH -
is invisible to rule four.

## Measured - the outstanding list

349 lookups in `compiler/src`; 10 inside or only reached from doors; **339
outside** (map reads 53 of 56, writes 36 of 39, searches 212 of 216,
matches 38 of 38), in 237 functions. By key type: 203 take a name type
(`SymbolStr`, its number, `ModulePath`) - 35 map reads, 141 searches, 27
writes; 136 take a `string`, many not names (the command line, vendor
registry, dependency resolution, diagnostics). 602 distinct origins: a
field read 233 (mostly a written name read back off an AST node -
`MemberAccessNode.member` alone 75 - which is rule one's question, a later
pass using the text), a call's return 163, a literal 128, an array element
44, a composed expression 15, a local 11, a lost chain 6, a global 2.

Rule four: **52 paths from 42 sites** - `DefTable.path_of` 17,
`ModulePath.as_sym` 8, `Symbol.name` 8, a type's display name 10,
`MangledName.as_string` 5, `DefTable.leaf_of` 4. Two are defects already
known and serve as controls: `DeclarationIndex::type_of_def` asks
`lookup_type` by a definition's path (the answer-by-path defect), and
`lookup_sole_entry` hands `leaf_of` to the family door.

## Measured - the 56 composed keys handed to `intern`

Every part read from the source and the facts (listed by
`scripts/ns-migration/8.409/composed_stmt.py`; each site's class in
`composed-keys.tsv` beside it):
22 compose only literals and counters (or a file path) - minted names; 10
compose written text (parser lexemes, C names, a method's declared name); 9
compose a local's name in the async lowering; **15 compose identity text**:
a module's path (`qualify_symbol_sym`, `_home`, `qualify_binding_sym`,

path (`register_function_signature`, both `qualify_spec_name`,
`spec_qualified_name`, `spec_base_name` twice, `member_template_key`,

(`qualified_name_of`, `refuse_module_type_collisions`). Three feed a lookup
at once: `refuse_module_type_collisions` hands `unit path + "::" + name` to
`module_named`; `member_template_key(path_of(d), member)` is the key
`template_in` reads; `global_cache_key_of` is the key codegen's global
registry reads and writes.

## Proof by inversion

A plant in `DeclarationIndex::lookup_sole_entry`:
`if (this.overload_index.contains_key(&(this.defs.leaf_of(d).id as u64))) { }`,

and `new 1 4 map ... identity ... DefTable.leaf_of`. Reverse: the list

The fixture's own cases are the planted spellings: a literal into a map
outside every door, a search and a `match` outside, identity text into a door

## Not done

No flow is converted; the list is the work. The check does not decide which

### 8.410 Whether a method call consumes its receiver is asked of the method the call was pinned to, never of the receiver type by the member's name; a borrowing overload beside a consuming one of the same name no longer leaks its receiver - 2026-09-29

## Why

The largest single origin on the flow list is a member access's written
name, `MemberAccessNode.member`: 92 rule-three paths from 55 sites (the
brief's 75 was not reproduced; `python scripts/spelling-flow.py
--violations | grep -c MemberAccessNode` gives 92). Grouped by the pass
that reads the name back:

| pass | paths | what it asks |
|---|---|---|
| sema: `call_resolver`, `method_binding`, `member_resolver` | 65 | the method, field or variant the member names on the receiver type - the FIRST resolution, since the receiver's type exists only here |
| monomorphization: `call_specializer` | 12 | the specialized counterpart of a method sema resolved in the template body |
| drop insertion, code generation (`OwnershipQuery`) | 14 | whether the method a call already resolved consumes its receiver |
| async lowering | 1 | a trait's method by leaf |

By kind: 66 method, 11 field, 1 variant (of the 78 left after this
entry), 0 associated type.

The split decides the rule. Sema's paths are rule three: the member cannot
be stamped by the name layer, which has no receiver type, so sema's
lookup is where it is resolved, and it must be one member door taking the
owner's identity and the leaf. The later passes are rule one: the call
already carries its answer, and reading the name again is a second
resolution. This entry takes the last group, the whole of one mechanism.

## What was measured before the change

`OwnershipQuery::type_method_consumes(recv_ty, ma.member)` was the fallback
behind `resolved_method` in `DropInserter.read_call` and
`CallEmitter.call_consumes_receiver`; it scanned the receiver type's
template, impl blocks and inline methods for ANY method of that leaf that
consumes. It ran whenever the pinned method said "does not consume", not
only when there was no pin. A probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.410/consume-probe.patch`)
printed both answers at every call, building the compiler, the tests
project, every test project and every example once each with plain
`cryo build` (`scripts/ns-migration/8.410/probe_run.sh`; 75 built, 49 did not: 47 expected compile
failures, and `native_syscalls_gate` and `vendor_raylib`, which need more
than a plain build):

| where | pinned | pin says | fallback says | calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| code generation | yes | no | no | 4,397 |
| code generation | yes | yes | yes | 632 |
| drop insertion | yes | no | no | 108,259 |
| drop insertion | yes | yes | yes | 1,603 |
| drop insertion | no | - | no | 36,131 |
| drop insertion | no | - | yes | 201 |

The fallback never changed an answer where a pin existed. All 201 calls it
alone answered sit in a generic owner's template body - receivers
`Option<T*>`, `Option<OA>`, `Poll<S::ReadIntoFut::Output>` - which drop
insertion walks (it skips generic functions, not methods of generic
owners) and nothing emits. The unpinned calls with a concrete receiver are
synthesized `drop` and `into_raw` calls, all "no" both ways.

## The wrong answer

The corpus above has no two overloads of one name where one consumes and
the other borrows. Written, it is a leak:

```cryo
implement<T> struct Token<T> {
    take(this) -> i32 { return 0; }                   // consumes
    take(&this, bump: i32) -> i32 { return bump; }    // borrows
}
function borrow_then_leave() -> i32 {
    const borrowed: Token<i32> = Token::<i32>::new(7);
    return borrowed.take(1);      // pinned: the borrowing overload
}
```

The pin said "borrows"; the fallback found `take(this)` and said
"consumes"; `borrowed` was marked moved and never dropped. The project
`overload_receiver_consumes_by_pin` counts drops: the tip's compiler
builds it and it exits 2 (the borrowed token's drop missing); this
entry's compiler, exit 0 and `overload-receiver ok`.

## What changed

Both sites ask `OwnershipQuery::method_consumes_receiver(resolved_method)`
and nothing else; a call with no pinned method has no receiver to consume.
`type_method_consumes`, `ast_method_consumes` and
`impl_blocks_method_consumes` are deleted. `MoveCheck` already asked only
the pin, so the three ownership passes now agree by construction.

The deleted helpers were the only inline scans of
`StructDeclNode.methods`, `UnionDeclNode.methods` and
`ClassDeclNode.methods`: lane-gate rule 1c refused their `SCANNED_ARRAYS`
entries as stale and `residue_classify.py` its `CLASS_OF_METHOD` rows
(`classified but no longer a read method in the tree`); both removed.
Regenerating `scripts/ns-migration/residue.md` dropped exactly the four
`ownership.cryo` rows; its other changed lines are line numbers in files
this entry does not touch, which `residue.py --check` does not compare
(it counts sites) and had gone stale over earlier commits.

## Predicted, then measured

- flow list: 4 rows and 14 rule-three paths leave, nothing new; lookups
  outside a door 339 -> 335. Measured: `spelling-flow: 335 lookups outside
  the doors of 345`, rule three 750 -> 736, `--check` named exactly the
  four rows stale.
- pending lint allows 527 -> 524; residue 251 -> 247 (J 176 -> 172);
  projects 108 -> 109. Measured as predicted.
- Not predicted, explained: `done.py --name-taking` 721 -> 718, the three
  deleted helpers; brace-import files 650 -> 651, the new project; the lane
  gate's LOOKUP_LOCAL 71 -> 70 (`ownership.cryo` 3 -> 2, golden
  `tests/lane-baseline.txt` re-pinned): the row counts a call on a non-store
  type that shares a store method's name, and the deleted
  `type_method_consumes` held one of the file's three
  `OwnershipQuery::qualified_name_of` calls, same-named as the resolver's;
  a debugging copy of the gate printing the row's sites showed the two left
  at lines 752 and 797.
- Warnings: 344 before and after, the same set compared as (code, file,
  message) - the tip's `cryo check` against this entry's clean build.

## Not done

The 78 member-access paths in sema and the monomorphizer. The
monomorphizer's 12 need the template body's pin carried across
substitution (`drop_stale_callee_pin` drops it today); sema's 65 are a
cascade of method finders (`method_by_name`, `get_method`,
`find_generic_method_in`, ...) that one member door would replace.
Drop insertion still walks template bodies of generic owners.

### 8.411 The type a definition was registered as is kept under the definition and read by it; a function sharing a type's path is no longer handed the type - 2026-09-29

## Why

`DeclarationIndex::type_of_def(d)` was `lookup_type(defs.path_of(d))`:
the identity's text re-derived into the type registry's key, rule four's
shape, and wrong wherever a function and a type share a path (allowed
since §8.401) - asked about the function, it answered the type.
`register_type` wrote the registry by `path_of(def)` for the same reason.

The brief's other items do not share this mechanism: each keys a
different store (the family index for `lookup_sole_entry`, the template
registry for `member_template_key`, codegen's global registry for
`global_cache_key_of`, the module graph for
`refuse_module_type_collisions`). `lookup_sole_entry` needs each
registered function entry to carry its definition, which none does
today; it has three callers, all language items. Not taken.

## Measured before the change

A probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.411/typedef-probe.patch`) recorded the
type under the definition at `register_type` and, at every `type_of_def`,
compared the by-path answer with the by-definition one, over the same
corpus as §8.410 (`scripts/ns-migration/8.410/probe_run.sh`, 76 built):
**one** disagreement, a `Function` definition answered a type by its path
and nothing by itself, in `import_type_beside_function_meets_module`.
Every other `type_of_def` in the corpus answered the same both ways.

## What changed

`register_type` also records the type in `def_types`, indexed by the
definition's slot in the definition table (`DefTable::slot`, which refuses
an id another table made); `type_of_def` reads it and nothing else. The
path-keyed map stays for `lookup_type`'s callers. 1 file, +18 / -4. A
struct layout change: clean build.

## What it changes

Only the second error of that compile-fail project, after its E0205 (which
the project asserts, unchanged):

```cryo
import ImportTypeBesideFunction::Color;             // a module
import ImportTypeBesideFunction::Vault::{ Color };  // a function AND an enum
function main() -> int {
    const v: i32 = Color::Green;
    return v as int;
}
```

Before: `E0200 mismatched types ... expected i32, found
ImportTypeBesideFunction::Vault::Color` - the qualifier's binding was the
function, and the function's path handed back the enum whose binding E0205
had just refused. After: `E0201 cannot find value Color::Green` - the
function names no type. What the qualifier should bind after a refused
collision is not settled by the spec (D5 rules only that the pair is an
error); this entry does not decide it.

## Predicted, then measured

- Flow list 788 -> 787, rule four 52 -> 51, lookups outside a door 335
  unchanged. Measured: 788 -> **786**: the one path is listed under rule
  three AND rule four (a `path_of` call's result reaching a lookup is both
  a spelling outside a door and identity text), rule three 736 -> 735. The
  miss is the double listing, which §8.409's plant also showed.
- Lane gate DEFID_PATH 50 -> 49 (`decl_index.cryo` 6 -> 5), predicted;
  golden re-pinned.
- Pending allows, name-taking, residue: unchanged, as predicted.

### 8.412 A field is found by one door, for every shape of receiver; a function-typed field a class inherits can be called - 2026-09-29

## Why

Rule three wants one member door per member kind, taking an owner and the
written leaf. Sema - where a member is resolved for the first time,
because the receiver's type exists only there - found a field through
four finders, tried one after another:

- `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_resolve_owner_field`: the abstract generic
  owner (`this.value` in a `Box<T>` method), off the template's
  declaration;
- `TypeChecker::check_field_access` (the door the table named): the arena
  type, a class's base chain derived-first, one pointer or reference and a
  resolved instantiation peeled;
- `MemberResolver::resolve_field_via_template`: an instantiation with no
  resolved type, off the template's declaration;
- `MemberResolver::try_field_function_call`: a call through a
  function-typed field, the receiver's OWN field list only.

Fourteen flow paths ran through the three that are not the door: eleven
from `MemberAccessNode.member`, three from a struct literal's
`FieldInit.field_name`.

## Measured before the change

A probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.412/field-chain-probe.patch`, on
`63c5b177`) asked all four at every field site - `.field` access, the
deref-coercion retry, the function-field call, the struct literal - and
logged who answered and what each of the others would have answered, over
the compiler and every test project and example
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.412/probe_run.sh`; tabulated by
`field_chain_tab.py` and `field_chain_shapes.py`): **524,705** lookups.

- **No two finders ever disagreed.** Wherever two answered, index and type
  agreed. The classifier's DIFF branch was proven live on two planted rows.
- **Each finder answers one receiver shape.** The owner scan and the
  template scan both answer an unresolved instantiation (`Iu`, and the
  same under one `&`), and always alike; the owner scan alone answers a
  struct literal of the bare generic template (`String { .. }` inside
  `String<A>::new`, 266 rows); the arena walk answers everything that
  peels to a struct, class or array. The arena walk and a template scan
  never both answered: no `CT` row in the table.
- **The order mattered once, and not for an answer:** 27,647 accesses on
  an unresolved non-owner receiver are declined ("defer") before any
  finder runs, though the template scan would have answered them. That
  decline is kept.

So the chain was a dispatch by shape written as a fallback, and one door
with one source per shape reproduces it.

## What changed

`MemberResolver::field_of(recv, leaf) -> FieldAnswer` is the door
`member-field` (the door table moves to it). One pointer or reference is
peeled; an unresolved instantiation, and a struct or class that is itself
a generic template (`GenericRegistry::is_template`), is read off the
template's declaration by `template_field`; everything else by the arena
walk, which `check_field_access` still does and only the door calls. The
field's type is seen through the receiver in every case. `FieldAnswer`
carries the type, the pin's depth and index, and the arena entry and its
declaring type for the visibility check (null for a template's field,
which had none before either).

The four sites ask the door once: `resolve_member_access`,
`member_type_on`, `try_field_function_call`, and the struct literal, which
asks exactly where it asked before (a struct or class, or the generic
owner - an unresolved `Pair<T, U> { .. }` literal still gets no field type
pre-monomorphization; answering it is a behaviour change left for its own
unit). `symbolic_resolve_owner_field` and `resolve_field_via_template` are
deleted.

## What it changes

One thing, and it is a correction:

```cryo
type class A { public: pad: i32; cb: (i32) -> i32; A() { this.pad = 1; this.cb = twice; } }
type class B : A { public: extra: i64; B() : A() { this.extra = 3; } }

const b: B* = new B();
const f: (i32) -> i32 = b.cb;   // compiled before: `.field` walks the base chain
return b.cb(21);                // before: E0358 "no method named `cb` found on type `main::B`"
```

A call through a function-typed field searched the receiver's own fields,
not its bases, while a read of the same field did. Through the door both
find A's `cb` one step up B's chain; the program returns 42. New project
`class_inherited_function_field_call`, declared in
`tests/started-compiling`.

## Proved

- **The door answers what the chain answered.** A second probe
  (`scripts/ns-migration/8.412/door-vs-chain-probe.patch`, the door with
  the old chain recomputed beside it in one process) over the same corpus:
  **483,348** door answers (348,981 in the projects and examples, 134,367
  building the compiler), **0** differing in index, depth or type. Control:
  the new project's `b.cb(21)` is reported DIFF (chain: none; door: depth
  1, index 1).
- **Inversion, the flow gate.** A second field finder planted outside the
  door - `check_field_access` asked again after the door misses in
  `resolve_member_access` - with the door row naming `field_of`:
  `spelling-flow: FAIL`, two `new` entries (`MemberAccessNode.member` to
  `StructType.field_index` and `ClassType.field_index`), rule three 723,
  predicted. The same mutant judged with the door row naming
  `check_field_access`, as before this change: **0** paths from the plant -
  a second caller of the old door passed as a door. Control, unmutated:
  `spelling-flow: OK -- 772 outstanding`.
- **Inversion, the new test.** `try_field_function_call` planted to refuse
  a field found up the base chain: the project is refused, E0358 at
  `b.cb`. Unmutated: builds, exits 42.

## Predicted, then measured

- Flow list 786 -> 772, rule three 735 -> 721, rule four 51: as predicted.
  Lookups 345 -> 340 predicted and measured with the helper form; outside a
  door 335 -> "330 or 331" predicted, **327** measured: the flow check
  counts a lookup reached only through a door as inside it, and
  `StructType/ClassType::field_index` lost their only other caller (the
  function-field finder). After the template scan was inlined (the lane
  gate's inline-scan table names the three declaration field lists, which
  a shared helper hid behind a parameter): 327 of **342**, predicted.
- Name-taking 718 -> 717 (-3 +2), pending allows 524 -> 521, residue
  247 -> 242 (J 172 -> 167, -8 +3), projects 109 -> 110.
- Lane gate: unchanged.

## The member door: the rest of the design

Kinds, by the flow list's paths from `MemberAccessNode.member` now: method
66 (sema 53, monomorphizer 12, async lowering 1), field 0 in sema, variant
1, associated type 0. Per kind, one door taking the owner and the leaf:

- **Field**: `field_of`, this entry.
- **Variant**: `EnumType::variant_index` is the door; `EnumType::get_variant`
  beside it is the duplicate to convert.
- **Associated type**: no door and no path yet; `ImplBlockNode`'s
  `assoc_binding_names[]` and `TraitDeclNode::assoc_types[]` are read by
  name today (residue J) and would be its body.
- **Method** - the large one. Sema resolves a method call several times
  over by name: `resolve_method_overload` selects and PINS the method
  (`resolved_method` and the callee pin), then `check_method_call_arg_types`,
  `lookup_method_param_types` and `resolve_method_call` each find it again
  by name to type the arguments and the return, through
  `lookup_method_with_inheritance`, `lookup_method_through_trait_impls`,
  the generic-owner and abstract-receiver finders and a nine-step generic
  method search (`find_generic_method_for_call`). The door is the
  selection: one function taking the receiver's type and the leaf and
  returning the method (its declaration and owner), and the typing reads
  the pin instead of finding again. The finders that only type a return
  go when the pin is read; the ones that select for receivers the
  selection does not handle today (the abstract generic owner, a bounded
  parameter or projection, a primitive's inherent block, a trait default)
  become shapes inside the door, one source per shape, as the field's
  did. The same measurement first: which finder answers which shape, and
  whether the by-name re-finds ever answer a method other than the pinned
  one - the drop-insertion leak of §8.410 was exactly that.

### 8.413 The entry a function definition was registered as is kept under the definition; the test runner's language items are no longer asked of their family by leaf - 2026-09-29

## Why

`DeclarationIndex::lookup_sole_entry(d)` asked the family index for
`(parent_of(d), leaf_of(d))` and answered its entry when the family had
exactly one: the definition's leaf - text an identity handed back - made
into a door's key, rule four's shape. A family holds every overload
declared under the leaf, so the answer was right only while the family
happened to have one member. Its three callers are the test runner's
generated `main`, naming `std::env::set_args`, `std::env::set_env` and
`std::test::runner::run_all` by their language items.

## Cost, measured before building it

§8.411 left this open on "each registered function entry would need to
carry its definition, and none does". The reverse is what the question
needs - the definition carries its entry - and every place a function
signature is registered has the definition in hand: `register_function_signature`
has four callers (free functions, `extern` declarations and intrinsics in
`type_resolution.cryo`, the closure specializer in `lambda_synth.cryo`).
One store and one parameter; a slice.

## What changed

`register_function_signature` takes `def`, the definition the signature
declares, and keeps the entry under the definition's slot
(`DefTable::slot`, which refuses a foreign id), as `def_types` keeps a
type (§8.411). A monomorphized clone passes none - it shares its template's
definition and would overwrite the template's entry - and so does a
synthesized closure specialization. `entry_of_def(d)` reads it;
`lookup_sole_entry` is deleted and the three readers call `entry_of_def`.
A struct layout change: clean build. 4 files, +42 / -20.

The entry is kept by a helper wrapping the two `register_signature` calls
rather than by one call fed from a `mut` local, because the local hid real
paths from the flow check: in that first shape the mangled symbol reached
`register_signature` through `mut link` assigned in a branch, and three
entries - the mangled name reaching the family scan, under rule three and
rule four - left the list while the flow still existed (rule three 719,
rule four 49). The facts record a local's INITIALIZER as its provenance,
not a later assignment. Not on the blind-spot list; not added here.

## Proved

- A probe at the three readers (`cryo test hashmap` over the unit suite)
  compared the family's sole entry with `entry_of_def`: all three name the
  same symbol (`C$3std.3env.8set_args$Fi_PPh$Rv` and the other two).
- Inversion: the store's write replaced by an invalid entry - `error:
  test-main synthesis failed`, `E0900 ... stdlib test runtime symbols not
  found in DI`, exit 1. Unmutated: the unit suite builds and passes.
- Warnings from a clean build: 344, the same SET as the previous tip's
  clean build (compared by (code, file, message); the comparator's control
  reports a removed warning as GONE).

## Predicted, then measured

- Flow list 772 -> 771, rule four 51 -> 50, rule three 721, lookups 327 of
  342: as predicted, after the helper shape (the first shape's 719/49 is
  the blind spot above).
- `_of_def(&this` readers in the index 2 -> 3.
- Name-taking, pending allows, residue, lane gate: unchanged, as
  predicted.

### 8.414 The flow check follows a local past its initializer: every assignment of a spelling to a local is recorded, and 26 origins it could not see join the list - 2026-09-29

## Why

The facts render a local's provenance from its INITIALIZER and nothing
else (`CallFacts::local_provenance`), and no record described an
assignment. So a spelling that reached a lookup through a `mut` local
assigned after its declaration was traced to whatever the local started
as. §8.413 met it by accident - three real paths left the list when a
value was routed through `mut link` - and the same shape routes a path
off the list on purpose. The check every conversion is measured by had
a hole that removes entries without removing flows.

```cryo
mut moved: string = "Option";
if (total > 0) { moved = name.text_of(); }   // no record described this
by_text.get(&moved);                         // key traced to "Option" only
```

## What changed

- The facts writer records `assign` - one per `=`, `+=`, ... whose
  target is a local or parameter by name and whose value is a spelling
  by the same test as a `sarg` - with the assigned value's provenance,
  the target as `local:<name>` or `param:<name>`, and the local's
  declaration line. Written beside `record_compare` from the one place
  sema resolves a binary expression, before monomorphization only.
  Readers that filter by kind (lane gate, residue) ignore it.
- `spelling-flow.py`: where a trace passes a local or parameter, it also
  follows every `assign` to it in the same function - a new rule,
  `reassign`, switchable like the others; a local declared with no
  initializer takes its assignments as its only values. The join is by
  function and name. Five functions declare two locals of one name; the
  join could cross them, and over-report only - dropping those joins
  changes nothing (797 either way).
- `facts-blind-spots.py`: `identity-text-reassigned`, question
  `assigned`, with a probe line. Listed BLIND first and run against the
  unmodified compiler (it held: 25 entries, 16 seen, 9 blind), then moved
  to SEEN by this change.
- The flow fixture gets `origin-reassigned`: a door-reached function whose
  key is reassigned a literal.

## Proved

- The list entry, the pair: the unmodified compiler (copied out of
  `compiler/build` before building) - `facts-blind-spots: OK -- 25 entries
  hold: 16 seen, 9 blind` with the entry BLIND; the new compiler over the

### 8.415 Method selection binds a generic method's own type parameters, so a call on a concrete receiver to a generic method is pinned - 2026-09-29

## Why

The method door's design: the overload selection
(`bind_method_on_receiver`) is the one place a method call's leaf becomes
a method, and the call's typing reads its pin. That needs the selection
to answer every call on a receiver it covers. Measured before building,
with a probe recording why the selection declined each call it left
unpinned, over the compiler's own build (60,891 method typings): on a
concrete receiver (struct, class, enum, primitive, array) it declined
about 690 typings, and every one but 19 was a call to a GENERIC method.
Across all pinned typings only 68 were generic methods, each pinned by
monomorphization, never by the selection: `args_bind_to_params` compares
each argument with its parameter, and a method's own type parameter
(`value: T` in `fold<T>`) equals no argument at any tier. Those calls
were typed by the name-keyed finder alone.

```cryo
implement struct Fnv128Hasher {
    fold<T>(mut &this, value: T) -> void { ... }
}
h.fold(Manifest::compiler_fingerprint());   // unpinned: `u128` binds no `T`
```

## What changed

- `method_args_bind` binds a generic candidate: each argument first
  unifies with its parameter through `InferCtx`, the one structural
  unifier, over the method's own parameters
  (`SymbolicChecker::symbolic_param_ref`, as the scope-call inference
  builds them), so `T` binds once and consistently across the call; an
  argument that does not unify binds by the tier's rule. A method with
  no type parameters binds exactly as before.
- Generic candidates are a SECOND selection: `bind_method_on_receiver`
  runs the whole selection (trait-stamped first, then any) over the
  non-generic candidates, and only when nothing binds, again over the
  generic ones (`select_method`, `pick_own_method`, `bind_on_impl_block`
  take `generic`). A call some non-generic overload takes is never taken
  by a generic one. The language spec does not rank a generic method
  against a same-named non-generic one; this order was chosen because it
  leaves every existing pin as it was, not as a ruling.
- The typing is untouched: `resolve_method_call` still asks the finder.
  1 file, +66 / -19.

## Proved

- Probe over the compiler's build, before and after (outside
  `call_resolver.cryo`, whose own lines this change moves): every site's
  typing count identical; non-generic pins 51,680 both; generic pins
  68 -> 737; unpinned 6,232 -> 5,563. No existing pin changed.
- `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` from a clean
  build: 4012 test and 1126 example objects, 0 moved; every gate OK.
  Monomorphization does not short-circuit a generic `resolved_method` -
  it specializes the call and re-pins the specialization - which is why
  the object code does not move.
- Compiler warnings, clean build: 344, the same set as HEAD's.
- The first build added an arena write to `call_resolver.cryo` (lane gate:
  ARENA_WRITE 44 -> 45, refused); routed through `symbolic_param_ref`,
  44.
- A consuming generic method (`take<T>(this, tag: T)`) called twice on
  one value is refused E0452 by the compiler before this change too; the
  move check does not depend on this pin.

## Predicted, then measured

- Predicted: generic pins up by about 700, unpinned down by the same, no
  pinned call changing; objects unmoved if monomorphization re-pins;
  flow list possibly moving (callee identities appear in the facts).
  Measured: +669 / -669, none changed, 0 objects moved; flow list 797
  unchanged, lane gate unchanged.
- What still reaches the finder unpinned on a concrete receiver: 19
  typings, each with an argument whose type is invalid - a method call
  on a dynamic array whose `Array<T>` is not yet registered types
  silently invalid (1,373 typings) and its result is an argument here.
  Plus the unresolved-instantiation, generic-owner and bounded-parameter
  receivers, which the selection does not cover at all.

### 8.416 A generic method call with a turbofish binds the turbofish first; converting the concrete receivers' typing to read the pin is blocked by a `void`-typed argument - 2026-09-29

## Why

The next step after 8.415 was the typing: for a receiver the selection
covers, read the pinned method's return instead of asking the name-keyed
finder, with an unpinned call naming no method. Built that way
(`.objcmp/s74/slice2-attempt.patch`, not landed), the compiler's own
build refused two calls the finder had been answering regardless of
their arguments.

The first was the selection's: a generic method with an explicit
turbofish.

```cryo
// spawn<C>(mut &this, ctx: C, body: (C) -> void)
s.spawn::<EmitWorkerCtx*>(&wcs[w], emit_worker_entry);
```

8.415 unified each argument with its parameter and ignored the turbofish:
`C` bound to `&EmitWorkerCtx` from the first argument, the function
argument then conflicted, and nothing bound - E0358 once the typing read
the pin.

## What changed

`method_args_bind`: an explicit turbofish (on the call or on the member)
binds the method's type parameters first, resolved as the scope-call
inference resolves one; an argument that does not unify is then compared
by the tier's rule against the parameter with the bindings substituted
(`TypeSubstitution`), so `&wcs[w]` binds `C = EmitWorkerCtx*` by the
reference-to-pointer rule. The turbofish is resolved by
`resolve_turbofish`, the scope-call inference's own block moved into a
helper both now call: resolving it inline added a
`ResolutionContext::new("")` site and the residue check refused the tree
(`call_resolver.cryo ResolutionContext::new (literal:""): tree 15, list
14`); moved, the file keeps its 14. The typing is untouched.

## Proved

- The compiler's facts, 8.415's tree against this one: unpinned calls
  5,270 -> 5,269, the one being `Instance.cryo:3735 .spawn` (the other
  moved records are this change's own lines).
- With the typing converted, the build no longer refuses `spawn`.
- `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` from a clean
  build: every gate OK, 4012 test and 1126 example objects, 0 moved.
  Compiler warnings 344, the same set as HEAD's. Residue 242, lane gate,
  flow list 797: unchanged.

## The second refusal: not fixed, and it blocks the typing conversion

`remaining.subslice(n, remaining.length())` in the `Write` trait's default
`write<T>` (`stdlib/io/traits.cryo:336`), in the check after
monomorphization, walking the template symbolically: a probe at the
failure printed `arg0 kind=Void`. `n`, bound by `Result::Ok(n)` from
`this.write_some(remaining)` on the abstract `This`, is typed `void`. The
selection is right to bind nothing to `start: u64` from a `void`; the
name-keyed finder answered `subslice` without looking at the arguments,
which is what hid the wrong type. The cause is in the abstract-receiver
arm (a bounded parameter's method return), another receiver shape. Not
routed around: excusing a `void` argument in the selection would be a
second path for the same question. It was the only refusal in the
compiler's own build; the test suite was not run with the conversion.

### 8.417 A call on `this` in a trait's default method is typed by the trait - `This` is bounded by the trait it is written in, and every default is walked with `This` abstract - 2026-09-29

## Why

8.416 left the typing conversion blocked on `n` typed `void` in the
`Write` trait's default `write<T>`:

```cryo
match (this.write_some(remaining)) {
    Result::Ok(n) => { remaining = remaining.subslice(n, remaining.length()); }
    ...
```

`this` is `This`, the one placeholder every trait's signatures are
resolved against. A default's `This` is any type implementing the trait,
so the trait itself is its bound - but no where-clause writes that bound,
the placeholder is shared by every trait and cannot say which one bounds
it, and the abstract-receiver arm (`lookup_method_through_param_bounds`)
searched only the method's and the impl's where-clauses. The call typed
as nothing, and `Result::Ok(n)` over an untyped subject bound `n` as
`void`.

## Measured first

A probe in `resolve_method_call` (`scripts/ns-migration/8.417/`), over
the compiler's own build, counted every typing in the abstract-receiver
arm and every typing that leaves through the "receiver with no type
symbol" exit, which returns invalid without a word. Per sema pass (the
check before monomorphization and the one after each print once):

| receiver | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `This` in a default with its own type parameters (walked symbolically) | 46 untyped in the arm | 0 untyped |
| `This` in a default without (walked plainly) | 65 untyped, through the silent exit | 0 untyped |
| `This`, both kinds, after | - | 74 typed, 23 typed `void` (`write_u8`, `write_uint` are declared `-> void`); the count of typings differs from 46 + 65 because the plain walk typed some expressions three times and a typed call exposes the calls on its result |
| a bounded parameter in an impl's copy of a default, through a projection bound (`value.compare(&best)` in `Iterator::min`/`max`, `core/iter.cryo:181`, `:202`) | 96 | 96 - not this change |
| a parameter whose method is on a supertrait (`T: Step`, `compare` on `Ord`, `core/ops.cryo:119`, `:152`) | 2 | 2 - not this change |
| a parameter bounded on its TYPE's declaration (`A: Allocator` - `reallocate`, `deallocate`, `drop`) | 13 | 13 - not this change |
| a receiver typed `void` upstream (`into_raw`, `fs/path.cryo:373`, `collections/string.cryo:260`) | 2 | 2 - not this change |
| an unresolved instantiation (`push`, `fs/path.cryo:322`, `:332`) | 2 | 2 - not this change |

A second finding came with the first: a default WITHOUT type parameters
was walked plainly, where `This` is not treated as abstract at all, so
every `this.m()` in such a body fell through to the silent exit - every
call on `this` in `Iterator::min`, `Read::read_exact`, `BufRead::take_front`
and the rest was untyped.

## What changed

- `SemaState::symbolic_trait`: the trait whose defaults are being walked,
  set by `visit(TraitDeclNode)`.
- `lookup_method_through_param_bounds`: a `This` receiver asks that trait
  (`TypeArena::is_this_placeholder`). The ask goes through
  `scan_param_bounds`, whose one `lookup_method_return` call now takes the
  trait as an implied bound before the written ones - a second call beside
  it grew the lane gate's routed-lookup row 36 -> 37.
- Every trait default is walked symbolically, not only a generic one.

Neither the untyped count nor any other arm moved otherwise.

## Proved, each part alone against the unmutated tree

`tests/tests/projects/trait_default_this_calls_typed`: a trait with no
implementor whose two defaults write `const s: string = this.count();`,
one with a type parameter of its own (line 22) and one without (line 17).

| compiler | line 17 | line 22 |
|---|---|---|
| HEAD | built | built |
| this change | E0200 | E0200 |
| the `This` branch alone (walk unchanged) | built | E0200 |
| the walk alone (`This` branch disabled) | built | built |

Declared in `tests/started-passing`: the baseline built it.

## Evidence

`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` from a clean
build: every gate OK; 4012 test and 1126 example objects, 0 moved.
Compiler warnings 344, the same set as HEAD's clean build (six moved
lines in the two edited files). Flow list 797, lane gate, residue:
unchanged. The first verify run failed on the baseline's
`ProcessAsync::two_children_join_concurrently`, the known load flake; the
re-run passed.

## Not done

The typing conversion (8.416's patch) is not re-applied here. The five
other untyped rows above are separate causes and are not fixed.

### 8.418 A bound written on a type's own declaration types calls in the type's methods; the calls on unbounded type parameters are counted - 2026-09-29

## Why

A call on a value of a type parameter is typed through the bounds in
scope: the enclosing function's `where` clause, the enclosing impl's, and
- in a trait's default method - the trait itself for `This`. A `where`
clause written on the type's own declaration was not among them, so a
call in one of the type's own methods typed as nothing and a wrong use of
its result compiled:

```cryo
type trait Sized2 { size(&this) -> u64; }

type struct Holder<T> where T: Sized2 {
    item: T;
    as_text(&this) -> u64 {
        const s: string = this.item.size();   // built; `size` returns u64
        return 0;
    }
}
```

## What the brief's figure was

The previous session counted 13 untyped calls as this shape (allocator
calls: `allocate`, `deallocate`, `reallocate`). They are not: `RawBuffer`,
`Array`, `HashMap`, `Rc`, `Arc`, `Box`, `Mutex` and `RwLock` declare their
methods inside the type's body and bound `A` nowhere those methods can see
- `where A: Allocator` appears only on their trait impls (`Drop`, `Eq`,
`Hash`, ..; `raw_buffer.cryo:33` and `:176-177`). They are calls on
UNBOUNDED parameters, counted below. The in-tree population of this entry's
shape is 0: the only two types with a type-level `where` (`MapIter`,
`FilterIter`, `core/iter.cryo:272,292`) restate it on their impls, and
their calls were already typed.

## What changed

`MethodBinding::lookup_method_through_param_bounds` also scans the bounds
written on the declaration of the type whose methods are being walked
(`owner_declared_bounds`: the walk's owner type, its template, and
`TemplateEntry::declared_where_bounds`, one accessor for the four
aggregate kinds). Which parameter a bound names is decided by the
parameter's declaration, as for the other clauses. The parameter-types
sibling (`param_types_through_param_bounds`, argument classification) is
NOT changed: no test observes it; it is the same one-line addition.

## Proved

- New project `type_declaration_bound_types_calls`, declared in
  `tests/started-passing`: the tip builds it; the change refuses line 21
  only (`E0200 ... expected string, found u64` at `src/main.cryo:21:27`);
  line 16, a correct use, passes.
- Inversion: `owner_declared_bounds` made to answer null - the project
  builds (`Compiled -> build/type_declaration_bound_types_calls.exe`).
  Unmutated: refused at 21:27, `aborting due to 1 error`.

## Calls on an unbounded type parameter, measured

A probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.418/unbounded-receiver-probe.patch`) at
every method call whose receiver is a type parameter counted the bounds in
scope naming it - function `where`, impl `where`, the owner declaration's
`where`; `This` excluded - over the compiler, every test project, every
example (`probe_run.sh`) and the unit suite (`cryo test` with a filter
matching nothing: the suite's files are compiled; `cryo build` in `tests/`
does not compile them). Tabulated by `unbounded_tab.py`. 140 distinct call
sites in the projects' builds (123 stdlib, 12 test projects, 5 examples,
all but the stdlib's bounded) plus the unit suite's.

Written on an unbounded parameter, every one in the stdlib - **22 sites**:

| type (parameter) | calls | sites |
|---|---|---|
| `RawBuffer` (`A`) | `allocate`, `deallocate`, `reallocate` | `collections/raw_buffer.cryo:122,155,161` |
| `Array` (`A`) | `allocate`, `deallocate`, `reallocate` | `collections/array.cryo:535,571,577` |
| `HashMap` (`A`) | `allocate`, `deallocate` | `collections/hashmap.cryo:538,563` |
| `Mutex` (`A`) | `allocate`, `deallocate` | `sync/mutex.cryo:190,196` |
| `RwLock` (`A`) | `allocate`, `deallocate` | `sync/rwlock.cryo:202,208` |
| `Rc`, `Arc`, `Box` (`A`) | `allocate` in `try_new_in` | `alloc/rc.cryo:131`, `alloc/arc.cryo:146`, `alloc/box.cryo:87` |
| `BufWriter` (`W`) | `write_some` | `io/buf.cryo:145` |
| `BufReader` (`R`) | `read` | `io/buf.cryo:367` |
| `BufStream` (`S`) | `drop` | `io/buf.cryo:641` |
| free functions (`O`, `T`) | `drop` | `future/executor.cryo:208,591`, `thread/_module.cryo:224,280` |

So 15 allocator calls on eight types, 2 I/O calls on two, and 5 `drop`
calls on a parameter with no bound.

Not counted as unbounded:
- `core/iter.cryo:181,202` (`compare` in `Iterator::min`/`max`): bounded
  through a projection (`This::Item: Ord`), which the probe does not count
  as naming the parameter; in the impls' copies it reads as unbounded.
  That is the separate projection-bounded shape.
- The unit suite: 4 sites, none written unbounded. Three are async
  functions WITH `where S: AtmRead` / `where D: AtmDrain`
  (`tests/tests/lang/async_trait_method.cryo:94,101,213`) whose lowered

  (`tests/tests/lang/enum_ctor_arg_inference.cryo:88`).
- Tests' projects and examples: 0. The probe reaches them - 12 and 5

Whether such a call is an error where it is written was not decided by
this change. Jake ruled it since, in plain text (2026-09-29): it is an
error, and the stdlib's calls get bounds; that is a separate change.

## Predicted, then measured

- Projects 111 -> 112.
