### 8.420 A method call on a type parameter no bound names is E0358 where it is written; the stdlib's seventeen such calls get bounds - 2026-09-29

## Why

Jake ruled in plain text (2026-09-29) that calling a method on a type
parameter with no bound is an error, as in Rust (`docs/cryo.md`, "Which
Method a Call Names"). The symbolic walk left such a call untyped and said
nothing, so a call that names nothing compiled until an instantiation
happened to supply the method:

```cryo
type trait Counter { count(&this) -> u64; }

type struct Unbounded<W> {
    w: W;
    total(&this) -> u64 {
        this.w.count();    // built before; now error[E0358]
        return 0;
    }
}
```

Now:

```
error[E0358]: no method named `count` found on type `W`
 --> src/main.cryo:17:16
 note: `W` is a type parameter with no bound, so it has no methods
 help: add a `where W: Trait` bound naming a trait that declares `count`
```

The code and the first line's wording are E0358's existing "no method
named" report; the note and the help are new wording.

## Counted first

`scripts/ns-migration/8.420/probe_run.sh` with a compiler built with
`unbounded-receiver-probe.patch` (the check's site printing instead of
reporting; `tab.py` tabulates), over the
compiler, `tests/`, every test project and example, and the unit suite: 22
distinct sites, every one in the stdlib - the same 22 the adopted change's
probe listed (8.418's table). After bounding (below): 5, and the 128 build
exits and every error line identical to before the bounds.

## What changed

- `MethodBinding::unbounded_receiver_param`: the receiver, peeled of
  pointers and references, is a type parameter other than `This` that no
  bound names in the function's `where`, the impl's, or the owner
  declaration's. An impl's copy of a trait default (`is_synth_default`) and
  an async lowering's `poll` (`is_synthesized_body`) are skipped: their
  source is walked where it is written, with its bounds. Asked only when the
  bounds lookup typed nothing, in the symbolic walk.
- `CallResolver::report_unbounded_receiver_call` reports it;
  `is_explicit_drop_call` is the one recognizer of `x.drop()`, now shared by
  W0015 and this check.
- stdlib: `where A: Allocator` on `RawBuffer`, `Array`, `HashMap`, `Mutex`,
  `RwLock`, `Rc`, `Arc`, `Box`; `where W: Write` on `BufWriter`, `where R:
  Read` on `BufReader` - the type declarations, which 8.418 made the walk
  read. Generated by `scripts/ns-migration/8.420/bound_unbounded_params.py`
  (`--check` re-verifies). 17 sites.

## Not bounded: five explicit destructor calls - OPEN for Jake

`future/executor.cryo:208,591` (`O`), `thread/_module.cryo:224,280` (`T`),
`io/buf.cryo:641` (`S`) call `.drop()` on a value of an unbounded
parameter. No trait can bound them: `T: Drop` would shut out every type
without a user destructor (an `i32` task output). Four release a value
behind a raw pointer in place; the replacement, `mem::drop(*p)`, is refused
(`E0453: cannot move a value that owns a destructor out of a pointer`,
measured in a scratch program). What is missing is a drop-in-place
function, as Rust's `ptr::drop_in_place`, whose name is not ruled. The
fifth is `BufStream`'s hand-written `drop` releasing `inner`, which field
glue releases again after the body.

Built as: `x.drop()` is not checked, recognized by W0015's predicate - the
language gives every type a destructor (a user impl, drop glue, or nothing
for `Copy`; `codegen/visit/call_emitter.cryo`). That is a reading, not a
ruling. If Jake rules the destructor call is a method call under ruling 1,
the exemption goes and the five sites need the drop-in-place function.

## Found: a bounded parameter whose bounds lack the method - OPEN for Jake

`function g<T>(x: &T) -> u64 where T: Counter { x.missing(); ... }` builds
before and after this change (Rust refuses it, E0599). The ruling covers
unbounded parameters only, so this is not refused. Population in the tree
for function- and owner-scoped bounds: 0 (the `func` and `owner` mutants
below, run over the whole corpus by `probe_err.sh`, add no error site to
the tree's; the same mutants refuse
the scratch program, so the instrument can report one).

## Proved

New project `unbounded_param_method_refused`, declared in
`tests/started-passing`: refuses 17:16 and 35:7 only (`aborting due to 2
errors`); the bounded calls at 25 and 31 and `(*p).drop()` at 40 build.
Mutants (`scripts/ns-migration/8.420/mutants.py`, each alone, source
restored after each):

| compiler | the project's test |
|---|---|
| tree (control) | passes |
| HEAD baseline (the old gate) | fails: builds the program |
| `off` - the check finds nothing | fails |
| `drop` - `x.drop()` checked too | fails: a third error |
| `owner` - owner bounds ignored | passes (equivalent here: a bounded call is typed before the check is asked) |
| `func` - function bounds ignored | passes (same) |

The last two change only the bounded-miss case above.

(`intrinsic function drop_in_place<T>(p: T*) -> void;` is

### 8.422 A method call's type is read off the method the selection chose; the typing's by-name re-lookup is deleted - 2026-09-29

## Why

Selection (`bind_method_on_receiver`) chose and pinned a method call's
method; typing (`resolve_method_call`) then looked the method up AGAIN by
its leaf - `lookup_method_with_inheritance` on the receiver, then
`lookup_method_through_trait_impls` - and a later override corrected the
type when the two disagreed. Rule one: a name is resolved once, where it is
written. The flow gate cannot see this finder (its key is composed, owner
and leaf), so the proof is a counter on the finders themselves.

## Measured first

Probe on HEAD `d1aef7c2` (`scripts/ns-migration/8.422/typing-site-probe.patch`,
run by `probe_run.sh` there over the compiler, `tests/`, every project and
example, and the unit suite): 282,913 entries into
`lookup_method_with_inheritance` (282,901 from the typing site) and 782 into
`lookup_method_through_trait_impls` (574 from typing). At the typing site:
258,390 typings had a pin and the finder's return equalled the pin's; 1,190
differed, every one a sibling specialization under one leaf (`cast`, `map`)
that the pin override already corrected; 13 had a pin and no finder return
(an adapter default only the trait-impl arm typed); 22,830 were on an
instantiation not yet minted (`Slice<u8>`, `Option<u8>` before mono), which
the selection never pinned - its peel stopped there - and 103 more of those
reached only through trait impls; 10 were blocked by
`trait_method_unavailable`, all on unminted receivers.

## What changed

- The selection covers the unminted instantiation. Its candidates are the
  template's: the declaration's methods, its inherent blocks, then the trait
  impls whose heads unify with the instantiation. Each list is bound through
  a view of the instantiation - the template's parameters for the
  declaration, the head's bindings (`add_head_param_bindings`) plus the
  where-only parameters (`bind_where_only_params`) for an impl block - as
  pre-solved unification slots, so an argument that matches builds no type.
  The chosen method is returned, not pinned: a template method pinned
  pre-mono reads to mono as a call needing no specialization. The post-mono
  pass pins the minted method as before.
- Typing reads the pin on a minted receiver and the selection's return on an
  unminted one. The trait-impl arm and `head_blocked` are deleted with the
  finder; `MethodBinding::trait_method_unavailable` and `methods_declare`
  are deleted.
- `TypeResolver::derive_where_assoc_bindings` derives a trait's
  generic-parameter slot too (`A` in `where I: Iterator<A>`), from the
  subject's own impl, so `FilterIter<TakeIter<Range<i32>>>` reaches `i32`.
- `TypeSubstitution::apply` honours an entry keyed by a projection, so the
  selection builds `Option<i32>`, never an `Option<..::Item>` no code
  demands (which the E0900 validator refused during development).
- A call whose argument failed to type, or whose arguments the argument
  check refused, types as invalid without a second E0358; an operator whose
  trait method refused its argument hands back the call instead of adding
  E0229.

## Evidence

- Finder entries over the same corpus after (`finder-entry-probe.patch`):
  `lookup_method_with_inheritance` 12, `lookup_method_through_trait_impls`
  208 - exactly the non-typing callers the before-run measured (the
  non-call member access in `member_resolver`; the generic-owner arm).
  Typing site: 0, against 282,901 before with the same counter.
- Every method call's final type, per build, HEAD against this tree
  (`final-type-probe.patch`): 490,519 typings before, 490,589 after (the
  difference is the edited files' own calls); outside the four edited
  files 8 differ, all a call whose
  argument had already failed - `get_or_insert(slot, [])` twice and
  `render_line_group` twice in the compiler pre-mono, four calls in
  `array_method_argument_mismatch` - old type -> invalid. Build outcomes of
  all 129 builds and the unit suite identical. This run predates the last
  two error-path changes (a refused call, a refused operator), which act
  only where an error was already reported; verify's census covers them.
- `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: every gate OK;
  objects 2 of 5,138 moved - `std/core/option.o` in `chain_default_same_param`
  and `chain_default_param_conflict`. Same 836 symbols; per-section
  disassembly identical but for RIP-relative displacements: `Option<i32>`'s
  functions are emitted at a different position because its instantiation
  is first minted at a different point. Order only.
- Clean-build compiler warnings 266 and 266, the same (code, file) counts.
- Flow list 797 -> 791 (the 6 paths into `NodeLocator::method_by_name`
  through the deleted `trait_method_unavailable`; the impl-block scan's 2
  paths moved to `bind_on_methods`). Residue unchanged at 242 (J 167),
  table regenerated: the impl-block scan is now counted under
  `local::MethodNode[]`, an existing justified class. Lane gate unchanged.

## Also recorded here

Rulings 14 to 18 (Jake, plain text, 2026-09-29) are added to the appendix of
`docs/resolution-rules.md`: the intrinsic's name and module, `BufStream`'s
explicit drop deleted, a bounded parameter's missing method is E0358,
the E0358 wording and ARENA_READ 65 approved, and no new permanent Python
instruments.

## Not done

`lookup_method_with_inheritance` survives for the non-call member access
(`member_resolver.cryo`, 12 entries), and `lookup_method_through_trait_impls`
for `resolve_method_return_via_template` (208). The selection still finds
candidates by scanning method lists by leaf; ruling 11 moves that to the
member-function door.

### 8.423 `BufStream`'s `drop` no longer releases its transport; field glue does, once - 2026-09-29

## Why

Ruling 15. `BufStream::drop` called `this.inner.drop()`, and field glue
releases every field of an aggregate after its own `drop` runs, so the
transport was released twice. The call was also one of the five `.drop()`
calls on an unbounded type parameter that 8.420 left exempt from E0358.

## Measured

New project `bufstream_releases_transport_once`: a `BufStream` over a
transport whose `drop` counts, released at scope exit; the exit code is the
count. Against `fe95596c`'s stdlib it exits 2 (released twice); against this
tree it exits 0 and prints `bufstream-release ok`.

## What it changes

Compiled output of every program that instantiates `BufStream<S>`: its
`drop` no longer calls `S`'s. In `examples/11-http-server`, 1 of 86 objects
changes, `std/net/socket/tcp.o`, where `BufStream<TcpStream>`'s `drop` is
emitted. `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"` reports 0
moved, because verify builds the baseline COMPILER at HEAD and compiles both
runs against the working tree's stdlib; a stdlib-only change is invisible to
it, and a `tests/started-passing` line for the project was refused for the
same reason ("the baseline census passes it").

## Left

The body still releases `rbuf`, `scratch` and `wbuf` by hand, which field
glue releases again; `Array`'s `drop` nulls its buffer, so the second
release frees nothing. Four `.drop()` calls on unbounded parameters remain
exempt (`future/executor.cryo`, `thread/_module.cryo`), for the
`std::core::ptr::drop_in_place` intrinsic (rulings 7 and 14).

### 8.424 Supertraits are bound where they are written and a bound reaches their methods; a bounded parameter's unknown method is E0358 - 2026-09-29

## Why

Ruling 16: a method call on a bounded type parameter whose bounds do not
declare the method is E0358, as it is for an unbounded one. Turned on alone
(`.objcmp/s78/ruling16-blocked-on-supertraits.patch`) it refused two correct
stdlib calls, `this.start.compare(&this.end)` in `Range`'s `Iterator` impl
(`stdlib/core/ops.cryo`), bound `T: Step` with `type trait Step : Ord`:
`compare` is the supertrait's, and the compiler kept a supertrait as a bare
`SymbolStr` (`BaseTraitInfo.name`) that nothing bound and nothing read.

## Measured before

* Traits declaring supertraits in the corpus: 2, `Ord : Eq`
  (`stdlib/core/cmp.cryo:122`) and `Step : Ord` (`stdlib/core/ops.cryo:16`);
  grep over every `.cryo` outside build trees, the stdlib copy under `dist/`
  aside.
* Readers of the stored name: none; `ASTCloner` copied the array and nothing
  else touched it. `TraitType.super_traits` was a second store with an adder
  no caller called, always empty.
* An unresolvable supertrait compiled silently: `type trait Sub : Nope { .. }`
  with an impl and a call built and ran (exit 0). So does an unknown trait in
  a `where` clause until something instantiates the function, and then it is
  reported as E0306 at the call ("the trait bound `P: AlsoNope` is not
  satisfied"), not where it is written.
* `docs/grammar.md` writes a supertrait as a `TraitBound`, a possibly
  qualified path; the parser took one identifier, so `: cmp::Ord` was a
  cascade of E0100 parse errors.

## What changed

* `BaseTraitInfo` is deleted; `TraitDeclNode.base_traits` is `TraitRef[]`,
  parsed by `parse_trait_ref` as a bound's trait is, and stamped in the name
  layer's `visit(TraitDeclNode*)` by `stamp_trait_ref_identity` through the
  `scope-type` door, with its arguments stamped too.
* `TraitType.super_traits` and `add_super_trait` are deleted.
* `GenericRegistry::trait_and_supertraits(DefId) -> DefId[]`: a trait and its
  supertraits, transitively, each once, walked by the stamped identities; a
  cycle ends at the first trait seen twice.
* The three bound scans in `MethodBinding` (`scan_param_bounds`,
  `scan_param_bound_param_types`, `scan_projection_bounds`) ask the chain, the
  bound's own trait first; a supertrait's return has `This` rebased only, the
  bound's arguments being the named trait's. One lookup site per scan, so
  the lane surface is unchanged (an intermediate version with a second site
  per scan moved `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 36 -> 38 and was restructured).
* The saved ruling-16 patch, applied unchanged: the E0358 check asks whether
  the receiver is a type parameter at all (`receiver_type_param`), and the
  "has no bound" note is kept for the unbounded case only.

## Proof by inversion

Three compilers over the same probes (`.objcmp/s79/`): the tip, the patch
alone without supertraits (`.objcmp/s78/cryo-r16.exe`), and this tree.

| probe | tip | patch alone | this tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x.missing()` under `T: Counter`, instantiated | E0358 on `Main::P`, post-mono | E0358 on `T` + 2 false `compare` | E0358 on `T` only |
| `T: Top`, `Top : Mid : Base`, calls `top`/`mid`/`base` | builds, exit 0 | E0358 `base`, `mid` + 2 `compare` | builds, exit 0 |
| `T: Step`, `a.compare(b)`, `a.equals(b)`, `for (i in 0..4)` | builds, exit 0 | 3 `compare` + 1 `equals` E0358 | builds, exit 0 |
| `A : B`, `B : A`, calls `a`, `b`, `zzz` | E0358 `zzz` on `Main::P` | E0358 `b`, `zzz` + 2 `compare` | E0358 `zzz` only; the cycle ends |
| `type trait Ranked : cmp::Ord` | E0100 cascade | - | builds, exit 0 |

New projects: `bounded_param_method_refused` (compile_fail; the tip BUILDS
it, nothing instantiating the bodies; this tree refuses `this.w.name_len()`
at 20:40 and `x.reset()` at 25:41 and nothing else) and
`supertrait_methods_through_bound` (run; the tip refuses it at parse, the
patch alone with 6 E0358s, this tree exits 0).

`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: objects 0 moved of
4,067 tests (the declared projects' 54 left out) and 1,126 examples; the one
declared started-passing and the one
started-compiling project are the baseline census's only failures. Compiler
warnings 344, the same set as `fe95596c`'s clean build (compared as
(code, file, message)). Roster 2550 -> 2552; projects 114 -> 116. Spelling
flow 791, unchanged.

## Left

* An unresolvable supertrait, and an unknown trait in a `where` clause,
  still compile until a bound scan reads them, when `TraitRef::definition()`
  records the missing answer and the build is refused at its end. Rule one
  says the name layer refuses them where they are written; the natural
  report is the one every other unbound type spelling gets
  (`refuse_unbound_type`: E0203 "cannot find type", E0240, E0155, E0154).
  Which code and wording a trait position gets is not decided here.
* A supertrait with generic parameters or associated types (`trait A<T> :
  B<T>`) is typed with `This` rebased only; its own arguments are not mapped
  through the subtrait's. None exists in the corpus.
* An `implement trait Step for X` is not checked for `X: Ord`.

### 8.425 An inherent method wins over a trait method whether either is generic - 2026-09-29

## Why

Ruling 13, and `docs/cryo.md` ("Which Method a Call Names"): an inherent
method wins over a trait method. Selection ran every candidate set's
non-generic methods before any set's generic ones, so a plain trait method
beat a generic inherent one:

```cryo
type trait Beta { go(&this, u: i32) -> i64; }
type struct IgTn { v: i32; }
implement trait Beta for IgTn { go(&this, u: i32) -> i64 { return 2; } }
implement struct IgTn { go<U>(&this, u: U) -> i64 { return 1; } }
ig.go(7);   // was 2, the trait's; now 1, the inherent method
```

## Measured before

A throwaway probe (`.objcmp/s79/selprobe.patch`) after every unstamped
selection listed each candidate that applies at any tier, as inherent or
trait and generic or not, and reported a call when a trait method was chosen
while an inherent one applied (ruling 13), or when the set the ruling would
choose from held both a generic and a non-generic applicable method (ruling
4). Control: the rulings' own examples (`k1.cryo`) report one of each.

Over the corpus (`probe_run.sh`: compiler, tests, 116 projects, 14
examples, unit suite; 132 builds): ruling 13, **0** calls. Ruling 4, 33
sites at first, every one an artifact - a generic method beside the
specialization minted from it (`String::push<T>` and its clone), which has
no generic parameters left; counted as generic by `spec_type_args`, 2
sites remained, both `Iterator::fold<Acc>` / `queue<T>` trait defaults
beside a specialized clone of the same default (`is_synth_default`,
`is_specialization`, no `spec_type_args`). Genuine pairs: **0**.

## What changed

`select_method` and `select_on_template` take the set they are asked for,
inherent or trait. Order: the stamped trait's methods (non-generic, then
generic), then the inherent set (non-generic, then generic), then the trait
set (non-generic, then generic). The stamped trait's generic methods now
come before unstamped non-generic ones; a stamp is the trait a bound named
where the call is written.

## Proof by inversion

`inherent_method_over_trait` gains `IgTn` (plain type), `GIgTn<T>`
(generic type) and a bound-directed call on `IgTn`. The previous compiler
prints `ig_tn=2 gig_tn=1 bound_ig_tn=2`; this one `ig_tn=1 gig_tn=1
bound_ig_tn=2`. Declared in `tests/started-passing`.

`make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: OK, objects 0
moved of 4,064 tests (the declared project's 57 left out) and 1,126
examples - the corpus-wide confirmation that no other call's pin moved,
the stamped reorder included. Compiler warnings: the same set of 344 from a
clean build. `pick_own_method` count 3 -> 2.

## Left

Ruling 4 (a generic and a non-generic method that both apply is an error)
is not built: no existing diagnostic fits (E0156 is two traits, E0154
module paths), and the code and wording are not decided. Measured
population 0. A post-mono check would also need a specialization to name
the generic method it was minted from; a trait default's clone does not
(`spec_type_args` is empty on it).

### 8.426 Two by-name method finders deleted; member access reads the member-function door - 2026-09-29

## Why

After 8.422, `MethodBinding::lookup_method_with_inheritance` (non-call member
access, `member_resolver.cryo`) and `lookup_method_through_trait_impls` (the
generic-owner arm of `resolve_method_return_via_template`) were the last
callers of two finders that answer "what does method `m` on owner `O` return"
from `DeclarationIndex::method_returns`, a table keyed by (owner, name) that
holds one return per name - overloads collapse into it - beside the
member-function door.

## Measured before

A throwaway probe (`.objcmp/s79/finderprobe.patch`) at each finder's entry
compared its answer with the door's (the family's entries' signatures'
returns, canonicalized), over 132 builds:

| finder | entries | answered | door agrees | neither answers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lookup_method_with_inheritance` | 12 | 4 | 4 | 8 |
| `lookup_method_through_trait_impls` | 213 | 0 | - | 213 |

The 12 are the deref-coercion member accesses in
`tests/lang/operator_overload.cryo` (`b.total()`, `b.bump_x(99)` answer;
`b.px`, `b.py` are fields and answer nowhere). The 213 are calls through
function-typed fields on generic owners (`this.f(x)`, leaves `f` and
`init`), which a method finder cannot answer. A control built the shape the
second finder's comment names - a trait default method on a generic owner
called on a symbolic receiver (`.objcmp/s79/k4.cryo`): selection types it,
the finder is never reached, and the program runs correctly.

## What changed

* `lookup_method_through_trait_impls` and its arm are deleted.
* `lookup_method_with_inheritance` is deleted; `member_resolver`'s two
  callers read `lookup_family_entries` for the owner and each base class
  (`MemberResolver::method_return_through_door`); the answer is the return
  every entry shares, invalid when the overloads' returns differ.

## Evidence

Lane surface re-pinned: `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 36 -> 33 (the three
`lookup_method_return` reads), `LOOKUP_OTHER` 44 -> 45 (the one door read,
which the gate counts as any name-keyed index read). Residue 242 -> 240 (J
167 -> 165), name-taking listing 718 -> 716, pending allows 519 -> 517.

### 8.427 An inherent method and a trait method that both apply are ambiguous; a bound names its method - 2026-09-29

## Why

Rulings 22, 24 and 25 (Jake, plain text, 2026-09-29; recorded in
`docs/resolution-rules.md`'s appendix with 21, and 13 marked superseded):
whenever an inherent method and a trait method of one name both apply to a
call, the call is an ambiguity error in every combination - no precedence -
reported as E0156 with a primary line naming the inherent method; and a call
written on a bounded type parameter means the bound's method, so an
instantiation can neither redirect it nor make it ambiguous. §8.425 had built
the opposite precedence (inherent first).

## Measured before

The 79th session's probe (`.objcmp/s79/r22probe.patch`: after every unstamped
selection, whether an inherent and a trait candidate both apply) over 132
builds found 180 distinct sites: 170 `equals` (`Str` declared `equals` inline
and again in its `Eq` impl, one body), 2 `File::stream_position` (inherent
beside `Seek`'s default), 8 `go` in the test projects written for the old
precedence. Two of the `equals` sites were generic code: `Option::contains`
and `Result::contains` call `inner.equals(value)` under `where T: Eq`; the
receiver is a match binding, not a parameter, so the dispatch annotator's
parameter rule never stamped it, and after monomorphization the call reached
selection as a concrete, unstamped receiver.

The same probe after each step (`.objcmp/s80/p2.out`), against the 79th run
as control (`.objcmp/s79/r22.out`, 180 sites):

| after | distinct sites |
|---|---|
| the bound stamp (step 1) and the two stdlib duplicates removed (step 2) | 4 (`go`, `inherent_method_over_trait:98,99,102` and `static_path_prefers_inherent_method:21`) |

Build outcomes of the 132 builds identical to the control's.

## What changed

* A call a bound answers in a generic body is stamped with the trait whose
  declaration answered (`member.resolved_trait`) where sema types it
  (`resolve_method_call` through `abstract_receiver_method_return`): any
  receiver whose type is a bounded parameter or a bounded projection - a
  parameter, a local, a match binding - and the supertrait when the method is
  a supertrait's. `BoundDirection` notes every trait the bounds (the
  function's, the impl's, the owner declaration's) answer through; two
  traits providing the name direct nothing, as before, and the instantiation
  reports the tie.
* The dispatch annotator's parameter rule is deleted: sema's stamp covers
  it. Probe (`.objcmp/s80/aprobe.patch`, 132 builds): the rule would have
  stamped 2,729 site-builds, every one already stamped by sema, 0 new; 6
  where sema's stamp is the supertrait the method is declared on (`compare`
  under `T: Step` is `Ord`'s) and the rule's was the bound.
* `Str`'s inline `equals` is deleted; its `Eq` impl carries the doc comment.
  `File::stream_position` moves from the inherent block into `implement
  trait Seek for struct File` as an override of the trait default: both
  bodies return `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_CUR)` (the default reaches it through
  `seek(SeekFrom::Current(0))`), so every caller, direct or through `Seek`,
  gets the one-call body and the behaviour is unchanged.
* Selection no longer writes the call while it searches: a candidate set is
  asked whether a method applies (`select_in_set`), and the call is bound
  once, by `commit_selection` (the tier-3 converter and the pin). Unstamped,
  the inherent set is asked, and when it binds, every trait whose method
  also applies is collected (`report_inherent_trait_tie`) and the call is
  refused as E0156; the inherent method stays the call's binding so typing
  does not cascade. A receiver that is an instantiation not yet minted is
  asked too, against the impls whose where-clauses hold for it, since a
  generic method's call is pinned to its specialization by
  monomorphization and never selected again; one whose arguments are still
  a generic body's parameters is asked where it is instantiated.
* E0156 has one formatter (`report_trait_method_tie`), which takes the
  inherent candidate. New wording, for Jake to see:

  ```
  error[E0156]: `go` is both an inherent method of `IgTn` and provided by a trait implemented for it
   note: candidate #1: the inherent method `IgTn::go`
   note: candidate #2: `Beta::go`, from `implement trait Beta for IgTn`
   help: neither outranks the other: call the trait's method as `(Beta for IgTn)::go(&ig, 7)`, or rename one of them
  ```

* The owner's printed name no longer threads through selection; the pin read
  it only for emptiness, which `bind_method_on_receiver` has already
  refused. `pin_method_callee_from_qname` is `pin_method_callee`.
* `docs/cryo.md` §13.4 states the rule.

## Tests

* `inherent_method_over_trait` becomes `inherent_trait_method_ambiguous`
  (compile_fail): all eleven receiver/method/block-order shapes are refused

* `inherent_trait_method_explicit` (run): the impl-qualified form and a call

* `bound_call_names_bound_method` (run): calls under `where T: Eq` on a

  P)::go(&p)`; exit 33 -> 23. `P::go(&p)` still names the inherent method.

### 8.428 An unknown trait in a bound or a supertrait is refused where it is written (E0242) - 2026-09-29

## Why

Ruling 23 (Jake, plain text, 2026-09-29; recorded in
`docs/resolution-rules.md`'s appendix): an unknown supertrait, or an unknown
trait in a `where` clause, is refused where it is written, with wording that
says trait ("cannot find trait `Foo` in this scope", Rust's), not E0203's
"cannot find type". The code was left to this session.

## Measured before

`stamp_trait_ref_identity` answered a bound's or a supertrait's trait with
`type_spelling_res` and, when nothing answered, left the reference unstamped
and said nothing: `type trait Sub : Missing { .. }`, `where T: Nowhere` on a
function, `where T: AlsoMissing` on a type declaration and `where T:
StillMissing` on an impl all compiled (exit 0). A call through such a bound
reported it at the instantiation instead (`f::<i32>(&a)`: E0306 "the trait
bound `i32: Nowhere` is not satisfied", at the call). An impl head's unknown
trait was already refused where written, as E0203 with the noun "trait".

## What changed

* New code E0242 (`E0242_UNDEFINED_TRAIT`, "Undefined Trait").
* `stamp_trait_ref_identity` refuses a spelling nothing answers with the
  resolver's one refusal (`refuse_unbound_type`), marked as naming a trait -
  the same report a type spelling gets (E0155 for a leaf two modules declare,
  E0240 for one the writer cannot reach), with E0242 and the noun "trait"
  where the name exists nowhere. Supertraits, where-clauses on functions,
  methods, impls and type declarations, and associated-type bounds all
  stamp through it.
* The resolver's `type_noun: string` is `naming_trait: boolean`; the impl
  head's unknown trait takes E0242 too (its wording already said trait).
* `docs/cryo.md` §11.3 states it.
* The spelling-flow list gains 4 rows (791 -> 795): the refusal's two
  lookups (the scope map and a module's exports), already listed from
  `stamp_named_annotation`, are now reached from the trait reference too.
  They leave the list when `refuse_unbound_type` stops looking a spelling
  up, for both origins at once.

## Evidence

* Over the corpus (the compiler, tests, 120 projects, the examples and the
  unit suite; `.objcmp/s80/p5.out` against `.objcmp/s80/p2.out`), every
  build's outcome and error lines are unchanged apart from the new test
  project: no corpus code names an unknown supertrait or bound trait. The
  control is that project, whose five E0242 lines the same grep reports.
* `unknown_trait_refused_where_written` (compile_fail): the four positions
  and a known-plus-unknown bound (`where T: Known + Absent`) each refused at
  the spelling, `Known` not reported, no "cannot find type". HEAD's
  compiler builds it (exit 0); declared in `tests/started-passing`.

## Left

* A call through a refused bound still adds E0306 at the instantiation
  (`f::<i32>(&a)` under `where T: Nowhere`): a cascade from the refused
  reference, which nothing marks as refused for the bound checker.

### 8.429 A static path naming an inherent and a trait method is ambiguous; a path call of a generic method runs its specialization; a refused bound is not reported again - 2026-09-29

## Why

Rulings 26-30 (Jake, plain text, 2026-09-29; recorded in
`docs/resolution-rules.md`'s appendix): ruling 22's ambiguity covers static
paths (`IgTn::go(&ig, 7)`); E0156's wording for an inherent method beside a
trait's and E0242 are approved; the explicit call of a generic trait method,
`(BetaG for NgTf)::go(&g, 7)`, which E0156's help proposes and which failed
at codegen, is fixed; and a call under `where T: Nowhere` does not add E0306
after the E0242 the bound already reported.

## Measured before

* Static paths with both an inherent and a trait method in the family
  (probe in `pin_scope_callee_combined`, every build of the compiler, tests,
  every project and example and the unit suite; `.objcmp/s81/sp.out`):
  **1 site**, `static_path_prefers_inherent_method/src/main.cryo:23`
  (`P::go(&p)`), the project written for the old precedence. An upper bound:
  the probe ignored whether the arguments fit. Control: `.objcmp/s81/sp/s2.cryo`,
  seven shapes, all reported.
* HEAD's answers, one file per shape (`.objcmp/s81/sp/`): a plain inherent
  method beside a trait's (`NnTf::go(&a, 7)`) ran the inherent one; a
  GENERIC inherent method beside a plain trait one (`IgTn::go(&ig, 7)`) ran
  the TRAIT's - the generic entry never fit the static selector, so the
  brief's "quietly means the inherent method" was not what HEAD did;
  `SNn::make()` with an inherent and a trait static method died at codegen
  (E0636).
* Every path call of a generic method with a receiver failed: `Q::go::<i32>(&q,
  7)` with only an inherent `go<U>` called the unspecialized template (LLVM
  "Incorrect number of arguments"), `R::go(&r, 7)`, `BetaG::go(&r, 7)` and
  `(BetaG for R)::go(&r, 7)` with only a trait's `go<U>` were E0636 "cannot
  resolve 'R::go'". `r.go(7)` worked. The static selector compared a generic
  entry's signature (`U`) with the argument (`i32`) and nothing fit; the
  single-entry path pinned the template itself; mono's `specialize_method_call`
  returned for any callee that was not a member access.
* `where T: Nowhere` with `f::<i32>(&a)`, `f(&a)` and `g::<i32>(&a)`: four
  E0242 and three E0306 (`.objcmp/s81/sp/c30.cryo`).

## What changed

* **Entry to declaration** (the first of selection's four prerequisites):
  the declaration index keeps, per entry, the node it was registered for
  (`overload_func_decl`, `entry_decl`, `entry_method`); `register_signature`
  and `register_function_signature` take it, all five registrations pass it.
* **Static selection** (`select_static_overload`) reads each entry's
  parameters through `static_entry_params`: a generic method's template takes
  its signature with the method's own parameters solved from the turbofish
  or the arguments after the receiver (`solve_method_bindings_at`, the method
  form's solver with an argument offset); a method-level specialization is not
  a candidate.
* **One pin funnel**, `pin_static_entry`, for the three places a static path
  pinned an entry: a generic method's template is stashed (type arguments,
  `resolved_method`) and the path typed through the bindings; anything else
  is pinned as before.
* **Mono**: `specialize_method_call` takes a path callee sema bound to a
  generic template; the method is that node, and its placement - the owner
  declaration or the impl block holding it - is found by identity
  (`path_method_placement`), not by the name ladder the member form uses.
* A pinned static path is typed from its entry on every walk (the rule the
  trait-owned path already had), so `Q::id(&q, 2u64)` beside `Q::id(&q, 3)`
  keeps its own return after monomorphization.
* **Ruling 26**: `choose_entry` reports an inherent fit beside trait fits as
  E0156 through the one formatter, the inherent method staying bound (one
  error, no cascade). The formatter takes the owner type and renders it
  itself, for both forms (`GnTf<i32>`, not the path's `GnTf`).
* **Ruling 30**: `TraitRef.refused` records that the name layer reported the
  spelling; the call-site bound checks (sema and mono) and
  `unsatisfied_trait_ref` (type positions, mono's instantiation check) skip a
  refused bound. A reference left unstamped without a report is still a
  failure.
* `docs/cryo.md` §13.4 states the path forms and how a generic method's
  parameters bind through a path.

## Evidence

* `path_call_generic_method` (run, exit 0): the inherent, trait-only,
  trait-path and impl-qualified forms, the ruling's
  `(BetaG for NgTf)::go(&g, 7)` beside an inherent `go<U>`, a turbofish, a
  return mentioning `U`, two instantiations of one method, and
  `(Mk for SNn)::make()`. HEAD refuses it (E0200 at `Q::id`); declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`.
* `static_path_inherent_trait_ambiguous` (renamed from
  `static_path_prefers_inherent_method`, compile_fail): six shapes, six E0156,
  the wording ruling 27 approved, and `Lone::go` (a trait method alone) not
  reported. `static_path_generic_owner_ambiguous`: the three generic-owner
  shapes, which resolve after monomorphization and so only when sema has no
  other error. `unknown_trait_bound_no_cascade`: exactly one error. All three
  declared in `tests/started-passing`.
* Control on ruling 30: `kf::<i32>(&a)` under `where T: Known`, `Known`
  declared and not implemented, still reports E0306 from both compilers.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`: OK, 0 of 4118
  test objects and 0 of 1126 example objects moved; census, lsp, cross,
  incr, blind, flow, fast OK. Warnings 344 -> 344, the same set (clean build).
* Gate movements: residue 240 -> 241, one class L site (the path method's
  context, built with an empty name as sema's others are) and one row
  re-keyed (mono's `ma` is now a local assigned in a branch); lane unchanged
  (the owner display moved into the formatter, ARENA_READ 65); flow list
  unchanged at 795 (a first version fed the template's leaf into the mono
  ladder and added 8 flows; placement by identity removed them); roster
  2555 -> 2558.

## Left

* A path call of a generic method on a GENERIC owner - `(BetaG for
  GR<i32>)::go(&gr, 7)`, `(BetaG for GgTf<i32>)::go(&e, 7)` - still fails at
  codegen (E0636): before monomorphization sema does not select for a path
  whose owner is an unminted instantiation, and the template's entries carry
  no link to their impl block (selection's fourth prerequisite). E0156's
  help proposes that form for `GgTf<i32>`.

### 8.430 Calling a private function-typed field from another module is refused; a qualified use after an import collision names its own item - 2026-09-29

## Why

Rulings 2 and 3 (Jake, 2026-09-29; recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md`'s
appendix): calling a private function-typed field from another module is
refused, as reading it already is; after an import collision, a qualified
use binds to the item its path names and only the bare name is refused.

## Measured before

* Ruling 2 (`.objcmp/s81/u3/r2`): `h.run(4)` from another module, `run` a
  private `(i32) -> i32` field, built and ran (exit 15); `const f = h.run;`
  was E0353 "field `run` of `R2::Hookmod::Hook` is private".  The call went
  through `MemberResolver::try_field_function_call`, which pinned the field
  and never ran the visibility gate the read path runs (`pin_field`).
* Ruling 3 (`.objcmp/s81/u3/r3`): with `parse` and `Doc` imported from both
  `Json` and `Toml`, the qualified uses `Toml::parse`, `Json::parse`, the
  full paths and `R3::Toml::Doc` bound to their own module's items (exit
  137, the expected 3721 mod 256), and the bare uses `parse("1")` and
  `Doc { .. }` were E0154 "`parse` is ambiguous: it is imported from both
  ...", one error each, with no error for the qualified uses beside them.
  The ruling's behaviour already held.  The two imports themselves are not
  refused: with no bare use the program builds.

## What changed

* `try_field_function_call` pins the field through `pin_field`, which runs
  `enforce_field_visibility` - one gate for a read and a call.
* `docs/cryo.md` states the call is a read.

## Evidence

* Corpus (138 builds with the changed compiler, `.objcmp/s81/r2c.out`,
  against the previous run `dp2.out`): every build's outcome and error lines
  identical; E0353 lines 15 and 15.  No corpus code calls a private
  function-typed field from outside its module.  Control:
  `private_function_field_call_refused` - HEAD builds and runs it (exit 24),
  this tree reports the one E0353 at `h.run(5)`, not at the declaring
  module's `this.run(x)` nor at the public field's call.  Declared in
  `tests/started-passing`.
* `import_collision_qualified_use` (run) and
  `import_collision_bare_use_refused` (compile_fail, exactly one error) pin
  ruling 3's behaviour; both pass on HEAD as on this tree.

## Left

* The ruling's example marks the second `import` line itself as the error
  ("`parse` imported twice", as Rust's E0252).  The compiler reports the
  collision at the bare use only, and not at all when the bare name is never
  used.  Refusing the import is a new diagnostic: a code and wording to be
  ruled before it is built.

### 8.431 A call on a bounded parameter reached through an index, a field or a trait default's copy names the bound's method - 2026-09-29

## Why

Ruling 33 (Jake, plain text, 2026-09-29; recorded in
`docs/resolution-rules.md`'s appendix with rulings 31-39): the
inherent-beside-trait ambiguity of 8.427 refuses a correct program.  A type
with an inherent `equals` beside its `Eq` impl could not call
`Array::index_of`: the call `this.ptr[i].equals(value)`, written under the
method's `where T: Eq`, carried no bound, was selected again by name after
monomorphization and met the tie.  The bound is recorded on the call from
every `where` level and from associated-type bounds.

## Measured before

* The design session's control (`.objcmp/mono-design/controls/r25`, copied to
  `.objcmp/s81/r25`): E0156 "`equals` is both an inherent method of `Q` and
  provided by a trait implemented for it" at `stdlib/collections/array.cryo:260`.
* The bound scan (`lookup_method_through_param_bounds`) already reads the
  function's, the impl's and the owner declaration's clauses and projection
  bounds.  It was never asked: in the pre-monomorphization walk the receiver
  had no type.  Probe (throwaway) over the corpus (141 builds; before
  `.objcmp/s81/bpb.out`): 113 method-call sites whose receiver the symbolic
  walk left untyped, 332 sites stamped with a bound.  Two refusals account
  for most: `resolve_array_access` returned no type for any base mentioning
  a type parameter, though a pointer's pointee and an array's element do not
  depend on it (`this.ptr[i]` on a `T*`), and `resolve_member_access` did
  the same for a field of an instantiation not yet minted (`node.key` on an
  `Entry<K, V>*`), which the field door answers.
* A third shape, found testing the associated-type case: an iterator of such
  a type calling `min()` was E0156 at `stdlib/core/iter.cryo:181` and `:202`
  (`value.compare(&best)` under `where This::Item: Ord`).  The trait's own
  walk stamps that call `Ord`; each implement block's COPY of the default is
  cloned before sema and walked with a concrete receiver, without the stamp.

## What changed

* `resolve_array_access`: the built-in rules (pointer, array, tuple) answer
  first; a base mentioning a type parameter is left untyped only when they
  fail and an `Index` overload would be needed.
* `resolve_member_access`: a field of a receiver mentioning a type parameter
  is answered by the field door (the template's field through the
  arguments); untyped only when the door has none.
* `MethodBinding::default_copy_bound_direction`: in an implement block's copy
  of a trait default, a receiver whose type is what a copied projection
  bound's subject (`This::Item`) denotes for the implementing type is
  directed by that bound; `bind_method_on_receiver` stamps it before
  selecting.  The trait-chain lookup it needs is shared with
  `scan_projection_bounds` (`bound_trait_declaring`), so the lane count does
  not move.

## Evidence

* Corpus after (`.objcmp/s81/bpc.out`): every build's outcome and error lines
  identical to before; untyped receivers 113 -> 11 (102 typed, none new);
  stamped sites 332 -> 364, none removed.  The 32 new: the design session's
  group A (`array.cryo:260, 670, 701, 719`; `hashmap.cryo:309, 336, 370, 428,
  477`), the associated-type copies (`iter.cryo:181, 202`, and the test
  `trait_default_primitive_item.cryo:27`, its own `This::Item: Zap`), the
  bounds `Clone`/`Eq`/`Hash`/`Allocator`/`Display`/`Debug` on the same index
  and field shapes, and ten `.drop()` calls on elements and fields named
  `Drop::drop` (the recursion inside a `Drop` impl that monomorphization's
  annotator stamped the same way).  The 11 left are call results
  (`value.compare(&best).is_lt()`, `raw.cast::<F>().as_ptr()`) - concrete
  receivers the symbolic walk does not reach, not a bound question.
* `bound_call_through_index_field_projection` (run, exit 0): a type with an
  inherent `equals` and `compare` beside `Eq`/`Ord`/`Hash` through
  `index_of`, `sort`, `HashMap::get`, `Iterator::min` and `max`.  HEAD refuses
  it (E0156 at `iter.cryo:181, 202`); declared in `tests/started-compiling`.
* Inversion, each piece reverted alone, the unmutated compiler as control
  (`.objcmp/s81/inv.sh`, `inv.log`): control builds and exits 0; index
  reverted -> E0156 at `array.cryo:260, 670, 701, 719`; field reverted ->
  E0156 at `hashmap.cryo:309, 336, 370, 428, 477`; default copies reverted ->
  E0156 at `iter.cryo:181, 202`.
* Gate movements: residue 241 -> 242, one class L site (the copy rule's
  context, built with an empty name); name-taking 709 -> 711 (the two new
  functions); lane and flow unchanged.
* verify moves one object, `CryoTests/Tests/Lang/AsyncTraitMethod.o`, by
  two function bodies and not by order: the `poll` of
  `atm_hold_and_drain<AtmTicker>`'s and of
  `atm_default_body_on_generic_owner<AtmTicker>`'s futures each gain one call,
  `Option<AtmHolder<AtmTicker>>::take` (disassembly of both builds'
  objects, `.objcmp/s82/`).  The async lowering releases a local it carries
  across an `await` at each completing `return`, hoisting the returned
  value first; it skips the release when that value has no type, and the
  local then lives until the finished future is dropped.  `return b * 100 +
  h.seen` with `h: AtmHolder<S>` had none before monomorphization, because
  `h.seen` is a field of an instantiation not yet minted - the field change
  above types it.  The release at the `return` is the lowering's intended
  behaviour, the one a function without suspends has; the skip was its
  fallback.  `async_carried_local_released_at_return` (run) observes the
  order: HEAD's program logs 231 (released with the future), this change's
  213 (released at the return); declared in `tests/started-passing`.

## Left

* The design session's other groups (B `.drop()` on an unbounded parameter,
  ruling 14's intrinsic; D concrete receivers pre-mono typing cannot reach;
  F2's `view.fmt(f)` inside `Debug for String`, ruling 31) are its slices.

### 8.432 A path through a bounded parameter is directed by sema, by the bound that declares its member - 2026-09-30

## Why

Slice 2 of the monomorphizer plan (`.objcmp/mono-design/DESIGN.md`): the
dispatch annotator, a pass run between sema and monomorphization, wrote two
trait stamps sema did not.  Its second rule directed `T::m(..)` - `T` a
parameter with exactly one bound - to that bound's trait.  This entry moves
that rule into sema, where the method-call form already is (8.427, 8.431),
and deletes it from the annotator.

## Measured before

* Probe (throwaway, `.objcmp/s82/annprobe.patch`; corpus of every test
  project and example, the unit suite and the compiler's own sources,
  `.objcmp/s82/c1/sites.txt`): the path rule stamped 11 sites -
  `varargs.cryo:76` `T::__pluck` (108 builds), `T::default()` in two unit
  tests, a fixture's `T::setup()`, the five shapes of
  `bound_directed_static_path`, `impl_static_return_through_head`'s
  `T::make()` and `examples/09-json-config`'s `T::try_from`.  Each is a
  parameter with one bound whose
  own trait declares the member, so sema's rule gives each the same trait.
* Sema left `T::m()` untyped and unstamped before monomorphization
  (`resolve_scope_call` returned at `symbolic_scope_is_generic_param`).
* The rules differ where a parameter has two bounds of which one declares
  the member (the annotator wrote nothing), or one bound whose SUPERTRAIT
  declares it (the annotator wrote the subtrait, whose implementation
  delivers nothing).  Both were refused at the instantiation for a type
  providing the member through two traits: E0156 "`make` is provided by
  more than one trait implemented for `P`".

## What changed

* `CallResolver::direct_param_path`: a path whose scope segment is a
  parameter in scope for the symbolic walk takes, as `resolved_trait`, the
  trait `MethodBinding::abstract_receiver_method_return` notes - the scan
  a call `x.m()` on a receiver of that parameter reads: every `where`
  level, supertraits nearest first, two traits answering leave it
  undirected.  Called from `resolve_scope_call` (the call) and
  `resolve_scope_resolution` (the value, `T::make`).  A head the writer
  qualified is left alone.
* `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_scope_param_type`: the parameter's abstract
  type, by the segment's stamp.
* `mono/dispatch_annotator.cryo`: the path rule, `single_bound_trait_for`
  and the bound lists threaded through every walker for it are deleted.
  The annotator keeps its other rule (below).

## Evidence

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-000311`): 0 of 4337 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; census, examples, lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow OK; the
  fast gate's only refusal was the flow list, re-written below.  Clean
  build: 344 warnings, the same set.
* Inversion: with `direct_param_path` returning at once (and the annotator
  rule already gone), `bound_directed_static_path` is refused - E0156 at
  `main.cryo:33` (impl-level bound), `:37`, `:41` (function bounds), `:45`
  (`T::go(t)`), `:49` (`T::make` as a value); the unmutated compiler builds
  it and exits 19.
* `bound_path_names_declaring_trait` (run, exit 0): `where T: Beta + Named`
  and `where T: Sub` (`Sub : Gamma`); HEAD refuses both (E0156 at
  `main.cryo:44` and `:49`); declared in `tests/started-compiling`.
* Flow list 795 -> 796: the path's member leaf joins the bound scan's
  existing sink through `direct_param_path`.  `subject_sym` 25 -> 24.

## Left

* The annotator's other rule - a call named like the enclosing trait-impl
  method is directed to that impl's trait - still stands.  It stamps 549
  sites over the same corpus: 448 `poll` calls the async lowering
  generates inside a future's `Future` impl, 92 `.drop()` calls, and 9
  others; 21 of the 549 were already pinned by sema.  Deleting it needs
  `view.fmt(f)` at `stdlib/fmt/display.cryo:507` rewritten as
  `(Debug for Str)::fmt(&view, f)` (ruling 31), and that form does not
  compile inside a generic method: "error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve
  'Str::fmt'".  The explicit path of a generic trait method binds its
  specialization only when its caller is not generic: in a generic body sema
  writes no pin before monomorphization and the substituter drops every
  callee pin a clone carries, so monomorphization's path branch has nothing
  to specialize.  The same defect leaves `this.s.go(w)` - a generic trait
  method on a concrete receiver inside an impl's generic method - calling
  the unspecialized template (LLVM "Incorrect number of arguments").
  Controls: `.objcmp/s82/r31b`, `r31d`, `r31e`, `r31f`, `dbgs`.

### 8.433 The trait-impl head table is keyed by the trait's definition - 2026-09-30

## Why

Slice 3 of the monomorphizer plan gives trait items an identity; impl
selection (`TraitChecker::select_impl` over `GenericRegistry::heads_for`)
is where a trait item is mapped to an impl, and its table was keyed by
`(defs.path_of(trait).id << 32) | target` - the text id of the trait's path
standing in for the trait (rule four).

## What changed

* `GenericRegistry::trait_impl_key` takes the trait's position in the
  definition table (`DefTable::slot`, which refuses an id another table
  made) where it took its path's interned id.  Registration and selection
  both go through it.

## Evidence

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-001938`): 0 of 4391 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; every gate OK but `fast`, whose one refusal was the
  `DEFID_PATH` row re-pinned here.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set.
* Lane `DEFID_PATH` 49 -> 48 (`generic_registry.cryo` 10 -> 9), golden
  re-pinned.  The spelling-flow list does not list this key: the flow check
  does not follow a path id through arithmetic into a map key, so its
  silence here was never evidence.

## Measured, not built: an inherent `drop` and `where T: Drop`

Ruling 32 says an inherent `drop` does not satisfy `where T: Drop`.  Today
`TraitChecker::type_implements_trait` answers `Drop` with
`has_inherent_drop` when no impl head exists for the type.

* Who relies on it (throwaway probe on that branch,
  `.objcmp/s82/dropprobe.patch`; every test project and example, the unit
  suite, the compiler's sources, and the editor built in place): four
  types, all in the unit suite - `RcT::Payload` (20 answers),
  `RcT::InlineDropRc` (3), `BoxT::InlineDropBox` (1),
  `IterFindFilterReleaseOnce::Item` (1).  None in the standard library,
  the examples, the compiler or the editor.
* Built and reverted (`.objcmp/s82/ruling32-inherent-drop.patch`: the
  branch deleted, the four types moved into `implement trait Drop`).  It
  does not refuse anything; it makes a working program leak:

  ```cryo
  type struct Counted {
      n: i32*;
      drop(mut &this) -> void { *this.n = *this.n + 1; }
  }
  function main() -> i32 {
      mut count: i32 = 0;
      { mut b: Box<Counted> = Box::new(Counted { n: &count }); }
      return count;   // parent: 1; with the branch deleted: 0, and no diagnostic
  }
  ```

  The containers' destructors are conditional impls
  (`implement<T> trait Drop for Box<T> where T: Drop`); a payload that no
  longer satisfies the bound leaves the box with no destructor at all.
  The ruling holds without a silent leak only once a container releases
  its payload through `std::core::ptr::drop_in_place<T>` with no `Drop`
  bound (ruling 14, the plan's slice 4), where an inherent destructor is
  the payload's drop code like any other.  So it lands with slice 4.

### 8.434 A path naming a trait implementation's generic method runs inside a generic body, and the dispatch annotator is deleted - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 31: a method two traits provide, called on a concrete receiver
inside an implementation of one of them, is E0156 - the enclosing impl's
trait does not choose.  The monomorphizer's dispatch annotator made it
choose (its one remaining rule: a call named like the enclosing trait-impl
method is stamped with that impl's trait), and `Debug for String`
(`stdlib/fmt/display.cryo:507`, `view.fmt(f)` on a `Str`, which has both
`Display::fmt` and `Debug::fmt`) relied on it.  The explicit form the
ruling asks for, `(Debug for Str)::fmt(&view, f)`, was E0636 "cannot
resolve 'Str::fmt'" inside a generic method.  Three causes, each measured
with a probe (`.objcmp/s83/unit2-with-probes.patch`) on
`.objcmp/s83/r31e`:

1. Sema's symbolic walk of the template selected no entry: the
   parameter types of a generic method's entry (`static_entry_params`)
   were refused when they mentioned any type parameter, so `w: W` (the
   caller's own parameter) matched nothing (`fits=0`).
2. The substituter dropped `resolved_method` on every clone.
3. Mono's path branch read the receiver's type off the first argument,
   which a clone carries untyped.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::static_entry_params`: in a template's symbolic walk a
  parameter bound to an enclosing parameter stays abstract, as a
  turbofish's already did (`solve_method_bindings_at`).
* `ASTTypeSubstituter::template_path_method_crosses`: a path call's
  `resolved_method` crosses the substitution when it is a generic method's
  template (own type parameters left) on an owner its receiver names
  without a type parameter.  `resolved_type_args` is substituted as
  before; the final pin is still dropped.  A sibling's specialization, or
  a generic owner's method, is dropped as before.
* `MonoCallSpecializer::specialize_method_call`: a path call's receiver
  is the pinned method's own receiver parameter
  (`receiver_param_type`); a generic owner's is not specialized there.
* `display.cryo:507` is `(Debug for Str)::fmt(&view, f)`.
* `mono/dispatch_annotator.cryo` (292 lines) and its per-module pass in
  `CompilerInstance` are deleted.  With it goes a whole load of every
  module before monomorphization.

```cryo
type trait Aa { go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32; }
type trait Bb { go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32; }
// S implements both.
implement trait Bb for T2 {
    go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32 { return this.s.go(w); }             // was: Bb's, then LLVM "Incorrect number of arguments"; now E0156
    go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32 { return (Bb for S)::go(&this.s, w); } // was: E0636 "cannot resolve 'S::go'"; now runs Bb's
}
```

## Evidence

* verify, in two runs because the baseline compiler cannot build the
  rewritten `display.cryo`:
  - the compiler change alone, `display.cryo` and the annotator as at HEAD,
    `--baseline HEAD --require-identical` (`.verify/runs/20260930-012203`):
    0 of 4391 test and 0 of 1126 example objects moved;
    `impl_qualified_path_in_generic_method` refused by HEAD and built;
    every gate OK but `fast` (the §0 project row).
  - everything, against a scratch commit holding the compiler change and
    the rewrite with the annotator kept (`s83-scratch-baseline`,
    `.verify/runs/20260930-010946`): 0 of 4447 test and 0 of 1126 example
    objects moved, so deleting the annotator moved nothing; the baseline
    census failed `trait_impl_same_name_call_ambiguous` only; the tree's
    census failed `ProcessAsync::two_children_join_concurrently` only, the
    known load flake, which passed in the other run's tree census and
    alone (`cryo test two_children_join_concurrently`).
* Clean build: 344 warnings, the same set as HEAD's compared by (code,
  file, message).  check-fast OK.
* The old form under the new compiler is ruling 31's E0156:
  `error[E0156]: `fmt` is provided by more than one trait implemented for
  `Str`` at `display.cryo:507:16`.
* Inversion, each alone against an unmutated control that builds and exits
  0 (`.objcmp/s83/mutate.py`): dropping the template pin in the
  substituter, refusing enclosing parameters in `static_entry_params`, and
  reading the receiver off the argument each bring back
  `error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve 'Str::fmt'` on
  `impl_qualified_path_in_generic_method`.
* New projects: `impl_qualified_path_in_generic_method` (run; the path in
  a trait impl's generic method, an inherent generic method and a generic
  free function, two instantiations each, and `{:?}` of a `String`),
  declared in `tests/started-compiling`; `trait_impl_same_name_call_ambiguous`
  (E0156), declared in `tests/started-passing`.

## Not done

* The method form with ONE trait providing the name,
  `this.s.go(w)` inside an impl's generic method, still calls the
  unspecialized template (LLVM "Incorrect number of arguments";
  `.objcmp/s82/r31b`).
* The pin compiler (`bin/cryo`) cannot compile a program that formats a
  `String` with `{:?}` against this standard library (E0636 at
  `display.cryo:507`); neither the standard library archive nor the
  compiler instantiates it, so nothing needs a re-pin yet.

### 8.435 A call on a bounded parameter records which trait method it names by position, and each trait implementation maps positions to its methods - 2026-09-30

## Why

Slice 3 of the monomorphizer plan (`.objcmp/mono-design/DESIGN.md`): a
trait call on a type parameter has to reach the right implementation's
method after monomorphization without a name - (trait, concrete type) ->
implementation -> the method at the call's position in the trait.  Today
the answer is found by the member's name among the receiver's methods, in
sema's post-monomorphization selection and in mono's finder chain.

## What changed

* `MemberAccessNode.resolved_trait_slot`: beside the trait a bound stamps
  on a call (`resolved_trait`), the position of the method among the
  trait's declared ones, found by the leaf in the trait's declaration where
  the call is written (`CallResolver::stamp_trait_item` ->
  `GenericRegistry::trait_item_slot`).  Every stamp a bound, a trait
  default's copy or an operator's desugaring writes goes through it.  The
  language items' stamps (a `for` loop's `next`) carry none: they are
  settled before the traits are registered.
* `ImplBlockNode.trait_item_methods`: position in the trait -> index in the
  block's methods (the written method, or the copy of its default).  Filled
  once per block, the first time `GenericRegistry::trait_item_method` asks -
  the one place a trait's method is matched to an implementation's by
  name.  Not at registration: a block's module can be walked before its
  trait's module registers the trait (see "Found" below).
* `MethodNode.spec_of`: a method specialization the monomorphizer mints
  names the generic method it was made from.
* The reader: `CallResolver::check_trait_item_table`.  When sema selects a
  trait's method by name for a stamped call on a concrete receiver, the
  table's answer - the implementation `select_trait_impl(trait, type)`
  picks, then its method at the recorded position - must be the method
  chosen or the method it is a specialization of; otherwise E0900.  No
  other reader yet: slice 6's monomorphizer mapping is the one that will
  use the table instead of a name.

```cryo
type trait Show { s_a(&this) -> i32; s_b(&this) -> i32; s_c(&this) -> i32 { return this.s_a() * 100; } }
type struct P { v: i32; }
implement trait Show for P { s_b(&this) -> i32 { return 2; } s_a(&this) -> i32 { return 1; } }
function via_bound<T>(x: &T) -> i32 where T: Show { return x.s_b() + x.s_c(); }
// x.s_b() records (Show, 1); for T = P: Show's impl for P -> table[1] = methods[0], `s_b`.
// x.s_c() records (Show, 2); table[2] = the copy of the default in P's impl.
```

## Evidence

* Corpus probe (`.objcmp/s83/unit1-probe.patch`, every test project and
  example and the unit suite, 145 builds; `.objcmp/s83/c2`): 32,752 stamped
  calls checked, 32,740 the same method and 12 a specialization of it
  (`fmt<W>`/`hash<H>` specializations appended to a non-generic impl,
  which the name selection picks over their template), 0 different, 0 with
  no implementation or no table entry; 43 carry no position, all a `for`
  loop's `next`.  The compiler's own sources build under the check
  (`cryo build` of `compiler/`, 344 warnings).
* Control by inversion (`.objcmp/s83/mutate1.py`): with each table built in
  the trait's reverse order, the build without the check exits 0 and runs;
  with it, `error[E0900]: `s_c` was selected by name as a trait's method,
  and the method table of the implementation the trait and the receiver
  select answers a different one` at each `x.s_c()`.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-024410`): 0 of 4447 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set.
* Lane `REGISTRY_READ` 12 -> 13 (`stamp_trait_item`'s lookup); spelling
  flow +2 and residue +3 J rows, all the stamp-site lookup and the
  registration match.

## Measured, not built

* Mono's finder chain, probed where its answer is used (`.objcmp/s83/c4`):
  164 agree with the table; 16 at one site (`key.hash(hasher)`,
  `stdlib/collections/hashmap.cryo:774`, for `String<GlobalAlloc>` and
  `Array<i32>`) do not.  The chain answers the owner specialization's copy
  of `hash<H>`; the table, asked at that moment, answers the TEMPLATE
  impl's copy of the same declaration (`select_trait_impl` returned the
  template head: the placed clone was not registered as a head yet,
  inferred).  Slice 6's mapping has to go through the owner
  specialization's placed clone by position, as the design says.  A
  mono-side check is not landed for this reason.
* A self-returning default through a bound (`it.take(2)` under
  `where I: Iterator`) agrees with the table (control `.objcmp/s83/srd`)
  but never occurs in the corpus.  The table reaches those defaults by
  position in the block, so they need no declaration-index entry for it;
  their entries (107 have none) are still missing for door-driven
  selection.

## Found

* A trait implementation whose module is walked before its trait's module
  gets none of the trait's default methods copied in:
  `synthesize_default_trait_methods` asks `get_trait_decl` before the trait
  is registered.  Two in the corpus: `implement trait Eq for struct W` in
  `bound_call_names_bound_method` and `implement trait Allocator for struct
  Arena` (`stdlib/alloc/arena_alloc.cryo:33`), seen in the build of
  `bound_call_names_bound_method`.  `Eq` has no default; `Allocator` has
  one, `reallocate`, which that build's `Arena` implementation did not
  receive.  Not followed further: whether anything calls `reallocate` on
  an `Arena` through the trait in such a build is untested.

### 8.436 A trait method reached through a field inside a generic body is specialized, and a trait's method is matched by name only through a door - 2026-09-30

## Why

Two pieces the monomorphizer plan needed before its later slices, both
ruled in plain text on 2026-09-30 (rulings 40-48 recorded in
`docs/resolution-rules.md` with this entry).

1. `this.s.go(w)` - a trait implementation's generic method on a concrete,
   non-generic receiver reached through a FIELD, inside any generic body -
   called the unspecialized template and failed LLVM verification.  In the
   clone the cloner resets the receiver expression's type, so
   `MonoCallSpecializer::specialize_method_call` re-derives it and then
   returned at the guard meant for a receiver that is a generic type's
   specialization; the guard was written as "not an inherent impl", so a
   trait impl on a non-generic owner was skipped too.
2. The position table of slice 3 (§8.435) matched an implementation's
   methods to its trait's by name in a second place beside the stamp's
   slot lookup.  The trait-method door is now the one place that happens.

## What changed

* `mono/call_specializer.cryo`: the guard also requires the re-derived
  receiver to be a generic type's specialization
  (`this.arena.inst_generic_base(recv_type).is_valid()`); a trait impl on a
  non-generic receiver is specialized from the call like an inherent one.
* Door `trait-method`, `GenericRegistry::trait_item_slot` (trait identity +
  leaf -> position among the trait's declared methods), marked and listed
  in the door table.  `GenericRegistry::fill_trait_item_table` places each
  of the block's methods through it, the first method of a position keeping
  it; it no longer scans the trait's declarations by name itself.

```cryo
type trait Bb { go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32; }
type struct S { v: i32; }
implement trait Bb for S { go<W>(&this, w: W) -> i32 { return this.v + sizeof(W) as i32; } }
type struct T2 { s: S; }
function via_free<W>(t: &T2, w: W) -> i32 { return t.s.go(w); }
// before: error[E0900]: LLVM module verification failed ... Incorrect number of
//         arguments passed to called function!
// after:  via_free(&t, 4 as u8) == 11, via_free(&t, 3 as i64) == 18
```

## Evidence

* New project `trait_method_through_field_in_generic_body` (run, exit 0):
  the call from a trait implementation's generic method, an inherent one
  and a free function, two instantiations each told apart by `sizeof(W)`.
  Declared in `tests/started-compiling`.
* Control by inversion (`.objcmp/s84/mut_guard.py`): the tree with the
  guard line alone reverted, built with `cryo build --build-dir=`, refuses
  the project with `LLVM reports: Incorrect number of arguments passed to
  called function!` (exit 1); the unmutated tree built the same way builds
  it and it exits 0.
* The doors check refused the marked `trait_item_slot` before the table row
  existed (`` `trait_item_slot` is marked as door `trait-method` and
  docs/resolution-rules.md lists no such door ``) and accepts it after: 12
  door functions, 11 doors.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-085104`): 0 of 4447 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; the declared project baseline exit 1, tree exit 0; every
  gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set as the baseline
  compiler's.  The compiler's own sources build with the new compiler.
* Spelling flow 798 -> 796 (the stamp's slot scan is a door's now, and the
  filler's scan is gone); residue 245 -> 244, J 168 -> 167 (the filler's
  `ImplBlockNode::methods[]` match); doors list 12 -> 13 lines; projects
  130 -> 131.

### 8.437 A module-qualified generic call records its template by the callee's definition, and the monomorphizer's scoped finder is deleted - 2026-09-30

## Why

Part of slice 5 of the monomorphizer plan (`.objcmp/mono-design/DESIGN.md`,
finding F7): every module-qualified generic call - `mem::swap(&a, &b)`,
`mem::offset(p, i)`, `Helpers::pick(x, y)` - reached the monomorphizer with
no template recorded, and `MonoCallSpecializer::find_scoped_function_template`
looked the template up again by the member's leaf inside the module the
path's segment names.  A bare generic call already records its template
where sema checks it (`call.resolved_template`); a qualified one did not,
although sema found the same template, by the same leaf, a few lines
earlier.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::resolve_module_qualified_function` takes the template by
  the definition the name layer bound the member to
  (`GenericRegistry::template_of(callee)`, where `callee` is the segment's
  `member_def`), not by the leaf inside the segment's module
  (`template_in(Def(module), member_name)`), and records it on the call
  (`call.set_resolved_template(tmpl.base_type)`), as the bare path does.
* `specialize_free_call` reads that record and nothing else for a call
  whose scope names a module.  `find_scoped_function_template` and
  `scoped_template_from_stamp` are deleted.

```cryo
import std::core::mem;
function main() -> i32 {
    mut a: i32 = 1; mut b: i32 = 2;
    mem::swap(&a, &b);   // before: mono found `swap` by its leaf in std::core::mem
    return a;            // after:  sema recorded the template of the definition `mem::swap` names
}
```

## Evidence

* Probe before converting (`.objcmp/s84/probe_u3.py`, corpus
  `.objcmp/s84/c3`: every test project and example, 145 builds, and the
  unit suite): at every module-qualified call to a generic function, the
  template by the callee's definition and the template by the leaf in the
  module are the same entry - 27,709 checks (9,909 before mono, 17,800
  after), 0 different, 0 found by one only.  The scoped finder answered
  13,569 calls over 454 sites (and 28,155 times answered nothing, for a
  non-generic function); every one of the 454 sites had sema's record, 0
  without.  4,024 scoped calls already reached mono with a recorded
  template (generic static methods).  DESIGN measured 16,576 over 457
  sites with the compiler's own build in its corpus; this corpus leaves it
  out.
* Inversion (`.objcmp/s84/mut_guard.py`, mode u3; scratch project
  `.objcmp/s84/mq` calling `mem::swap(&a, &b)` and a generic function of
  its own module, `Helpers::pick(..)`): the HEAD compiler - finder, no
  record - builds it and it exits 0; the new tree with the new
  `set_resolved_template` line alone removed - no finder, no record -
  refuses it: `error[E0636]: codegen: cannot resolve 'mem::swap'` and
  `'Helpers::pick'`; the new tree builds it and it exits 0.  With the
  finder in place the record's absence was invisible.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-094117`): 0 of 4501 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set.
  The compiler's own sources build with the new compiler.
* Lane `REGISTRY_READ` 13 -> 11 (the two `template_in` asks, re-pinned in
  `tests/lane-baseline.txt`); residue 244 -> 242, J 167 -> 165; name-taking
  functions 712 -> 710; pending allows 517 -> 515; `require_scope_res(`
  21 -> 20; `.require(Text::new("` 28 -> 27.  The spelling flow does not
  move (796): it does not see `template_in`, whose key is composed
  (`member_template_key`).

## Measured, not built: the calls the async lowering generates

Ruling 36 says the async lowering pins the calls it generates itself.
Measured (`.objcmp/s84/probe_async.py`, corpus `.objcmp/s84/c1`, figures
in `.objcmp/s84/unit2-measure.txt`): at each `.await` the lowering
(`AsyncLower::method_call0`/`method_call1`) writes six method calls -
`Option::take`, `Option::unwrap_ptr`, `Option::unwrap`, `Poll::is_pending`,
`Poll::into_ready` and the sub-future's `Future::poll` - 551 generated call
spans in the corpus.  Every one is selected by name after monomorphization
(10,392 selections, plus 1,304 re-visits of a call already bound), and none
before it (0) - in a non-generic async body as well as a generic one, where
DESIGN's F6 counted only cloned calls (89 sites).

Not built, because the pin has nothing to name the methods by: a method
has no `DefId`.  The name layer stamps a definition on free functions and
types only (`resolver/name_resolution.cryo:226-405`); a probe at
`DeclarationIndex::register_methods_through` (`.objcmp/s84/probe_def.py`)
printed an invalid `def` for every `take`, `unwrap`, `unwrap_ptr`,
`is_pending`, `into_ready` and `poll` it registered.  So the language-item
table, which is how the plan said the lowering would name them, cannot
hold a method, and asking the member-function door for `Option`'s `take`
would build a name and look it up.  Left for a decision; the options are
in the handoff.

### 8.438 Every method is a definition of the type or trait that declares it - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 49: methods get `DefId`s, registered by the name layer like other
items, so compiler-generated code can name a method by identity (method
language items) instead of building a name to look up.  Until now the name
layer stamped a definition on free functions and types only; a method was
identified by its declaration node, its overload entry (owner, leaf and
signature) and, for a trait's method, its position among the trait's
methods.  The 765 methods written in trait declarations and implement
blocks did mint an id - through `declare_method`'s scope symbol - but with
the MODULE as parent and kind `Function`, stamped on nothing and read by
nothing; the 5,282 written in type bodies minted none.

## What changed

* `DefKind::Method`.  The name layer registers every method it walks, with
  its owner as parent, and stamps the id on the declaration (`func.def`):
  a type body's methods under the type (`NameResolver::define_body_methods`),
  a trait's declared methods under the trait, an implement block's methods
  - inherent or trait - under the type its head names, a primitive
  included (`NameResolver::impl_owner_def`).  The scope symbol
  `declare_method` makes carries the same id; `Resolver::is_definition`
  no longer registers a second, module-parented one.
* The two lowerings that create methods register them too: an async
  future's `poll` under the future, a closure's `call` and `drop` under the
  closure's struct.  One registration path for all of them,
  `CompilationContext::define_method`, which also keeps the declaration
  under the id (`DeclarationIndex::keep_method_decl` / `method_decl_of`).
* Not registered: a copy.  A trait default placed in an implementation and
  every monomorphized clone carry no id (the cloner copies none), so no
  instantiation is a definition.
* A primitive's definition is registered once, by whichever stage asks
  first (`DefTable::primitive`), and kept under its position in the
  primitive table (`ResBase::primitive_position`, now the ordered form of
  the `primitive` door; `is_primitive_spelling` is that position being
  present).  The name layer asks it for `implement i32 { .. }`; type
  declarations ask it for the primitive's type, where they registered it
  themselves before.
* The reader, and the agreement check: `DeclarationIndex::register_methods_through`,
  where the type layer files each method under the family (owner type,
  leaf), refuses a method whose definition disagrees - not a `Method`, a
  parent other than the owner's definition, another leaf, or registered
  for another node - as an internal compiler error.  The two sides answer
  "where does this method live" independently: the name layer from where
  the method is written, the index from the type the head or body
  resolved to.  A method's overload entry is kept under its definition
  (`entry_of_def` answers it), as a free function's is.

```cryo
type trait Bb { go(&this) -> i32; }             // Main::Bb::go, parent Bb
type struct S { v: i32; get(&this) -> i32 { return this.v; } }   // Main::S::get, parent S
implement trait Bb for S { go(&this) -> i32 { return 2; } }      // Main::S::go, parent S
implement i32 { twice(&this) -> i32 { return this * 2; } }       // i32::twice, parent i32
```

How the new id relates to what identified a method before: it names the
same declaration as the node (`method_decl_of(func.def)` is the node);
for a method of a non-generic owner it answers the overload entry
(`entry_of_def`), while a generic owner's methods have entries only per
instance, which carry no id; a trait's declared method has both an id and
its position among the trait's methods (`trait_item_slot`), not yet
linked; `MethodNode.spec_of` still links a method specialization to its
template by node.

## Evidence

* Census before the change (`.objcmp/s85/probe_census.py`, reverted): over
  the compiler and the standard library (`cryo check src/main.cryo`),
  5,282 methods in type bodies (107 constructors), 668 in implement blocks
  (194 inherent and 167 trait on declared types, 132 inherent and 175
  trait on primitives), 97 declared in traits (48 required, 49 with a
  default).  Over 145 project and example builds and the unit suite
  (`.objcmp/s85/c1`), no implement head named anything but a type or a
  primitive, and every one of the declaration index's method registrations
  - written, default copies, monomorphized placements, async futures,
  closures - carried no id.
* Control on the check (`.objcmp/s85/mut_owner.py`): a compiler that files
  a trait implementation's methods under the trait refuses
  `tests/tests/projects/trait_method_through_field_in_generic_body` with
  `internal compiler error: method `go` is registered on
  `TraitMethodThroughFieldInGenericBody::Main::S`, and its definition says

  101); the unmutated compiler builds it (exit 0).  The compiler's own

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-102920`): 0 of 4501 test and 0 of 1126 example
  objects moved; every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set as

* Lane `LOOKUP_LOCAL` stays 70; one `DefTable::register` call moved from
