### 8.439 The async lowering names the methods it calls by definition, and nothing selects them by name - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 36 (the async lowering pins the calls it generates) and ruling 49
(generated code names methods through method language items).  At every
`.await` the lowering writes six method calls - `Option::take`,
`Option::unwrap`, `Option::unwrap_ptr`, `Poll::is_pending`,
`Poll::into_ready` and the awaited future's `Future::poll` - by building
each method's leaf, and every one was selected by that leaf after
monomorphization: 10,392 selections over the corpus (8.437's measurement),
plus 13,239 passes through the monomorphizer's finder chain, which also
looks methods up by the member's leaf.

## What changed

* Six method language items: `OptionTake`, `OptionUnwrap`,
  `OptionUnwrapPtr`, `PollIsPending`, `PollIntoReady`, `FuturePoll`,
  claimed through the `lang-item` door where the type declarations claim
  the types, from each method's definition (8.438).  A method is claimed
  only when it is written in the module that declares its owner
  (`PassRegistry::claim_method_items`), so an implementation elsewhere
  that gives `Option` a method of the same path is never the one generated
  code calls.
* `AsyncLower::method_call0`/`method_call1` take the item, not a name, and
  write its definition on the call (`CallExprNode.named_method`, carried by
  the cloner, never cleared).  The member is the method's leaf, for
  printing only.  An item no declaration claimed is an E0900 where the
  lowering needs it.
* `FunctionDeclNode.copy_of`: the definition a copy stands for - a
  monomorphized clone's template, an implementation's copy of a trait
  default - set by the cloner and carried through further copies.  It
  registers nothing: a copy is still no definition.  The declaration index
  keeps each owner's copies by that identity
  (`DeclarationIndex::method_entry_on(owner, def)`: the definition's own
  entry when it is declared on the owner, else the owner's copy).  A
  specialization of a generic method is not kept there: it is an
  instance, the definition and its own type arguments.
* The binding after monomorphization (`CallResolver::bind_named_method`,
  reached from `bind_method_on_receiver` after the receiver is unwrapped)
  maps the definition to the receiver's method by identity: a trait's
  declared method through the implementation selected by (trait, type) and
  the method's position (`GenericRegistry::trait_item_position`, by
  definition); any other through `method_entry_on`.  No name is asked.  A
  receiver still written in a generic body's parameters is left for the
  copies that substitute them, as the name path left it; a concrete
  receiver without the method is E0900.  The monomorphizer's
  `specialize_method_call` returns at once for such a call: what it
  specializes is a method's own type parameters, and no item has any.

```cryo
async function relay(f: Fut) -> i64 { return await f; }
// lowered, at the await - before: `sub.poll(cx)` selected by the leaf `poll`;
// after: the call carries Future::poll's definition, bound to Fut's
// `implement trait Future for Fut` method at poll's position in Future.
```

## Evidence

* Probe (`.objcmp/s85/probe_named.py`, reverted), marking each call the
  lowering builds independently of `named_method`; corpus
  `.objcmp/s85/c2` (145 project and example builds and the unit suite):
  10,392 post-monomorphization visits of lowered calls not yet bound (the
  figure 8.437 measured as selections by name), all 10,392 through the
  identity binding - 9,183 bound, 1,209 on a receiver still in a generic
  body's parameters and left for its copies; 0 reached the selection by
  name; 0 found no method; 0 visits before monomorphization.  Build
  outcomes and errors identical to 8.437's corpus, build for build.
* Control on the probe (`.objcmp/s85/mut_unnamed.py`): the same probe on a
  compiler whose lowering does not write `named_method` counts 49
  selections by name and 0 by identity on
  `async_carried_local_released_at_return`; the change counts 0 and 49.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-110723`): every gate OK; 6 of 4501 test objects
  moved (`AsyncGenericFunction.o`, `AsyncReceiverRefresh.o`,
  `FutureCombinator.o`, and the projects
  `async_carried_local_released_at_return`, `generic_caller_receiver_args`,
  `impl_field_method_through_receiver`), 0 of 1126 examples.  All six are
  emission order only: the three projects' IR compared as multisets of
  definitions, each reference to a private constant replaced by its
  contents (`.objcmp/s85/llset.py`; a copy with one reference repointed is
  reported different), and the three unit objects function by function
  with `.rdata` references resolved to their bytes
  (`.objcmp/s85/objset.py`): 0 differing functions, 0 missing.  Cause,
  measured: the same tree without the monomorphizer's early return builds
  those three projects to IR byte-identical to HEAD's
  (`.objcmp/s85/var_mono.py`).  The finder chain run on the lowered `poll`
  was what first reached the awaited future's `poll` specialization; in
  `generic_caller_receiver_args` that definition is now emitted later, and
  nothing else moves.  Programs' output unchanged.  Clean build 344
  warnings, the same set.
* Name-taking functions 713 -> 711 (`method_call0`, `method_call1`).  Lane,
  residue and spelling flow unchanged.

### 8.440 A second explicit import of an already-imported name is refused at the import (E0243) - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 47 (the code and primary line approved as ruling 50): a second import
bringing in an already-imported name is refused at the import line itself,
as Rust refuses a second `use` (E0252).  Until now two brace entries naming
one leaf from two modules bound nothing wrong at the import and were
refused at each bare USE (E0154), and the same declaration imported twice
was accepted silently.

## What changed

* E0243 (`E0243_NAME_IMPORTED_TWICE`): "`parse` is imported twice", the
  label "`parse` is imported again here" on the second import, the note
  "first imported here" on the first.  The second import binds nothing;
  the first stays the name's, so the bare uses after it report nothing
  more, and a qualified path names its own module's item as before.
* Explicit only: a brace entry against an earlier brace entry, in the same
  namespace - another module's item of the leaf, or the same item again
  (also by another path, `std::test::{ TestError }` beside
  `std::test::error::{ TestError }`).  Wildcards keep their use-site
  ambiguity (E0154), and a brace entry after a wildcard is unchanged.
* `Resolver::declare_import` takes `explicit` and answers the earlier
  explicit binding when it refuses; it reads the name's bindings once and
  answers both of its questions from them (whether one names the target,
  whether an explicit entry already holds the namespace), which deletes
  `import_target_in` and its pending allow.  `Resolver.explicit_imports`
  records the bindings brace entries made.  The name layer reports
  (`NameResolver::refuse_repeated_import`), once per name per import.
* NOT emitted: ruling 47's help, "remove one of the imports, or import one
  under another name with `as`".  The grammar has no `as` for an imported
  item (`ImportForm` aliases only a whole path), and
  `import R47::Toml::parse as tparse;` is refused (`E0500: cannot find
  module `R47::Toml::parse``), so the help would send people to a form
  that does not exist.  Left for a decision.
* Tests: new project `import_twice_refused_at_import` (two modules' `parse`
  and `Doc`, one module's `shape` imported twice: three E0243 at lines 6, 6
  and 7, nothing at the uses).  `import_collision_bare_use_refused` (was
  E0154 at the bare use) and `import_collision_qualified_use` (was a run
  project, exit 0) are E0243 at the second import now, the qualified uses
  still reporting nothing; the run-time check that `Toml::parse` answers
  Toml's `parse` beside a colliding import is gone with the program that
  made it.  The negatives `E0154_ambiguous_bare_call` and
  `E0154_ambiguous_bare_type_annotation` collided through brace entries and
  collide through wildcards now, keeping E0154's two shapes.  The unit test
  `lang/generic_static_owner_binding.cryo` imported `TestError` and
  `expect_eq` twice (a generator's leftover); the second imports are
  deleted.  `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 states the rule.

```cryo
import Json::{ parse };
import Toml::{ parse };              // error[E0243]: `parse` is imported twice
const b: i32 = Toml::parse("1");     // Toml's `parse`, as before
```

## Evidence

* Population before building (`.objcmp/s85/probe_imports.py`, reverted),
  every import binding that meets an import binding of its name in the same
  namespace: compiler and standard library - 0 brace-after-brace, 4,189
  brace entries after a wildcard naming the same item, 2 wildcard pairs;
  145 project and example builds (`.objcmp/s85/c3`) - 3 brace-after-brace,
  all in the two `import_collision_*` projects; the unit suite, measured
  again with its build directory cleared - 2, both
  `generic_static_owner_binding.cryo`.  The corpus's unit leg first printed
  0 lines (a false zero - nothing was measured), and the compile-fail
  suite was not in the population at all: its two E0154 negatives were
  found by verify's census, not by the probe.
* Before and after on the new project: HEAD reports E0154 at each bare use
  (`parse` line 11, `Doc` line 13 twice) and accepts `shape` imported
  twice; the tree reports the three E0243 at the imports and nothing at a
  use.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-120946`): the baseline's census fails on exactly
  the three projects declared in `tests/started-passing`, the tree's
  passes; 0 of 4445 test objects (the declared projects' 56 left out) and
  0 of 1126 examples moved - `generic_static_owner_binding`'s object too,
  whose source lost two lines: predicted to move, it carries no line
  numbers.  Every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings, the same set.
* Roster re-pinned with `--update` (two rows changed, one added);
  `--merge` had kept both projects' old rows beside their new ones.
  Pending allows 515 -> 514, braced-import files 658 -> 657, projects
  131 -> 132.  Lane and spelling flow unchanged: the check's lookup is the
  one `declare_import` already made.

## Measured, not built: ruling 46

`const f = IgTn::go;` with an inherent `go` and a trait's `go`: for a STATIC
method the value is already E0156 (`const m = SNn::make;`: "`make` is both
an inherent method of `SNn` and provided by a trait implemented for it").
For a method with a receiver, `IgTn::go` in value position is not a method
value at all: it takes the OWNER's type (`const f: i32 = IgTn::go;` reports
"expected `i32`, found `R46::Main::IgTn`"), with or without a second `go`,
and `sema.cryo`'s `scope_static_method_type` says an instance method is not
a value on its own.  Whether a method with a receiver is a value
(`(&IgTn, i32) -> i64`, as Rust's `fn` item is) is a language question left
for a decision; the ambiguity cannot be reported for a value the language
does not yet say exists.

### 8.441 Two call shapes in generic bodies are typed before monomorphization - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 35: a call sema cannot type before monomorphization gets its typing
completed, not looked up during monomorphization.  The monomorphizer plan's
conversion needs every call in a template body to carry a first-pass
answer (a pin, a selection on the template, or a bound's trait stamp).

## Measured first

A throwaway probe (`.objcmp/s86/probe.patch`, reverted) printed, for every
method call sema's first pass visits, whether it left an answer and whether
the walk was a template body's.  Corpus: the compiler, the tests tree,
every project, example and tool, and the unit suite (`.objcmp/s86/corpus.sh`,
151 builds; the compile-fail files are not in it - verify's census covers
them).  Control: the probe marks `main`'s calls `sym=0` and the template's
`sym=1` on a scratch project, and prints the answered and unanswered calls
of both.

Unanswered template-body calls at HEAD, by site (`c1/none-sym.txt`):

* `x.cast::<F>().as_ptr()` - 9 sites (`future/executor.cryo:697, 707`,
  `thread/_module.cryo:386, 393, 710`, `thread/local.cryo:127`,
  `sync/mpsc.cryo:144, 208`).  A method called with the body's own
  parameter as explicit argument returned no type: the explicit-argument
  typing resolved `F` in a context that binds no parameter, and gave up.
* `const { inner }: PathBuf<A> = this; inner.into_raw()` - 2 sites
  (`collections/string.cryo:260`, `fs/path.cryo:373`).  A destructure whose
  type names the body's parameter registered every binding as `void`.
* Not this unit: `.drop()` on an unbounded parameter (5 sites, the
  `drop_in_place` slice); function-pointer field calls (`iter.cryo:285`,
  `thread/local.cryo:128`), which are not method calls; `this.tids.push`
  on a `u64[]` field, a builtin array method that is unanswered in
  non-generic code too; `value.compare(&best)` in `Iterator::min`/`max`'s
  default copies, unanswered in some copies and stamped in others (below).
* The plan's own example, `inner_ptr.strong.fetch_add(..)` in
  `alloc/arc.cryo`, is already answered: the probe prints a selection on
  the template (`ans=sel`) at `arc.cryo:164`, `181` and `290`.

## What changed

* `MethodBinding::resolve_method_return_with_explicit_args`: in a template
  body, the explicit arguments and the return annotation are resolved with
  the body's parameters bound (`symbolic_bind_params`, which also makes the
  resolution demand-free), bound after the owner's so those win.  An
  argument naming the body's parameter types the return abstractly
  (`NonNull<F>`); an argument naming nothing still leaves the call untyped.
* `Sema::visit(DestructureDeclNode)`: in a template body, each binding is
  typed as its field seen through the destructured type, through the
  member-field door (`MemberResolver::field_of`), where it was `void`.  The
  shape checks (every field bound, none twice) stay with the
  specialization, as before.
* New run project `generic_body_calls_typed_before_mono` (both shapes).

```cryo
function via_explicit<F>(m: &Maker, f: F) -> F {
    return m.wrap::<F>(f).unwrap_v();   // was untyped; now Wrap<F>, `unwrap_v` selected
}
via_destructure(mut this) -> T {
    const { w, n }: Outer<T> = this;    // `w` was void; now Wrap<T>
    return w.unwrap_v();
}
```

## Evidence

* The same corpus with the change (`c2`): exactly the 11 sites leave the
  unanswered set, nothing else in it moves, and every build's exit code is
  the one it had.  On the scratch projects the probe shows the pair: at
  HEAD `unwrap_v` is `ans=none` at both shapes, with the change `ans=sel`.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-134241`): 0 of 4445 test objects and 0 of 1126
  examples moved; every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings.
* §0: projects 132 -> 133.  Lane and spelling flow unchanged: the
  destructure asks the member-field door, which is already a door.
* What remains of the plan's slice 5: `Iterator::min`/`max`'s
  `value.compare(&best)` in default copies whose `This::Item` bound does
  not stamp (3,840 unanswered visits against 2,701 stamped, 2 sites), and
  the `.drop()` sites, which the `drop_in_place` slice owns.

### 8.442 An import collision is recorded in the namespace it is in - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 56: types and values are separate namespaces.  A type `Tag` from
one module and a function `Tag` from another, both imported, were refused
at every use - E0154 at each type position, E0231 "`Tag` is a type, not a
function" at the call - because `Scope::insert_import` recorded a tie
between any two imports of one leaf from different modules, whatever their
namespaces, and kept only the first as the name's binding.

## What changed

* `Resolver::declare_import`: the import a new one competes with is the
  binding in the new target's namespace (`binding_beside`, which
  `explicit_binding_beside` became with an `explicit_only` flag, and
  `namespace_of`); with none there, another module's item of the leaf is a
  second binding of the name (`add_overload`), chosen by namespace at a
  lookup exactly as one module's type and function are
  (`Resolver::import_target`).
* The tie record carries its namespace (`Scope.ambig_ns`;
  `insert_import`, `is_ambiguous`, `get_ambiguous_module_ids` take it;
  `Resolver::is_ambiguous`, `get_ambiguous_modules`, `ambiguous_modules_from`
  too).  The value lane asks `Namespace::Value`, the type lane
  (`leaf_in_module_scope`) `Namespace::Type`, `resolve_path` its own `ns`.
  So two wildcards' types `Tag` refuse the type uses and leave a third
  module's function `Tag` callable, and the tie names the two TYPES'
  modules whichever import came first.
* E0243 was already namespace-aware (8.440); unchanged.
* Tests: run project `import_type_and_function_same_leaf` (brace entries
  type-then-function, wildcards function-then-type); compile-fail project
  `import_type_tie_beside_function_refused` (E0154 at the two type uses on
  line 9, nothing on line 8's call, no E0231); run project
  `qualified_path_beside_bare_import` (ruling 54: `Toml::parse(..)` beside
  a bare import of Json's `parse` calls Toml's, the bare `parse` Json's).
  `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 states the rule.

```cryo
import Shapes::{ Tag };           // a type
import Labels::{ Tag };           // a function
const t: Tag = Tag { id: 3 };     // was E0154 twice; Shapes's type
const n: i32 = Tag(4);            // was E0231; Labels's function
```

## Evidence

* Population: a probe at the new second-binding branch
  (`declare_import`, reverted) over the compiler, tests tree, every
  project, example and tool, and the unit suite (`.objcmp/s86/n1`, 151
  builds): **0** firings.  Control: the same probe prints the pair on the
  scratch project `.objcmp/s86/u2`.  No existing program changes; the
  compile-fail files are covered by verify's census.
* Before and after, scratch projects `.objcmp/s86/u2`-`u2h`: brace
  type-then-function, function-then-type, two wildcards, wildcard then
  brace - HEAD E0154 at each type use plus E0231 (or a third E0154) at the
  call, the tree exits 0; two types by wildcard beside a function - HEAD
  E0231 at the call, the tree only the two E0154; two types by brace -
  E0243 at both.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-141654`): the baseline's census fails on exactly
  the two declared projects (`tests/started-compiling`,
  `tests/started-passing`); 0 of 4555 test objects (the declared projects'
  57 left out) and 0 of 1126 examples moved.  Its `fast` gate refused two
  §0 rows this entry moves: the tie-refusal row's check now greps
  `is_ambiguous(node.name, Namespace::Value)` (1), and projects 133 -> 136;
  check-fast then refused braced-import files 657 -> 660 (the three new
  projects).

### 8.443 An import entry binds its declaration under an alias (`as`) - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 52: import aliasing, built on this branch despite the 2026-09-28
freeze - `import Toml::{ parse as toml_parse };` and
`import Toml::parse as toml_parse;` - with the alias naming the same
definition, and E0243's help suggesting it.  Before: the brace form was a
parse error (`E0100: expected '}', found 'as'`) and the single form was
`E0500: cannot find module `U3::Toml::parse``.

## What changed

* `ImportDeclNode.specific_aliases` (parallel to `specific_imports`, empty
  for no `as`; the cloner copies it); `add_specific_import(name, alias)`.
  The parser reads `Ident ("as" Ident)?` per brace entry of an `import` (an
  `export` takes none).
* `import A::B as C;` with two or more segments IS `import A::{ B as C };`:
  the parser builds that node, and discovery's scanner records `A` as the
  import and `A::B` as an entry, as it does for the brace form.  The one
  question an entry is already asked - an item `A` offers, else a
  sub-module of `A` - answers which the path names; no second lookup was
  added.  A one-segment path and an `export` stay a whole-module alias.
* Name layer (`process_import`, the brace branch): every declaration
  offered under the entry's name is bound under `bind_as` (the alias, or
  the name), with the declaration as its target - so the alias resolves by
  identity through `Resolver::import_target`, like any import.  A
  sub-module entry with an alias binds the module under the alias (as the
  whole-module alias does) instead of bringing in its exports.
* E0243 now carries ruling 47's help: "remove one of the imports, or import
  one under another name with `as`".  An alias is a name like any other:
  two entries binding one alias in one namespace are E0243.
* **Found and fixed on the way (a defect from 8.440):** a brace import of an
  OVERLOADED function was E0243 at its own single entry (`import
  U3::Json::{ conv };` with `conv(i32)` and `conv(i64)`: "`conv` is
  imported twice", at HEAD too).  `Resolver::declare_import` takes
  `check_repeat`; an entry checks only the first declaration it binds in
  each namespace against earlier imports, and its other declarations there
  join that binding.  None in the corpus (verify moved nothing).
* `docs/grammar.md` (`ImportEntry`), `docs/cryo.md` 14.3.

```cryo
import Json::{ parse };
import Toml::{ parse as toml_parse };   // was E0100
import Toml::twice as tw;               // was E0500
const a: i32 = parse("1") * 10 + toml_parse("1");   // 12
```

## Evidence

* Scratch programs (`.objcmp/s86/u3*`), each before (HEAD) and after:
  brace alias and single-form alias beside a bare import of the other
  module's `parse` (HEAD E0100 / E0500; after, exit 0); an aliased type
  with its static and a method, an aliased generic function with and
  without turbofish, an aliased overloaded family, a function value
  through an alias (exit 0); two entries aliasing `p` (E0243 with the
  help); an alias does not bring the original name in (`parse` alone is
  E0202).
* Behaviour change, measured: `import U3::Toml as T;` where `U3` is no
  module is now E0500 at the import ("cannot find module `U3`"), as
  `import U3::{ Toml };` is.  At HEAD it compiled and `T::parse(..)` was
  E0233 at the use - a whole-module alias does not work at a use at HEAD
  either way.  No file in the tree outside `legacy/` writes an import with
  `as` (`git ls-files '*.cryo' | xargs grep "^\s*\(import\|export\) [^;]* as "`).
* A first version added a lookup of the path's prefix in the name layer
  for the single form; it moved the lane gate (GRAPH_READ 46 -> 48), the
  approved-names count of `module_named`, the residue and the spelling
  flow.  Reading the single form as the brace form moved none of them.
* New projects: `import_alias_binds_same_item` (run; declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`), `import_alias_imported_twice` (compile-fail,
  E0243 and the help; declared in `tests/started-passing`).  §0: projects
  136 -> 138, braced-import files 660 -> 662.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-150639`): the declared projects fail the
  baseline and pass the tree; 0 of 4612 test objects (their 56 left out)
  and 0 of 1126 examples moved; every gate OK.  Clean build 344 warnings.
  The pin needs no re-pin: nothing it compiles writes `as` in an import.

### 8.444 Module aliases name the module, `import A::B as C;` refuses an item-and-module tie, and `export` entries take `as` - 2026-09-30

## Why

Rulings 57, 58 and 59 (recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md` with 60 and
61 in this commit).  Before: `import Json as J;` bound `J` to nothing a use
could reach (`J::twice(3)` E0233, `J::Tag` E0203, `J::LIMIT` E0201);
`import U1::Json as J;` with no module `U1` was E0500 at discovery; when
`A` offered an item `B` and `A::B` was a module the item was chosen
silently; an `export` entry's `as` was a parse error (E0100); and
`export M as F;` offered nothing to importers (E0502).

## What changed

* A module alias's binding carries the module's own `DefId` (the graph's
  `ModuleInfo.def`, read by the index `find_module_index` already
  answered).  `NameResolver::module_alias_match` reads the module off the
  binding - an `Import` whose definition is a `DefKind::Module` - and the
  three places a path's head is asked what module it names
  (`stamp_module_scope`, `walk_module_rooted_type`, `type_spelling_res`)
  take that answer for a head bound to an alias, and the module-spelling
  question for any other head; everything after the head is the same
  module-offering walk a spelled module gets.  No lookup was added.
* `ImportDeclNode.path_entry` marks `import A::B as C;` (still parsed as
  the entry `B` of `A`).  The prefix need not be a module: the loader's
  scanner records the entry's position (`import_entry_items`), an
  unresolved owner defers to the item loop, which already asks whether the
  entry is a module and reports E0500 for the whole path when it is not
  (`ModuleLoader::module_not_found`, E0500's builder, now shared).  In the
  name layer the sub-module question (`sub_module_index`) is asked of a
  path entry even when the prefix offers the item, and both answering is
  E0244 at the import, the alias bound to nothing.
* An alias spelled like another module the file imports is E0205 in
  `refuse_module_type_collisions`, which already refuses a type named like
  a module; an alias spelled like its own module is not a collision.  The
  modules are compared by `DefId`.
* `export M::{ f as g }`: the parser takes `as` in an export's brace
  entries.  The binding is made public and exported
  (`Resolver::export_symbol`); `Resolver::exports_named` and the three
  export-list walks hand a reader what an exported binding names
  (`Resolver::declaration_of`), never the binding, so no import chains
  through another.  An import binding records the module that declared
  its target in every branch (`osym.source_module`; the brace branch's
  `through_export` flag is gone), so two routes to one declaration never
  read as a tie.  `export M as F;` and `export A::{ Sub as S }` export the
  module alias.
* `docs/grammar.md`, `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 and 14.5.

```cryo
import Json as J;                 // J::twice(3), J::Tag::make(4), J::Kind::B, J::LIMIT
import U1::Json as J2;            // was E0500: `U1` is no module
import Shapes::Json as S;         // error[E0244] when `Shapes` declares `Json` too
export Fmt::{ printf as print };  // was E0100; importers get `print`
```

### 8.445 A qualified call to an overloaded function selects its signature, and an integer literal is `i32` among differing overloads - 2026-09-30

## Why

Rulings 60 and 61.  Before: `Json::conv(1 as i32)` with `conv(i32)` and
`conv(i64)` was "error[E0900]: codegen: `..::Json::conv` names several
functions and the call was not pinned to one of them" plus E0636; and a
literal argument took the parameter type of whichever overload the name's
binding happened to carry, so `conv(1)` called `conv(i64)` when `conv(i32)`
was declared first and `conv(i32)` when it was declared second.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::pin_family_signature(call, callee)`: the selection a bare
  call already made (the family's entries through the member-function
  door, `select_family_overload` over the argument types, the chosen entry
  pinned as `CalleePin::Decl`), moved out of
  `try_pin_overload_mangled_callee` and now also called by
  `resolve_module_qualified_function` for a non-generic member.  The door
  call itself is `family_entries`.  A qualified call no longer pins the
  whole family.
* `family_param_hints`: a call to a free-function family with several
  signatures hints its arguments only where the signatures of its arity
  agree - the rule `lookup_method_param_types` already applies to a
  method's overloads.  A literal at a differing position keeps its default
  type (`i32` for an integer), and that is what selects.  After the pin the
  arguments are classified against the signature chosen.
* `refuse_unmatched_family_call`: an overloaded free-function call no
  signature of its arity accepts is E0214, the method path's error and
  wording ("no overload of `conv` accepts these arguments", "no `conv`
  takes `(boolean)`", the candidates), with a help line when an argument is
  a numeric literal: "an integer literal is `i32` where the overloads
  differ in its type; write the type you mean with `as`".  Before, such a
  call reached codegen unpinned (E0636 and E0633, or E0900 and an LLVM
  verification failure).  A family with no signature of the call's arity
  stays the arity check's.

```cryo
public function conv(x: i32) -> i32 { return 32; }
public function conv(x: i64) -> i32 { return 64; }
Json::conv(1 as i32)   // 32; was E0900 + E0636
conv(1)                // 32 in either declaration order; was 64 with conv(i32) declared first
put(1)                 // put(u8) / put(i64): error[E0214]; was put(i64) by declaration order
```

## Evidence

* Measured before the change, with a throwaway probe compiler
  (`.objcmp/s87/probe61.exe`, the patch's lines in `.objcmp/s87/probe61.py`,
  driver `corpus61.sh`, join `an61.py`, output `.objcmp/s87/c61/`) over the
  compiler, the unit suite (5,229 probe lines), every project, example and
  tool, and the 227 negatives (47 stop before sema): 5 calls in the corpus
  reach an overloaded free-function family, none with a numeric literal
  where the signatures differ (they write casts); 201 overloaded method
  calls, 1 with a literal at a differing position (the negative project
  `inherent_trait_method_ambiguous`), already left at `i32` by the method
  path.  Control: the scratch `l61a` logs its four calls, each pinned to
  `conv(i64)`.  So no corpus call changes target, and no standard-library
  call does.
* Scratch (`.objcmp/s87/l61a`, `l61b`, the two declaration orders): bare
  `conv(1)` was 64 / 32, now 32 / 32; `Json::conv(1)` was E0900, now 32.
* Old HEAD (`3e47a499`) over the new projects: the literal project compiled
  and exited 1, the no-match literal project compiled and exited 56
  (`put(i64)`).  The verify baseline (`e10cfb8d`) fails exactly the four
  declared projects.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-172538`): 0 of 4,838 test objects and 0 of 1,126
  examples moved - a single-signature qualified call's `Decl` pin emits what
  its family pin did; every gate OK.
* Warnings: 344, the same set.
* Gates: lane unchanged (a first version of the E0214 builder rendered types
  through `type_display_name` and moved LOOKUP_ROUTED 33 -> 35; it uses
  `render_param_list` as the method error does).  Spelling flow 796, the

  same row re-keyed (`local:callee` -> `param:callee`).  §0:
  `resolve_module_qualified_def(` 6 -> 5, braced-import files 668 -> 671,
  projects 144 -> 148.
* New projects: `overload_qualified_call_selects` (run; declared in

### 8.446 A method with a receiver, named by path, is a function value taking the receiver first - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 51 (and ruling 46's E0156 for it).  Before: `const f = IgTn::go;`
for `go(&this, u: i32) -> i64` was typed as the owner `IgTn`, so a call
through it was "error[E0202]: cannot find function `f` in this scope" and
`const g: (&IgTn, i32) -> i64 = IgTn::go;` was E0200; an inherent `go`
beside a trait's was never reported at the path.

## What changed

* `SemaVisitor::scope_method` (the `get_method` both value questions ask,
  moved out of `scope_static_method_type`) and
  `scope_receiver_method_type`: the method's signature with its receiver
  parameter's type first (`&IgTn`, `mut &IgTn`, `IgTn`).
  `resolve_scope_resolution` asks it after the static branch and pins the
  value through `pin_scope_value_static_method` with that type - the form a
  method's entry is registered under in the declaration index - so the
  entry is chosen by `entry_of_signature` / `choose_entry` exactly as a
  static method's value is: an inherent method beside a trait's is E0156,
  and `(Beta for IgTn)::go` answers the delivered entry's type.
* A method generic in its own parameters, or a signature naming a generic
  owner's parameter, is not taken as a value (the type is invalid and the
  path keeps its old answer): a generic static method's or generic free
  function's value without type arguments already fails LLVM verification
  ("Incorrect number of arguments passed to called function!"), and this
  change does not extend that.
* `docs/cryo.md`: "A method as a value".

```cryo
const f = IgTn::go;                    // (&IgTn, i32) -> i64; was typed `IgTn`
const n: i64 = f(&ig, 7);              // was E0202
const b = IgTn::bump;  b(&ig, 10);     // mut &this
const t = IgTn::take;  t(ig);          // by-value this
const g = (Beta for IgTn)::go;         // the trait's
const h = IgTn::go;                    // error[E0156] when Beta also provides `go`
```

## Evidence

* Measured before landing, with the change and a probe line at the new
  branch (`.objcmp/s87/probe51.exe`, driver `corpus51.sh`, output
  `.objcmp/s87/c51/`) over the compiler, unit suite, projects, examples,
  tools and negatives: 0 sites.  Control: the scratch `m51` logs its three
  paths (twice, one per sema pass); the driver's unit leg is live (the
  previous probe logged 5,229 lines through it).  No existing program
  changes meaning.
* A first version pinned with the receiver-less signature: no entry
  matched (`M51ENT` showed entries registered as `(&IgTn, i32) -> i64`),
  so the pin fell back to the family and the tie reached codegen as
  "E0900 ... names several functions".  Pinning with the receiver-first
  type reports E0156 at the path.
* Old HEAD (`3e47a499`) over the new projects: E0202 (6 errors), and E0202
  at the later call instead of E0156.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-181750`): the baseline fails exactly the two
  declared projects; 0 of 4,950 test objects and 0 of 1,126 examples moved;
  every gate OK.  Warnings: 344, the same set.
* Gates: lane unchanged; spelling flow 796, the two `get_method` rows moved
  from `scope_static_method_type` to `scope_method`; residue unchanged.
  §0: `signature_refused` mentions 15 -> 16, projects 148 -> 150.
* New projects: `method_value_takes_receiver_first` (run; declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`), `method_value_inherent_trait_ambiguous`
  (E0156; `tests/started-passing`).

### 8.447 An implementation's copy of a trait default answers a call on its projection-bounded receiver before monomorphization - 2026-09-30

## Why

Ruling 35: a call sema cannot type before monomorphization gets its typing
completed.  `Iterator::min` and `max` call `value.compare(&best)` under
`where This::Item: Ord`.  In an implementation's copy of the default,
`This::Item` is a type the implementation gives, and sema has to see the
receiver as the bounded projection the default was written on.  In most
copies it did not: the call carried no trait stamp and no return type, and
the `.is_lt()` / `.is_ge()` after it was untyped with it.  After
monomorphization the same question was asked again on the concrete copy and
answered there, so programs compiled; the answer was missing only where the
monomorphizer plan needs it, before monomorphization.

## Measured first

A throwaway probe (`.objcmp/s88/probe1.patch`, reverted) printed, for every
first-pass method call, whether it left an answer, and for the copy's bound
the receiver's and the subject's type kind.  On a scratch project with a
generic iterator and a plain one (`.objcmp/s88/u1d`):

* `implement<I, A> Iterator<A> for TakeIter<I> where I: Iterator<A>`: the
  subject `This::Item` stayed an unreduced projection.  The function that
  answers the copy's bound resolved it in a fresh context holding `This`
  only; reducing `TakeIter<I>::Item` from there needs `A`, which only a
  where-clause on a still-generic `I` determines.  The copy's signature and
  locals were resolved in the implementation's context, which binds `Item`
  to `A` directly; the bound's subject never was.
* An implementation whose item is a pointer (`Iterator<T*>`): the receiver
  `value: T*` was peeled to `T` before the comparison and the subject `T*`
  was not.
* Copies whose item is a target parameter (`implement<T> Iterator<T> for
  Cnt<T>`) or a concrete type already matched.
* Both failing shapes are stdlib-wide: every build compiles every
  `Iterator` implementation's copy.

Corpus (`.objcmp/s88/corpus.sh`: the compiler, the tests tree, every
project, example and tool, the unit leg, and each of the 179 negative files
checked alone; 396 builds), unanswered first-pass visits at HEAD
(`.objcmp/s88/cb/none-sites.txt`): `compare` 9,159 at each of
`core/iter.cryo:181` and `:202`, and the `is_lt` / `is_ge` after them
4,749 each.

## What changed

* `Resolver::resolve_func_signature`: a `where` clause's projection subject
  is resolved with the signature, in its context, and kept on the
  projection annotation (`ProjectionAnnotation.resolved`, a field that was
  read and never written) when it reduced.  In an implementation's copy of
  a default that context binds the implementation's associated types.  The
  annotation's clone already drops the field, so a specialization resolves
  its own.
* `Cloner`: a copied function owns its bounds (`TraitBound.clone()`), as it
  owns its parameters.  It shared the source's bound list, so every copy of
  `min` had the one subject annotation; with the cache, the first
  implementation's answer became every other's (measured: unanswered
  copies rose from 27 to 42 on the scratch project before this).
* `MethodBinding::default_copy_bound_return` replaces
  `default_copy_bound_direction`: the subject is peeled as the receiver is,
  and the bound's trait method's return is returned as well as noted.  The
  stamp in `bind_method_on_receiver` and the abstract-receiver typing
  (`lookup_method_through_param_bounds`, for a receiver that is one of the
  block's parameters) both ask it, so the stamp and the call's type come
  from one question.

```cryo
implement<I, A> trait Iterator<A> for struct TakeIter<I> where I: Iterator<A> { .. }
// TakeIter's copy of `min`, where This::Item: Ord:
if (value.compare(&best).is_lt()) { .. }
// before: `compare` unanswered and untyped, `is_lt` unanswered
// after:  `compare` stamped Ord (position 0) and typed Ordering, `is_lt` selected
```

## Evidence

* The same corpus with the change (`.objcmp/s88/cf/`): exactly those four
  sites leave the unanswered set (9,159 / 9,159 / 4,749 / 4,749 -> 0);
  every other site's set is unchanged, and every build's exit code is the
  one it had.  The base run's compiler entry was refused by the probe
  compiler (a missing lint allowance in the tree it built, since fixed);
  rebuilt alone (`selfb.out`), it differs from the after-run's only in the
  same four sites.
* What is still unanswered in template bodies: the five `.drop()` calls on
  an unbounded parameter (`future/executor.cryo:208, 591`,
  `thread/_module.cryo:224, 280, 410`), which the `drop_in_place` slice
  owns; function-pointer field calls (`core/iter.cryo:285`,
  `thread/local.cryo:128`) and a builtin `u64[]` push
  (`thread/_module.cryo:718`), which are not method selections; and
  `T::try_from(v).unwrap_or(fallback)` in `examples/09-json-config` (a
  static call on a bounded parameter, untyped before monomorphization;
  pre-existing, not followed).
* No program changes: the post-monomorphization pass already answered these
  calls on the concrete copy.  A program whose item type has an inherent
  `compare` beside `Ord`'s, through `take(3).min()`, returns the `Ord`
  answer at HEAD and with the change (`.objcmp/s88/u1t`).
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-201112`): 0 of 5,004 test objects and 0 of 1,126
  examples moved; every gate OK.
* Gates: lane, residue and spelling flow unchanged; §0 unchanged (the
  replaced function keeps the name-taking count at 712).  Warnings: 344,
  the same set (`cryo check`, compared as sets).

### 8.448 An intrinsic can be generic, and `drop_in_place<T>` releases through the destructor found by identity - 2026-09-30

## Why

Rulings 7 and 14: a generic value behind a pointer is released through a
compiler intrinsic, `std::core::ptr::drop_in_place<T>(p: T*)`, as Rust's
`ptr::drop_in_place` emits each type's drop code after monomorphization.
The monomorphizer plan (its slice 4) lowers it through the trait tables
by identity rather than by building `(*p).drop()` and selecting `drop` by
name.  Before this, an intrinsic could not be generic:
`intrinsic function drop_in_place<T>(p: T*) -> void;` was
`E0100: expected '(', found '<'`.  The standard library cannot declare it
until the pinned compiler parses it, so this lands the compiler half; the
library half follows the re-pin.

## Measured first

* A bodiless generic function (`function dip<T>(p: T*) -> void;`, scratch
  `.objcmp/s88/bl`) is typed, specialized and pinned like any generic
  function today; only codegen failed, declaring the specialization with
  `linkonce_odr` linkage ("Global is external, but doesn't have external or
  weak linkage").  So a generic intrinsic can be a generic function in
  every pass before codegen.
* A specialization's name is minted (`13drop_in_place$Li$G`), so the name
  table gives it no kind: a probe at registration printed kind `Call` for
  every specialization and the intrinsic's kind for the declaration.

## What changed

* Parser: `intrinsic function name<T, ..>(params) -> R where ..;` is a
  `FunctionDeclNode` with no body and `is_intrinsic` set (carried by the
  cloner); a body is the ordinary "expected `;`".  `docs/grammar.md`
  updated.
* Registration (`register_decl_in_index`): an intrinsic function's entry
  is marked with its kind - the declaration's from `IntrinsicKind::from_name`,
  a specialization's from the declaration it is a copy of (`copy_of`), on
  both of the specialization's entries.  New kind `DropInPlace`.
* `CalleePin::intrinsic_kind`: how a call with a pin lowers, read off the
  pinned entry or family.  Codegen's `pinned_intrinsic_kind` asks it, and
  so does drop insertion.
* Drop insertion (`lower_drop_in_place`, first thing `read_call` does):
  a call whose pin lowers as `DropInPlace` is rewritten in place into
  `(*p).drop()` and bound by `CallResolver::bind_destructor`: the
  implementation `Drop` and the type select
  (`GenericRegistry::select_trait_impl`), then its method at `Drop::drop`'s
  position, found by definition (`trait_item_position`, new method
  language item `DropDrop`).  A type with no implementation is left
  unpinned, which codegen's existing arms release with the glue, or not at
  all for a `Copy` type.  A method merely named `drop` is never the
  destructor.
* Codegen never declares an intrinsic function, and `try_emit` declines
  `DropInPlace`: a call that reached codegen unlowered has no symbol and is
  codegen's E0636.

```cryo
intrinsic function drop_in_place<T>(p: T*) -> void;
function release<T>(p: T*) -> void { drop_in_place::<T>(p); }
release::<Counted>(a);   // Counted's `implement trait Drop`, once
release::<Holder>(h);    // no implementation: its field's glue
release::<i32>(&x);      // nothing
release::<Inh>(i);       // an inherent `drop` is not called
```

## Evidence

* New run project `drop_in_place_releases_by_destructor` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`): a `Drop` implementation runs once, a
  glue-only aggregate releases its field, a type with both runs its
  destructor and then its field's glue, `i32` is untouched, and an inherent
  `drop` is not called.  Mutation: binding the rewritten call by name
  (`bind_synthesized_method_call`, the route synthesized drops take today)
  instead of by identity makes it exit 6 (the inherent `drop` ran); the
  identity binder exits 0.  At HEAD the declaration is the parse error
  above.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-203914`): the baseline fails exactly the declared
  project; 0 of 5,004 test objects and 0 of 1,126 examples moved; every
  gate OK.
* Gates: lane surface unchanged in total, one `family_intrinsic_kind`
  lookup moved from `codegen/visit/call_emitter.cryo` to
  `AST/expression.cryo` with `CalleePin::intrinsic_kind` (golden re-pinned;
  residue regenerated, 242 sites, the same row moved).  Spelling flow
  796 -> 797: `IntrinsicKind::from_name` now also reads
  `FunctionDeclNode.name` at registration, beside the listed
  `IntrinsicDeclNode.name`.  §0: `IntrinsicKind::` in call_emitter 4 -> 3,
  `from_name(` 1 -> 2, `mark_intrinsic(` in type_resolution 1 -> 3,
  braced-import files 671 -> 672, projects 150 -> 151, spelling flow 796 ->
  797.  Warnings: 344, the same set.
* Not in this entry: the standard library's declaration in
  `std::core::ptr`, the five `.drop()` calls on an unbounded parameter it
  replaces, and removing E0358's `.drop()` exemption - after the re-pin.
  Rulings 32 and 44 (an inherent `drop` does not satisfy `T: Drop`, and
  only `implement trait Drop` is a destructor) land with those.

### 8.449 A generic intrinsic is reachable from every module, and `drop_in_place` takes `&place` - 2026-09-30

## Why

Declaring `drop_in_place` in `std::core::ptr` and calling it from
`std::thread` and `std::future::executor` (the next entry) failed with the
compiler of 8.448 in two ways, found by building those calls:

* `error[E0353]: `std::core::ptr::drop_in_place` is private and cannot be
  called from `std::thread``.  A generic intrinsic is a function
  declaration, and a function is private unless written `public`; every
  other intrinsic is exported where the name layer declares it
  (`name_resolution.cryo`, `export_symbol` on `IntrinsicDeclaration`).
* `drop_in_place::<C>(&(*p).ctx)` reached the linker as a call
  (`undefined reference to `..drop_in_place$..Ctx..``): an argument written
  `&place` is typed as a reference, and the lowering took only a pointer.

This lands ahead of the library change because verify's baseline is the
previous compiler over the working tree's library: with the library change
in the same commit, every unit test that spawns a thread fails in the
baseline on the first point, and a unit failure cannot be declared.

## What changed

* Parser: a generic intrinsic is public, as every intrinsic declaration is.
* `DropInsertion::lower_drop_in_place`: the released place's type is the
  argument's pointee or referent.

## Evidence

* New run project `generic_intrinsic_from_another_module` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`): a generic intrinsic declared in a sibling
  module is called through that module, on a pointer and on `&(*h).c`.  At
  HEAD: `error[E0353]: `GenericIntrinsicFromAnotherModule::Rel::drop_in_place`
  is private`.  Mutation: without the referent branch the `&place` call
  reaches the linker undefined.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-211544`): the baseline fails exactly the declared
  project; 0 of 5,058 test objects and 0 of 1,126 examples moved; every
  gate OK.
* §0: projects 151 -> 152, braced-import files 672 -> 673.  Lane, residue,
  spelling flow unchanged.  Warnings: 344, the same set.

### 8.450 The standard library releases a generic value through `std::core::ptr::drop_in_place`, and `.drop()` on an unbounded parameter is E0358 - 2026-09-30

## Why

Rulings 7 and 14.  Five calls in the library released a value of an
unbounded type parameter with `.drop()`, which names no method a bound
gives; E0358 exempted any call spelled `.drop()` so they compiled, and they
were selected by name after monomorphization.  With the intrinsic declared
they are released by identity, and the exemption goes.

## What changed

* `std::core::ptr::drop_in_place<T>(p: T*)` is declared (`stdlib/core/ptr.cryo`).
* The five calls: `future/executor.cryo` (`rp.drop()` on `&sh.result`,
  twice) and `thread/_module.cryo` (`(*rptr).drop()` twice; and the
  spawn-failure path, which copied the payload's `ctx` out and dropped the
  copy, now releases it in place) call it.
* `CallResolver`: E0358 applies to `x.drop()` on a type parameter as to
  any other call (`is_explicit_drop_call` now serves only W0015).
* New compile-fail project `drop_on_unbounded_param_refused` (declared in
  `tests/started-passing`; the baseline built it): `(*p).drop()` on an
  unbounded `T` is E0358 at `10:10`, "no method named `drop` found on type
  `T`", and `ptr::drop_in_place::<T>(p)` beside it is accepted.  The
  `.drop()` function leaves `unbounded_param_method_refused`, whose header
  said the call was the language's and not refused; its assertions are
  unchanged.
* New run project `thread_detached_result_released_once` (ruling 20): a
  detached thread's result is released exactly once, by the handle when
  the thread finished first and by the thread when `detach` came first.

```cryo
function release<T>(p: T*) -> void {
    (*p).drop();                   // error[E0358]: no method named `drop` found on type `T`
    ptr::drop_in_place::<T>(p);    // T's destructor, its glue, or nothing
}
```

* Warnings: 344 -> 341, the three W0015 "explicit destructor call" at the
  converted `thread/_module.cryo` sites (the compiler links `std::thread`),
  compared as sets.

  (`.verify/runs/20260930-213909`): the baseline fails only the declared

  baseline compiler lowers the intrinsic too, so the library compiles the

* Gates: lane, residue and spelling flow unchanged.  §0: projects 152 ->

### 8.451 Only a `Drop` implementation is a destructor, synthesized drops bind it by identity, and the containers release what they hold through `drop_in_place` - 2026-09-30

## Why

Rulings 32 and 44, which land with the intrinsic (ruling 14, §8.448-§8.450).
A method merely named `drop` was a destructor in five places: the drops
the compiler synthesizes (scope exit, field glue, argument temporaries,
`delete`) bound `x.drop()` BY NAME (`bind_synthesized_method_call`), and
`OwnershipQuery::has_inherent_drop` made such a type non-`Copy`, gave it a
drop, forbade partial moves out of it, made `delete` call it, and let it
satisfy `where T: Drop`.  The containers required `where T: Drop` of their
payloads, so a payload with only field glue (no implementation) was never
released, and with ruling 32 alone `Box<T>` of a type with only an inherent
`drop` would have lost its destructor.

## What changed

* Every synthesized drop binds through `CallResolver::bind_destructor`: the
  `Drop` implementation that APPLIES (head selects, where-clause holds,
  `TraitChecker::select_impl`), its method at `Drop::drop`'s position; none
  -> unpinned -> glue, or nothing for `Copy`.  A dynamic `T[]` is released
  by the destructor of the `Array<T>` it is laid out as (the mapping the
  method binder uses).  `delete p` binds the pointee's destructor
  (`bind_pointee_destructor_call`); a pointer receiver anywhere else is
  `Copy` and reaches nothing.  `bind_synthesized_method_call` is deleted.
* `has_inherent_drop`, `ast_has_drop`, `impl_blocks_have_drop` and
  `GenericRegistry::inherent_impl_has_method` are deleted; `is_copy`,
  `needs_drop`, both `has_user_drop`s, `delete` and the trait checker's
  `T: Drop` arm ask only for an implementation.
* `bind_destructor` previously used `GenericRegistry::select_trait_impl`,
  which for a specialization with no placed clone answers the template
  head without its where-clause; with every synthesized drop routed there,
  the compiler's own build failed to link (`undefined reference to
  C$tr$...Drop$f...Array-4drop`, from `Array<Suggestion>`).
* Library: `Box`, `Rc`, `Weak` (both), `Arc`, `HashMap` (`remove`, `clear`,
  `Drop`), `HashSet`, `Pair`, `mpsc::Receiver`, `Mutex`, `RwLock`,
  `ThreadLocal::clear`, `Array::set/truncate/clear` drop the bound and
  release through `ptr::drop_in_place`; `Array::resize` is `T: Copy`.
  **`Array`'s own `Drop` implementation keeps `where T: Drop`** (it releases
  through the intrinsic): releasing glue-only elements there makes the
  compiler, built against the library, lose methods checking its own
  source (`error[E0215]: method `require` takes 0 argument(s)`, 71 errors)
  - it still reads an element after its array is dropped.  Bisected:
  `.objcmp/s89/stdA..D` (only `array.cryo` from HEAD: clean; only the
  `Drop` impl from HEAD: clean; only the `Drop` impl new: 71 errors).
  Element types it now would release, from a probe in the lowering:
  `MethodInfo`, `EnumVariantInfo`, `TemplateEntry`, `Scope`,
  `SpecializationEntry`, `MonomorphRequest`, `ModuleInfo`, `Diagnostic`,
  `Suggestion`, `VTableSlot`, `ParamPlan`, `TraitRef`, `TraitBound`,
  `VendorEntry`, `AsyncDecl`, `ProjSpec`, `Argument`.  Not fixed here.
* 74 types whose destructor was an inherent `drop` become `implement trait
  Drop for ...` (19 library, 43 test, 1 example, 11 editor), by
  `scripts/ns-migration/8.451/inherent_drop_to_trait.py` (reproduces all 58
  files byte for byte from HEAD).  The inventory: a probe in
  `has_inherent_drop` over 396 builds (compiler, tests, every project,
  example and tool, the unit leg, each negative) found 47 type names; a text
  sweep found those plus `ArgvBuf` (POSIX-only), `CompletionItem` (unused)
  and `Inner` (a negative stopped early).  The run project
  `drop_in_place_releases_by_destructor`'s `Inh` stays: it checks that a
  method merely named `drop` is not one.
* The lambda synthesizer's empty inherent `drop` on a closure is no longer
  called at scope exit; glue releases the captures, as before.
* New run project `containers_release_payload_in_place` (declared in
  `tests/started-passing`).

```cryo
type struct Inh { v: i32; }
implement struct Inh { drop(mut &this) -> void { .. } }   // an ordinary method
{ mut i: Inh = Inh { v: 1 }; }                            // calls nothing now
type struct Holder { c: Counted; }                        // glue only
{ mut b: Box<Holder> = Box::new(..); }                    // releases `c` now; leaked before
{ mut a: Array<Counted*> = ..; }                          // releases no pointee now; did, then the pointee again
```

## Evidence

* HEAD leaked: scratch probe `.objcmp/s89/glue` at HEAD: `box<glue>
  drops=0`, `array<glue> 0`, `rc<glue> 0`; `array<ptr> 2`, `box<ptr> 1`
  (a container of pointers released each pointee, which its owner then
  released again).
* The new project, three ways: new compiler + new library exit 0; HEAD
  compiler + HEAD library exit 1 (Box leaks a glue-only payload); HEAD
  compiler + new library exit 10 (scope exit calls the inherent `drop`).
  An intermediate version that followed a pointer receiver in
  `bind_destructor_call` made it exit 8 (a container of pointers released
  a pointee).  Its `Array<Holder>` case was added after the facts build
  refused the unbounded-head selection; it was not run against that
  mutation.
* The unit test `NewStructInitArrayMove::struct_literal_value_drops_array_once`
  failed (count 0, want 2) until `T[]` was mapped to `Array<T>`.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20260930-232835`): the baseline fails only the declared
  project; tree census OK; examples 0 of 1,126 moved; tests 2 of 5,170
  moved, both explained: `drop_in_place_releases_by_destructor/Main.o`
  (`Inh` is now `Copy`) and `MoveLambda.o` (the closure's empty inherent
  `drop` is no longer called before its glue); lsp, cross, incr, blind,
  flow OK; fast failed on one §0 row, fixed here.
* Warnings 341 -> 331: the ten W0015 "explicit destructor call" at the
  converted `.drop()` sites in `box`, `rc`, `array` (4), `hashmap` (3) and
  `thread/local`; compared as sets (`cryo check src/main.cryo`, HEAD vs
  tree).
* Gates: lane LOOKUP_LOCAL 70 -> 69 and REGISTRY_READ 11 -> 10 (the deleted
  `has_inherent_drop`'s registry reads; golden re-pinned); spelling flow

  `call_resolver` 2 -> 3.
* Pins: the previous pin made a generic intrinsic private and refused

### 8.452 A call a generic body's template pins to an inherent method keeps that answer in every specialization, bound by identity - 2026-10-01

## Why

The first piece of the monomorphizer conversion (`.objcmp/mono-design/DESIGN.md`
slice 6): a template pin survives substitution and is mapped to the
specialization's method by identity, so the call is not selected again by
its member's name after monomorphization (rule 1).  The shape taken first is
the one with an identity map already in the tree: a call whose receiver is
an unminted instantiation of a generic type and whose selection there is an
inherent method of that type with no type parameters of its own
(`this.len()` in `Array<T>`).  `DeclarationIndex::method_entry_on(owner,
def)` answers the specialization's copy of the template's definition, as it
does for the method language items (`bind_named_method`).

## What changed

* `CallExprNode.template_method: DefId`: written by `commit_selection` when
  the selection is made on an unminted instantiation
  (`CallResolver::pin_template_method`: the method's definition's parent is
  the instantiation's template, and the method has no type parameters);
  copied by the cloner; never cleared by the substituter.
* `bind_method_on_receiver`: a call carrying the pin, on a receiver that is
  minted and mentions no type parameter, is bound by
  `bind_template_method` (`method_entry_on`) and nothing else; no copy
  leaves it unbound for code generation to refuse.
* Mono's method finder chain is NOT skipped for these calls: skipping
  `specialize_method_call` for them (as for `named_method`) makes the unit
  build fail - `error[E0900]: unresolved generic instantiation after
  monomorphization: 'std::core::result::Result<?, ?>'` twice - although
  the chain answers nothing for a non-generic method; something before the
  chain's answer (`derive_receiver_type`,
  `canonicalize_default_template_recv`, the self-returning-default check)
  has a side effect a later stage needs.  Not diagnosed; deleting the chain
  must keep it.
* New run project `generic_body_call_keeps_written_answer` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`): the baseline re-selected `this.m()` in
  `Bx<i32>`'s copy of `run` by name and refused it.

```cryo
type trait Tr { m(&this) -> i32; }
type struct Bx<T> { v: T; }
implement<T> struct Bx<T> {
    m(&this) -> i32 { return 1; }
    run(&this) -> i32 { return this.m(); }   // inherent `m`, where written
}
implement trait Tr for struct Bx<i32> { m(&this) -> i32 { return 2; } }
Bx::<i32> { v: 0 }.run()   // 1; was error[E0156]: `m` is both an inherent method of `Bx<i32>` and provided by a trait implemented for it
b.m()                      // on a `Bx<i32>` directly: still E0156
```

## Evidence

* Measured at `44490db3` before the change (probe `.objcmp/s89/probe6.py`,
  corpus `.objcmp/s89/corpus6.sh`: the compiler, `tests/`, every project,
  example and tool, the unit leg, each negative; 401 entries): the
  substituter nulls 15,758 method pins (`resolved_method` + callee),
  154,037 path callee pins and 40,326 bare-call pins; mono's finder chain
  answers step 1: 31, 2: 231, 3: 4, 4: 142, 5: 2,434, 6: 13, 7: 85,
  8: 689, path 14, self-returning default 71, and nothing 76,748 times
  (every answer a generic method); in placed specializations' bodies sema's
  post-mono pass keeps a pin 26,452 times and selects by name 156,302 times
  (104,287 pinned, 52,015 left unbound).  The compiler build alone: keeps
  1,808, selects 7,943 + 1,152.
* Agreement (probe `.objcmp/s89/probe6b.py`, the by-name selection run
  beside the identity answer, same corpus): 66,437 agree, 0 disagree;
  5 with no copy, all in programs that are refused anyway (2 negatives,
  3 compile-fail projects), whose diagnostics are unchanged.  The compiler
  build alone: 6,937 agree.
* Mutation: `bind_template_method` answering nothing makes `examples/01-hello`
  fail (`error[E0358]: no method named `next` found on type
  `std::core::slice::SliceIter<u8>``, 18 times): nothing behind the identity
  path selects by name.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261001-004526`): the baseline refuses only the declared
  project; 0 of 5,227 test objects and 0 of 1,126 examples moved; every
  gate OK.
* Warnings: 331, the same set (`cryo check src/main.cryo`).

### 8.453 A call carrying a template pin no longer passes through mono's by-name method finders; its deferred copy is materialized by identity - 2026-10-01

## Why

8.452 left mono's finder chain running for template-pinned calls, because
skipping it broke the unit build with `error[E0900]: unresolved generic
instantiation after monomorphization: 'std::core::result::Result<?, ?>'`
twice.  Diagnosed: the side effect is `try_instantiate_self_returning_default`.
An inherent method whose signature grows its owner (`Option<T>::as_ref ->
Option<T*>`, `Result<T, E>::as_ref -> Result<T*, E*>`) is deferred - placed
in the receiver's specialization flagged `is_lazy_self_growing`, never
instantiated eagerly - and is materialized only by a call that names it.
That instantiation was found by the member's name (`find_self_returning_default`)
and is what mints `Result<i32*, i32*>` (the `?` arguments are pointers, which
have no qualified name).  Skipping it left the instantiation sema's typing
creates unmonomorphized.

## What changed

* `specialize_method_call`: a call with `template_method` goes to
  `materialize_deferred_copy` and nothing else - none of the finders, no
  self-returning-default search by name.
* `materialize_deferred_copy(call, d, recv)`: in the receiver's
  specialization's placed impl blocks, the method whose `copy_of` is `d`
  and which is still deferred; a copy already instantiated (same `copy_of`,
  unflagged) is reused.  By identity throughout.  A method the
  specialization made eagerly needs nothing.
* `try_instantiate_self_returning_default` keeps its by-name finder (the
  unpinned calls still use it) and hands the instantiation to
  `instantiate_deferred`, shared with the identity path.

```cryo
mut opt: Option<i32> = Option::Some(10);
opt.as_ref()        // template pin: Option<T>::as_ref; Option<i32>'s copy
                    // is instantiated for this call, found by its copy_of
```

## Evidence

* Probe over the corpus at `666e28ef` (`.objcmp/s90/probe1.patch`, driver
  `.objcmp/s90/corpus.sh`, 401 entries: compiler, `tests/`, every project,
  example and tool, the unit leg, each negative): template-pinned calls
  entered `specialize_method_call` 78,774 times; the self-returning
  default search answered 7 (all `as_ref`, unit leg:
  `tests/stdlib/option.cryo:270,282,300,309`, `result.cryo:162,172,184`);
  the finder chain answered 0, the default-template canonicalization moved
  0.  Control for the chain's zero: `.objcmp/s90/ctl`, `Ov<T>` with
  `put(i32)` and `put<U>(U, i32)`, `o.put(7)` in `main` - the chain answers
  the generic `put<U>` by name (`S90 CHAIN n=1`), then drops it for want of
  type arguments.
* Agreement (`.objcmp/s90/probe2.patch`, same corpus, identity and by-name
  answers side by side): 7 agree, 0 disagree, 73,764 neither; every build's
  exit status equals the run at `666e28ef`.
* Mutation: `materialize_deferred_copy` returning at once makes the unit
  leg fail with the two `Result<?, ?>` E0900s (rc 1); unmutated it builds.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261001-014509`): 0 of 5,281 test objects and 0 of 1,126
  examples moved; every gate OK.
* Warnings: 331, the same set.

### 8.454 A call a bound answered is bound on a minted receiver through the implementations' method tables, never by its member's name - 2026-10-01

## Why

Slice 6 of `.objcmp/mono-design/DESIGN.md`, second piece: a call that
recorded a trait and the position of the trait's method where it is written
(`x.s_req()` under `where T: Show`; an operator desugared through `Mul`)
was selected again by its member's name on each concrete receiver, the
trait only restricting the candidates; the slot tables of 8.435 were
consulted only to check that selection.  That check was itself wrong
for a trait implemented at several trait arguments: it asked
`select_trait_impl`, which answers the FIRST implementation, so a correct
program was refused.

```cryo
implement trait Mul<f32, V> for struct V { mul(&this, rhs: &f32) -> V { .. } }
implement trait Mul<V, V>   for struct V { mul(&this, rhs: &V) -> V { .. } }
a * a    // was: error[E0900]: `mul` was selected by name as a trait's method, and
         // the method table of the implementation the trait and the receiver select answers a different one
```

## What changed

* `bind_method_on_receiver`: on a minted receiver (no unminted template), a
  call with a recorded trait position is bound by `bind_trait_item` when
  every answer the implementations give is a plain method (no type
  parameters of its own, not a per-call default).  Those shapes are bound to
  a specialization and still select by name (DESIGN slice 6 pieces 3-4).
* `trait_item_answers(member, recv)`: every implementation of the trait for
  the receiver (`GenericRegistry::heads_for`, registration order), each
  one's method at the recorded position.  Replaces `trait_item_answer`.
* `bind_trait_item`: the first answer the arguments bind to, at the lowest
  tier any binds (`args_bind_to_params`, the rule every candidate set
  uses); `commit_selection` applies an `![implicit]` converter at tier 3 as
  before.  No answer binding leaves the call unbound - no method outside the
  trait's implementations is a candidate (ruling 25).
* `check_trait_item_table` accepts a selection equal to (or a
  specialization of) any implementation's answer; it still guards the
  by-name shapes.
* New run project `trait_at_two_arguments_selects_by_argument` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`).

```cryo
function sh<T>(x: &T) -> i32 where T: Show { return x.s_req(); }
// in sh<P>: Show's implementation for P, slot of `s_req` -> P's s_req
```

## Evidence

* Population at `88c35bea` (probe `.objcmp/s90/probe2.patch`, corpus
  `.objcmp/s90/corpus.sh`, 401 entries): stamped calls on a minted
  receiver reaching selection: 26,225 whose answer is plain (tier 0:
  23,070, tier 1: 3,155, tier 3: 0), 18,770 answered by a generic method,
  12 by a specialization of one (`value.fmt(f)` in `fmt/display.cryo`),
  4 stamped with no position (`for` desugaring of `next`,
  `tests/lang/for_in.cryo:212,226`), 1 whose by-name pass found nothing
  (the negative `E0214_overload_set_no_match.cryo:37`); 18,646 already
  pinned by mono.
* Agreement (`.objcmp/s90/probe3.patch`, both answers side by side, same
  corpus plus the new project): 26,392 agree in method and tier
  (26,390 with one implementation, 2 with two), 0 disagree, 1 bound by
  neither (that negative; its E0214 is unchanged).  The difference from the
  population is the new project (167) and that negative (1), by entry.
* The new project, three ways: this compiler exits 0 (`two-arguments ok`);
  `88c35bea`'s refuses it with the E0900 above; a mutant considering only
  the first implementation refuses it with E0214.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261001-022331`): the baseline fails only the declared
  project; 0 of 5,281 test objects and 0 of 1,126 examples moved; every
  gate OK.
* Warnings: 331, the same set (lines shift in `call_resolver.cryo`).
* §0: projects 156 -> 157; braced-import files 675 -> 676 (the new

### 8.455 A call in a generic body on a minted receiver keeps the plain method sema selected for it in every specialization - 2026-10-01

## Why

Slice 6, the 89th session's piece 1: a method call in a generic body whose
receiver is already a minted type (`s.length()` on a `Str` inside `Box<T>`) is
pinned by sema where it is written, and the substituter drops that pin in
every clone, so sema's pass after monomorphization selected the method
again by its member's name - on a receiver that is the same type in every
copy.  The template pin of 8.452 now covers it.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::pin_minted_method`, at the unstamped non-generic selection
  in `bind_method_on_receiver`: during a generic body's walk
  (`in_symbolic_check`), a selection on a minted receiver that mentions no
  type parameter records `template_method` when the method has no type
  parameters of its own, is not a per-call default (self-returning or
  lazily grown), and `method_entry_on(receiver, def)` is the method's own
  entry.  After monomorphization `bind_template_method` binds that entry;
  mono's `specialize_method_call` goes to `materialize_deferred_copy`,
  which finds nothing to do for such a method.
* Left by name: stamped calls (8.454 binds the plain ones), generic methods,
  per-call defaults, and a method reached through another type (a base
  class's method, where the receiver's entry for the definition is not the
  method's own).
* Doc comments of `template_method` and `bind_template_method` widened.

```cryo
type struct Bx<T> { v: T; s: Str; }
implement<T> struct Bx<T> {
    n(&this) -> u64 { return this.s.length(); }   // Str::length, by its definition in Bx<i32>, Bx<f64>, ...
}
```

## Evidence

  template pin, the by-name selection run first with the pin hidden, then
  the identity binding; corpus `.objcmp/s90/corpus.sh`, 401 entries):
  newly pinned shape (the definition is the receiver's own) 5,399 agree,
  0 disagree; 8.452's shape (a copy) 74,163 agree, 0 disagree, 5 with no

  `E0358_hashmap_get_noncopy`, `E0358_push_slice_non_copy`), the same five

  `generic_body_call_keeps_written_answer`, which the probe's own by-name

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261001-032209`): census, examples, incr, blind, flow and

### 8.456 A call to a method with type parameters of its own is instantiated from the method sema selected, found by its definition, once per receiver and type arguments - 2026-10-01

## Why

Slice 6, generic methods.  A call to a method with type parameters of its
own (`o.put(1, 2)` for `put<U>(&this, u: U, w: i32)`) was instantiated
from a method mono found again by its member's name - the first generic
method of that name in the receiver's stores, with no arity check - and its
type arguments were solved by sema against a method also found by name.
Two generic overloads of one name (ruling 34) therefore instantiated the
one-argument declaration for the two-argument call, and the module failed
LLVM verification.  The instance was deduplicated by its mangled symbol.

## What changed

* Sema records the method it selected on the call: `pin_generic_method`, in
  `commit_selection` for a minted receiver, writes `template_method` = the
  method's definition (a copy's `copy_of`) for a method with type
  parameters of its own; `pin_template_method` (an unminted instantiation
  in a generic body) no longer skips such methods.  Per-call defaults
  (self-returning, lazily grown: `map`, `take`) are left to the chain.
  Nothing is recorded in the pass after monomorphization.
* Sema solves the call's type arguments, and its return, against the
  selected method: `find_generic_method_for_call` takes the selection's
  `chosen` and, for a generic method, finds its declaration and the type or
  impl block it is written in by identity (`chosen_declaration`,
  `method_site`); `stash_owner_generic_method_bindings` uses the template's
  method the selection chose.  The by-name search stays for a call with no
  selection (a turbofish checked before selection, a deref-coerced
  receiver).
* Mono maps the pin: `receiver_method_of` = the receiver's entry for the
  definition (`method_entry_on`) and its placement (`method_placement`, the
  path call's `path_method_placement` widened to the receiver's
  specialization stores and reused); `instantiate_generic_method` (the
  chain's tail, extracted) mints or reuses the instance.  The chain itself
  is extracted unchanged into `find_generic_method_by_name` for calls with
  no pin.
* Instances are kept in `MonoState.method_instances`, keyed by (receiver
  type, definition) with the type arguments compared by identity; the
  mangled-symbol dedup (`method_specs`) now serves only generic static
  methods.  An instance is looked up before the method is cloned.
* `copy_entries` no longer files an instance of a generic method as the
  receiver's copy of its definition: a trait default's instance whose symbol
  carries no `$MG` arguments (`Stderr`'s `write<Slice<u8>>`) was answering
  `method_entry_on(Stderr, Write::write)`.
* `DeclarationIndex::method_func_of`: a trait's declared method is
  registered as its `FunctionDeclNode`, not a `MethodNode`.

  held by that declaration or block".

  its own is not bound by `bind_template_method` (that would bind the
  uninstantiated copy); a call mono left unpinned is still selected by name
  there (see Remaining).

```cryo

    put<U>(&this, u: U) -> i32 { return 1; }
    put<U>(&this, u: U, w: i32) -> i32 { return 2; }
}
o.put(1) + o.put(1, 2) * 10   // 21; was E0900 (LLVM: incorrect number of arguments)
```

### 8.457 A call to a per-call default or through a bound is bound to the receiver's method by its definition or its trait position, never found by name - 2026-10-01

## Why

Slice 6, bound calls and per-call defaults.  Two kinds of call still
reached mono's by-name finders: a call a trait bound answered (`value.
hash(&h)` with `T: Hash`, `it.fold(..)` with `I: Iterator`), and a trait
default the receiver instantiates per call because its signature mentions
`This` (`take`, `map`, `Option<T>::as_ref`), found by
`try_instantiate_self_returning_default` / `find_self_returning_default`.
Both looked the method up by its member's name on the receiver.  When two
traits give one type a same-named default returning `This`, the name
lookup took the first trait's, so a call through `T: Bb` ran `Aa`'s default
- a silent miscompile at the tip:

```cryo
type trait Aa { keep(this) -> Option<This> { return Option::None; } }
type trait Bb { keep(this) -> Option<This> { return Option::Some(this); } }
type struct S { x: i32; }
implement trait Aa for struct S { }
implement trait Bb for struct S { }
function via_b<T>(x: T) -> i32 where T: Bb {
    match (x.keep()) { Option::Some(_) => { return 2; } Option::None => { return 1; } }
}
// via_a(s) + via_b(s) * 10 printed 11 (Aa's keep both times); now 21
```

## What changed

* Mono has one dispatch for a mapped call, `bind_receiver_method`: a
  method with type parameters of its own -> its instance
  (`instantiate_generic_method`); a default instantiated per call ->
  `instantiate_deferred`, reusing the instance an earlier call made, found
  among the block's methods by `copy_of`; any other method -> nothing here
  (the pass after monomorphization binds it).
* It is fed two ways, both by identity:
  - the template pin (`template_method`), through `receiver_method_of`: the
    deferred copy of the definition first (`deferred_copy_of`: the blocks
    placed under the receiver's specialization, then
    `trait_impls_of`), else the receiver's index entry and its placement;
  - NEW: a call a bound answered (`resolved_trait` and
    `resolved_trait_slot`), through `trait_item_on` = the receiver's ONE
    implementation of the trait - the blocks placed under its
    specialization when the receiver is one, else the registry's
    `heads_for` - and `trait_item_method(block, slot)`.  A receiver
    implementing the trait at several trait arguments (null) still goes to
    the chain.
* `materialize_deferred_copy` is folded into the above.
* Sema: `pin_generic_method` -> `pin_instantiated_method`, which also pins
  per-call defaults on a minted receiver; `pin_template_method` records a
  trait default's `copy_of` on an unminted receiver.

Project `bound_call_runs_bound_traits_default` (run), declared in
`tests/started-passing`: the tip prints `bound default 11` and exits 1.

## Evidence

* Corpus agreement (probe `.objcmp/s91/probe4.patch`, corpus `.objcmp/s91/
  c3`, 401 entries incl. the unit leg and each negative):
  - template-pinned: 3,235 generic and 71 per-call-default answers agree
    with the chain; 4 disagree, all in the ruling-34 project (the chain was
    wrong); 1 identity-none on the first walk of `it.take(2).fold(..)`
    (`tests/tests/lang/local_type_inference.cryo:79`), whose re-walk
    agrees; 1 chain-none in a refused project.
  - bound calls: 266 generic and 1 default answer agree; 3 disagree - the
    new project (the chain was wrong) and 2 in
    `inherent_trait_method_explicit`, where the chain instantiated the
    INHERENT `IgTn::go<U>` for `x.go(0)` through `T: Beta`; identity names
    `Beta::go`.
  - by-name residue: `find_generic_method_by_name` generic answers 352 ->
    0, by-name `try_instantiate_self_returning_default` 0; control: a
    mutant that does not pin per-call defaults reports 1 on
    `.objcmp/s91/tk`.
* verify against HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261001-074232`, plain `make verify`;
  the host had 18 GB free): every gate OK - census, examples 14, lsp,
  cross, incr, blind, flow, fast.  The declared project: the baseline
  census fails it alone (`projects: 155 passed, 1 failed`), the tree's
  passes.
* Objects: tests 1 of 5,389 moved, examples 0 of 1,126.  The predicted
  mover (`inherent_trait_method_explicit`) did NOT move: the tip's wrong

  `TakeIter<SliceIter<i32>>::fold<i32>` instance on the impl block placed

* Warnings: 331 under both compilers, the same (code, file:line) set

## Remaining (slice 6)

* A bound call whose receiver implements the trait at several trait

* Then delete `find_generic_method_by_name` and its finders,
