### 8.481 A pointer comparison or pointer arithmetic on `T*` is typed in the generic body - 2026-10-02

## Why

The symbolic walk of a generic body returned no type for any binary
operation with a symbolic operand (`resolve_binary`), and a `T*` is symbolic,
as is `null` (a void operand). So `this.ptr == null`, `this.ptr != null` and
`ptr + count` in `Array<T>`, `HashMap<K, V>`, `RawBuffer<T>`, `mem.cryo:47` and
`ptr.cryo:25` were left untyped in the template, and every copy was typed by
the pass after monomorphization: the `copy template-untyped-fill` cell, 5,569
writes, 5,523 of them `BinaryExpression`. The pointer rules in
`TypeChecker::check_binary_op` read the operands' top-level kinds only
(pointer against pointer, function, string, reference or `null` gives `bool`;
pointer plus or minus a number gives the pointer), so `T` is never needed.

```cryo
function first<T>(p: T*) -> boolean { return p != null; }   // bool, in the template
```

## What changed

* `resolve_binary` hands an operation to `check_binary_op` in the symbolic walk
  when `pointer_rule_settles`: one operand is a pointer, and each operand is a
  pointer, `null`, or a settled type. Any other symbolic operand still leaves
  the node untyped.

## Evidence

* The gauge (`--emit=postmono-writes` over the corpus, `.objcmp/s99/pmp2` this
  change; control `.objcmp/s99/pmu2`, built before it), compared over the same
  149 reports (`.objcmp/s99/pmu2-149`): `copy template-untyped-fill`
  **5,557 -> 71**, `copy same` +5,486, the same number; no other copy cell
  moves. Left in the cell: two calls at `fs/path.cryo:322,332`, `static match`
  arms in `random/source.cryo:100-103`, and `math::abs<T>` / `clamp<T>`
  (`math/_module.cryo:190,252`), which apply `<` and `-` to a `T` with no bound -
  the shape ruling 82 refuses on the template, so building ruling 82 refuses
  those two stdlib functions as written.
* The non-copy and argument cells that moved in the same comparison are
  8.480's, not this change's (`pmu2` was built before 8.480): the argument
  check now reaching `String` parameters inserts the `![implicit]` conversion
  in the first pass, so `Text::tag("hello")` against `tag(s: String)`
  (`module_suffix_tie_checks_arguments`) and 8 calls in the unit leg are no
  longer argument replacements after monomorphization: corpus `arg
  replaced=yes` **16 -> 1**, `body fill` 32 -> 17. The rest of those cells
  move only in `compiler` and `tools/CryoLSP`, whose source changed.
* Census with this compiler: OVERALL PASS, 227 compile-fail, 160 projects
  (`.objcmp/s99/census-p2.out`); the compiler checks its own source clean
  (`selfcheck-p2.out`). verify against HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261002-222222`):
  all gates OK, objects **0 moved**. Clean build 331 warnings, the same set.

### 8.482 Monomorphization pins a call bound as written in each copy and in each body it walks - 2026-10-03

## Why

The pass after monomorphization wrote the pin of 117,251 calls the
monomorphizer could already answer by identity (gauge `--emit=postmono-writes`
over the corpus, `.objcmp/s99/pmp2`). Each call had recorded where it is
written what it names - `template_method` and `template_recv`, the trait and
position a bound answered, or a generated call's `named_method` - and the
monomorphizer found that method on the receiver in `specialize_method_call`
and then dropped it unless it had to instantiate it. Four families:

```cryo
implement<T> trait Clone for enum Option<T> where T: Clone {
    clone(&this) -> Option<T> { ... Option::Some(value.clone()) ... }  // bound call on `T`
}
parts.push(this.substr(start, n));   // `Array<string>` not minted where written
Pair::<A, B>::new(a, b)              // static method of a generic owner
this.fut.take()                      // a call `await` lowering generates
```

A copy's body is walked once, when it is made, often before the
instantiations it names are minted; that is why the binding was left to a
later pass.

## What changed

* `bind_receiver_method` pins a method bound as written (no type parameters
  of its own, not a per-call default) on a minted, concrete receiver
  (`pin_plain`).
* A call whose receiver or owner is an instantiation not minted yet is queued
  (`queued_binds`) and bound by the same identity once the instantiation's
  methods are registered: `bind_queued_calls`, run at the end of
  `run_generic_expression_resolution`. Only a method bound as written is
  pinned there; an instance minted there would never be registered.
* A static call on a generic owner pins the owner's entry for the recorded
  method once the owner is minted. A path whose owner the copy's
  substitution wrote (`spec_owner`: the owner's own name inside its body, or
  `T::f()`) is bound on that owner (`bind_on_substituted_owner`); a trait
  item there needs the owner's single implementation.
* A call the compiler generates records the receiver it was built on
  (`template_recv`, `async_lower.cryo` `method_call0/1`); monomorphization
  binds it as the pass after it did (`bind_named_call`, `named_method_on`),
  reading the receiver's implementations the way bound calls do
  (`trait_heads_on`, split out of `trait_item_on`).

## Evidence

* Gauge, like-for-like over the same 149 reports (`.objcmp/s100/c10-149`
  against `.objcmp/s99/pmp2`): pins the pass after monomorphization changed
  **117,251 -> 802**. Left: 780 calls on a receiver typed by an unnormalised
  projection (`value.compare(&best)` with `This::Item: Ord`, `core/iter.cryo:181,202`;
  generated calls on `Option<S::Fut>`), which wait for projection
  normalisation; 4 `T::try_from(x)` whose `T` has several `TryFrom`
  implementations (arguments choose); 14 static calls in non-generic bodies
  that recorded no owner; 4 others. Type and argument cells unchanged.
* Agreement: a probe build (`.objcmp/s100/probe_agree_lib.py`) has the pass
  after monomorphization clear every pin this change wrote, bind the call
  itself and compare: **140,172 agree, 0 disagree**, over the corpus plus the
  standard library built alone (`.objcmp/s100/c10`). Control: the same probe
  with mono pinning the template's method instead of the receiver's
  (`mut1.py`, alone, unmutated control beside it) reports 2,153
  disagreements on seven examples (`.objcmp/s100/mm1`); an earlier draft
  that read a generated call's implementation from the registry instead of
  the specialization's blocks drew 84, fixed by `trait_heads_on`.
* Reducing a projection in the receiver (`trait_spec.reduce_projections`)
  was tried and dropped: it fills the projection type's `resolved_type` in
  place, and the standard library built alone then fails GenericValidation
  with E0900 on `Option<?>` and `Poll<?>` (`.facts/stdlib.log`, first
  `make facts` this session). The corpus driver does not build the
  standard library alone; this session's copy (`.objcmp/s100/corpus-pm.sh`) does.
* Corpus build outcomes identical to before (exit code and report per
  entry). Census OVERALL PASS, 227 compile-fail, 160 projects; verify against
  HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261003-001611`): all gates OK, objects **0 moved**.
  The compiler checks its own source clean; clean build 331 warnings, the same set.

### 8.483 Monomorphization writes each copied expression's type, its projections reduced - 2026-10-03

## Why

A copy of a generic body was cloned untyped (only identifiers carried a
type), so every expression type in every copy - 2,243,154 writes over the
corpus - was computed by the type check after monomorphization, which is
the pass being removed. 97% of those were the template's first-pass type
under the copy's substitution; 26,894 more were that type with an
associated-type projection reduced, which substitution alone does not do:

```cryo
min(mut &this) -> Option<This::Item> where This::Item: Ord { ... }
// copied for SplitIter: Option<SplitIter::Item> substituted, Option<Str> reduced
```

## What changed

* A clone made for monomorphization (`ASTCloner::for_monomorphization`, and
  `for_specialization`, which builds on it) carries every expression's
  template type. Other clones - a closure's specialized function, a trait
  default copied before the type check - stay untyped, because the type
  check walks them and passes over what is already typed.
* The substituter writes each expression's type as the copy sees it
  (`ASTTypeSubstituter::in_copy`): the substitution applied, then each
  projection whose base that makes concrete reduced, without demanding the
  instantiations that builds. The call's `template_recv` is reduced the same
  way, so a bound call on a projection-typed receiver
  (`value.compare(&best)` with `This::Item: Ord`) is now pinned by
  monomorphization too.
* One projection reducer, `TypeResolver::reduce_projections(ty, memo)`;
  `MonoTraitSpecializer::reduce_projections` is it with `memo`. Without
  `memo` it records nothing on the projection type: recording the answer
  there makes every type holding the projection read as concrete, and the
  standard library built alone then fails GenericValidation (8.482).
* The spelling-flow entry for the trait's associated-type table moves with
  the walker (`scripts/spelling-flow.outstanding.tsv`, same flow, new function).
* Gauge: `--emit=postmono-writes` gains `copy-entry` rows, each type write in
  a copy compared with the type the copy entered with: `same` is a write that
  changes nothing.

## Evidence

* Gauge over the corpus plus the standard library alone (`.objcmp/s100/c12`),
  like-for-like 149 reports (`c12-149-sum.txt`): copy writes **2,238,402 same,
  4,680 change, 72 none** - 99.79% no-ops. Before (gauge only, types not
  carried; `g0.exe` on seven examples, `.objcmp/s100/m-g0`): 58,491 same, 42,680
  change, 85,510 none of 186,681; the same seven with this change: 185,655 /
  1,012 / 14. Substitution without the reduction (`p5b.exe`, `m-p5b`): 2,293
  change, the 1,281 more all projections.
* Left (4,680), all first-pass answers the template got wrong, not
  substitution: async-lowered nodes (`BinaryExpression` 2,853,
  `UnaryExpression` 634 - `buf.cryo:541`, `void`/`T*` against `u32`/`&T`),
  literal widths in a struct literal of an unminted instantiation (`Literal`
  1,119 - `RefIter::<T> { index: 0 }`, `array.cryo:180`, `i32` against `u64`),
  a bare generic base on a constructor (`ScopeResolution` 70,
  `combinator.cryo:282`).
* Pins: the type check after monomorphization changed **802 -> 22**
  (like-for-like); the probe of 8.482 over the same run: **142,006 agree,
  0 disagree**.
* **This bullet is wrong; 8.485 corrects it.** The run it reports had
  `--emit=postmono-writes` on, and that instrument changes demand.
  Demand (ruling 85, not built): with the substituter in demanding mode
  (`dm.exe`) the seven examples raise no GenericValidation error, and the
  standard library built alone raises 25 (`ClonedIter<RefIter<SocketAddr>>`
  and the like, `.objcmp/s100/dm-std.log`): instantiations only a copy's
  written types name. They are demanded when the pass after

* Corpus build outcomes identical. verify against HEAD
  (`.verify/runs/20261003-010835`): census, examples, lsp, cross, incr, blind,

## Why

`resolve_struct_literal` gave a field's value its expected type only when the
literal's type was a minted struct or class, or the generic owner inside its
own body. A literal of any other instantiation not minted yet left every
value without one, so a literal took the default `i32` and a bare generic
constructor its bare base, and the type check after monomorphization

```cryo
Src::<Result<i64, i64>> { v: Result::Ok(3) }                     // `Result` first, `Result<i64, i64>` after
```

## What changed

* The literal asks the member door for the field (`MemberResolver::field_of`)
  for an unminted instantiation too; the door already reads such a field off
  the template through the instantiation's arguments.

## Evidence

### 8.485 The async lowering types the nodes it builds as the type check types written ones - 2026-10-03

## Why

The async lowering runs after the first type check and builds the poll
state machine's nodes with types of its own choosing, which the type check
after monomorphization then re-typed in every lowered body and every copy
of one - 4,282 changed writes in non-generic bodies and 4,175 in copies
over the corpus. Four shapes, each the lowering disagreeing with the type
check's rule for the same node written by hand:

```cryo
this.state = 3;          // lowered: typed `void`;        type check: `u32`, the target's type
this.recv = &stream;     // lowered: typed `TcpStream*`;   type check: `&TcpStream`
return Poll::Ready(());  // lowered: `()` typed `()`;     type check: `void*`
Fut { slot: null, .. }   // lowered: `null` typed `u8*`;  type check: `void*`
```

## What changed

* One assignment builder, `AsyncLower::assign_stmt`, typed by its target;
  `assign_member_stmt`, `assign_field_of_stmt` and `assign_local_stmt` are it.
* `addr_of` types `&e` as an immutable reference to `e`'s type, whatever
  pointer slot it is stored in, and leaves it untyped when `e` is.
* The unit value and a pointer field's zero value are typed by
  `LiteralResolver::null_literal_type` - the rule the type check types a
  written `null` or `()` by, split out of `resolve_null_literal` and handed
  to the lowering at wiring. It types `()` as `void*`; that is the type
  check's existing answer, carried over, not decided here.

## Correction to 8.483

8.483's demand bullet is wrong. Its run had `--emit=postmono-writes` on,
and that instrument changes demand: `PostmonoWrites::record_substituted`
applies each copy's substitution first, in no-demand mode, so the
substituter's own apply finds the instantiation already made. With the
instrument off and the substituter demanding (`.objcmp/s100/dm.exe`, run
`.objcmp/s100/cdm2`) **all 181 builds of the corpus fail** - 150 logs carry
GenericValidation's E0900, `01-hello` fifteen of them
(`HashMapIter<String, String>`, `KeysIter<..>`, `ValuesIter<..>`) - where the
same compiler with the instrument on builds 108 (`.objcmp/s100/cdm`). The
instantiations named are types in the bodies of methods no program calls;
ruling 85 has them demanded and emitted, which is not built. Demand is to be
measured with the instrument off.

  (`.objcmp/s101/probe.patch`, tallied by `classes.py`). Over the corpus
  (compiler, standard library alone, tests, every project, example and tool,

  non-copy `change` **4,282 -> 84** (`BinaryExpression` 3,650 -> 0,

  reads the cells non-zero there.

  `Option<u8>` 28), operands of `-` and `?:` in `future_combinator.cryo`,

### 8.486 A call's arguments, a for-loop binding and a static call's owner are answered where they are written - 2026-10-03

## Why

After 8.485 the type check after monomorphization still changed 84 types
in non-generic bodies and 22 call targets.  Measured by shape (probe
`.objcmp/s101/probe.patch`, corpus runs `c2` -> `c8`), three were first-pass
or monomorphization gaps with one cause each:

```cryo
o.unwrap_or(0)                 // o: Option<u8> - `0` typed i32 first, u8 after
a.push(Option::None)           // a: Array<Option<i32>> - bare `Option` first
for (mut i: i64 = 0; await aw_lt(i, 3); i++) { }   // `0` typed i32 first, i64 after
Token::<i32>::new(7)           // `new` in `implement<T> struct Token<T>`: pinned only after mono
HashSet::<i32>::default()      // a trait's static method on a generic owner: the same
```

* A method call's arguments took their expected types from
  `param_types_from_template_decl`, which scanned a template's declaration
  by the method's leaf and knew struct and class templates only, and
  returned their parameters unsubstituted; an enum instantiation not minted
  yet (`Option<u8>`) got none.
* A `for` loop's binding typed its initializer with no expected type and
  never checked it against the declared type - in every `for` loop; it was
  visible only where the async lowering turned the binding into an
  assignment the pass after monomorphization re-typed.
* The owner stash of a static call on a generic owner found the method by
  scanning the declaration's own methods by the path's leaf, so a method
  written in an impl block or a trait got no stash, and monomorphization,
  which needs it, left the call to the pass after it.

## What changed

* `lookup_method_param_types`, for an instantiation not minted yet, reads
  the parameters off the candidates the selection itself tries on it
  (`collect_on_template`, shared with `check_args_on_template`), seen
  through it, merged where they agree (`agreed_candidate_params`).
  `param_types_from_template_decl` and `scan_decl_method_param_types` are
  deleted.
* The `for` loop's binding goes through `check_var_decl` and
  `register_var_decl_local`, as a declaration statement does; its own rule
  (an annotation is required unless the initializer is a lambda) stays.
  Four `0u32` suffixes this made redundant (W0014) are dropped
  (`declaration_emitter.cryo`, `future/reactor.cryo`).
* `stash_static_owner_bindings_for` reads the method recorded where the call
  is written (`record_template_static`); monomorphization's
  `specialize_static_method_on_generic_owner` admits a non-generic static
  method held by the template's declaration, one of its impl blocks
  (`template_holds`) or a trait's declaration, and binds it on the minted
  owner by that identity (`path_method_on`), as it already did for one held
  by the declaration.
* `scripts/spelling-flow.py` counts a map method's key passed as an `arg`
  as it counts one passed as a `sarg`.  The first change gives calls on an
  unminted `HashMap<string, ..>` their key parameter's type, which turns
  those records from `sarg` into `arg`; the old check then lost 16 map reads
  and 9 writes it had listed.  Its self-test is the pair: with the new
  compiler the old check fails 8 of its cases (`map-outside`,
  `map-resolved`, `write-outside` and the origins behind them), the new one
  passes all 14, and it passes all 14 with the old compiler too.

## Behaviour change

A `for` loop binding whose initializer does not fit its declared type is
refused, as any declaration is: `for (mut j: i32 = s.length(); ..)` is
E0200 and `for (mut i: u8 = 300; ..)` E0010, both compiled before. No
corpus program is one (409 outcomes identical).  New negative test
`E0200_for_init_narrowing`.

## Evidence

### 8.487 The generic template registry is keyed by definition - 2026-10-03

## Why

Ruling 12: the registry of generic templates is keyed by identity. It was
keyed by the template's path text (`name_index`, interned qualified name to
entry), so two definitions written under one path were one key: a generic
type and a generic function `Wrap` in one module left one template, the
function's, and the type's `type_index` slot pointed at it.

```cryo
type struct Wrap<T> { v: T; }
function Wrap<T>(x: T) -> Wrap<T> { return Wrap::<T> { v: x }; }
const a: Wrap<i32> = Wrap::<i32> { v: 3 };   // E0204: no field `v` on `Wrap`
```

Every reader already held a definition (`template_of(def)`,
`register_impl_block(target)`) and turned it back into its path to ask;
`template_in(container, leaf)` composed `owner::leaf` text as the key - rule
four, identity text rebuilt into a key.

## What changed

* `name_index` is deleted.  `def_entries` holds each template's entry by its
  definition's slot in the definition table, as the declaration index's
  per-definition stores do; `register_template` writes it,
  `entry_index_of` reads it for `template_of` and `register_impl_block`.
* `GenericRegistry::template_in` is deleted.  A template named as a member
  of a path's segment is found as any member is, through the member-function
  door: `CompilationContext::member_template(container, leaf)` takes the
  family `lookup_family_entries` hands back for the segment's definition
  and answers the one entry whose definition is a template (null for none,
  or for several).  A module-qualified value asks `template_of` of the
  callee the name layer bound.
* `member_template_key` stays as the registration's display name and the
  name its placeholder type is minted under; nothing finds a template by it.

## Evidence

### 8.488 A registered type is kept under its definition only - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity, and rule four forbids
an identity's text becoming a key.  `register_type` kept each type twice:
under its definition (`def_types`, read by `type_of_def`) and under the
definition's path text (`type_map`, read by `lookup_type`).  The path copy
had five readers, every one holding an identity it turned back into text or
a primitive's spelling:

* `impl_owner`, `type_name_key` and `spelling_type_answered` asked a
  primitive's type by the spelling its `Res::PrimTy` stamp carries;
* `scope_qualifier_type` asked a primitive the same way, and a clone's
  segment by `lookup_type_name(spec_owner)` - the definition's path, as a key;
* `register_methods_through` asked a by-value `this` receiver's type by
  `lookup_type_name(owner)`, the same.

```cryo
// a primitive's type, read by the spelling the stamp carries
implement i32 { twice(this) -> i32 { return this * 2; } }
// a clone's segment: after substitution `T::default()` names `i32`
function zero<T>() -> T where T: Default { return T::default(); }
```

## What changed

* `type_map` and `DeclarationIndex::lookup_type` are deleted, with
  `TypeUtils::lookup_type_exact`, the funnel's forwarding body.
* A primitive's type is read through its definition,
  `type_of_def(defs.primitive(n))`: the primitive table's answer is the
  primitive's identity, and its type is registered under that definition.
* A clone's segment and a by-value receiver read
  `type_of_def(registered_def(ty))`: the definition the type was registered
  as, asked for the type it holds.

## Evidence

* Agreement, old key against new, at every read over the corpus (probe
  `.objcmp/s102/probe.patch`, run `.objcmp/s102/c1`, compiler + stdlib +
  tests + every project, example and tool, the unit leg, each negative
  file): 854,041 reads, **0 differ** - `impl_owner` 709,936, `type_name_key`
  73,443, `scope_qualifier_type` 70,626, `spelling_type_answered` 6.  The
  by-value receiver branch was reached by no corpus program (0 reads): every
  receiver arrived with its type resolved.  95,484 registrations; one path
  held two definitions, `E0207_redefined_type` (a type declared twice, a
  refused program), and no read asked for it.
* Corpus build outcomes identical to the previous run (`.objcmp/s101/cg1`)
  but for the project added since.
* Gates moved: flow list 766 -> 757 (nine paths into the deleted copy: the
  primitive's spelling 4, a definition's path through `lookup_type_name` 3,
  `register_type`'s write keyed by `path_of` 2; rule three 718 -> 710, rule
  four 48 -> 47); residue 226 -> 224 (J 150 -> 149, the `type_name_key`
  primitive row; N 25 -> 24, the funnel body); lane `LOOKUP` 5 -> 3
  (`type_name_key`'s call and the funnel's), `LOOKUP_OTHER` 46 -> 45 (the
  clone segment's `lookup_type_name`), `DEFID_PATH` 45 -> 44
  (`register_type`'s path read), and `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 69 -> 61: that row counts
  other types' methods named like a store method, and with
  `DeclarationIndex::lookup_type` gone the same-named `lookup_type` methods
  of `drop_insertion` and `move_check` (4 each, over their own local tables)
  stop matching - nothing in those files changed; name-taking functions
  699 -> 697 and pending allows 499 -> 497 (the two deleted functions).
* The residue self-test's fixture named the two deleted methods and took
  their class (S, stamp-derived) from the real classifier, which now holds
  none: no read in the compiler is stamp-derived.  The fixture classes its
  two doors and the funnel's forwarding call itself, as it already injects
  a fixture override for its literal-site case.  With the classifier
  edited and the self-test not, the self-test failed every case ("read
  methods called in the tree with no class: DeclarationIndex::lookup_type,
  TypeUtils::lookup_type_exact"); with both, it reports what it reported
  at HEAD: "baseline accepted, 14 facts and 5 list mutations behaved, 13
  literal-rule cases".
* verify against HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261003-071445`): census, examples,
  lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow OK; objects **0 moved** (5,663 + 1,126);
  its `fast` leg failed on the residue self-test above, and `make

### 8.489 An overload family is keyed by its owner's definition - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  The member-function
door's store - every family of overloads, `func_type_refs` and
`overload_index` - was keyed by `family_slot`: the owner's PATH text and the
leaf, packed (`path_of(owner) << 32 | leaf`).  The owner arrived as an
identity (`FamilyOwner::Def` or `FamilyOwner::Type`) and was turned into its
path to build the key - rule four, identity text become a key, in a shape
the flow check cannot see because the key is built arithmetically.  Two
owners written under one path shared their families:

```cryo
namespace P1::Main;                       // src/main.cryo
type struct Sub { x: i32; }
implement struct Sub { get(&this) -> i32 { return 1; } }

namespace P1::Main::Sub;                  // src/main/sub.cryo
function get() -> i32 { return 2; }       // the module's `get`: same old key as the method's
```

That program is refused (E0205, "`P1::Main::Sub` is a module"), and the
corpus has no compiling program in which two family owners share a path, so
no output depended on it.

## What changed

* `family_slot` keys by the owner's definition: a `Def`'s own, a `Type`'s
  the definition it was registered as, by its slot in the definition table,
  one above it so the root (no definition) keeps a key of its own.  The
  door still takes (owner identity, leaf).  Every family read and write goes
  through `family_slot`, so the whole store moves at once.
* `family_owner_path` stays, for text only: the qualified name the Cryo
  mangling encodes and the family as a diagnostic spells it.
* `family_slot`'s pending allow becomes a written reason.

## Evidence

* Agreement, old key against new, at every `family_slot` call over the
  corpus (probe `.objcmp/s102/probe-f.patch`, run `.objcmp/s102/c2`, same
  population as 8.488's): 1,074,439 distinct (old, new) pairs over 411
  compilations, **no key mapping to two keys on either side**
  (`.objcmp/s102/pairs.sh`).  Control: the program above, through the same
  probe and script, reports one old key mapping to two new ones; the
  same program with the type renamed (`Sbx`) builds and reports none.  Build outcomes identical
  to 8.488's run.
* Predicted and seen: flow list 757 unchanged (the arithmetic key is one of
  the facts' listed blind spots), lane counts unchanged, pending allows
  497 -> 496.
* verify against HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261003-092343`): census, examples,
  lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK; objects **0 moved** (5,663 +
  1,126).
* Jake's rulings of 2026-10-03 (95-104) are recorded in the appendix of
  `docs/resolution-rules.md` with this change; none is built here.
* The compiler checks its own source clean; clean build 331 warnings, the
  same (code, file) set.

### 8.490 A trait's declaration is kept under the trait's definition - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  The generic
registry's table of trait declarations - the declaration default-method
synthesis clones from and the trait-method door finds a method's position
in - was written and read by the trait's PATH text (`trait_decl_index`,
interned path to position), although `register_trait_decl` and
`get_trait_decl` were each handed the trait's definition: rule four, an
identity's text become the key.

```cryo
type trait Show { show(&this) -> i32 { return 1; } }
type struct P { v: i32; }
implement trait Show for P { }        // the default is cloned from Show's declaration
```

## What changed

* `trait_decl_index` is deleted.  `trait_decl_slots` holds each trait's
  position in `trait_decl_nodes` by the definition's slot in the definition
  table, as the template entries are held (`def_entries`);
  `trait_decl_position` reads it for `register_trait_decl` and
  `get_trait_decl`.

## Evidence

* Agreement, old key against new, over the corpus (probe
  `.objcmp/s102/probe-t.patch`, run `.objcmp/s102/c4`): the old key's answer
  is right exactly when the position it finds was registered under the same
  definition (`trait_decl_keys`).  16,747 registrations, none finding
  another definition's entry under its path; 5,065,616 reads, **0 differ**.
  Build outcomes identical to 8.489's run.  The probe counts on a small
  trait program (45 registrations, 16,406 reads,
  `.objcmp/s102/ctlt/ok.cryo`); a collision could not be built: two traits
  under one path are refused before registration (E0207, and E0205 for a
  trait beside a module of its path).
* Gates moved: lane `DEFID_PATH` 44 -> 41 (predicted); flow list 757 -> 751:
  predicted 2-3, measured 6 - each of the three `path_of`-keyed accesses is
  listed under rule three and rule four both, as 8.411's single path was.
* verify against HEAD (`.verify/runs/20261003-101135`): census, examples,
  lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK; objects **0 moved** (5,663 +
  1,126).
* The compiler checks its own source clean; clean build 331 warnings, the
  same (code, file) set.

## Measured, not converted: the method return-type table

`DeclarationIndex.method_returns`, a method's return by (owner type, method
leaf), measured over the same corpus (probe `.objcmp/s102/probe-m.patch`,
run `.objcmp/s102/c3`): 175 keys are written by two different methods, 10
of them with different returns (`string::parse_int`,
`Executor::block_on`, `thread::Builder::spawn`, an inherent method beside
a trait's of one leaf, two instances of one generic method), and the last
write wins.  Of 1,092,136 reads, 3 hit such a key, all in
`path_call_generic_method` (`Q::id<U>`, instances returning `u64` and
`i32`), where the call's pin replaces the answer and the project passes.
Its eight readers ask it BEFORE a method is selected, so none holds the
method's definition to key it by: the conversion is each reader reading
the return of the method it selects (a trait's declared method through the
`trait-method` door), not a re-key.

### 8.491 A method call's type is read off the method it selects; the method return-type table is deleted - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity, and rule one has a
name answered once.  `DeclarationIndex.method_returns` held a method's
return under (owner type, method leaf): a private copy of the
member-function door with one slot per leaf, where an owner's two methods
of one leaf - an inherent method beside a trait's, two traits' methods,
two instances of a generic method - kept whichever was registered last.
Its eight readers asked it BEFORE a method was selected, so a call was
typed by a guess the selection then had to overwrite, and a call the
selection refused kept the guess.

```cryo
type trait Alpha { go(&this) -> string; }
type trait Beta { go(&this) -> i64; }
type struct P { v: i32; }
implement trait Alpha for P { go(&this) -> string { return "a"; } }
implement trait Beta for P { go(&this) -> i64 { return 5; } }

const s: string = P::go(&p);   // E0156 (a tie), and before this entry a
                               // second, false E0200: the refused call
                               // was typed `i64`, Beta's, registered last
```

## What changed

* The table, its writer `register_method`, its reader
  `lookup_method_return` (the index's and `TypeUtils`'s) and the trait
  arm's registration into it are deleted.
* Every entry of the member-function door keeps its return in its
  owner's parameters (`entry_owner_return`): an implement block's method
  returns in the block's own parameters, bound to the owner's through the
  head, which is what a reader substituting the owner's arguments needs.
  `register_signature` takes it, so no entry is without one.
* A static call (`Owner::m(..)`) is selected first and typed after
  (`type_static_call`): a pinned call has its entry's return; a call the
  selection typed keeps that type (a generic method's template, its own
  parameters bound by the call); otherwise the method it selects: a
  trait's declared method through the `trait-method` door for a call
  through the trait's own path, the method recorded where the call is
  written on a generic owner (by its definition), the one method an
  impl-qualified head's implementation delivers, or the owner's only
  method of the leaf.  When nothing is selected the call has no type;
  the selection reported why.  `owner_declares_member` asks the member
  doors whether the owner declares the member at all, and a call whose
  owner does is argument-checked whether or not it was typed
  (`claimed`): the table's guess was what had let a refused call reach
  the argument check.
* `try_resolve_type_or_variant` no longer asks the owner's method: that
  was a second answer to the question `try_resolve_static_method` had
  just asked with the same owner and leaf.
* The expected-type rewrite of a generic static return answers the
  expected type itself; it asked the expected type's method of the same
  leaf, which is a different owner's method whenever the return's base
  is not the call's owner.
* A generic receiver's impl-block method (`resolve_method_return_via_template`)
  reads the return of the method the call's selection chose.
* The bound scans (`scan_param_bounds`, `bound_trait_declaring`) read a
  trait's declared method's return through the `trait-method` door, by
  the trait's definition (`trait_declared_return`,
  `GenericRegistry::trait_item_return`).
* The for-in's "has an `iter` method" asks the member-function door.

## Evidence

* Agreement, old key against new, over the corpus (compiler, stdlib,
  tests, every project, example and tool, the unit leg, each negative
  file; `.objcmp/s103/corpus.sh`).  Run `c1` (probe
  `.objcmp/s103/probe-m.patch`): at each of the eight readers, the table
  against the member doors' answer - a trait owner through the
  `trait-method` door, a type through its family; **1,073,816 reads, 0
  differ** (R1 static path 532,210; R2 the template's method 12,001; R3
  the second asking 261,209, every one answered nothing; R4 the expected
  type's method 83,704; R5 a generic receiver's impl-block method 74,236;
  R6/R7 the bound scans 84,704 and 25,745; R8 the for-in 7).  Control:
  the comparator mutated to read a family's first entry instead of its
  last reports 4 differ on `IgTn::go` (`i32` against `i64`) where the
  unmutated one reports agree (`.objcmp/s103/ctl1`).
* Run `c2` (probe `.objcmp/s103/probe-sel.patch`): what a static call
  selects, after the pin.  Pinned 177,811 (6,922 where the table's
  guess was not the pinned entry's return - `NonNull::new` guessed
  `NonNull<T>`, the pin's instance `NonNull<u8>` - and the pin's answer
  replaced it); the recorded template method 93,170 (4 of them a
  trait's declared method) and the trait's own path 6, all agree, plus
  1 (`BetaG::go(&r, 7)`, a generic trait method through its trait's
  path) that the trait's own path answers once it is asked first; the
  only method 2, agree; nothing selected 7, every
  one a call the selection refused (an E0156 tie, an impl-qualified
  arity or missing member), which the table had typed with the method
  registered last.  The expected-type rewrite: in all 6,808 reads where
  the expected type's method answered, it answered the expected type
  itself.
* Run `c3` (probe `.objcmp/s103/probe-r5.patch`): the generic receiver's
  method from the call's selection against the table, 74,236 reads, 0
  differ (73,873 with a selection, 363 without, where the table had
  nothing either).
* Behaviour: run `c4`/`c5` against `c2` (the tip's behaviour), log for
  log over 411 builds with the output directory normalized.  `c4` found
  one regression, fixed before this entry: `E0215_impl_qualified_arity`

  call whose arguments fit nothing was left untyped and so skipped the
  argument check.  The head now selects the method it delivers, and a
  claimed call is argument-checked untyped.  `c5`, with that fixed: the

* `path_call_generic_method` (`Q::id(&q, 41u64)`) is the shape the

## Not converted

* `refused_methods`, the set of methods whose written signature the name

### 8.492 The arena keeps no table of user-defined types by name - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  The type arena
kept five get-or-create tables of user-defined types - struct, class,
enum, trait, alias - keyed by the qualified name's text
(`decl_type_key`: namespace `::` leaf), so a second creation under one
name answered the first's type.  That is the defect 8.488 removed from
the declaration index, one level down: two definitions written under one
name became one type.

```cryo
type struct CfD { a: i32; }
type struct CfD { b: i64; }   // E0207; and the second definition was
                              // handed the first's type
```

## What changed

* `struct_cache`, `class_cache`, `enum_cache`, `trait_cache` and
  `alias_cache` are deleted.  The creators allocate: a definition's type
  is created once, where it is declared, and kept under the definition
  by the declaration index (`register_type`, `type_of_def`); the name
  they are handed is the type's own, for display and mangling.
* `add_name_alias` and `reserve_spec_names`, which wrote specialization
  names into the tables, are deleted: nothing read them.

## Evidence

* Census over the corpus (probe `.objcmp/s103/probe-arena.patch`, run
  `c6`): every creation logged as a hit or a miss with its site, every
  table write with its writer, and at each site holding a definition, a
  hit compared with the definition its type was registered for.
  **67,405 creations, 1 hit**: `E0207_redefined_type`'s second `CfD`,
  handed the first's type (`collide`).  No definition was created twice.
  `reserve_spec_names` wrote 42,176 entries and none was read;
  `add_name_alias` and monomorphization's `create_concrete_type` were
  never reached.  The language server builds a fresh context per
  recompile, so no arena is declared into twice there either.  Control:
  the same probe reports the E0207 hit and its writer, so the zeros
  elsewhere are its answer.
* `E0207_redefined_type`'s output is unchanged.
* Gates moved: lane `ARENA_WRITE` 43 -> 41 (the two deleted writers'
  calls); flow list 747 -> 708 (predicted about 39: every path into the
  creators' and the two writers' tables, rule three 35, rule four 4);
  pending allows 492 -> 484; name-taking 696 -> 694.

### 8.493 A generic function's placeholder type is one per template - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  A generic function
template's placeholder type - the type the generic registry keeps its
instantiations under (`type_index`, `template_of_type`) - was minted
get-or-create by the function's qualified name.  Cryo overloads by
signature, so two generic functions of one name in one module are two
templates under one name: they shared one placeholder, the registry
answered the last-registered overload for both, and the compiler crashed
instantiating the overload it was not asked for.

```cryo
function pick<T>(a: T) -> T { return a; }
function pick<T>(a: T, b: T) -> T { return b; }

const x: i32 = pick(3);   // the compiler segfaulted here
```

## What changed

* `TypeArena.func_template_cache` is deleted; `create_function_template`
  allocates.  Each template's placeholder is created once, where the
  template is registered (`register_generic_template`,
  `register_static_method_templates`), and kept on its entry, which the
  registry keeps under the definition.

## Evidence

* Census over the corpus (probe `.objcmp/s103/probe-ft.patch`, run `c7`):
  each creation logged as new, again for the same definition, or for
  another.  **17,575 creations (15,825 functions, 1,750 static methods),
  0 again**: no template is registered twice, and no corpus program
  overloads a generic function.  Control `.objcmp/s103/ctl4`: the same
  probe reports `collide` for `Ctl4::Main::pick`.  Build outcomes
  identical to the run before.
* New project `generic_function_overloads_are_two_templates`, declared in
  `tests/started-passing`: the HEAD compiler crashes (exit 139, no
  diagnostic), this one builds it and it runs.
* Not fixed, found beside it: with both overloads declared, the
  two-argument call `pick(4, 5)` is refused "no overload of `pick` accepts
  these arguments" (E0214) before and after this change, where the same
  call to a lone two-argument `pick` builds (`.objcmp/s103/ctl6`).
  Overload selection among generic free functions; separate.
* Gates moved: flow list 708 -> 702 (every path into the placeholder
  table, rule three 4, rule four 2); pending allows 484 -> 483.

### 8.494 An implicit converter is kept by its definition, and a refused method by its family - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  Two stores in the
declaration index were not:

* `refused_methods`, the methods whose written signature the name layer
  refused, was keyed by the owner's `TypeRef` and the method's leaf - the
  key shape of the method return-type table §8.491 deleted, a private copy
  of the member-function door's question.
* `implicit_converters` was keyed correctly (the argument and return
  types) but held, as its value, the converter's owner's bare name and its
  leaf.  A use site rebuilt a call from those names and resolved it again:
  a free-function converter's name was looked up in the scope of the CALL
  SITE, and a static converter's owner was taken from the type it RETURNS,
  so a converter declared on another type was looked for on the wrong one.

```cryo
![implicit]
function to_celsius(value: i32) -> Celsius { .. }
const d: i32 = show(4);           // was E0214 "mismatched types"

implement struct Meters {
    ![implicit]
    static to_feet(m: Meters) -> Feet { .. }
}
const f: i32 = show(Meters { v: 2 });   // was E0233 "cannot find `Meters::to_feet`"
```

## What changed

* `refused_methods` is keyed by `family_slot` - the owner's definition and
  the leaf, the member-function door's own key.  `pack_method_key` is
  deleted with it.
* `implicit_converters` holds the converter's `DefId`.  The registration
  walk takes no owner name (`register_converter_methods`,
  `register_converter_fn`).  `build_implicit_conversion` builds the call
  from the definition: a function's identifier carries `Res::Def` of it; a
  method's path names the type that declares it (the definition's parent)
  and the call is pinned to that method's entry (`method_entry_on`) before
  it is resolved.  An owner that is a generic template not yet built

* `generic_converter_methods` and `register_generic_converter_method`, one
  write and no reader, are deleted.

### 8.495 The constant table is keyed by definition, and the duplicate-type check by parent and leaf - 2026-10-03

## Why

Rule two keys every declaration store by an identity.  Two stores keyed by
composed path text remained:

* `ConstantTable` (`by_qualified`, `enums_by_qualified`) was keyed by the
  interned text `module::name`.  The name layer composed it at the
  declaration (`intern_qualified`), and every reader rebuilt it from an
  identity it already held: a bare constant's stamp turned back into its
  path (`path_of(d)`), a module path's constant as `path_of(module) +
  "::" + member`, an enum by `path_of(q)` - rule four's shape.
* The E0207 duplicate-type check in the type-declaration pass kept a list
  of `decl_type_key(name, namespace, file)` texts.

```cryo
const N: i64 = 3;
type enum Sz { A = 2; B = 5; }
mut a: i32[N];        // folded from the stamp's definition
mut b: i32[Sz::B];    // the enum by its definition, the variant by its leaf
```

## What changed

* `ConstantTable.by_def` / `enums_by_def`, keyed by the definition's
  slot.  `register` takes the constant's `DefId` (the one the name layer
  just declared), `register_enum` the enum's own (`node.def`, so
  `record_enum_decl` now runs after the enum is declared).
  `intern_qualified` and `NameResolver::record_const_value_in` are deleted.
* Readers: a bare name reads its stamp (`index_of(d)`); a module path reads
  the constant the name layer bound on the node (`member_def`); an enum
  path reads its base definition.  `fold_scoped_res` takes the node, not
  the member's spelling.
* The duplicate-type check keys `(parent definition, declared leaf)`; its
  message prints the second definition's path.
* `scripts/ns-migration/residue_classify.py` drops the class for the deleted
  `intern_qualified`; the residue self-test's three literal-rule cases that
  used it as a fixture use `ModuleGraph::find_module_index`, another method
  the tables class.

  `.objcmp/s104/c5`, probe `.objcmp/s104/edit_probe2.py`):
  * constants and enums: 355,099 registrations (340,839 constants, 14,260
    enums), every one with a definition, none colliding; 2,399 reads -
    2,365 bare stamps (1 a miss), 27 module paths (17 integer, 10 real), 6
    enum variants - old key and definition agree on all.
  * duplicate types: 67,045 checks, every declaration with a definition;
    1 duplicate (`E0207_redefined_type`), found by both keys; 0 disagree.
* Control: the converted lookups asked one slot off refuse both array
  sizes above (E0239 twice); the converted compiler builds and runs it

### 8.496 Generic functions overloading one name are each called by the arity that selects them - 2026-10-03

## Why

Two generic functions may overload one name (§8.493 gave each its own
placeholder type).  A call to the one the name's stamp did not name was
refused, and with the refusal fixed in sema the two instantiations at the
same type arguments still collided:

```cryo
function pick<T>(a: T) -> T { return a; }
function pick<T>(a: T, b: T) -> T { return b; }

const y: i32 = pick(4, 5);           // was E0214 "no overload of `pick` accepts these arguments"
const w: i32 = pick::<i32>(8, 9);    // was E0200
```

* `find_fn_template_for_call` asked only the template the identifier's
  stamp names - one definition of the family - and rejected it on arity,
  so the call fell to the non-generic overload selection over `T`-typed
  signatures.
* A function specialization is pinned, and its clone registered, by the
  family `(root, minted identifier)`.  The identifier is the mangling of
  the template's NAME and its arguments, so `pick<i32>(a)` and
  `pick<i32>(a, b)` are one family holding two clones, and codegen refused
  the pin (E0900 "`4pick$Li$G` names several functions").

## What changed

* `find_fn_template_for_call` reads the callee's family (the
  member-function door, by the stamped definition's owner and leaf): the
  one declaration of the call's arity is the call's template, if it is
  generic; two of that arity are the overload selection's to tell apart.
* A function specialization's family is owned by its template's
  definition: the clone registers under `FamilyOwner::Def(copy_of)`
  (`type_resolution.cryo`), monomorphization pins `Def(entry.def)`
  (`call_specializer.cryo`, a call and a function value), and sema's two
  turbofish pins name `Def(template.def)` instead of the root family
  `minted_family` gave a bare identifier.  The clone's linker symbol is
  passed explicitly and does not change.

## Evidence

* New project `generic_function_overloads_select_by_arity`, declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`: five calls, inferred and turbofished, at both
  arities.  The HEAD compiler refuses it (E0214 x2, E0200 x3); this one
  builds it and it runs.
* Full corpus with the change (`.objcmp/s104/c7`): every build log
  identical to the previous commit's run (`c6`) except warning positions in
  `compiler` and `tools/CryoLSP`.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261003-232946`): every gate OK; tests 5,825 objects
  (the new project's 54 left out as declared), examples 1,126, 0 moved.
* Clean build: 331 warnings, the same (code, file) set as 8.495's.
* Gates moved: projects 168 -> 169.  Lane counts, the flow list (684) and
  the residue list unchanged.

### 8.497 A generic owner's path substitutes its written arguments into any return - 2026-10-04

## Why

A method of a generic owner that returns its bare type parameter, called
through a path that writes the owner's arguments, kept the parameter as
its type:

```cryo
type struct Box2<T> { v: T; }
implement struct Box2<T> {
    get(&this) -> T { return this.v; }
    at(&this) -> T* { return &this.v; }
}

const c: i32 = Box2::<i32>::get(&bx);   // was E0200: found `T`
const p: i32* = Box2::<i32>::at(&bx);   // was E0200
```

`try_resolve_generic_return` substituted the owner's written arguments
only into a return that is an unresolved instantiation
(`Result<Arc<T, A>, E>`), and returned anything else - a bare `T`, a `T*` -
untouched.

## What changed

* The owner's written arguments are substituted into any return that
  holds a type parameter.  The expected-type fallback still answers only
  an instantiation of the generic the expected type names.

## Evidence

* New project `generic_owner_path_returns_parameter`, declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`: the HEAD compiler refuses it (E0200 twice);
  this one builds it and it runs.
* Not changed: the same calls written without the owner's arguments,
  `Box2::get(&bx)`, are still E0200 twice (`.objcmp/s104/bx2`) - a bare
  generic name inferring its arguments from the call is ruling 98's, and
  not built.
* Predicted beforehand: a few movers, from programs typing such a call
  without a declared type and relying on the pass after
  monomorphization.  Measured: none.  Full corpus (`.objcmp/s104/c8`):
  416 build logs, 0 differ from the previous commit's run (`c7`).
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261003-235452`): every gate OK; tests 5,879 objects
  (the new project's 54 left out as declared), examples 1,126, 0 moved.
* Clean build: 331 warnings, the same (code, file) set as 8.496's.
* Gates moved: projects 169 -> 170.

### 8.498 Three of `module_named`'s four outside callers ask by identity - 2026-10-04

## Why

`ModuleGraph::module_named`, the module-by-path door, is ruled private to
the name layer and the module loader.  Four callers outside them turned
text into a module:

* the export check (`check_export_grants`), which rebuilt the exporting
  module from the export's path text and asked whether `path::item` is a
  module, though the name layer had answered both where the export is
  written;
* `mark_implicit_closure`, handed `LangModule::Prelude.path()` /
  `LangModule::Interp.path()` as strings, and beside it the prelude
  namespace found by comparing every module's namespace with that path;
* codegen's AST-node allocation, which named the family
  `"compiler::codegen::ast_arena"` / `"cryo_ast_arena_alloc"` by literal
  text (`module_family_named`);
* `module_family_named` itself, for the parent of a name the compiler
  minted qualified.

## What changed

* The name layer records, on an `export`, the entries that name a
  declaration the module marks `private` and no sub-module
  (`ImportDeclNode.private_export_entries`), in the branch that already
  decided so; the export check reports E0241 from that record, still once
  the graph is whole.
* `ModuleGraph::lang_module(m: LangModule)` answers a module the compiler
  imports on a program's behalf from the fixed `LangModule` table;
  `mark_implicit_closure` takes the `LangModule`, and the prelude set is
  read off the graph's answer.
* `LangItem::AstArenaAlloc` (`compiler::codegen::ast_arena::cryo_ast_arena_alloc`),
  claimed where the function is registered like every function item;
  `emit_raw_alloc` resolves it through `lang_function`, as `Alloc`.
* Not converted: `module_family_named`'s remaining caller,
  `minted_parent_family`, parses the parent out of a minted qualified name
  - the family key's write side.
* Not done: making `module_named` private.  Cryo's `private` confines a
  method to the one module that declares it, and the name layer
  (`resolver/name_resolution.cryo`) and the loader (`module_loader.cryo`)
  are modules of their own; `protected`'s nesting reach exists only for
  classes; and the language is frozen for this work.  How the ruling is
  to be expressed is open.
* `scripts/ns-migration/approved-names.tsv`: `module_named`'s callers per
  file - `instance.cryo` 3 -> 0, `module_graph.cryo` 1 -> 2 (`lang_module`)
  - and its reason text drops the three uses that are gone.

## Evidence

* Full corpus (`.objcmp/s104/c9`) against the previous commit's run (`c8`):
  417 build logs, the only differences in `compiler` and `tools/CryoLSP`:
  one W0005 gone with the deleted prelude scan (its `u32` counter against
  an `i64` length), and warning positions.  `reexport_private` reports the
  same E0241; no other source of E0241 remains, so the record is what
  fires.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261004-002557`): every gate OK; tests 5,933 and examples
  1,126 objects, 0 moved.  The compiler's own objects (where the AST
  allocator call now resolves by language item) are not among them; the
  stage-2 compiler builds the LSP, the other OS and the census.
* Clean build: 330 warnings, the (code, file) set of 8.497's less that one
  W0005 in `instance.cryo`.
* Gates moved: flow list 684 -> 681; name-taking 686 -> 685
  (`mark_implicit_closure`); residue 215 -> 211 (J 143 -> 139); lane

### 8.499 An associated type is found through one door, and asked by its position after that - 2026-10-04

## Why

An associated type (`type Item;` in a trait) has no definition of its own;
its identity is its trait and its position among the trait's associated
types.  It was looked up by its leaf in seven places, none of them a door:

* `TraitDeclNode::assoc_type_index` and `lookup_assoc_type`, the trait's
  declaration asked by leaf;
* `ImplBlockNode::lookup_assoc_binding`, an implementation's `type Item =
  ..;` (or the positional header's binding) asked by leaf - mostly with the
  leaf of the trait's own declaration (`adecl.name`), identity text fed
  back into a lookup;
* `ResolutionContext::lookup_assoc_binding`, `This::Item`'s binding by
  leaf;
* `TypeResolver::resolve_concrete_member` and `concrete_projection`, handed
  the leaf by six callers, four of which held the position already;
* the symbolic projection type (`AssocProjectionType`) carried only the
  leaf, so every reduction, the bound-argument substitution
  (`subst_assoc_by_member`, which matched a projection by leaf whatever its
  trait), the projection-bound scan (`scan_projection_bounds`) and the
  `async` future checks compared leaves.

```cryo
function first<I>(it: mut &I) -> Option<I::Item> where I: Iterator {
    return it.next();   // `Item` is found once: (Iterator, "Item") -> position 0
}
```

## What changed

* **Door `assoc-type`**: `TraitDeclNode::assoc_type_index` - the trait's
  declaration (in hand) plus a leaf, to the position.  Listed in
  `docs/resolution-rules.md`'s door table with its `/// Door` marker and a
  written reason.  Its callers are where a leaf is written or minted: a
  written projection (`I::Item`, `This::Item`, a bound's subject), an
  implementation's written binding, the `async` desugar's minted
  `<Method>Fut`, and `await`'s `Output` of the language's `Future`.
* `AssocProjectionType.slot`: the position, set where the projection is
  made (`create_assoc_projection` takes it).  `member` stays for display and
  mangling only.  The reducers (`reduce_projections`,
  `reduce_assoc_projections`) read `slot`.
* `resolve_concrete_member` and `concrete_projection` take the position;
  `project_member` asks the door once and `project_slot` projects by
  position (the where-bound deriver's abstract subject uses it directly).
* An implementation's bindings carry a position (`assoc_binding_slots`):
  a written one is placed through the door when the block is first asked
  (`ImplBlockNode::assoc_binding_at`), a writer holding the position
  records it (`bind_assoc_slot`: the positional header, the `async`
  lowering).  A written name the trait does not declare stays unplaced, so
  a trait that gains the type later (the `async` desugar) still answers.
* `This::Item`'s binding in a resolution context is keyed by (trait,
  position) (`AssocBinding`).
* `subst_assoc_slot` (was `subst_assoc_by_member`) replaces a projection
  of the bound trait's associated type at that position - the trait now
  has to match too.  `scan_projection_bounds` matches a bound's subject to
  the receiver's projection by (trait, position) (`bound_subject_is`).
* `FunctionDeclNode.async_fut_slot` (was `async_fut_assoc`, a name): the
  position of an `async` trait method's future; `impl_binds_assoc_via_async`,
  `bind_async_trait_assoc` and `awaited_keeps_recv_ptr` compare positions.
* Deleted: `TraitDeclNode::lookup_assoc_type`, both `lookup_assoc_binding`s.
* `scripts/lane-gate.py`: the two `SCANNED_ARRAYS` entries for the deleted
  scans (`ImplBlockNode.assoc_binding_names`,
  `ResolutionContext.assoc_bindings`) go - rule 1c refused them as stale;
  `TraitDeclNode.assoc_types`' reason names the door.
  `scripts/ns-migration/residue_classify.py`: the three deleted methods'
  and the deleted scan's classes go, the door's reason is rewritten;
  `residue.md` regenerated.
* Not converted: `create_assoc_projection` still interns a projection by
  (base, member leaf, trait) - the type's own structure, not a lookup -
  and a projection naming no trait keeps only its leaf (slot -1; nothing
  reduces it, as before).  The method-leaf comparisons beside the
  associated-type ones (`impl_binds_assoc_via_async` and
  `bind_async_trait_assoc` matching an implementation's method to the
  trait's by leaf) are the `trait-method` door's question and stay.

## Evidence

* Agreement, every converted reader computing the old leaf answer beside
  the new position answer (probe build, `.objcmp/s105/u1-probe.patch`),
  full corpus - 417 runs: compiler, stdlib, tests, 185 projects, examples
  and tools, the unit leg, 228 negative files (`.objcmp/s105/c2`): 0
  disagreements;
  sites fired: implementation binding 31,848, `This::Item` binding
  170,813, carried slot against the door at reduction 51,348 + 2,908,
  bound-argument substitution 3,979, projection-bound scan 1,454, `await`
  future 45, where-bound trait round trip 4 (counts read off interleaved

* Controls, each mutation built alone, over stdlib + tests +
  `examples/13-closures`, against the unmutated probe build (0 BAD, all
  three build): the door answering position + 1 -> 20 binding and 804

  matching position + 1 -> 46 disagreements; the bound scan matching

* Full corpus with the final compiler (`.objcmp/s105/c3`) against HEAD's

  in `compiler` and `tools/CryoLSP` - the same warnings, at positions moved

* `make selfhost-check` at the parent commit (da6a9eed), before this

* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261004-015036`): every gate OK; tests 5,933 and examples

### 8.500 A capturing closure passed to an overloaded function specializes the overload its arguments select - 2026-10-04

## Why

A call that passes a capturing closure to a function-typed parameter of a
free function is pinned to a clone of the callee whose parameter is typed
as the closure's struct (`LambdaSynth::try_specialize_for_closure_args`).
The pass treated the identifier's `Def` stamp as the callee, but a stamp
names a FAMILY - the name layer cannot choose among overloads, and the call
resolver selects the signature by the arguments.  So for an overloaded name
the pass mixed three answers:

* the signature: `func_type_of_res(stamp)`, which answers the signature
  registered LAST in the family (`func_type_refs`, one slot per family);
* the declaration cloned: the FIRST top-level function whose key equals the
  stamp's path (`find_top_level_function_by_key(path_of(def))`);
* the cache of specializations: keyed by the stamp's path.

```cryo
function run(f: (i32) -> i32, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 { return f(x) * 100 + y; }
function run(f: (i32) -> i32, x: i32) -> i32 { return f(x); }

const add_bias = (x: i32) -> i32 { return x + bias; };
run(add_bias, 32);          // cloned the 3-parameter `run` under the 2-parameter signature: compiler crash

pick(add_bias);  pick(add_bias, 1);   // the second call reused the first's clone: E0214
```

Measured before the fix (the HEAD compiler, `.objcmp/s105/cs1`, `cs2`): a
compiler segfault, and E0214 "no overload of `pick` accepts these
arguments"; the same programs with a named function in place of the
closure (`cs1n`, `cs2n`) build and exit 42.  An instrument at the pass
showed the stamp's definition with a 3-parameter AST and a 2-parameter
signature for the first program, and both calls of the second asking the
same definition.  Keying the cache and the AST by the stamp's definition
alone (the first attempt) changed neither outcome: the defect was which
overload, not only how the cache was keyed.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::closure_call_entry`: the entry of the stamp's family the
  call's arguments select, through the selection every call makes
  (`select_family_overload`), each closure argument standing for the
  function type it is called as - what the function-typed parameter it is
  passed to must be.  `LambdaSynth::closure_call_type` answers that type
  (the closure's `__call__` signature after the receiver);
  `is_closure_struct_type` asks it.
* `try_specialize_for_closure_args` takes the selected entry: the
  signature is the entry's own (`entry_signature`), the declaration cloned
  is the one the entry was registered for, found in the root by its
  definition (`top_level_function_of`), and the specialization is cached
  under that definition.  The generic-callee refusal (E0458) still asks
  the stamp's declaration.
* Deleted: `find_top_level_function_by_key` (the root scanned by each
  function's key against the stamp's path).
* Two projects: `closure_argument_selects_overload` (exit 42; declared in
  `tests/started-passing` - the baseline crashes, which is no refusal) and
  `closure_argument_to_two_overloads` (exit 42; declared in
  `tests/started-compiling` - the baseline refuses it with E0214).  Roster
  merged, 2607 -> 2609.
* Not done: `DeclarationIndex::func_type_of_def(d)` still answers the
  family's last-registered signature, not `d`'s own; its other readers (a
  callee's argument hint, `call_resolver.cryo:345`; `resolve_direct_call`'s
  return, `:3060`; `sema.cryo:1810`) are left - a direct call is typed by
  the pin its selection makes, and overloads differing in return type type
  correctly (`.objcmp/s105/ft1`, exit 42).

## Evidence

* Control on the new test: the cache keyed by the stamp's definition again
  (`m4`) -> `closure_argument_to_two_overloads` fails, E0900 (LLVM
  verification); the fix builds both projects and both exit 42.
* `make verify ARGS="--baseline HEAD --require-identical"`
  (`.verify/runs/20261004-023430`): the baseline census fails on exactly
  the two declared projects (the first with exit 0xC0000005, the second
  with E0214); the tree builds both; every gate OK; tests 5,933 and
  examples 1,126 objects, 0 moved, the declared projects' 108 left out.
* Full corpus with the final compiler (`.objcmp/s105/c4`) against unit 1's
  (`c3`): 417 logs, every build status the same, the two new projects
  build; the only differences are the five W0015 positions in
  `call_resolver.cryo` the new function moved, in `compiler` and
  `tools/CryoLSP`.
* Clean build: 330 warnings, the same (code, file) set.
* Gates moved: flow list 653 -> 651 (rule three 616, rule four 35); lane
  DEFID_PATH 38 -> 37 (`lambda_synth.cryo` 2 -> 1, re-pinned); name-taking
  676 -> 675; pending allows 463 -> 462; `decl_fn_key` sites 7 -> 6;
  projects 170 -> 172.

### 8.501 `abs`, `checked_abs` and `clamp` are methods of each numeric primitive - 2026-10-04

## Why

Ruling 112: `abs`, `clamp` and `checked_abs` are per-primitive functions, as
Rust's `i32::abs` is, not generic functions with trait bounds - their bodies
compare with and negate from a literal `0`, and no trait says a literal
converts to `T`.  With them, ruling 82 (an operator the bounds do not
license is refused on the template) can apply to the standard library.

```cryo
const a: i32 = (-5 as i32).abs();
```
