### 8.526 Rulings 139-144: an overloaded value's help types its binding, a call of a non-function is refused, a projection no trait answers is refused where it is written, and monomorphization reports every unbound call - 2026-10-06

## Why

Jake's rulings of 2026-10-06 (appendix, 139-144).  139: E0154 on an
overloaded function used as a value shows the fix.  142: `one()(3)`, a call
through a computed value that is no function, was accepted by the type check
(found by the 113th).  143: a projection whose trait is unknown, or does not
declare the member, was kept as an `AssocProjection` interned by its written
leaf (the arena's `slot = -1` case, STORES.md #7) - and, measured here, it is
not "always an error path": `function c<I>(it: &I) -> I::Item { .. }` with no
bound, or `I::Nope` under a bound that declares no `Nope`, compiled with no
error.  144: with the second type check deleted (8.520), nothing reported a
call left unbound except code generation's own E0636.

```cryo
const f = twice;           // E0154 ... help: give the variable a function type
                           //   to pick one: `const f: (i32) -> i32 = twice;`
const a: i32 = one()(3);   // E0213 expected function, found `i32`
function b<I>(it: &I) -> I::Nope where I: Seq { .. }   // E0203 associated type `Nope` not found for `I`
```

## What changed

* 139 - `CallResolver::value_overload_signature` takes the value node; its
  help line is `give the variable a function type to pick one: `const
  <binding>: <first overload's signature> = <value>;``, the binding being
  the declaration the value is the whole initializer of
  (`SemaState.untyped_binding` / `untyped_init`, set by an unannotated
  declaration), else `f`.
* 142 - a computed callee whose type is no function is E0213 at the callee,
  "expected function, found `T`", label "call expression requires
  function" (`refuse_call_of_non_function`); the call's type is invalid.
  E0213 `NON_CALLABLE` was declared and never emitted; it is used rather
  than a new number beside it (question for Jake).
* 143 - trait declarations are registered in the generic registry by
  NameDeclaration (`forward_declare_node`), before any module's names are
  resolved, and TypeResolution's second registration of the same node is
  deleted.  The name layer collects each projection written on a type
  parameter - a qualified name stamped `TypeRelative(GenericParam, 1)`, or
  a `where`-clause subject - and, once the module's bounds are all in
  (`check_param_projections`), asks the `assoc-type` door of each bound:
  none declares the member, or two do, is E0203 where it is written and the
  annotation is stamped `Err`.  `This::Member` is refused where `This`
  stands for no trait or for one that declares no such type
  (`check_this_projection`).  `ProjectionAnnotation.refused` carries the
  refusal on a projection node (it has no stamp), and
  `TypeAnnotation::refused` reads it, so a signature reporter does not
  report it again.  `TypeResolver::project_member` returns invalid in that
  case; it no longer mints a leaf-keyed projection.  Supertraits are not
  consulted, as the type resolver's `bound_declaring` does not.
* 144 - `MonoCallSpecializer`: every body is walked through `walk_body`,
  which records the function the calls are in; each walked call left
  without a pin is recorded, and `report_unbound_calls` (run by
  `CompilerInstance::monomorphize` after the last module's queued binds)
  reports each one nothing binds - no pin, and not a call through a
  function-typed local, a constructor, a variant, a function-typed field, a
  `Drop` release or a computed function value (`call_is_bound`, the
  shapes code generation calls through) - as E0900 in ruling 86's words.
  The walk now visits a `?`'s desugared `match`, whose error arm's
  `Result::Err(..)` it never saw.  Code generation's E0636 refusal is an
  E0900 assertion ("should never happen").

## Evidence

* Coverage probe (`.objcmp/s114/unit1-with-probes.patch`): each call node
  marked when mono's walk visits it and stamped with whether it was built
  before monomorphization ended; code generation logged every call it
  emitted.  Full corpus at HEAD's behaviour (`s114/cP2`): the calls built
  before monomorphization ended that reached code generation unvisited were
  1,159 sites, every one a `?`'s desugared error arm (the source line holds
  `?`, on a continuation line, or the `async` function's head its lowered
  `?` is placed at).  With the change (`s114/cU`): 597,893 emitted calls
  visited, 796,747 built after monomorphization (drop insertion and the
  passes after it), and **0** built before it unvisited.
* Control: a mutation stripping the pin of each call in a `main.cryo`
  (`S114CTL=unpin`): monomorphization reports "internal: call to `inc` in
  `main` reached codegen with no resolved function (written at
  main.cryo:7)" and code generation is never reached, while `f(a)` through
  a function-typed local is left alone; with the report also off
  (`unpin-noreport`), code generation's assertion fires instead.
* Projections: over the full corpus at HEAD's behaviour the leaf-keyed
  case was reached **0** times, negatives included; with the change only in
  the new negative.  The new registration agreed with TypeResolution's
  18,693 times of 18,693; control: without it, all 44 of the tests leg
  disagree and the leg fails (the name layer then sees no trait).
* Corpus `s114/cP2` vs `s114/cU`, 455 entries: status changes exactly the
  three new tests; diagnostic sets otherwise identical (the compiler's own
  warnings move lines in pairs).
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, objects 0 moved of
  6,906 test and 1,126 example objects (predicted: the `?` walk revisits
  only variant calls, and the rest touches refused programs and reports);
  census, examples, lsp (461 warnings), cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file) multiset.
* Lane: LOOKUP_ROUTED 25 -> 27 (`call_resolver.cryo` 12 -> 14: the two type
  displays rulings 139 and 142 put in diagnostic text - re-pinned, question
  for Jake), ARENA_READ 62 -> 61, ARENA_WRITE 41 -> 40.  Residue 211 -> 213,
  J 138 -> 140 (the name layer's two `assoc-type` door asks).
* §0: projects 192 -> 193, negatives 230 -> 232, E0203 negatives 8 -> 9;
  roster +3.  Declared in `tests/started-passing`: the project and both

### 8.528 A definition's overloads and a type's constructors are read off registered entries, not asked by the definition's leaf - 2026-10-06

## Why

Store #5 of `.objcmp/merge-audit/STORES.md`: three readers held a
definition's identity and asked the member-function door with its parent
and its own leaf, `lookup_family_entries(Def(parent_of(d)), leaf_of(d))` -
identity text fed back into a key (rule 4).  Sema's `family_entries` (the
overloads of a bound callee), `family_signatures_of` (the same, or a type's
constructors under `(type, the type's leaf)`) and codegen's
`resolve_function` (the functions codegen calls by a definition it holds:
the allocator's entry points, `std::env::set_args`).

```cryo
function twice(x: i32) -> i32 { .. }
function twice(x: i64) -> i64 { .. }
twice(3)        // the overloads of the definition `twice` binds: read off its entry
Node(1)         // a class's constructors: the family its constructor registered in
```

## What changed

* `DeclarationIndex`: each entry records the family it is registered in
  (`overload_func_family`); a type definition records the family its
  constructors register in (`ctor_families`, written where a method marked
  `is_constructor` registers).  `family_entries_of_def(d)` reads the family
  off `d`'s own entry, `constructor_entries_of(d)` off the type.
* `CallResolver::family_entries` and `family_signatures_of` ask those;
  `SymbolResolver::resolve_function(d)` is `resolve_decl(entry_of_def(d))`.

## Evidence

* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file) multiset.

### 8.529 Rulings 145-148: a projection through a supertrait resolves through it, and a call through a local or field of no function type is E0213 - 2026-10-06

## Why

Jake's rulings of 2026-10-06 (appendix, 145-148).  145 keeps E0213 for
ruling 142; 146 accepts LOOKUP_ROUTED 25 -> 27 (8.526's two diagnostic type
displays).  147: `x(3)` on an `i32` local was E0202 "cannot find function
`x`" and `h.n(4)` on an `i32` field E0358 "no method named `n`".  148: a
projection names only the associated types its bound trait itself declares,
so `I::Item` under `I: DoubleEnded` (`DoubleEnded : Iterator`) was refused
since 8.526 (E0203), and before it the compiler crashed.

```cryo
type trait Both : Source { take_back(mut &this) -> Option<This::Item>; }
function sum_with<I>(it: mut &I, f: (I::Item) -> i32) -> i32 where I: Both { .. }
const a: i32 = x(3);       // E0213 expected function, found `i32`
const b: i32 = h.n(4);     // E0213 expected function, found `i32`
```

## What changed

* 148 - the name layer's two projection checks (`check_param_projections`,
  `check_this_projection`) ask the `assoc-type` door of each bound trait
  and every trait it inherits (`GenericRegistry::trait_and_supertraits`, by
  the identities stamped on each supertrait); the type resolver's
  `trait_declaring` answers the declaring trait the same way, so the
  projection is (base, slot in the supertrait, the supertrait), and the
  impl that binds it is the type's impl of the supertrait.  Two different
  traits declaring the member - two bounds, or a trait and one it inherits
  - is ambiguous (E0203, as rustc's E0221); the `This` form says so in its
  own message, label "more than one of `T` and the traits it inherits
  declares `X`".
* 147 - `resolve_direct_call`: a local whose type is not a function is
  E0213 at the callee; a method call that finds no method, no
  function-typed field and no deref target, and the receiver has a field
  of the name (`MemberResolver::field_of`, the member-field door), is
  E0213 at the member access.  `refuse_call_of_non_function` takes the
  callee's span.

## Evidence

* Agreement probe (`.objcmp/s115/name_resolution.probe.cryo`,
  `call_resolver.probe.cryo`): every projection the name layer checks,
  answered by the bound alone and through its supertraits.  Full corpus
  `s115/cP` (456 entries): 4,232 bound projections and 6,782 `This`
  projections agree; the 6 that differ (none -> ok) are the new project's
  `I::Item` under `Peek`/`Both` and `This::Item` in `Both`.  No trait in the
  corpus re-declares an inherited associated type (ok -> ambiguous: 0); no
  supertrait was unstamped when asked (0).  Ruling 147's paths: a call
  through a non-function local 0 times, a failed method call with a field of
  the name 0 times (8 failed method calls, none with such a field).
* Controls (env `S115CTL`, same binary): `skipself` (each bound's own trait
  skipped) - 10 bound projections flip ok -> none per stdlib build and the
  build fails; `nosuper` (`This` ignores supertraits) - the new project's 4
  `This` projections agree as none/none and it fails with 4 E0203.
* Corpus `s114/cS5` vs `s115/cP`: status changes exactly the new project;
  diagnostic sets otherwise identical (the compiler's own warnings move
  lines).
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, 0 moved of 6,906
  test and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK.  Declared in

### 8.530 Module globals are registered and read by their definition, and codegen caches a global's value by its registration slot - 2026-10-06

## Why

Store #3 of `.objcmp/merge-audit/STORES.md`, with ruling 141 (codegen's
`GlobalRegistry` is re-keyed when the module-globals table is converted).
The index's globals were parallel arrays written with a dedup on (leaf,
source-file text) and read by (leaf, module): `global_entry_of_def(d)`
asked with `defs.leaf_of(d)` and the module `d`'s parent is - identity
text fed back into a key (rule 4) - and the directive pass and the extern
symbol record re-derived the same (leaf, module) pair from the declaration.
Codegen cached each global's LLVM value under `format("%s::%s", ns, leaf)`
interned, from the registration's module on one side and the declaration's
binding namespace or the unit's module on the other.

```cryo
const LIMIT: i32 = 8;                  // registered under its definition
const n: i32 = LIMIT + other::LIMIT;   // `LIMIT` by its stamp; `other::LIMIT` through the member-global door
```

## What changed

* A global's declaration carries the definition it is: `VarDeclNode.def`
  and `IntrinsicConstDeclNode.def`, stamped by NameDeclaration where it
  declares the name (a C-imported global too), copied by the cloner.
* `DeclarationIndex`: `def_globals` (definition slot -> registration slot);
  `register_global(def, leaf, ..)` files one slot per definition, a second
  registration of it refreshing the module, type and thread-local flag;
  `global_slot_of_def` / `global_entry_of_def`; `record_global_extern_symbol`
  and `mark_global_thread_local` take the definition.  `global_slot` and
  `global_entry_in_module` are gone; the one question by a written leaf -
  `mod::NAME`, sema's `scope_global_type` - is a new door, `member-global`
  (`global_in_module(leaf, module)`), listed in `docs/resolution-rules.md`.
  The leaf array is `module_global_leaves`: data for mangling, scanned only
  by that door.
* Codegen: `GlobalRegistry` is an array indexed by the registration slot;
  `DeclarationEmitter::global_cache_slot(node)` and
  `SymbolResolver::resolve_global_entry` use `entry.slot`;
  `global_cache_key_of` is deleted.
* `scripts/lane-gate.py`: the stale `GlobalRegistry` exclusion (it owns no
  map) and the stale `module_global_files` scanned-array entry removed,
  `module_global_keys` renamed `module_global_leaves` - each demanded by the
  gate's own staleness rules.

## Evidence

* Agreement probe (`.objcmp/s115/u2probe/`): each registration's slot by
  definition against the old (leaf, file) dedup; each `global_entry_of_def`
  against the old (leaf, parent module) scan; the directive and extern
  correctors against their old (key, module); codegen's registry kept a
  shadow map under the old text key, compared at every read and every
  registration.  Full corpus `s115/cG` (458 entries): 379,839 registrations,
  360,893 reads by definition, 95 directive corrections, 3 extern-symbol
  records, 134,100 codegen registrations and 32,801 codegen reads - **0**
  disagreements; no global registered without a definition.
* Controls (env `S115CTL`, `examples/11-http-server`): `defoff` (the
  definition answers the previous slot) - 304 + 2 disagreements and 72
  errors; `cgnull` (the registry answers nothing) - 14 disagreements and
  the build fails.
* Corpus `s115/cP` vs `s115/cG`: status changes only the two negatives
  8.529 added after `cP` ran.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, 0 moved of 6,960
  test and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file) multiset.
* Lane: LOOKUP_OTHER 43 -> 42, REGISTER 17 -> 16, LOOKUP_LOCAL 43 -> 42
  (re-pinned).  Spelling flow 633 -> 617 (14 outstanding lines dropped);
  residue 211 -> 210, J 138 -> 137; name-taking methods 674 -> 668;
  `pending` reasons 451 -> 442; doors 15 -> 16; lane exclusions 15 -> 14.

## Why

Left by 8.528 (store #5): code generation's three constructions asked the

`resolve_family(Type(t), id.name, arity)` for `Point(1, 2)`,

`resolve_family(Def(base), node.base_ctor_name, arity)` for a derived
class's base-constructor call.  The type's definition records the family
its constructors register in (`constructor_entries_of`, 8.528), so the
question needs no name.

  `decl_visit_emitter` (the base's definition) call it.

### 8.532 A generic call whose return names its parameter's associated type has the type the argument's impl binds - 2026-10-06

## Why

Found by the 115th (8.529, "found, not fixed") and by a read-only audit
(`.objcmp/merge-audit-2/REPORT.md`, `r/r148`) against ruling 148: a generic
free function returning `Option<I::Item>` or `I::Item`, called with a
concrete `I`, gave the call the substituted type with the projection still
in it - `Option<Count::Item>` - and the caller's annotation refused it
(E0200 "expected `Option<i32>`, found `Option<i32>`", the two printing
alike).  A plain bound fails the same way, before ruling 148 too; 148 only
makes the supertrait form reach it.

```cryo
function first_of<I>(it: mut &I) -> Option<I::Item> where I: Source { .. }
const a: Option<i32> = first_of(&c);   // `Count`'s impl binds `Item = i32`
```

## What changed

* `CallResolver::subst_free_call_return`: the substituted return is built
  without demanding its instantiations (as the substituter's `in_copy`
  does) and then reduced (`TypeResolver::reduce_projections`, no memo), so
  a projection the substitution made concrete is the type the impl binds.
  Building it with demand left `Option<Count::Item>` demanded and never
  monomorphized (E0900 "unresolved generic instantiation ... `Option<?>`") -
  the second of two hypotheses, measured on the repro.

## Evidence

* Probe (each substituted return, reduced against unreduced): full corpus
  `s115/cR` (459 entries) - 59,215 asks, 5 reduced, all in the new project;
  52,773 of the unchanged ones in the symbolic walk.

  without it refuses it with 5 E0200.  The audit's repro and its
  plain-bound twin exit 4 as predicted.
* Corpus `s115/cK2` vs `s115/cR`: status changes only the new project.

### 8.533 Monomorphization's leftover name rewrites deleted; a projection-typed parameter takes the type the impl binds through a method and a path - 2026-10-07

## Why

Two findings of the read-only audit at `8364e089`
(`.objcmp/merge-audit-2/REPORT.md` section 3) and one of the 115th's
"not checked" (8.532).

* Monomorphization still rewrote a generic static method's body TEXT "so the
  post-mono sema pass re-resolves it": a struct literal's `struct_type` and a
  local's annotation `name` were set to the owner specialization's qualified
  name.  That pass is gone (8.520); nothing reads either field after
  monomorphization (`struct_type`'s readers are the name layer, the type
  resolver's literal-to-annotation helper - which resolves by the literal's
  stamp - the cloner and the dumper).  Which literal or annotation names the
  owner was decided by comparing the written spelling with the owner's leaf
  (`gsm_owner_leaf`), a rule-3 shape.
* About ten comments still described the deleted pass as live.
* The 115th fixed a generic FREE call returning `Option<I::Item>` and did not
  try a method call or a module-qualified call.  The returns are right through
  both; a PARAMETER typed by the projection is not:

```cryo
pull_or<I>(&this, it: mut &I, d: I::Item) -> I::Item where I: Source { .. }
const x: i32 = p.pull_or(&c, 100);      // E0214 "expected `I::Item`, found `i32`"
const y: i32 = Gen::take_or(&c, 100);   // the same
```

  Two causes.  `TypeUtils::arg_type_part_is_concrete` called an unreduced
  projection settled (it is no more settled than the parameter it projects
  from), so the argument checks of a method call and of a path call judged
  `100` against the literal `I::Item`.  And method selection
  (`method_args_bind`) substituted the method's bindings into the parameter
  and compared the argument with `Count::Item` unreduced, so with the first
  cause fixed the method was not selected at all (E0358 "no method named
  `pull_or`").

## What changed

* `MonoCallSpecializer`: `gsm_owner_leaf` / `gsm_owner_spec` are replaced by
  `gsm_owner_def`, the owner template's definition; `names_gsm_owner` asks a
  literal's or an annotation's stamp whether it names it.  The two text
  writes are deleted; the two type writes stay.
* `arg_type_part_is_concrete`: an `AssocProjection` is not settled.
* `method_args_bind`: a method with type parameters of its own and no owner
  view judges the argument against the parameter `seen_through` its bindings
  (projections the bindings make concrete reduced to what the impl binds),
  as the view branch beside it already did.
* Comments: `call_specializer.cryo` (4), `call_resolver.cryo`, `sema.cryo`,
  `method_binding.cryo` ("GATED: mono-after-sema (R1)"), `dead_code.cryo`,
  `pass_id.cryo`, `lambda_synth.cryo`, `expression.cryo`.
* New project `projection_param_through_method_and_path`: a receiver method,
  a static method, `Gen::f(..)` and `ProjPath::Gen::f(..)`, returning
  `Option<I::Item>` and taking `d: I::Item`, under a plain bound and through
  a supertrait.  Declared in `tests/started-compiling` (HEAD: 4 E0214).

## Evidence

* Probe (corpus `s116/c1`, 440 entries incl. every project's `tests/`, the
  unit leg and each negative): the owner gate asked 9 times (all
  `stdlib/collections/string.cryo:132`, `String::from<T>`'s local), old
  spelling answer == new stamp answer 9/9, and every time the local's type
  ALREADY was the owner specialization - the type write changes nothing in

  parameters reaching the argument check: 4, all in the new project;
  selection answers that differ from the unreduced substitution: 2, both in

  fired 0 times (comment reworded, guard kept).

  sets): 1 status change, the new project (exit 1 -> 0, its 4 E0214 gone);

* Controls: `S116CTL=gsm` (stamp gate answers no) shows the 9 asks

  owner); re-pinned.  §0: projects 195 -> 196, braced-import files
  686 -> 688; roster +1.

## Found, not fixed

* An argument for a projection-typed parameter of a generic FREE function or
  a module-qualified one is never checked against the type the impl binds:

### 8.534 Rule 1 checked by the compiler: every written name leaves the name layer answered - 2026-10-07

## Why

Rule 1 (a written name is resolved once, where it is written) was checked
only lazily: `ResSlot::require` tallies a node some consumer asks for and
finds unanswered, so a node nobody asks for is never checked, and a
`require` reached in a forked codegen child is lost.  The audit at
`8364e089` (section 2.3) puts this check first of the four compiler checks
that are to replace the Python guards: it needs no conversion first.

## What changed

* New `compiler/resolver/stamp_check.cryo`: `StampCheck`, a walk of its own
  over a module's whole tree - declarations, bodies, patterns, every type
  annotation tree, bounds - counting each name-bearing slot left `Pending`:
  an identifier, a path's scope segment, a struct literal's and a `new`'s
  type, an enum pattern's enum, a constant named by a pattern, a written
  type name, an impl's target, a class's base, and a bound's trait (neither
  stamped nor refused).  A `Lang` slot (a claimed language item) is an
  answer.  Member names and calls are not in it: the type check and
  monomorphization answer those.
* `run_module_resolution` runs it over each module after its NameResolution
  run while the build is clean, and refuses the build with E0900 "N written
  name(s) left name resolution with no answer; first: identifier at
  file:line:col" before any later stage.
* The check found a real hole at once: the name layer never walked the
  expression inside a `typeof(..)` TYPE (`const y: typeof(x) = 7;`), so `x`
  was unanswered and sema found it by its spelling.
  `NameResolver::stamp_annotation` now walks a `Typeof` operand.  Side
  effect: 5 W0001 "unused variable" warnings in `tests/lang/typeof.cryo` -
  locals used only inside `typeof(..)` - are gone; they were false.

## Evidence

* Population (probe build, corpus `s116/c2`, 460 entries): 6 unanswered
  slots, all identifiers inside `typeof(..)` in `tests/lang/typeof.cryo`
  (the unit leg fails with the E0900).  After the `typeof` fix (`s116/c3`):
  0.  Coverage on a hello-world-sized build (all of its stdlib modules): the
  walk visited 5,290 identifiers, 2,921 type names, 1,018 path scopes, 308
  impl targets, 134 struct literals, 16 constant patterns.
* The gate pair, over the same broken tree (a probe that makes the name
  layer skip stamping one identifier, `zz_unstamped`, in a 6-line program):
  with the stamp check off (only the old tallies), the build SUCCEEDED and
  the program ran correctly (exit 0) - a later stage resolved the unstamped
  local by its spelling and nothing noticed; with it on, the build is
  refused: "E0900: 1 written name(s) left name resolution with no answer;
  first: identifier at src/main.cryo:5:12".
* Corpus `s116/c0` (HEAD before 8.533) vs `s116/c3`: 1 status change (8.533's
  project), diagnostic-set changes: that project, the 5 W0001 above, and the
  compiler's own warnings' probe line shift.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, 0 moved of 7,069
  test and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file) multiset; the new
  compiler type-checks its own source (and so passes its own check).
* §0: braced-import files 688 -> 689 (`stamp_check.cryo`).  The check's
  report kind is an enum, so the name-taking count does not move.

## Not done

* No committed test plants an unanswered name: doing so needs a fault
  injection hook in the compiler (asked in the handoff).
* The later stages' own stage table (members after the type check, calls
  after monomorphization) is not built; `require` and
  `report_unbound_calls` remain the check there.
* A local identifier left unstamped is resolved by a later stage by its
  spelling (the gate pair shows it).  The new check makes it unreachable;
  the lookup that would answer it is still there.

### 8.535 Stores #8 and #9: codegen holds intrinsics and externs under their entry's symbol; a clone's alias entry is told apart by its template - 2026-10-07

## Why

Two rows of the store list (`.objcmp/merge-audit/STORES.md`, rule 4: an
identity's text never feeds a key).

* #8: code generation's `FunctionRegistry` is keyed by the linker symbol
  every pin names a function by, but three registrations used other text:
  an intrinsic under its bare name and again under `decl_fn_key`'s
  qualified-name text, and an extern-block function under its Cryo name.
  A read-only research agent traced all four registry readers (the three
  prologues and `SymbolResolver::held_symbol`): every one asks with an
  entry's symbol.  The qualified-text key was read by nothing; an extern
  with `![symbol("..")]` was held under a key no reader asks with (its pins
  name the link symbol, found by `held_symbol`'s module lookup instead).
* #9: `register_signature` told a specialization's alias entry (the clone
  registered again under its minted identifier, in its template's family)
  apart by the id of `decl_fn_key`'s qualified-name text.

## What changed

* `declare_intrinsic`: held under `entry_symbol(entry_of_def(node.def))`;
  the `decl_fn_key` registration is deleted.  `declare_extern_block`: held
  under `entry_symbol(func.overload_entry)`.  A declaration no registration
  reached is held under nothing - no pin can name it.
* `DeclarationIndex.overload_func_owner: u32[]` (text ids) is
  `overload_func_alias_of: DefId[]`; `register_signature`'s `alias_of` is
  the clone's `copy_of`, invalid for every other registration.
* `scripts/lane-gate.py`: the stale `SCANNED_ARRAYS` entry for
  `overload_func_owner` removed (a `DefId[]` is not a scanned spelling).

## Evidence

  every one with an entry whose symbol IS the bare name it was held under;
  extern registrations 124,561, every one with an entry - 124,559 whose

### 8.536 An argument for a projection-typed parameter is checked against the type the impl binds, in every call shape - 2026-10-07

## Why

The 116th's "found, not fixed" (8.533): a parameter typed by a type
parameter's associated type was never judged against the argument in a plain
or module-qualified generic call, and a method call refused the mistake with
the wrong error.

```cryo
function take_or<I>(it: mut &I, d: I::Item) -> I::Item where I: Source { .. }
// `Count`'s `Item` is `i32`
const a: i32 = take_or(&c, true);       // compiled; `true` passed as the i32
const b: i32 = Gen::take_or(&c, true);  // the same
const m: i32 = h.pick(&c, true);        // E0358 "no method named `pick`"
```

Three causes, one per shape.  A plain generic call returns as soon as its
type arguments are inferred and is never argument-checked: the inference's
conflict report is the only check its arguments get, and a projection formal
binds nothing, so it conflicts with nothing.  A path call checks its
arguments against the family's declared signature, where `I::Item` is not
settled (8.533) and is skipped.  A method call's argument check gathers the
candidate's declared parameters, skips the projection the same way, reports
nothing, and the call falls through to "no method named" because the
selection (which since 8.533 sees the projection through the bindings) bound
nothing.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::params_seen_through(subst, decl, params)`: each parameter
  whose declaration holds a projection is `seen_through` the substitution
  (bases made concrete, projections reduced to what the impl binds) when
  that settles it; every other parameter is as given.  So the change moves
  only projection positions - a plain `T` or `i32` parameter is checked, or
  skipped, exactly as before.
* Plain call: `check_free_call_projection_args`, run where the inferred call
  returns, checks the projection positions alone against the template's
  parameters under the call's stashed type arguments.
* Path call: `check_scope_call_arg_types` passes the family's signature
  through `free_call_params` (the template of the callee's definition, the
  call's stashed type arguments).
* Method call: `check_method_call_arg_types` keeps the chosen candidate's
  declaration and passes its parameters through `method_call_params`, which
  binds the method's own type parameters as the selection does (turbofish,
  then unifying each parameter with its argument).
* New negative `E0214_projection_argument.cryo`: the three shapes, each
  E0214 "mismatched types" at `true`, beside accepted calls with `4`.
  Declared in `tests/started-passing` (HEAD: E0358 on the method line, the
  other two compiled).

## Evidence

### 8.541 Stores #2 and #4: a copy is registered in no family, a declaration's family comes from its definition; `CalleePin::Family` deleted - 2026-10-07

## Why

Store #2's remaining half and store #4 (ruling 157: finished together),
and ruling 152: the calls recorded as an owner and a name, which code
generation looked up again, are retired before the merge.

A function declaration's family was found by `decl_fn_family`, which
parsed the declaration's NAME: a qualified name named its module by its
parent's text (`module_family_named` -> `module_of_minted_parent`), a bare
one by its source file.  A monomorphized copy was then registered twice -
in `(its file's module, the minted identifier)` and again in
`(Def(template), the minted identifier)` - both families keyed by the
minted text.  Five call pins named a family by an owner and a leaf
(`CalleePin::Family`), three of them composed from `defs.leaf_of(def)`,
identity text fed back into a key.

## What changed

* `CompilationContext::fn_family_of(def)` is `Def(defs.parent_of(def))`:
  a written function's, extern's and intrinsic's family owner, read off the
  definition; the leaf is the name it is written with.
* A copy (no definition of its own, a `copy_of`) is registered by
  `DeclarationIndex::register_copy_signature` under no family: one entry
  (`file_entry` with slot 0), its symbol mangled by the factored
  `mangle_function_symbol` under `copy_module_family(copy_of)` - the module
  declaring what it copies, the module the text answer named - and the
  instance recorded against that one entry.  The closure-argument
  specialization registers the same way.  The second registration and
  `overload_func_alias_of` (now always invalid) are deleted.
* The async rewrites reset the family off the node's own entry
  (`reset_family_of_entry`) instead of re-deriving it from the name, which
  the rewrite had renamed (`main$async`).
* `CalleePin::Family` is deleted.  A module-qualified call, a function
  named as a value (bare or through a path) and a static method named as a
  value pin `CalleePin::Decl` of the family's only entry, read off the
  definition (`family_entries_of_def`) or the owner the path names; an
  overloaded family nothing chose stays unpinned, where code generation
  refused the family as naming several symbols.  The turbofish call of a
  generic TYPE (`Cell::<i32>(4)`) pinned a minted family no registration
  ever filled - code generation found nothing to call at HEAD - and is no
  longer pinned (mono's unbound-call report).  `decl_fn_family`,
  `minted_family`, `minted_parent_family`, `module_family_named`,
  `module_of_minted_parent`, `family_intrinsic_kind`, `family_return_type`
  and `CalleePin::is_family` are deleted.

### 8.542 Store #6: trait-impl coherence is keyed by the head's identities - 2026-10-07

## Why

The last store keyed by text.  Coherence filed each source trait impl
under an interned string (`coherence_key_for`): types folded to `#T<id>`
and impl parameters to `#n`, but an impl parameter was recognised by
comparing SPELLINGS (`impl_param_index`), a bound's trait by its path's
text, and any name with no type identity - a projection `I::Item` among
them - by its spelling.  So `Make<I::Item> for Wrap<I>` and the same head
written with `J` were two keys.

## What changed

* `TypeResolutionPasses::coherence_key_of` builds the head as tags and
  values: a type by its arena id (`res_key`), an impl parameter by its
  position read off the stamp (`impl_param_position` over the parameters'
  `sym_id`, a where-bound's `subject_sym`), a bound's trait by its
  definition's slot, and a projection through an impl parameter by the
  parameter's position, the trait a where-bound on it names whose
  declaration has the member, and the member's position there - the
  `assoc-type` door, asked with the written path's last segment
  (`projection_key`).  A part with no identity (a name already refused)
  leaves the head out of the check.
* `GenericRegistry::register_coherence_head` files a key in a pool and
  matches it whole (chained by a hash of the tokens).  The interned-text
  index, `register_coherence`, `coherence_key_for`, `type_name_key`,
  `ann_canon_key` and `impl_param_index` are deleted; the call site's
  comment no longer names another language's rule.
* New negative `E0308_projection_head_duplicate`, pinned to the
  duplicate-head wording, declared in `tests/started-passing`.

  for every source trait impl in the 466-entry corpus): 123,056 heads agree
  on the conflict answer (3 of them conflicts); 1 head unkeyed, in the
  negative `E0302_trait_head_undeclared_param`, already refused.  The first
  probe (`c4`) left 857 heads unkeyed - projections `I::Item` in trait
  arguments - which is why projections get `projection_key`.  The one
  disagreement is the new negative: HEAD's text key saw two heads and
  only the overlap check refused the second ("overlaps"); the identity key
  sees one head ("implemented at most once per type").

  duplicate-head wording, fails under the control and under HEAD's

### 8.543 Rule 2 checked by the compiler: typed table keys, and E0157 on a store field keyed by text or a raw number; rulings 160-163 recorded - 2026-10-07

## Why

Rule 2 says a store's key comes from an identity or a door.  Every one of
the compiler's 47 hash-table fields was keyed by `u64`, `u32`, `i64` or
`string`, so an identity reached a table only as a number (`TypeRef::key`,
`DefTable::slot`, `SymbolID::key`) and nothing told it apart from a
spelling's interned id.  A check over key types could not exist until the
identity-keyed tables had key types of their own.  Ruling 161: the check
reuses E0157 and its allow-with-reason marker.

## What changed

* Key types, each made only from the identity it stands for and hashed as
  the number it replaces: `TypeKey` (`TypeRef::table_key`), `SymbolKey`
  (`SymbolID::table_key`), `DefKey` (`DefTable::table_key`, refused as
  `slot` refuses another table's id), `FamilySlot` (made only by
  `family_slot`, the member-function door's key), `CopyKey`,
  `ConversionKey`, `InstanceKey` (owner type + method definition) and
  `TraitImplKey` (trait definition + target type).
* 23 of the 47 fields moved onto them: the declaration index's
  `func_type_refs`, `type_reverse`, `copy_entries`, `instance_entries`,
  `array_elem_to_type`, `implicit_converters`, `overload_index`,
  `refused_methods` (and the `FamilySlot[]` arrays beside them); the
  constant table's two; the template registry's `type_index`,
  `cache_index`, `mono_set`, `inherent_owner_index`, `trait_head_index`;
  the arena's `generic_param_cache`; sema's `closure_spec_keys`; the move
  check's `types`; the resolver's `import_targets` and `explicit_imports`;
  the monomorphizer's `spec_index`, `instance_keys` and
  `materialized_insts`.  `lookup_implicit_converter`,
  `register_implicit_converter`, `is_template` and `update_type_index`
  take the `TypeRef`s, not their numbers.
* The check (`DirectiveProcessingPasses::lint_store_keys`): in a module
  under the root namespace the spelling types are declared in, a struct,
  class or union field whose type is `HashMap` or `HashSet` keyed by an
  integer, a `string` or a spelling type is E0157 at the field unless the
  field carries `![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "...")]`.  The table
  types are recognised by identity: `HashMap` and `HashSet` are language
  items now.  Directives on fields are validated (target `field`); an
  allow of the spelling lint may sit on a function, a method or a field.
* The other 24 fields carry allows with written reasons: the interner,
  scope ribs (the resolver's scopes, sema's locals), the module graph's
  path-keyed tables, diagnostics and the source cache, source positions
  (the resolution map, dead code), the linker symbols of codegen and
  extern C declarations, the type interner's and coherence's structural
  hashes, codegen's type cache (keyed by the number a `Type` carries; no
  handle is held there), module discovery's namespace text, and the
  `--emit=facts` scratch.
* New project `store_key_lint_refuses_raw_key`; `spelling_lint_directive_shapes`
  expects "only applies to function, method or field, not struct".
* `docs/resolution-rules.md`: rulings 160-163; its comparisons with
  another language are restated on Cryo's own terms.

```
error[E0157]: `Store.by_id` keys a table by `u32`, not by an identity
 --> src/main.cryo:40:5
 help: key it by the identity's own key (`TypeRef::table_key`, `DefTable::table_key`, `SymbolID::table_key`), or say why it cannot: `![allow(lookup_by_spelling, reason = "...")]` on the field
```

## Evidence

* The gate pair, over a tree with `type struct PlantedStore { by_leaf:
  HashMap<u32, OverloadId>; }` planted in `decl_index.cryo`: HEAD's
  compiler, `cryo check src/main.cryo`: "No errors found."; this
  compiler: "error[E0157]: `PlantedStore.by_leaf` keys a table by `u32`,
  not by an identity" at the field.  Restored.  The same pair on the new
  project: HEAD built it and it returned 7; this compiler refuses the four
  planted fields (E0157) and the reasonless allow (E0152), and leaves the
  `DefKey`-keyed table, the reasoned allow and the `app` module's
  `HashMap<string, i32>` alone.
* Control on the instrument: before any allow was written, the check over
  `compiler/src` refused exactly the 28 fields left unconverted at that
  point (47 - 19); four more were converted after it, leaving 24.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,181 test
  and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK (lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow,
  fast).  The census fails on one project, `spelling_lint_directive_shapes`,
  the deliberate wording change (ruling 93): verify keys
  `tests/started-passing` by name and the project is declared there
  already, so the run was taken with that one expectation at its old
  wording, and the tree's census failed it alone ("output missing ...
  function or method, not struct"); with the new wording the project
  passes (`make test ARGS=spelling_lint`: 5 passed).
* Inversion control: `CopyKey` without its owner half - every test and
  example fails to build (500 errors), verify FAIL.  Restored.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file, message) multiset as
  the clean build at `614d2ee0`.
* Lane unchanged; flow 600 outstanding as listed (the table types are
  matched by language item, not by qualified name).  §0: braced-import

### 8.544 Ruling 65: a declaration named like an explicit import or a module alias is E0205 - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 65: a local declaration and an import of the same name in the same
namespace is E0205; neither the local winning silently nor an alias being
dropped silently is allowed.  `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 states it.  The scope
let a declaration take an import's slot in either order (the import then
reachable only by path), and a module alias - bound as an ordinary
binding - lost to a same-named type with no word at all.

## What changed

* `Scope` records every binding added under a name it already binds
  (`meetings`: the binding the name held, the one added), in `insert` and
  `insert_import`, which already find the existing entry; no lookup is
  added.
* `Resolver::import_meetings_in(scope)` pairs each import binding (or
  alias) with the declaration it met; `NameResolver::refuse_import_redeclarations`,
  run once per module after its walk, refuses a pair whose import is an
  explicit entry (`is_explicit_import`) or a module alias and whose two
  sides share a namespace (modules and types share the type namespace).
  A glob's or the prelude's binding is still shadowed by a declaration.

```
error[E0205]: the name `Tag` is already declared in this scope: it is imported
 --> src/main.cryo:9:1
 note: imported here
 --> src/main.cryo:5:1
 help: rename the declaration, or import the item under another name with `as`
error[E0205]: the name `Loc` is already declared in this scope: it is a module's import alias
 help: rename the declaration or the alias
```

The wording is this change's (E0205 kept, as the ruling says).

## Evidence

* New project `import_name_redeclared_locally` (started-passing): HEAD
  built it and it returned 5 (the local `Tag` won); here `Tag` (braced
  import), `Loc` (module alias) and `one` (imported function, local
  function) are E0205 at the declaration with the import noted, and
  `Mark` - an imported type beside a declared function - is not refused.
* Fallout ruling 162 asks to fix with the change: none.  The census with
  this compiler passes every unit test, negative and project; the compiler,
  the standard library, the examples and the editor build.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, 0 moved of 7,181
  test and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK.
* §0: braced-import files 696 -> 697, projects 202 -> 203.

### 8.545 Ruling 4: a non-generic and a generic method that both accept a call are ambiguous (E0154) - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 4: when a generic and a non-generic method of one name both apply
to a call, the call is ambiguous; neither wins by being non-generic.
`docs/cryo.md` 13.4 states it.  Method selection tried each candidate set
in two passes, non-generic first, and returned on the first bind, so the
generic method was never looked at.  A `Type::method` path whose fitting
inherent entries were such a pair bound nothing and reached code
generation as an internal error.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::report_generic_tie`: after a method call selects a
  non-generic method in the inherent set or the trait set, the generic
  pass of the same set is asked with a scratch selection (the way
  `report_inherent_trait_tie` asks); a generic method that binds too is
  E0154 at the member, with both candidates noted.  Skipped where the
  inherent/trait tie check is (an instantiation still in a generic
  body's parameters).
* `CallResolver::report_static_generic_tie`, from `choose_entry`: several
  inherent entries fit a `Type::method` call and they are a non-generic
  and a generic method - the same E0154; the non-generic entry stays
  bound so the tie is the call's one error.

```
error[E0154]: `put` is ambiguous: a non-generic and a generic method of `Box2` both accept these arguments
 --> src/main.cryo:21:20
 note: candidate #1: `put`, not generic
 note: candidate #2: `put`, generic
 help: a method is not preferred for being non-generic; rename one of them
```

E0154 ("Ambiguous Call") is reused; the wording is this change's.

## Evidence

* New project `generic_and_plain_method_both_apply` (started-passing):
  `b.put(1)` on a plain owner, `h.take(2)` on `Holder<i64>` and
  `Box2::put(&b, 4)` are E0154; `b.put(true)`, which only the generic
  method accepts, is not.  HEAD let the two method calls bind the
  non-generic method silently and reported the path call only as "E0900:
  internal: call to `put` in `main` reached codegen with no resolved
  function".
* Fallout ruling 162 asks to fix with the change: none.  No overload set in
  the standard library, the compiler, the editor, the examples or the
  tests pairs a non-generic and a generic method that one call fits; the
  project above is the control that the check reaches both owners and the
  path form.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: OK, 0 moved of 7,181
  test and 1,126 example objects; every gate OK.
* §0: projects 203 -> 204.

### 8.546 Rulings 113 and 64: a braced import naming an item and a module is E0244; a brace export offers only what it lists - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 113: every braced import of a name that is both an item and a
module is an error, aliased or not, and E0244's help suggests renaming
one of the two rather than the braced form.  Ruling 64: `export A::{ a };`
exposes `a` and nothing else of `A`.  `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 and 14.5 state
both.  E0244 was asked of the path form only (`import A::B as C;`); a
braced entry never looked for the sub-module once the item was found.  A
brace export was recorded by the module loader as a whole-module
re-export edge, so every public item of `A` was offered through it, and
only an aliased entry exported its own binding.

## What changed

* `process_import`: every entry asks for the sub-module
  (`sub_module_index`), and an entry whose module offers an item under the
  name and has a sub-module of it is E0244, braced or not.
  `refuse_item_or_module_import`'s help: "rename the item `Json` or the
  module `A::Json`".
* `ModuleLoader`: the scan records whether each `export` is the brace form
  (`export_braced`); a brace export gets the imported-namespace edge and
  no re-export edge.  The name layer exports each braced entry's binding,
  aliased or not.
* Fallout fixed with the change (ruling 162):
  `import_path_item_or_module_explicit` imported the item through
  `import A::{ Json as json_item };`, the form now refused; it keeps its
  module-form assertion (`import A::Json;` names the module) and the
  braced form moves to the new negative project.
  `import_path_item_or_module_refused` expects the new help.

```
error[E0244]: `ImportBracedItemOrModule::Json` names both an item of `ImportBracedItemOrModule` and a module
 --> src/main.cryo:3:1
 help: rename the item `Json` or the module `ImportBracedItemOrModule::Json`
```

## Evidence

* New projects (started-passing): `import_braced_item_or_module_refused` -
  HEAD imported the item through both braced entries and the program
  returned 2; here both are E0244.  `export_braces_offer_listed_only` -
  HEAD offered `Inner::b` through `export Inner::{ a };` and the program
  returned 3; here `Facade::b()` is E0233 and `Facade::a()` resolves.
* No other fallout: the census passes every other unit test, negative and
  project; the compiler, standard library, examples and editor build.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,180 test
  and 1,126 example objects (one object fewer than before in both runs:
  the edited project no longer imports the item's module); every other
  gate OK.  The census failed one project, `import_path_item_or_module_refused`,
  taken at its old help wording because verify matches started-passing
  by project name and that project is declared already (ruling 93); with
  the new wording it passes (`make test ARGS=item_or_module`: 3 passed).
* §0: braced-import files 697 -> 698, projects 204 -> 206.

### 8.547 Ruling 66 with 165: a path continues through a module alias into its sub-modules, and loads the sub-module it names; rulings 164-166 recorded - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 66: `import Json as J;` then `J::Inner::deep()` names
`Json::Inner::deep`.  Ruling 165: the sub-module a path names is loaded
even when nothing imports it.  `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 states both.  Two
defects stood in the way.  Resolution: the scope segment `J::Inner` was
asked as a module spelling, which knows nothing of the alias, and the walk
of a written type asked the alias's module for an exported TYPE `Inner`,
so both ended at E0203 "cannot find type `J::Inner`".  Loading: discovery
follows imports, so `Json::Inner` was never compiled, and even
`import json;` + `json::Inner::deep()` failed.

## What changed

* `ModuleLoader::scan_tokens` records the name each import binds (its
  last segment or alias; a brace entry's alias or last segment) and, past
  the header, every path whose head is one of them, with each proper
  prefix of the rest.  `discover_module` joins the bound module's
  namespace with that prefix and discovers the module the namespace map
  holds under it.  Loading only: no edge is recorded, since a loaded module
  is reached by the path written to it, and the reachability of that path
  is the name layer's question.
* `CompilationContext::modules_written_as` takes a `root`: with one, the
  spelling continues a path that already named that module and matches the
  module whose path is the root's followed by the spelling, reachable
  through what reached the root.  The one implementation of the relation,
  so the alias step adds no second reachability rule and no new read of the
  module graph.
* `NameResolver::alias_path_match` continues a path from an alias-bound
  head through each later segment.  `walk_module_rooted_type` looks the
  head of its prefix up (it did only for a one-segment prefix) and hands the
  module the whole written path names back to `stamp_module_scope`, which
  uses it for an unbound scope segment; no second lookup of the head.
* Rulings 164-166 recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md`.

```cryo
import ImportAliasPathSubModule::Json as J;
const n: i32 = J::Inner::deep();             // was E0203
const d: i32 = J::Inner::Deeper::bottom();
const p: J::Inner::Pt = J::Inner::Pt { v: 5 };
```

## Evidence

* New project `import_alias_path_sub_module` (started-compiling): through
  an alias, a function, a deeper sub-module, a function value, a type in a
  parameter, a struct literal, a static, an enum variant and its match
  arms; and `IapsmToml::Sub::three()` with only `import IapsmToml;`.  No
  file imports any of the three sub-modules.  HEAD: E0203 at every alias
  path; here it builds and exits 0.
* Controls, each built and run over the project: the loader's discovery
  skipped - E0203 "cannot find type `J::Inner`" at every alias path (the
  module is not in the program); the name layer's answer for an unbound
  segment left as before - `J::Inner::Pt` in a type position resolves (the
  walk's prefix) and every scope segment is E0203 again.
* `docs/cryo.md` 14.3's snippet, with `Json` and `Json::Inner` beside it:
  `cryo check` "No errors found."; HEAD E0203.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,180 test
  and 1,126 example objects, none only-tree: the loader loads no module
  into any program the corpus already builds.  Every gate OK but `fast`,
  which reported the three §0 rows below before they were moved.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same (code, file, message) set as at
  HEAD.  check-fast OK.
* Lane surface unchanged: a first version asked the module graph for the
  sub-module from the name layer and GRAPH_READ went 38 -> 40, refused;
  the step moved into `modules_written_as`.
* Not covered, a question for Jake: `import A::Toml;` then
  `Toml::Sub::f()`.  The loader loads `A::Toml::Sub`; the path is E0240
  "`Toml::Sub` is not reachable from this module", since only an alias's
  head carries reachability into sub-modules and a plain module import's
  head is matched as a spelling.  Before this change the same path was
  E0203, the module unloaded.
* §0: spelling-flow outstanding 600 -> 603, name-taking functions
  659 -> 661, projects 206 -> 207.

### 8.548 Ruling 68: a generic function or a generic owner's method used as a value is one instance of it - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 68: a generic function or method used as a value infers its type
arguments from its use; ruling 125 files an instance under the template's
definition and its type arguments.  `docs/cryo.md` 2.5 and 13.4 state it.
The type check gave `idf` the template's own signature, `(T) -> T`, and
read no turbofish on a value, so `const h: (i32) -> i32 = idf;` was E0200
and `const k = idf::<i64>;` typed `k` as `(T) -> T`; monomorphization
pinned an instance only for a turbofished bare name, resolving the
turbofish a second time.  A module's generic function as a value pinned
nothing.  A generic owner's method had no value at all: `Wrap::get` was
E0201, and the path typed as the owner.

## What changed

* `CallResolver::generic_value_type`: a generic value's type arguments are
  the turbofish's (through `resolve_generic_scope_type`, defaults filled)
  or those the expected function type binds, unified with the signature;
  a parameter neither binds is E0307 at the value, and a function's
  where-clause is checked for the instance (E0306), as a call's is
  (`check_call_where_bounds` takes the use's span).  The value's type is
  the signature with the arguments (`subst_params`, shared with the call
  path).
* The arguments are kept on the node - `IdentifierNode.value_type_args`
  for `idf`, `ScopeResolutionNode.value_type_args` for `m::idf` (the
  template is `member_def`) - and monomorphization pins
  `CalleePin::Instance` of the template applied to them, concretized under
  the copy's substitution (`value_instance`).  Code generation already
  emitted an `Instance`-pinned value.
* A generic owner's method (`Wrap::get`, `Wrap::<i32>::get`, a static
  `Wrap::make`): `generic_owner_method_value` takes the owner template's
  one entry through the member-function door, writes its signature
  receiver first with the receiver as the owner over the declaring block's
  parameters (an `implement<T>` block's own `T`, found in the signature by
  its symbol), infers or reads the owner's arguments, and records the
  owner instance (`spec_owner`) and the method's definition.
  `bind_path_value` binds the instance's method, concretizing the owner
  inside a generic body, and queues the value until the owner's instance
  is minted (`queued_path_values`); one never bound is E0900, not a null
  value.  The queue is listed in `lane-gate.py`'s excluded arrays.

```cryo
function idf<T>(x: T) -> T { return x; }
const h: (i32) -> i32 = idf;                    // idf::<i32>
const k = idf::<i64>;                           // (i64) -> i64
const g: (&Wrap<i32>) -> i32 = Wrap::get;
const n: i32 = apply(idf, 9);                   // apply(f: (i32) -> i32, x: i32)
const e = idf;
// error[E0307]: cannot infer `T` for `idf` used as a value
//  help: write the type arguments, `idf::<...>`, or give the binding a function type
```

## Evidence

* New projects: `generic_function_value` (started-compiling) - twelve
  checks: turbofish, annotation, `tag::<i32>`, `Wrap::get`,
  `Wrap::<i32>::get`, `Wrap::make`, a function-typed parameter for `i32`
  and `i64`, `gm::twice_of` both ways, and inside generic bodies; HEAD
  refuses it (E0200, E0201), here it exits 0.
  `generic_function_value_refused` (started-passing): E0307 twice and
  E0306; HEAD accepted `const g = idf;` silently and reported the bound as
  a type mismatch.
* Controls, each built and run over the project: monomorphization not
  reading the arguments - E0900 "unresolved generic instantiation"; the
  type check not unifying with the expected type - E0307 at every value
  that relies on it.
* `docs/cryo.md` 2.5 and 13.4: the generic values check; the 2.5 snippet's
  `const n: i32 = h(3);` at top level is E0202, as it is at HEAD for a
  non-generic function (calling a module-level constant of function type
  is not supported; not this change).
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,239 test
  and 1,126 example objects.  The tree census failed one unit test,
  `ProcessAsync::two_children_join_concurrently`, under the concurrent
  gates; it passes alone, and its objects are identical to the baseline's.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same set.  check-fast OK.
* A first version minted the impl block's parameter handles in the arena
  (`create_generic_param`), and the lane gate refused ARENA_WRITE 40 -> 41;
  the handles are read from the signature instead.
* Not covered: a method with type parameters of its own (`G::pick<U>`)
  as a value, an overloaded generic family, and an impl block's
  where-clause on the owner instance.
* Found, not fixed (HEAD too): a field read straight off a call through a
  function value that returns a one-field struct (`mk(15).v`) fails LLVM
  verification - the call's result is not spilled before the GEP.
* §0: excluded arrays 39 -> 40, `signature_refused` uses 16 -> 17,
  projects 207 -> 209.

### 8.549 A generic struct's literal without type arguments is the instance its use names or its fields bind - 2026-10-07

## Why

`const b: Boxy<i32> = Boxy { v: 3 };` failed in code generation (E0638, no
field slot) and `second(Pair { a: 1, b: 5 })` with
`second<A, B>(p: Pair<A, B>) -> B` left the call unbound (E0900): a generic
struct's literal written without arguments kept the template as its type,
outside a generic body as much as inside one.  A struct literal argument
was also given no expected type, so `boxed_value(Boxy { v: 7 })` could not
take the parameter's instance.

## What changed

* `resolve_struct_literal`: outside a generic body, a literal of a generic
  struct or class written without arguments is the instance the expected
  type names (`promote_to_expected_instantiation`), its fields read from
  that instance so a value takes the field's real width; with no such
  expected type, the instance its field values bind - each field's
  declared type unified with its value's (`instance_from_fields`,
  demanded, since an argument may be its only use).  The template still
  answers the literal's shape (arity, union).  Inside a generic body
  nothing changes.
* A struct literal argument receives the parameter's type as its expected
  type, as a call or a path argument does.

## Evidence

* New project `generic_struct_literal_instance` (started-compiling): an
  annotation, an `i64` field given `4000000000`, a non-generic
  parameter, a generic function's argument, and a literal nested in
  another literal's field; HEAD E0200, here it exits 0.
* Controls, each built and run over the project: promotion from the
  expected type off - E0214 "expected `Boxy<i64>`, found `Boxy<i32>`" at
  the argument; inference from the fields off - E0200 "found `B`".
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,294 test
  and 1,126 example objects.  The tree census failed
  `ProcessAsync::two_children_join_concurrently` again under the
  concurrent gates; `make test-census` alone passes every entry (2,219
  unit, 236 compile-fail, 207 projects).
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same set.  check-fast OK.
* Not fixed, measured: `first_ok(Result::Ok(4), 9)` with
  `r: Result<T, T>` - the variant's payload binds only `T` of `Ok`, the
  call's binding never reaches the argument, and code generation refuses
  the unresolved payload (E0600); `const r = Result::Ok::<i32, i32>(4);`
  then matched is E0238; `Cell::<i32>(4)` for a generic class's
  constructor reaches code generation with nothing to call (E0900).
* §0: projects 209 -> 210.

### 8.550 Rulings 167 and 168: the loader's path door, and a plain import carries reachability into sub-modules; rulings 167-170 recorded - 2026-10-07

## Why

Ruling 167: the module loader's matching of a body path's head against the
file's imports, and of the path's continuation against the namespaces files
declare, goes through a door rather than standing as three outstanding
lookups.  Ruling 168: `import A::Toml;` then `Toml::Sub::three()` loaded
`A::Toml::Sub` (§8.547) and was refused as E0240 "`Toml::Sub` is not
reachable from this module", since only an alias carried reachability past
its head.

## What changed

* `docs/resolution-rules.md` lists a `loader-path` door with two
  functions: `ModuleLoader::binding_of`, the head of a body path to the
  import that binds it, and `ModuleLoader::sub_module_file`, the bound
  module (asked by its file, the loader's identity for a module) plus the
  written continuation to the file declaring that sub-module's namespace.
  `discover_module` calls the second instead of reading the two namespace
  maps itself.  The kinds-of-door paragraph names the loader's door.
* `CompilationContext::modules_written_as`: a spelling of more than one
  segment also reaches a module whose path is an imported module's
  followed by the spelling past its head.  The imported modules the head
  can name are gathered in the same walk over the graph (one `ns_imports`
  call site, as before), and the candidates are judged after it, in graph
  order, so `found` and `other` keep their order.  Brace entries count:
  they are imports of the module.
* `docs/cryo.md` 14.3 states that a plain import's name continues into the
  module's sub-modules.
* Rulings 167-170 recorded.  Ruling 170 (a fully spelled path no import
  leads to loads nothing) is the loader's behaviour already; it gets a
  test.

```cryo
import A::Toml;
const n: i32 = Toml::Sub::three();         // was E0240
const p: Toml::Sub::Pt = Toml::Sub::Pt { v: 4 };
```

## Evidence

* New project `import_plain_path_sub_module` (started-compiling): a
  function, a deeper sub-module, a type in a parameter and an annotation,
  a struct literal, a function value, and a brace entry's binding
