### 8.551 A module-level global no fold answers is computed before `main`; a global of function type is called; a struct a function value returns is read - 2026-10-07

## Why

Three defects at module level and in function values.  `const n: i32 =
Json::twice(3);` built and read 0: code generation folds a global's
initializer when it can and gave every other initializer the zero value,
silently - the standard library's own `std::io::stdio::NEWLINE` and
`std::net::http::request::HTTP_VERSION` (`Str::new(..)`) were zero in every
program, and `request.cryo` writes "HTTP/1.1" by hand around it.  Calling a
module-level constant of function type (`const t: (i32) -> i32 = twice;`,
then `t(3)`) was E0202 "cannot find function `t`", which `docs/cryo.md`
2.5's `const n: i32 = h(3);` runs into.  And `mk(15).v`, a field of a small
struct returned through a function value, failed LLVM verification: the
register-shaped return was used as the struct.

## What changed

* Code generation: a global whose initializer no fold answers is recorded
  (`StartedGlobals`), given zero storage and never marked LLVM-constant;
  after the module's bodies, `__cryo.global_init` (internal, one per
  module) evaluates each initializer as written, stores it, and is
  registered in `llvm.global_ctors` at priority 101 + the module's place in
  the build order (`CompilationContext::active_order_position`, set by
  `switch_to_module`), so a module's globals are computed after those of
  the modules it imports.  The store's width coercion is
  `ExprOps::init_store_value`, shared with a local's initializer.
* Monomorphization walks module-level initializers, as it walks bodies, so
  a generic call or a generic function used as a value there is
  instantiated (`const h: (i32) -> i32 = idf;`).
* Sema: a call whose callee is a module's global is typed by the global's
  type - a function type is called through, any other is E0213 at the
  callee, as for a local.  Code generation loads the global and calls
  through it; mono counts such a call as bound.
* `CallEmitter::reshape_call_result`: the small-aggregate return reshape a
  direct call did is now one method, and a call through a function value
  uses it too.
* `docs/cryo.md` §3 Globals states that a non-constant initializer is
  computed before `main`, in build order.

```cryo
import Json;
const n: i32 = Json::twice(3);           // 6 (was 0)
const t: (i32) -> i32 = twice;
function main() -> i32 { return t(3) + mk(15).v; }   // was E0202; then LLVM verify
```

## Evidence

* New projects: `global_call_initializer_value` (started-passing: HEAD
  builds it and exits 1, a call-initialized global reading 0) and
  `global_initializer_at_start` (started-compiling: HEAD E0202 at each call
  of a function-typed global) - a cross-module call, a call reading another
  module's started global, a generic call, a `mut` global, a struct, the
  2.5 snippet, function values in globals, and `mk(15).v`.  New negative
  `E0213_call_of_non_function_global` (started-passing: HEAD reported
  E0202).
* Measured before the change (an instrumented compiler printing every
  global that fell to zero with an initializer, over the census, the
  examples and the compiler): only `NEWLINE`, `HTTP_VERSION` and the probe.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD`: every gate OK; objects 832 test and 161
  example moved.  Attributed by a control with the function-value reshape
  off, hashed the way verify does over the same population: only
  `stdio.o` (each project's copy) and `request.o` move - the two globals now
  computed at start; every other move is a call through a function value
  returning a small aggregate (`option.o`, `convert.o`, `error.o`,
  `ptr.o`, the async and closure unit tests), now reloaded at its struct
  type.  That control also fails `global_initializer_at_start` at
  `mk(15).v` (LLVM verify).  Controls for the rest, each a probe built and
  run (the intermediate compilers of this change): no start-up initializer
  - 0 again; no mono walk of module-level initializers - E0900
  "unresolved generic instantiation" for `const h: (i32) -> i32 = idf;`;
  mono not counting a call through a global as bound - E0900 "call to `t`
  ... reached codegen with no resolved function".  The code generation
  load of a function-typed global had no control of its own.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same set; the whole log equal line for
  line with positions and timings masked.  check-fast OK.
* Found, not fixed: a module-level global with no annotation whose
  initializer is a function value (`const k = idf::<i64>;`, `const t =
  twice;`) is never registered - type resolution registers a global only
  when its type is known before sema - so reading it is E0201.
* §0: projects 212 -> 214, negatives 236 -> 237.

### 8.552 A generic enum's variant and a generic class's construction are the instance their use names - 2026-10-08

## Why

Three inference gaps measured in §8.549.  `first_ok(Result::Ok(4), 9)`
with `r: Result<T, T>`: the variant's payload binds only `T` of `Ok`, so
the argument stayed the generic `Result` and code generation refused its
payload (E0600).  `const r = Result::Ok::<i32, i32>(4);` then matched: the
type arguments written on a variant CALL were ignored (a payload-less
variant's were not), so `r` was `Result<T, E>` and the arms disagreed
(E0238 "expected `T`, found `E`").  `Cell::<i32>(4)`, a generic class
constructed by value: the construction was typed as the template, which
has no constructor code generation can call (E0900 "found nothing to
call"), or no method (E0358).

## What changed

* `CallResolver::try_resolve_type_or_variant`: type arguments written on
  the variant (`scope.generic_args`) name the instantiation, through
  `demanded_scope_type`, as `Option::None::<i32>` already did.
* `CallResolver::retype_variant_arguments`, after a generic free call's
  bindings are all known: an argument that is a variant path or variant
  call still typed as its generic enum takes the parameter's type with the
  bindings substituted, when that is an instance of the same enum.
* `CallResolver::construction_instance`: a by-value construction of a
  generic type is the instance its turbofish names, else the one the
  expected type names.  `resolve_direct_call` takes the call for it.

```cryo
const a: i32 = first_ok(Result::Ok(4), 9);   // 4 (was E0600)
const r = Result::Ok::<i32, i32>(4);          // Result<i32, i32> (was Result<T, E>)
const c = Cell::<i64>(8000000000);            // Cell<i64> (was E0900 / E0358)
```

## Evidence

* New project `generic_instance_from_use` (started-compiling): both
  variants as arguments, a turbofish on `Ok` and on `Err` with an `i64`
  error, a class built by turbofish, by expected type, and unannotated
  with a turbofish; HEAD E0238 / E0358, here it exits 0.
* Controls, each built and run: the variant turbofish and the argument
  retype off - E0238 at both turbofish matches, and the `first_ok` probe
  E0600 again; the construction instance off - E0358 "no method named
  `get`" on `Cell`.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: 0 moved of 7,518 test
  and 1,126 example objects, none only-tree.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same set; the log equal line for line.
  check-fast OK.
* Not covered: `const c = Cell(4);` with nothing naming the instance is
  still E0358 (the constructor's arguments do not infer the instance);
  `err_or(Result::Ok(1), 6000000000)` with `r: Result<T, E>`, where `T` is
  bound only inside the variant's payload, is still an unbound call (E0900).
* §0: projects 214 -> 215.

### 8.553 Rule four checked by the compiler: a definition's name is a sealed `DeclName`, and text computed from one is refused at a door or a table key; ruling 171 recorded - 2026-10-08

## Why

Rule four ("the text an identity hands back never feeds a lookup key") was
enforced by the Python tracer alone (its rule-four rows, 29).  The merge
audit's design: a display-only type returned by `path_of` / `leaf_of`, plus
a check for what the type cannot stop - text formatted out of it and
interned.  Ruling 149 will need a sealed type for a declaration's own name
(registering, printing, mangling, passing along); this is that type.

## What changed

* `compiler/src/compiler/resolver/decl_name.cryo`: `DeclName`, one private
  `SymbolStr`.  `DeclName::of` seals (the one new function taking a
  spelling, allowed with a reason), `DeclName::spelling` hands the interned
  name to a node synthesized to carry it, and `InternTable::shown` gives
  the bytes for a message or a mangled symbol.  No equality, no `Display`.
* `DefTable::path_of` / `leaf_of`, `DeclarationIndex::family_owner_path`,
  `GenericRegistry::find_trait_defining_method`,
  `MethodBinding::lookup_trait_defining_method` and
  `TraitChecker::diagnose_method_bounds_failure` return `DeclName`.  All 49
  readers the type check refused are converted: 22 displays to
  `InternTable::shown`, the rest to `.spelling()`, and one rule-four
  lookup to identity - `check_scope_call_arg_types` asked
  `lookup_func_type_overloads(parent, leaf_of(callee))` for a callee it held;
  it reads `family_entries_of_def(callee)`.  Two editor sites take
  `.spelling()`.
* `compiler/src/compiler/sema/identity_text.cryo`, `IdentityTextCheck`,
  called from sema at every call, assignment and local: in modules under
  `compiler` (ruling 164's population), a value is identity text when its
  type is `DeclName`, when it is a local an initializer or assignment of
  identity text wrote, or when it is computed from identity text
  (concatenation, a cast, an index, a field, a call handed it as argument
  or receiver whose result is not a scalar).  Refused with E0157 (ruling
  161's code): identity text as an argument of a door (a declaration whose
  doc comment opens with the door marker) or as the key of a `HashMap` /
  `HashSet` method.  Exempt: a door's own body, and a declaration allowed
  `lookup_by_spelling` with a reason.
* `DirectiveProcessingPasses::compiler_text_of` classifies the compiler's
  text types in one match (`CompilerText`); `spelling_type_of` and the new
  `carries_identity_text` read it, so the spelling-flow list's one match
  row moves rather than grows.
* `register_methods_through` carries an allow: it interns each method's
  link symbol mangled from its trait's path.  `mangle_function_symbol`'s
  existing allow covers its two.
* `scripts/spelling-flow.py`: `DeclName.spelling(` is identity text and
  `InternTable.shown(` passes through.  A method call's provenance follows
  its first argument, not its receiver, so without these the tracer lost
  two rule-four rows of `report_trait_method_tie` - lost to the
  instrument, not fixed.  With them its view is unchanged.

```cryo
// refused (E0157): `intern` is handed text read off a definition, which is
// shown and never looked up by
const key: SymbolStr = intern.intern(intern.shown(this.defs.path_of(d)) + "::new");
// accepted: shown
const msg: string = fmt::format("`%s` is declared here", intern.shown(this.defs.path_of(d)));
```

## Measured

* Before the allows: the new compiler refused 3 sites in its own source,
  all link symbols interned from a mangled path (`decl_index.cryo` 1155,
  1346, 1367).  With them: 0.
* Planted in `check_method_def`, `intern.intern(intern.shown(defs.path_of(d)) + "::new")`
  (then `this.defs.path_of(d).shown(intern)`): the HEAD compiler's
  `cryo check src/main.cryo` printed `No errors found.`; the new one
  refused at `decl_index.cryo:775:50`.  Restored.
* Project `identity_text_refused_at_door` (started-passing): five planted
  leaks - formatted, as is, through a local, through an assignment, a hash
  table key - refused; a message, a door asked by a literal, a door's
  body and an allowed declaration not.  The HEAD compiler builds it.
  Control: local tracking off - 4 errors, `through_local` (51:25) passes,
  so the test's `51:25` and `5 errors` fail.
* `make verify --baseline HEAD --require-identical`: every gate OK; 0
  moved of 7,572 test and 1,126 example objects.
* Clean build: 329 warnings, the same set; the log differs only in the
  module count (166 -> 168 local).
* §0: name-taking 662 -> 663 (`DeclName::of`); projects 215 -> 216;
  D15's braced-import files 699 -> 702 (the three new files);
  residue table regenerated (line numbers in `sema.cryo` moved; J 128
  unchanged); spelling-flow 600, the one match row renamed.

## Not covered

* Identity text handed to a parameter of type `string` or `SymbolStr` and
  looked up by the callee, or returned as one, is not followed: the check
  is per function.  Ruling 149 closes the parameter half - once every
  function taking `SymbolStr` is a door, identity text reaching one is a
  door's argument.  Returns: `lookup_type_name`, `scope_owner_key`,
  `ann_head_key`, `target_key`, `poll_identity`, `option_identity` hand
  back `.spelling()` as a `SymbolStr` (registration keys among them).
* Comparisons: 7 sites still compare identities by their path text
  (`annotation_unifies`, `is_thread_safety_denied`, `enum_try_shape` x2,
  `is_self_growing_instantiation`, `check_method_def`, the `Array` element
  registration in specialization), now spelled `.spelling().equals(...)`.
  Comparing is not a sink: the type arena has no type-to-definition map,
  which the identity form of most of them needs.
* The allow marker exempts a whole declaration, and the 451 pending allows
  exempt theirs; ruling 149 deletes the pending ones.
* Other identity text (a type's display name, `ModulePath::as_sym`,
  `MangledName::as_string`, `Symbol.name`) is not yet a `DeclName`.
* Ruling 171 recorded.

### 8.554 Unwritten global types and variant payload bindings; ruling 171 measured, not built; no other language named in comments - 2026-10-08

## Why

Two gaps §8.551 and §8.552 found.  A module-level variable with no written
type (`const n = 5;`, `const k = idf::<i64>;`) was never registered:
type resolution registers a global only when its type is written, and
nothing registered one whose type is its initializer's, so every read was
E0201 / E0202 - cryo.md §3 allows the annotation to be left out, and §2.5
writes `const k = idf::<i64>;` at module level.  And
`err_or(Result::Ok(1), 6000000000)` with `r: Result<T, E>`: the variant is
typed as the bare enum (its payload binds only the variant's own
parameters), PASS A unified `Result<T, E>` with it and bound the
function's `T` and `E` to the enum's own placeholders, and the literal pass
then skipped `d` because `E` looked bound - E0200 "expected `i64`, found
`E`".

## What changed

* `TypeResolutionRunner::register_module_global`: the global registration
  type resolution did inline, shared.
* `Sema::type_unwritten_globals`, before any body: every module-level
  variable with no written type and an initializer is checked and, once
  typed, registered; `visit(VarDeclNode*)` skips it after.
* `CallResolver::bind_from_variant_payload`, in PASS A before the
  reliability test: a variant call typed as its bare enum binds nothing as
  a whole; its payload arguments bind the enum's parameters
  (`InferCtx` over the enum's template), and those bind the call's through
  the parameter's type arguments.  `variant_scope_of` is shared with
  `retype_variant_arguments`.

```cryo
const n = 5;                  // i32, readable everywhere (was E0201)
const k = idf::<i64>;         // (i64) -> i64, callable (was E0202)
const x: i64 = err_or(Result::Ok(1), 6000000000);   // 6000000000 (was E0200)
```

## Measured

* No program in the tree declares an unannotated module-level variable
  (0 matches; the same grep with an annotation finds 1,538), so no object
  was predicted to move.
* Projects `global_type_from_initializer` (exit 68: read above, below and
  from an importing module; a generic function value and a plain one
  called) and `variant_payload_binds_call` (exit 15: `T` from the payload
  with `E` from a literal, and the reverse), both started-compiling; the
  HEAD compiler refuses each (E0201/E0202; E0200 x2).
* The skip in `visit(VarDeclNode*)` has no observable effect: switched
  off, a bad initializer is still reported once (the sink drops an
  identical repeat), so no test pins it; it keeps each global checked
  once.
* Not covered: `ok_or(Result::Ok(5), 1)` - nothing names `E` - is refused
  as "expected `i32`, found `T`", which names the wrong parameter.
  `const z: boolean = Result::Ok(1);` passes the type check: an
  initializer whose type still carries an unbound parameter is not
  compared.

## Ruling 171 (`Text`): measured, not built

* `Text` was added in §8.386 so the gates that count functions taking a
  spelling could tell message text from names among `string` parameters;
  the compiler's own lint reads only `SymbolStr` and `QualifiedName`, and
  the facts writer treats `string` as a key and `Text` as not one.  Its
  readers are the Python gates (name-taking, the lane gate, residue, the
  spelling-flow trace).
* Population: about 441 functions take a `Text` parameter (446 parameter
  records in `.facts/compiler.facts`), 2,934 `Text::new` wraps and 343
  `.as_string()` unwraps, in 104 compiler files and 5 editor files.
* Replaced by `string`, the gates lose the distinction they were given:
  §8.386-8.389 moved name-taking down 346, the lane gate's LOOKUP_OTHER
  down 49 and REGISTER 13, and residue down 49; deleting `Text` moves them
  back, and the lane gate, a ratchet, would be re-pinned upward.  Not
  safe under "no rule gets weaker"; parked.  It becomes safe when those
  gates stop reading `string` parameters as spellings, or are deleted.

## Comments

The 85 comment lines in `tests/`, `stdlib/`, `compiler/` naming another
language, its compiler or its package tool are reworded to state the rule
itself, each in place with its line count unchanged; the negative
`E0213_call_of_non_function` quotes its message instead.  The
`HTTP_VERSION` comment in `stdlib/net/http/request.cryo` no longer calls
its start-up initialization fragile.  Not touched: `.todo/`,
`scripts/ns-migration/`.

* §0: projects 216 -> 218; D15's braced-import files 702 -> 703.

### 8.555 Sema's locals are asked by the binding the name layer stamped; E0157 accepts a door by its marker; rulings 171 (amended), 172, 173 recorded - 2026-10-08

## Why

Ruling 149 makes the spelling lint door-only for lookups, and the pending
allows go by converting each lookup to a door or an identity.  Sema kept
a second scope beside the `scope-value` door: `ScopeManager` registered
every parameter, local, pattern binding and capture under its spelling
(`SemaState.locals`, `local_muts`, `local_kw_spans`, four parallel undo
logs, `param_ids`, `payload_binding_ids`, `alias_binding_ids`,
`lambda_outer_locals`) and asked them again by the identifier's spelling,
although the name layer had already stamped each use `Res::Local(sym)`.
Two locals of one spelling in one function were one entry: the payload
set was never scoped, so a `mut` local spelled like an earlier match
payload read as a payload, and in `const {a, a} = p; return a;` the use
read the second, void-typed registration rather than the binding it was
resolved to.

## What changed

* `LocalBinding { sym, ty, is_mut, kw_span }`, one record per binding, in
  `SemaState.bindings: HashMap<SymbolKey, LocalBinding>` with one undo
  log; `payload_bindings`, `alias_bindings`, `param_bindings`
  (`HashSet<SymbolKey>`) and `outer_bindings` replace the spelling-keyed
  arrays and maps.
* `ScopeManager`: `declare(sym, ty, is_mut)`, `set_kw_span`, `type_of`,
  `binds`, `is_mutable`, `kw_span_of`, `names_param`, `names_payload`,
  `names_alias`, `outer_type_of`, `reset`; the nine spelling-taking
  functions are deleted, and `PatternResolver::note_alias_binding` with
  them (`bind_arm_name` / `bind_payload` take the pattern's binding).
* Every declaration site passes the binding its node carries
  (`VarDeclNode.sym_id`, `DestructureBinding.sym_id`,
  `PatternNode.binding_sym`, `PatternBinding.sym_id`, the receiver's
  `receiver_sym`); every reader passes `ident.res.local_sym()`.  A
  `static match` arm's narrowing re-declares each live binding whose type
  names the parameter.
* The spelling lint accepts a door: `DirectiveProcessingPasses::is_door`
  (moved from the rule-4 check, which now calls it) reads the
  ``/// Door `id`.`` marker, and `lint_spelling_params` skips a door's
  parameters.  The nine allows on doors stay until the pins carry this:
  the pinned compiler's lint has no door exemption and refuses the tree
  without them (9 E0157 from `make cryo`).
* Not changed, kept as the old code had it: entering a lambda empties
  `param_bindings` and leaving it does not restore them, so after a lambda
  the enclosing function's parameters no longer count as caller-backed for
  E0455.

## Measured

* Agreement, old (by spelling) against new (by binding) at every reader,
  both answered in one compiler (`.objcmp/s123/u1-probe.patch`), over the
  corpus (`.objcmp/s123/c1`: compiler, stdlib, tests, every project and
  its `tests/`, examples, tools, the unit leg, the 232 negative files):
  3,200,000+ asks; 28 disagree, all explained.  27 are the payload bit at
  the assignment check and `subject_is_caller_backed`, where it is not
  read - the never-scoped spelling set calling a later local a payload.
  One is a type: `generic_destructure_shape_refused`'s `const {a, a}`,
  already refused (E0205); the use reads its stamped binding, typed `T`,
  not the void second registration; the project's report is unchanged.
* Controls: `S123CTL=narrow` (narrowing not re-declared) -> 407
  disagreements over the stdlib (1 without); `S123CTL=nosym` (no binding
  inserted) -> 9,832 over `examples/01-hello`.
* Lint: the HEAD compiler over the tree with the nine door allows deleted
  -> 9 E0157, one per door; this compiler -> 0; this compiler with
  `EnumType::get_variant`'s allow deleted -> E0157 on it.
* Clean build 328 warnings; against 329 the one missing is the W0015 of
  the deleted `keys.drop()` in `narrow_static_match_arm`, as predicted.
* Pending allows in `compiler/src`, measured and classified at the tip
  (`.objcmp/s123/ALLOWS.md`, generated by `.objcmp/s123/allows.py` from
  `.facts/compiler.facts`): 391 - door 4, lookup 82, lookup through a
  pending callee 46, register 2, AST carrier 43, carry 214.  Of the 214

* §0: flow list 600 -> 581 (19 entries); name-taking 663 -> 653; pending

### 8.556 A path's member and a callee's variant are asked of the member doors; `get_variant` and `TraitType::get_method` deleted - 2026-10-08

## Why

Beside the `member-variant` and `member-function` doors, sema still asked
a type's own lists by spelling: `EnumType::get_variant` (the door
`variant_index` runs the same first-match loop and answers the position),
and `StructType`/`ClassType`/`EnumType::get_method` where a path's member
was only asked whether it exists (`scope_member_binds_type`,

* `scope_member_binds_type` and `validate_enum_scope_member` ask

* `callee_names_ret_variant`, `async_poll_output_of` (`Ready`) and the
  import-shadow suggestion ask `variant_index`; `EnumType::get_variant` is
  deleted, and the uncalled `TraitType::get_method`.
* Not converted: the `get_method` readers that use the `MethodInfo` they
  get back (`scope_method`, `enforce_method_visibility`, the checker's
  closure call, `lambda_synth`'s `__call__`), and the import-shadow
  suggestion's whole-arena scan, which is a suggestion and belongs behind

## Measured

* Agreement (`.objcmp/s123/u2-probe.patch`, corpus `.objcmp/s123/c3`): 1,418
  asks, 0 disagree - `callee_names_ret_variant` 1,021, the suggestion 396,
  `validate_enum_scope_member` 1.  The struct and class branch of
  `scope_member_binds_type` and the `Ready` read are asked by no corpus

  (`.objcmp/s123/r2`: `S::get`, `S::hello` a trait default, `S::shout`,
  `S::nothing`, `C::nothing`, `E::first`, `E::nothing`, `E::A`) asks all

### 8.558 Ruling 179: E0157 refuses a spelling where it is looked up outside a door, not where it is taken - 2026-10-08

## Why

The spelling lint refused every function declaring a `SymbolStr` or
`QualifiedName` parameter that had no allow.  Of the 375 pending allows in
the compiler, most sit on functions that only carry a written name toward
the doors - syntax-tree constructors and setters, pass-along helpers - and
the lint could not tell them from a function that searches by the name.
Ruling 179: refuse a spelling only where it reaches a lookup outside a door.

## What changed

* New `compiler::sema::spelling_lookup::SpellingLookupCheck`, run by sema
  over every function body (every module, as the lint was).  Each
  non-receiver parameter of a spelling type seeds a binding; the check
  follows it into locals (initializer and assignment), through `&`, `*`,
  casts, element reads, members that are text, a `SymbolStr`'s number,
  concatenation and conditionals, and into the text a non-door call returns
  when handed it.  It refuses (E0157, at the parameter, once per
  parameter, with a secondary label at the site) a held spelling that is a
  hash table's key, an operand of `==`/`!=`, a `match`'s subject, or an
  operand of a boolean call that is handed other text and is either an
  operation of text (a text receiver: `equals`, `starts_with`, an array's
  `contains`) or handed the spelling as plain text.  A spelling handed as a
  spelling to another function is that function's to look up.  Doors, and
  bodies allowed with a reason, are exempt, as for the rule-4 check.
* `DirectiveProcessingPasses::lint_spelling_params` deleted; the directive
  pass keeps the store-key field lint only.
* Every allow is kept in this change: the pinned compiler that builds the
  tree still has the old lint.  Deleting the ones the new check no longer
  needs follows a re-pin.
* Tests: `spelling_lint_refuses_unallowed` asserted the old rule (five
  carriers refused) and is replaced by `spelling_lint_refuses_lookup`: six
  lookups refused (a comparison in a method, a search, a hash-table key
  behind a reference, a `match` on an element's number, a path's text
  compared, a body under `deny`), and a carrier, a pass-along helper, a door
  with no allow, a depth read and a receiver accepted.  The HEAD compiler
  refuses 10 there, carriers included.  The bodies of
  `spelling_lint_directive_shapes`, `_empty_reason` and `_missing_reason`
  now look their spelling up, so an allow still counting is what keeps them
  quiet; `directive_shapes` loses its `deny` case to the new project,
  because E0157 now comes from sema and its directive errors stop the build
  before sema runs (so in all three, "a malformed allow still counts" is
  held by that stop, not by the allow).

## Measured

* Probe (`S124_PROBE`, ignores allows but not doors; patch kept as
  `.objcmp/s124/u2-probe.diff`) over the compiler's own source: 413
  functions take a spelling, 73 look one up outside a door - 71 of them
  pending, 2 with a written reason (`template_field`,
  `check_destructure_shape`).  Against the pending allows' classification
  (from the facts report): ast-carrier 43 free / 0 refused; carry 203 / 3
  (`owned_by_current_module` compares, `FunctionRegistry::register` keys a
  table, `codegen_struct_literal` scans - shapes the facts classifier did
  not see); lookup 10 / 64, the 10 reaching only doors (`family_answer`,
  `keyword_primitive`, `modules_of`, `fresh_member_flag_name`,
  `specialized_identifier`, `pin_scope_callee_combined`,
  `try_pin_static_method_overload`, `suggest_similar_method` - its one
  comparison is on the suggestion door's answer -, `project_member`,
  `trait_declaring`); lookup-via-callee 43 / 3 (each also compares
  itself); register 0 / 1.  So 304 pending allows are no longer needed.
* Two defects found by the probe and fixed before it was believed: the
  call's type was read off the node before sema stores it (only 31
  refused), and a spelling handed to an unrelated boolean helper with other
  text read as a comparison (`try_emit_arith_macro`).
* Control: with the comparison sinks switched off (`S124_CTL`) the probe
  refuses 11 functions, not 73.
* LSP (`tools/CryoLSP`, out of scope here): 39 functions take a spelling,
  25 look one up; its 39 pending allows are left as they are.
* Clean build 328 warnings, the same set; the new compiler's `check
  src/main.cryo` over its own source (every allow still in place) reports
  nothing.
* verify `--require-identical`: the baseline's census fails exactly the
  declared `spelling_lint_refuses_lookup`; 0 objects moved (7,681 +
  1,126).  §0 row D53 re-pointed at the new check; D15 braced-import
  files 703 -> 704 (the new module).

### 8.560 Rulings 180 and 176: a closure keeps the enclosing parameters; `Cell(4)` infers its instance from the constructor's arguments - 2026-10-08

## Why

* Entering a lambda replaced sema's set of the enclosing function's
  parameters with an empty one and never put it back, so after a closure a
  pointer parameter stopped counting as the caller's storage and
  `return &binding` from a `match` over it was refused as a local's
  address (E0455) (ruling 180).
* A generic class constructed by value with neither written type arguments
  nor an expected type stayed the template, which has no methods (E0358)
  and no constructor code generation can call (ruling 176).

## What changed

* `LambdaSynth`: `param_bindings` is swapped out for the lambda's body and
  swapped back after it, beside the other per-function tables.
* `CallResolver::construction_instance`: after the turbofish and the
  expected type, `instance_from_constructor_args` infers the class's type
  arguments from its one constructor taking that many arguments, as a
  generic free call's are (`infer_free_call_bindings`): known argument types
  first, a literal's own type for a parameter nothing else binds; any
  parameter left unbound, or two constructors of that arity, leaves the
  template as it was.  `docs/cryo.md` §9.2 says so.
* Projects `closure_keeps_enclosing_parameters` and
  `generic_class_infers_from_constructor`, declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`.

## Measured

* HEAD's compiler refuses `closure_keeps_enclosing_parameters` with E0455
  at both returns (13:41, 23:41), one after a plain closure and one after a
  capturing one; with the change it builds and exits 0, the writes through
  both returned pointers reaching the caller's slot.
* HEAD's compiler refuses `generic_class_infers_from_constructor` with
  E0358 at each method call on an unannotated construction (`Cell(4)`,
  `Cell(big)`, `Pair(7, big)`); with the change it builds and exits 0
  (`Cell(big)` holds 8000000000, so `T` is `i64` there, and `Pair` binds
  each parameter from its own argument).

  declared projects and the tree builds and runs both; 0 other objects
  moved (7,681 + 1,126).  §0: projects 218 -> 220.

### 8.561 Ruling 181: the async lowering keys the locals it tracks, renames and rebinds by their binding - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Ruling 181: the async lowering's pending allows are converted next, its
  locals keyed by binding.  Every question the lowering asked about a local
  - is it read in this state, how does this state first touch it, does its
  last use give it away, where is its top-level assignment, which frame
  local is an address rooted in - compared the spelling of each use with
  the local's, as did the alpha-rename before flattening (a scope stack of
  spellings) and the final rebind of `poll`'s uses (another one).  15
  pending allows, and 3 written ones on functions that only hand a leaf to
  the field or variant door.
* Rulings 182-185 recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md`.

## What changed

* `sema/async_lower.cryo`: every walk that asked about a local takes its
  binding (`key: SymbolID`) and asks a use by `res.local_sym()`
  (`names_binding`); a declaration answers by `decl_key`.  Renamed by
  `scripts/ns-migration/8.561/key_async_walks.py` (the parameter, in 21
  methods) and `frame_roots.py` (the frame-root walks answer with the root
  USE, not its spelling); the comparisons by hand.
* Every use the lowering writes names the binding it means
  (`ident_bound`; the unbound `ident` is deleted): a minted temporary
  (`mint_temp` returns a `MintedLocal`), a destructure's `__ds` and field
  temporaries, `__rv`, a fresh declaring-state local, `this` (`poll`'s
  receiver) and `cx`.  A re-declaration that moves a value between the
  future and the frame - a parameter's shadow and take, a carried value's
  take, a promoted value's reload, a carried aggregate's pointer (one key
  per value) - is recorded as a STAND-IN for the binding it carries.
* The rename (`disambiguate_locals`) is a table from binding to fresh
  spelling (`RenameMap`); no scope stack.  `rebind_poll_locals` walks
  scopes of keys: a declaration declares its stand-in key, or its own
  binding, and a use takes the innermost declaration of the binding it
  names.  The receiver substitution asks the method's receiver binding.
* Frame roots and diagnostics: `PollSm.frame_keys`; `source_name(key,
  shown)` replaces `strip_local_marker`.
* Deleted: `RenameCtx`, `BindingRename` (`push_orig`, `index_of`),
  `rc_lookup`/`rc_enter`/`rc_leave`/`rc_bind`, `is_frame_name`,
  `strip_local_marker`, `ident`, the never-read `inplace_ptrs`.  All 18
  allows in the file deleted; the pin builds the tree with its own lint.
* Name resolution: an arm's alternatives (`A(v) | B(v)`) declare ONE
  binding per name - a later alternative answers with the binding the
  arm's scope already holds (`declare_pattern_binding`, through the
  `scope-value` door).  The rename keyed by binding needs this to spell the
  alternatives alike, which is what HEAD's spelling rename produced; the
  arm body's `v` already named the first alternative's binding.
* `scripts/lane-gate.py`: the stale exclusion of `BindingRename` and six
  stale scanned arrays (`AsyncLower.frame_locals`, `BindingCapture.names`,
  `BindingRename.orig`, `PollSm.frame_names`, `RenameCtx.orig`,
  `RebindCtx.names`), each deleted or keyed by binding here; the gate
  refused them.  `spelling-flow.outstanding.tsv`: 17 entries regenerated
  away, none added.
* Project `match_alternatives_bind_one_value`: alternatives binding a
  scalar and an owning payload, in a function and across an `await`.

### 8.565 The module graph's edge recorders only record; an edge is deduplicated as a module, once resolved - 2026-10-09

## Why

* `ModuleInfo::add_dependency`, `add_imported_namespace`, `add_reexport`
  and `add_submodule` each compared the namespace being recorded against
  the ones already recorded (and two against the module's own name), by
  spelling, and carried a pending allow.  The edges are recorded as text
  only because a module still loading inside a cycle is not in the graph
  yet; `resolve_edges` turns them into modules once discovery is done.
  Whether two edges are the same edge, or an edge back to the module
  itself, is a question about modules, and is asked there.

## What changed

* The four recorders push the namespace and nothing else; their allows
  are deleted (a function that only carries a spelling needs none).
* `ModuleGraph::modules_of` takes the module to leave out and whether to
  keep each module once: dependencies drop the module itself, re-exports
  drop it and keep each module once, imported namespaces and submodules
  keep each module once - the old rules, now judged by the module's index
  after `module_named` (the `module-by-path` door) answers.  Dependencies
  were never deduplicated and still are not.
* `scripts/lane-gate.py`: the three `written_*` arrays dropped from the
  scanned tables (nothing scans them now; the gate refused them as
  stale).  `spelling-flow.outstanding.tsv` regenerated: 7 entries gone,
  none added.

## Measured

* Probe: every module's four resolved edge lists, as module indexes, plus
  its unresolved-dependency count, printed after `resolve_edges`, with
  HEAD's behaviour and with the change, over the corpus without the

### 8.566 Note: the `--ast` dumper's colours, and how the fix is tested - 2026-10-09

Not a resolution change; recorded here with the change that replaces its
first test.

* The syntax-tree dumper wrote its colours as `\033[..m`.  The lexer has
  no octal escapes, so `\033` is a NUL followed by "33", and `printf` stops
  at the NUL: every `--ast` line ended at its first colour.  The fix (in
  the commit before this one) writes them as `\x1b`, the hex escape the
  lexer reads as ESC.
* That commit tested it with a new Python verify gate; the Python gates
  are being deleted before the merge, so the gate, its script and its
  fixture are removed again.  The test is now the project
  `string_hex_escape_is_esc` (outcome `run`): `\x1b` is byte 27, a colour
  sequence written with it has its full length, and a dump-shaped line
  printed through `printf` keeps every colour and its node.  With the
  line written as `\033` instead, the project fails ("output missing").
* What no test covers: the dumper's own text.  A project cannot pass
  `--ast` to its build, so nothing builds a program with it; the dumper
  file holds no `\033` after the fix.

### 8.567 Rulings 188-194: written reasons for the comparison primitive and the C-import path, three dead path methods deleted, `\0` before a digit refused, an arm's alternatives held to one binding each - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Rulings 188-194 (recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md` with this
  change).  Of the compiler's 45 pending allows, nine were either the
  comparison itself, dead, or a key that is no name in the program.
* The lexer read `"\033"` as a NUL and then "33" without a word, and the
  renderer, the highlighter and the syntax-tree dumper had each fallen
  into it (§8.566).
* An arm's alternatives (`A(v) | B(v)`) declare one binding per name
  (§8.561); nothing checked that each alternative binds every name, at
  one type, so `A(r) | B(w) => { r * w }` compiled and its body read a
  name the alternative that matched never set.

## What changed

* Written reasons: `SymbolStr::equals` ("the comparison primitive
  itself"), `ModuleGraph::register_c_import_module` (the graph creating
  the path of a module only it makes), `FunctionRegistry::register` and
  `get` (keyed by the linker symbol, as the registry's index already
  said; every caller hands a mangled or C symbol), and
  `owned_by_current_module`, which compares two source-file paths (its
  parameter renamed `source_file`, its comment corrected).
* `QualifiedName::equals`, `starts_with`, `ends_with` deleted (no caller
  in the compiler or the editor's facts).  `scripts/lane-gate.py` drops
  `QualifiedName.parts` from its scanned arrays (stale: nothing scans it
  now) and the flow list loses their three entries.
* `codegen_struct_literal` counts its initializers by their member pins;
  the field names only name a field in a message, and its allow is
  deleted (the lint read `field_names.length` as a comparison of the
  names).
* Lexer: `Lexer::refuse_digit_after_nul`, asked at every backslash of a
  string, a character literal and an f-string's own text (a hole's
  literals are lexed again with the hole), reports E0013 (new, "`\033` is
  not an escape ...") with a help line giving the hex escape the digits
  spell in octal (`\033` is `\x1b`).  A character literal so refused is
  consumed through its closing quote, so it is not also reported as
  multi-character.  The three comments describing the old silent reading
  are removed; `docs/cryo.md` §1.4 says there are no octal escapes.
* Patterns: `PatternBinding.written_mut` records a payload binding's
  `mut` (the parser dropped it).  `PatternResolver::check_alternatives_agree`,
  on the committed walk after an arm's patterns are bound, compares each
  alternative's bindings, at any depth, with the first's by binding:
  one bound only in a later alternative, one the first binds that a later
  one does not, one at another type, and one written `mut` in only one,
  each E0407 (new), labelled at both places.  `docs/cryo.md` §7.2
  states the rule.
* Negative tests: `E0013_digit_after_nul_escape` (a string, a character
  literal, an f-string), `E0407_alternatives_bind_different_names`,
  `_types`, `_mutability`; declared in `tests/started-passing`.

## Measured

* The corpus with HEAD's compiler and with this one, both over this tree
  (494 entries, every project's tests, the unit leg, every negative
  file): every log identical as a multiset but the four new negatives;
  status lines identical but the three E0407 files (rc 0 -> 1).  No
  program in the corpus writes `\0` and a digit (comments only), and the
  only arms whose alternatives bind names are
  `match_alternatives_bind_one_value`'s, which agree.  Controls: the four
  new files are refused by this compiler and accepted by HEAD's ("No
  errors found"; the character literal alone was E0003 multi-character);
  a scratch file shows the check reaches a statement `match` and nested
  payloads (`Some(A(v)) | Some(B(v))`).
* verify `--require-identical`: 0 objects moved (7,911 + 1,126); the
  baseline's census fails only on the four declared negatives.  Clean
  build 325 warnings, the same set.
* §0: pending allows 84 -> 75 (compiler 45 -> 36); flow 510 -> 507;
  name-taking 609 -> 607; negative files 237 -> 241.

## Why

  `private` and putting its door in the store's own file, so a lookup
  written by hand anywhere else is refused.  Ruling 189: the scope table
  first.  Ruling 187: a door goes with the store it reads most.

  "private" means "this file".

## Measured before

* `Scope` (`resolver/scope.cryo`) was read by name outside its file in
  two files: `resolver/resolver.cryo` (the `scope-value` door and the
  resolver's walks, every name-taking method) and
  `resolver/name_resolution.cryo` - four loops over `scope.symbols` that
  read only each entry's binding, and two `scope.find(name)` in
  `module_declarers_of_leaf` / `type_declarers_of_leaf`.  Nothing in the
  editor reads a `Scope`.
* `EnumVariantInfo.name`, made private and listed by the compiler: seven
  readers outside `types/user_defined.cryo` - three did-you-mean pools
  (`pattern_resolver`, `sema` x2), a codegen message, the populator's copy

  `pattern_resolver` that found an arm's variant by comparing variant
  names inline (`ep.variant_name.id == vname.id`), outside the door.

### 8.570 A generic body checks bindings, returns, assignments and branches with each type parameter one opaque type; a `static match` arm narrows the declared return type; rulings 201-202 - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Rule five (the answers are right).  The generic body is checked once
  and its copies are never checked again, but four checks - a binding's
  initializer, a `return`, an `=`, and the agreement of two branches -
  were skipped outright whenever either type mentioned a type parameter
  (`symbolic_defer_type`, "decided once monomorphized", which nothing
  decides).  `const v: T = xs.get(0);` (an `Option<T>`) compiled, and
  `first::<i32>` over `[5]` returned 0: the copy read the option's tag
  word as the element.  The `smallest` example in `docs/cryo.md` 11.3
  compiled for the same reason and exited 127.
* Rulings 201-202 recorded with this change.

## Measured before (a probe at the four sites, every skipped pair that
`can_assign` refuses, over the corpus: 494 entries)

* 54 distinct sites.  34 hold an unreduced projection (`This::SendFut`
  in `io/traits.cryo`, the async and projection tests): not yet a type,
  still deferred.  20 are `return`s in `stdlib/math` `min`/`max` inside
  `static match (T)` arms (`f64 => { return libc::fmin(a, b); }`):
  correct code, refused only because the declared return type `T` is
  resolved once for the body while the arm's locals were already
  narrowed to `f64`.  No binding, assignment or branch site in the
  corpus, and so no latent miscompile there.  The control
  (`b_optT2`, the audit's repro) was caught by the probe at the binding.

## What changed

* `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_judgeable`: in a generic body a type is
  judged unless it holds an unreduced projection; a parameter is one
  type, assignable from itself only.  The binding, `return` and branch
  checks ask it instead of `symbolic_defer_type`, which now serves only
  the destructure's field registration.  `type_has_unresolved_projection`
  recurses through arrays, tuples and function signatures too.
* `SemaVisitor::assignment_judgeable`: an `=` side is judged when it is
  settled, or in a generic body when its only unsettled parts are the
  body's own parameters.
* `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_narrowed` (with `symbolic_param_of`): the
  declared return type read through the enclosing `static match` arms'
  narrowings, used as the `return`'s expected type and as the type it is
  checked against.  Without the expected-type half, a first build
  refused the stdlib: 12 E0200 at `return Result::Ok(loaded)` and
  `Result::Err(loaded)` in `sync/atomic.cryo`, the value typed
  `Result<T, T>` against a narrowed `Result<u8, u8>` (672 across the
  corpus, the same 12 in each of 56 entries that build the stdlib).
* `docs/cryo.md` 11.3: the `smallest` example takes `T: Ord + Copy` and
  unwraps `get`'s option (built and run: 2); a paragraph states that a
  parameter is one type in its body, and that an arm narrows the return.
* Five negatives, one per check plus the narrowed arm (declared in
  `tests/started-passing`), and one unit-test file, `lang/generic_body_param_is_one_type.cryo` (five tests: the
  `match` and `unwrap` forms, a narrowed arm's return, the default arm).

## Not done

* Call arguments in a generic body are still skipped the same way when
  either side holds a parameter (`args_fit_params_loosely`,
  `apply_implicit_conversions_only` and the argument check skip any type
  `arg_type_is_concrete` refuses).  Not measured here.
* `get`'s `where T: Copy` is not enforced at a call under `T: Ord +
  Clone` (the old `smallest` example passed it).
* Two implementations of one generic trait for one type
  (`Conv<i32>`, `Conv<i64>`), called through `where T: Conv<X>`, are
  still an internal E0900 per copy.  `trait_item_on` and
  `named_method_on` (`mono/call_specializer.cryo`) pick an implementation
  by trait and receiver only; the call records the trait and the slot
  but not the bound's trait arguments.  The fix records them at the call
  in sema, carries them through the cloner and the substituter, and
  compares them with each head's trait arguments in mono.

## Proof

* Corpus (494 entries + the 4 new negatives) against §8.569's run: every
  log identical as a multiset and every status line identical; the new
  negatives each report one E0200 at their `//~` line; the unit leg's
  log differs only in its filtered count (2,219 -> 2,224, the new file).
* Controls: HEAD's compiler over the five negatives - `cryo check` exit
  0, no error, each; this tree's, one error each at the `//~` line (the
  branch negative was written after the corpus run and checked alone).  This tree's first build, with the narrowing used
  only for the comparison and not as the expected type, refused the
  stdlib (`sync/atomic.cryo`, 12 E0200), so the narrowing as the
  expected type is what lets the arms through.  `b_optT2` refused; `d_smallest_where_ord_clone`
  refused twice (E0200 at both `get(..).clone()` bindings).
* verify `--require-identical`: 0 objects moved (7,912 + 1,126);
  census, examples, lsp, cross, incr, check-fast OK; the baseline census
  fails on exactly the five declared negatives.  Clean build 325
  warnings, the same set.
* §0: negatives 241 -> 246; braced-import files 704 -> 705 (the new

### 8.572 Octal escapes in string and character literals; E0013 refuses a malformed one; ruling 203 - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Ruling 203 (recorded with this change) replaces ruling 192's refusal of
  `\0` followed by a digit with C's octal escapes.

## Measured before

* Every Cryo source in the tree with a backslash and a digit (the grep
  controlled on a file holding `"\1"` and `"\033"`): only comments and
  the E0013 negative itself.  So no program but that negative changes
  meaning, and no compiled object should move.
* A string's bytes after an embedded NUL do not survive to the program
  (`"a\0b"`: the byte after the NUL is not `b`, with this compiler and
  with HEAD's) - the literal is kept as C text.  Not changed here.

## What changed

* `Lexer::octal_escape` reads one to three octal digits, stopping at the
  first that is not one.  The string decoder (`process_escape_sequences`,
  shared by the lexer, the f-string parser and the C importer) and both
  character decoders (`CodegenUtil::decode_char_lexeme`,
  `sema_decode_range_bound`) read an octal escape through it; a character
  literal's lexing consumes up to two more octal digits.
* `refuse_digit_after_nul` is `refuse_bad_octal_escape`: E0013
  (`E0013_BAD_OCTAL_ESCAPE`) for `\8` / `\9` ("is not an escape: an octal
  escape's digits are `0` to `7`") and for a value past `\377` ("is out of
  range: an octal escape is one byte, `\0` to `\377`"), in a string, a
  character literal and an f-string's text.
* `E0013_digit_after_nul_escape.cryo` is replaced by
  `E0013_bad_octal_escape.cryo` (declared in `tests/started-passing`); the
  project `string_octal_escape_is_esc` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`) runs `"\033[1m"`, `"\0123"`, `"\18"`,
  `'\033'`, `'\0'`, `'\177'` and prints an ESC sequence.
  `docs/cryo.md` lists the escape.

## Proof

* The new negative: HEAD's compiler accepts it (no error); this tree's
  reports four E0013 at its four `//~` lines and nothing else.
* The new project: HEAD's compiler refuses it (E0013 at `\033`); this
  tree's builds it, it exits 0 and prints `033 [ 1 m b o l d 033 [ 0 m`.
  `string_hex_escape_is_esc` still exits 0.
* §0: projects 222 -> 223; name-taking 610 -> 611 (`octal_escape` takes
  the literal's text as a `string`; it looks nothing up).

### 8.573 A call's arguments are checked against the instantiated parameters, in a generic body with each type parameter one type; a method's where-bound on the owner's parameter is checked there; rulings 204-207 - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Rule five.  A generic body is checked once and its copies never again,
  and §8.570 found that call arguments skipped their check the way its
  four checks had.  Measured here, the hole is wider: a generic free
  call's arguments were checked only where the parameter held a
  projection, so a call that writes its type arguments had none checked
  at all, in a generic body or out of one.  `id::<i32>(xs.get(0))` (an
  `Option<i32>`) compiled and the program corrupted its heap
  (0xC0000374); `id::<T>(xs.get(0))` and `take_i32(xs.get(0))` in a
  generic body compiled and each copy over `[5]` returned 0;
  `xs.push(xs.get(0))` on the body's `Array<T>` passed sema and failed in
  code generation (E0900, no resolved method).
* `Array::get`'s `where T: Copy` was not enforced in a body whose bounds
  give `T` only `Clone`: the old `smallest` example passed it.
* Rulings 204-207 recorded with this change.

## Measured before (a probe at the argument check's skip, every pair
skipped in a generic body, over the corpus: 500 entries)

* 1,323 distinct skipped pairs.  955 were arguments of generic free calls
  whose parameter the check was handed as invalid (only a projection's
  parameter was passed through); 290 more the probe's looser predicate
  called mismatches were a callee's own unsubstituted parameter
  (`ptr::drop_in_place::<T>(this.ptr)`: the caller's `T*` against the
  callee's `T*`), not a defect.  The probe saw no `Array<T>` method call
  at all: an unminted receiver's call returns before the check.

## What changed

* `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_params_settle`: a type holding a parameter
  is still one type when every parameter in it is the body's own and it
  holds no unreduced projection.  `SemaVisitor::assignment_judgeable`
  (§8.570) is that or settled; `CallResolver::arg_side_judgeable` is that
  or `arg_type_names_one_type`, and `check_args_against_params` judges
  any pair both sides of which it accepts.  Its special refusal of a bare
  parameter's value for a concrete parameter is deleted: the general
  check judges the pair, with the same message.
* Inside a `static match (T)` arm both sides of an argument are read
  through the arm's narrowing (`symbolic_narrowed`), so a field declared
  `T` is the arm's type as a local is.  Without it the stdlib was refused
  (27 E0214 at `&this.value` in `sync/atomic.cryo`: `&T` for `u8*`).
* `params_seen_through` instantiates every parameter through the call's
  type arguments, not only a projection's; one it leaves open (a callee
  parameter neither bound nor the body's own) is as given and not judged.
  `check_free_call_projection_args` is `check_generic_free_call_args` and
  hands every parameter through it; a qualified generic call
  (`free_call_params`) and a method's own type parameters
  (`method_call_params`) are instantiated the same way.
* A call on the body's own unminted instantiation of its owner
  (`Array<T>`) is checked against the template's candidates seen through
  it (`check_args_on_template`), whether or not the selection bound one.
* `CallResolver::check_symbolic_method_bounds`: in a generic body, each
  where-bound of the chosen method on an unminted receiver whose subject
  is one of the owner's parameters must hold of the receiver's argument
  for it - a parameter of the body by the bounds in scope
  (`MethodBinding::param_bounded_by`), a settled type by its impls.  The
  E0358 it reports is the concrete case's, emitted by one function
  (`emit_method_bound_unmet`); for a parameter the help reads "add `T:
  Copy` to the bounds in scope here" (my wording).
* `tests/tests/lang/bit_intrinsics.cryo`: three `expect_eq` calls passed
  an `i32` constant expression where the first argument bound `T` to
  `u32`; the argument is now checked as a concrete `(u32, u32)` call's is
  (and is refused there too, at HEAD), so each is written `(...) as u32`.
  The asserted values are unchanged.
* `docs/cryo.md` 11.3: the rule covers a call's argument, a method's
  where-bound and an arm's field, with the two refusals shown.
* Four negatives (declared in `tests/started-passing`), one project
  (`static_match_arm_field_is_arm_type`, declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`: HEAD refuses `widen(this.value)` in an `i64`
  arm, E0214 "expected `i64`, found `T`"), and one unit-test file,
  `lang/generic_body_call_args.cryo` (a turbofish call taking the body's
  `T`; a `T` pushed onto the body's `Array<T>` from `get` under `T: Copy`).

## Proof

* Corpus (500 entries + the new files) against HEAD's compiler: every
  status line identical but the three new negatives HEAD accepts (and
  the fourth's, which HEAD refuses with E0900); every log identical as a
  multiset but those four and the unit leg's, which differs only by the
  three `bit_intrinsics` refusals before they were cast.  No program in
  the corpus compiled because of the hole.  That run predates the
  deletion of the bare-parameter refusal; `type_parameter_for_concrete_param`
  is refused with the same report after it, and verify's census covers
  the rest.
* verify `--require-identical`: 0 objects moved (7,970 + 1,126); census,
  examples, lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK; the baseline census
  fails on exactly the declared files.  Clean build 325 warnings, the
  same set; the clean build log, line numbers masked, identical.
* Controls: HEAD's compiler over the four negatives - three exit 0 with
  no error, one E0900; this tree's, the expected code at each `//~` line.
  The first build without the arm's narrowing refused the stdlib (above),
  so the narrowing is what lets `atomic.cryo`'s arms through.  The audit's
  `d_smallest_where_ord_clone` is refused at both `get` calls (E0358)
  besides its two E0200.
* §0: negatives 246 -> 250; projects 223 -> 224; braced-import files 705
  -> 706; `subject_sym` 26 -> 27, `param_syms` 101 -> 104,
  `TypeKind::GenericParam` 38 -> 39.

### 8.574 A generic type's own methods are registered under the template; twelve method-list scans by leaf ask the member-function or the trait-method door - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Ruling 204 (recorded in §8.573): the member-function door answers a
  generic type's own methods, registered under the template itself, so a
  lookup made inside the generic body has a door.  Until now a generic
  owner's methods entered families only per instance, and every scan of
  a template's method list - and, with it, of a type's `MethodInfo` list
  or an implement block's - compared each method's name with the written
  member.  Ruling 195's lint (not landed) raises these thirteen sites.

## What changed

* `FamilyOwner::Template(DefId)`: a generic type's definition as the
  owner of the methods it declares.  Its families are keyed apart (the
  definition half of `FamilySlot` carries its top bit), so no existing
  reader asking `Def` of the definition, or `Type` of an instance, sees a
  template's declarations.  A first build keyed them under `Def` and the
  stdlib was refused: a static call on `Array::<T, GlobalAlloc>` inside
  its own body found the template's entry and typed `void`.
* `DeclarationIndex::register_template_methods`: each method written in a
  generic type's declaration or in an implement block whose head names
  the template is an entry of `(Template(def), leaf)` - its signature in
  the template's parameters, no linker symbol, no definition kept, the
  entry its own method (two methods of one signature are two entries).
  Registered by type resolution for source declarations.
* `DeclarationIndex::methods_named(owner, leaf)`: the door's entries read
  back as methods; `holds_method` asks a method's membership by identity;
  `impl_family_owner` names an implement block's owner.
  `GenericRegistry::impl_methods_at_leaf`: every method of a trait
  implementation the trait-method door places at the leaf's position;
  `methods_owner_of(def)`: `Template` for a template, else `Def`.
* Converted, each keeping its own order and filters, with the name test
  replaced by membership in the door's answer:
  `CallResolver::lookup_method_param_types`, `check_method_call_arg_types`
  (both its own-list and its trait-impl walks), `pick_own_method` (owner
  threaded per base class), `bind_on_methods` (callers hand in the
  answer: the template's family, or `block_methods_named` - an inherent
  block's family, a trait implementation's by the trait door),
  `try_resolve_generic_static_method`,
  `resolve_static_method_return_via_template`,
  `check_static_scope_method_args`; `MethodBinding::resolve_method_return_with_explicit_args`;
  and four scans of a trait's declared methods by position from the
  trait-method door: `find_generic_method_on_receiver_bounds`,
  `TypeResolutionPasses::impl_binds_assoc_via_async`,
  `AsyncLower::bind_async_trait_assoc`, `awaited_keeps_recv_ptr`.
* Gates: `lane-gate.py` drops `ImplBlockNode.methods` and
  `local.MethodInfo` from `SCANNED_ARRAYS` (nothing scans them inline
  now); `residue_classify.py` classifies the two new compositions and
  drops the two retired tables; residue and the flow list regenerated;
  the lane golden re-pinned (`LOOKUP_OTHER` 17 -> 26, `REGISTRY_READ` 10
  -> 19: the scans' leaves now reach the counted door calls).

## Not done

* The collect_vtable_slots walk compares two declared methods' names
  (an override) - a written reason when the lint lands.
* Ruling 204's own example does not compile at HEAD or here:
  `this.map::<i64>(g)` inside `Box<T>` is typed `Box<U>`.  In a generic
  owner's body `resolve_method_call` types `this.m(..)` by
  `symbolic_find_owner_method` (a by-name scan of the declaration, which
  never applies the turbofish) before the explicit-argument path is
  reached.  Next: type it from the selection's `chosen` (which the door
  now answers) through `resolve_method_return_with_explicit_args`.

## Proof

* Agreement probe (each converted test computed both ways, a line per
  disagreement and per site's first hit) over the corpus, 504 entries:
  all fifteen probe sites live; outcomes and every log, probe lines
  removed, identical to §8.573's corpus but for the files that commit
  added.  Disagreements: 285, all one-way (the door omits a method the
  name test found), in two classes the index leaves out by design - a
  method whose signature the name layer refused
  (`E0203_refused_signature_no_cascade`: `method_bad`, `param_bad`) and
  the iterator adapters' self-returning default templates (`take`, `map`,
  `filter`, `skip` on user iterators in the unit tests), which are
  registered per instantiation.
* Controls: the door's answer missing its last entry - 53,484
  disagreements over the stdlib alone across the seven family-backed
  sites, and the stdlib refused; the trait-door positions shifted by one
  - disagreements at `bind_on_methods`, the trait-impl walk,
  `find_generic_method_on_receiver_bounds` and `bind_async_trait_assoc`
  in both directions, and at `impl_binds_assoc_via_async` (E0309 at type
  resolution, alone).
* verify `--require-identical`: 0 objects moved (8,027 + 1,126); census,
  examples, lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK.  Clean build 325
  warnings, the same set.
* §0: flow 498 -> 482; name-taking 611 -> 614; residue 200 -> 202 (J 127
  -> 129); `REGISTRY_READ` 10 -> 19; `this.slot_of(id)` 9 -> 10;
  `node.spec_owner` 1 -> 2.

### 8.575 Inside a generic type's own body, a call of its generic method types with the written type arguments; the owner-method finders ask the template's family - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Ruling 204's example did not compile: inside `Box<T>`,
  `const b: Box<i64> = this.map::<i64>(g);` was E0200 "expected
  `Box<i64>`, found `Box<U>`".  A call on the generic owner's own
  receiver is typed in `resolve_method_call`'s generic-owner branch from
  `symbolic_resolve_owner_method_return` (or, failing it,
  `resolve_method_return_via_template`), both reading the declared return
  with the owner's arguments substituted and the method's own parameters
  left as written; the explicit-argument path that binds them is only
  reached for other receivers.  Both finders scanned the template's
  declaration by name (two of the compiler's pending allows).

## What changed

* In the generic-owner branch, a call that writes type arguments has its
  return refined by `resolve_method_return_with_explicit_args`, as on any
  other receiver.
* `SymbolicChecker::symbolic_find_owner_method` and
  `MethodBinding::resolve_method_return_via_template` keep their own
  rules (non-static, the declaration's own list, exactly one) and ask
  membership in the template's family (`FamilyOwner::Template`, §8.574)
  instead of comparing names; their pending allows are deleted.
* Project `generic_body_own_method_turbofish` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`: HEAD refuses it with that E0200) runs the
  example and prints `widened 42`.

## Proof

* Agreement probe at both converted tests over the corpus (505 entries):
  99,628 checks (58,613 and 41,015), 0 disagreements; every log, probe
  lines removed, identical to §8.574's run but for the new project.
  Control: the door's answer missing its last entry - 345 and 326
  disagreements over the stdlib alone, and the stdlib refused.
* verify `--require-identical`: 0 objects moved (8,027 + 1,126); census,
  examples, lsp, cross, incr, blind, flow, fast OK; the baseline census
  fails on exactly the declared project.  Clean build 325 warnings, the
  same set.
* §0: projects 224 -> 225; pending allows 58 -> 56 (compiler 19 -> 17);
  flow 482 -> 477; lane `LOOKUP_OTHER` 26 -> 28 (golden re-pinned, no §0
  row: the two finders' leaves now reach `methods_named`).

### 8.576 E0157 follows a spelling read off a field; the entry point is an identity; rulings 208-210 - 2026-10-09

## Why

* Ruling 195: rule three for names on syntax nodes and type objects is
  held by the spelling lint, which followed only a spelling handed in as
  a parameter.  `decls[i].name.equals(node.name)` in a function taking no
  spelling was invisible to it; the 128th measured 61 such sites.
* Ruling 208: the program's entry point was recognised by comparing a
  function's name with `"main"` in four places (and the unused-function
  lint in a fifth), so every free function named `main` in any module
  was emitted as the C entry point and two of them refused the link.

## What changed

* `SpellingLookupCheck` follows a spelling read off a field of something
  that is not itself text, in every body, and refuses it at a hash
  table's key, a `match`'s subject, a boolean call handed other text, and
  an `==`/`!=` whose other side is a spelling too.  Diagnostic (ruling
  206): "`f` looks up a spelling read off a field", the site labelled
  "looked up here, outside a door".
* The entry point (ruling 208): `CompilationContext.entry_file` (the file
  the compilation started on) and `entry_fn`, recorded by
  `NameDeclarationPass::record_entry_fn` from the entry module's own
  binding `main` when it names a function.  `declare_function`,
  `codegen_function_prologue`, `emit_function_decl`, `desugar_async_main`
  and the unused-function lint compare the definition with it.
* The language's own names by identity: `GenericRegistry::names_lang_method`
  asks the trait-method door whether a written leaf names the method a
  language item claimed, compared by position.  The explicit-`drop`
  warning, `drop` on a `Copy` value, drop insertion's explicit-drop move
  and the async `poll` check use it.  The lowering's `Poll::Ready` and
  `Poll::Pending` are recognised by the variant pin it wrote
  (`is_poll_variant`); `Poll`, `Result` and `Option` by definition
  (`SemaVisitor::enum_decl_def`).  New language items: the compiler's
  `ASTNode` (which `new` routes to the arena) and its three text types
  (`SymbolStr`, `QualifiedName`, `DeclName`), which the lint's own type
  test matched by path text.
* Field positions: a destructure binding carries the field index sema
  pinned (`DestructureBinding.field_index`), which codegen reads instead
  of scanning the fields by name; a struct literal's missing-field check
  reads its initializers' pins.
* The keywords: the parser marks an identifier read from `this` or
  `This` (`IdentifierNode.is_this_keyword`, `is_this_type_keyword`) and a
  scope written `This::` (`ScopeResolutionNode.scope_is_this_type`); the
  name layer's `This::member` stamp and the editor's four `this` checks
  (ruling 205) read the mark.
* Written reasons: duplicate-declaration checks (ruling 200; the parser's
  impl generic list, the resolver's duplicate parameter and binding, each
  moved into a helper of its own, template disambiguation, vtable slots,
  the method-definition self-check), comparison primitives (ruling 188;
  `ModulePath::equals`, `is_within`), the module graph's own
  registrations, the C importer's own names, the dumper's shorthand, two
  diagnostics' offers, the `_` convention, file paths, and the two
  primitive-identity comparisons in impl-head unification.
  `modules_written_as` carries one too: it is the module-path relation
  and needs the import table the graph does not hold; it moves with the
  module graph's lock.
* `CallResolver::try_diagnose_forin_noncopy` is deleted: the where-bound
  check reports a for-in over a non-`Copy` element first (E0358 "the
  trait bound `String: Copy` is not satisfied"), so it never answered.
* Project `module_main_is_an_ordinary_function` (declared in
  `tests/started-compiling`: HEAD's link refuses two `main`s) exits 7
  through a sub-module's `main`.
* Rulings 208-210 recorded in `docs/resolution-rules.md`, with the lint's
  paragraph.

## Proof

* Inversion: a planted `decls[i].name.equals(node.name)` in a sema helper
  - HEAD's compiler checks the compiler with it, 0 errors; the new one
  refuses it, E0157 at the comparison.  Restored.
* Corpus (506 entries, the compiler, stdlib, tests, every project with
  its tests/ folder, examples, tools, the unit leg and each negative
  file), HEAD's compiler against the new one: every log identical as a
  multiset after the `This::` parser fix (the first run caught
  `This::make` refused in two projects).
* Control (`names_lang_method` always false, destructure index shifted by
  one), over every entry but the negative files: no entry builds (0 of
  257, against 170), the stdlib build crashing, and the stdlib's 233
  explicit-drop warnings are gone.
* §0: projects 225 -> 226; flow 477 -> 472; residue 202 -> 208 (J 129 ->
  134, N 21 -> 22); lane `REGISTRY_READ` 19 -> 23, `GRAPH_READ` 38 -> 39,
  `DEFID_PATH` 35 -> 33 (golden re-pinned); receiver-spelling sites 6 ->
  2; name-taking 614 -> 616; compiler pending allows unchanged at 17.
